children.translated_text: Śrīḥ (Auspiciousness)
<s>Kramadīpikā</s> (Light on the Sequence [of Worship])

An <s>āgama-nibandha</s> (compendium of sacred tradition) devoted to the exposition of the worship of the blessed Lord <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, accompanied by the commentary composed by <s>Vidyā-Vinoda Śrī Govinda Bhaṭṭācārya</s>.
(1) First <s>paṭala</s> (chapter)
Him who delights in the pleasure of playing the flute,
Whose chest is anointed with divine fragrance,
Who steals the heart-wealth of the <s>Vallavī</s>s (cowherd women),
I meditate upon that ineffable <s>Gopanandana</s> (son of the cowherd).

children.text: viśiṣṭa-śiṣṭācārānumita-śruti-bodhita-kartavyatāka-prāripsita-pratibandhaka-durita-nivṛtty-asādhāraṇa-kāraṇam iṣṭa-devatā'nusmaraṇa-pūrvakaṃ maṅgalam āśīr-vyājena kṛtaṃ śiṣya-śikṣārtham ādau nibadhnāti kalāttamāyety ādinā |
children.translated_text: The <s>maṅgala</s> (auspicious invocation), which is the uncommon cause for the removal of sins that obstruct the desired undertaking — the duty taught by <s>śruti</s> as inferred from the distinguished conduct of the learned — is performed under the guise of a benediction, preceded by the remembrance of the chosen deity; he composes this at the beginning for the instruction of the disciple, starting with '<s>kalāttamāyā</s>' etc.
He whose form is assumed through a fraction of <s>Māyā</s>'s power,
Who is charming with the softly resonating sound of the flute,
Who, dwelling in the heart, bewilders the three worlds —
May the beloved of the <s>Gopī</s>-folk be for your prosperity! // Krd_1.1 //

children.text: gopī-jana-vallabho yuṣmākaṃ śriye sampade 'stu bhūyād iti yojanā | gopījanasya gopāṅganā-janasya vallabhaḥ svāmī | tathā ca gopī-janasyaivāvijñāta-vinaya-prakarasyāpi vallabhaḥ kiṃ punaḥ sādhakasyāśeṣa-pūjā-vidhāna-kovidasyeti bhāvaḥ | yad vā gopī prakṛtir jano mahad-ādir anayor vallabhaḥ preraka ity arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: The construction is: may the beloved of the <s>Gopī</s>-folk be for your prosperity, your wealth. '<s>Gopī-jana-vallabha</s>' means the lord of the <s>Gopī</s> folk, the cowherd women. And thus, he who is the beloved even of the <s>Gopī</s> folk whose discipline is not fully known — how much more so of the practitioner who is skilled in all the procedures of worship: this is the purport. Alternatively, '<s>Gopī</s>' means <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), '<s>jana</s>' means <s>Mahat</s> (the great principle) and the rest, and their '<s>vallabha</s>' means the impeller — this is the meaning.

children.text: kīdṛśaḥ kalāyāṃ jñāna-svarūpe svasmin āttāyāḥ prāptāyā adhyastāyā māyāyā lavakena leśena vikṣepātma-svabhāvena āttā prāptā mūrtir yena sa tathoktaḥ | etena tasya śarīra-sambandhe 'pi na svarūpānusandhāna-pracyutir āvaraṇa-śakter aprāmāṇyād iti bhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Of what nature? '<s>Kalā</s>' means the essential nature of knowledge, i.e., in himself; '<s>āttāyāḥ</s>' means of [<s>Māyā</s>] that has arrived, been superimposed; '<s>māyāyāḥ</s>' of <s>Māyā</s>; '<s>lavakena</s>' by a fraction, whose nature is projection; '<s>āttā</s>' obtained; '<s>mūrtiḥ</s>' form — by whom: he is so described. By this, it is implied that even in connection with a body, there is no falling away from the contemplation of his essential nature, since the concealing power has no validity.

children.text: atha vā kalā bandhane, tathā ca bandhanātmaka-saṃsāra-pravartanārthaṃ svīkṛta-māyā-leśātmaka-jala-tattvātmanāṅgīkṛta-mūrtir iti | toyena jīvān visasarja bhūmyām iti |
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, '<s>kalā</s>' means bondage; and thus: he who has assumed a form through the water-principle, consisting of a fraction of <s>Māyā</s> accepted for the purpose of setting in motion <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) whose nature is bondage. As [the scripture says]: 'Through water he sent forth beings upon the earth.'

children.text: athavā, saṃmohana-mantra-rūpakaṃ kāma-bījaṃ sakala-gopāla-mantrāṇāṃ bījam udāharati kaleti | kaś ca laś ca kalau tābhyām attau gṛhītau sambaddhau māyā-lavakau caturtha-svarānusvārau tābhyām āttā svīkṛtā bīja-rūpā mūrtir yena saḥ tathoktaḥ kala ity atrākāra uccāraṇārthaḥ |
children.translated_text: Or yet again, he presents the seed-syllable of the <s>Gopāla-mantra</s>s, which is a <s>kāma-bīja</s> (desire seed-syllable) in the form of an enchanting <s>mantra</s>, with the word '<s>kala</s>.' '<s>Ka</s>' and '<s>la</s>' are '<s>kalau</s>'; by these two, '<s>attau</s>' means grasped, connected; '<s>māyā-lavakau</s>' the two fractions of <s>Māyā</s>, [i.e.,] the fourth vowel and <s>anusvāra</s>; by these, '<s>āttā</s>' means accepted; '<s>mūrtiḥ</s>' the form consisting of the seed-syllable — by whom: he is so described. The '<s>a</s>'-sound in '<s>kala</s>' is for pronunciation purposes.

children.text: punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ | kalam avyaktaṃ madhuraṃ yathā syāt tathā kvaṇan śabdāyamānaḥ veṇur vaṃśaḥ kala-kvaṇaṃś cāsau veṇuś ceti kala-kvaṇad-veṇuḥ | tasya ninādena ramyaḥ sarva-mukha-prada ity arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: Again, of what nature? '<s>Kalam</s>' means indistinct, sweet, as it may be; '<s>kvaṇan</s>' sounding; '<s>veṇuḥ</s>' the bamboo flute — '<s>kala-kvaṇat</s>' and '<s>veṇu</s>' [form a compound] '<s>kalakvaṇadveṇu</s>.' By its sound, '<s>ramyaḥ</s>' means charming, pleasing to all — this is the meaning.

children.text: punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ | hṛdi śritaḥ hṛt-paṅkaje sthitaḥ hṛdi dhyeya ity arthaḥ | yad vā sarva-prāṇināṃ hṛdaye 'ntaryāmi-rūpeṇa sthita ity arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: Again, of what nature? '<s>Hṛdi śritaḥ</s>' means situated in the lotus of the heart, i.e., to be meditated upon in the heart — this is the meaning. Or, situated in the heart of all living beings in the form of the inner controller — this is the meaning.

children.text: kiṃ kurvan | trayāṇāṃ lokānāṃ samāhāras trilokī | trailokyaṃ vyākulayan kartavyeṣu vicāra-śūnyaṃ kurvan māyayā mohayann ity arthaḥ | tad uktaṃ gītāyāṃ -
children.translated_text: Doing what? The aggregate of three worlds is '<s>trilokī</s>.' '<s>Vyākulayan</s>' the three worlds means making them devoid of discrimination regarding duties, bewildering through <s>Māyā</s> — this is the meaning. As stated in the <s>Gītā</s>:

children.text:
īśvaraḥ sarva-bhūteṣu hṛd-deśe 'rjuna tiṣṭhati |
bhrāmayan sarva-bhūtāni yantrārūḍhāni māyayā || iti |
children.translated_text: 'The Lord dwells in the heart-region of all beings, O <s>Arjuna</s>, causing all beings to revolve, mounted on a machine, through <s>Māyā</s>.'

children.text: atra laghu-dīpikā-kāraḥ kalātta-māyety-ādinā gopī-jana-vallabha ity anena ca bīja-sahito 'tra daśākṣaraḥ sūcitaḥ | kala-kvaṇad ity ādinā dhyānaṃ sūcitaṃ | trilokīṃ vyākulayann ity anena ca vaśyādi-prayogāḥ sūcitāḥ ity āha || KrdC_1.1 ||
children.translated_text: Here the author of the <s>Laghu-Dīpikā</s> says: by '<s>kalāttamāyā</s>' etc. and '<s>Gopī-jana-vallabha</s>', the ten-syllable [<s>mantra</s>] together with the seed-syllable is indicated. By '<s>kala-kvaṇat</s>' etc., the <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is indicated. By '<s>trilokīṃ vyākulayan</s>', the applications such as <s>vaśya</s> (subjugation) etc. are indicated. // KrdC_1.1 //
Preceded by obeisance to the preceptor, he declares his undertaking:
The pair of dust particles, arisen from the lotus-pair of the guru's feet,
Honored, bowing with my head,
Having examined what has been spoken here by <s>Nārada</s> and others,
I shall describe the method of worship of <s>Śārṅgapāṇi</s> (the bow-wielding [<s>Viṣṇu</s>]). // Krd_1.2 //

children.text: iha granthe śārṅga-pāṇeḥ śrī-kṛṣṇasya yajana-vidhiṃ pūjāhomādikaraṇa-prakāraṃ vivicya vivecanaṃ kṛtvā kathayāmi āsamāpter vartamānatvāt | tathā ca, prācīna-granthebhyaḥ sva-granthasyopādeyatā darśitā | kīdṛśam ? nārada-gautama-prabhṛtibhir gaditam | etena svokteḥ svātantryaṃ nirākṛtam iti bhāvaḥ | kiṃ kṛtvā ? mūrdhnā mastakena mahitāḥ pūjitā ye rajaḥ-kaṇakā dhūli-leśās tān praṇamya kīdṛśān guru-caraṇa-dvayam eva padma-dvayaṃ tad-utthān tad-udbhavān | etena guru-bhart-bhatty-atiśayaḥ sūcitaḥ | tathā guru-dhyānaṃ śirasi kartavyam ity api sūcitam || KrdC_1.2 ||
children.translated_text: In this treatise, having examined — i.e., having made a critical analysis of — the method of worship of <s>Śārṅgapāṇi</s>, <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, the procedure for <s>pūjā</s> (worship), <s>homa</s> (fire-offering) and the like, I shall describe [it] — the present tense [is used] because it continues to the end. And thus, the superiority of one's own treatise over earlier treatises is shown. Of what kind? Spoken by <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, and others. By this, the independence of one's own statement is refuted — this is the purport. Having done what? Having bowed with the head to the honored dust particles — the minute particles of dust — of what kind? Arisen from the pair of the guru's feet, which are themselves a pair of lotuses. By this, the supreme devotion to the preceptor-lord is indicated. Also, that meditation on the guru should be performed at the crown of the head is indicated. // KrdC_1.2 //
To state the superiority of the <s>Gopāla-mantra</s> over other <s>mantra</s>s, he sets the stage:
Of those born as <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, <s>Kṣatriya</s>s, <s>Vaiśya</s>s, and the fourth [<s>Śūdra</s>s],
Of ascetics, forest-dwellers, householders, and celibate students,
Through <s>japa</s> (recitation), <s>huta</s> (oblation), <s>yajana</s> (sacrifice) and the like, among <s>mantra</s>s,

children.text: phalati hi kaścana kasyacit kathañcit // Krd_1.3 //
children.translated_text: Indeed some [<s>mantra</s>] bears fruit for some person somehow. // Krd_1.3 //

children.text: hi yataḥ manūnāṃ gopāla-mantra-vyatiriktānāṃ madhye kaścana mantrorāśyādinā śodhitaḥ kṣiti-sura-prabhṛtīnāṃ varṇānāṃ madhye muni-vanavāsi-prabhṛtīnām āśramāṇāṃ cakārāt strīṇāṃ madhye kasyacit kathaṃcij janasya bhāgya-vaśāj japa-homādibhir ādi-śabdena tarpaṇādeḥ parigrahaḥ | phalati phalaṃ dadātīti yojanā | hi śabdo 'trāvadhāraṇa iti kaścit kṣitisuro brāhmaṇaḥ | nṛpaḥ kṣatriyaḥ | viṭ vaiśyaḥ | turīyaḥ śūdraḥ | munir yatiḥ | vanavāsī vānaprasthaḥ | gṛhasthaḥ kṛta-dāra-parigrahaḥ | varṇī brahmacārī || KrdC_1.3 ||
children.translated_text: Since (<s>hi</s>) among <s>mantra</s>s other than the <s>Gopāla-mantra</s>, some <s>mantra</s>, purified through <s>rāśi</s> (zodiacal compatibility) and the like, for some person among the <s>varṇa</s>s (classes) beginning with <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, and among the <s>āśrama</s>s (stages of life) beginning with ascetics — the word '<s>ca</s>' includes women — by fortune, through <s>japa</s>, <s>homa</s>, and the like — the word '<s>ādi</s>' includes <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) etc. — bears fruit, i.e., yields results: this is the construction. The word '<s>hi</s>' here indicates emphasis. '<s>Kṣiti-sura</s>' means a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>; '<s>nṛpa</s>' a <s>Kṣatriya</s>; '<s>viṭ</s>' a <s>Vaiśya</s>; '<s>turīya</s>' a <s>Śūdra</s>; '<s>muni</s>' a renunciant; '<s>vanavāsī</s>' a forest-dweller; '<s>gṛhastha</s>' one who has taken a wife; '<s>varṇī</s>' a <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate student). // KrdC_1.3 //
Now he states that the <s>Gopāla-mantra</s> is efficacious for all:
In all <s>varṇa</s>s (classes) and <s>āśrama</s>s (stages of life),
For women of various names and birth-distinctions,
A bestower of desired fruits
Is this <s>Gopālaka-mantra</s>, [acting] swiftly indeed. // Krd_1.4 //

children.text: siddhādi-gaṇanānirapekṣa evaiṣa prathopasthito vakṣyamāṇa-daśākṣara-gopāla-mantro na tu gopāla-viṣayako mantra-gaṇo 'tiprasaṅgāt |
children.translated_text: This forthcoming ten-syllable <s>Gopāla-mantra</s> that has presented itself is independent of calculations such as <s>siddha</s> etc.; it is not the class of <s>mantra</s>s pertaining to <s>Gopāla</s> [in general], to avoid over-extension.
'A <s>dvija</s> (twice-born) who gives to a <s>Śūdra</s> a <s>mantra</s> conjoined with <s>svāhā</s> and <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ),
The <s>Śūdra</s> would go to hell, and the <s>dvija</s> would be reborn as a <s>Śūdra</s>.'

children.text: ity āgama-virodhāt | lakṣaṇāpatteś ca | vāñchitānāṃ svābhimatānāṃ phalānāṃ drāg eva jhaṭity eva dātā keṣu sarveṣu varṇeṣu brāhmaṇādiṣu sarvāśrameṣu brahmacāri-prabhṛtiṣu nārīṣu nānāhvaya-janmabheṣu nānā-prakāra-nāmasu tahtā nānā-prakāra-janma-nakṣatreṣu stasv apīty arthaḥ || KrdC_1.4 ||
children.translated_text: [This restriction does not apply here] because of contradiction with the [present] <s>āgama</s> (scripture); and because of the application of secondary meaning. '<s>Vāñchitānām</s>' means of desired; '<s>phalānām</s>' of fruits; '<s>drāg eva</s>' means instantly; '<s>dātā</s>' bestower — in whom? In all <s>varṇa</s>s, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s and so on; in all <s>āśrama</s>s, <s>brahmacārin</s>s and so on; for women of various names and various birth-<s>nakṣatra</s>s (birth-constellations) — in them also: this is the meaning. // KrdC_1.4 //

children.text: evaṃ saty api guru-caraṇa-śuśrūṣā-paropasthitāya mantro deya iti vyanakti-
children.translated_text: Even so, he clarifies that the <s>mantra</s> should be given to one who has presented himself through devoted service to the guru's feet:
Surely, by the sidelong glance of <s>Acyuta</s> (the Unfallen One),
<s>Bhakti</s> (devotion) directly becomes the cause.
For the attainment of that fourfold fruit, therefore,
One endowed with <s>bhakti</s> is qualified [to receive initiation] in <s>Hari</s> and the <s>Guru</s>. // Krd_1.5 //

children.text: yasmān nūnaṃ niścitam acyuta-kaṭākṣa-pātena śrī-kṛṣṇa-kṛpāvalokane bhaktir añjasā tattvataḥ kāraṇaṃ tatas tasmāt kāraṇāt tac catuṣṭaya-phalāptaye prasiddha-dharmādi-puruṣārtha-catuṣṭaya-rūpa-phala-prāpty-arthaṃ harau viṣṇau gurau mantra-dātari ca bhakti-yukta-puruṣo dīkṣādāv adhikṛto 'dhikārī bhavatīty arthaḥ | etena guru-devatayor abhedena dhyānaṃ kartavyam iti sūcitam || KrdC_1.5 ||
children.translated_text: Since surely, i.e., certainly, by the sidelong glance of <s>Acyuta</s>, i.e., by the gracious look of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) directly, i.e., in truth, becomes the cause; therefore, for the attainment of that fourfold fruit — i.e., for obtaining the result in the form of the well-known four <s>puruṣārtha</s>s (aims of human life) beginning with <s>dharma</s> — a person endowed with <s>bhakti</s> is qualified, i.e., has the right, for <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) and the rest, in <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) and in the <s>Guru</s> (the giver of the <s>mantra</s>). By this, it is indicated that meditation should be performed on the <s>Guru</s> and the deity as non-different. // KrdC_1.5 //
Now he describes the sequence of worship:
Having bathed, wearing clean, pure, fine garments, with washed feet, hands, and face,

Having performed <s>ācamana</s> (sipping water for purification), with hands sealed with <s>pavitra</s> (purificatory ring) and <s>mudrā</s>, resplendent with white <s>ūrdhvapuṇḍra</s> (vertical forehead mark),
Facing east, having firmly assumed <s>padmāsana</s> (lotus posture) or <s>svastikāsana</s>,

children.text: vāsīnaḥ sva-gurūn gaṇādhipam atho vandeta baddhāñjaliḥ // Krd_1.6 //
children.translated_text: Seated, one should salute one's preceptors and <s>Gaṇādhipa</s> (Lord of the hosts [<s>Gaṇeśa</s>]) with joined palms. // Krd_1.6 //

children.text: snātaḥ sva-gṛhyokta-vidhinā āgamokta-vidhināpīti kecit | nirmale viśade prakṣālite sūkṣme vastre yasya sa tathoktaḥ | dhauteti prakṣālita-pāṇi-pāda-vadanaḥ | svācāntaḥ smṛty-ukta-vidhinā kṛtācamanaḥ | sa-pavitreti pavitra-sahitaḥ mudrā-yukta-hastaḥ supavitreti-pāṭhe atiśobhana-pavitreṇa mudritaḥ mudrā-sambaddho tilakenojjvalaḥ | prācī-dig-vadanaḥ pūrvābhimukhaḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Snātaḥ</s>' means bathed according to the method prescribed in one's own <s>Gṛhya</s> [<s>Sūtra</s>]; some say also according to the method prescribed in <s>Āgama</s>. '<s>Nirmale</s>' means bright, washed, fine garments — he who has such is so described. '<s>Dhauta</s>' means one whose hands, feet, and face are washed. '<s>Svācāntaḥ</s>' means one who has performed <s>ācamana</s> according to the method prescribed in <s>Smṛti</s>. '<s>Sa-pavitra</s>' means possessing the <s>pavitra</s> (purificatory ring), with hands sealed with <s>mudrā</s>; in the reading '<s>supavitra</s>', one sealed with an exceedingly beautiful <s>pavitra</s>, connected with <s>mudrā</s>; resplendent with the <s>tilaka</s> (forehead mark). '<s>Prācī-dig-vadana</s>' means facing east.

children.text: atra prāg-vadanasya kaṇṭhoktatvāt prāg-vadanaṃ mukhyaṃ tad-asambhave tūdaṅmukhatvaṃ rātrau tu sarva-pūjāsvedodaṅmukhatvaṃ purāṇe ca tathaivābhidhānāt | anantaraṃ sudṛḍhaṃ yathā syāt tathā padmāsanaṃ svastikaṃ vā kṛtvā | tatra padmāsanaṃ prasiddhaṃ, svastikaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ tu -
children.translated_text: Here, since facing east is prescribed in the <s>Kaṇṭha</s> [texts], facing east is primary; when that is not possible, then facing north; but at night, in all worship, facing north [is prescribed], as stated also in the <s>Purāṇa</s>s. Then, having assumed the <s>padmāsana</s> or <s>svastikāsana</s> firmly. The <s>padmāsana</s> there is well known; the definition of <s>svastikāsana</s> is:

children.text: jānūrvor antare samyak kṛtvā pāda-tale ubhe |
children.translated_text: 'Having properly placed both soles of the feet between the knees and thighs,
Sitting with the body erect — they call that <s>svastikāsana</s>.'

children.text: āsīna upaviṣṭaḥ sva-gurūn gaṇeśaṃ ca vandeta | atho śabdaś cārthe 'nukta-samuccayena tenāgre durgāṃ pṛṣṭhe kṣetra-pālaṃ vandeta tad uktaṃ gautamīye vāme guruṃ dakṣiṇato gaṇeśaṃ durgāṃ puraḥ kṣetrapatiṃ ca paścāt | iti |
children.translated_text: Seated, i.e., having sat down, one should salute one's preceptors and <s>Gaṇeśa</s>. The word '<s>atho</s>' in the sense of 'and' — by unexpressed inclusion, one should also salute <s>Durgā</s> in front and <s>Kṣetrapāla</s> (guardian of the sacred field) behind. As stated in the <s>Gautamīya</s>: 'The <s>Guru</s> on the left, <s>Gaṇeśa</s> on the right, <s>Durgā</s> in front, and the <s>Kṣetrapati</s> (lord of the field) behind.'

children.text: prayogaś ca guṃ gurbhyo namaḥ, gaṃ gaṇapataye namaḥ, duṃ durgāyai namaḥ, kṣeṃ kṣetrapālāya namaḥ | baddhāñjaliḥ kṛtāñjali-puṭaḥ sann ity arthaḥ | atra śāradā-tilakokta-krameṇaitad boddhavyaṃ dakṣiṇe pūjā-dravya-sthāpanaṃ vāme jala-kumbha-sthāpanaṃ pṛṣṭhe kara-prakṣālana-pātra-sthāpanaṃ purato dīpa-cāmarādy-upakaraṇa-sthāpanam iti || KrdC_1.6 ||
children.translated_text: The practice is: '<s>guṃ gurbhyo namaḥ</s>' (obeisance to the preceptors), '<s>gaṃ gaṇapataye namaḥ</s>' (obeisance to <s>Gaṇapati</s>), '<s>duṃ durgāyai namaḥ</s>' (obeisance to <s>Durgā</s>), '<s>kṣeṃ kṣetrapālāya namaḥ</s>' (obeisance to <s>Kṣetrapāla</s>). '<s>Baddhāñjaliḥ</s>' means having made the <s>añjali</s> gesture (joined palms). Here, this should be understood according to the sequence stated in the <s>Śāradā-Tilaka</s>: placement of worship materials on the right, placement of water vessel on the left, placement of hand-washing vessel behind, and placement of lamp, <s>cāmara</s> (fly-whisk) and other implements in front. // KrdC_1.6 //
He states what is to be done before <s>bhūtaśuddhi</s> (purification of the elements):
Then, having purified the hands with the <s>astra-mantra</s> (weapon-<s>mantra</s>),
Having performed the three claps, sealing of the directions, and [establishing] the fire enclosure,
This body, composed of the [five] elements,
The pure-minded one should purify in sequence. // Krd_1.7 //

children.text: tatas tad-anantaraṃ bhūtātmakaṃ pṛthivyādi-pañca-mahābhūtamayam etad aṅgaṃ śarīraṃ śuddha-matiḥ viśada-matiḥ viśodhayed devatātmakaṃ kuryād ity arthaḥ | nādevo devam arcayed iti vacanāt | krameṇa vakṣyamāṇa-prakāreṇa | kiṃ kṛtvā ? astra-mantreṇaiva astrāya phaḍ ity anena tan-mantrāṅgāstra-mantreṇaiva vā, gandha-puṣpābhyāṃ hastau saṃśodhya kara-nyāsaṃ kṛtvāstra-mantreṇaivordhvordhvaṃ tāla-trayaṃ kuryāt | tad uktaṃ śāradāyām-kara-nyāsaṃ samāsādya kuryāt tāla-trayaṃ tataḥ iti |
children.translated_text: Then, thereafter, this body — composed of the five great elements beginning with earth, i.e., '<s>bhūtātmaka</s>' — the pure-minded one should purify, i.e., make it divine in nature: this is the meaning. Because [of the maxim]: 'One who is not a god should not worship a god.' In sequence, i.e., according to the procedure to be described. Having done what? With the <s>astra-mantra</s> itself, '<s>astrāya phaṭ</s>' — or with the <s>astra-mantra</s> that is an auxiliary of that [main] <s>mantra</s> — having purified the hands with sandal-paste and flowers, having performed <s>karanyāsa</s> (hand-consecration), one should perform the three claps upward with the <s>astra-mantra</s> itself. As stated in the <s>Śāradā</s>: 'Having performed <s>karanyāsa</s>, one should then perform the three claps.'

children.text: anantaram astra-mantreṇaiva choṭikayā daśa-dig-bandhanaṃ astra-mantreṇaiva vahni-prākāraṃ jalenātmanaḥ pariveṣṭana-rūpaṃ vidhāya kṛtvā | atra sampradāyaḥ hṛt-padma-karṇikā-sthaṃ dīpa-śikhā-nibhaṃ jīvātmānaṃ haṃsa iti mantreṇa suṣumṇā-vartmanā mastakopari sahasra-dala-kamalāvasthita-paramātmani saṃyojya pṛthavy-ādi-pañca-viṃśati-tattvāni tatra vilīnāni vibhāvya bhūta-śuddhiṃ kuryāt || KrdC_1.7 ||
children.translated_text: Next, with the <s>astra-mantra</s> itself, sealing the ten directions with a finger-snap, and with the <s>astra-mantra</s> itself establishing a fire-wall — a surrounding enclosure of water around oneself — having done [all this]. Here the tradition is: one should visualize the individual soul, resembling a lamp-flame, stationed in the pericarp of the heart-lotus, [then] with the <s>mantra</s> '<s>haṃsa</s>' join it via the path of the <s>suṣumṇā</s> with the Supreme Self stationed in the thousand-petalled lotus above the head; and visualizing the twenty-five principles beginning with earth as dissolved therein, one should perform <s>bhūtaśuddhi</s> (elemental purification). // KrdC_1.7 //
He describes <s>bhūtaśuddhi</s> (elemental purification):
In the opening of the <s>Iḍā</s> [channel], [one should meditate on] the smoky, ever-moving seed-syllable with a fragment,
One should first contemplate the <s>mantra</s> that causes the desiccation of all worlds.
filling one's own body entirely with that extended form [of wind],

children.text: viśoṣya vyāmuñcet pavanam atha mārgaṇa-khamaṇeḥ // Krd_1.8 //
children.translated_text: having dried [the body], one should then release the breath through the path of the sun (the right nostril). // Krd 1.8 //

children.text:
iḍā-vaktre vāma-nāsā-puṭe salavakaṃ bindu-sahitaṃ satata-gati-bījaṃ vāyu-bījaṃ yam iti rūpaṃ pūrvaṃ prathamaṃ mantrī sādhakaḥ smaret | kim bhūtam ? dhūmraṃ kṛṣṇa-varṇaṃ | punaḥ kimbhūtam ? sakaleti | pañca-bhūta-maya-deha-śoṣakaṃ tathā ca vāma-nāsā-puṭena vāyum ākarṣan ṣoḍaś-vāraṃ vāyu-bījaṃ japed iti bhāvaḥ | anantaraṃ sakalaṃ sarvaṃ svakīyaṃ śarīraṃ tena bīja-mayena vāyunā pratata-vapuṣā vistīrṇa-śarīreṇāpūrya pūrayitvā deha-stha-vāyor bāhyenaikyaṃ vicintya viśoṣaṃ nītvā catuḥ-ṣaṣṭhi-vāraṃ vāyu-bījaṃ kumbhakena japtvā khamaṇeḥ sūryasya mārgeṇa piṅgalayā dakṣiṇa-nāsā-puṭena recanenaiva vāyu-bījaṃ dvātriṃśad-vāraṃ japan vāyuṃ vyāmuñcet tyajed ity arthaḥ || KrdC_1.8
||
children.translated_text: In the mouth of <s>Iḍā</s> (the left nostril passage), in the left nostril, [one should contemplate] the <s>vāyu-bīja</s> (wind seed-syllable) '<s>yaṃ</s>' — endowed with <s>bindu</s> (dot) and <s>la</s>-suffix, the seed of perpetual motion — the <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) should first recall it. Of what nature? Smoky, dark-colored. Further, of what nature? 'Sakala' means: desiccating the body made of five elements. And thus, drawing in air through the left nostril, one should recite the <s>vāyu-bīja</s> sixteen times — this is the meaning. Next, having filled one's entire body with that seed-formed wind of extended form, contemplating the unity of the internal and external wind in the body, having brought it to desiccation, reciting the <s>vāyu-bīja</s> sixty-four times with <s>kumbhaka</s> (breath retention), through the path of <s>khamaṇi</s> (the sun), through <s>Piṅgalā</s> (the right channel), through the right nostril, by <s>recaka</s> (exhalation) alone, reciting the <s>vāyu-bīja</s> thirty-two times, one should release the breath — this is the meaning. // KrdC 1.8 //
Through that very path, [contemplating] the wind as dissolved,
contemplating the seed-syllable as crimson, belonging to the swift-kindler [fire],
filling the body and burning it completely, through the left [nostril]

children.text: muñcet samīraṃ saha bhasmanā bahiḥ // Krd_1.9 //
children.translated_text: one should release the breath outward along with the ashes. // Krd 1.9 //

children.text: tenaiva kha-maṇeḥ sūryasya mārgeṇa dakṣiṇa-nāsā-puṭena vilīnaḥ sambaddho māruto vāyur yatra tad āśuśukṣaṇer vahner bījaṃ ram iti aruṇam aruṇa-varṇaṃ vicintya vāyunāpūrya tad-bījasya ṣoḍaśa-vāra-japena pūrakaṃ kṛtvānantaraṃ kumbhakena caturguṇaṃ raṃ-bījaṃ japan dehaṃ paridahya tad-ūrdhvaṃ ram iti dvātriṃśad-vāraṃ japan vāmata iḍā-mārgeṇa vāma-nāsā-puṭena bhasmanā saha bahiḥ samīraṃ vāyuṃ muñced ity arthaḥ || KrdC_1.9 ||
children.translated_text: Through that very path of <s>khamaṇi</s> (the sun), through the right nostril, where the dissolved and bound <s>māruta</s> (wind) resides — the seed-syllable '<s>raṃ</s>' of <s>āśuśukṣaṇi</s> (fire, the swift-kindler), crimson-colored, should be contemplated. Having filled with wind and performed <s>pūraka</s> (inhalation) with sixteen recitations of that seed-syllable, then with <s>kumbhaka</s> (retention) reciting the '<s>raṃ</s>'-seed fourfold [sixty-four times], having burned the body, thereafter reciting '<s>raṃ</s>' thirty-two times, through the left, through the <s>Iḍā</s> channel, through the left nostril, one should release the breath outward along with the ashes — this is the meaning. // KrdC 1.9 //
Now [the author] shows the arising [of the new body]:
The exceedingly pure [syllable] following <s>ṭa</s> — [i.e., <s>ṭha</s>, the moon-seed] — through the path of the nectar-rayed [moon], [one should bring] the moon,
the crescent on the forehead, from there [causing] the shower composed of all syllables;

children.text: la-para-japān nipātya racayec ca tayā sakalaṃ
children.translated_text: by recitation of [the syllable] following <s>la</s> [i.e., <s>va</s>, the water-seed], causing it to descend, one should fashion with that [nectar shower] the entire

children.text: vapur amṛtaugha-vṛṣṭim atha vaktra-karāṅgam idam // Krd_1.10 //
children.translated_text: body — this [form] with face, hands, and limbs — with a flood of nectar-rain. // Krd 1.10 //

children.text:
ṭasya paraṣ ṭa-paraḥ ṭha-kāras tam atīva śuddhaṃ śvetaṃ vidhuṃ candra-bīja-rūpam amṛtāṃśu-pathena vāma-nāsā-puṭena ṣoḍaśa-vāra-japena lalāṭa-candraṃ brahma-randhra-stha-candraṃ nayatu prāpayatu | nanu, sarva-śarīrasya dagdhatvāt katham amṛtāṃśu-pathena candra-bīja-nayanam iti cen, na | pūrvoktasya bhāvanātmakatvāt | athānantaram amutaḥ amṛtāṃśor lalāṭa-candrād brahma-randhra-stha-śaśaṅkāt sakalārṇa-mayīm mātṛkā-mayīm amṛta-samūha-vṛṣṭiṃ la-paro va-kāraḥ varuṇa-bījam iti yāvat taj-japena kumbhakena catuḥ-ṣaṣṭhi-vāra-japena nipātya utpādya tathā mātṛkā-mayyā vṛṣṭyā idaṃ sakalaṃ śarīraṃ racayed āracayet | kīdṛśam ? vapur vaktra-karāṅgaṃ vaktraṃ ca karaś ca aṅgam avayava-rūpaṃ
yatra tat tathā vaktra-karāḍhyam iti pāṭhe vaktrāḍhyaṃ karāḍhyaṃ cety arthaḥ | anantaraṃ dakṣiṇa-nāsā-puṭena vāyuṃ recayet lam iti pṛthvī-bījaṃ pīta-varṇaṃ dvātriṃśad-vāraṃ japan tat śarīraṃ sudṛṣṭaṃ cintayet | tad-anu so 'ham ity ātma-mantreṇa brahma-randhrāj jīvaṃ hṛdayāmbhojam ānayed iti sampradāyaḥ || KrdC_1.10 ||
children.translated_text: The one following <s>ṭa</s> is <s>ṭha</s>-kāra — that exceedingly pure, white moon, the form of the <s>candra-bīja</s> (moon seed-syllable), through the path of the nectar-ray, through the left nostril, with sixteen recitations, one should bring the crescent on the forehead — the moon situated at the <s>brahmarandhra</s> (crown aperture). Now, since the entire body has been burned, how can the moon-seed be brought through the nectar-path? No [objection is valid], because the previously described [process] is of the nature of meditation. Then, from that nectar-ray — from the crescent on the forehead, from the moon situated at the <s>brahmarandhra</s> — [one should bring down] a shower of nectar composed of all syllables (<s>mātṛkā</s>). The one following <s>la</s> is <s>va</s>-kāra, the <s>Varuṇa-bīja</s> (water seed-syllable) — by recitation of that, with <s>kumbhaka</s> (retention), sixty-four recitations, causing it to descend — producing it — and with that <s>mātṛkā</s>-composed rain, one should fashion this entire body. Of what kind? A body with face, hands, and limbs — that which has face, hands, and limb-forms. In the reading 'vaktrāḍhyaṃ karāḍhyaṃ,' it means 'adorned with face and adorned with hands.' Then through the right nostril one should perform <s>recaka</s> (exhalation), reciting '<s>laṃ</s>' the <s>pṛthvī-bīja</s> (earth seed-syllable), yellow-colored, thirty-two times, and should visualize that body as well-formed. Thereafter, with the self-mantra '<s>so'ham</s>' (I am He), one should bring the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) from the <s>brahmarandhra</s> to the heart-lotus — this is the tradition. // KrdC 1.10 //
Now [the author] shows the <s>mātṛkā-nyāsa</s> (placement of the alphabet):
On the head, face-circle, [pairs of] eyes, ears, nose, cheeks, lips,

children.text: dvayeṣu sa-śiromukheṣu ca iti kramād vinyaset |
children.translated_text: and teeth — on these pairs, together with head and face — one should place [the vowels] in sequence;
and the consonants on the joints of hands and feet, on their tips, with care,
and on the sides, back, navel, and abdomen — the [letters] beginning with <s>ya</s>-, and then // Krd 1.11 //
on the heart, armpits, hump [of the back], base of the hands, arms,
pair of feet, abdomen, and face — the wise one [should place] those that have arrived [there];
beginning with the heart, through this path, daily
one should perform the <s>nyāsa</s> (placement) for the attainment of a purified body. // Krd 1.12 //

children.text:
atra śiraḥ-śabdo lalāṭasyopalakṣakaḥ lalāṭa-mukham āvṛteti śāradādarśanāt ekatrākṣara-dvayasyāpi nyāsāpātāc ca | vadana-vṛttaṃ mukha-maṇḍalaṃ dṛk-śravaṇa-ghoṇa-gaṇḍoṣṭha-dantānāṃ dvayam iti samāsaḥ | dvayam iti dṛg-ādāv api sarvatra sambadhyate | ghoṇā nāsikā, dad-dvaye danta-paṅkti-dvaye ity ukteṣu sthāneṣu acaḥ ṣoḍaśa-svarān krameṇaikākṣara-krameṇa vinyaset tathā halaś ca kādīni vyañjanāni ca tatra kādīni viṃśaty-akṣarāṇi ādarāt ādara-pūrvakaṃ kara-pāda-sandhiṣu tad-agrakeṣu ca vinyaset | anantaraṃ ya-kārādīni pañcākṣarāṇi sa-pārśva-yuga-pṛṣṭha-nābhy-udarakeṣu pārśva-yugena saha vartate yat pṛṣṭha-nābhy-udaraṃ tatra vinyaset | tathānantaram anena vakṣyamāṇa-mārgeṇa yādyān
varṇān hṛdayādi-sthāna-gatān atrāpi kara-pad-yugayor udara-vaktrayoś ca hṛdaya-pūrvaṃ yathā syāt tathā anvahaṃ pratidinaṃ nyasatu | kara-pad-yugādīnāṃ pūrvaiḥ padaiḥ samastānām api hṛdaya-pūrvam iti kriyā-viśeṣaṇena saha sambandhaḥ sāpekṣatvād atrāsamāsa iti tu tulya-pradhāna-sāpekṣa-viṣayaṃ draṣṭavyam | kim-arthaṃ śuddha-kalevara-siddhaye śuddha-śarīra-sampādanārtham ity arthaḥ || KrdC_1.11-12 ||
children.translated_text: Here the word 'head' is an indicator for the forehead, since [we find in] the <s>Śāradātilaka</s>: 'the forehead and face are covered,' and also because two syllables are placed on a single [location]. 'Face-circle' means the face-maṇḍala. 'Eyes, ears, nose, cheeks, lips, and teeth — their pairs' is a compound; 'pair' applies to all beginning with eyes. 'Nose' means the nostrils; 'teeth-pair' means the two rows of teeth — on the stated locations, the <s>ac</s>-vowels, the sixteen vowels, should be placed in sequence, one syllable at a time. And likewise the consonants (<s>hal</s>), the letters beginning with <s>ka</s> — the twenty consonants [from <s>ka</s> to <s>pa</s> groups] — with care, on the joints of hands and feet and on their tips, should be placed. Then the five letters beginning with <s>ya</s> should be placed on the sides, back, navel, and abdomen — that which is 'with the pair of sides,' meaning the back, navel, and abdomen together with the pair of sides. Then, through the path to be described, the letters beginning with <s>ya</s> placed at the heart and other locations — here too for the pairs of hands and feet, abdomen and face — 'beginning with the heart' means so that [the placement] starts from the heart, [performed] daily. The connection of the hand-feet-pairs etc. with the preceding verses and with the qualifier 'beginning with the heart' is maintained through syntactic expectancy; though [the terms are] equally prominent, the non-compounding here should be understood as applicable to the case of equally prominent terms with mutual expectancy. For what purpose? For the attainment of a purified body — meaning for the accomplishment of a pure body. // KrdC 1.11-12 //
Thus having fashioned the body with half a hundred letters,
with those [letters] endowed with half-moon (<s>ardha-candra</s>), <s>anusvāra</s>, and <s>visarga</s>,
having placed [them], with the forms (<s>mūrtis</s>) headed by <s>Keśava</s>,
together with the powers (<s>śaktis</s>) beginning with <s>Kīrti</s> (fame), one should perform <s>nyāsa</s> in sequence. // Krd 1.13 //
Now I shall describe the forms of the syllables,
the powers pervading all worlds:
<s>Keśava</s> [paired with] <s>Kīrti</s> (fame), <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> [with] <s>Kānti</s> (radiance),
<s>Mādhava</s> likewise [with] <s>Tuṣṭi</s> (satisfaction). // Krd 1.14 //

children.text: ity ukta-prakāreṇa vapuḥ śarīram arṇa-śatārdhena pañcāśad-varṇaiḥ āracayya racayitvā anantaraṃ tair eva pañcāśad-varṇaiḥ sārdha-kṣapeśa-sa-visargaka-sobhayaiḥ | ardha-kṣapeśena saha vartanta iti sārdha-kṣapeśāḥ ardha-candra-sahitāḥ taiḥ sānusvārair ity arthaḥ | sa-visargakaiḥ visarga-sahitaiḥ sobhayair anusvāra-visarga-sahitaiḥ vinyasya tathādau śarīra-sampādanārthaṃ śuddher mātṛkākṣarair vinyasya tad-anantaraṃ teṣv eva lalāṭādiṣu mātṛkā-sthāneṣu aṃ nama ity ādīn kṣaṃ nama ity antān, tathā aḥ nama ity ādīn kṣaḥ nama ity antān varṇān vinyased ity arthaḥ | evaṃ caturvidho mātṛkā-nyāsa uktaḥ |
children.translated_text: By the method just described, having fashioned the body with half a hundred letters — fifty phonemes — then with those very fifty phonemes endowed with half-moon, <s>anusvāra</s>, and <s>visarga</s>: 'with half-moon' means accompanied by the half-crescent, i.e., with <s>anusvāra</s> — this is the meaning; 'with <s>visarga</s>' means accompanied by <s>visarga</s> — [letters] accompanied by both <s>anusvāra</s> and <s>visarga</s> — having placed [them], first for the purpose of body-purification with the <s>mātṛkā</s> letters, and then on those very locations beginning with the forehead — the <s>mātṛkā</s> stations — [one should place the letters] from '<s>aṃ namaḥ</s>' to '<s>kṣaṃ namaḥ</s>', and likewise from '<s>aḥ namaḥ</s>' to '<s>kṣaḥ namaḥ</s>' — this is the meaning. Thus four types of <s>mātṛkā-nyāsa</s> have been described.

children.text: nanu, katham arṇa-śatārdhakenety ukta-varṇānām eka-pañcāśattvād ity ucyate kṣa-kāreṇākṣara-dvayasyaikī-karaṇāt | la-tvena la-kāra-dvayasyaikīkaraṇād vā | loka-prasiddher vā prakaraṇenaika-pañcāśat-saṅkhyāyās tātparye 'dhigate pañcāśad-varṇa eva ka-pañcāśat-saṅkhyā-para iti prapañca-sāra-vivaraṇe śrī-premānanda-bhaṭṭācārya-śiromaṇayaḥ | vastutas tu arṇa-śatārdhaṃ ca ka cārṇa-śatārdhakaṃ tenākṣarāṇām eka-pañcāśattvm āyātam | asama-vibhāge vā ardha-śabdaḥ | keśava-nyāsam āha-vinyasya keśaveti | keśavaḥ puraḥsaraḥ prathamo yāsāṃ mūrtīnāṃ tāḥ tathā ca keśavādi-mūrti-sahitaiḥ kīrtyādi-śakti-yuktaiś ca mātṛkākṣarair lalāṭādiṣūkta-sthāneṣu yathā-kramaṃ nyāsaḥ kāryaḥ || KrdC_1.13-14 ||
children.translated_text: Now, how is it said 'with half a hundred letters' when the stated letters number fifty-one? It is answered: because the two letters of <s>kṣa</s> are combined into one; or because the two <s>la</s>-kāras are combined into one; or due to common convention, since in context the purport of the number fifty-one being understood, 'fifty letters' itself conveys the number fifty-one — thus [say] <s>Śrī Premānanda Bhaṭṭācārya Śiromaṇi</s> in the <s>Prapañcasāra-vivaraṇa</s>. In reality, however, 'half a hundred letters plus one' is 'half-a-hundred-and-one,' thus the number of letters comes to fifty-one. Or the word 'half' [is used] for unequal division. [The author] states the <s>Keśava-nyāsa</s>: 'having placed with <s>Keśava</s>' — <s>Keśava</s> is the foremost of the <s>mūrtis</s> (divine forms), thus together with the <s>mūrtis</s> headed by <s>Keśava</s> and endowed with the <s>śaktis</s> (powers) beginning with <s>Kīrti</s>, the <s>nyāsa</s> of <s>mātṛkā</s> letters should be performed on the stated locations beginning with the forehead, in proper sequence. // KrdC 1.13-14 //

children.text: govindaḥ puṣṭi-yuto viṣṇu-dhṛtī sūdanaś ca madhvādyaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Govinda</s> [paired with] <s>Puṣṭi</s> (nourishment), <s>Viṣṇu</s> [with] <s>Dhṛti</s> (steadfastness), and <s>Madhusūdana</s> [with]

children.text: śāntis trivikramaś ca kriyā-yuto vāmano dayā-yuktaḥ // Krd_1.15 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śānti</s> (peace), and <s>Trivikrama</s> [with] <s>Kriyā</s> (action), <s>Vāmana</s> [with] <s>Dayā</s> (compassion). // Krd 1.15 //

children.text: sūdanaś ca madhvādyaḥ madhusūdanaḥ ity arthaḥ // Krd_1.15 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Sūdana</s> with <s>Madhu</s> at the beginning' means <s>Madhusūdana</s> — this is the meaning. // Krd 1.15 //

children.text: śrīdhara-yutā ca medhā hṛṣīka-nāthaś ca harṣayā yuktaṃ |
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīdhara</s> is paired with <s>Medhā</s> (intellect), and <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> is paired with <s>Harṣa</s> (joy),
<s>Padmanābha</s> [with] <s>Śraddhā</s> (faith), and <s>Dāmodara</s> likewise paired with <s>Lajjā</s> (modesty). // Krd 1.16 //

children.text: hṛṣīka-nātho hṛṣīkeśa ity arthaḥ | ambujanābhaḥ padmanābhaḥ || KrdC_1.16 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hṛṣīka-nātha</s> means <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> — this is the meaning. <s>Ambujanābha</s> means <s>Padmanābha</s> (lotus-naveled). // KrdC 1.16 //
<s>Lakṣmī</s> [is paired] with <s>Vāsudeva</s>; <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> is paired with <s>Sarasvatī</s>;

children.text: prādyo dyumnaḥ prīti-sameto 'niruddhako ratir imāḥ svaropetāḥ // Krd_1.17 //
children.translated_text: <s>Pradyumna</s> is paired with <s>Prīti</s> (love); <s>Aniruddha</s> [with] <s>Rati</s> (desire) — these are accompanied by vowels. // Krd 1.17 //
'<s>Prādyodymna</s>' means <s>Pradyumna</s>. // KrdC 1.17 //

children.text: cakrijaye gadidurge śārṅgī prabhayānvitas tathā khaḍgī |
children.translated_text: <s>Cakrī</s> (discus-bearer) [with] <s>Jayā</s> (victory), <s>Gadī</s> (mace-bearer) [with] <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Śārṅgī</s> (bow-bearer) endowed with <s>Prabhā</s> (splendor), and <s>Khaḍgī</s> (sword-bearer)

[with] <s>Satyā</s> (truth), <s>Śaṅkhī</s> (conch-bearer) [with] <s>Caṇḍā</s> (the fierce one), <s>Halī</s> (plough-bearer) [with] <s>Vāṇī</s> (speech), and <s>Musalī</s> (pestle-bearer) [with] <s>Balā</s> (strength) and <s>Siṃhī</s>. // Krd 1.18 //

children.text: śūlī vijyā pāśī virajā viśānvito 'mbuśīr bhūyaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Śūlī</s> (trident-bearer) [with] <s>Vijyā</s>, <s>Pāśī</s> (noose-bearer) [with] <s>Virajā</s>, [one] endowed with <s>Viśā</s> (poison), the water-armed; and further,

children.text: vimadā muknda-yuktā nandaja-sunandaje smṛtiś ca nandi-yutā // Krd_1.19 //
children.translated_text: <s>Vimadā</s> paired with <s>Mukunda</s>, <s>Nandaja</s> [with] <s>Sunandā</s>, and <s>Smṛti</s> (memory) paired with <s>Nandī</s>. // Krd 1.19 //

children.text: nara-ṛddhī naraka-jitāsamṛddhir atha śuddhi-yug ghariḥ kṛṣṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Nara</s> [with] <s>Ṛddhi</s> (prosperity), <s>Narakajit</s> (conqueror of <s>Naraka</s>) [with] <s>Samṛddhi</s> (abundance), then <s>Hari</s> paired with <s>Śuddhi</s> (purity), <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>

children.text: buddhi-yutaḥ satya-yuta-bhaktir mati-yuktaḥ syāt tataḥ śauriḥ // Krd_1.20 //
children.translated_text: paired with <s>Buddhi</s> (wisdom), <s>Satya</s> (truth) [paired with] <s>Bhakti</s> (devotion), and <s>Mati</s> (thought) paired — then <s>Śauri</s>. // Krd 1.20 //

children.text: kṣamayā śūro ramayā janārdano meca-bhū-dharaḥ kledī |
children.translated_text: <s>Śūra</s> [with] <s>Kṣamā</s> (forbearance), <s>Janārdana</s> [with] <s>Ramā</s> (beauty), the cloud-mountain-bearer [with] <s>Kledinī</s> (the moistening one),

children.text: viśvādya-mūrti-yuktā klinnā vaikuṇṭha-yuk tathā vasudā // Krd_1.21 //
children.translated_text: <s>Viśvādyamūrti</s> (the primeval universal form) [with] <s>Klinnā</s> (the softened one), and <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> paired likewise with <s>Vasudā</s> (the wealth-giver). // Krd 1.21 //

children.text: kledī kledinīty arthaḥ | chando-bhaṅga-bhayāt tathoktaḥ | viśvādi-mūrtir iti viśva-mūrtir ity arthaḥ || KrdC_1.18-21 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Kledī</s>' means '<s>Kledinī</s>' — this is the meaning. It is stated thus due to fear of breaking the meter. '<s>Viśvādi-mūrti</s>' means '<s>Viśvamūrti</s>' (universal form) — this is the meaning. // KrdC 1.18-21 //

children.text: puruṣottamaś ca vasudhā balinā ca varā balānujopetā |
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣottama</s> [with] <s>Vasudā</s>, <s>Balin</s> [with] <s>Varā</s> (the excellent one), and <s>Balānuja</s> (younger brother of <s>Bala</s>) [paired],

children.text: bhūyaḥ parāyaṇākhyā bālaḥ sūkṣmā vṛṣaghna-sandhye ca // Krd_1.22 //
children.translated_text: and further the one named <s>Parāyaṇa</s>, <s>Bāla</s> [with] <s>Sūkṣmā</s> (the subtle one), and <s>Vṛṣaghna</s> [with] <s>Sandhyā</s> (twilight). // Krd 1.22 //

children.text: savṛṣā prajñā prabhā varāho niśā ca vimalo 'moghā |
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛṣā</s> [with] <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom), <s>Prabhā</s> [with] <s>Varāha</s> (boar), <s>Niśā</s> (night) [with] <s>Vimala</s> (the pure one), <s>Amoghā</s> (the unfailing one),

children.text: narasiṃha-vidyute ca praṇigaditā mūrtayo halāṃ śakti-yutāḥ // Krd_1.23 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Narasiṃha</s> [with] <s>Vidyut</s> (lightning) — thus the <s>mūrtis</s> (divine forms) are proclaimed, each paired with their <s>śaktis</s> (powers), [corresponding to] the consonants. // Krd 1.23 //
'<s>Amoghā</s>' is the word-division here. // KrdC 1.22-23 //
[The author] shows the method of the previously stated <s>nyāsa</s> of <s>Keśava</s>-headed <s>mūrtis</s> and <s>Kīrti</s>-headed <s>śaktis</s>:
Having uttered the letter with half-moons prefixed,
the <s>mūrtis</s> (forms) and <s>śaktis</s> (powers) ending in the dative, and the salutation,
having uttered [these], one should place [them]; with [the letters] beginning with <s>ya</s>, the seven <s>dhātus</s> (bodily constituents),

children.text: prāṇaṃ jīvaṃ krodham apy ātmane 'ntān // Krd_1.24 //
children.translated_text: <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), <s>krodha</s> (anger), and those ending in '<s>ātmane</s>' (for the self). // Krd 1.24 //

children.text:
purastāt prathamaṃ varṇān a-kārādi-kṣakāraāntān uktvā kathambhūtān varṇān sārdha-candrān sa-bindūn anantaraṃ mūrtīḥ keśavādyāḥ śaktīḥ kīrtyādyāḥ ṅe 'vasānāḥ ity ubhayena sambadhyate tan na hṛdaya-grāhi prayāsatteḥ lāghavāc ca aṃ keśavāya kīrtyai nama iti prayoge keśavāyety atra namaḥ-padasya yogābhāvāc caturthy-anupapattiḥ na hi viṣṇave sūryāya nama iti bhavati | bhavati ca viṣṇave namaḥ sūryāya nama iti (tathā ca keśavāya namaḥ kīrtyai nama iti) prayogāpattiḥ ubhayatra vā ca-kāro deyaḥ samuccaya-khyāpanārthaḥ | sa śriye cāmṛtāya cetivat tathā mātṛkākṣarāṇām api ubhaya-sambandhārthaṃ dviḥ-prayogāpattiḥ | aṃ keśava-kīrtibhyāṃ nama iti prayoge tu naite doṣāḥ patanti tatra dvandva-samāsa-vaśāt
sahitāvasthitayor evopasthitau caturthy-arthānvaya-sambhavāt varnānvaya-sambhavāc ca agnīṣomayor iva sahitāvasthitayor devatātvam | kathaṃ tarhi yādiṣu tvag-ādi-prayogaḥ kāryam ? ity ucyate yaṃ tvag-ātmane puruṣottama-vasudhābhyām namaḥ, raṃ asṛg-ātmane bali-parābhyāṃ nama ity evaṃ rūpa iti | mantram uktāvali-kāreṇa tathaivābhidhānāt | ātmane ity asya sub-anta-pratirūpaka-nipātatvenādoṣād iti tu prapañca-sāra-vivaraṇe paramānanda-bhaṭṭācāryābhyāḥ | tathā ca aṃ keśava-kīrtibhyāṃ nama iti prayogaḥ mantram uktāvalī-kāra-laghu-dīpikā-kāra-tripāṭhi-rudropādhyāya-vidyādharācārya-paramānanda-bhaṭṭācārya-saṃmataḥ | aṃ keśavāya kīrtyai nama iti prayogaḥ padmapādācārya-prabhṛtīnāṃ saṃmata iti | jñātvā yathā-guru-sampradāyaṃ
vyavahartavyam iti | atraiva nyāsa-viśeṣam āha-yādibhir iti ya-kārādyair daśabhir akṣaraiḥ saha sapta dhātūn tvag-asṛṅ-māṃsa-medo 'sthi-majja-śukrākhyān ātmane 'ntān ātmane iti śabdaḥ ante yeṣāṃ te tathā prāṇaṃ jīvaṃ krodhaṃ ca ātmane 'ntaṃ hṛdayādiṣu yathā-sthāneṣu vinyasyed ity arthaḥ | prāṇaṃ śaktim ity api pāṭhāntaram || KrdC_1.24 ||
children.translated_text: First, having stated the letters from a-kāra to kṣa-kāra, [the question arises:] what kind of letters — with half-moon, with <s>bindu</s> (dot) — then the forms such as <s>Keśava</s> etc., the powers such as <s>Kīrti</s> etc., ending in ṅe — this connects with both [the letters and the names], but that is not convincing to the heart, because of the effort involved, and because of economy. Moreover, in the usage 'aṃ keśavāya kīrtyai namaḥ,' the dative case of 'keśavāya' is unjustified since the word namaḥ has no connection [with it], for one does not say 'viṣṇave sūryāya namaḥ' — rather one says 'viṣṇave namaḥ, sūryāya namaḥ.' Thus the correct usage would be 'keśavāya namaḥ kīrtyai namaḥ.' Or the particle 'ca' should be given in both places to indicate conjunction, as in 'sa śriye cāmṛtāya ca.' Likewise, for the <s>mātṛkā</s> (mother) letters also, if both connections are intended, the usage would need to be doubled. But in the usage 'aṃ keśava-kīrtibhyāṃ namaḥ,' these faults do not arise, because by virtue of the <s>dvandva</s> compound, the dative meaning connects with both standing together, just as <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> together form the deity [Agniṣomau]. Then how should the usage with tvak (skin) etc. in the ya-series be done? It is said: 'yaṃ tvag-ātmane puruṣottama-vasudhābhyāṃ namaḥ, raṃ asṛg-ātmane bali-parābhyāṃ namaḥ' — such is the form. Because the author of the <s>Mantroktāvalī</s> has stated the mantra in just this way. As for ātmane — since it functions as a particle resembling a <s>subanta</s> (declined form), there is no fault — thus [say] <s>Paramānanda Bhaṭṭācārya</s> in the <s>Prapañcasāra Vivaraṇa</s>. Thus the usage 'aṃ keśava-kīrtibhyāṃ namaḥ' is approved by the authors of the <s>Mantroktāvalī</s>, the <s>Laghudīpikā</s>, <s>Tripāṭhī Rudropādhyāya</s>, <s>Vidyādharācārya</s>, and <s>Paramānanda Bhaṭṭācārya</s>. The usage 'aṃ keśavāya kīrtyai namaḥ' is approved by <s>Padmapādācārya</s> and others. Having understood [both], one should follow the tradition of one's own teacher. Here he states a particular installation — with the ten letters beginning with ya-kāra, one should install the seven <s>dhātu</s>s (bodily constituents) — called skin, blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow, and semen — ending in ātmane, along with <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), and <s>krodha</s> (anger), ending in ātmane, in the heart and other appropriate places — this is the meaning. 'Prāṇaṃ śaktim' is also an alternative reading.
He states the meditation for the <s>Keśavādi-nyāsa</s> (installation beginning with <s>Keśava</s>) — with 'udyat' etc.
Whose radiance is like a hundred rising suns, resplendent as heated gold,
On both sides attended by the daughter of the ocean [<s>Lakṣmī</s>] and by <s>Viśvadhātrī</s> (the sustainer of the universe),
Adorned with various ornaments sparkling with diverse gems, wearing yellow garments,
I salute <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who holds the conch, lotus, <s>Kaumodakī</s> (mace), and discus in his hands.

children.text: ahaṃ viṣṇuṃ vande | kīdṛśaṃ ? udyann udayaṃ gacchan pradyotanaḥ sūryas tasya yac-chataṃ tasyeva ruci-dīptir yasya taṃ punaḥ tapteti vahni-madhya-nikṣipta-kāñcanavad gauraṃ | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ pārśva-dvandve iti dakṣiṇa-vāma-pārśva-dvaye jaladhi-sutayā lakṣmyā tathā viśva-dhātryā pṛthivyā juṣṭaṃ sevitam | punaḥ kimbhūtaṃ ? nānā-vidha-ratnena śobhito nānā bahu-prakāra ākalpo bhūṣaṇaṃ yasya | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? āpīteti āsamyak prakāreṇa pīte vastre yasya taṃ | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? daraḥ śaṅkhaḥ padmaṃ kamalaṃ kaumodakī gadā cakram etāni pāṇau yasya tam | atra ūrdhvādhaḥ krameṇa vāma-bhāge śaṅkha-padme dakṣiṇa-bhāge gadā-cakre iti bodhyam || KrdC_1.25 ||
children.translated_text: I salute <s>Viṣṇu</s>. Of what kind? Whose radiance is like that of a hundred suns rising — that is, going upward — [the word] pradyotana means the sun; [he is] fair like gold placed in the midst of fire. Again of what kind? On both sides — on the right and left sides — attended by the daughter of the ocean, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, and by <s>Viśvadhātrī</s>, the earth. Again of what kind? Adorned with various types of gems — diverse ornaments of many kinds. Again of what kind? Wearing well-donned yellow garments. Again of what kind? Having in his hands the conch, the lotus, the <s>Kaumodakī</s> (mace), and the discus. Here it should be understood that in the upper-lower order, on the left side are the conch and lotus, on the right side are the mace and discus.
He states the fruit of meditation and installation — with 'dhyātvā evam' etc.
He who, having meditated on the Supreme Person in this manner,
Installs daily with the letters conjoined with <s>Keśava</s> and the other [names],
With intelligence, longevity, memory, firmness, fame, beauty, prosperity,

children.text: saubhāgyaiś ciram upabṛṃhito bhavet saḥ // Krd_1.26 //
children.translated_text: And good fortune — he becomes enriched for a long time.

children.text: evam ukta-prakāraṃ parama-pumāṃsaṃ viṣṇuṃ dhyātvā yo 'nudinaṃ pratyahaṃ keśavādi-sahitair mātṛkākāair vinyasyet sa puruṣaḥ | medhādibhiś ciraṃ bahu-kālam upabṛṃhita upacito bhavati medhā dhāraṇāvatī buddhiḥ āyur jīvanaṃ smṛtiḥ smaraṇaṃ dhṛtir dhairyaṃ kīrtir utkṛṣṭa-karma-kathā kāntiḥ saundaryaṃ lakṣmīr aiśvaryaṃ saubhāgyaṃ sarva-priyatvam || KrdC_1.26 ||
children.translated_text: Having meditated on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Supreme Person, in the manner described above, whoever installs daily with the <s>mātṛkā</s> letters conjoined with <s>Keśava</s> and the other [names] — that person becomes enriched for a long time with intelligence and the rest. <s>Medhā</s> is retentive intellect; <s>āyus</s> is life-span; <s>smṛti</s> is memory; <s>dhṛti</s> is steadfastness; <s>kīrti</s> is the narration of excellent deeds; <s>kānti</s> is beauty; <s>lakṣmī</s> is lordship; <s>saubhāgya</s> is being dear to all.
He states a particular installation — with 'amum' etc.
This very [procedure], preceded by [the seed-syllable of] <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>),
Whichever wise person performs —
Having attained the most excellent <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>, prosperity),

children.text: punar ante haritāṃ vrajaty asau // Krd_1.27 //
children.translated_text: He finally goes to <s>Hari</s> (attains the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>).

children.text: yaḥ paṇḍito manuṣyaḥ amum eva vidhiṃ keśavādi-nyāsa-prakāraṃ ramā-puraḥsaraṃ śrī-bījam ādau dattvā prabhajet karoti asau pumān iha loke prathīyasīṃ mahatīṃ ramāṃ lakṣmīṃ samupetya prāpya punar ante avasāne haritāṃ viṣṇutvaṃ vrajati prāpnotīty arthaḥ || KrdC_1.27 ||
children.translated_text: Whatever learned person performs this very procedure — the method of <s>Keśavādi-nyāsa</s> — preceded by <s>Ramā</s>, that is, having placed the <s>Śrī-bīja</s> (seed-syllable of <s>Śrī</s>) at the beginning — that man, in this world having attained the most excellent, great <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>, prosperity), at the end, at the final time, goes to <s>Hari</s>, that is, attains the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — this is the meaning.
He shows the <s>tattva-nyāsa</s> (installation of principles) — with 'ity acyutī' etc.
Thus, having made one's body [identical with] <s>Acyuti</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), one should perform the <s>tattva-nyāsa</s> (installation of principles),
With the letters preceded by ma and ending in ka, accompanied by salutation;

children.text: bhūyaḥ parāya ca tad-āhvayam ātmane ca
children.translated_text: Then again, for the Supreme, with the name of that [principle], and for the self,
Ending with salutation — one should extract the <s>tattva-mantra</s>s (principle-mantras) in order.

children.text:
iti pūrvokta-prakāreṇa acyutīkṛta-tanuḥ sampādita-viṣṇu-śarīraḥ tattva-
nyāsaṃ vakṣyamāṇa-prakāraṃ vidadhīta kuryāt | prakāraṃ darśayati-maḥ pūrvo yasya sa ma-pūrvaḥ | kaḥ paro yasya sa ka-paraḥ | naty-upetaṃ namaḥ-śabda-sahitam | tathā ca ma-kārādi-vyutkrameṇa ka-kāra-paryantam ekaikākṣaraṃ namaḥ-pada-sahitaṃ kṛtvā bhūyo 'nantaraṃ parāyeti-padaṃ dattvā anantaraṃ tad-āhvayaṃ teṣāṃ tattvānām ādvayaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ nāma dattvā anantaraṃ ātmane iti padaṃ dattvā anantaraṃ naty-antam namaḥ-padam ante dattvā krameṇa tattva-manūn tattva-mantrān uddharatu || KrdC_1.28 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, having made one's body [identical with] <s>Acyuti</s> — that is, having made the body into <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s form — in the manner described above, one should perform the <s>tattva-nyāsa</s> of the kind to be described. He shows the method: ma-pūrva means that which has ma as the first; ka-para means that which has ka as the last; accompanied by the word namaḥ (salutation). Thus, taking each letter in reverse order from ma-kāra to ka-kāra, combining it with the word namaḥ, then placing the word parāya (for the Supreme), then giving the name of those principles [to be described], then giving the word ātmane (for the self), then placing the word namaḥ at the end — one should extract the <s>tattva-mantra</s>s, the mantra formulas of the principles, in order.

children.text: adhunā tattvānāṃ nāmāni nyāsaṃ sthānaṃ ca darśayati-
children.translated_text: Now he shows the names and installation places of the <s>tattva</s>s (principles) —
In the entire body, having applied the seed-syllable, the <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner of mantras) should install <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) in the center,

children.text: nyasatu matim ahaṅkāraṃ manaś ceti mantrī |
children.translated_text: Then intellect, ego, and mind;
In the face, heart, private parts, and feet — the group of [elements] beginning with sound,
Then the group of qualities, and [the faculties] beginning with hearing, stationed from the agent onwards.

children.text:
sakala-vapuṣi sarvāṅga-vyāpake jīvaṃ prāṇaṃ ca mantre āyojya tena nyasyatu tathā ca maṃ namaḥ parāya jīvātmane namaḥ bhaṃ namaḥ parāya prāṇātmane namaḥ iti dvayaṃ sarva-śarīre vinyasyed ity arthaḥ | iti tattva-padaṃ dattvā maṃ namaḥ parāya jīva-tattvātmane namaḥ iti kecit tat-prayogān kurvanti tan na pramāṇābhāvāt mūrti-pañjara-nyāse 'pi mūrti-pada-prayogāpatteḥ | atra makarādīnāṃ bindu-sāhityaṃ sampradāyāvagataṃ boddhavyam | madhye hṛdaye matim ahaṅkāraṃ manaś ca mantra āyojya tena mantrī nyasyatu tathā baṃ namaḥ parāya mana ātmane namaḥ phaṃ namaḥ parāya ahaṅkārātmane namaḥ paṃ namaḥ parāya mana ātmane namaḥ iti trayaṃ hṛdi vinyasyed ity arthaḥ | atho 'nantaraṃ kamukha-hṛdaya-guhyāṅghriṣu pañcasu
sthāneṣu śabda-pūrvaṃ guṇa-samudāyaṃ śabda-sparśa-rūpa-rasa-gandhātmakaṃ mantre āyojya tena nyasyatu tathā ca naṃ namaḥ parāya rūpātmane namaḥ iti hṛdaye, thaṃ namaḥ parāya rasātmane namaḥ iti guhye, taṃ namaḥ parāya gandhātmane namaḥ pādayor vinyasyed ity arthaḥ | athānantaraṃ śrotra-tvag-dṛk-jihvā-ghrāṇātmakaṃ karṇādi-sthitaṃ karṇa-tvag-dṛk-jihvā-ghrāṇeṣu sthitaṃ yathā syāt tathā nyasyatu tathā ca ṇaṃ namaḥ parāya śrotrātmane namaḥ iti śrotrayoḥ ḍhaṃ namaḥ parāya tvag-ātmane namaḥ iti tvaci, ḍaṃ namaḥ parāya dṛg-ātmane namaḥ iti netrayoḥ | ṭhaṃ namaḥ parāya jihvātmane namaḥ iti jihvāyāṃ | ṭaṃ namaḥ parāya ghrāṇātmane namaḥ iti ghrāṇayor iti vinyasyet || KrdC_1.29 ||
children.translated_text: In the entire body, pervading all limbs, one should install the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) and <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath) by means of mantras. Thus: 'maṃ namaḥ parāya jīvātmane namaḥ' and 'bhaṃ namaḥ parāya prāṇātmane namaḥ' — these two should be installed on the entire body — this is the meaning. Some, adding the word <s>tattva</s>, perform it as 'maṃ namaḥ parāya jīva-tattvātmane namaḥ' — that is not valid due to lack of authority, since it would also entail using the word <s>mūrti</s> in the <s>mūrti-pañjara-nyāsa</s>. Here, the association of <s>bindu</s> (dot) with the ma-kāra and other letters should be understood as known from tradition. In the center, the heart — intellect, ego, and mind — applying these through mantras, the <s>mantrī</s> should install them. Thus: 'baṃ namaḥ parāya mana ātmane namaḥ,' 'phaṃ namaḥ parāya ahaṅkārātmane namaḥ,' 'paṃ namaḥ parāya mana ātmane namaḥ' — these three should be installed in the heart — this is the meaning. Then, in the five places — face, heart, private parts, and feet — the group of sensory qualities consisting of sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, applying through mantras, one should install: 'naṃ namaḥ parāya rūpātmane namaḥ' in the heart, 'thaṃ namaḥ parāya rasātmane namaḥ' in the private parts, 'taṃ namaḥ parāya gandhātmane namaḥ' at the feet — this is the meaning. Then the [faculties] consisting of hearing, skin, sight, tongue, and smell — stationed in the ears, skin, eyes, tongue, and nose — one should install: 'ṇaṃ namaḥ parāya śrotrātmane namaḥ' at the ears, 'ḍhaṃ namaḥ parāya tvag-ātmane namaḥ' at the skin, 'ḍaṃ namaḥ parāya dṛg-ātmane namaḥ' at the eyes, 'ṭhaṃ namaḥ parāya jihvātmane namaḥ' at the tongue, 'ṭaṃ namaḥ parāya ghrāṇātmane namaḥ' at the nostrils — thus one should install.
With 'vāg-ādi' etc. —
The group of faculties beginning with speech, in their own abodes; the group [of elements] beginning with space,

children.text: mūrdhyāsye hṛdaye śire caraṇayor hṛt-puṇḍarīkaṃ hṛdi |
children.translated_text: At the head, mouth, heart, the liṅga (generative organ), and feet; the heart-lotus in the heart;
The orbs of sun, moon, and fire, pervaded by twelve, sixteen, and ten digits respectively,

children.text: vahnīnāṃ ca yatas tu bhūta-vasum uṣyanty ākṣarair mantravit // Krd_1.30 //
children.translated_text: The knower of mantras should install with the letters [corresponding to] the fifth, eighth, seventh, and second [from ya-kāra].

children.text:
vāg-ādīndriya-vargaṃ vāk-pāṇi-pāda-pāyūpasthātmakaṃ karmendriya-pañcakaṃ mantre āyojya ātma-nilayeṣu mukha-pāṇi-pāda-pāyūpastheṣu nyasyatu | tathā ca aṃ namaḥ parāya vāg-ātmane namaḥ iti mukhe | jhaṃ namaḥ parāya pāṇy-ātmane namaḥ iti pāṇyoḥ | jaṃ namaḥ parāya pādātmane namaḥ iti pādayoḥ | chaṃ namaḥ parāya pāyv-ātmane namaḥ iti pāyau | caṃ namaḥ parāya upasthātmane namaḥ ity upasthe vinyasyed ity arthaḥ | ākāśa-pūrvaṃ gaṇam ākāśa-vāyv-agni-jala-pṛthivy-ātmakaṃ mantre āyojya mūrdhany āsye hṛdaye śive liṅge caraṇayor nyasyatu | tathā ca ṅaṃ namaḥ parāya ākāśātmane namaḥ iti śirasi | dhaṃ namaḥ parāya vāyv-ātmane namaḥ iti mukhe | gaṃ namaḥ parāyāgny-ātmane namaḥ iti hṛdaye
| khaṃ namaḥ parāya jalātmane namaḥ iti liṅge | kaṃ namaḥ parāya pṛthivy-ātmane namaḥ iti pādayor nyasyed ity arthaḥ | hṛt-puṇḍarīkam ity āder ayam arthaḥ | hṛt-puṇḍarīkaṃ tathā sūryoḍḍarād-vahnīnāṃ bimbāni sūrya-candrāgnīnāṃ maṇḍalāni trīṇi dviṣaḍ-aṣṭa-yug-daśa-kalā-vyāptāni dvādaśa-ṣoḍaśa-daśa-kalā-yuktāni yatas tu bhūta-vasu-muny-akṣy-akṣaraiḥ yato ya-kārād yo bhūta-varṇaḥ pañcama-varṇaḥ śa-kāraḥ vasu-varṇo 'ṣtamārṇo ha-kāraḥ muni-varṇaḥ saptamaḥ sa-kāraḥ akṣi-varṇo dvitya-varṇo rephaḥ | etaiś ca sahitāni mantre āyojya hṛdi nyasyatu | tathā ca-śaṃ namaḥ parāya hṛt puṇḍarīkātmane namaḥ | haṃ namaḥ parāya dvādaśa-kalā-vyāpta-sūrya-maṇḍalātmane namaḥ
| saṃ namaḥ parāya ṣoḍaśa-kalā-vyāpta-candra-maṇḍalātmane namaḥ | raṃ namaḥ parāya daśa-kalā-vyāpta-vahni-maṇḍalātmane namaḥ iti catuṣṭayaṃ hṛdaye nyasyatu || KrdC_1.30 ||
children.translated_text: The group of faculties beginning with speech — the five action-faculties consisting of speech, hands, feet, excretory organ, and generative organ — applying through mantras, one should install in their own abodes: mouth, hands, feet, excretory organ, and generative organ. Thus: 'aṃ namaḥ parāya vāg-ātmane namaḥ' at the mouth; 'jhaṃ namaḥ parāya pāṇy-ātmane namaḥ' at the hands; 'jaṃ namaḥ parāya pādātmane namaḥ' at the feet; 'chaṃ namaḥ parāya pāyv-ātmane namaḥ' at the excretory organ; 'caṃ namaḥ parāya upasthātmane namaḥ' at the generative organ — this is the meaning. The group beginning with space — consisting of space, wind, fire, water, and earth — applying through mantras, one should install at the head, mouth, heart, the liṅga, and feet. Thus: 'ṅaṃ namaḥ parāya ākāśātmane namaḥ' at the head; 'dhaṃ namaḥ parāya vāyv-ātmane namaḥ' at the mouth; 'gaṃ namaḥ parāyāgny-ātmane namaḥ' at the heart; 'khaṃ namaḥ parāya jalātmane namaḥ' at the liṅga; 'kaṃ namaḥ parāya pṛthivy-ātmane namaḥ' at the feet — this is the meaning. The meaning of 'hṛt-puṇḍarīkam' etc. is as follows: the heart-lotus, and the orbs of sun, moon, and fire — three circles — pervaded by twelve, sixteen, and ten digits respectively. From ya-kāra: the bhūta-letter, the fifth letter, is śa-kāra; the vasu-letter, the eighth, is ha-kāra; the muni-letter, the seventh, is sa-kāra; the akṣi-letter, the second, is ra-kāra. With these conjoined, applying through mantras, one should install in the heart. Thus: 'śaṃ namaḥ parāya hṛt-puṇḍarīkātmane namaḥ'; 'haṃ namaḥ parāya dvādaśa-kalā-vyāpta-sūrya-maṇḍalātmane namaḥ'; 'saṃ namaḥ parāya ṣoḍaśa-kalā-vyāpta-candra-maṇḍalātmane namaḥ'; 'raṃ namaḥ parāya daśa-kalā-vyāpta-vahni-maṇḍalātmane namaḥ' — these four should be installed in the heart.
One desiring strength should install in the places beginning with space, together with the <s>lāva</s> (offerings).
Then <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (the Supreme), the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Cosmic Person), <s>Viśva</s> (the Universal), <s>Nivṛtti</s> (cessation), <s>Sarva</s> (all), <s>Hati</s> (?), and the <s>Upaniṣad</s> —

children.text: athānantaraṃ parameṣṭhi-pumāṃsau viśva-nivṛttī sarva ity upaniṣado rahasyān ṣopara-balārṇair iti ṣa-kāraḥ rephasya upa samīpaṃ tena repha-samīpa-vartinau ya-kāra-la-kārau lakṣyete va-kāro la-kāraś ca etaiḥ salavakair bindu-sahitaiḥ sahitān ākāśādi-sthāne nyasyed ākāśādi nyāsa-sthāneṣu mūrdhnyāsye hṛdaye liṅge caraṇayor nyasyet || KrdC_1.31 ||
children.translated_text: Then next, <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> and <s>Pumāṃs</s> [are associated with] <s>viśva</s> (universe) and <s>nivṛtti</s> (cessation); '<s>sarva</s>' is from the secret <s>Upaniṣad</s>s; by the syllables '<s>ṣopara-balārṇa</s>' — the letter <s>ṣa</s>, and '<s>upa</s>' means 'near' <s>repha</s> (the letter <s>ra</s>), by which the letters <s>ya</s> and <s>la</s> positioned near <s>repha</s> are indicated; <s>va</s> and <s>la</s> — with these [syllables] <s>sa</s>, <s>la</s>, and <s>va</s>, combined with <s>bindu</s> (nasal dot), one should place [them] at the stations beginning with <s>ākāśa</s> (space); at the <s>nyāsa</s> (placement) stations beginning with <s>ākāśa</s> — on the head, mouth, heart, generative organ, and feet, one should place [them]. (KrdC 1.31)
Here he states a particular detail — '<s>Vāsudeva</s>' etc.:

children.text: nārāyaṇaś ca kramaśah parameṣṭhyādibhir yutaḥ // Krd_1.32 //
children.translated_text: And <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, in order, combined with <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> and the others. (Krd 1.32)
<s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, <s>Pradyumna</s>, and <s>Aniruddha</s>,

children.text: kramaśaḥ krameṇa parameṣṭy-ādibhiḥ sahitā vāsudevādayo nyasnīyā tathā ca ṣaṃ namaḥ parāya vāsudevāya parameṣṭhyātmane namaḥ iti śirasi | yaṃ namaḥ parāya saṅkarṣaṇāya puruṣātmane namaḥ iti mukhe, laṃ namaḥ parāya pradyumnāya viśvātmane nama iti hṛdaye | vaṃ namaḥ parāya aniruddhāya nivṛttyātmane nama iti liṅge, laṃ nama iti hṛdaye | vaṃ namaḥ parāya aniruddhāya nivṛty-ātmane nama iti liṅge | laṃ namaḥ parāya nārāyaṇāya sarvātmane nama iti caraṇayoḥ | vinyasyed ity arthaḥ | kecit tu parameṣṭhyāder anantaraṃ vāsudevādeḥ prayogaṃ kurvanti || KrdC_1.32 ||
children.translated_text: 'In order' means sequentially; <s>Vāsudeva</s> and the others should be placed combined with <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> and the others. Thus: '<s>ṣaṃ namaḥ</s> — obeisance to the supreme <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the <s>Parameṣṭhy-ātman</s> (supreme-self)' — on the head; '<s>yaṃ namaḥ</s> — obeisance to the supreme <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, the <s>Puruṣātman</s> (person-self)' — on the mouth; '<s>laṃ namaḥ</s> — obeisance to the supreme <s>Pradyumna</s>, the <s>Viśvātman</s> (universal-self)' — on the heart; '<s>vaṃ namaḥ</s> — obeisance to the supreme <s>Aniruddha</s>, the <s>Nivṛtty-ātman</s> (cessation-self)' — on the generative organ; '<s>laṃ namaḥ</s> — obeisance to the supreme <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the <s>Sarvātman</s> (all-self)' — on the feet. 'One should place' — this is the meaning. Some, however, perform the application of <s>Vāsudeva</s> and the others after <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> and the others. (KrdC 1.32)
Then the <s>kopa-tattva</s> (anger-principle), the two syllables <s>kṣa</s> and <s>ra</s> combined with <s>bindu</s>,
The knower of that should place <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> on all the limbs.
Thus the <s>nyāsa</s> (placement) consisting of <s>tattva</s>s (principles) has been stated in order;
It should be [applied] upon images, <s>viśva-mūrti</s> (universal forms), and the like, establishing one's own [divine] presence. (Krd 1.33)

children.text: tatas tad-anantaraṃ krameṇa gurūpadeśa-krameṇa taj-jñaḥ nṛsiṃha-bīja-jñaḥ kṣarau kṣa-kāra-repha-au-kāra iti milita-svarūpaṃ bindu-yuktaṃ tathā kopa-tattvaṃ nṛsiṃhaṃ ca mantre āyojya sarva-gātreṣu nyasyet | tathā ca-kṣrauṃ namaḥ parāya nṛsiṃhāya kopātmane namaḥ iti sarva-gātreṣu nyasyed ity arthaḥ | tattva-nyāsam upasaṃharati ity ukta-prakāreṇa tattvātmako nyāsaḥ kathito bhavati | kīdṛśaḥ ? viśva-mūrty-ādiṣu sva-sānnidhya-kṛt kṛṣṇa-sānnidhya-kṛt bimbādiṣv iti kecid bimbaṃ pratimā mūrtiḥ śarīram ādi-padena maṇi-mantrādi-sakalasya parigrahaḥ eteṣu hareḥ sānnidhyaṃ karotīty arthaḥ | kvacin martyādiṣv iti pāṭhaḥ || KrdC_1.33 ||
children.translated_text: 'Then' — after that, 'in order' — in the sequence [taught by] the guru's instruction; the knower of the <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> <s>bīja</s> (seed-syllable): <s>kṣa</s>, <s>ra</s>, and <s>au</s> combined together, joined with <s>bindu</s>, and the <s>kopa-tattva</s> (anger-principle), and <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> — having incorporated [these] into the <s>mantra</s>, one should place [it] on all the limbs. Thus: '<s>kṣrauṃ namaḥ</s> — obeisance to the supreme <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, the <s>Kopātman</s> (anger-self)' — one should place [this] on all the limbs — this is the meaning. He concludes the <s>tattva-nyāsa</s> (principle-placement): the <s>nyāsa</s> consisting of <s>tattva</s>s has been described in the stated manner. Of what kind? Establishing one's own presence — that is, establishing the presence of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — in images (<s>viśva-mūrti</s>) and the like; some [say] '<s>bimba</s>' means image, icon, body, and the word '<s>ādi</s>' comprehends all [objects] such as gems, <s>mantra</s>s, etc.; the meaning is that it establishes the proximity of <s>Hari</s> in these. In some [readings] the text reads '<s>martyādiṣu</s>' (in mortals, etc.). (KrdC 1.33)
He states the purpose of this <s>nyāsa</s> — 'thus performed' etc.:
Thus performed, one becomes certainly qualified
For <s>japa</s> (recitation) and other [practices] of all <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> <s>mantra</s>s.
With the <s>mantra</s> of the <s>tattva</s>s of wind-restraint, one should practice;

children.text: tattvam iha japtum asau manucchati // Krd_1.34 //
children.translated_text: This one desires to recite the <s>tattva</s> <s>mantra</s> here. (Krd 1.34)

children.text: tattva-nyāse kṛte dhruvaṃ niścitam adhikṛto bhavati na kevalaṃ gopāla-viṣaya-mantra-kathanād atraiva api tu sakala-vaiṣṇava-mantra-japādiṣv apīty arthaḥ | adhunā prāṇāyāma-prakāram āha-pavana-saṃyamanam iti | asau sādhakaḥ yaṃ manum iha vyavahāra-bhūmau japtum icchati amunā mantreṇa pavana-saṃyamanaṃ prāṇāyāmaṃ caratu kuryād ity arthaḥ || KrdC_1.34 ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>tattva-nyāsa</s> is performed, one becomes certainly — that is, without doubt — qualified; not only from reciting the <s>mantra</s> pertaining to <s>Gopāla</s>, but also for <s>japa</s> and other [practices] of all <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> <s>mantra</s>s — this is the meaning. Now he describes the method of <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control) — '<s>pavana-saṃyamana</s>' (restraint of the wind): the <s>sādhaka</s> (practitioner), whichever <s>mantra</s> he desires to recite here in the practical domain, with that <s>mantra</s> he should perform <s>pavana-saṃyamana</s>, i.e., <s>prāṇāyāma</s> — this is the meaning. (KrdC 1.34)
Here he states another method — 'or alternatively' etc.:
Or alternatively, in all <s>Hari</s>-<s>mantra</s>
<s>japa</s> (recitation) procedures, from the root <s>mantra</s>,
One of pure intellect should practice the restraint of breath
According to the prescribed method, with the count of <s>tattva</s>s. (Krd 1.35)

children.text: mūla-mantrato mūla-mantreṇa | vakṣyamāṇa-daśākṣareṇeti kecit | vastutas tu saptākṣara-gopī-jana-vallabha-mantreṇa tasyaiva mūla-mantratvenābhidhānāt tad-vacanasya prayojanāntarābhāvāt tattva-saṅkhyayāṣṭāviṃśati-vāraṃ caturviṃśati-vāram iti kecit || KrdC_1.35 ||
children.translated_text: 'From the root <s>mantra</s>' — by means of the root <s>mantra</s>. Some [say] by the forthcoming ten-syllable [<s>mantra</s>]. But in reality, by the seven-syllable <s>Gopī-jana-vallabha</s> <s>mantra</s>, since that alone is designated as the root <s>mantra</s>, and because there is no other purpose for that statement. 'With the count of <s>tattva</s>s' — twenty-eight times; some [say] twenty-four times. (KrdC 1.35)
Before the <s>japa</s> and after it also,
A triad is prescribed by the wise.
One who here performs sixteen daily, that sun-like [person],

children.text: paripūyate sa khalu māsato 'ṃ haṃsaḥ // Krd_1.36 //
children.translated_text: He is indeed purified within a month — O <s>Haṃsa</s>! (Krd 1.36)

children.text: purato japādau paścāc ca tat-trayaṃ budhair vihitaṃ prāṇāyāma-trayaṃ, recakādi-trayam iti kecit | etena japāṅgatvāc ca tatrādy-ante 'yaṃ darśitaḥ || KrdC_1.36 ||
children.translated_text: 'Before' — at the beginning of <s>japa</s>, and after — a triad prescribed by the wise means a triad of <s>prāṇāyāma</s>s; some [say] a triad of <s>recaka</s> (exhalation) and so forth. By this, since [<s>prāṇāyāma</s>] is an auxiliary of <s>japa</s>, it is shown at the beginning and end thereof. (KrdC 1.36)

children.text: sanātanaḥ: japasya purata ādau parataḥ ante ca iti prāṇāyāmeṣu kālaḥ | tat trayaṃ prāṇāyāma-trayam iti saṅkhyā | yo jano dinaśaḥ pratyahaṃ ṣoḍaśa-prāṇāyāmān ācaret, sa māsataḥ māsenaikena aṃhasaḥ pāpāt paripūyate śuddho bhavatīti sāmānyataḥ phalam | paraṃ ca sarvaṃ purvaṃ likhitam eva || (hari-bhakti-vilāsa 5.132)
children.translated_text: <s>Sanātana</s> [comments]: 'Before' means at the beginning of <s>japa</s>, 'after' means at the end — this is the time for <s>prāṇāyāma</s>s. 'That triad' — a triad of <s>prāṇāyāma</s>s — this is the count. The person who daily performs sixteen <s>prāṇāyāma</s>s, he is purified from sin (<s>aṃhas</s>) within one month — this is the general result. And everything else has been written previously. (<s>Hari-bhakti-vilāsa</s> 5.132)
Here he states another method — 'or alternatively' etc.:
With the <s>mantra</s> born of the limb [seed-syllable of] desire, the restraint [of breath]
In all <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-<s>mantra</s> recitation practices,
One should practice seven <s>kṛti</s> (twenty-syllable meter) times combined as one,
And reduce [sin] with that which removes all evil and suffering. (Krd 1.37)

children.text: kṛtīti kṛti-cchandaso viṃśaty-akṣaratvāt sahitam ekaṃ yatra tādṛśa-sapta-kṛti-vāram | athavā sahitāni militāni eka sapta-kṛtayaḥ ubhayatrāṣṭāviṃśati-vāram ity arthah | sarveṣu kṛṣṇa-manujāpakarmasu aṅga-janma-manunā kāma-bījena prāṇāyāmam abhyasaṃs tanuyāt | prathamam ekaṃ tataḥ sapta tato viṃśati tato 'bhyāsa-pāṭave 'ṣṭāviṃśati-vāram ity arthaḥ | kaścit tu prathamaṃ sapta tato viṃśatis tata ekaṃ tato 'ṣṭāviṃśati-vāram abhyāsa-krameṇeti tātparyam āha tatra pramāṇaṃ sa eva praṣṭavyaḥ || KrdC_1.37 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Kṛti</s>' — since the <s>kṛti</s> meter has twenty syllables, 'combined as one' means seven <s>kṛti</s>-counts [equaling] that number. Or alternatively, combined [means] together — one and seven <s>kṛti</s>s — in both cases twenty-eight times is the meaning. In all <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-<s>mantra</s> recitation practices, one should practice <s>prāṇāyāma</s> with the <s>aṅga-janma-manu</s>, i.e., the <s>kāma-bīja</s> (desire seed-syllable), and reduce [sins]. First one [time], then seven, then twenty, then with proficiency in practice, twenty-eight times — this is the meaning. Someone, however, [says]: first seven, then twenty, then one, then twenty-eight times in the sequence of practice — that is the purport. For the authority on that, he himself should be questioned. (KrdC 1.37)
He describes the method of <s>prāṇāyāma</s> for a specific <s>mantra</s> — 'twenty-eight' etc.:
Reciting the ten-syllable <s>mantra</s>, which is twenty-eight in count and grants the desired fruit,

children.text: nāyacchet pavanaṃ susaṃyata-matis tv aṣṭau daśārṇena cet |
children.translated_text: One of well-controlled mind should restrain the breath; but if with the eight-syllable [<s>mantra</s>],

children.text: abhyasyann avivāram anyam anubhir varṇānurūpaṃ japan
children.translated_text: Practicing without interruption, reciting another [<s>mantra</s>] proportionate to its syllables,

children.text: kuryād recaka-pūrvakam anipaṇaḥ prāṇa-prayogaṃ naraḥ // Krd_1.38 //
children.translated_text: A person, skilled [in the practice], should perform the application of breath beginning with <s>recaka</s> (exhalation). (Krd 1.38)

children.text:
susaṃśita-matir vimala-buddhiḥ aṣṭāviṃśati-saṃkhyaṃ daśārṇaṃ daśākṣara-mantraṃ japan prāyacchet prāṇāyāmaṃ kuryāt kīdṛśaṃ daśārṇam iṣṭa-phaladaṃ svābhimata-phaladaṃ tatra daśākṣara-mantrasya vāra-catuṣṭayaṃ japena recakam | aṣṭa-vāra-japena pūrakaṃ ṣoḍaśa-vāra-japena kumbhakaṃ kuryād iti guru-sampradāyaḥ | aṣṭādaśārṇe cet prāṇāyāmaḥ kriyata iti śeṣaḥ | tadā ravivāraṃ dvādaśa-vāram abhyasyan prāṇāyāmaṃ kuryād iti guru-sampradāyaḥ | anya-manubhir anya-mantraiś cet prāṇāyāmaḥ kriyate | tadā varṇānurūpaṃ mantra-varṇānāṃ tāratamyena japaṃ kurvan kuryāt | atra svalpākṣarair mantrair bahu-vāram analpākṣarair mantraiḥ svalpa-vāraṃ japed ity arthaḥ | kīdṛśaḥ ? sādhakaḥ
recaka-pūraka-kumbhakākhya-karma-kuśala ity arthaḥ | recakasya tyāgasya pūrvakarmaṇī pūraka-kumbhake tatra nipuṇā iti rudradharaḥ | tac cintyam evam api recake naipuṇyālābhāt prapañca-sārānusāriṇo 'sya granthasya śāradā-granthānuyāyitvāc ca || KrdC_1.38 ||
children.translated_text: 'Of well-controlled mind' — of purified intellect. Reciting the ten-syllable <s>mantra</s> twenty-eight times, one should perform <s>prāṇāyāma</s>. Of what kind is the ten-syllable [<s>mantra</s>]? Granting the desired fruit — one's own wished-for result. There, the <s>guru</s> tradition [prescribes]: four recitations of the ten-syllable <s>mantra</s> for <s>recaka</s> (exhalation), eight recitations for <s>pūraka</s> (inhalation), and sixteen recitations for <s>kumbhaka</s> (retention). If <s>prāṇāyāma</s> is performed with the eighteen-syllable [<s>mantra</s>] — this is to be supplied — then one should practice <s>prāṇāyāma</s> twelve times without interruption on Sunday — this is the <s>guru</s> tradition. If <s>prāṇāyāma</s> is performed with other <s>mantra</s>s, then proportionate to the syllables — one should recite according to the relative [number] of <s>mantra</s>-syllables. The meaning here is: with <s>mantra</s>s of few syllables, one should recite many times; with <s>mantra</s>s of many syllables, fewer times. Of what kind is the practitioner? 'Skilled in the practice called <s>recaka</s> (exhalation), <s>pūraka</s> (inhalation), and <s>kumbhaka</s> (retention)' — this is the meaning. <s>Rudhradhara</s> [says]: '<s>pūraka</s> and <s>kumbhaka</s> are the preliminary practices of <s>recaka</s> (release), and therein one should be skilled.' But that is debatable, since there is no attainment of skill in <s>recaka</s> alone, and this text follows the <s>Prapañcasāra</s>, and also follows the <s>Śāradā</s> text. (KrdC 1.38)
Now he demonstrates the method of <s>prāṇāyāma</s> — 'one should exhale the breath' etc.:
The skilled one should exhale the breath through the right [nostril],
Then fill through the left [nostril], and through the central <s>nāḍī</s> (channel) again
Should retain. The triad beginning with <s>recaka</s> (exhalation) should be
In measures named <s>kalā</s> (sixteen), <s>danta</s> (thirty-two), and <s>vidyā</s> (sixty-four), without lapse. (Krd 1.39)

children.text:
dakṣiṇo vicakṣaṇaḥ puruṣaḥ dakṣayā dakṣiṇa-nāḍyā mārutaṃ vāyuṃ recayet tyajet tathā vāmayā vāma-nāḍyā tyakta-vāyuṃ pūrayed madhyayā suṣumṇayā nāḍyā mārutaṃ vāyuṃ dhārayed ity ukta-prakāreṇa recakādi-trayaṃ recaka-pūraka-kumbhakākhya-tritayam īritaṃ kathitaṃ recakādiṣv avadhi kālam āha-kalād anteti | kalāḥ ṣoḍaśa, dantā dvātriṃśad, vidyāḥ catuḥṣaṣṭhi-rūpā etat-saṅkhyāka-mātrātmakam ity arthaḥ | atra bhairava-tripāṭhino yatra mantra-gaṇanayā prāṇāyāmaḥ | tatra kumbhaka-kāla evoktaḥ śvāsābhyāsa-krameṇa prāṇāyāma-saṅkhyayā mantra-japaḥ kāryo nirgama-prāṇāyāme tu recakādi-gaṇanā kāryety āhuḥ | mātra-śabdena ca vāmāṅguṣṭhe kaniṣṭhādy-aṅgulīnāṃ pratyekaṃ
parva-traya-sparśa-kālaḥ kathyate vāma-hastena vāma-jānu-maṇḍalasya prādakṣiṇyena sparśa-kālaś ca | yad atra rudropādhyāyair uktaṃ yadyapy atra recakaṃ prathamam uktaṃ tad-anantaraṃ pūrakaṃ tathāpi prathamaṃ pūrakam anantaraṃ kumbhakaṃ jñeyaṃ yato gṛhīta-ghṛtasya tyāgo bhavati | yat punar vyatyāsena kathanaṃ tad-gopanāya evaṃ kalā-dantetyādy api vyatyāsena boddhavyam | iḍyotkarṣayed vāyum ity ādi śāradā-darśanāt | evaṃ ca gṛhīta-catur-guṇena dhāraṇaṃ tad-ardhena tyāga ity api darśitaṃ bhavatīti, tan na prapañca-sārānusāriṇo granthasyāsya śāradānuyāyitvāt prapañca-sāre recakāditvasyaivoktatvāt pūrakāditvasyāṣṭāṅgayogāntarbhūta-prāṇāyāma-viṣayatvāt | yad uktaṃ gṛhītasya tyāgo bhavati tatrocyate svābhāvika-vāyu-dhāraṇasyātrāpi
sattvād anyathā śarīra-pātāpatteḥ | yad uktaṃ vyatyāsena gopanārthaṃ kathanam iti tad ayuktam | mantra-bhinnasyānuṣṭhāna-bhāgasya ṛju-mārgeṇaiva vaktuṃ yuktatvāt | yad uktaṃ gṛhīta-caturguṇenaiva dhāraṇaṃ tad-ardhena tyāga iti tad apy ayuktaṃ pramāṇābhāvāt | dakṣiṇāmūrti-saṃhitāyām aṅgulī-niyamo 'pi prāṇāyāme kathito, yathā-
  kaniṣṭhānāmikāṅguṣṭhair yan nāsāpuṭa-dhāraṇam |
  prāṇāyāmaḥ sa vijñeyas tarjanī-madhyame vinā || iti || KrdC_1.39 ||
children.translated_text: 'The skilled one' — the discerning person; through the right <s>nāḍī</s> (channel) one should exhale — release — the breath; then through the left <s>nāḍī</s> one should fill [with] the released breath; through the middle [<s>nāḍī</s>], the <s>suṣumṇā</s> channel, one should retain the breath. In the stated manner, the triad beginning with <s>recaka</s> — the three named <s>recaka</s> (exhalation), <s>pūraka</s> (inhalation), and <s>kumbhaka</s> (retention) — has been described. He states the time-limit for the <s>recaka</s> and the others: '<s>kalā</s>' is sixteen, '<s>danta</s>' is thirty-two, '<s>vidyā</s>' is of the form sixty-four — [each stage] consisting of that number of <s>mātrā</s>s (measures), this is the meaning. Here, the followers of the <s>Bhairava-tripāṭhin</s> [tradition state that] where <s>prāṇāyāma</s> [is measured] by counting <s>mantra</s>s, only the time of <s>kumbhaka</s> (retention) is specified; through the sequence of breath-practice, <s>mantra</s>-recitation should be done with the count of <s>prāṇāyāma</s>; but in the outgoing <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, the counting of <s>recaka</s> and so forth should be done — so they say.
