By the word '<s>mātrā</s>' (measure), the time of touching each of the three joints of the fingers from the little finger onward on the left thumb is described; and also the time of a clockwise circuit touching the left knee-circle with the left hand. What <s>Rudropādhyāya</s> stated here: 'Although here <s>recaka</s> is stated first, followed by <s>pūraka</s>, nevertheless one should understand <s>pūraka</s> first, then <s>kumbhaka</s>, since the release of what has been taken [in] occurs [afterward]. The reversed statement is for the sake of concealment; likewise the <s>kalā-danta</s> etc. should also be understood in reversed [order]' — [this is refuted because] the <s>Śāradā</s> [text] shows '<s>iḍyotkarṣayed vāyum</s>' etc. And [the claim that] retention [should be] four times the intake, and release half of that — is also shown [by him]. But that is not [correct], since this text follows the <s>Prapañcasāra</s> and the <s>Śāradā</s>, and in the <s>Prapañcasāra</s> the order beginning with <s>recaka</s> is stated, while the order beginning with <s>pūraka</s> pertains to <s>prāṇāyāma</s> within <s>Aṣṭāṅga-yoga</s>. As for the statement that release of what is taken occurs — to that it is replied: even here there is natural retention of breath, otherwise bodily death would result. As for the statement that the reversed order is for concealment — that is improper, since the practical portion, distinct from the <s>mantra</s> [portion], should be stated straightforwardly. As for the statement that retention is four times the intake and release is half — that too is improper, for lack of authoritative source. In the <s>Dakṣiṇāmūrti-saṃhitā</s>, the regulation of fingers in <s>prāṇāyāma</s> is also stated, as follows: 'That closing of the nostrils with the little finger, ring finger, and thumb — that should be known as <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, without the index and middle fingers.' (KrdC 1.39)

children.text:
sanātanaḥ: tad eva krama-dīpikoktyā saṃvādayan tatraiva kiṃcid viśeṣaṃ ca darśayati-recayed iti | dakṣayā dakṣiṇa-nāḍyā, dakṣiṇaḥ vidvān janaḥ | madhya-nāḍyā suṣumṇayā dhārayet | evaṃ recaka-pūraka-kumbhakākhyaṃ trayaṃ syāt | recakādiṣu triṣu krameṇāvadhikālam āha-kalāḥ ṣoḍaśa | dantā dvātriṃśat | vidyāś catuḥṣaṣṭhis tat-tat-saṅkhyaka-mātrātmakam ity arthaḥ | mātrā ca-vāmāṅguṣṭhena vāma-kaniṣṭhādy-aṅgulīnāṃ pratyekaṃ parva-traya-samparka-kālaḥ | vāma-hastena vāma-jānu-maṇḍalasya prādakṣiṇyena sparśa-kālo vā | tatrāpy aṅguli-niyamo 'py uktaḥ-
kaniṣṭhānāmikāṅguṣṭhair yan nāsā-puṭa-dhāraṇam |
prāṇāyāmaḥ sa vijñeyas tarjanī-madhyame vinā || iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Sanātana</s>: Harmonizing [this] with the statement of the <s>Kramadīpikā</s>, he shows a particular distinction there — 'one should exhale,' etc. By the right [channel], the right <s>nāḍī</s> (channel), 'right' [means] a learned person. One should retain [breath] through the middle <s>nāḍī</s>, the <s>suṣumṇā</s>. Thus there would be the triad called <s>recaka</s> (exhalation), <s>pūraka</s> (inhalation), and <s>kumbhaka</s> (retention). He states the progressive time-durations in the three [stages] beginning with <s>recaka</s> — sixteen <s>kalā</s>s (units); thirty-two teeth; sixty-four <s>vidyā</s>s (sciences) — meaning [durations] consisting of that many <s>mātrā</s>s (time-units) respectively. And a <s>mātrā</s> is: the time of touching each of the three joints of the fingers beginning with the little finger of the left hand, using the left thumb. Or the time of touching the circumference of the left knee with the left hand in a clockwise [motion]. And regarding the finger-rule, it is also stated: 'The holding of the nostrils with the little finger, ring finger, and thumb — that should be known as <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control), without the index and middle fingers.'

children.text: tatra teṣu prāṇāyāmeṣu purvaṃ recakādiṣu saṅkhyoktā | atra ca prāṇāyāmeṣv iti bhedaḥ || [hari-bhakti-vilāse 5.131]
children.translated_text: There, in those <s>prāṇāyāma</s>s, the number was previously stated for <s>recaka</s> and the rest. And here the distinction is 'in the <s>prāṇāyāma</s>s.' [<s>Hari-bhakti-vilāsa</s> 5.131]

children.text: prakṛtam upasaṃharann ātma-yāgārthaṃ dehe pīṭha-kalpanāṃ darśayati-prāṇāyāmam ity ādinā |
children.translated_text: Summarizing what was commenced, he shows the construction of the <s>pīṭha</s> (ritual seat) upon the body for the purpose of self-worship — beginning with '<s>prāṇāyāma</s>m,' etc.

children.text: prāṇāyāmaṃ vidhāyety atha nija-vapuṣā kalpayed yoga-pīṭham |
children.translated_text: Having performed <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control), one should then construct the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s> (seat of meditation) with one's own body.
One should place the <s>ādhāra-śakti</s> (foundation power), <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), <s>Kamaṭha</s> (tortoise), <s>Kṣamā</s> (earth), and the <s>kṣīra-sindhu</s> (ocean of milk),
And <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> (the White Island), and the great pavilion brilliant with jewels, and the <s>kalpa-vṛkṣa</s> (wish-fulfilling tree),
In the region of the heart — and again upon the two shoulders, two thighs, face, waist, and two flanks. [Krd 1.40]
<s>Dharma</s> (righteousness) and the rest, <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) and the rest, and the four feet and limbs
Upon the heart; then the <s>Śeṣa</s>-<s>mantra</s> (Serpent-mantra),
The sun, moon, and fire, conjoined with the syllables of <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ),
With [their] respective initial syllables — <s>sattva</s> (goodness), <s>rajas</s> (passion), and <s>tamas</s> (darkness). [Krd 1.41]

children.text:
iti pūrvokta-prakāreṇa prāṇāyāmaṃ vidhāya kṛtvā athānantaraṃ nija-vapuṣā nija-śarīreṇa yāga-pīthaṃ pūjā-pīṭhaṃ kalpayet kalpanā-prakāram āha-nyasyed iti | hṛd-deśe hṛdi ādhāra-śakty-ādi-kalpa-vṛkṣāntaṃ nyaset | kamaṭhaḥ kūrmaḥ śeṣo 'nantaḥ kṣīra-sindhuḥ kṣīra-samudraḥ ratnena ujjvalaḥ mahito yaḥ mahā-maṇḍapaḥ ratna-maṇḍapaḥ iti yāvat tathā cādhāra-śaktaye namaḥ prakṛtyai nama iti navakaṃ nyased hṛdīty arthah | bhūyo 'anantaraṃ aṃsa-dvayor udvaya-vadana-kaṭī-pārśva-yugmeṣu dharmādy-adharmādi-pāda-gātra-catuṣṭayaṃ vinyasyet | pāda-gātrayoś catuṣṭayaṃ pāda-gātra-catuṣṭayam ity ubhayatra sambadhyate | pāda-catuṣṭayaṃ gātra-catuṣṭayaṃ dharmādi-dharma-jñāna-vairāgyaiśvarya-rūpa-pāda-catuṣṭayam
| aṃsa-dvayor udvaye ca dharmāya namaḥ dakṣiṇorau, ity evaṃ prādakṣiṇya-krameṇa vinyaset | śāradāyāṃ mukha-pārśva-nābhi-pārśveṣv iti krama-darśanāt | etac ca bhairava-tripāṭhino 'pi saṃmatam | eteṣu yathāśruta-krameṇaiveti vidyādharācāryāḥ | athānantaraṃ śeṣam anantam abjaṃ padmaṃ sūryendu-vahnīn sūrya-somāgni-maṇḍalāni | kīdṛśān ? tān praṇavāṃśa-yuktān praṇavasyoṅkārasyāṃśāḥ | avayavā a-kāro-kāra-ma-kārās tair yuktān sahitān tatrādau sa-bindu-praṇavāṃśādi-sāhityaṃ sampradāyato boddhavyam | svādy-akṣaraiḥ sa-bindu-svīya-svīya-prathamākṣaraiḥ sahitāni sattva-rajas-tamāṃsi tathā ca hṛt-padme anantāya namaḥ, padmāya namaḥ, aṃ dvādaśa-kalā-vyāpta-sūrya-maṇḍalātmane namaḥ, uṃ
ṣoḍaśa-kalā-vyāpta-candra-maṇḍalātmane namaḥ, maṃ daśa-kalā-vyāpta-vahni-maṇḍalātmane namaḥ, saṃ sattvāya namaḥ, raṃ rajase namaḥ, taṃ tamase namaḥ || KrdC_1.40-41 ||
children.translated_text: 'Salutation to the essence of the moon-disc pervaded by sixteen <s>kalā</s>s; maṃ — salutation to the essence of the fire-disc pervaded by ten <s>kalā</s>s; saṃ — salutation to <s>sattva</s>; raṃ — salutation to <s>rajas</s>; taṃ — salutation to <s>tamas</s>.' [Commentary on Krd 1.40-41]

Thus, having performed <s>prāṇāyāma</s> in the manner previously described — then next, one should construct the <s>yāga-pīṭha</s> (worship-seat) with one's own body. He states the method of construction — 'one should place,' etc. In the region of the heart, one should place [everything] from <s>ādhāra-śakti</s> (foundation power) to <s>kalpa-vṛkṣa</s> (wish-fulfilling tree). <s>Kamaṭha</s> is the tortoise; <s>Śeṣa</s> is <s>Ananta</s>; <s>kṣīra-sindhu</s> is the ocean of milk; the great pavilion brilliant with jewels — that is, the jeweled pavilion. And thus, '<s>ādhāra-śaktaye namaḥ</s>, <s>prakṛtyai namaḥ</s>' — the set of nine should be placed in the heart. Then next, upon the two shoulders, two thighs, face, waist, and two flanks, one should place the four feet and limbs of <s>dharma</s> and the rest, <s>adharma</s> and the rest. The compound 'feet-and-limbs-fourfold' applies to both — fourfold feet and fourfold limbs. <s>Dharma</s> and the rest means the fourfold feet in the form of <s>dharma</s>, <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), and <s>aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty). Upon the two shoulders and the two [thighs], '<s>dharmāya namaḥ</s>' on the right thigh — thus one should place in clockwise order. From the <s>Śāradā</s>[-tilaka], the order shown is: on the face, flanks, navel, and sides. And this is also accepted by the <s>Bhairava</s>-Tripāṭhins. The <s>Vidyādharācārya</s>s [hold that one should place] in exactly the order as heard. Then next, <s>Śeṣa</s> (the remainder) [means] <s>Ananta</s>; <s>abja</s> means lotus; the sun, moon, and fire — that is, the discs of the sun, moon, and fire. Of what kind? Conjoined with the parts of <s>Praṇava</s> — the parts, i.e., components of <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ), are the letters a, u, and ma — conjoined with these. Therein, first the association with the <s>Praṇava</s>-components with <s>bindu</s> (dot) is to be understood from the tradition. With [their] respective initial syllables accompanied by <s>bindu</s> — <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>. And thus: in the heart-lotus, '<s>anantāya namaḥ</s>, <s>padmāya namaḥ</s>, aṃ — salutation to the essence of the sun-disc pervaded by twelve <s>kalā</s>s, uṃ —'
The triad beginning with <s>ātman</s> (self), together with the seed[-syllable] of the self, with the particles of space, fire, and <s>māyā</s> (illusion),

children.text: jñānātmānam athāṣṭa-dikṣu parito madhye ca śaktīr nava |
children.translated_text: The <s>jñānātman</s> (knowledge-self), and then the nine <s>śakti</s>s (powers) all around in the eight directions and in the center —

children.text: nyastvā pīṭham anuṃ ca tatra vidhivat tat-karṇikā-madhyagaṃ
children.translated_text: Having placed [these and] the <s>pīṭha</s> (seat), and [the syllable] 'anuṃ' there according to rule, situated in the center of its pericarp,

children.text: nityānanda-citi-prakāśam amṛtaṃ saṃcintayen nāma tat // Krd_1.42 //
children.translated_text: One should meditate upon that name — the immortal [reality], whose nature is eternal bliss and consciousness-radiance. [Krd 1.42]

children.text:
ātmādi-trayam ātmāntarātmā paramātmeti lakṣyam | kīdṛśam ? ādi-bīja-sahitaṃ sa-binduṃ svīya-svīya-prathamākṣara-rūpa-bīja-sahitam iti vidyādharācāryāḥ | ādiḥ praṇavas tat-sahitam iti tripāṭhinaḥ | vyoma ha-kāraḥ | agniḥ rephaḥ | māyā dīrghaḥ īḥ | lavo binduḥ | etaiḥ saha jñānātmānaṃ bhuvaneśvarī-bīja-sahitaṃ hṛt-padme nyased iti pūrveṇānvayaḥ | tathā ca āṃ ātmane namaḥ | aṃ antarātmane namaḥ | paṃ paramātmane namaḥ | hrīṃ jñānātmane namaḥ | iti hṛdi vinyaset | athānantaraṃ aṣṭa-dikṣu paritaḥ prādakṣiṇyena madhye ca karṇikāyāṃ nava-śaktīr vimalotkarṣiṇyādyā nyasyet | padmasya pūrvādi-kesareṣu prādakṣiṇyena vimalāyai namaḥ | utkarṣiṇyai namaḥ | jñānāyai namaḥ | kriyāyai
namaḥ | yogāyai namaḥ | prahvayai namaḥ | satyāyai namaḥ | īśānāyai namaḥ | karṇikāyām anugrahāyai namaḥ | iti nyaset | pīṭha-mantraṃ ca tatra nyasyaḥ | etasyopari vakṣyamāṇaṃ pīṭha-mantraṃ-oṃ namo bhagavate viṣṇave sarva-bhūtātmane vāsudevāya sarvātma-saṃyoga-yaugapadya-pīṭhātmane namaḥ iti mantraṃ nyaset | tad ukta-rūpe pīṭhe vidhivad gurūpadiṣṭa-mārgeṇa tat sarvopaniṣat-prasiddhaṃ dhāma brahma-caitanyaṃ cintayet | kīdṛśam ? tat-karṇikā-madhya-gaṃ hṛt-padma-karṇikā-madhya-stham ity arthaḥ | etad-dhyānopayogi-rūpam uktaṃ svābhāvika-rūpam āha | kīdṛśam ? nityeti avināśi-caitanyaṃ svataḥ-prakāśa-svarūpam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? amṛtaṃ śuddha-svarūpam ity arthaḥ | tatrādhāra-śattyādayaḥ sarve mantrāḥ

children.translated_text: Should be understood from tradition as ending with '<s>namaḥ</s>' in the dative case, beginning with <s>Praṇava</s>. [Commentary on Krd 1.42]

The triad beginning with <s>ātman</s> has as its referent <s>ātman</s> (self), <s>antarātman</s> (inner self), and <s>paramātman</s> (supreme self). Of what kind? Together with the initial seed[-syllable] — accompanied by the seed in the form of [their] respective initial syllables with <s>bindu</s>, according to the <s>Vidyādharācārya</s>s. The initial [syllable] is <s>Praṇava</s> — accompanied by that, according to the Tripāṭhins. <s>Vyoma</s> (space) is the letter 'ha'; <s>agni</s> (fire) is the letter 'ra'; <s>māyā</s> (illusion) is the long vowel 'ī'; <s>lava</s> (particle) is <s>bindu</s> (the dot). Together with these, the <s>jñānātman</s> (knowledge-self) accompanied by the seed-syllable of <s>Bhuvaneśvarī</s> should be placed in the heart-lotus — this connects with the preceding [verse]. And thus: 'āṃ — salutation to <s>ātman</s>; aṃ — salutation to <s>antarātman</s>; paṃ — salutation to <s>paramātman</s>; hrīṃ — salutation to <s>jñānātman</s>' — these should be placed in the heart. Then next, in the eight directions clockwise, and in the center — that is, in the pericarp — the nine <s>śakti</s>s beginning with <s>Vimalā</s> and <s>Utkarṣiṇī</s> should be placed. In the eastern and subsequent petals of the lotus, clockwise: '<s>Vimalāyai namaḥ</s>; <s>Utkarṣiṇyai namaḥ</s>; <s>Jñānāyai namaḥ</s>; <s>Kriyāyai namaḥ</s>; <s>Yogāyai namaḥ</s>; <s>Prahvayai namaḥ</s>; <s>Satyāyai namaḥ</s>; <s>Īśānāyai namaḥ</s>; in the pericarp, <s>Anugrahāyai namaḥ</s>' — thus one should place [them]. And the <s>pīṭha-mantra</s> (seat-mantra) should be placed there. Upon this [seat], the <s>pīṭha-mantra</s> to be stated [later] — 'Oṃ, salutation to the Blessed Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the soul of all beings, to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, to the essence of the seat of the simultaneous union of all selves — namaḥ' — this <s>mantra</s> should be placed. Upon the seat of the described form, according to rule, by the path instructed by the guru, one should meditate upon that renowned abode of all <s>Upaniṣad</s>s — the <s>Brahman</s>-consciousness. Of what kind? Situated in the center of that pericarp — meaning situated in the center of the pericarp of the heart-lotus. He states the nature useful for this meditation, [and then] the essential nature. Of what kind? Eternal — imperishable consciousness, self-luminous in nature. And of what kind? Immortal — meaning of pure essence. Therein, all the <s>mantra</s>s beginning with <s>ādhāra-śakti</s>
He shows the <s>pīṭha-śakti</s>s (seat-powers) —
<s>Vimalā</s>, <s>Utkarṣaṇī</s>, <s>Jñānā</s>, <s>Kriyā</s>, and <s>Yogā</s> — [these are] the <s>śakti</s>s (powers);

children.text: prahvī satyā tatheśānā'nugrā navamī tathā // Krd_1.43 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prahvī</s>, <s>Satyā</s>, and likewise <s>Īśānā</s>, and <s>Anugrā</s> as the ninth. [Krd 1.43]
'<s>Vimalā</s>,' etc. [Commentary on Krd 1.43]
He extracts the <s>pīṭha-mantra</s> (seat-mantra) — beginning with '<s>tāra</s>m' (the syllable Oṃ), etc.

children.text: evaṃ hṛdayaṃ bhagavān viṣṇuḥ sarvānvitaś ca bhūtātmā |
children.translated_text: Thus: 'heart' [means <s>namaḥ</s>], 'the Blessed Lord,' '<s>Viṣṇu</s>,' 'endowed with all,' and 'the soul of beings' —

children.text: ṅe 'ntāḥ sa-vāsudevāḥ sarvātma-yutaṃ ca saṃyogaṃ // Krd_1.44 //
children.translated_text: [All] ending in the dative case, 'together with <s>Vāsudeva</s>,' and '<s>saṃyoga</s>' (union) conjoined with 'all-self.' [Krd 1.44]

children.text: yogāvadhaś ca padmaṃ pīṭhāt ṅe-yuto natiś cānte |
children.translated_text: '<s>Yoga</s>' at its conclusion, and '<s>padma</s>' (lotus), '<s>pīṭha</s>' (seat) followed by the dative ending, and 'salutation' at the end —
The great <s>pīṭha-mantra</s> (seat-mantra) is made manifest; this is sufficient for worship. [Krd 1.45]

children.text: tāraḥ praṇavaḥ | hṛdayaṃ namaḥ | bhagavān iti ca viṣṇur iti ca sarvānvitaḥ sarva-pada-sahitaḥ bhūtātmā sarva-bhūtātmeti | ete trayaḥ sa-vāsudevāḥ vāsudevena saha catvāraḥ pratyekaṃ ṅe 'ntāś caturthy-antāḥ kāryāḥ | sarvātma-yutaś ca saṃyogaḥ sarvātma-saṃyoga iti svarūpaṃ yogāvadhau yoga-śabdānte padma-padmeti svarūpaṃ ṅe-yutaḥ pīṭhātmā caturthy-antaḥ pīṭhātmā etasyānte natir namaḥ-śabdaḥ | upasaṃharati pīṭheti ayaṃ pīṭha-mahā-manur uktaḥ kathitaḥ | kīdṛśaḥ ? saparyāsu pūjāsu paryāptaḥ samarthaḥ || KrdC_1.44-45 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tāra</s> is <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ). 'Heart' [means] <s>namaḥ</s>. 'The Blessed Lord,' '<s>Viṣṇu</s>,' and 'endowed with all' — together with the word 'sarva' (all), 'soul of beings' [means] 'soul of all beings.' These three, 'together with <s>Vāsudeva</s>' — with <s>Vāsudeva</s>, [making] four — each should be made to end in the dative case. 'Union conjoined with all-self' — [this gives] '<s>sarvātma-saṃyoga</s>.' At the conclusion of <s>yoga</s> — at the end of the word <s>yoga</s>, '<s>padma</s>-<s>padma</s>' — [this gives] the form. With the dative ending, '<s>pīṭhātmā</s>' (essence of the seat) ends in the dative. At its end, 'salutation' — the word '<s>namaḥ</s>.' He summarizes — 'the <s>pīṭha</s> [mantra]' — this great <s>pīṭha-mantra</s> has been stated, declared. Of what kind? Sufficient — capable — for worship. [Commentary on Krd 1.44-45]

children.text: sanātanaḥ: tāraḥ praṇavaḥ | tato hṛdayaṃ nama iti padam | tataś ca bhagavān iti viṣṇur iti ca | sarvānvitaḥ sarva-śabda-yukto bhūtātmā sarva-bhūtātmeti | ete trayaḥ sa-vāsudevā vāsudeva-sahitāḥ pratyekaṃ ṅe 'ntāś caturthy-antāḥ | tataś ca sarvātmanā yutaṃ saṃyogaṃ sarvātma-saṃyogam iti napuṃsakatvam ārṣam | tataś ca yogasyāvadhau ante padmaṃ yoga-padmam iti | tad-ante ṅe-yuktaś caturthy-antaḥ pīṭhātmā | tad-ante ca natiḥ namaḥ-śabdaḥ | evaṃ oṃ namo bhagavate viṣṇave sarva-bhūtātmane vāsudevāya sarvātma-saṃyoga-yoga-padma-pīṭhātmane nama iti siddham | tathā ca śāradā-tilake-
children.translated_text: <s>Sanātana</s>: <s>Tāra</s> is <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ). Then 'heart' — the word '<s>namaḥ</s>.' Then 'the Blessed Lord,' and '<s>Viṣṇu</s>.' 'Endowed with all' — conjoined with the word 'sarva,' 'soul of beings' [means] 'soul of all beings.' These three, together with <s>Vāsudeva</s> — accompanied by <s>Vāsudeva</s>, each ending in the dative case. Then 'union conjoined with all-self' — '<s>sarvātma-saṃyoga</s>m'; the neuter gender is Vedic [usage]. Then at the end of <s>yoga</s> — '<s>padma</s>' — [giving] '<s>yoga-padma</s>m.' At its end, with the dative ending — '<s>pīṭhātmā</s>' in the dative. And at its end, 'salutation' — the word '<s>namaḥ</s>.' Thus the complete [mantra] is established: 'Oṃ namo bhagavate viṣṇave sarva-bhūtātmane vāsudevāya sarvātma-saṃyoga-yoga-padma-pīṭhātmane namaḥ.' And thus in the <s>Śāradā-tilaka</s> —

children.text: namo bhagavate brūyād viṣṇave ca padaṃ vadet |
children.translated_text: 'One should say salutation to the Blessed Lord, and then utter the word <s>Viṣṇu</s>;'
'Then [one should say] soul of all beings, to <s>Vāsudeva</s>.'

children.text:
sarvātma-saṃyoga-padād yoga-padma-padaṃ punaḥ |
pīṭhātmane hṛd-anto 'yaṃ mantras tārādir īritaḥ || iti |
children.translated_text: 'From the word union of all selves, again the word yoga-lotus; to the essence of the seat — this <s>mantra</s> ending with heart (<s>namaḥ</s>), beginning with <s>tāra</s> (Oṃ), is declared.'
And in the <s>Sanat-kumāra-kalpa</s> —

children.text: oṃ namaḥ padam ābhāṣya tathā bhagavate-padam |
children.translated_text: 'Having uttered Oṃ namaḥ, then the word to the Blessed Lord;'

children.text: vāsudevāya ity uktvā sarvātmeti padaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: 'Having said to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, then the word <s>sarvātma</s> likewise;'

children.text:
saṃyoga-yogety uktvā ca tathā pīṭhātmane padam |
  vahni-patnī-samāyuktaḥ pīṭha-mantra itīritaḥ || iti || [ha.bha.vi. 5.144-5]
children.translated_text: 'Having said <s>saṃyoga-yoga</s>, then the word to the essence of the seat — conjoined with the consort of fire [i.e., <s>svāhā</s>], this is declared as the <s>pīṭha-mantra</s> (seat-mantra).' [<s>Hari-bhakti-vilāsa</s> 5.144-5]
He shows the purification of the hands — beginning with 'of the [two] hands,' etc.
Having made the pair of hands
Consisting of <s>mantra</s>, by the method to be described,
One should perform everything with the <s>mantra</s>-

children.text: varṇaiḥ paramaṃ jyotir anuttamaṃ hares tat // Krd_1.46 //
children.translated_text: Syllables — that supreme, unsurpassed radiance of <s>Hari</s>. [Krd 1.46]

children.text: karayor yugalam abhidhāsyamāna-mārgāt | vyāpayyety ārabhya vidhiḥ samīritaḥ kare ity antaṃ vakṣyamāṇa-prakāreṇa mantra-varṇair mantrātmakaṃ mantra-svarūpaṃ vidhāya kṛtvā ābhyāṃ karābhyāṃ sakalaṃ pūrvoktaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ ca nyāsa-pūjādikaṃ vidadhīta kuryāt | mantra-varṇa-karaṇa-ka-kāra-śodhane hetum āha-paramam ity ādinā | yasmāt tan-mantra-varṇaṃ hareḥ kṛṣṇasya paramaṃ tejaḥ-svarūpam ity arthaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ ? punaḥ anuttamaṃ nāsty uttamaṃ yasmāt tathety arthaḥ | sakalaṃ vidadhīteti paratrāpi kākākṣi-golaka-nyāyena yojanīyam | tathā ca tad hṛdaya-paṅkaja-sthaṃ harer anuttamaṃ jyotis tejaḥ sakalaṃ vidadhīta ṣaḍ-aṅga-nyāsena sāvayavaṃ kuryād iti laghu-dīpikā-kāraḥ || KrdC_1.46 ||
children.translated_text: The pair of hands — by the method about to be described. The procedure beginning with 'pervading' up to 'in the hand' — by the method to be explained, having made [the hands] consisting of <s>mantra</s>, having the nature of <s>mantra</s>, with the <s>mantra</s>-syllables — with these two hands one should perform everything previously mentioned and to be mentioned — <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement), worship, and the rest. He states the reason for the purification through <s>mantra</s>-syllables — beginning with 'supreme,' etc. Because those <s>mantra</s>-syllables are the supreme radiance of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) in nature. Of what kind? And unsurpassed — meaning that than which there is nothing higher. 'One should perform everything' — this should also be connected with what follows, by the principle of the crow's eye [i.e., double application]. And thus, that unsurpassed radiance of <s>Hari</s>, situated in the heart-lotus, one should perform [the ritual of] everything — one should make [it] possessed of [all] parts through the six-limbed <s>nyāsa</s> (placement), according to the author of the <s>Laghu-dīpikā</s>. [Commentary on Krd 1.46]
Thus [ends] the first <s>paṭala</s> (chapter) in the <s>Kramadīpikā</s> composed by <s>Keśavācārya</s>. ||1||

(2)
Second Chapter

children.text: karayor yugalaṃ vidhāyety ādinā sūcitaṃ mantram uddhartum ādau gopāla-mantreṣv api maulībhūtau daśākṣarāṣṭādaśākṣarau prathamaṃ saṃstauti-vakṣye manum iti |
children.translated_text: In order to extract the <s>mantra</s> indicated by 'having made the pair of hands,' etc., he first praises the ten-syllabled and eighteen-syllabled [<s>mantra</s>s] as the most fundamental among the <s>Gopāla</s>-<s>mantra</s>s — 'I shall declare the <s>manu</s>,' etc.
I shall declare the <s>manu</s> (<s>mantra</s>) whose own nature is celebrated in the three worlds,
Sought by sages who have accumulated inexhaustible merit,
Whose domain is [the Lord] whose banner bears <s>Pakṣīndra</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>, king of birds), bestowing wealth, <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>kāma</s> (desire),
And <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), skilled in action for all undertakings. [Krd 2.1]

children.text: mantraṃ vakṣye uddhariṣyāmi | kīdṛśaṃ ? tribhuvaneti tribhuvane trailokye prathitaḥ khyāto 'nubhāvaḥ prabhāvo yasya tathā tam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? munibhir mumukṣubhir vimṛgyam anveṣaṇīyam | kimbhūtair munibhiḥ ? akṣīṇeti akṣīṇaḥ sa-pūrṇaḥ puṇya-nicayaḥ sukṛta-samūho yeṣāṃ tathā taiḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? pakṣīti pakṣīndro garuḍaḥ sa eva ketuḥ cihnaṃ yasya sa pakṣīndra-ketuḥ śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ tad-viṣayaṃ tat-pratipādakam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? vastv iti vasu dhanaṃ tathā ca puruṣārtha-catuṣṭaya-pradam ity arthaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? sakaleti aśeṣa-vaśya-karma-kuśalam || KrdC_2.1 ||
children.translated_text: I shall declare — that is, extract — the mantra. Of what kind? Whose power and influence is renowned in the three worlds. Again of what kind? Sought by sages who desire liberation. What kind of sages? Those whose accumulated merit — that is, collection of good deeds — is undiminished, complete. Again of what kind? The lord of birds, <s>Garuḍa</s>, is the emblem — thus <s>Pakṣīndra-ketu</s> means <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>; pertaining to him, that is, revealing him. Again of what kind? <s>Vasu</s> means wealth, and thus it bestows the four goals of human life — this is the meaning. Again of what kind? Skilled in all subjugation rites without exception.
Extremely secret, a fire for the heap of cotton that is ignorance,
Bestowing mastery of speech upon people,
Removing sin, the sole cause for warding off
Poison, untimely death, planetary afflictions, diseases, and the like.

children.text: punaḥ kīdṛśam ? atiguhyam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? abodheti abodho mithyā-jñāna-rūpaḥ sa eva tūla-pracayaḥ | tatra jvalano vahnir iva taṃ samastājñāna-nāśakam ity arthaḥ ? punaḥ kīdṛśam ? narāṇāṃ sādhakānāṃ vāg-adhipatya-daṃ vāgaiśvarya-pradam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? duritāpaharaṃ duḥkha-prāpakāniṣṭa-nivārakam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? viṣaṃ sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca apamṛtyur akāla-maraṇaṃ graho nava-graha-janitāniṣṭaṃ rogo vāta-pittādi-janita-śarīra-dausthyam evam ādīnām aśubhādīnāṃ nivāraṇe eko 'dvitīyo hetuḥ kāraṇam || KrdC_2.2 ||
children.translated_text: Again of what kind? Extremely secret. Again of what kind? <s>Abodha</s> means having the nature of false knowledge — that itself is the heap of cotton; a fire in that [heap], burning like a blaze — that is, it destroys all ignorance — this is the meaning. Again of what kind? Bestowing mastery of speech — granting sovereignty over speech — upon practitioners. Again of what kind? Removing sin — averting undesirable things that bring suffering. Again of what kind? Poison, both plant-derived and animal-derived; untimely death, premature dying; planetary affliction, the evil caused by the nine planets; disease, bodily illness caused by wind, bile, etc. — the sole, unequalled cause for the prevention of these and other inauspicious things.
Granting victory in battle, granting fearlessness in the forest,
Granting easy crossing when overwhelmed by water,
Increasing men, horses, chariots, and elephants,
Bestowing sons, cows, land, wealth, and grain.

children.text: punaḥ kīdṛśam ? pradhane saṃgrāme jayadam | vipine 'bhayadaṃ bhaya-haram | salila-plavane toyam antaraṇe sukha-santaraṇa-dātāraṃ saptir hayaḥ tathā ca manuṣyāṇāhayaratha-dvipādīnām upacaya-karaṃ tathā sutādi-pradam || KrdC_2.3 ||
children.translated_text: Again of what kind? Granting victory in battle; granting fearlessness — removing fear — in the forest; in flooding by water, granting easy crossing. <s>Sapti</s> means horse. Thus it increases men, horses, chariots, elephants, and the like; and it bestows sons and the rest.
Producing strength, vigor, valor, an abundance of brilliance,
Voice, complexion, beauty, and good fortune;
A jewel of crores of universes, bestowing the eight primary qualities —
Why say more? — it grants everything.

children.text: balaṃ śarīra-sāmarthyaṃ vīryaṃ śukraṃ prabhāvo vā, śauryaṃ parābhibhāvakaṃ tejaḥ, eteṣāṃ nicayaḥ samūhaḥ | pratibhā buddhiḥ sphūrti-rūpā svaro dhvaniḥ | varṇo gauratvādiḥ | kāntir dīptiḥ pratibhā-svara-varṇa-kāntir ity ekapadaṃ tathā ca pratibhā-svara-varṇa-kāntir dedīpyamāna-varṇa-śobheti kaścit subhagatvaṃ samasta-lokādarakatvam eteṣāṃ kartāraṃ dātāram ity arthaḥ | punaḥ kṣubhitā samohitāṇḍa-koṭir brahmāṇḍa-koṭir yena tathā taṃ saṃsāra-mohakam ity arthaḥ | punaḥ aṇimādi-guṇāṣṭaka-dam aṇima-laghima-garima-mahimeśitva-vaśitva-prākāmya-prāpty-ākhya-guṇāṣṭaka-pradam ity arthaḥ | punaḥ kiṃ bahunā, atra jagati akhiladaṃ samastābhīṣṭa-pradam ity arthaḥ || KrdC_2.4 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bala</s> is bodily capacity; <s>vīrya</s> is seminal potency or might; <s>śaurya</s> is the overpowering splendor; their <s>nicaya</s> is the aggregate. <s>Pratibhā</s> is intelligence in the form of spontaneous insight; <s>svara</s> is voice; <s>varṇa</s> is fairness of complexion and the like; <s>kānti</s> is radiance. According to some, <s>pratibhā-svara-varṇa-kānti</s> is a single compound meaning 'the beauty of a brilliantly radiant complexion.' <s>Subhagatva</s> is being revered by all people — it produces and bestows these. Again: by whom crores of universes are agitated and deluded — that is, it deludes worldly existence — this is the meaning. Again: bestowing the eight qualities beginning with <s>aṇimā</s> — the eight qualities called <s>aṇimā</s> (minuteness), <s>laghimā</s> (lightness), <s>garimā</s> (heaviness), <s>mahimā</s> (magnitude), <s>īśitva</s> (lordship), <s>vaśitva</s> (control), <s>prākāmya</s> (irresistible will), and <s>prāpti</s> (attainment) — this is the meaning. Again: why say more? — in this world it grants everything, all that is desired — this is the meaning.
Now he extracts the ten-syllable <s>mantra-rāja</s> (king of mantras) — beginning with 'śārṅgī' etc.
The bearer of <s>Śārṅga</s> (the bow) [= ga], with the upper tooth [= o]; the hero with the left eye [= ī] joined — the second syllable;

children.text: śūlī saurir bālo balānuja-dvayam athākṣara-catuṣṭayam // Krd_2.5 //
children.translated_text: The bearer of the trident [= ja], the son of <s>Sūrya</s> [= ba], the child [= ba], and the pair of the younger brother of <s>Bala</s> [= lla] — thus the four syllables.
The fourth of the hero [= ?], with the face, reversed — the eighth is the friend of fire [= ya];

children.text: tad-dayitākṣara-yugmaṃ tad-uparigas tv evam uddharen mantram // Krd_2.6 //
children.translated_text: The pair of syllables of his beloved — placed above that; thus one should extract the mantra.

children.text: śārṅgī ga-kāraḥ kīdṛśo 'yaṃ sottaradanta uttara-danta-paṅktau nyasyamānaḥ uttara-danta o-kāras tena sahita etena prathamākṣaram uddhṛtaḥ | śūraḥ pa-kāraḥ | kīdṛśo 'yaṃ vāmākṣi-yuk vāmākṣi caturtha-svaraḥ tena sahita etena dvitīyākṣaram uddhṛtam akṣara-catuṣkaṃ krameṇa punaḥ kathyate śūlī ja-kāraḥ bālo ba-kāraḥ balānuja-dvayaṃ saṃyukta-la-kāra-dvayaṃ lla iti svarūpam ity akṣara-catuṣkam uddhṛtam śūra-turīyaḥ śūrasya pa-kārasya caturthaḥ | kīdṛśo 'yaṃ sānana-vṛttaḥ ānana-vṛttenākāreṇa saha vartate iti sānana-vṛttaḥ ayaṃ ca saptamaḥ syād mantrasya saptamo bhavatīty arthaḥ | aṣṭamo 'gni-sakho vāyuḥ ya-kāra iti yāvat | tathā ca mantrasyāṣṭamo varṇo ya iti boddhavyaḥ | tad-uparigaṃ
pūrvokta-varṇānantary-viśiṣṭaṃ tad-dayitākṣara-yugalaṃ svāheti svarūpam ity akṣara-dvayam uddhṛtam || KrdC_2.5-6 ||
children.translated_text: Distinguished by being immediately after the previously stated letters — the pair of syllables of his beloved, whose form is 'svāhā' — thus the two syllables are extracted.

The bearer of <s>Śārṅga</s> is ga-kāra. Of what kind? With the upper tooth — placed in the upper row of teeth — the upper tooth is o-kāra; combined with that, the first syllable is extracted [= go]. The hero is pa-kāra. Of what kind? Joined with the left eye — the left eye is the fourth vowel [= ī]; combined with that, the second syllable is extracted [= pī]. The four syllables are stated in order: the bearer of the trident is ja-kāra; the child is ba-kāra; the pair of the younger brother of <s>Bala</s> is the conjunct double la-kāra, whose form is 'lla' — thus the four syllables are extracted. The fourth of the hero — the fourth of pa-kāra [the hero]. Of what kind? With the face reversed — existing with ā-kāra as the mouth-form — and this would be the seventh [syllable] of the mantra — this is the meaning. The eighth is the friend of fire, <s>Vāyu</s>, which is ya-kāra. Thus the eighth letter of the mantra should be understood as ya. The pair of syllables of his beloved, placed above —
With 'prakāśita' etc. —

children.text: prakāśito daśākṣaro manus tv ayaṃ madhu-dviṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: This ten-syllable mantra of the enemy of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>/<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) has been revealed;
It especially increases devotion to the pair of lotus feet [of the Lord].

children.text: madhudviṣaḥ śrī-gopāla-kasyāyaṃ daśākṣaro mantra uddhṛtaḥ | kīdṛśo viśeṣato viśeṣeṇa padāravinda-yugma-bhakti-vardhanaḥ śrī-gopāla-kṛṣṇa-caraṇābja-yugale yā bhaktir ārādhyatvena jñānaṃ tat samṛddhikāraka ity arthaḥ || KrdC_2.7 ||
children.translated_text: This ten-syllable mantra of <s>Śrī Gopāla</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>, has been extracted. Of what kind? Especially — it particularly increases devotion to the pair of lotus feet of <s>Śrī Gopāla Kṛṣṇa</s>; that is, it enriches the knowledge that recognizes him as the object of worship — this is the meaning.
He shows the <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer) etc. of the mantra — with '<s>Nārada</s>' etc.
<s>Nārada</s> is declared as the sage of this [mantra];
The meter is said by the sages to be <s>Virāṭ</s>;
The deity is the auspiciousness of all worlds,
The son of <s>Nanda Gopa</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), thus declared.

children.text: amuṣya pūrvokta-mantrasya muniḥ ṛṣir nāradaḥ kīrtitaḥ kathitaḥ | ṛṣibhir gautamādibhir virāṭ-chanda uktam | devatā nana-gopa-tanayaḥ śrī-gopāla-kṛṣṇa uktaḥ | kīdṛśaḥ ? sakala-loka-maṅgalaḥ sarva-jana-kalyāṇa-hetuḥ | etena ṛṣy-ādīnāṃ śirasi rasanāyāṃ hṛdi krameṇa nyāsaḥ kārya iti sūcitaṃ prapañca-sāre | tathā vidhānāt prayogaś ca daśākṣara-gopāla-mantrasya nārada-ṛsaye namaḥ śirasi | virāṭ-chandase namo mukhe | śrī-gopāla-kṛṣṇāya devatāyai namaḥ hṛdi ity evambhūtaḥ | asya mantrasya nārada-ṛṣiḥ | evaṃ chando-devatayor api yojyam iti kecit || KrdC_2.8 ||
children.translated_text: The sage (<s>ṛṣi</s>) of the aforementioned mantra is declared to be <s>Nārada</s>. The meter is stated by the sages <s>Gautama</s> and others as <s>Virāṭ</s>. The deity is stated to be the son of <s>Nanda Gopa</s>, <s>Śrī Gopāla Kṛṣṇa</s>. Of what kind? The auspiciousness of all worlds — the cause of welfare for all people. By this it is indicated, as in the <s>Prapañcasāra</s>, that the installation of the <s>ṛṣi</s> etc. should be done in order at the head, tongue, and heart. Thus, according to the prescribed practice for the ten-syllable <s>Gopāla</s> mantra: '<s>Nārada</s>-ṛṣaye namaḥ' at the head; '<s>Virāṭ</s>-chandase namaḥ' at the mouth; '<s>Śrī-Gopāla-Kṛṣṇāya</s> devatāyai namaḥ' at the heart — such is the form. The sage of this mantra is <s>Nārada</s>. Similarly, one should apply [this pattern] for the meter and deity as well — thus say some.
Now he shows the five limbs of this mantra — beginning with 'aṅgāni' etc.
The five limbs [are formed] with the <s>cakra</s>s (disc-weapons), accompanied by the beloved of the fire-god [= svāhā],
Endowed with the face-circle and vi-su [prefixes] of this [mantra];
Together with [the cakra] named <s>Asurāntaka</s> (destroyer of demons), which is employed for the protection of the three worlds,
And here they are declared with case-endings [dative suffixes].
At the heart is the salutation [namaḥ]; at the head is the beloved of the fire-god [svāhā];
With vaṣaṭ at the topknot; huṃ is stationed at the armor;
With phaṭ is the weapon — thus the five limbs are declared,
With the dative case; and if at the eyes, vauṣaṭ is stated.

children.text:
amuṣya iha śāstre aṅgāni pañca kathitāni | kāni tāni ? tatrāha hṛdaye natir iti | hṛdaye natir namaḥ-padaṃ śirasi pāvaka-priyā svāheti sa-vaṣaṭ vaṣaṭ-pada-sahitā śikhety arthaḥ | hum api varmaṇi sthitaṃ varmaṇi kavace hum api padaṃ sthitam ity arthaḥ | sa-phaḍ astraṃ phaṭ-pada-sahitam astram ity arthaḥ | ity anena prakāreṇa sa-caturthi yathā syāt tathaivam aṅga-pañcakam uditaṃ kathitaṃ caturthyā ca hṛdayādīnāṃ yogaḥ kāryaḥ | kaiḥ saha cakraiś cakra-śabdaiḥ | kīdṛśaiḥ ? mukha-vṛtta-visūpapannair mukha-vṛttam ā-kāraḥ vi iti su iti svarūpam etaiḥ pratyekam upapannaiḥ sambaddhaīh trailokya-rakṣaṇa-yujāpi trailokya-rakṣaṇaṃ yunaktīti tad-yug etādṛśena cakreṇa api-śabdāc cakrair iti vibhidyānvayaḥ kāryaḥ | tathā ca cakreṇeti asurāntakākhya-pūrveṇa
cakreṇety arthaḥ | ca samuccaye | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ vibhakti-yuktaiḥ ? caturthī-yuktais tasyā eva prakṛtatvād etasyāpi padasya vibhidyānvayaḥ kāryaḥ dṛśor yadi iti yadi kvacin mantre dṛśor nyāso 'sti tadā tatra vauṣaḍ iti uditaṃ kathitam |
children.translated_text: Of this [mantra], in this treatise, five limbs are declared. What are they? He states: at the heart is the salutation, the word namaḥ; at the head is the beloved of the fire-god, svāhā; with vaṣaṭ — accompanied by the word vaṣaṭ — is the topknot, this is the meaning; huṃ is stationed at the armor, meaning the word huṃ is placed at the kavaca (armor); with phaṭ — accompanied by the word phaṭ — is the weapon (astra), this is the meaning. In this manner, the five limbs are declared with the dative case, and the dative should be connected with hṛdaya (heart) and the others. With what? With the cakra words. Of what kind? Endowed with the face-circle, ā-kāra, and vi and su — connected with each of these respectively. Also with the <s>cakra</s> that is employed for the protection of the three worlds; and by the word 'api,' separately with the <s>cakra</s>s — the syntactic connection should be made with both. Thus the meaning is: with the <s>cakra</s> named <s>Asurāntaka</s> (destroyer of demons). The particle 'ca' indicates conjunction. Again of what kind? With case-endings — with dative, since that is the relevant case; the syntactic connection of this word also should be made separately. 'If at the eyes' — if in some mantra there is installation at the eyes, then there vauṣaṭ is stated.

children.text:
atra jvālā-cakrāyety api yojyam iti laghu-dīpikā-kāraḥ | prayogaś ca-ācakrāya svāhā hṛdayāya namaḥ | vi-cakrāya svāhā śirase svāhā su-cakrāya svāhā śikhāyai vaṣaṭ | trailokya-rakṣaṇa-cakrāya svāhā kavacāya huṃ | jvālā-cakrāya svāhā netra-dvayāya vauṣaṭ asurāntaka-cakrāya svāhā astrāya phaḍ iti aṅgulīṣv aṅga-mantra-nyāse tu tat-tad-aṅga-mantrānte aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ tarjanībhyāṃ svāhā ity ādi yojyam | āgamāntare hrīṃ aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ hrīṃ tarjanībhyāṃ svāhā | tata ity ādi-darśanāt tenāṅguṣṭhādiṣu hṛdayāya namaḥ ity ādi-prayogāś cintyāḥ | asamavetārthakatvād mānābhāvāc ceti kecit | anye tu yathā-śrutāṅga-mantrasyaiva nyāsair aṅgulīṣv atideśān āhur ācyāryāḥ || KrdC_2.9-10
||
children.translated_text: Here, 'jvālā-cakrāya' should also be connected — thus says the author of the <s>Laghudīpikā</s>. The practice is: 'ā-cakrāya svāhā hṛdayāya namaḥ'; 'vi-cakrāya svāhā śirase svāhā'; 'su-cakrāya svāhā śikhāyai vaṣaṭ'; '<s>trailokya-rakṣaṇa-cakrāya</s> svāhā kavacāya huṃ'; '<s>jvālā-cakrāya</s> svāhā netra-dvayāya vauṣaṭ'; '<s>asurāntaka-cakrāya</s> svāhā astrāya phaṭ.' For the installation of the limb-mantras on the fingers, at the end of each respective limb-mantra one should add: 'aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ' (for the thumbs), 'tarjanībhyāṃ svāhā' (for the index fingers), and so on. In another <s>āgama</s> tradition: 'hrīṃ aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ,' 'hrīṃ tarjanībhyāṃ svāhā.' From the occurrence of 'tataḥ' etc. [in that tradition], the practices of 'hṛdayāya namaḥ' etc. at the thumbs and other [fingers] should be considered. [This approach is] without defect due to having non-inherent meaning and lacking authority — thus say some. Others, however — the teachers — say that the limb-mantra as literally heard should be extended to the fingers by analogy.
He shows the ten limbs —
With the ten mantra-letters, accompanied by crescent-marks [<s>anusvāra</s>],
The group of ten limbs is declared, ending with namaḥ;
Heart, head, then topknot and armor-weapon,
Together with the two sides, hips, back, and crown.

children.text: mantrārṇair mantrākṣarir namo 'ntaṃ yathā syād evam aṅgānāṃ daśakam udīritaṃ kathitaṃ kīdṛśair upeta-candra-khaṇḍaiḥ sānusvāraiḥ sthānāny āhuḥ-hṛdayaṃ śīrṣaṃ mastakaṃ tat-paścāt śikhā prasiddhā tanutraṃ kavacaṃ astraṃ daśa-dikṣu pārśva-yugala-kaṭi-pṛṣṭha-mūrdha-sahitaṃ pūrvoktam ity arthaḥ | kaṭir nābher adha iti tripāṭhinaḥ | prayogas tu goṃ hṛdayāya nama iti pīṃ śirase svāhā ity ādi || KrdC_2.11 ||
children.translated_text: With the mantra-letters — ending with namaḥ — the group of ten limbs is declared. Of what kind? Accompanied by crescent-marks, that is, with <s>anusvāra</s>. The places are stated: heart, head (crown of the head), then after that the topknot (well-known), the body-armor (kavaca), the weapon in the ten directions, together with the pair of sides, hips, back, and crown — [these are] as previously stated, this is the meaning. The hip is below the navel — thus says <s>Tripāṭhin</s>. The practice is: 'goṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ,' 'pīṃ śirase svāhā,' and so on.

children.text: adhunāsya mantrasya bīja-śakty-adhiṣṭhātṛ-devatā-prakṛti-viniyogān darśayati vakṣya ity ādinā |
children.translated_text: Now he shows the <s>bīja</s> (seed), <s>śakti</s> (power), presiding deity, <s>prakṛti</s> (source), and application of this mantra — beginning with 'vakṣye' etc.
I shall declare the <s>bīja</s> (seed) and <s>śakti</s> (power) of this mantra —
The wielder of the discus, the lord of <s>Śacī</s> (<s>Indra</s>), illuminating the left eye;
Together with <s>Pradyumna</s> — this <s>bīja</s> (seed-syllable) is established;
The <s>mantra-Pradyumna</s>, this enchanter of the world.

children.text: asya mantrasya pūrvoktasya sa-śakti-śakty-ādi-sahitaṃ bījaṃ vakṣye bījam āha-cakrīti ka-kāraḥ | kīdṛśo 'yaṃ śakrī śakro la-kāraḥ tad-yuktaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? vāma-netra-pradīptaḥ vāma-netraṃ caturtha-svaras tat-sahitaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? sa-pradyumnaḥ pradyumno binduḥ tat-sahitaḥ tathā cakrīm iti siddhaṃ bhavati | etad asya bījaṃ pradiṣṭaṃ kathitam | ayam eva prādyumno mantra ity arthaḥ | kimbhūtaḥ ? jagan-mohano viśva-vaśya-karaḥ || KrdC_2.12 ||
children.translated_text: Of this previously stated mantra, I shall declare the <s>bīja</s> (seed-syllable) together with <s>śakti</s> (power) and the rest. He states the <s>bīja</s>: '<s>cakrī</s>' — this is ka-kāra. Of what kind? '<s>śakrī</s>' — <s>śakra</s> is la-kāra; conjoined with that. Again of what kind? 'Illuminated by the left eye' — the left eye is the fourth vowel [ī]; accompanied by that. Again of what kind? 'With <s>Pradyumna</s>' — <s>Pradyumna</s> is the <s>bindu</s> (dot); accompanied by that. Thus '<s>klīṃ</s>' is established. This <s>bīja</s> of this [mantra] has been declared. This is indeed the <s>Prādyumna</s> mantra — this is the meaning. Of what kind? World-enchanting, causing the universe to be subject [to the practitioner]. // KrdC 2.12 //
He states the <s>śakti</s> (power) — with '<s>haṃsa</s>' etc.:
<s>Haṃsa</s> [is] <s>meda</s> (fat), conjoined with the curved and round [letters],
<s>Pautrī</s> (granddaughter), endowed with the eye-letter and the rest — this is the pair of letters;
The <s>śakti</s> (power) is declared by all hosts of gods,
[she is] the beloved of the praiseworthy <s>Agni</s> (fire), the granter of desires. // Krd 2.13 //

children.text: haṃsaḥ sa-kāraḥ | kimbhūtaḥ ? medo va-kāraḥ vaktra-vṛttam ā-kāraḥ ābhyām upetaḥ sambaddhaḥ tathā pautrī ha-kāraḥ | kimbhūtaḥ ? netrādir ākāras tenānvitaḥ | tathā ca svāheti siddham asau yugārṇo varṇa-dvayātmikā śaktiḥ proktā tatheyaṃ vahner vallabhā kimbhūtā kāmadā ākāṅkṣita-pradā | kathambhūtasya vahner gīrvāṇa-vṛndair vandyasya sarvadeva-samūhaiḥ pūjyasya || KrdC_2.13 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Haṃsa</s> is sa-kāra. Of what kind? '<s>Meda</s>' is va-kāra; 'curved-round' is ā-kāra; conjoined with these two. And '<s>pautrī</s>' is ha-kāra. Of what kind? 'Eye-initial' — ā-kāra; endowed with that. Thus '<s>svāhā</s>' is established. This pair of letters constitutes the <s>śakti</s>. And she is the beloved of <s>Agni</s> (fire). Of what kind? The granter of desires — the bestower of what is wished for. Of what kind of <s>Agni</s>? One who is worshipped by all hosts of gods, honored by the assemblies of all deities. // KrdC 2.13 //
He states the application — with '<s>viniyoga</s>' etc.:
The application of this mantra is for the four goals of human life (<s>puruṣārtha</s>);

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ prakṛtir ity ukto durgādhiṣṭhātṛ-devatā // Krd_2.14 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is said to be the <s>prakṛti</s> (source); <s>Durgā</s> is the presiding deity. // Krd 2.14 //

children.text: asya mantrasya puruṣārtha-catuṣṭaya-sādhanāya viniyoga ity arthaḥ | prakṛtir mūla-kāraṇaṃ mantrotpādakaḥ mantra-svarūpa ity arthaḥ | adhiṣṭhātṛ-devatām āha-durgādhiṣṭhātṛ-devateti || KrdC_2.14 ||
children.translated_text: The application of this mantra is for the accomplishment of the four goals of human life — this is the meaning. <s>Prakṛti</s> means the root cause, the generator of the mantra, the essential nature of the mantra — this is the meaning. He states the presiding deity: '<s>Durgā</s> is the presiding deity.' // KrdC 2.14 //
He states the meaning of the mantra — with '<s>gopāyati</s>' etc.:

children.text: gopāyeti sakalam idaṃ gopāyati paraṃ pumāṃsam iti gopī |
children.translated_text: '<s>Gopāyati</s>' — she who protects all this, and [she who] conceals the Supreme Person — [such is] '<s>gopī</s>';

children.text: prakṛtes tasyā jātaṃ jana iti nadādikaṃ pṛthivy-antam // Krd_2.15 //
children.translated_text: that which is born from that <s>prakṛti</s> (nature) is '<s>jana</s>' (creation) — [i.e.,] the [evolutes] beginning with <s>nada</s> (primordial vibration) and ending with earth. // Krd 2.15 //

children.text: idaṃ sakalaṃ nāma-rūpābhyāṃ vyākṛtaṃ jagad gopāyati rakṣati tat-kāraṇatvāt svārthe āyaḥ | tathā paraṃ pumāṃsaṃ nitya-śuddha-buddham uktānandādvayātmakaṃ brahma-svarūpaṃ gopāyati gup gopana-kutsanayoḥ ajñātatvena viṣayīkarotīti vyutpattyā mahad-ādi-pṛthivy-antaṃ mahat-tattvādi-pṛthivī-paryantaṃ sakalaṃ kārya-jātaṃ jana ucyate || KrdC_2.15 ||
children.translated_text: She protects — that is, guards — this entire world manifested through name and form, because she is its cause; the reflexive suffix [in <s>gopāyati</s>] is used in its own sense. And she conceals the Supreme Person — the eternally pure, awakened, blissful, non-dual <s>Brahman</s> in its essential nature — '<s>gopāyati</s>' from the root <s>gup</s> meaning 'to protect' and 'to conceal,' by the etymology 'she makes [Him] an unknown object.' All creation born [from her] — from <s>mahat</s> (the great principle) down to earth — the entire effect-series is called '<s>jana</s>.' // KrdC 2.15 //
From the conjunction of these two — <s>gopī</s> and <s>jana</s> — '<s>vallabha</s>' (beloved lord) [means] one who is the support through pervading;

children.text: vallabha ity upadiṣṭaṃ sāndrānandaṃ nirañjanaṃ jyotiḥ // Krd_2.16 //
children.translated_text: thus it is taught — [he is] the concentrated bliss, the stainless light. // Krd 2.16 //
'<s>Svāhā</s>' means 'I offer myself to that radiance';

children.text: yaḥ kārya-kāraṇeśaḥ paramātmety acyutaikatāsya manoḥ // Krd_2.17 //
children.translated_text: He who is the lord of cause and effect — the Supreme Self; through this mantra, identity with <s>Acyuta</s> (the Imperishable) [is attained]. // Krd 2.17 //

children.text: anayoḥ gopī-janayor avidyā tat-kāryayoḥ samīraṇād antaryāmitvena svasya kārye preraṇād niyamanādi iti yāvad āśrayatvato adhiṣṭhātṛtvena vyāptyā vyāpakatvena vallabhaḥ svāmīty upadiṣṭaṃ kathitam | paraṃ jyotir brahma-caitanyam | kīdṛśaṃ jyotiḥ ? sāndrānanda-niratiśayānandaika-svarūpam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? nirañjanaṃ māyā-kāluṣya-rahitaṃ svāheti tasmai sva-tejase sva-prakāśa-cid-rūpāya paramātmane svātmānaṃ jīvaika-svarūpaṃ gamayāmi samarpayāmi tad-ātmakatāṃ prāpayāmīti svāhā-śabdārthaḥ | prathama iti-śabdaḥ svāhā-śabdopasthāpakaḥ | dvitīyas tu prakāra-pradarśakaḥ | tasmai kasmai tatrāha-ya iti | yaḥ kārya-kāraṇayor jana-prakṛtyor īśaḥ svāmī adhiṣṭhātā tathā paramātmā nirupādhi-caitanyatvāc cety

children.translated_text: by this manner, for this worshipper, identity with <s>Acyuta</s> — non-difference with <s>Acyuta</s> — arises. // KrdC 2.16-17 //

Of these two — <s>gopī</s> and <s>jana</s> — that is, of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and its effects — 'from conjunction' means by virtue of His being the inner controller, through impelling His own effects, through regulation and the like; 'as the support' means by being the substratum; 'through pervading' means by being all-pervasive — '<s>vallabha</s>' means the master — thus it is taught, declared. The supreme light, the consciousness of <s>Brahman</s>. Of what kind? Of the nature of concentrated, unsurpassed bliss. Again of what kind? Stainless — free from the impurity of <s>māyā</s> (illusion). '<s>Svāhā</s>' means 'to that, to one's own radiance, to the self-luminous consciousness-formed Supreme Self, I offer my own self — I surrender the individual soul's essential nature — I bring about identity with That' — this is the meaning of the word '<s>svāhā</s>.' The first word 'iti' introduces the word '<s>svāhā</s>.' The second shows the manner. 'To that one' — to whom? He answers with 'yaḥ': He who is the lord, the master, the ruler of cause and effect — of <s>jana</s> and <s>prakṛti</s> — and who is the Supreme Self, because He is unconditioned consciousness —
He states the meaning in another way — with 'athavā':
Or, by the word '<s>gopījana</s>' is meant the totality of the world-protecting powers;

children.text: tasya svānanyasya svāmī vallabha iti ha nirdiṣṭaḥ // Krd_2.18 //
children.translated_text: of that [totality], the master who is non-different from his own [powers] is called '<s>vallabha</s>' — thus it is clearly stated. // Krd 2.18 //

children.text: athavā gopījana iti śabdena sakala-viśva-rakṣaṇa-śakti-samudāyaḥ kathyate | tatra gopī-padena śaktir ucyate | jana-padena tasyāḥ samūhaḥ | tasya śakti-samūhasya svānanyasya svābhinnasya śakti-śaktimator abheda-vivakṣayā svāmī niyantā āśrayo vallabha iti hasya sphuṭaṃ nirdiṣṭa udita ity arthaḥ | svāhā-śabdārthas tu pūrvokta eva boddhavyaḥ | laghu-dīpikā-kāras tu-avana-śakti-samudāyaḥ avanaṃ sthitiḥ tatra kāraṇa-bhūtānāṃ śaktīnāṃ samudāyaḥ samūhaḥ jagat-pāliny-ādi-gaṇaḥ | uktaṃ ca mahadbhiḥ jagat-pālinīty ādyāḥ proktās tāḥ sthitaye kalā iti tasya svāmī nāyaka ity arthaḥ || KrdC_2.18 ||
children.translated_text: Or, by the word '<s>gopījana</s>' is denoted the totality of powers for protecting the entire universe. There, by the word '<s>gopī</s>' is meant <s>śakti</s> (power); by the word '<s>jana</s>,' the collectivity thereof. Of that collectivity of powers, '<s>vallabha</s>' means the controller, the support, who is non-different from his own [powers] — with the intention of expressing non-difference between <s>śakti</s> (power) and <s>śaktimān</s> (the possessor of power) — clearly stated, declared — this is the meaning. The meaning of '<s>svāhā</s>' should be understood as stated before. The author of the <s>Laghudīpikā</s> however [explains]: 'the totality of protective powers' — <s>avana</s> means sustenance; the collectivity of powers that are its cause — the group beginning with '<s>Jagatpālinī</s>' (protectress of the world). As the great ones have said: 'Those called <s>Jagatpālinī</s> etc. are the <s>kalā</s>s (digits) declared for sustenance.' Of that [collectivity], '<s>svāmī</s>' means the lord — this is the meaning. // KrdC 2.18 //
He states the meaning in yet another way — with 'athavā':

children.text: athavā vraja-yuvatīnāṃ dayitāya juhomi māṃ madīyam
apīty arpayet samastaṃ brahmaṇi sugaṇe samasta-sampattyai // Krd_2.19 //
children.translated_text: — one should surrender everything to <s>Brahman</s> endowed with qualities, for the attainment of all prosperity. // Krd 2.19 //
Or, to the beloved of the <s>Vraja</s> maidens, I offer myself and all that is mine

children.text: gopī-jano gopāṅganā-janas tasya vallabho niratiśaya-prema-viṣayaḥ tasmai vraja-yuvatīnāṃ gopa-ramaṇīnāṃ dayitāya hṛdayānanda-dāyine svāhā juhomi | kiṃ māṃ svātmānaṃ madīyam api ātmīya-suhṛd-ādikam api ity anena prakāreṇa sa-guṇe brahmaṇi saṃsāra-pravartake parameśvareśvare sarvaṃ samarpayet | kim artham ? samasta-sampattyai sarvaiśvaryāya || KrdC_2.19 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Gopī-jana</s>' means the people who are cowherd women; their '<s>vallabha</s>' is the object of their unsurpassed love — to that beloved of the <s>Vraja</s> maidens, the cowherd women, the bestower of delight to the heart — '<s>svāhā</s>,' I offer. What? Myself, my own self, and also all that is mine — my friends and the like. By this manner, one should surrender everything to <s>Brahman</s> endowed with qualities — to the Supreme Lord who sets <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of existence) in motion. For what purpose? For the attainment of all prosperity — for complete sovereignty. // KrdC 2.19 //

children.text: aṣṭādaśākṣara-mantroddhārāya tad-antarbhūtau kṛṣṇa-govinda-śabdau prathamato vivicya darśayati-kṛṣ-śabda iti |
children.translated_text: For the extraction of the eighteen-syllable mantra, he first separately shows the two words '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' and '<s>Govinda</s>' contained within it — with '<s>kṛṣ</s>-śabda' etc.:
The word '<s>kṛṣ</s>' denotes existence (<s>sattā</s>),
and '<s>ṇa</s>' is of the nature of bliss (<s>ānanda</s>); therefore [the name] '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' [means existence-bliss];
also because of drawing away (<s>karṣaṇa</s>) the sins of devotees,
and because his mantra-formed body is of that color [dark]. // Krd 2.20 //
Because the word '<s>go</s>' denotes knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>),
[He who] is attained by that [knowledge] is '<s>Govinda</s>';
'He knows' — that is, [He who knows] the aggregate of words — [is] '<s>Govinda</s>';
also from the investigation of '<s>go</s>' (the senses/cattle). // Krd 2.21 //

children.text:
kṛṣ-śabdaḥ sattārthaḥ | tatra śaktaḥ | kṛṣ sattāyām ity atra kvib-antaḥ sattā-vācaka iti kāścit | kṛṭ ṇaś ca ṇa-kāraś ca ānandātmaka ānanda-vācī | nanda ānanda iti dhātor eka-deśa-grahaṇād iti kaścit | tato dvandve kṛte 'trādarśaṃ ādyaci-kṛte ca kṛṣṇaḥ sad-ānanda ity arthaḥ | prakārāntareṇa kṛṣṇa-śabdaṃ vyutpādayati bhakteti bhaktānām agha-karṣaṇāt pāpa-parimārjanāt kṛṣṇa ity arthaḥ | bhaktādi-karṣaṇād iti pāṭhe ādi-śabdenābhakta-grahaṇaṃ bhaktasya karṣaṇaṃ sva-sthāna-nayanam abhaktasya karṣaṇaṃ naraka-nayanam ity arthaḥ | prakārāntareṇa vyutpattim āha-tad-varṇeti | kṛṣṇa-varṇa-śarīratvāt kṛṣṇaḥ mantramaya-śarīrasya vācya-vācakayor abhedena vivakṣayā | go ity ādi | gaur jñānaṃ
go-śabdasya vācakatvāt jñāna-vācakatvāt tena jñānenopalabhyate prāpyate jñāyate iti govindaḥ | vid lābhe ity asya dhātoḥ prakārāntaram āha-vettīti | go-śabdaḥ śabda-vācī | vid jñāne dhātuḥ | gāṃ śabda-rāśiṃ śabda-samudāyaṃ mātṛkāṃ vettīti govindaḥ | prakārāntaram āha-go-vicāraṇād go-śabda-vicāraṇād govindaḥ | athavā gāva indriyāṇi teṣāṃ vicāraṇād viśeṣeṣu prati-niyata-viṣayeṣu pravartanād govindaḥ | athavā gāvaḥ paśu-viśeṣā iti | tathā ca śrutiḥ-paśavo div-pādaś catuṣpādaś ca iti | teṣāṃ viśeṣeṣu puṇya-pāpeṣu cāraṇāt pravartanād govindaḥ | athavā, gāvaḥ paśu-viśeṣāḥ teṣāṃ rakṣanād govindaḥ | api-śabdaś cārthe || KrdC_2.20-21 ||
children.translated_text: The word '<s>kṛṣ</s>' denotes existence; it is capable of [conveying] that [meaning]. '<s>Kṛṣ</s> in the sense of existence' — here, with the <s>kvib</s>-suffix, it denotes existence — thus some [say]. And '<s>ṇa</s>,' ṇa-kāra, is of the nature of bliss, a word denoting bliss — by grasping a portion of the root '<s>nand</s>' meaning 'to rejoice' — thus some [say]. Then, forming a <s>dvandva</s> compound and applying the initial vowel shortening, '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' means 'existence-bliss' — this is the meaning. In another way he etymologizes the word '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' — with '<s>bhakta</s>' etc.: from the drawing away (<s>karṣaṇa</s>) of the sins (<s>agha</s>) of devotees, i.e., from the removal of sins, [He is called] '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.' In the reading '<s>bhaktādi-karṣaṇāt</s>,' the word '<s>ādi</s>' includes non-devotees: the drawing of devotees means bringing them to His own abode; the drawing of non-devotees means consigning them to hell — this is the meaning. In another way he states the etymology — with '<s>tad-varṇa</s>' etc.: because He has a body of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (dark) color, [He is called] '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' — since the denoted and the denoting are treated as non-different for the mantra-formed body. '<s>Go</s>' etc.: '<s>go</s>' means knowledge, because the word '<s>go</s>' denotes knowledge; He who is attained, reached, known by that knowledge is '<s>Govinda</s>' — from the root '<s>vid</s>' meaning 'to obtain.' He states another way — with '<s>vetti</s>' etc.: the word '<s>go</s>' denotes speech; the root '<s>vid</s>' means 'to know'; He who knows <s>gā</s>, the aggregate of words, the collection of speech, the <s>mātṛkā</s> (mother syllabary) — [is] '<s>Govinda</s>.' He states another way: from the investigation of '<s>go</s>' — from the investigation of the word '<s>go</s>' — [He is] '<s>Govinda</s>.' Or, '<s>go</s>' means the senses; from their investigation — from directing them toward their specific, assigned objects — [He is] '<s>Govinda</s>.' Or, '<s>go</s>' means cattle, a specific [type of] animal. As the <s>śruti</s> states: 'animals, both bipeds and quadrupeds.' From directing them toward their specific [paths] of merit and demerit — [He is] '<s>Govinda</s>.' Or, '<s>go</s>' means cattle; from protecting them — [He is] '<s>Govinda</s>.' The word '<s>api</s>' is used in the sense of 'and.' // KrdC 2.20-21 //
Now he extracts the mantra:
These two names [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Govinda</s>], in order, with the fourth case-ending,
placed before the mantra and after the <s>Manmatha-bīja</s> (Kāma seed-syllable);
if [they] were [so placed], [it becomes] the eighteen-syllabled supreme mantra —
this one, more secret than the secret, a wish-fulfilling gem. // Krd 2.22 //

children.text: ete abhikhye nāmanī kṛṣṇa-govindākhye anukrameṇa turya-vibhaktyā pratyekaṃ caturthī-vibhaktyā saha mantrāt pūrvokta-daśākṣara-gopāla-mantrād ādau manmatha-bījāt paścāt kāma-bījānantaram atha ced yadi syātāṃ bhavataḥ tadā eṣo 'ṣṭādaśārṇo mantra-śreṣṭho bhavati | etasya balād eva daśākṣare 'pi kāma-bīja-sāhityaṃ kecid icchanti | kīdṛśaḥ ? guhyād guhyaḥ | guhyād api guhyaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? vāñchitasya cintā-mātreṇābhīṣṭa-prada ity arthaḥ || KrdC_2.22 ||
children.translated_text: These two names — called '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' and '<s>Govinda</s>' — in order, each with the fourth case-ending (dative), placed at the beginning of the previously stated ten-syllable <s>Gopāla</s> mantra, after the <s>Manmatha-bīja</s> (Kāma seed-syllable, <s>klīṃ</s>), if they were [so placed], then this becomes the eighteen-syllabled supreme mantra. By the force of this very [teaching], some desire the accompaniment of the <s>Kāma-bīja</s> in the ten-syllable [mantra] as well. Of what kind? More secret than the secret — secret even beyond what is [already] secret. Again of what kind? A wish-fulfilling gem that grants the desired merely by thinking of it — this is the meaning. // KrdC 2.22 //
He also states the <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer) and the rest — with 'pūrva' etc.:

children.text: pūrva-pradiṣṭe muni-devate 'sya chandas tu gāyatram uśanti santaḥ |
children.translated_text: The seer and deity of this [mantra] are the ones previously stated; the meter, the wise declare, is <s>Gāyatrī</s>;

children.text: aṅgāni mantrārṇa-catuṣkair varmāvasānāni yugārṇam astram // Krd_2.23 //
children.translated_text: the limbs (<s>aṅgas</s>) are [formed] by groups of four mantra-letters ending with the armor (<s>varma</s>); the weapon (<s>astra</s>) is a pair of letters. // Krd 2.23 //

children.text: asya mantrasya pūrva-pradiṣṭe prathama-mantra-sambandhitayā kathite muni-devate boddhavye | punaḥ santo gāyatra-chanda uśanti vadanti | aṅgānīti mantrārṇa-catuś catuṣkair mantra-sambandhi-varṇānāṃ caturbhiś caturbhir akṣaraiḥ kṛtvā ṣoḍaśākṣarair varmāvasānāni kavacāntāni catvāry aṅgāni bhavanti | avaśiṣṭaṃ yugārṇam varṇa-dvayam astrākhyam aṅgaṃ bhavati | prayogaś ca-klīṃ kṛṣṇāya hṛdayāya namaḥ govindāya śirase svāhā, gopī-jana-śikhāyai vaṣaṭ, vallabhāya kavacāya huṃ, svāhā astrāya phaṭ || KrdC_2.23 ||
children.translated_text: The seer and deity of this mantra should be understood as those declared in connection with the first mantra. Furthermore, the wise declare the meter to be <s>Gāyatrī</s>. As for the limbs: with groups of four, i.e., four letters each belonging to the mantra, [forming] sixteen letters in total, the four limbs ending with the armor (<s>kavaca</s>) are formed. The remaining pair of letters constitutes the limb called the weapon (<s>astra</s>). And the application is: '<s>klīṃ kṛṣṇāya</s>' for the heart with <s>namaḥ</s>; '<s>govindāya</s>' for the head with <s>svāhā</s>; '<s>gopī-jana</s>' for the topknot with <s>vaṣaṭ</s>; '<s>vallabhāya</s>' for the armor with <s>huṃ</s>; '<s>svāhā</s>' for the weapon with <s>phaṭ</s>. // KrdC 2.23 //
He states the seed-syllable etc. — with '<s>bīja</s>' etc.:

children.text: bījaṃ śaktiḥ prakṛtir viniyogaś cāpi pūrvavad amuṣya |
children.translated_text: The <s>bīja</s> (seed), <s>śakti</s> (power), <s>prakṛti</s> (source), and application of this [mantra] are the same as before;

children.text: pūrvatarasya manorathaṃ kathayāmi nyāsam akhila-siddhi-karam // Krd_2.24 //
children.translated_text: I shall now declare the <s>nyāsa</s> (installation) of the earlier [ten-syllable mantra], which grants all <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural attainments). // Krd 2.24 //

children.text: amuṣyāsya mantrasya bījaṃ śaktiḥ prakṛtir viniyogaḥ pūrva-mantre yāni bījādīni kathitāni tāny atrāpi jñātavyānīty arthaḥ | pūrvatarasyeti athānantaraṃ pūrvatarasya manor daśākṣara-gopāla-mantrasyākhila-siddhi-karaṃ samasta-siddhi-dāyakaṃ nyāsaṃ kathayāmīti pratijñā || KrdC_2.24 ||
children.translated_text: Of this mantra, the <s>bīja</s>, <s>śakti</s>, <s>prakṛti</s>, and application — the seed-syllable etc. that were stated for the previous mantra — should be understood as applying here as well — this is the meaning. 'Of the earlier' — then next, [he declares] the <s>nyāsa</s> of the earlier mantra, the ten-syllable <s>Gopāla</s> mantra, which grants all <s>siddhis</s>, bestows all supernatural attainments — this is the promise. // KrdC 2.24 //
Now he describes the sequence of <s>nyāsa</s> for the ten-syllable [mantra] — with '<s>vyāpayya</s>' etc.:
Having pervaded both hands with the mantra in its meaning,
internally and externally, on the sides, enclosed by <s>tāra</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>) — [thus should] the wise one [do];
the <s>nyāsa</s> (installation) should be performed with the letters situated between pairs of <s>tāra</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>),
crested with <s>bindu</s> (dots), dear to the heart. // Krd 2.25 //

children.text:
atho 'nantaraṃ budhena paṇḍitena varṇair mūla-mantrākṣarair nyāso vidheyaḥ kāryaḥ | kiṃ kṛtvā ? mūla-mantraṃ hastayor antar madhye tathā hastayor eva bāhye pṛṣṭhe tathā hastayor eva pārśve vyāpayya vyāpakatayā vinyasyety arthaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ mantram ? tāra-ruddhaṃ praṇava-puṭitam | kīdṛśaiḥ varṇaiḥ tāra-yugmāntarasthaiḥ praṇava-dvaya-madhya-gataiḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? bindūttaṃsair binduḥ śiro 'laṅkāro yeṣāṃ te tathā sānusvārair ity arthaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? hārda-hṛdyair hārdena namaḥ-padena hṛdyair manojñaiḥ sahitair ity arthaḥ | prayogaś ca-oṃ goṃ oṃ namaḥ dakṣāṅguṣṭha-parva-traye oṃ pīṃ oṃ namaḥ tarjanyām ity ādi | oṃ llaṃ oṃ namo vāma-kaniṣṭhikāyām ity ādi || KrdC_2.25
||
children.translated_text: Then, next, the learned one should perform <s>nyāsa</s> (installation) with the letters, i.e., the syllables of the <s>mūla-mantra</s> (root mantra). Having done what? Having spread the <s>mūla-mantra</s> inside, i.e., in the middle of the hands, then on the outer back of the hands, then on the sides of the hands — pervading them, i.e., installing by way of pervasion: this is the meaning. What kind of <s>mantra</s>? '<s>Tāra-ruddha</s>' means enclosed in <s>praṇava</s> (the syllable Oṃ). With what kind of letters? '<s>Tāra-yugmāntarastha</s>' means situated between two <s>praṇava</s>s. Again, of what kind? '<s>Bindūttaṃsa</s>' means those having <s>bindu</s> (dot) as their head-ornament, i.e., with <s>anusvāra</s>. Again, of what kind? '<s>Hārda</s>' means endowed with the word <s>namaḥ</s> (salutation), which is pleasant to the heart: this is the meaning. The practice is: 'Oṃ goṃ Oṃ namaḥ' on the three joints of the right thumb; 'Oṃ pīṃ Oṃ namaḥ' on the index finger, and so on; 'Oṃ llaṃ Oṃ namaḥ' on the left little finger, and so on. // KrdC_2.25 //
He states the locations for the letter-installation described above, starting with '<s>śākhāsu</s>' etc.:

children.text: śākhāsu trīṇi parvāṇy adhi daśasu pṛthag-dakṣiṇāṅguṣṭha-pūrvaṃ
children.translated_text: On the ten branches [fingers], three joints each, separately, beginning with the right thumb

children.text: vāmāṅgaṣṭhāvasānaṃ nyasatu vimala-dhīḥ sṛṣṭir uktā karasthā |
children.translated_text: And ending with the left thumb — the pure-minded one should install; the <s>sṛṣṭi</s> (creation [order]) on the hands is thus stated.
The <s>sthiti</s> (preservation [order]), beginning with both thumbs, on both hands; the <s>saṃhṛti</s> (dissolution [order]), beginning with the left,

children.text: dakṣāṅguṣṭhāntikaitat trayam api sṛjati sthity-upetaṃ ca kāryam // Krd_2.26 //
children.translated_text: Ending with the right thumb — this triad, together with <s>sthiti</s>, should also be performed. // Krd_2.26 //

children.text:
daśasu śākhāsu aṅgulīṣu pṛthak kṛtvaikaṃ trīṇi parvāṇi adhi parva-trayaṃ vyāpya, tripāṭhinas tu trīṇi parvāṇi iti parva-traye adhīti upari aṅguly-agre ca pṛthag ekaikaśaḥ | tathā ca prathama-parvaṇi oṃ dvitīye oṃ tṛtīye oṃ aṅguly-agre namaḥ iti evam anyatrāpīty āhuḥ | dakṣiṇāṅguṣṭha-pūrvaṃ prathama-nyāsādau yathā syāt tathā vāmāṅgaṣṭhāvasānaṃ vāmāṅgaṣṭho 'vasāne nyāsānte yathā syād evaṃ viśada-dhīr vimala-buddhīr nyasatu | evaṃ ca karasthā sṛṣṭir uktā kare sṛṣṭi-nyāsa-prakāra ukta ity arthaḥ | aṅguṣṭha-dvandva-pūrvā sthitir ubhaya-kare hasta-dvaye dakṣiṇa-kare 'ṅguṣṭhādika-niṣṭhāsu vinyasya vāma-kare 'py aṅguṣṭhādika-niṣṭhāsv aṅguliṣu nyased ayaṃ sthiti-nyāsa uktaḥ | saṃhṛtir
vāma-pūrvā dakṣeti saṃhṛtiḥ saṃhāraḥ vāmāṅguṣṭha-pūrvā dakṣiṇāṅguṣṭhāvasānā ayaṃ ca saṃhāra-nyāsa uktaḥ | etat trayam api sṛṣṭi-sthiti-saṃhārātmakaṃ trayam api sṛjati sthity-upetaṃ kāryaṃ ca sṛṣṭy-ādi-nyāsa-pañcakaṃ kāryam ity arthaḥ || KrdC_2.26 ||
children.translated_text: On the ten branches, i.e., fingers, having separated them, one [should install] on three joints, i.e., pervading the three joints. But those who follow the <s>Tripāṭhī</s> [tradition] say: 'three joints' means on each of the three joints and separately on the fingertip, one by one. Thus, on the first joint Oṃ, on the second Oṃ, on the third Oṃ, on the fingertip <s>namaḥ</s> — thus in other cases too, they say. Beginning with the right thumb, so that the first installation starts there, ending with the left thumb so that the left thumb is at the end of the installation — thus the pure-minded one should install. And thus the <s>sṛṣṭi</s> (creation) on the hand is stated, meaning the method of <s>sṛṣṭi-nyāsa</s> on the hands is described. The <s>sthiti</s> (preservation), beginning with both thumbs, on both hands — having installed on the fingers from thumb to little finger on the right hand, one should install on the fingers from thumb to little finger on the left hand too — this is the <s>sthiti-nyāsa</s> described. The <s>saṃhṛti</s> (dissolution), beginning with the left, ending with the right thumb — this is the <s>saṃhāra-nyāsa</s> described. This triad — the three consisting of <s>sṛṣṭi</s>, <s>sthiti</s>, and <s>saṃhāra</s> — together with <s>sthiti</s>, should be performed; meaning all five installations should be done. // KrdC_2.26 //
'<s>Tataḥ</s>' etc.:
Then, in the order of <s>sthiti</s> (preservation), the learned one should install the ten auxiliaries on the [ten] fingers.

children.text: tad-aṅga-pañcakaṃ tathā vidhiḥ samīritaḥ kare // Krd_2.27 //
children.translated_text: The five auxiliaries of that [<s>mantra</s>] likewise — thus the method on the hands has been declared. // Krd_2.27 //

children.text: tatas tad-anantaraṃ sthiti-kramāt sthiti-nyāsa-krameṇa daśasv aṅgulīṣu budhaḥ paṇḍitaḥ daśāṅgakāni pūrvokta-mantra-daśāṅgāni vinyaset | tad-aṅga-pañcakaṃ tatheti tathā tena prakāreṇa sthiti-krameṇa tad-aṅga-pañcakaṃ purvokta-pañcakaṃ pūrvoktāṅga-pañcakaṃ daśasu aṅgulīṣu vinyaset | kara-nyāsa-jātam upasaṃharati vidhir iti | evaṃ cāyaṃ vidhiḥ prakāraḥ kare hasta-dvaye samīritaḥ kathita ity arthaḥ || KrdC_2.27 ||
children.translated_text: Then, i.e., thereafter, in the <s>sthiti</s> order, i.e., in the sequence of <s>sthiti-nyāsa</s>, the learned one should install the ten auxiliaries — the ten auxiliaries of the previously mentioned <s>mantra</s> — on the ten fingers. 'The five auxiliaries of that, likewise' — means in the same manner, by the <s>sthiti</s> method, the five auxiliaries previously stated should be installed on the ten fingers. He concludes the hand-installation: '<s>vidhiḥ</s>' — thus this method, this procedure, has been declared, told, on the hands, i.e., on both hands: this is the meaning. // KrdC_2.27 //

children.text: mātṛkā-nyāsa-viśeṣaṃ darśayan tattva-nyāsaṃ ca krameṇāha-puṭitair iti |
children.translated_text: Showing a special aspect of the <s>mātṛkā-nyāsa</s> (mother-letter installation) and also the <s>tattva-nyāsa</s> (principle installation) in sequence, he says '<s>puṭitaiḥ</s>' etc.:
With the <s>mātṛkā</s> (mother) letters enclosed, O lord of <s>mantra</s>s,
Having installed with <s>bindu</s>s (dots), as before,
By the distinction of the paths of dissolution and creation,
The ten <s>tattva</s>s (principles) also, conjoined with the <s>mantra</s> letters. // Krd_2.28 //

children.text: athāntara-manunā daśārṇena puṭitair mātṛkākṣaraiḥ sa-bindubhiḥ sānusvāraiḥ purovat pūrvavad yathā pūrvaṃ lalāṭādiṣu nyāsa evam abhivinyasya anu paścān mātṛkā-nyāsa-viśeṣa-karaṇānantaraṃ vakṣyamāṇāni daśa-tattvāni vinyaset | kīdṛśāni mantra-varṇa-bhāñji mantrākṣara-yuktāni | kathaṃ daśa-tattvāni vinyaset ? tatrāha-saṃhṛti-sṛṣṭi-mārga-bhedāt prathamaṃ saṃhāra-krameṇa tad-anantaraṃ sṛṣṭi-krameṇety arthaḥ || KrdC_2.28 ||
children.translated_text: Now, with the <s>mātṛkā</s> letters enclosed in the inner <s>mantra</s> of ten syllables, with <s>bindu</s>s (dots), i.e., with <s>anusvāra</s>s, as before — just as previously on the forehead and other places, having installed thus — after, i.e., after performing the special <s>mātṛkā-nyāsa</s>, one should install the ten <s>tattva</s>s to be described. Of what kind? Conjoined with <s>mantra</s> letters. How should one install the ten <s>tattva</s>s? He says: by the distinction of the paths of dissolution and creation — first in the order of dissolution, then in the order of creation: this is the meaning. // KrdC_2.28 //
He shows the method of dissolution and creation — '<s>saṃhṛtāu</s>' etc.:
In dissolution, the supreme <s>mantra</s> proceeds downward;
On the path of creation, it returns in reverse.
The extraction [of these <s>mantra</s>s] is indeed as previously stated;
I shall now describe the installation procedure. // Krd_2.29 //

children.text: asau manu-varyaḥ manu-śreṣṭhaḥ saṃhṛtau saṃhāra-nyāse anugato yathaivāsti tathaiva sṛṣṭi-mārge sṛṣṭi-kara-nyāse pratiyāto bhavet tad-viparīto bhavet | uddhāra-prakāram āha-uddhṛtir iti | eṣāṃ tattvānāṃ khalu niścayena uddhṛtir uddhāraḥ pūrvoktavad yathā pūrvam ukta-tattva-nyāse | naty-upetaṃ bhūyaḥ parāya ca tad-āhvayam ātmane ca naty-antam uddharatu tattva-manūn krameṇa iti prakāreṇety arthaḥ | adhunā nyāsaṃ kathayāmīti sāmprataṃ nyāsa-sambandhi-tattva-nāma-kathanaṃ tat-sthāna-kathanaṃ ca karomīty arthaḥ || KrdC_2.29 ||
children.translated_text: That supreme <s>mantra</s>, as it exists in the <s>saṃhāra-nyāsa</s> (dissolution installation), so in the <s>sṛṣṭi</s> (creation) path, i.e., in the <s>sṛṣṭi</s> hand-installation, '<s>pratiyātaḥ</s>' means it goes in reverse. He states the method of extraction — '<s>uddhṛtiḥ</s>' etc.: the extraction, i.e., the derivation, of these <s>tattva</s>s is certainly as previously stated, i.e., in the manner described before for the <s>tattva-nyāsa</s>. 'I now describe the <s>nyāsa</s>' means: I now state the names of the <s>tattva</s>s related to the installation and their locations: this is the meaning. // KrdC_2.29 //
He states the names of the <s>tattva</s>s — '<s>mahī</s>' etc.:
Earth, water, fire, wind, space, ego, the great [principle],

children.text: punaḥ prakṛti-puruṣau para imāni tattvāny atha |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), <s>Puruṣa</s> (cosmic person), and the Supreme — these are the <s>tattva</s>s (principles). Now,

children.text: padāndhu-hṛdayāsyakāny adhi tu pañca madhye dvayaṃ
children.translated_text: At the feet, the private parts, the heart, the face, and the head — five [in these places]; in the middle, two;

children.text: trayaṃ sakala-gaṃ tato nyasatu tad-viparyāsataḥ // Krd_2.30 //
children.translated_text: Three pervading the entire body — one should install, and then in reverse order. // Krd_2.30 //

children.text:
mahī pṛthivī | salilaṃ jalaṃ | pāvakaḥ tejaḥ | anilo vāyuḥ | viyad-ākāśaḥ | garvo 'haṅkāraḥ | mahān mahat-tattvam | prakṛtiḥ puruṣaḥ | paraś ca imāni pṛthivy-ādīni tattvāni tattva-pada-vācyāni | nyāsa-sthānam āha-atheti | athānantaraṃ pañca tattvāni pṛthivy-ādīni nyasatu | kutra padāndhu-hṛdayāsyakāny adhi pādayoḥ | andhau liṅge | hṛdaye | āsye mukhe | ke śirasi | adhi saptamy-arthe madhye hṛdaye tattva-dvayaṃ trayaṃ sakala-gaṃ sakalāṅga-vyāpakaṃ tatas tad-anantaraṃ tad-viparyāsataḥ ukta-saṃhāra-viparīta-rītyā nyasatu | prayogaś ca-oṃ goṃ namaḥ parāya pṛthivy-ātmane namaḥ iti pāda-dvaye ity ārabhya oṃ hāṃ namaḥ parāya paramātmane namaḥ ity antaḥ saṃhāraḥ oṃ hāṃ namaḥ parāya paramātmane namaḥ ity ārabhya oṃ
goṃ namaḥ parāya pṛthivy-ātmane namaḥ pāda-dvaye iti sṛṣṭi-nyāsaḥ | sṛṣṭi-nyāse trayaṃ sarva-śarīre, mahad-ahaṅkārau hṛdi ākāśaḥ śirasi | vāyv-agni-salila-mahyaḥ mukha-hṛdaya-liṅga-pāda-dvayeṣu, jñeyāḥ | kecit tu tattva-padāntar-bhāvena nyāsam icchanti tac cintyam || KrdC_2.30 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Mahī</s>' is earth; '<s>salila</s>' is water; '<s>pāvaka</s>' is fire (radiance); '<s>anila</s>' is wind; '<s>viyat</s>' is space; '<s>garva</s>' is <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle); '<s>mahān</s>' is the <s>mahat-tattva</s> (great principle); <s>Prakṛti</s>, <s>Puruṣa</s>, and the Supreme — these <s>tattva</s>s, beginning with earth, are denoted by the word <s>tattva</s>. He states the places of installation — '<s>atha</s>' etc.: then, next, one should install five <s>tattva</s>s beginning with earth. Where? At the feet; '<s>andha</s>' at the generative organ; at the heart; at the face (<s>āsya</s>); at the head (<s>ka</s>) — in the seventh case [locative], meaning 'upon.' In the middle, i.e., at the heart, two <s>tattva</s>s; three pervading all limbs (<s>sakala-ga</s>). Then, thereafter, in reverse order — in the manner opposite to the described dissolution order — one should install. The practice is: 'Oṃ goṃ namaḥ <s>parāya pṛthivy-ātmane namaḥ</s>' at both feet, and so on up to 'Oṃ hāṃ namaḥ <s>parāya paramātmane namaḥ</s>' — this is the dissolution. From 'Oṃ hāṃ namaḥ <s>parāya paramātmane namaḥ</s>' beginning, down to 'Oṃ goṃ namaḥ <s>parāya pṛthivy-ātmane namaḥ</s>' at both feet — this is the <s>sṛṣṭi-nyāsa</s> (creation installation). In the <s>sṛṣṭi-nyāsa</s>, three on the whole body; <s>mahat</s> and <s>ahaṅkāra</s> at the heart; space at the head; wind, fire, water, and earth at the face, heart, generative organ, and both feet respectively — this should be understood. Some, however, wish to perform the installation subsuming the word <s>tattva</s> — that is debatable. // KrdC_2.30 //
'<s>Guptatama</s>' etc.:
This <s>nyāsa</s> (installation) is declared to be the most secret, fashioned with the ten principles.

children.text: kāryo 'nyṣv api sadbhir gopāla-manuṣu jhaṭiti phala-siddhyai // Krd_2.31 //
children.translated_text: It should be performed by the wise in other <s>Gopāla-mantra</s>s too, for the swift attainment of results. // Krd_2.31 //

children.text: ayaṃ proktaḥ kathito nyāsaḥ sadbhiḥ paṇḍitaiḥ anyeṣv api gopāla-mantreṣu uddhṛta-daśākṣara-vyatirikteṣv api kāryaḥ | kīdṛśaḥ ? guhyatamaḥ atiśayena guptaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? tattva-daśaka-parikptaḥ tattvānāṃ daśakaṃ tattva-daśakaṃ tena parikpta udghāṭita ity arthaḥ | kim artham ? jhaṭiti phala-siddhyai śīghra-phala-prāptyai || KrdC_2.31 ||
children.translated_text: This <s>nyāsa</s>, as stated, as described, should be performed by the wise, the learned, in other <s>Gopāla-mantra</s>s too — those other than the extracted ten-syllable [<s>mantra</s>]. Of what kind? Most secret — exceedingly hidden. Again, of what kind? Fashioned with the ten principles (<s>tattva-daśaka</s>), i.e., revealed by means of the group of ten <s>tattva</s>s. For what purpose? For the swift attainment of results, for obtaining results quickly. // KrdC_2.31 //
He states another <s>nyāsa</s> — '<s>ākeśāt</s>' etc.:
From the hair to the feet, with both arms,
The supreme <s>mantra</s> enclosed in <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ) — one should then install on the body.
Three times on the head; at the eyes, ears, nose,
Mouth, heart, belly, generative organ, knees, and feet — likewise the syllables. // Krd_2.32 //

children.text: athānantaraṃ dorbhyāṃ hastābhyāṃ dhruva-puṭitam praṇava-puṭitaṃ manu-varaṃ mantra-śreṣṭhaṃ daśākṣaraṃ gopāla-mantram ākeśād āpādaṃ keśādi-pāda-paryantaṃ triśaḥ sva-dehe vinyased iti vidyādharācārya-tripāṭhi-prabhṛtayaḥ | eteṣāṃ mata ākeśād āpādad iti pāṭhaḥ | adhunā sṛṣṭi-sthiti-saṃhāra-krameṇa mantrākṣara-nyāsam āha-mūrdhanīty ādi | tathā daśākṣarāṇi praṇava-puṭitāni mūrdhādi-vakṣyamāṇa-sthāneṣu vinyaset | sthānāny āha-mūrdhanīti | mūrdhni cakṣuṣor ubhaya-netre ekam evākṣaraṃ śrutayoḥ karṇayoḥ atrāpy -ekam eva ghrāṇe nāsā-yugme tatrāpy ekam eva mukhaṃ hṛdayaṃ jaṭharaṃ śivaṃ liṅgam jānu-dvaye ekaṃ, pāda-dvaye ekam eteṣu daśasu sthāneṣu daśākṣarāṇi

children.translated_text: should be installed: this is the meaning. // KrdC_2.32 //

Then, next, with both arms, i.e., with both hands, the supreme <s>mantra</s> enclosed in <s>praṇava</s>, the excellent <s>mantra</s>, the ten-syllable <s>Gopāla-mantra</s> — from the hair to the feet, three times on one's own body — one should install: thus say <s>Vidyādharācārya</s>, <s>Tripāṭhī</s>, and others. According to their view, the reading is '<s>ākeśād āpādāt</s>.' Now he states the installation of <s>mantra</s> syllables in the order of <s>sṛṣṭi</s>, <s>sthiti</s>, and <s>saṃhāra</s> — '<s>mūrdhani</s>' etc.: likewise, the ten syllables enclosed in <s>praṇava</s> should be installed at the head and other locations to be described. He states the locations — '<s>mūrdhani</s>' etc.: at the crown of the head; at both eyes — one syllable for both; at the ears — here too just one; at the nose, the pair of nostrils — here too just one; at the mouth; the heart; the belly; the generative organ (<s>śiva</s>); at both knees — one; at both feet — one. At these ten locations, the ten syllables

children.text: uktā sṛṣṭiḥ śiṣṭair eṣā sthitir api
children.translated_text: The <s>sṛṣṭi</s> (creation [order]) is declared by the learned; the <s>sthiti</s> (preservation [order]) also,
Declared by the sages, goes from the heart to the face.
The <s>saṃhāra</s> (dissolution [order]) goes from the feet to the head — this triad,

children.text: viracayec ca sṛṣṭim anu sthitim // Krd_2.33 //
children.translated_text: One should perform, and after <s>sṛṣṭi</s>, the <s>sthiti</s> [again]. // Krd_2.33 //

children.text: śiṣṭair āgama-jñair eṣā sṛṣṭir uktety arthaḥ | sthitir api sthiti-nyāso 'pi munibhir nāradādibhir hṛdayādi-mukhāntikā abhihitā hṛdayam ārabhya mukha-paryantaṃ kathitā | tatra kramaḥ hṛdaya-jaṭhara-liṅga-jānu-pāda-mūrdhākṣi-śravaṇa-ghrāṇa-mukhānīti saṃhāro 'ṅghry-ādi-mūrdhāntaḥ kāryaḥ | tatra mantrākṣarāṇi pratilomena deyānītīdaṃ tritayaṃ viracayatu anu paścād etat tritaya-karaṇānantaraṃ punaḥ sṛṣṭim sthitim ca viracayatu | tathā ca pañca nyāsāḥ kāryā ity arthaḥ | prayogas tu goṃ namaḥ pīṃ namaḥ ity ādi ||33||
