children.translated_text: By the learned, i.e., those who know the <s>āgama</s>s — this <s>sṛṣṭi</s> is stated: this is the meaning. The <s>sthiti-nyāsa</s> also, by sages such as <s>Nārada</s> and others, is declared '<s>hṛdayādi-mukhāntikā</s>' — from the heart up to the face. The order there is: heart, belly, generative organ, knees, feet, head, eyes, ears, nose, and face. The <s>saṃhāra</s> from the feet to the head should be performed. There, the <s>mantra</s> syllables should be given in reverse order. This triad should be performed; then after that, i.e., after performing this triad, one should perform <s>sṛṣṭi</s> and <s>sthiti</s> again. Thus five installations should be done: this is the meaning. The practice is: 'goṃ namaḥ, pīṃ namaḥ' and so on. // 33 //

children.text: yeṣām āśramiṇāṃ yad-anto nyāsas tad darśayati -nyāsa iti |
children.translated_text: He shows for which <s>āśramin</s>s (members of life-stages) which terminal <s>nyāsa</s> applies — '<s>nyāsa</s>' etc.:
This <s>nyāsa</s> is prescribed to end with <s>saṃhāra</s> (dissolution) for <s>maskarin</s>s (renunciants) and <s>vaikhānasa</s>s (forest hermits).

children.text: sthity-anto gṛhamedhiṣu sṛṣṭy-anto varṇinām iti prāhuḥ // Krd_2.34 //
children.translated_text: It ends with <s>sthiti</s> (preservation) for householders; and ends with <s>sṛṣṭi</s> (creation) for celibate students — thus they say. // Krd_2.34 //

children.text: ayaṃ nyāsaḥ maskari-vaikhānaseṣu saṃhārānto vihitaḥ maskarī sannyāsī vaikhānaso vānaprasthaḥ, tathā tābhyāṃ nyāsa-trayaṃ kāryam ity arthaḥ | gṛha-medhiṣu gṛhastheṣu ayaṃ nyāsaḥ sthity-anto vihitaḥ | tathā gṛhasthaiḥ pañca nyāsāḥ kāryā ity arthaḥ | varṇināṃ brahmacāriṇām ayaṃ nyāsaḥ sṛṣṭy-anto vihitaḥ | tathā ca brahmacāribhir nyāsa-catuṣṭayaṃ kāryam ity arthaḥ | iti pūrvoktam artha-jātaṃ prāhuḥ prācīnā āgamajñā iti śeṣaḥ || KrdC_2.34 ||
children.translated_text: This <s>nyāsa</s> is prescribed to end with <s>saṃhāra</s> for <s>maskarin</s>s (renunciants) and <s>vaikhānasa</s>s (forest hermits) — '<s>maskarin</s>' means a <s>sannyāsin</s> (renunciant); '<s>vaikhānasa</s>' means a <s>vānaprastha</s> (forest-dweller). Thus those two should perform three installations: this is the meaning. For <s>gṛhamedhin</s>s, i.e., householders, this <s>nyāsa</s> is prescribed to end with <s>sthiti</s>. Thus householders should perform five installations: this is the meaning. For <s>varṇin</s>s, i.e., <s>brahmacārin</s>s (celibate students), this <s>nyāsa</s> is prescribed to end with <s>sṛṣṭi</s>. Thus <s>brahmacārin</s>s should perform four installations: this is the meaning. '<s>Iti prāhuḥ</s>' — thus say the ancient knowers of <s>āgama</s>: this completes [the statement]. // KrdC_2.34 //
'<s>Vairāgya</s>' etc.:

children.text: vairāgya-yuji gṛhasthe saṃhāraṃ kecid āhur ācāryāḥ |
children.translated_text: Some <s>ācārya</s>s (teachers) prescribe <s>saṃhāra</s> (dissolution) for a householder endowed with <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion);

children.text: sahajānau vana-vāsini sthitiṃ ca vidyārthināṃ sṛṣṭim // Krd_2.35 //
children.translated_text: And <s>sthiti</s> (preservation) for the forest-dweller by birth; and <s>sṛṣṭi</s> (creation) for students of knowledge. // Krd_2.35 //

children.text: kecid ācāryāḥ vairāgya-yukta-gṛhasthe saṃhārāntaṃ nyāsam āhuḥ | kiṃ ca sahajānau vana-vāsini sapatnīke sthitiṃ sthity-antaṃ nyāsam āhuḥ | tathā brahmacāri-bhinnānāṃ vidyārthinām api sṛṣṭim sṛṣṭy-antaṃ nyāsam āhur ity arthaḥ || KrdC_2.35 ||
children.translated_text: Some teachers prescribe the <s>nyāsa</s> (placement) up to <s>saṃhāra</s> (dissolution) for a householder endowed with <s>vairāgya</s> (detachment). Furthermore, for one naturally [qualified], a forest-dweller with a co-wife, they prescribe the <s>nyāsa</s> up to <s>sthiti</s> (maintenance). And for students seeking knowledge other than <s>brahmacārin</s>s, they prescribe the <s>nyāsa</s> up to <s>sṛṣṭi</s> (creation) — this is the meaning. (KrdC 2.35)
He demonstrates the finger-regulation for the stated syllable-<s>nyāsa</s> — beginning with 'on the head' etc.:
On the head the middle [finger] is prescribed; the same with the index finger at the eyes;
At the ears, without the thumb; the ring finger combined with the great [thumb] —

children.text: nasi ca vadane sarvāḥ sajyāyasī hṛdi tarjanī
children.translated_text: At the nose; and at the mouth, all [fingers]; at the heart, the index with the great [thumb];

children.text: prathamaja-yutā madhyā nābhau śravo-vihitā śive // Krd_2.36 //
children.translated_text: The middle combined with the first-born [thumb] at the navel; [as] prescribed at the ears, on the <s>śiva</s> (generative organ). (Krd 2.36)

children.text: tā evāṅgulayo jānvoḥ sāṅguṣṭhās tu pada-dvaye |
children.translated_text: Those same fingers at the knees; with the thumb at the pair of feet;

children.text: sthānārṇayor vinimayo bhaven nāsty aṅguli-sthānayoḥ // Krd_2.37 //
children.translated_text: There may be interchange of station and syllable, but not of finger and station. (Krd 2.37)

children.text:
madhyā madhyāṅguliḥ śirasi mūrdhni vihitā nyāsa-karaṇatvena tathā madhyāṅgulyā nyāsaḥ śirasi kārya ity arthaḥ | saiva madhyā tarjanikānvitākṣṇi nayana-yugale vihitā | tathā ca madhyamā-tarjanībhyām akṣṇor nyāsaḥ kāryaḥ | śravasi śrotra-yugale rahitāṅguṣṭhā aṅguṣṭha-rahitā sarvāṅgulayo vihitāḥ | nasi nāsā-yugale jyeṣṭhānvitā aṅguṣṭha-yuktā upakaniṣṭhakā anāmikā vihitā | vadane sarvāṅgulayo vihitāḥ | hṛdi sajyāyasī jyeṣṭhā-sahitā sāṅguṣṭha-tarjanī vihitā | nābhau jaṭhare nābhi-padena jaṭharam upalakṣitam iti vidyādharaḥ | nābhi-padasya mukhya evārtha iti laghu-dīpikā-prabhṛtayaḥ | prathamaja-yutā aṅguṣṭha-yuktā madhyamā vihitā | śive liṅge tathā vihitā yathā jaṭhare sāṅguṣṭhā madhyā
tathety artha iti kecit | śravo vihitā śiva iti pāṭhe śrotra-yugale yā aṅguṣṭha-rahitās tāḥ śive vihitā ity arthaḥ | jānvos tā evāṅgulayaḥ aṅguṣṭhena rahitāḥ sarvāṅgulaya ity arthaḥ | pada-dvaye sāṅguṣṭhāḥ sarvāṅgulayo vihitāḥ | sthānārṇayor ity ādinā sthānaākṣaraayor vinimayo viparyayo bhavati | yathā-goṃ sṛṣṭau mūrdhni | sthitau hṛdaye | saṃhṛtau pādayor nyāsa iti | evam aṅgulī-sthānayor viparyayo nāsti | kintu sṛṣṭau sthitau saṃhṛtau vā yatra sthāne yāṅgulir vihitā tayaivāṅgulyā tatra stāne nyāsaḥ kārya ity arthaḥ | || KrdC_2.36-37 ||
children.translated_text: 'Middle' — the middle finger; 'on the head' — prescribed on the crown for the purpose of performing <s>nyāsa</s>; thus, the <s>nyāsa</s> with the middle finger should be done on the head — this is the meaning. That same middle [finger] combined with the index finger is prescribed at the eyes — the pair of eyes. Thus, <s>nyāsa</s> at the eyes should be done with the middle and index fingers. At the ears — the pair of ears — without the thumb, all fingers are prescribed. At the nose — the pair of nostrils — the ring finger (<s>anāmikā</s>) combined with the great [finger] — the thumb — is prescribed. At the mouth, all fingers are prescribed. At the heart, the index finger together with the great [finger] — with the thumb — is prescribed. At the navel — the belly; the <s>Vidyādhara</s> [says] the word '<s>nābhi</s>' indicates the belly. 'The primary meaning of the word <s>nābhi</s> [is navel]' — so say the <s>Laghu-dīpikā</s> and others. The middle [finger] combined with the first-born — the thumb — is prescribed. On the <s>śiva</s> — the generative organ — prescribed as at the belly, i.e., with the thumb and middle finger — this is the meaning, according to some. In the reading '<s>śravo vihitā śive</s>': those [fingers] without the thumb that are [prescribed] at the pair of ears are prescribed on the <s>śiva</s> — this is the meaning. At the knees, those same fingers — all fingers without the thumb — this is the meaning. At the pair of feet, all fingers with the thumb are prescribed. By 'interchange of station and syllable' etc.: there may be reversal of station and syllable. For example: '<s>goṃ</s>' — in creation, on the crown; in maintenance, at the heart; in dissolution, at the feet — thus is the <s>nyāsa</s>. But there is no such reversal of finger and station; rather, in creation, maintenance, or dissolution, whichever finger is prescribed at a given station, with that very finger the <s>nyāsa</s> should be done at that station — this is the meaning. (KrdC 2.36–37)
Now he describes the <s>vibhūti-pañjara-nyāsa</s> (splendor-cage placement) — 'I declare' etc.:
I declare another excellent <s>nyāsa</s>, called <s>bhūti</s> (splendor), bestowing prosperity,
Consisting of ten repetitions of the <s>mantra</s>, most secret among the best of <s>mantra</s>-practitioners. (Krd 2.38)

children.text: aparaṃ bhūty-abhidhaṃ bhūtir iti nāma yasya tad bhūti-nāmakaṃ vacmi kathayāmi | kīdṛśam ? nyāsa-varaṃ nyāsa-śreṣṭham ity arthaḥ | punaḥ bhūti-karam aiśvarya-karam | punaḥ mantra-daśāvṛtti-mayaṃ mantrasya daśāvaraṇa-ghaṭitam | punaḥ sādhaka-śreṣṭhair guptatamam atiguhyam || KrdC_2.38 ||
children.translated_text: 'Another' — called <s>bhūti</s> (splendor), having the name <s>bhūti</s> — I declare, I describe. Of what kind? 'Excellent <s>nyāsa</s>' — the best among <s>nyāsa</s>s, this is the meaning. Further, '<s>bhūti-kara</s>' — bestowing sovereignty. Further, 'consisting of ten repetitions of the <s>mantra</s>' — composed of ten coverings of the <s>mantra</s>. Further, 'most secret' — extremely hidden, among the best of practitioners. (KrdC 2.38)
He states the station of <s>nyāsa</s> — beginning with '<s>ādhāra</s>' etc.:
The <s>ādhāra</s> (base), <s>dhvaja</s> (generative organ), navel, heart, throat, mouth, the pair of shoulders and thighs, the nape of the neck —
The navel, flanks, heart, pair of breasts, the sides, the back, and the buttocks;
The head, eyes, ears, nose, cheeks, the joints of hands and feet, the tips and branches;

children.text: tat-prācyādi-diśāsu mūrdhni sakale doṣṇoś ca sakthnos tathā // Krd_2.39 //
children.translated_text: The top of the head, in the directions beginning with east, on the entire crown, and on both arms and both thighs likewise. (Krd 2.39)
The head, eyes, mouth, [station] called throat, heart, belly, <s>kanda</s> (bulb),
Scrotum, knees, soles of the feet — in this manner, with syllables arisen from <s>mantra</s>s —
One should place [them] at the ears, cheeks, shoulders, breasts, sides,
Buttocks, thighs, surfaces, knees, shanks, and feet, in pairs. (Krd 2.40)

children.text:
ādhāro vṛṣaṇasyādhas trikoṇaṃ mūlādhāra-sthānam | dhvajo liṅgam | nābhiḥ hṛdhayaṃ galaḥ mukhaṃ aṃsoru-dvayam | eteṣv ekāvṛttiḥ | kandharā ghāṭā kandharā kaṇṭha iti laghu-dīpikā-kāraḥ | nābhi-kukṣi-hṛdayam uroja-yugalaṃ stana-dvayam | pārśveti pārśva-yugam | aparaṃ pṛṣṭha-deśaḥ | śroṇir jaghana-deśaḥ | śroṇiḥ kaṭiḥ | aparaṃ śroṇyāḥ aparabhāgaḥ iti tripāṭhinaḥ | eteṣu dvitīyāvṛttiḥ | kaṃ śiraḥ | āsyaṃ mukham | akṣiṇī netra-yugalam | śrutī śravaṇa-dvayam | na iti nāsikā-dvayaṃ kapola-dvayam eteṣu tṛtīyā vṛttiḥ | kara-padeti kara-padayoḥ pratyekaṃ sandhi-catuṣṭayaṃ sandhiṣv aṅguly-agreṣu aṅgulīṣu ca | atra dakṣiṇa-kare caturthā vṛttiḥ | evaṃ vāma-kare pañcamā
vṛttiḥ | iti pakṣa-dvayaṃ ca vidyādharas tu karayor ekā vṛttiḥ, pādayor ekā vṛttir ity āha | tac cintyam | mūla-granthāt tathāpratīteḥ | pādayoḥ sandhiṣv aṅguly-agreṣv aṅgulīṣu ca | atrāpi dakṣiṇa-pāde ṣaṣṭhā vṛttiḥ | vāma-pāde saptamā vṛttiḥ | ata eva hasta-pādayor nyāsa-catuṣṭayam iti tripāṭhinaḥ | ke mastaka-madhye tat-prācyādi-diśāsu mastaka-pūrvādi-caturdikṣu sakale mūrdhni sakale mastake prādakṣiṇyena vyāpakatayā doṣṇoś ca bāhu-yuge tathā sakthnor ūru-mūlasyādhiṣṭhānayor madhya-pradeśayor eteṣv aṣṭamā vṛttiḥ | mastakasya pūrvādi-diśāsv ekā vṛttiḥ | ekā vṛttir mūrdhādiṣv iti vidyādharācāryāḥ | tac cintyam |
children.translated_text: '<s>Ādhāra</s>' — below the scrotum, the triangular <s>mūlādhāra</s> (root-base) station. '<s>Dhvaja</s>' is the generative organ. Navel, heart, throat, mouth, the pair of shoulders and thighs — on these [constitutes] the first repetition. '<s>Kandharā</s>' is the nape; '<s>kandharā</s>' means the neck, according to the <s>Laghu-dīpikā</s> author. Navel, flanks, heart, pair of breasts — the two nipples. '<s>Pārśva</s>' — the pair of sides. '<s>Apara</s>' — the back region. '<s>Śroṇi</s>' — the hip region; '<s>śroṇi</s>' means the waist. '<s>Apara</s> of <s>śroṇi</s>' — the rear part of the buttocks, according to the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s. On these [constitutes] the second repetition. '<s>Ka</s>' — the head. '<s>Āsya</s>' — the mouth. '<s>Akṣiṇī</s>' — the pair of eyes. '<s>Śrutī</s>' — the pair of ears. '<s>Na</s>' — the pair of nostrils; the pair of cheeks — on these [constitutes] the third repetition. At the hands and feet — at each, four joints; at the joints, fingertips, and fingers. Here, on the right hand [constitutes] the fourth repetition. Similarly, on the left hand [constitutes] the fifth repetition. These are the two views; the <s>Vidyādhara</s>, however, says: on both hands [is] one repetition, on both feet [is] one repetition. That is questionable, since it is not so understood from the root text. On the feet — at the joints, fingertips, and fingers. Here too, on the right foot [constitutes] the sixth repetition; on the left foot, the seventh repetition. Therefore, on hands and feet there are four <s>nyāsa</s>s, according to the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s. '<s>Ka</s>' — in the center of the head; in the directions beginning with east from the top of the head — in the four directions from the crown; on the entire crown, with circumambulation; on both arms; and likewise on both thighs — at the root of the thighs, the base-stations, the middle regions — on these [constitutes] the eighth repetition. 'One repetition in the directions of the head from east etc.; one repetition on the crown and so forth' — so say the <s>Vidyādharācārya</s>s. That is questionable.

children.text: tathā pada-svarasāt śiraḥ-prabhṛtiṣv ekāvṛtti-pratīteḥ | śiro mastakam | akṣīti netra-yugalam | āsyaṃ mukham | kaṇṭhaṃ | hṛdayaṃ | tundam udaram | kando mūlādhāraḥ | svādhiṣṭhānam iti tripāṭhinaḥ | andhuṃ liṅgaṃ | jānu | prapad iti pāda-yugalaṃ teṣu, eteṣu navamāvṛttiḥ | śrotra-yugale gaṇḍa-yugale | aṃsa-yugale | stana-yugale | pārśva-yugale | sphig-yugale nitamba-yugale | evam uru-jānu-jaṅghāṅghri-yugale | eteṣu daśamāvṛttiḥ | ittham anena prakāreṇa manūtthān mantra-sambandhino varṇān nyaset | prayogaś ca - goṃ namo mūlādhāre, pīṃ namaḥ liṅge, jaṃ namaḥ nābhau ity ādi || KrdC_2.39-40 ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, from the natural [reading] of the verse, one understands a single repetition beginning with the head etc. '<s>Śiras</s>' — the head. '<s>Akṣi</s>' — the pair of eyes. '<s>Āsya</s>' — the mouth. The throat. The heart. '<s>Tunda</s>' — the belly. '<s>Kanda</s>' — the <s>mūlādhāra</s> (root-base); '<s>Svādhiṣṭhāna</s>' — according to the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s. '<s>Andhu</s>' — the generative organ. Knees. '<s>Prapad</s>' — the pair of feet. On these [constitutes] the ninth repetition. The pair of ears, pair of cheeks, pair of shoulders, pair of breasts, pair of sides, pair of buttocks (<s>nitamba</s>); likewise the pairs of thighs, knees, shanks, and feet — on these [constitutes] the tenth repetition. 'In this manner' — by this method, one should place the syllables arisen from <s>mantra</s>s — the letters connected with the <s>mantra</s>. The practical application is: '<s>goṃ namaḥ</s>' at the <s>mūlādhāra</s>, '<s>pīṃ namaḥ</s>' at the generative organ, '<s>jaṃ namaḥ</s>' at the navel, and so on. (KrdC 2.39–40)
He states the fruit of <s>nyāsa</s> — 'thus' etc.:
Thus has been described the <s>vibhūti-pañjara</s> (splendor-cage),
Granting all happiness, wealth, <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation),
Delighting the minds of men and women,
And increasing devotion to the lotus feet of <s>Hari</s>. (Krd 2.41)

children.text: anena prakāreṇa vibhūti-pañjaraṃ kathitam | kīdṛśam ? sakala-sukhārtha-dharma-mokṣadaṃ puruṣārtha-catuṣṭaya-pradam | punar nara-taruṇī-mano-rañjanaṃ puruṣa-nārī-cittāhlādakaṃ na kevalaṃ sarvānurañjanam | api tu hari-caraṇābje bhakti-vardhanam || KrdC_2.41 ||
children.translated_text: In this manner the <s>vibhūti-pañjara</s> (splendor-cage) has been described. Of what kind? Granting the four <s>puruṣārtha</s>s (goals of human life) — all happiness, wealth, <s>dharma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s>. Further, delighting the minds of men and women — gladdening the hearts of males and females; not merely pleasing to all, but also increasing devotion to the lotus feet of <s>Hari</s>. (KrdC 2.41)
He describes the <s>mūrti-pañjara-nyāsa</s> (form-cage placement) — '<s>sphūrti</s>' etc.:
Now, for the awakening of this <s>mantra</s>, the <s>mūrti-pañjara</s> (form-cage) is proclaimed,
Destroying suffering, planetary afflictions, poison, and enemies; granting fame, prosperity, beauty, and nourishment. (Krd 2.42)

children.text: athānantaram asya daśākṣara-mantrasya sphūrtaye uddīpanāya mūrti-pañjaraṃ kīrtyate | kimbhūtam ? ārtiḥ pīḍā | graho graha-janitam aśubhaṃ viṣaṃ sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca | ariḥ śatruḥ | tān hantīty arthaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? kīrty-ādi-dam | kīrtiḥ prakhyātiḥ | śrī-sampattiḥ saundaryaṃ puṣṭir balaṃ pradadātīti tathā || KrdC_2.42 ||
children.translated_text: Now, next, for the awakening — the stimulation — of this ten-syllable <s>mantra</s>, the <s>mūrti-pañjara</s> is proclaimed. Of what nature? '<s>Ārti</s>' — suffering; '<s>graha</s>' — the inauspiciousness born of planets; '<s>viṣa</s>' — poison, both stationary and mobile; '<s>ari</s>' — enemies; it destroys these — this is the meaning. Again, of what kind? Bestowing fame etc.; '<s>kīrti</s>' — renown; '<s>śrī</s>' — wealth and beauty; '<s>puṣṭi</s>' — strength — it bestows these, thus it is so. (KrdC 2.42)
Now he elaborates the <s>nyāsa</s> — '<s>Keśava</s> etc.' etc.:
With the <s>mūrti</s>s (forms) of the six pairs beginning with <s>Keśava</s>,
[Combined with] the solar [deities] beginning with <s>Dhātṛ</s>, ending with '<s>namaḥ</s>,'
With syllables born of the twelve-syllable [<s>mantra</s>], with vowels
Devoid of neuter letters, one should place in order. (Krd 2.43)

children.text: keśavādibhiḥ pūrvokta-yuga-ṣaṭka-mūrtibhiḥ saha dhātṛ-pūrva-mihirās tān krameṇa nyasatu | kīdṛśān ? namo 'ntakān namaḥ-padāntān | punaḥ kaiḥ saha ? dvādaśākṣara-bhavākṣarair vakṣyamāṇa-dvādaśākṣara-mantra-sambandhibhir dvādaśākṣaraiḥ saha | etad uktaṃ bhavati-ādau svarāḥ | tato namaḥ-padam iti | prayogas tu oṃ aṃ oṃ keśava-dhātṛbhyāṃ namaḥ | oṃ aṃ oṃ keśava-dhātre nama iti tripāṭhinaḥ || KrdC_2.43 ||
children.translated_text: With [the forms] beginning with <s>Keśava</s>, together with the previously mentioned <s>mūrti</s>s of the six pairs — the solar [deities] beginning with <s>Dhātṛ</s> — one should place them in order. Of what kind? Ending with '<s>namaḥ</s>' — ending with the word <s>namaḥ</s>. Again, with what? With the syllables born of the twelve-syllable [<s>mantra</s>] — together with the twelve syllables connected with the forthcoming twelve-syllable <s>mantra</s>. What is stated [amounts to] this: first the vowels, then the word '<s>namaḥ</s>.' The practical application is: '<s>oṃ aṃ oṃ Keśava-Dhātṛbhyāṃ namaḥ</s>'; or '<s>oṃ aṃ oṃ Keśava-Dhātre namaḥ</s>' — according to the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s. (KrdC 2.43)
Now he states the station of <s>nyāsa</s> in the <s>mūrti-pañjara-nyāsa</s> — 'forehead-belly' etc.:
On the forehead, belly, heart, and the hollow of the throat,
On the right side, at the end of the arm, and at the throat;
On the left triad [side, arm-end, and throat], and on the back, at the hump [nape], likewise
On the crown — [following] the six-pair syllable-<s>mantra</s>. (Krd 2.44)

children.text: bhāle lalāṭe | udare | hṛdaye | gala-kūpa-tale kaṇṭhe | vāmetare vāmād itarad dakṣiṇaṃ dakṣiṇa-pārśve bhujānte gale ceti | vāma-traye vāma-pārśve vāma-bhujānte gale ca | pṛṣṭhe kakudi | athānantaraṃ anv iti pāṭhe 'py ayam eva boddhavyaḥ | tathā tena prakāreṇa mūrdhny ṣaḍ-yuga-varṇa-manuṃ dvādaśākṣara-mantraṃ nyased ity arthaḥ || KrdC_2.44 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhāla</s>' — the forehead. The belly. The heart. '<s>Gala-kūpa-tala</s>' — at the throat. '<s>Vāmetara</s>' — other than left, i.e., the right; on the right side, at the end of the arm, and at the throat. 'Left triad' — the left side, the end of the left arm, and the throat. On the back, at the <s>kakud</s> (nape). Then — following; in the reading '<s>anv</s>,' the same [meaning] should be understood. 'In that manner' — by that method, on the crown, one should place the twelve-syllable <s>mantra</s> of the six-pair syllables — this is the meaning. (KrdC 2.44)
He states the purpose of the complete <s>mantra</s>-<s>nyāsa</s> on the head — '<s>caitanya</s>' etc.:
Having a body of consciousness-nectar, with the radiance of ten million suns,
He, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, stationed on the crown, pervades the entire body.
Like pure milk poured —
He pervades [the body], diffused through the manifested syllables of the <s>mantra</s>. (Krd 2.45)

children.text: sa prasiddho vāsudevo mūrdhastho mastaka-sthaḥ san vapur akhilaṃ samastaṃ vapuḥ śarīraṃ vyāpnoti sva-tejasety arthaḥ | kimbhūto vāsudevaḥ ? caitanyāmṛtaṃ tad eva vapur yasya sa tathā | yad vā caitanyaṃ sva-prakāśam amṛtaṃ mokṣas tad eva vapur yasya sa tathā | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? arka-koṭir iva tejo yasya sa tathā | vapur kīdṛśam ? prakaṭita-mantra-varṇa-kīrṇam prakaṭitā ye mantra-varṇā dvādaśākṣarodgatās tair ākīrṇaṃ vyāptam | kim iva ? suvimala-pāyasi sunirmale jale siktaṃ nikṣiptam audhasyaṃ dugdham iva || KrdC_2.45 ||
children.translated_text: That well-known <s>Vāsudeva</s>, stationed on the crown — being situated on the head — pervades the entire body, all the body, with his own radiance — this is the meaning. Of what nature is <s>Vāsudeva</s>? Consciousness-nectar itself is his body — so he is. Or: consciousness, self-luminous, and <s>amṛta</s> (nectar/liberation) — these constitute his body — so he is. Again, of what kind? Whose radiance is like ten million suns — so he is. The body — of what kind? 'Diffused through the manifested <s>mantra</s>-syllables' — pervaded by the manifested syllables arisen from the twelve-syllable [<s>mantra</s>]. Like what? Like milk (<s>audhasya</s>) poured into pure, clear water — that is, like milk mixed into pure <s>pāyasī</s> (water). (KrdC 2.45)
He concludes the body-<s>nyāsa</s>s — '<s>sṛṣṭi-sthiti</s>' etc.:
The <s>sṛṣṭi</s> (creation) and <s>sthiti</s> (maintenance) [<s>nyāsa</s>s], the ten [repetitions], the five-limb pair,
The triad beginning with <s>muni</s> [sages] — at the head, mouth, and heart —
One should place [them]; and having formed the <s>mudrā</s>s (gestures),
Again, the binding of the ten directions should be done. (Krd 2.46)

children.text: mūrti-pañjarasya pūrva-kṛtyaṃ darśayati sṛṣṭi-sthitītyādi iti rudradharaḥ | tac cintyam | tatra pramāṇābhāvāt | mūrdhany akṣṇor ity ādinā pūrvam ukte sṛṣṭi-sthitī punaḥ sva-dehe vinyasya tathā daśa-pañcāṅga-yugmaṃ daśāṅgaṃ pañcāṅgaṃ ca vinyasya | ṛṣy-ādi-tritayaṃ kāsya-hṛtsya vinyased ity arthaḥ | vakṣyamāṇa-mudrāṃ grathayitvā baddhvā bhūyaḥ punar api diśāṃ daśakaṃ bandhanīyam | oṃ sudarśanāyāstrāya phaṭ ity anena vakṣyamāṇena mantreṇety arthaḥ || KrdC_2.46 ||
children.translated_text: He shows the preliminary act of the <s>mūrti-pañjara</s> (image-cage [installation]) — with 'sṛṣṭi-sthiti' etc. — thus says <s>Rudradhara</s>. But that is questionable, since there is no authority for it. Having previously installed the <s>sṛṣṭi</s> (creation) and <s>sthiti</s> (preservation) on one's own body by the method stated earlier with 'mūrdhany akṣṇoḥ' etc., and having installed the pair of ten and five limbs — the ten limbs and the five limbs — one should install the triad of <s>ṛṣi</s> etc. at the mouth, heart, and head — this is the meaning. Having formed, i.e., bound, the <s>mudrā</s> to be described, then again the binding of the ten directions [should be performed] with the mantra to be described: 'Oṃ sudarśanāyāstrāya phaṭ' — this is the meaning.
He states the extraction of the twelve-syllable mantra — beginning with 'tāra' etc.
The <s>tāra</s> (praṇava, Oṃ), the heart [namaḥ], <s>Viśvamūrti</s> [= bha], the bearer of <s>Śārṅga</s> [= ga],
Ending with flesh [= va], between those two — the auspicious deities [= su-de-vā];
The best of mantras with twelve syllables [six pairs] is declared,
Directly the easily accessible gateway to the city of liberation.

children.text: tāraṃ praṇavam | hārdaṃ hṛdayaṃ namaḥ iti yāvat | viśva-mūrtir bha-kāraḥ | śārṅgī ga-kāraḥ | māṃsānte māṃso la-kāraḥ | tasyānto va-kāra iti | te iti svarūpam | vā iti svarūpam | ya iti svarūpam | tayor vāyayor madhye sudevāḥ su-de-vety-akṣara-trayam | tathā ca oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāyeti prasiddhaḥ ṣaḍ-dvandvārṇo mantra-varyo dvādaśākṣaro mantra-śreṣṭha uktaḥ kathitaḥ | kīdṛśaḥ ? mokṣa-puryāḥ sākṣād avyavadhānena sugamyaṃ dvāraṃ sugama upāya ity arthaḥ || KrdC_2.47 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tāra</s> is <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ). <s>Hārda</s> means the heart, i.e., namaḥ. <s>Viśvamūrti</s> is bha-kāra. The bearer of <s>Śārṅga</s> is ga-kāra. At the end of flesh — flesh is la-kāra, its end is va-kāra. 'Te' is its own form [the syllable te]. 'Vā' is its own form. 'Ya' is its own form. Between those two 'vā' and 'ya,' 'sudevāḥ' — the three syllables su, de, vā. Thus 'Oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya' is the well-known [mantra] with six pairs of syllables, i.e., twelve syllables — the best of mantras, thus declared. Of what kind? Directly, without obstruction, it is the easily accessible gateway — the means of approach — to the city of liberation.
He shows the twelve <s>Āditya</s>s (solar deities) of the twelve-syllable [mantra] — beginning with '<s>Dhātṛ-Aryama</s>' etc.
<s>Dhātṛ</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Aṃśu</s>, <s>Bhaga</s>, together with <s>Vivasvat</s> and <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: pūṣāhvaya-parjanyau tvaṣṭā viṣṇuś ca bhānavaḥ proktāḥ // Krd_2.48 //
children.translated_text: The one called <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Parjanya</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, and <s>Viṣṇu</s> — these are declared as the solar deities.

children.text: dhātā aryamā mitraḥ varuṇaḥ aṃśuḥ bhagaḥ vivasvān indraḥ pūṣāḥ parjanyaḥ tvaṣṭā viṣṇur ete dvādaśa bhānavaḥ kathitāḥ || KrdC_2.48 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dhātṛ</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Aṃśu</s>, <s>Bhaga</s>, <s>Vivasvat</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Parjanya</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s> — these twelve are declared as the solar deities.
Now he states the installation of the eighteen-syllable mantra — beginning with 'atha tu yuga' etc.

children.text: atha tu yuga-randhrārṇasyāhaṃ manor nyasanaṃ bruve
children.translated_text: Now I shall declare the installation procedure of the mantra with eighteen syllables [literally: yuga-randhra letters];
One should perform the five-limb [installation] on both hands, on the five fingers;

children.text: tanum anu manuṃ vyāpayyātha triśaḥ praṇavaṃ sakṛn
children.translated_text: Having pervaded the body with the mantra three times, then the <s>praṇava</s> once,

children.text: manujalipayo nyāsyā bhūyaḥ padāni ca sādaram // Krd_2.49 //
children.translated_text: The syllables of the <s>manu</s> (mantra) should be installed with joined palms; and then the <s>pada</s>s (words) also, with reverence.

children.text: anantaraṃ punar yuga-randhrārṇasya yuga-randhre rāja-dantatvād randhra-śabdasya para-nipātaḥ | yuga-randhram akṣarāṇāṃ yatra sa yuga-randhrārṇaḥ tasya | randhraṃ nava | tathā cāṣṭādaśākṣarasya manor mantrasyāhaṃ nyasanaṃ nyāsaṃ bruve kathayāmīti pratijñā | kara-dvaye aṅguli-pañcake pañcāṅgaṃ pūrvoktaṃ mantrākṣaraiḥ parikptaṃ kara-nyāsaṃ kuryāt | kaniṣṭhāyām astra-nyāso draṣṭavyaḥ | athānantaraṃ tanum anu lakṣyīkṛtya triśaḥ tri-vāraṃ mantraṃ vyāpayya vyāpakatayā vinyasya punaḥ praṇavaṃ sakṛd eka-vāraṃ vinyasya anantaraṃ manuja-lipayo nyāsyā mantrākṣarāṇi nyasatu | bhūyo 'nantaraṃ sādaraṃ yathā syād evaṃ padāni pañca padāni nyāsyāni || KrdC_2.49 ||
children.translated_text: Next, of the <s>yuga-randhrārṇa</s> — <s>yuga-randhra</s> means nine, since the word 'randhra' has the value of a royal tooth [= nine by the numeral system]; <s>yuga-randhra</s> of syllables means having that [number], i.e., eighteen. Thus this is the declaration: I shall state the installation of the mantra with eighteen syllables. On both hands, on the group of five fingers, one should perform the five-limb [installation] as previously described, fashioned with the mantra-syllables as hand-installation. The weapon-installation should be observed on the little finger. Then, having pervaded — installed in a pervading manner — the mantra three times on the body, then installing the <s>praṇava</s> once, thereafter one should install the mantra-syllables (<s>manuja-lipi</s>). Then, with reverence, one should install the five <s>pada</s>s (words) [of the mantra].
He states the places for mantra-syllable installation — with 'kaca-bhuvi' etc.
At the birthplace of hair [the head], at the forehead, between the pair of eyebrows, at the ears, at the eyes,
At the pair of nostrils, at the face, at the neck, at the heart, at the navel, at both hips, at the generative organ;
The clear-minded one should install the syllables at the knees and feet; at the head certainly,
And at the eyes, mouth, heart, private parts, and feet, one should place the group of five <s>pada</s>s.

children.text:
kacasya keśasya bhūr-utpatti-sthānaṃ śiraḥ tatra | lalāṭe bhrū-yugmāntare bhrū-madhye śravaṇākṣṇor yugale no nāsikā-yugale ca | vadane grīvāyāṃ hṛdi nābhau kaṭy-ubhaye vāma-kaṭir dakṣiṇa-kaṭiś ca | andhau liṅge | eteṣu tathā jāvy-aṅghryoś ca śitadhir nirmala-matiḥ
akṣarāṇi mantra-sambandhīni nyasatu | atra jānvor ekam akṣaraṃ nyaset | aṅghryor ekam akṣaraṃ nyaset | tathā śirasi mastake dhruvaṃ nyaset | pada-pañcaka-nyāsa-sthānāny āha-nayaneti | nayana-yugalaṃ mukhaṃ hṛdayaṃ guhyaṃ aṅghriś ca - eteṣu mantra-sambandhi pada-pañcakaṃ klīm ity ekam, anyāni spaṣṭāni arpayen nyaset || KrdC_2.50 ||
children.translated_text: The birthplace of hair (<s>kaca</s>) is the head — there. At the forehead; between the pair of eyebrows, i.e., at the brow-center; at the pair of ears and eyes; at the pair of nostrils; at the face; at the neck; at the heart; at the navel; at both hips — left hip and right hip; at the generative organ. At these places, as well as at the knees and feet, the clear-minded one should install the syllables related to the mantra. Here, one syllable should be installed at the knees, and one syllable at the feet. Likewise, one should certainly install at the head, i.e., the crown. He states the places for the five-<s>pada</s> installation — with 'nayana' etc.: at the pair of eyes, at the mouth, at the heart, at the private parts, and at the feet — at these places one should install the five <s>pada</s>s related to the mantra. <s>Klīṃ</s> is one [<s>pada</s>]; the others are clear.
With 'pañcāṅgāni' etc. —

children.text: pañcāṅgāni nyased bhūyo muny-ādīn apy anyat sarvam |
children.translated_text: One should install the five limbs again, and the sage etc. and everything else

children.text: tulyaṃ pūrveṇātho vakṣye mudrā bandhyā manvor yāḥ syuḥ // Krd_2.51 //
children.translated_text: Is the same as before; now I shall declare the <s>mudrā</s>s (hand-gestures) that are to be formed for the mantras.

children.text: pañcāṅgāni bhūyaḥ punar api śarīre nyaset | tathā muny-ādīn ṛṣy-ādīn | anyat sarvaṃ keśavādi-jātaṃ pūrveṇa tulyaṃ samānam eva | atra daśa-tattvādi-nyāseṣu mantrasya dvir āvṛtti-viśeṣa iti laghu-dīpikā-kāraḥ | atho 'nantaraṃ manvor daśākṣarāṣṭādaśākṣarayor yā mudrā bandhyā bandhanīyāḥ syur bhaveyus tā mudrā vakṣye kathayāmi || KrdC_2.51 ||
children.translated_text: The five limbs should be installed again on the body. Likewise the sage etc., i.e., the <s>ṛṣi</s> and others. Everything else related to <s>Keśava</s> etc. is the same as before — identical. Here, in the installations of the ten <s>tattva</s>s etc., there is a special double repetition of the mantra — thus says the author of the <s>Laghudīpikā</s>. Now I shall declare — state — the <s>mudrā</s>s that are to be bound, i.e., formed, for the two mantras, the ten-syllable and the eighteen-syllable.
He shows the <s>mudrā</s>s for the heart and other limb-installations — beginning with 'anaṅguṣṭhā' etc.
The fingers of the hand, straight, without the thumbs,
Form the <s>mudrā</s> at the heart and at the head;
A fist with the thumb below — that is indeed [the mudrā] for the topknot;
The fingers of both hands together are for the armor.
With fists raised like arrows on both arms,
A sound produced by the thumb and index finger,
Scattered in all directions — is declared the weapon-<s>mudrā</s>;
Where there are eyes [in the mantra], the index and middle fingers [form the mudrā].

children.text: anaṅguṣṭhā aṅguṣṭha-rahitā ṛjavo 'vakrā hasta-śākhā hastāṅgulayo hṛdaye mudrā bhavet | śīrṣake ca śirasi tā eva mudrā jñeyāḥ | khalu niścaye | adho 'ṅguṣṭhā muṣṭiḥ adho 'ṅguṣṭho yasyāṃ muṣṭau evaṃ kṛtā muṣṭiḥ śikhāyāṃ mudrā bhavet | varmaṇi kavace kara-dvandvāṅgulayaḥ syuḥ mudrā-pada-vācyā bhavanti | dhvaniḥ śabdo 'stra-mudrā kathitā | kimbhūto dhvaniḥ ? nārācavad bāṇavad muṣṭyoddhato yo bāhus tasya yugmakaṃ dvayaṃ tasyāṅguṣṭha-tarjanībhyāṃ karaṇābhyām uditaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? viṣvag daśa-dikṣu viṣaktaḥ vistīrṇaḥ yatra mantre 'kṣiṇī bhavataḥ netrāṅgam asti tatra tarjanī-madhyame milite mudrā || KrdC_2.53 ||
children.translated_text: Without the thumb — devoid of the thumb — the straight, unbent fingers of the hand form the <s>mudrā</s> at the heart. At the head also, those same <s>mudrā</s>s should be understood. Indeed — a term of certainty — a fist with the thumb below, i.e., a fist made with the thumb underneath, forms the <s>mudrā</s> for the topknot. For the armor (<s>kavaca</s>), the fingers of both hands together become what is denoted by the word <s>mudrā</s>. The sound — the weapon-<s>mudrā</s> — is declared. Of what kind is the sound? The pair of arms raised with fists like arrows, produced by the thumb and index finger as instruments. Again of what kind? Scattered, spread in the ten directions. Where in the mantra there are eyes, i.e., the eye-limb exists, there the index and middle fingers joined form the <s>mudrā</s>.
He states the flute-<s>mudrā</s> — with 'oṣṭha' etc.
The left thumb is placed on the lip; its little finger
Is joined with the right thumb; the right little finger is extended;
The index, middle, and ring fingers are slightly curled and moved —

children.text: veṇu-mudreha kathitā suguptā preyasī hareḥ // Krd_2.55 //
children.translated_text: This is declared here as the flute-<s>mudrā</s>, most secret, the beloved of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: vāma-hastāṅguṣṭho 'dhare lagna iti sambandhaḥ kāryaḥ | tasya vāma-hastasya yā kaniṣṭhikā pañcamī aṅgulī sā dakṣiṇāṅguṣṭha-saṃyuktā dakṣiṇa-hastāṅguṣṭhe sambaddhā kāryā | tat-kaniṣṭhikā dakṣiṇa-hasta- kaniṣṭhikā prasāritā akuṭilā kāryā | ubhaya-hasta-tarjanī-madhyamānāmikāḥ kiñcit saṃkucya cālitāś cālanīyā | ittham iha śāstre veṇu-mudrā kathitā suguptā granthāntare 'tyanta-guptā | yato hareḥ parameśvarasya śrī-kṛṣṇasya preyasī vallabhā || KrdC_2.54-55 ||
children.translated_text: The connection should be made: the left thumb is placed on the lower lip. The little finger, i.e., the fifth finger, of that left hand is to be joined — connected — with the right thumb. The right little finger is to be extended — made straight. The index, middle, and ring fingers of both hands should be slightly curled and moved — made to flutter. In this manner, the flute-<s>mudrā</s> is declared in this treatise, most secret — extremely hidden in other texts. Because it is the beloved, the cherished one, of <s>Hari</s>, the supreme Lord <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>.
With 'nocyante' etc. —
The garland, <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, and <s>Kaustubha</s> [mudrās] are not stated here due to being well-known;
Among the <s>mudrā</s>s of <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), the <s>mudrā</s> in the shape of a <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) fruit is declared.

children.text: mālā-śrī-vatsa-kaustubha-mudrāḥ prasiddhatvān nocyante mayā grantha-kartrāprasiddham iha prakāśyata iti śeṣaḥ | ata eva gale vanamālābhinayanaṃ vanamālā-mudrā | uttānita-vāma-tarjanī-kaniṣṭhopari adhomukha-dakṣiṇa-kara-kaniṣṭhikā-tarjanīke saṃyojya dakṣiṇa-karāṇāmikā-madhyamāṅgulī-dvayaṃ vāma-karāṅguṣṭhopari kṛtvā vāma-kara-madhyamopakaniṣṭhike dakṣiṇa-hastāṅguṣṭhasyādhaḥ kuryād eṣā śrīvatsa-mudrā | vāma-kaniṣṭhikayā dakṣiṇa-kaniṣṭhikāṃ niṣpīḍya vāmānāmikayā dakṣiṇa-tarjanīṃ niṣpīḍya śiṣṭa-vāmāṅgulī-trayam upari kṛtvā vāma-tarjanī-sahita-dakṣiṇa-hastāṅguli-traya-mukham ekatra yojayed eṣā kaustubha-mudrā || KrdC_2.56 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>mudrā</s>s of the garland, <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, and <s>Kaustubha</s> are not stated by me, the author, because they are well-known — what is not well-known is revealed here, this is implied. Therefore, the <s>vanamālā-mudrā</s> (forest-garland mudrā) is the representation of a forest garland at the throat. The <s>Śrīvatsa-mudrā</s>: placing the inverted left index and little fingers above, joining the downward-facing right little and index fingers upon them, placing the right ring and middle fingers above the left thumb, then placing the left middle and ring fingers below the right thumb — this is the <s>Śrīvatsa-mudrā</s>. The <s>Kaustubha-mudrā</s>: pressing the right little finger with the left little finger, pressing the right index finger with the left ring finger, placing the remaining three left fingers above, and joining the tips of the three right fingers together with the left index finger — this is the <s>Kaustubha-mudrā</s>.
He states the <s>bilva-mudrā</s> (wood-apple mudrā) — with 'aṅguṣṭha' etc.
Having raised the left thumb upright and then bound it with the thumb of the other hand,
Pressing its tip with the fingers, and likewise with the fingers of the left hand,

children.text: baddhvā gāḍhaṃ hṛdi sthāpayatu vimala-dhīr vyāharan māra-bījaṃ
children.translated_text: Having bound firmly, the pure-minded one should place [it] at the heart while uttering the <s>Māra-bīja</s> (Kāma seed-syllable [klīṃ]);

children.text: bilvākhyā mudrikaiṣā sphuṭam iha kathitā gopanīyā vidhijñaiḥ // Krd_2.57 //
children.translated_text: This <s>mudrā</s> called <s>bilva</s> is clearly declared here and is to be kept secret by those who know the rules.

children.text: vāmāṅguṣṭhaṃ uddaṇḍitam daṇḍākāram ūrdhvaṃ kṛtvādhaḥ kartavyaṃ tathānantaram itara-karāṅguṣṭena baddhvā tasya ca pīṭhe dakṣiṇa-karāṅguṣṭhas tiraṅ-kārya ity arthaḥ | tasyāgraṃ dakṣiṇa-karāṅguṣṭhāgram aṅgulibhiḥ pīḍayitvā dhṛtvā tā api dakṣiṇa-karāṅgulayo 'pi vāma-hastāṅgulībhir gāḍhaṃ yathā syād evaṃ baddhvā vimala-dhīḥ śuddha-buddhiḥ hṛdi hṛdaye sthāpayet | māra-bījaṃ kāma-bījaṃ vyāharan uccārayan | itthaṃ bilvākhyā eṣā sphuṭam vyaktaṃ yathā syād evam iha-śāstre kathitā vidhijñaiḥ prakāra-jñair gopanīyā || KrdC_2.57 ||
children.translated_text: Having raised the left thumb upright in a rod-like manner, then it should be placed below; then binding it with the thumb of the other [right] hand — the right thumb should be placed horizontally at its base, this is the meaning. Pressing — holding — its tip, i.e., the tip of the right thumb, with the fingers [of the right hand]; those right-hand fingers too should be firmly bound with the left-hand fingers — the pure-minded, clear-intellected one should place [it] at the heart. While uttering the <s>Māra-bīja</s>, the <s>Kāma-bīja</s> (seed-syllable of desire [klīṃ]). In this manner, this [mudrā] called <s>bilva</s> is clearly — distinctly — declared in this treatise, and is to be kept secret by those who know the procedures.
He states the fruit of this [mudrā] — with 'mana' etc.

children.text: mano-vāṇī-dehair yad iha ca purā vāpi vihitaṃ
children.translated_text: Whatever has been done here [in this life] or formerly, through mind, speech, and body,

children.text: tvamatyā matyā vā tad akhilam asau duṣkṛti-cayam |
children.translated_text: Whether through lack of understanding or with understanding — all that heap of evil deeds,

children.text: imāṃ mudrāṃ jānan kṣapayati naras taṃ sura-gaṇā
children.translated_text: A man who knows this <s>mudrā</s> destroys; the hosts of gods

children.text: namanty asyādhīnā bhavati satataṃ sarva-janatā // Krd_2.58 //
children.translated_text: Bow to him; all people become constantly subject to his will.

children.text: asau naro manuṣyaḥ imāṃ mudrāṃ jānan tad akhilaṃ sampūrṇaṃ duṣkṛti-cayaṃ pāpa-rāśiṃ kṣapayati dūrīkaroti yan manasā vācā dehenāmatyājñānena matyā jñānena vā divā-rātri-vihitaṃ divase rātrau vā kṛtam | yad iha ca purā vāpi vihitam iti pāṭhe iha janmani janmāntare vā vihitam ity arthaḥ | na kevalaṃ pāpaṃ dūrīkaroti api tu sura-gaṇā devā namanti | tathāsya mudrākartuḥ satataṃ sarvadā sarva-jana-samūho vaśyo bhavatīty arthaḥ || KrdC_2. 58 ||
children.translated_text: This man, knowing this <s>mudrā</s>, destroys — removes — all that complete heap of sins committed by mind, by speech, by body — whether through ignorance or through [deliberate] knowledge — done during the day or at night. In the reading 'yad iha ca purā vāpi vihitam,' the meaning is: done in this birth or in a previous birth. Not only does he remove sin, but moreover, the hosts of gods bow [to him]. And all the multitude of people is always subject to the will of the performer of this <s>mudrā</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: sanātanaḥ (hari-bhakti-vilāse 6.42) : asau nara imāṃ bilvākhyāṃ mudrāṃ jānan tat-tad-duṣkṛta-nicayaṃ pāpa-samūham akhilaṃ niḥśeṣaṃ kṣapayati vināśayati | kam ? yaṃ mano-vāk-kāyaiḥ iha asmin purā pūrva-janmani ca amatyā ajñānena matyā vā jñānena vihitam | divārātri-vihitam iti pāṭhe dine rātrau ca kṛtam | yat tado napuṃsakatvaṃ mahākavi-svātantryād avyayatvād vā | yad vā, yat yasmāt kṣapayati tat tasmān namantīty anvayaḥ | mudrā-lakṣaṇāni ca guhyatvān na likhitāni | tathā coktam-
children.translated_text: <s>Sanātana</s> (<s>Hari-bhakti-vilāsa</s> 6.42): That person, knowing this <s>mudrā</s> called <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple), completely destroys, without remainder, the entire accumulation of sins (<s>duṣkṛta</s>). Which [sins]? Those committed by mind, speech, and body, in this [life] and in previous births, whether through ignorance or through knowledge. In the reading '<s>divārātri-vihita</s>,' [sins] committed by day and night. The neuter gender [of '<s>yat tat</s>'] is due to the poet's license or its indeclinable nature. Alternatively, the construction is: because (<s>yat</s>) [this <s>mudrā</s>] destroys [sins], therefore (<s>tat</s>) they bow [to it]. The characteristics of <s>mudrā</s>s are not written down due to their secret nature. As stated:

children.text:
guruṃ prakāśayed vidvān mantraṃ naiva prakāśayet |
akṣa-mālāṃ ca mudrāṃ ca guror api na darśayet || iti |
children.translated_text: 'The learned one should reveal the <s>guru</s> (teacher) but should never reveal the <s>mantra</s>; one should not show the <s>akṣamālā</s> (rosary) or the <s>mudrā</s> even to the <s>guru</s>.'

children.text: atra ca tad-vijñānārtham uddiśyante | tathā cāgame-
children.translated_text: And here they are pointed out for the purpose of understanding them. As in the <s>Āgama</s>:
'An <s>añjali</s> (offering gesture) formed with properly cupped flowers in both hands
Is declared by the best of teachers to be the <s>Āvāhanī</s> (invocatory) <s>mudrā</s>.
When [the fingers are] all turned face-downward, it is called <s>Sthāpanī</s> (establishing [<s>mudrā</s>]).
With both fists clasped together and both thumbs raised,
This <s>mudrā</s> is designated for <s>Sannidhāna</s> (bringing near) by those who know the <s>Tantra</s>s.
That very same [<s>mudrā</s>], with the thumbs enclosed within [the fists], is declared for <s>Saṃnirodha</s> (restraining).
The installation of the limbs by the limbs themselves is considered the <s>Sakalīkaraṇī</s> (totalization) [<s>mudrā</s>].
A fist made with the right hand, with the index finger extended downward at length —
This is the <s>Avaguṇṭhana-mudrā</s> (veiling <s>mudrā</s>), if rotated all around.
All the little fingers and ring fingers facing each other,
And likewise the index and middle fingers — this is proclaimed the <s>Dhenu-mudrā</s> (cow <s>mudrā</s>).
With thumbs interlocked and the fingers of the hands extended,
This is declared by the wise to be the <s>Mahā-mudrā</s> (great <s>mudrā</s>) for the rite of consecration.
Holding the left thumb with the right fist in this manner,
And joining the four fingers at the back of that fist,
This is called the <s>Śaṅkha-mudrā</s> (conch <s>mudrā</s>) in the rites of <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> worship.
When the pairs of thumbs and little fingers face each other,
And the remaining fingers are spread out — then that is considered the <s>Darśinī</s> (showing) [<s>mudrā</s>].
When the fingers are interlocked with each other and the two middle fingers are raised

children.text: saṃlagnau ca tadā mudrā gadeyaṃ parikīrtitā ||
children.translated_text: And joined together — then this <s>mudrā</s> is proclaimed as <s>Gadā</s> (mace [<s>mudrā</s>]).
Both palms facing each other in the shape of a lotus,
The middle fingers and thumbs laid down like the pericarp [of a lotus] —
This is called the <s>Padma</s> (lotus) [<s>mudrā</s>]; and that same [<s>mudrā</s>] with the middle fingers joined
And thumbs touching is indeed the <s>mudrā</s> named <s>Bilva</s> (wood-apple).

children.text: agre tu vāma-muṣṭeś ca itarā tu yadā matā |
children.translated_text: When the other [right hand] is placed at the front of the left fist,
Then this is the <s>mudrā</s> known by the practitioners as <s>Muṣala</s> (pestle).
The tip of the left index finger should be joined to the end of the middle finger;

children.text: prasārya tu karaṃ vāmaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ karam eva ca ||
children.translated_text: Then extending the left hand and the right hand also,
Joining [them] at the right shoulder, then in the manner of releasing an arrow,
One should perform [it] with the index finger and thumb — this is proclaimed
As the <s>Śārṅga-mudrā</s> (bow <s>mudrā</s>) by the sages; one should display [it] in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> worship.
The little finger and ring finger pressed down by the right thumb,
With the rest extended — this is proclaimed the <s>Khaḍga-mudrā</s> (sword <s>mudrā</s>).
Having fashioned the left thumb and index finger in the shape of a noose,

children.text: dakṣiṇe muṣṭim ādāya tarjanīṃ ca prasārayet ||
children.translated_text: Taking the right hand into a fist and extending the index finger,
With that very [index finger] the <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) should touch the base of the left thumb —
This is designated as the <s>Pāśa-mudrā</s> (noose <s>mudrā</s>) in the worship of <s>Keśava</s>.
Slightly curving the index finger and pressing it down with the rest,
One should display the <s>Aṅkuśa</s> (goad [<s>mudrā</s>]) likewise, grasping with the right fist.
Joining the little fingers at each other's backs, one after another,

children.text: tarjany-agraṃ samaṃ kṛtvā kaniṣṭhāgraṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: Making the tips of the index fingers level, and likewise the tips of the little fingers,

children.text: īṣad ālambitaṃ kṛtvā itarau pakṣavat tataḥ |
children.translated_text: Slightly lowering [them], and then extending the others like wings —
This is the <s>Gāruḍī-mudrā</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s> <s>mudrā</s>), remembered in the rite of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> worship.
There, the little fingers and index fingers of both hands facing each other,
And likewise the middle and ring fingers — one should press them with the thumbs.
One should carefully display this <s>mudrā</s> named <s>Śrīvatsa</s> at the heart.
Likewise, one should join the little fingers facing each other;
And likewise the index and ring fingers, with the hands at each other's backs,
Raised and joined to each other, the fingers placed at the chest;
And in the middle region, joining the left middle and index fingers

children.text: saṃyojya maṇibandhe tu dakṣiṇe yojayet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the right wrist, one should then join [them]
And in some [texts]:
The right ring finger joined at the back to the right little finger,
The little finger bound with the other [left little finger], and likewise the right index finger
At the left thumb — this <s>mudrā</s> is well known as the <s>Kaustubha</s> [<s>mudrā</s>].
Should bind the left ring finger at the base of the right thumb;
And joining the left thumb and middle finger, the remaining
Four [fingers] joined to each other — [this is] the <s>mudrā</s> named <s>Kaustubha</s>.
The left thumb placed at the lips, its little finger
Joined with the right thumb, the right little finger extended,
The index, middle, and ring fingers slightly curled and moved —
This is designated as the <s>Veṇu-mudrā</s> (flute <s>mudrā</s>), very secret, dear to <s>Hari</s>.
Extending the arm with fingers spread, O fair-faced one,

children.text: prāṅmukhaṃ tu tataḥ kṛtvā abhayaṃ parikīrtitam ||
children.translated_text: Then turning [the palm] forward — this is proclaimed as <s>Abhaya</s> (fearlessness).
Extending the right arm and placing it upon the knee,
One should display [the palm] outstretched, O goddess — this is <s>Vara</s> (the boon-granting [<s>mudrā</s>]), the accomplisher of all purposes.
With both index fingers upturned, in upward-downward sequence,
Expanding gradually like a garland — this is proclaimed the <s>Vanamālā</s> (forest-garland [<s>mudrā</s>]).
Raising the left thumb upright, then with the other hand's thumb, the bride [of <s>Kāma</s>],
Having pressed its tip with the fingers and likewise with the left hand's fingers,

children.text: baddhvā gāḍhaṃ hṛdi sthāpayatu vimala-dhīr vyāharan māra-bījaṃ
children.translated_text: Having bound firmly, the pure-minded one should place [it] at the heart while uttering the <s>kāma-bīja</s> (seed-syllable of desire) —

children.text: bilvākhyā mudrikaiṣā sphuṭam iha kathitā gopanīyā vidhijñaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: This is the <s>mudrā</s> called <s>Bilva</s>, clearly described here, to be kept secret by those who know the rules.
In the <s>Kramadīpikā</s> (2.57):
And in the <s>Agastya-Saṃhitā</s>:
'The <s>Āvāhinī</s> (invocatory), <s>Sthāpanī</s> (establishing), <s>Sannidhīkaraṇī</s> (bringing near),
The <s>Susaṃnirodhinī</s> (restraining) <s>mudrā</s>, and <s>Sammukhīkaraṇī</s> (making face-to-face),
And <s>Sakalīkaraṇī</s> (totalization), and likewise the <s>Mahā-mudrā</s> (great <s>mudrā</s>),
<s>Śaṅkha</s> (conch), <s>Cakra</s> (disc), <s>Gadā</s> (mace), <s>Padma</s> (lotus), <s>Dhenuka</s> (cow) — and the <s>Bhagāruḍhā</s> [<s>mudrā</s>s],

children.text: śrīvatsaṃ vana-mālāṃ ca yoni-mudrāṃ ca darśayet ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, <s>Vanamālā</s> (forest-garland), and <s>Yoni-mudrā</s> — one should display [these].'
'The flower-offering brought from the <s>Mūlādhāra</s> to the <s>Dvādaśānta</s> (twelfth point [above the head]),
Offered with the radiance situated at the three stations, in images and the like —
This should be the <s>Āvāhanīyā</s> (invocatory) <s>mudrā</s> in the rite of worship, O sage.
This very same [<s>mudrā</s>] turned face-downward is used again for establishing.',
'Both hands made into fists with raised thumbs —
This is the <s>mudrā</s> called <s>Sannidhīkaraṇa</s> (bringing near), in the rite of deity worship.',
'That very same [<s>mudrā</s>] with thumbs enclosed within [the fists] becomes the <s>Saṃnirodhinī</s> (restraining) <s>mudrā</s>.
A pair of fists turned palm-upward is considered the <s>Sammukhīkaraṇī</s> (face-to-face) [<s>mudrā</s>].
The installation of the limbs by the limbs themselves is likewise the <s>Sakalīkaraṇī</s> (totalization) [<s>mudrā</s>].
Both hands spread open with thumbs joined to each other —
This is declared to be the <s>Mahā-mudrā</s> (great <s>mudrā</s>), which resolves deficiency and excess.
The little finger, ring finger, and middle finger enclosed within, between the thumbs, at the front,
The fingers hidden in the middle, cupped all around
By both hands — this <s>mudrā</s> is called <s>Śaṅkha</s> (conch) in the worship of the gods.',
'By intertwining and encircling with the fingers, with mutual touching reversed,
Carefully making a circle, O sage —
This is declared as the <s>Cakra-mudrā</s> (disc <s>mudrā</s>). Then next is the <s>Gadā-mudrā</s> (mace <s>mudrā</s>):
With fingers clasped facing each other, the middle fingers raised.',
'Then, placing both thumbs in the middle and both hands surrounding [them],
Making a circle properly with the fingers, O ascetic —

children.text: padma-mudrā bhaved eṣā dhenu-mudrā tataḥ param |
children.translated_text: This is the <s>Padma-mudrā</s> (lotus <s>mudrā</s>). Then next is the <s>Dhenu-mudrā</s> (cow <s>mudrā</s>):
The ring and little fingers with the index fingers [crossed], and the middle fingers
Clasped facing each other — then the one named <s>Kaustubha</s>.
The little fingers joined to each other, facing each other mutually,
The left index and middle fingers [placed] between the middle and ring fingers,
The left ring finger touching, adorned by the index and middle fingers,
With both thumbs alternately bent — this has the characteristics of <s>Kaustubha</s>.',
'The little fingers joined to each other, separated in reverse,
Thumbs placed beneath — this is the <s>mudrā</s> named <s>Garuḍa</s>.',
'The index finger and thumb in the middle, the pair of middle and ring fingers,
The middle [finger] between the little and ring fingers, both hands at the tips of the index fingers,
O sage — this is the <s>Śrīvatsa-mudrā</s>. Then comes the <s>Vanamālā</s> (forest-garland):
A fist of little, ring, and middle fingers with the index finger raised,
Rotated at the head with both index fingers high — O celestial one,
The <s>mudrā</s> called <s>Yoni</s> is declared, with both hands contracted.',
'The pair of ring fingers situated within the index finger, thumb, and middle finger, the thumbs placed at the base of the middle fingers — this should be known in worship, O sage.'
He states the <s>astra-mantra</s> (weapon-<s>mantra</s>) — '<s>praṇava</s>' etc.:
At the end of <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ) and <s>hṛt</s> (<s>namaḥ</s>), with the dative
'<s>Sudarśana</s>' and likewise the word '<s>astra</s>' (weapon),
Having uttered [the <s>mantra</s>] ending with '<s>phaṭ</s>' — with this
<s>mantra</s>, using the <s>astra-mudrā</s> (weapon gesture), one should seal the ten directions. // Krd_2.59 //

children.text: praṇava oṃkāraḥ | hṛt namaḥ | etayor avasāne 'nte sa-caturthi-sudarśanaṃ caturthī-vibhakti-sahitaṃ sudarśanam iti padam etasyānte tathāstra-padaṃ caturthy-antam astra-padam | punaḥ kīdṛk ? phaḍ-antam phaṭ-śabdāntam uktvā amunā manunā anena mantreṇa astra-mudrayā daśa-haritaḥ kalpayet daśa-dig-bandhanaṃ kuryād ity arthaḥ || KrdC_2.59 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Praṇava</s>' is Oṃ-kāra; '<s>hṛt</s>' is <s>namaḥ</s>. At the end of these two, '<s>sa-caturthi-sudarśana</s>' means the word '<s>sudarśana</s>' with the dative case-ending; at the end of this, likewise the word '<s>astra</s>' ending in the dative case. Again, of what kind? '<s>Phaṭ-anta</s>' means ending with the sound '<s>phaṭ</s>.' Having uttered [this], with this <s>mantra</s>, using the <s>astra-mudrā</s>, one should seal the ten directions, i.e., perform the sealing of the ten directions: this is the meaning. // KrdC_2.59 //

children.text: prāk kṛtaṃ nyāsa-jātam upasaṃharan agnim apaṭale vakṣyamāṇaṃ dhyānaṃ sūcayati-itīti |
children.translated_text: Concluding the previously described collection of <s>nyāsa</s>s, he indicates the <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) to be described in the next chapter — '<s>iti</s>' etc.:
Thus, having performed the entire procedure,
Proficient in the method of creation and destruction of the universe,
Sought by the <s>Śruti</s>s (sacred texts), unborn, having the <s>mantra</s> as [his] body —
One should meditate upon the beloved of the <s>Gopa</s> (cowherd) women. // Krd_2.60 //

children.text: ity anena prakāreṇa samasta-vidhiṃ pūrvoktam akhila-nyāsādikaṃ vidhāya nirvartya gopa-vadhū-jana-vallabhaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ smaratu cintayatu | kīdṛśaṃ kṛṣṇam ? jagad-utpatti-sthiti- vināśa-karaṇa-dakṣam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? śruti-vimṛgyam upaniṣad-gamyam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? ajam utpatti-rahitam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? manu-vigrahaṃ manu-śarīram ity arthaḥ || KrdC_2.60 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in this manner, having performed the entire procedure — the previously described complete <s>nyāsa</s>s and so on — one should meditate upon, i.e., contemplate, the beloved of the <s>Gopa</s> women, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. Of what kind is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>? Proficient in the creation, preservation, and destruction of the universe. Again, of what kind? '<s>Śruti-vimṛgya</s>' means accessible through the <s>Upaniṣad</s>s. Again, of what kind? '<s>Aja</s>' means without birth, without origin. Again, of what kind? '<s>Manu-vigraha</s>' means having the <s>mantra</s> as his body: this is the meaning. // KrdC_2.60 //

Thus ends the second chapter in the <s>Kramadīpikā</s> composed by <s>Śrī Keśavācārya</s>.
||2||
(3) Third <s>Paṭala</s> (chapter)
Now he describes the <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation on the deity) common to both <s>mantra</s>s:
Now, with trees whose branches bow down under clusters of fresh blossoms and new shoots,
From which fragrant honey oozes forth with manifest sweetness,
Entwined with lovely creepers bearing fresh, blossoming flower-clusters —

children.text: smarec chiśiritaṃ śivaṃ sita-matis tu vṛndāvanam // Krd_3.1 //
children.translated_text: The pure-minded one should meditate upon <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, cool and auspicious. // Krd_3.1 //

children.text:
athānantaraṃ sita-matiḥ nirmala-matiḥ vṛndāvanaṃ smarec cintayet | kimbhūtam ? drumaiḥ vṛkṣaiḥ śiśiritaṃ śītalī-kṛtam | drumaiḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? prakaṭeti udbhaṭa-saurabham | atha ca udgalito mādhvīko madhu yasmin tat | atha ca utphullaṃ praphullam | atha ca sad-dedīpyamānam etādṛśaṃ prasūnaṃ puṣpaṃ tathā nava-pallavaḥ anayor yaḥ prakaraḥ samūhaḥ | tena namrāḥ śākhā yeṣāṃ te tathā taiḥ | prakaṭa-saurabhākulita-matta-bhṛṅgollasat-prasūneti pāṭhe prakaṭa-saurabheṇākulitaṃ sarvato vyāptam | atha ca matta-bhṛṅgollasan matta-bhramareṇa śobhamānam etādṛśaṃ yat prasūnam ity arthaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? praphullā vikasitā yā nava-mañjarī tayā lalitā manoharā yā vallarī latāgra-śākhā tasyāś ceṣṭitaṃ
calanaṃ yeṣu taiḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? śivaṃ kalyāṇa-pradam || KrdC_3.1 ||
children.translated_text: Then, the pure-minded one should meditate upon <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. Of what kind? Cooled by trees. By what kind of trees? Those with prominent [fragrance] — outstanding aroma. And moreover, from which honey flows forth. And moreover, blossoming — fully bloomed. And moreover, resplendent — brightly shining — such flowers and fresh sprouts, of which the cluster, the assemblage, causes the branches to bow down — by those [trees]. In the reading '<s>prakaṭa-saurabhākulita-matta-bhṛṅgollasatprasūna</s>': by prominent fragrance, pervaded everywhere; and moreover, made beautiful by intoxicated bees — such is the flower — this is the meaning. Again of what kind? The fresh blossom-clusters (<s>nava-mañjarī</s>) that are fully blown, whose graceful creeper-tips are in motion — by those [trees]. Again of what kind? Auspicious — bestowing welfare. // KrdC 3.1 //

children.text: sanātanaḥ: itaḥ-prabhṛti ye 36-ślokāḥ prāpyante te śrī-hari-bhakti-vilāse uddṛtāḥ śrī-sanātana-gosvāmi-prabhupādānāṃ vyākhyātāś ca | teṣāṃ vyākhyāyās tu atratyāyā nātivisādṛśyatvāt sātra noddhriyate | tatraiva te draṣṭavyāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Sanātana</s>: The 36 verses obtained hereafter have been cited in the <s>Śrī Hari-bhakti-vilāsa</s> and commented upon by <s>Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmī Prabhupāda</s>. Since their commentary is not very dissimilar to the one here, it is not reproduced here. Those [verses] should be consulted there.
Again of what kind?
With the delightful tasting of the nectar of blossoming flowers, the buzzing sounds
issuing from the mouths of roaming bees filling its interior;
with birds such as pigeons, parrots, <s>śārikā</s> (mynahs), <s>para-bhṛta</s> (cuckoos), and others
making it resound here and there, and filled with the dancing of peacocks (<s>bhujaga-śatru</s>, 'enemy of serpents'). // Krd 3.2 //

children.text: vṛndāvanaṃ jhaṅkṛtaiḥ śabda-viśeṣair mukharitāntaraṃ śabdāyamānābhyantaram | kīdṛśaiḥ ? jhaṅkṛtaiḥ vikāśinyāḥ praphullāyāḥ sumanasaḥ puṣpasya yo rasaḥ madhu tasya yad-āsvādanam avalehanaṃ tena mañjulair manoharaiḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? sañcareti sañcaranto bhramanto ye śilīmukhodgatair bhramarās teṣāṃ mukhebhya udgataiḥ samutthitaiḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? vṛndāvanaṃ kapoteti pārāvata-śuka-śārikā-kokila-prabhṛtibhiḥ pakṣibhir itas tato virāṇitaṃ śabdāyitam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? bhujaga-śatrur mayūras tasya nṛtyenākulaṃ vyāptam ||2||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndāvana</s> — its interior made resonant by buzzing sounds. By what kind of buzzing? Those that are delightful due to the tasting — the licking — of the nectar of blossoming, fully-opened flowers. Again of what kind? Issuing from the mouths of roaming, wandering bees (<s>śilīmukha</s>). Again of what kind? <s>Vṛndāvana</s> — made resound here and there by birds such as pigeons, parrots, <s>śārikā</s>s (mynahs), cuckoos (<s>kokila</s>), and others. Again of what kind? Filled with the dancing of the peacock — the enemy of serpents. // 2 //
Again of what kind?
By breezes carrying sprays from the undulating waves of the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>),
dusted with pollen from the hearts of fully-opened lotuses in lakes,
which kindle the passion of the <s>Vraja</s> beauties, fluttering their garments —
served constantly by such breezes. // Krd 3.3 //

children.text: mārutair vāyubhiḥ anārataṃ sarvadā niṣevitam | kīdṛśair mārutaiḥ ? kalindeti kalinda-duhitur yamunāyāś calantyo yā laharyaḥ tāsāṃ yā vipruṣo jala-bindavaḥ tāsāṃ vāhibhiḥ | etena vāyoḥ śaityam uktam | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? vinidreti vinidraṃ praphullaṃ yat sarasīruhaṃ padmaṃ tasya yad udaram abhyantaraṃ tatra yo rajaś cayo dhūlī-samūhaḥ tena uddhūsaraiḥ, etena saurabhyam uktam | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? pradīpiteti pradīpito 'tiśayito manobhavaḥ kāmo yāsāṃ vraja-vilāsinīnāṃ gopa-sundarīṇāṃ tāsāṃ yāni vāsāṃsi vastrāṇi teṣāṃ vilolana-paraiḥ cālanā-śaktaiḥ | etena mānyam uktam || KrdC_3.3 ||
children.translated_text: Served constantly, at all times, by breezes. By what kind of breezes? Those carrying the sprays — water-droplets — from the moving waves of the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>). By this, the coolness of the breeze is indicated. Again of what kind? Dusted with the pollen — the dust-masses — from the interior of fully-opened lotuses in the lake. By this, the fragrance is indicated. Again of what kind? Having the power to flutter the garments of the <s>Vraja</s> beauties, the cowherd maidens, whose passion (<s>manobhava</s>, desire) is kindled. By this, the gentleness is indicated. // KrdC 3.3 //
Again of what kind?
With coral-like fresh sprouts, emerald-like leaves, clusters of diamond
and pearl buds, and fruits of various <s>padmarāga</s> (ruby) [gems],
exceedingly massive, served by all seasons at all times, granting desires —

children.text: tad-antaram api kalpakāṅghripam udañcitaṃ cintayet // Krd_3.4 //
children.translated_text: in the midst of that [<s>Vṛndāvana</s>] one should also meditate upon a <s>kalpavṛkṣa</s> (wish-fulfilling tree), towering high. // Krd 3.4 //

children.text:
tad-antar api vṛndāvana-madhye kalpakāṅghripam api cintayet | kīdṛśam ? udañcitam ucchritam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? sthaviṣṭham sthūlataram | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? pravālo vidrumaḥ sa eva nava-pallavaḥ kisalayaṃ yasya tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? marakato yo maṇi-viśeṣaḥ sa eva chadaṃ patraṃ yasya tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? vajraṃ hīrakaṃ mauktikaṃ muktāḥ | anayor yaḥ prakaraḥ samūhaḥ sa eva korakaḥ puṣpa-kalikā yatra tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ?
kamala-rāgaḥ padma-rāga-maṇiḥ sa eva nānā-vidhaṃ phalaṃ yatra tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? akhilair ṛtubhiḥ ṣaḍbhir api ṛtubhiḥ satataṃ sevitaṃ sadā parigṛhītam | etena sarva-puṣpānvitatvaṃ darśitam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? kāmadam ākāṅkṣita-pradam || KrdC_3.4 ||
children.translated_text: In the midst of that <s>Vṛndāvana</s> too, one should meditate upon a <s>kalpavṛkṣa</s> (wish-fulfilling tree). Of what kind? Towering, lofty. Again of what kind? Exceedingly massive. Again of what kind? Having coral as its fresh sprouts — tender leaves. Again of what kind? Having emerald — a special gem — as its leaves. Again of what kind? Having clusters of diamonds and pearls — an assemblage of the two — as its flower-buds. Again of what kind? Having various <s>padmarāga</s> (ruby) gems as its manifold fruits. Again of what kind? Served by all six seasons at all times — constantly embraced [by them]. By this, it is shown that [the tree] has all flowers at all times. Again of what kind? Granting desires — bestowing what is wished for. // KrdC 3.4 //
Shining like the sun risen over a row of golden peaks,
beneath that [tree], a golden ground from which showers of nectar-spray [fall];
its floor set with blazing gems, brilliant with heaps of flower-pollen —

children.text: smaret punar atandrito vigata-ṣaṭtanaṅgāṃ budhaḥ // Krd_3.5 //
children.translated_text: the wise one should diligently meditate [upon this ground], free from the six waves [of worldly affliction]. // Krd 3.5 //

children.text:
budhaḥ paṇḍitaḥ atandritaḥ nirālasyaḥ ālasya-rahitaḥ san asya kalpa-vṛkṣasyādhastāt | kanaka-sthalīṃ suvarṇa-mayīṃ bhūmim | punaḥ smaret cintayet | kimbhūtāṃ suhemeti | śobhamānā suvarṇa-śṛṅga-paṅktir yasya | tathā tasmād udayācalād udita-bhānuvat prakaṭita-sūryavat prakaṭita-sūryavat bhāsvarāṃ dedīpyamānāṃ suhema-śikharācale 'py uditeti pāṭhe śobhanaṃ hema-śṛṅgaṃ yatra acale parvate tasmin api-śabdo bhinna-kramaḥ kanaka-sthalīm ity asyānantaraṃ draṣṭavyam | asya kīdṛśasya amṛteti ? amṛtasya yaḥ śīkaraḥ kaṇas tasyāsāro yaḥ samūhaḥ patanaṃ tac-chāliṃ yathā syāt tathā tasyāmṛta-kaṇa-samūha-saṃvarṣiṇaḥ | kīdṛśīm ? pradīptaiḥ pīpyamāna-maṇibhiḥ padma-rāgādibhiḥ baddha-bhūmim
| punaḥ kīdṛśīm ? kusumeti kusuma-reṇu-puñjair ujjvalām | punaḥ kīdṛśīm ? vigateti vigatā dūrībhūtā ṣaṭ-taraṅgāḥ kāma-krodhādayaḥ aśanāyāpi pāsāśoka-moha-jarā-mṛtyavo vā yasyās tām || KrdC_3.5 ||
children.translated_text: The wise, learned one, diligent, free from laziness, beneath that wish-fulfilling tree, should meditate upon a golden ground — a surface made of gold. Again, of what kind? Having a beautiful row of golden peaks, shining like the sun risen from the mountain of sunrise — blazing like the manifested sun. In the reading '<s>suhema-śikharācale 'py udita</s>': on a mountain with beautiful golden peaks, [the sun having] risen there too — the word '<s>api</s>' is in displaced order, to be read after '<s>kanaka-sthalīm</s>.' Of what kind is this [ground]? Having showers of nectar-spray, meaning raining down drops of ambrosia. Of what kind? Having a floor paved with blazing, radiant gems such as rubies and the like. Again of what kind? Brilliant with heaps of flower-pollen. Again of what kind? Free from the six waves — in which the six waves, namely desire, anger, hunger, thirst, delusion, old age, and death, are absent. // KrdC 3.5 //
On the supreme <s>yoga-pīṭha</s> (meditation seat) set upon that gem-paved floor,
having visualized an eight-petalled crimson lotus,
in its center, with the radiance of the rising sun,
one should then meditate upon <s>Mukunda</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), comfortably seated. // Krd 3.6 //

children.text: tasyāḥ kanaka-sthalyāḥ yad-ratna-kuṭṭimaṃ ratna-baddha-bhū-bhāgaḥ | tatra niviṣṭaṃ sthitaṃ mahiṣṭhaṃ mahad yoga-pīṭhaṃ tatrāṣṭa-patram aṣṭau patrāṇi yatra tat tathāruṇaṃ lohitam | ata evodyatāditya-sannibham | evambhūtaṃ padmaṃ vicintya | athānantaram amuṣyāruṇa-varṇāṣṭa-dala-kamalasya madhye mukundamṃ kṛṣṇaṃ cintayet | kīdṛśam ? sukha-niviṣṭhaṃ sukhāsīnam ādi-kulakam ata ārabhya || KrdC_3.6 ||
children.translated_text: Upon that golden ground, the gem-paved floor — the ground-surface set with gems — there, the supreme <s>yoga-pīṭha</s> (meditation seat) is set. Upon that, having visualized an eight-petalled lotus — having eight petals — crimson, red; hence like the rising sun. Having visualized such a lotus, then in the center of that crimson eight-petalled lotus, one should meditate upon <s>Mukunda</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. Of what kind? Comfortably seated — seated at ease. This is the opening verse of a series [describing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s form]. // KrdC 3.6 //
Again of what kind?
With a radiance equal to <s>Indra</s>'s sapphire, crushed collyrium, a mass of clouds,
or a freshly-bloomed dark-blue lotus;
with a mass of soft, dark, dense, curling locks of hair;
with a charming, splendid peacock-feather crest upon his head. // Krd 3.7 //

children.text: sūtrāma-ratnam indranīla-maṇiḥ dalitāñjanaṃ bhinnāñjanaṃ ghṛṣṭa-kajjalam iti megha-puñjo megha-samūhaḥ pratyagra-nīla-jalajanma navīna-nīla-padmam eṣāṃ samānā bhā dīptir yasya tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? susnigdheti susnigdhāḥ sucikkaṇā nīlāḥ śyāmā ghanā niviḍāḥ kuñcitāḥ kuṭilāḥ ye keśās teṣāṃ jālaṃ samūho yatra tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? rājann iti | rājat śobhamānaṃ manojñaṃ manoharaṃ yac-chiti-kaṇṭha-śikhaṇḍaṃ mayūra-picchaṃ tad eva cūḍāyāṃ yasya tam || KrdC_3.7 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Sūtrāma-ratna</s>' is the <s>indranīla</s> (sapphire) gem; 'crushed collyrium' means ground collyrium — rubbed kohl; 'cloud-mass' means a mass of clouds; 'fresh dark-blue water-born' means a newly-bloomed dark-blue lotus — [his] radiance is equal to these. Again of what kind? Having a mass of soft, smooth, dark, black, dense, thick, curling, wavy locks of hair. Again of what kind? With a charming, delightful peacock-feather on the crest of his head — that which has such a <s>śitikaṇṭha-śikhaṇḍa</s> (peacock-plume) as its crown. // KrdC 3.7 //
Again of what kind?
With a head-ornament fashioned from <s>Pārijāta</s> flowers of the celestial tree, attended by bees;
with ear-ornaments of fully-bloomed fresh blue lotuses (<s>utpala</s>);
with a <s>gorocanā</s> (bright yellow pigment) <s>tilaka</s> (forehead mark) gleaming on his forehead, made radiant by his dancing curls;
with gracefully arching eyebrows. // Krd 3.8 //

children.text: rolambo bhramaras tena lālitaṃ prītyā sevitaṃ yat sura-druma-prasūnaṃ pārijāta-puṣpaṃ tena kalpitaḥ racita uttaṃsaḥ śiro-bhūṣaṇaṃ yena sa tathā tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? utkacaṃ vikasitam yan navotpala-karṇa-pūram | tad eva karṇābharaṇaṃ yasya sa tathā tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? lolāś cañcalā alakāḥ keśa-viśeṣās taiḥ sphuritaṃ śobhamānaṃ yad-bhāla-talaṃ lalāṭa-talaṃ tatra pradīptaṃ gorocanā-tilakam yasya sa tathā tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? uccala- cilli-mālaṃ cañcala-bhrū-latākam || KrdC_3.8 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Rolamba</s>' is a bee; attended by it with love, a flower of the celestial tree — <s>Pārijāta</s> blossom — a head-ornament fashioned from that. Again of what kind? With fully-bloomed fresh blue lotuses as ear-ornaments — those being his ear-decorations. Again of what kind? With dancing, moving curls — special locks of hair — by which the forehead-surface is made splendid, upon which a <s>gorocanā</s> (bright yellow pigment) <s>tilaka</s> gleams. Again of what kind? With graceful, moving arched eyebrows — like creeper-tendrils. // KrdC 3.8 //
With a face beautiful as the full autumn moon's unblemished orb,
with broad eyes like lotus petals,
with cheek-surfaces [bright as] mirrors, illuminated by the rays of gem-sparkling crocodile-shaped earrings,
with a finely raised, beautiful nose. // Krd 3.9 //
Again of what kind?

children.text: āpūrṇaḥ sampūrṇaḥ śāradaḥ śarat-sambandhī gatāṅkaḥ śaśāṅka-bimbaś candra-maṇḍalas tadvat kāntaṃ manoharam ānanaṃ mukhaṃ yasya tathā tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? kamala-patravad viśāle vistīrṇe netre yasya sa tathā tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? ratneti ratnaiḥ sphuranc chobhamānaṃ yan makara-kuṇḍalaṃ makarākāra-kuṇḍalaṃ tasya ye raśmayaḥ taiḥ pradīptā śobhamānā gaṇḍa-sthalī sa eva mukuro darpaṇo yasya tathā tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? unnateti unnatā manoharā nāsā yasya sa tathā tam || KrdC_3.9 ||
children.translated_text: 'Full' means complete; 'autumnal' means belonging to autumn; the moon's orb — unblemished, without its mark — [his] face is as beautiful as that. Again of what kind? With broad, expansive eyes like lotus petals. Again of what kind? With crocodile-shaped earrings sparkling with gems, by whose rays his cheek-surfaces shine like mirrors. Again of what kind? With a raised, beautiful nose. // KrdC 3.9 //
Again of what kind?
With lips more beautiful than vermilion; with a body illuminated by the radiance
of a gentle smile [bright as] the moon, <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) flowers, and <s>mandāra</s> blossoms;
with a beautiful conch-like neck adorned with a brilliant necklace
made of a profusion of forest coral-flowers and blossoms. // Krd 3.10 //

children.text: sindūravan manoharo adharo yasya sa tathā tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? indu-kundeti induś ca kundaṃ kunda-puṣpaṃ mandāraḥ śukla-mandāraḥ arka-puṣpaṃ vā tadvan manda-hasitam īṣad-dhāsyaṃ tasya dyutir dīptiḥ tathā dīpitā śobhitā āśā diśo yena sa tathā tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? vanyeti vanyaṃ vanyodbhavaṃ yat pravāla-kusumaṃ nava-pallava-puṣpaṃ tasya yaḥ samūhas tenāvakptaṃ sampāditaṃ yad graiveyakaṃ kaṇṭhābharaṇaṃ tenojjvalo dedīpyamāno manoharaḥ kambu-kaṇṭhaḥ trirekhāṅkitaḥ kaṇṭho yasya sa tathā tam || KrdC_3.10 ||
children.translated_text: With lips as beautiful as vermilion. Again of what kind? The moon, <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) flowers, and white <s>mandāra</s> (sun-flower) blossoms — a gentle smile like those, whose radiance illuminates the directions — [he has] a body thus illuminated. Again of what kind? With a brilliant, splendid, beautiful conch-shaped neck — marked with three lines — adorned with a necklace fashioned from a profusion of forest-born coral-flowers and tender blossom-sprouts. // KrdC 3.10 //
Again of what kind?
With shoulders adorned by dangling garlands of <s>Santāna</s> (celestial) and <s>Campaka</s> flowers,
frequented by intoxicated bees;
with a broad chest adorned by rows of pearl necklaces like constellations,
with the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem shining like the sun upon the expanse of his chest. // Krd 3.11 //

children.text: mattāḥ kṛta-madhu-pānā bhramantaś carantau ye bhramarās tair juṣṭaṃ sevitam | atha ca vilambamānam evambhūtaṃ yat-santāna-kapra-sava-dāma kalpa-vṛkṣa-puṣpa-dāma tena dāmnā pariṣkṛtaḥ svalaṅkṛto aṃso yasya sa tathā tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? hārāvaly eva bhagaṇo nakṣatra-samūhaḥ | tena rājitaṃ śobhitaṃ pīvaraṃ māṃsalaṃ yad-uro hṛdayaṃ tad eva vyoma-sthala ākāśa-bhūmiḥ tayā lasitaḥ śobhitaḥ kaustubha eva bhānuḥ sūryas tena yuktam | atra rūpakālaṅkāra eva nopamālaṅkāraḥ nakṣatra-gaṇa-sūryayor asambandhatvāt | evaṃ ca saty eka-kāle dvayoḥ śobhā labhyata iti bhāvaḥ || KrdC_3.11 ||
children.translated_text: Intoxicated bees, having drunk honey, wandering about — by these [bees], frequented, attended upon. And further, the garland of <s>kalpa-vṛkṣa</s> (wish-fulfilling tree) flowers — such a garland of wish-fulfilling tree blossoms, hanging low — by that garland, adorned is the shoulder of him who is so. Again, of what kind? The cluster of stars (<s>nakṣatra</s>s) is like a necklace-string; by that, resplendent is the broad, fleshy chest — that very [chest] is the expanse of the sky; shining therein is the <s>Kaustubha</s> [gem], which is the sun — endowed with that. Here the figure of speech is <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), not <s>upamā</s> (simile), since the constellation-group and the sun are [presented as] non-different. And thus, the beauty of both [realms] is obtained at one time — this is the import. (KrdC 3.11)
Again, of what kind?
Well-marked with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> sign, with elevated shoulders,
With arms reaching to the knees — stout, well-rounded, and finely-formed;
With a belly [slender] down to the waist, with a noble and deep navel,
With a charming line of body-hair [resembling] a cluster of female bees. (Krd 3.12)

children.text: śrīvatsa-lakṣaṇa-sulakṣitam unnatāṃsam ājānu-pīna-parivṛtta-sujāta-bāhum ābandhurodaram udāra-gambhīra-nābhiṃ bhṛṅgāṅganā-nikara-mañjula-roma-rājim || KrdC_3.12 ||
children.translated_text: Well-marked with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> sign, with elevated shoulders, with arms reaching to the knees — stout, well-rounded, and finely-formed, with a belly [slender] down to the waist, with a noble and deep navel, with a charming line of body-hair [resembling] a cluster of female bees. (KrdC 3.12)
Again, of what kind?
With armlets, bracelets, finger-rings studded with various gems,
Neck-ornament, girdle with [small bells], anklets, and a waist-band;
With limbs anointed with a divine unguent of two kinds,
With hips encased in deeply yellow garments. (Krd 3.13)

children.text: nānā-maṇibhir indranīlādibhir ghaṭitāḥ sambaddhāḥ | aṅgadā bāhu-valayās tathā kaṅkaṇā ūrmir mudrikā graiveyaṃ grīvālaṅkāraḥ rasanayā kṣudra-ghaṇṭikayā saha āsamantāt vartate yau nūpurau tunda-bandhaḥ udara-bandhanārthaṃ suvarṇa-ḍorakam ete alaṅkārā yasya sa tathā tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? divyaḥ paramotkṛṣṭo yo 'nurāgaḥ sugandhi-cūrṇaṃ tena piñjaritā nānā-varṇā aṅga-yaṣṭi-raṅga-latā yasya sa tathā tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? āpītam atiśayena pītaṃ yad vastraṃ tena parito vīto veṣṭito nitamba-bimbo yena sa tathā tam | yadyapi strī-kaṭyāṃ nitamba-pada-prayogaḥ kośe dṛśyate tathāpi tadvan manoharatayā puṃskaṭyām api prayogo na viruddhaḥ || KrdC_3.13 ||
children.translated_text: 'Studded with various gems' — fashioned, bound together, with gems such as sapphires etc. '<s>Aṅgada</s>' — arm-bands; '<s>kaṅkaṇa</s>' — bracelets; '<s>ūrmi</s>' — finger-ring; '<s>graiveya</s>' — neck-ornament; with a girdle along with small bells; '<s>nūpura</s>' — anklets extending all around; '<s>tunda-bandha</s>' — a golden cord for binding the belly — these are the ornaments of him who is so. Again, of what kind? The divine — supremely excellent — fragrant powder, by which the body-limb, the vine-like figure, is made variegated in color — of him who is so. Again, of what kind? '<s>Āpīta</s>' — exceedingly yellow — the garment by which the hip is completely wrapped — of him who is so. Although the word '<s>nitamba</s>' is seen in dictionaries used for women's hips, nevertheless, on account of [his] similar captivating beauty, its use for the male hip is not contradictory. (KrdC 3.13)
Again, of what kind?
With beautiful thighs and knees, with well-rounded, lovely shanks,
With beautiful, elevated forefeet that put to shame the beauty of a tortoise;
With a row of toenails gleaming like ruby mirrors, with resplendent
Reddish toes [like] petals — [having such] beautiful lotus-feet. (Krd 3.14)

children.text: kāntau kamanīyau unnatau uccau yau prapadau pādāgrau tābhyāṃ ninditā tiraskṛtā kūrmasya kacchapasya kāntiḥ dīptir yena sa tathā tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? māṇikya-ghaṭito yo darpaṇas tadval lasantī śobhamānā nakha-paṅktiḥ tathā rājantyaḥ śobhamānā yā raktāṅgulayas tā eva cchadanāni patrāṇi taiḥ sundaraṃ pāda-padmaṃ yasya sa tathā tam || KrdC_3.14 ||
children.translated_text: The forefeet — the front of the feet — which are beautiful and elevated, by which the luster of the tortoise is put to shame, surpassed — of him who is so. Again, of what kind? A mirror fashioned of rubies — gleaming like that is the row of toenails, and resplendent, shining are the reddish toes — those very [toes are like] petals; by these, beautiful are the lotus-feet — of him who is so. (KrdC 3.14)
Again, of what kind?
With soles of the feet — reddish, charming — marked with [the signs of]
Fish, goad, discus, conch, banner, barleycorn, lotus, and thunderbolt;
Whose limbs are fashioned from the entire essence of grace,
Whose bodily beauty surpasses that of <s>Manobhava</s> (Kāmadeva, the god of love). (Krd 3.15)
