children.text: matsyo mīnaḥ aṅkuśo astra-viśeṣaḥ ariś cakro daraḥ śaṅkhaḥ ketur dhvajaḥ yavaḥ prasiddhaḥ abjaṃ padmaṃ vajraḥ kuliśākāras trikoṇaḥ etaiḥ sulakṣitaṃ samyak vihitaṃ yad aruṇatarāṅghri-talaṃ lohitatara-caraṇa-talaṃ tenābhirāmaḥ sarva-jana-priyas tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? lāvaṇyasya saundaryasya yaḥ sāra-samudāya utkṛṣṭa-bhāga-samudāyaḥ tena vinirmitaṃ ghaṭitaṃ yad aṅga-saundaryaṃ tena ninditā tiraskṛtā manobhavasya kāmadevasya kāntiḥ śarīra-śobhā yena sa tathoktam || KrdC_3.15 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Matsya</s>' — fish; '<s>aṅkuśa</s>' — a special weapon [goad]; '<s>ari</s>' — discus; '<s>dara</s>' — conch; '<s>ketu</s>' — banner; '<s>yava</s>' — the well-known [barleycorn]; '<s>abja</s>' — lotus; '<s>vajra</s>' — triangular thunderbolt-shape. By these, well-marked — properly endowed — are the exceedingly reddish soles of the feet, the very red soles — by which he is pleasing to all people, of him who is so. Again, of what kind? The entire collection of the finest essence of grace (<s>lāvaṇya</s>) — the aggregate of the most excellent portions of beauty — by that is fashioned, composed, the beauty of the limbs; by that, surpassed — put to shame — is the bodily splendor of <s>Manobhava</s> (<s>Kāmadeva</s>, the god of love) — of him who is thus described. (KrdC 3.15)
Again, of what kind?
Through the holes of the flute filled by [his] lotus-mouth,
With divine melodies produced by the playful movement of [his] fingers;
Perpetually melting, drawing toward [him] the entire succession
Of generations of all living beings — an ocean of infinite bliss. (Krd 3.16)

children.text: śaśvan nityaṃ dravī-kṛtānayatī-kṛtā vikṛṣṭā ākṛṣṭā samasta-jantoḥ prāṇinaḥ santāna-santatiḥ santāna-paramparā yena sa tathā tam | kaiḥ ? āsyam evāravindaṃ padmaṃ tena paripūritaṃ yad veṇu-randhraṃ vaṃśī-randhram atra lolantī cañcalā yā karāṅgulis tayā samīritāḥ samutpāditā ye divyā utkṛṣṭā rāgā dhvanayaḥ svarās tair ity arthaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? ananteti | aparimitānanda-samudram || KrdC_3.16 ||
children.translated_text: 'Perpetually' — constantly; 'melted' — made to dissolve, 'drawn' — attracted, the continuous succession of generations of all living beings — by whom he is so. By what [means]? The mouth itself is a lotus — by that [lotus-mouth] the holes of the flute (<s>vaṃśī</s>) are filled; there the playful, moving fingers produce — generate — divine, exquisite melodies, sounds, musical notes — by these, this is the meaning. Again, of what kind? '<s>Ananta</s>' — an ocean of immeasurable bliss. (KrdC 3.16)
Again, of what kind?
By cows whose eyes are fixed upon [his] lotus-face,
Moving slowly, stumbling under the weight of [their] heavy udders;
With grass-shoots remaining [half-eaten], bitten by the tips of [their] teeth,
With dangling tail-creepers — thus surrounded. (Krd 3.17)

children.text: athānantaraṃ gobhir abhivītaṃ sarvato-veṣṭitam | kimbhūtābhiḥ ? mukhāmbuje parameśvara-mukha-padme vilīne sambadde locane yāsāṃ tās tathā tābhiḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśābhiḥ ? ūdhobhareti stana-gaurava-skhalana-sālasālpa-gamana-śīlābhiḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśābhiḥ ? dantāgreṇa daṣṭaḥ pariśiṣṭa-tṛṇāṅkuro bhakṣaṇāvaśiṣṭa-tṛṇāṅkuro yābhis tās tathā tābhiḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśābhiḥ ? ālambīti ālambinī lambamānā vāladhi-latā yāsāṃ tās tathā tābhiḥ || KrdC_3.17 ||
children.translated_text: Then — next — surrounded on all sides by cows. Of what quality [are they]? Those whose eyes are fixed, merged upon the lotus-face of the Supreme Lord — by such [cows]. Again, of what kind? Stumbling from the weight of [their] udders — moving slowly, sluggishly, with a languid gait — by such [cows]. Again, of what kind? Those with grass-shoots remaining — remnants of eating left [half-chewed] — bitten by the tips of [their] teeth — by such [cows]. Again, of what kind? Those whose tail-creepers hang down, dangling — by such [cows]. (KrdC 3.17)
Again, of what kind?
By calves whose mouths are full and still from sucking at lactating teats,
From whose [mouths] frothy milk trickles — [calves] charming [in appearance];
And also by calves whose ears are raised upward, attentive to the captivating,
Deep-toned song produced by the flute. (Krd 3.18)

children.text: tarṇakaiś caika-vārṣikaiś cābhivītam iti pūrveṇānvayaḥ | kīdṛśaiḥ ? prasraveṇa kṣarad-dugdhena saha vartate yat stana-vicūṣaṇaṃ dantoṣṭhena stanākarṣaṇaṃ tena paripūrṇo niścalaḥ sthiraś ca ya āsyāvaṭaḥ mukha-vivaraṃ tataḥ kṣaritaṃ galitaṃ yat phenilaṃ sa-phenaṃ dugdhaṃ tena mugdhair manoharaiḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? veṇv iti | veṇur vaṃśī tena pravartitā cālitā manoharā āhlāda-kāriṇī mandrānalpā yā gītir gānaṃ tatra dattam uccaṃ karṇa-yugalaṃ yais tathā taiḥ || KrdC_3.18 ||
children.translated_text: 'By calves' — year-old calves — 'also surrounded' — this connects with the previous [verse]. Of what kind [are they]? From sucking at the teat along with flowing milk, the mouth-cavity is full and still — from that trickles, drips, frothy, foam-laden milk — by such charming, delightful [calves]. Again, of what kind? The flute (<s>vaṃśī</s>) — by that is produced, set in motion, a captivating, delightful, deep — not faint — song, singing — toward which their pair of ears is raised high — by such [calves]. (KrdC 3.18)
Again, of what kind?
By young bulls and heifers — with butting of soft heads on fresh horns,
With excited prancing, with unsteady hoof-tips striking [the ground];
Plump, with abundant dewlaps at the throat, with tails held
Erect — by such groups of young bulls and heifers. (Krd 3.19)

children.text: vatsataraḥ traivārṣiko balīvardaḥ | vatsatarī traivarṣikī gauḥ | etayor nikāyaiḥ samūhaiḥ pratyagraṃ navīnaṃ śṛṅgaṃ yasminn evambhūtaṃ yat mṛdu mastakaṃ tatra yaḥ samprahāraḥ abhighātaḥ anya-vatsatarasya yudhyataḥ tena yaḥ saṃrambhaḥ krodhātiśayas tena yad valganam itas tato vicalanaṃ tena vilolaḥ anavasthitaḥ khurāgra-pāto yeṣāṃ te tathā taiḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? āmeduraiḥ susnigdhaiḥ puṣṭair iti vā | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? bahulātiśayitā sāsnā yatra sa evambhūto galo yeṣāṃ te tathā taiḥ | sāsnā ca gala-kambalaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? udagra-pucchaiḥ || KrdC_3.19 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Vatsatara</s>' — a three-year-old bull. '<s>Vatsatarī</s>' — a three-year-old cow. By the groups of these: fresh, new horns — on which are soft heads — therein the butting, striking [by] another young bull fighting — from that, the excessive agitation, by which the prancing — moving here and there — [causes] unsteady, unstable hoof-tip falls — by such [animals]. Again, of what kind? '<s>Āmedura</s>' — very sleek, or well-nourished. Again, of what kind? With exceedingly large dewlaps at the throat — of such [animals]; the '<s>sāsnā</s>' is the throat-flap (dewlap). Again, of what kind? With erect tails. (KrdC 3.19)
Again, of what kind?
By great bulls too, whose lowing shakes the circle of the quarters,
Wearied by the weight of [their] broad humps;
With ear-flaps raised, drinking in the nectar-sound of the flute,
With wide, expanding nostrils uplifted [in delight]. (Krd 3.20)

children.text: mahadbhir ukṣabhir balīvardair apy abhivītam | kīdṛśaiḥ ? hambā-raveṇa svara-viśeṣeṇa kṣubhitaḥ kṣobhaṃ prāpito dig-valayo dik-samūho yais te tathā taiḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? pṛthur atiśayito yaḥ kakudbharaḥ apara-gala-bharaḥ sa eva bhāras tena khinnaiḥ alasaiḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? uttambhiteti ūrdhvaṃ stambhitā utthāpitā yā śruti-puṭī tayā paripītam atiśayena śrutaṃ yad vaṃśasya dhvānāmṛtaṃ śabda-rūpāmṛtaṃ tenodvṛttā ūrdhvaṃ prāpitā vikāśinī prasphuṭā viśālā dīrghā ghoṇā nāsā yeṣāṃ te tathā taiḥ || KrdC_3.20 ||
children.translated_text: By great bulls — oxen — also surrounded. Of what kind [are they]? Whose lowing — a particular sound — agitates, disturbs the circle of the quarters, the whole compass of directions — by such [bulls]. Again, of what kind? By the exceedingly broad hump — the back-neck burden — wearied, languid from that weight. Again, of what kind? The ear-flaps are raised upward, propped up — through them is deeply drunk the nectar-sound of the flute — the nectar in the form of sound — by which the nostrils are uplifted, raised, expanding, wide-open, broad — of such [bulls]. (KrdC 3.20)
Again, of what kind?
By <s>gopa</s>s (cowherds) of equal qualities, temperament, age, playfulness,
And attire, with flutes and <s>vīṇā</s>s producing modulated sweet tones;
Devoted to deep and high, clear singing, skilled in performing
Graceful dance with swaying arm-creepers. (Krd 3.21)

children.text: gopaiś cābhivītam | kīdṛśaiḥ ? samāneti guṇa udayādiḥ śīlaṃ dhairyādi vayo bālyādi vilāsaḥ krīḍanaṃ veśaḥ saṃsthāna-viśeṣaḥ samānāḥ tulyāḥ guṇa-śīlādayo yeṣāṃ te tathā taiḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? mūrcchāṃ prāpitaḥ kalo 'vyakta-madhuraḥ svaro rāgo yatra veṇuś ca vīnā ca | veṇu-vīṇair mūrcchita-kala-svare veṇu-vīṇe yeṣāṃ taiḥ tathā | tad uktam-
children.translated_text: By <s>gopa</s>s (cowherds) also — surrounded. Of what kind? '<s>Samāna</s>' — qualities such as excellence etc., temperament such as fortitude etc., age such as childhood etc., playfulness — sport, attire — particular mode of dress — [all] equal, the same — by those whose qualities, temperament, etc. are thus the same. Again, of what kind? '<s>Mūrcchā</s>' — [the tones] having attained <s>mūrchanā</s> (modulation), an indistinct-sweet sound, a musical mode — in the flute and <s>vīṇā</s>; by those whose flutes and <s>vīṇā</s>s have modulated sweet tones. As it is said:
'Where the musical note, having been modulated, attains the quality of a melodic mode (<s>rāga</s>) —

children.text: mūrchanām iti tāṃ prāhuḥ kavayo grāma-sambhavām |
children.translated_text: That the learned call <s>mūrchanā</s> (modulation), born of the musical scale (<s>grāma</s>);

children.text: sapta-svarās trayo grāmā mūrchanās tv eka-viṃśatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: There are seven notes, three scales, and indeed twenty-one <s>mūrchanā</s>s.'

children.text: punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? mandrocceti mandraṃ nīcaiḥ uccam atiśāyitaṃ tāro yati-viśeṣas tena paṭu spaṣṭaṃ yad gānaṃ tat-parais tad-āsaktaiḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? viloleti vilolā yā dor-vallarī bāhu-latā tayā yal lalitaṃ manoharaṃ lāsyaṃ nṛtyaṃ tasya vidhānaṃ karaṇaṃ tatra dakṣaiḥ kuśalaiḥ || KrdC_3.21 ||
children.translated_text: Again, of what kind? '<s>Mandra</s>' — deep, low; '<s>ucca</s>' — exceedingly high '<s>tāra</s>' — a particular tempo; by that, clear, distinct singing — devoted to that, absorbed in it. Again, of what kind? The swaying arm-creepers — by which graceful, charming <s>lāsya</s> (dance) — its performance, execution — in that, skilled, accomplished. (KrdC 3.21)
Again, of what kind?
By children walking about, with jingling bell-clusters tied
To the fleshy waist-region near the shanks, swaying [as they move];
Charming, with tiger-claw necklaces fashioned as throat-ornaments,
With indistinct, sweet speech — surrounded by such toddlers. (Krd 3.22)

children.text: pṛthukair bālakaiḥ parītaṃ veṣṭitam | kīdṛśaiḥ ? jaṅghā-samīpe pīvarā māṃsalā yā kaṭīra-taṭī kaṭī-sthalī tasyāṃ nibaddhā vyālolā cañcalā yā kiṅkiṇi-ghaṭā kāñcī-samūhaḥ, tasya raṭitaiḥ śabdair aṭadbhiḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? mugdhair manoharaiḥ | punaḥ kimbhūtaiḥ ? tarakṣu-nakhena vyāghra-nakhena kalpitā sampāditā kaṇṭha-bhūṣā kaṇṭhālaṅkāro yais te tathā taiḥ | bālakānāṃ rakṣārthaṃ kaṇṭhe vyāghra-nakha-bandhanaṃ kriyate yataḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ?
avyaktam aspaṣṭam atha ca mañjulaṃ manoharam evambhūtaṃ vacanaṃ yeṣāṃ te tathā taiḥ || KrdC_3.22 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Avyakta</s>' — indistinct, and yet '<s>mañjula</s>' — charming, delightful — such speech of those [children] — by such [toddlers]. (KrdC 3.22)

By toddlers — small children — surrounded, encircled. Of what kind? At the shank-region, the fleshy waist-area — on that are tied swaying, jingling bell-clusters — a group of small bells forming a girdle — by the sound of these, walking about. Again, of what kind? Charming, delightful. Again, of what nature? With tiger-claw — by a tiger's claw — fashioned, made throat-ornaments — of such [children]. Since for the protection of children, the tying of tiger claws at the throat is done. Again, of what kind?
Again, of what kind?
Now, of the graceful, beautiful <s>gopī</s> women —
Of those [gopīs] with broad, firm, and massive hips, [making them] slow in movement;
Clinging to [their bodies are] three folds [of skin] bent by the weight of heavy breasts,
With a line of hair sprouting [along] the expanded [belly]. [Krd 3.23]

children.text: athānantaraṃ manohara-gopa-strīṇām ālībhiḥ paṅktibhiḥ samantāt sarvataḥ satataṃ nitya-sevitam ity aṣṭama-ślokenānvayaḥ | kimbhūtānām ? pṛthu bṛhan nivirīṣo niviḍo yo nitambaḥ kaṭi-paścād-bhāgaḥ, tena mantharāṇāṃ gamanāśaktānām | punaḥ kimbhūtānām ? gurur atiśayito yaḥ kuca-bharaḥ stana-gauravaṃ tena bhaṅguram īṣan nāṃ yad avalagnaṃ madhya-pradeśaḥ tatra yad-bali-trayaṃ tatra vijṛmbhitā vitatā roma-paṅktir yāsāṃ tāsām || KrdC_3.23 ||
children.translated_text: Then next — of the enchanting cowherd women, by their rows of companions, from all sides, constantly, perpetually attended — this connects with the eighth verse. Of what kind? 'Broad' means large; 'firm' means dense; the 'hip' is the posterior part of the waist — made slow, i.e., unable to walk, by that [heaviness]. Again, of what kind? 'Heavy' means excessive; the 'breast-weight' is the heaviness of the bosom — by that, slightly bent is the 'middle region' (waist); there, the three folds; there, the extended line of hair — of those [women] who possess such [features]. [Commentary on Krd 3.23]
Again, of what kind?
By the exceedingly sweet and beautiful flute-music of that [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] —
The nectar-sap causing the sprouting of the desire-tree at their feet;
With clusters of buds [i.e., goosebumps], lovely, with raised hair-
Rising, adorning the creeper-like limbs [of those gopīs]. [Krd 3.24]

children.text: tasya śrī-kasyātimadhuraṃ atiprīti-dāyakaṃ cāru manoharaṃ yad veṇu-vādyāṃ vaṃśī-ravaḥ sa evāmṛta-rasaḥ amṛta-rūpa-jalaṃ tena pallavito vṛddhy-unmukhaḥ aṅgajāṅghripaḥ kāma-vṛkṣo yāsāṃ tās tathā tāsām | aṅgajāṅghripasyeti pāṭhaḥ | punaḥ kimbhūtānām ? mukula-visaraḥ kalikā-samūhaḥ tadvad ramyo manoharo yo rūḍha upacito romodgamo romotthānaṃ tena samalaṅkṛtā gātra-vallarī deha-latā yāsāṃ tās tathā tāsām || KrdC_3.24 ||
children.translated_text: Of that blessed one — his exceedingly sweet, supremely delightful, beautiful, enchanting flute-music — that itself is the nectar-sap, nectar-like water; by that, sprouting, i.e., growing, is the desire-tree at [their] feet — of those [women] who have such [a condition]. The reading '<s>aṅgajāṅghripasya</s>' [is also found]. Again, of what kind? 'Clusters of buds' — a mass of flower-buds; similarly lovely, beautiful, the raised hair-rising, i.e., the standing up of body-hair — by that adorned is the body-creeper, the vine-like body — of those [women] who possess such [features]. [Commentary on Krd 3.24]
Again, of what kind?
By the exceedingly beautiful gentle smile of that [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], like moonlight —
The ocean of passion, expanded by [that] radiance, with its
Exceedingly restless waves, [producing] spray-like
Drops — [of those gopīs] covered with drops of perspiration resembling those. [Krd 3.25]

children.text: tasya kṛṣṇasyātimanoharo ya īṣad-dhāsaḥ sa eva candra-raśmis tena parijṛmbhita ucchalito yo rāga-samudras tasyāticañcalo yas taraṅgaḥ kallolaḥ tadīyā ye jala-kaṇāḥ teṣāṃ yaḥ samūhas tena samas tulyo yaḥ śrama-bindur gharma-jala-binduḥ tena santatānāṃ vyāptānām || KrdC_3.25 ||
children.translated_text: Of that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — the exceedingly beautiful gentle smile, that itself is the moonbeam; by that, expanded, i.e., surging, is the ocean of passion; its exceedingly restless waves, billows — their water-droplets, whose mass is similar, i.e., equal to the drops of perspiration, sweat-droplets — of those [women] pervaded, i.e., covered by those. [Commentary on Krd 3.25]
Again, of what kind?
By the exceedingly graceful, gently [arched] eyebrow-bow of that [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>],
By the rain of <s>Kāma</s>'s (Love-god's) arrows — the sharp side-glances fallen [from it] —
With all vital points shattered, limbs trembling,
Afflicted by unbearable trembling spread [throughout their bodies]. [Krd 3.26]

children.text: tasya śrī-kṛṣṇasyātimanoharo mandaḥ anatidīrgho yaś cilli-cāpo bhrū-latā saiva dhanus tasmād udgataṃ tīkṣṇaṃ kaṭākṣaḥ sa eva kāma-bāṇas tasya vṛṣṭyātyanta-pātena dalitaṃ cūrṇitaṃ yat sakalaṃ marma tenānāyattaṃ yad aṅgaṃ tatra prasṛtā vyāptā duḥsahā kampa-vedanā yāsāṃ tās tathā tāsām || KrdC_3.26 ||
children.translated_text: Of that blessed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — the exceedingly beautiful, gentle, not overly long eyebrow-creeper, that itself is the bow; from that, the sharp [glance], the side-glance, that itself is <s>Kāma</s>'s arrow; by its rain, i.e., excessive falling — shattered, crushed are all the vital points; thereby uncontrolled are the limbs; there, the spread, pervasive, unbearable trembling-pain — of those [women] who are thus. [Commentary on Krd 3.26]
Again, of what kind?
Of that [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] — the exceedingly beautiful actions, form, and splendor —
Eager in the practice of drinking [their] nectar-essence,
Of those [gopīs] whose [eyes are] rivers carrying a flood of love-waters,
With languid, tremulous lotus-eyes. [Krd 3.27]

children.text: praṇayenaiva premṇaiva yo jala-pravāhas taṃ vahanti yās tathā tāsām | kābhyām ? lajjādinārdha-nimīlita-padmalocanābhyāṃ sa-vilāsa-cañcalita-netra-padmābhyām ity api pāṭhaḥ | kimbhūtānām ? tasya parameśvarasyātiruciraṃ yat karma śṛṅgāra-ceṣṭā-viśeṣaḥ rūpa-śobhā kāminī-mano-rañjikā kāntiḥ te evāmṛta-rasau tayor yat pānam atyanta-cakṣur-vyāpāras tat-karaṇe sākāṅkṣābhyām | subhaga-kamreti pāṭhāntaram | subhagaḥ sundaraḥ kamraḥ kamanīyaḥ subhaga-kamanīyayor eka-paryāyayor grahaṇam adbhutatvād rūpasyeti tripāṭhinaḥ || KrdC_3.27 ||
children.translated_text: By love itself, by affection itself, the flood of water — those [gopīs] who carry that, of them. By which [eyes]? By [their] half-closed lotus eyes due to shyness and the like; the reading 'with playfully trembling lotus-eyes' is also found. Of what kind? Of that Supreme Lord — the exceedingly beautiful actions, i.e., special amorous gestures, the beauty of form, i.e., the radiance that enchants the minds of lovers — these two are themselves the nectar-essences; their drinking, i.e., the constant activity of the eyes [in gazing] — eager in accomplishing that. The alternate reading is '<s>subhaga-kamra</s>' — '<s>subhaga</s>' means beautiful, '<s>kamra</s>' means charming; the grasping of 'beautiful' and 'charming' as synonyms is due to the wonderfulness of [his] form, according to the Tripāṭhins. [Commentary on Krd 3.27]
Again, of what kind?
With loosening braids, from which fall full-blown flowers, dripping
Honey — [those gopīs] constantly attended by swarms of bees greedy for that [honey];
With soft speech faltering from the intoxication of love-madness; with swaying girdles, heaving
[And] loosening the knot of Chinese silk garments, revealing the luster of [their] hips. [Krd 3.28]

children.text: viśraṃsan skhalan yaḥ keśa-pāśas tasmāt prabhraṃśyad yad vikasitaṃ puṣpaṃ tasmād galantī yā mādhvī puṣpa-rasaḥ tatrātyantāsakto yaś cañcarīko bhramaras tasya samūhena muhur vāraṃ vāraṃ saṃsevitānām | punaḥ kim-bhūtānāṃ māreti |
children.translated_text: The loosening, i.e., slipping, hair-braid — from that, the falling full-blown flowers; from those, the dripping honey, the nectar of flowers — there, the extremely attached bees, the <s>cañcarīka</s>s (black bees); by their swarms, again and again attended. Again, of what kind — beginning with '<s>māra</s>' —

children.text: kāma-kṛtonmādena yā mattatā tayā skhalantī aspaṣṭā mṛdvī komalā manoharā gīrvāṇī yāsāṃ tās tathā tāsām unmāda-madau śṛṅgāra-viśeṣau | tad uktaṃ śṛṅgāra-tilake-
children.translated_text: The intoxication produced by passion (<s>Kāma</s>) — by that state of inebriation, the faltering, indistinct, soft, delicate, enchanting speech — of those [women] who have such [speech]. '<s>Unmāda</s>' and '<s>mada</s>' are special varieties of the erotic sentiment (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>). Thus it is stated in the <s>Śṛṅgāra-tilaka</s> —
'Where activity arises through heavy breathing, weeping, trembling,

children.text: vyāpāro jāyate yatra sa unmādaḥ smṛto yathā ||
children.translated_text: And manifold gazing — that is remembered as <s>unmāda</s> (love-madness).'

children.text: evaṃ madasyāpi lakṣaṇaṃ boddhavyam iti kecit | punaḥ kīdṛśīnām ? ālolā cañcalā yā kāñcī-rasanā tathā ucchvasantī dṛḍhā bhavantī yā nīvī vastra-granthiḥ | nīvī strī-vasana-granthāv iti koṣāt | tayā viślathamānaṃ cīna-sicayaṃ cīna-deśotpannaṃ sūkṣma-vastraṃ tasyānte madhye āviḥ prakaṭā nitamba-tviṭ nitamba-kāntir yāsāṃ tās tathā tāsām || KrdC_3.28 ||
children.translated_text: Similarly, the definition of <s>mada</s> (intoxication) should be understood, according to some. Again, of what kind? The swaying, restless girdle-belt; and the tightened, firm knot of the garment-tie — '<s>nīvī</s>' is the knot of a woman's garment, according to the lexicon; by that, the loosening Chinese silk garment — silk cloth produced in China, a fine fabric; at its end, in the middle, the visible, manifest luster of the hips — of those [women] who possess such [features]. [Commentary on Krd 3.28]
Again, of what kind?
With stumbling, graceful lotus-feet, by the gentle impact [of whose steps]
The tinkling jeweled anklets fill the directions with sound;
With quivering lower lips, with budding, lash-fringed eye-
Pairs [like] lotuses in a lake, with flashing earrings. [Krd 3.29]

children.text: skhalitam anāyattaṃ lalitaṃ manoharaṃ yat pāda-padmaṃ tasya yo manda īṣad abhighātaḥ ābhighāta-kvaṇita-maṇi-tulākoṭyākulāśā-mukhānām calad-adhara-dalānāṃ kuḍmalat-pakṣmalākṣi-dvaya-sarasi-ruhaṇām ullasat-kuṇḍalānām || KrdC_3.29 ||
children.translated_text: Stumbling, unsteady, graceful, enchanting lotus-feet — [Commentary on Krd 3.29]
Again, of what kind?
With lips like red shoots, wilting from the heat
Of the wind of the longest sighs;
With lotus-hands radiant with various gifts —
[Those gopīs] by whose rows of companions [it is] constantly attended from all sides. [Krd 3.30]

children.text: dīrgho yaḥ śvāsa-vāyus tena yo 'bhitāpaḥ tena pramlānī-bhavan raktauṣṭha-pallavo yāsāṃ tās tathā tāsām | punaḥ kimbhūtānām ? vividhopāyanena śobhamānāni hasta-kamalāni yāsāṃ tās tathā tāsām || KrdC_3.30 ||
children.translated_text: The long breath-wind — by its heat, the wilting red lip-shoots — of those [women] who have such. Again, of what kind? With lotus-hands shining with various offerings — of those [women] who have such. [Commentary on Krd 3.30]
Again, of what kind [is the place]?
Of those [gopīs] — with garlands of expanded blue lotuses [resembling their] long, restless, dark eyes,
His entire body fully worshipped, [that place being] the abode of manifold amorous sports;
Bearing a delightful garland of honey-bees — the love-intoxicated eyes —
Tasting the nectar flowing from their innocent lotus-faces. [Krd 3.31]

children.text: mukundaṃ tāsāṃ gopa-sundarīṇām āyataṃ dīrghaṃ lolaṃ cañcalaṃ nīlaṃ śyāmaṃ yan nayanaṃ tad eva vyākośaṃ nīlotpalaṃ praphullaṃ nīlāmbujaṃ teṣāṃ sragbhir mālābhiḥ samparipūjitā adhikataram arcitā sakalā tanur yasya sa tathā tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? vividha-vilāsa-sthānam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? tan-mugdhānaneti tāsāṃ yan manoharaṃ mukhaṃ tad eva padma-samūhas tasmāt vigalan sravan yo mādhvī-raso makarandaḥ tam āsvādayituṃ śīlaṃ yasyāḥ tām praṇayena prītyā udgata-madaṃ yad akṣi-yugalaṃ saiva bhramara-mālā paṅktis tāṃ manohāriṇīṃ bibhrāṇam || KrdC_3.31 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mukunda</s> — of those beautiful cowherd women, the long, restless, dark eyes — those themselves are the expanded, fully-bloomed blue lotuses; with garlands of those, his entire body is supremely worshipped — him whose whole body is thus. Again, of what kind? The abode of manifold amorous sports. Again, of what kind? Their innocent, enchanting faces — those themselves are a mass of lotuses; from them, the flowing, dripping nectar-essence, the honey — [the garland] whose nature is to taste that; the pair of eyes intoxicated with love — those themselves are the bee-garland, the row of bees; that enchanting [garland] — bearing it. [Commentary on Krd 3.31]
Now, after the meditation on the Supreme Lord, he describes the meditation on the worshipper's divine attendants and others —
Beyond the <s>gopī</s>s, cowherds, and cattle,
One should visualize before Him the assembly of gods,
Seekers of wealth, headed by <s>Viriñci</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), <s>Trinayana</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),
And <s>Śatamanyu</s> (<s>Indra</s>), devoted to hymns of praise. [Krd 3.32]

children.text: asya parameśvarasyāgrato gopī-go-paśūnāṃ bahir gīr-vāṇa-ghaṭa-deva-samūhaṃ smaret yadyapi bahiḥ-śabda-yoge pañcamī jñāpitā tathāpi jñāpaka-siddhaṃ na sarvatreti ṣaṣṭhī-prayoge 'pi na doṣaḥ | kim-bhūtām ? vittārthinīṃ jñānārthinīṃ vā dhanārthinīṃ yad vā parameśvara-cittāpaharaṇa-parāṃ yad vā dharma-kāma-mokṣārthinīm | punaḥ kim-bhūtām ? virañcir brahmā īśaḥ śakraḥ tat-pramukhām | punaḥ kim-bhūtām ? stavana-parām || KrdC_3.32 ||
children.translated_text: Before this Supreme Lord, beyond the <s>gopī</s>s, cows, and cattle, one should visualize the assembly of gods. Although the fifth case [ablative] is indicated with the word '<s>bahiḥ</s>' (beyond), still, since 'what is established by an indicatory marker does not apply everywhere,' there is no fault in using the sixth case [genitive] either. Of what kind? Seekers of wealth — seekers of knowledge, or seekers of riches, or devoted to stealing the heart of the Supreme Lord, or seekers of <s>dharma</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s>. Again, of what kind? Headed by <s>Viriñci</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), <s>Īśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), and <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>). Again, of what kind? Devoted to praise. [Commentary on Krd 3.32]
To his right, a host of sages,
With firm desire for <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), devoted to the <s>Veda</s>s;
And behind [him], the foremost yogis — those seeking
Liberation through <s>samādhi</s> (deep meditation) — <s>Sanaka</s> and the others. [Krd 3.33]

children.text: tasya parameśvarato dakṣiṇato dakṣiṇa-vibhāge tadvad iti pāṭhe tenaiva prakāreṇa muni-nikaraṃ muni-samūhaṃ smaret | kīdṛśam ? āmnāya-paraṃ vedādhyayana-param | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? niścalā dharma-vāñchā yasya taṃ yat tu mananāt munir ity abhidhānāt eṣāṃ dharma-vāñchā na yuktā tena muni-śabdo 'tra ṛṣy-upalakṣaka iti tan na, dharma-śabdenātrātma-jñānābhidhānāt | tad uktaṃ yājñavalkyena-ayaṃ tu paramo dharmao yad yogenātma-darśanam iti |
children.translated_text: To the right of that Supreme Lord — in the right portion — likewise (in the variant reading 'in that same manner'), one should visualize a host of sages, an assembly of sages. Of what kind? Devoted to the <s>Veda</s>s — devoted to Vedic study. Again, of what kind? Whose desire for <s>dharma</s> is firm. Now, since '<s>muni</s>' (sage) is so called from '<s>manana</s>' (contemplation), the desire for <s>dharma</s> in the conventional sense is not appropriate for them; therefore the word '<s>muni</s>' here indicates <s>ṛṣi</s>s (seers) — [but] that is not so, because the word '<s>dharma</s>' here refers to self-knowledge. Thus <s>Yājñavalkya</s> has stated: 'This indeed is the supreme <s>dharma</s> — the vision of the self through <s>yoga</s>.'

children.text: athānantaraṃ parameśvarasya paścād-bhāge sanakādyān yogeśvarān smaret | kim-bhūtān ? mokṣaika-parān | punaḥ kim-bhūtān ? samādhinopaviṣṭān || KrdC_3.33 ||
children.translated_text: Then next, behind the Supreme Lord, one should visualize <s>Sanaka</s> and the other lords of <s>yoga</s>. Of what kind? Solely devoted to liberation. Again, of what kind? Seated in <s>samādhi</s> (deep meditation). [Commentary on Krd 3.33]
On the left, with their consorts, the <s>Yakṣa</s>s, <s>Siddha</s>s,
<s>Gandharva</s>s, <s>Vidyādhara</s>s, and <s>Cāraṇa</s>s,
Together with <s>Kinnara</s>s; and the chief <s>Apsaras</s>es,
Seekers of desires, with dancing, singing, and instrumental music. [Krd 3.34]

children.text: athānantaraṃ deva-vāma-bhāge sa-strīkān yakṣādīn smaret | kim-bhūtān ? kinnara-sahitān | punaḥ kim-bhūtān ? sarva-nartana-gīta-vādyaiḥ karaṇa-bhūtair vāñchitārthinaḥ | tathā pradhāna-bhūtā apsarasaḥ urvaśī-mukhyāḥ smaret || KrdC_3.34 ||
children.translated_text: Then next, on the left side of the Lord, one should visualize the <s>Yakṣa</s>s and others, accompanied by their wives. Of what kind? Together with <s>Kinnara</s>s. Again, of what kind? With dancing, singing, and instrumental music as their means — seekers of desired objects. And the chief <s>Apsaras</s>es, headed by <s>Urvaśī</s>, one should visualize. [Commentary on Krd 3.34]
White as a conch, the moon, and <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) flowers, knower of all <s>āgama</s>s (scriptures),
With a mass of matted locks tawny like a streak of lightning;
Desiring unwavering devotion to those lotus feet [of the Lord],
Having completely abandoned all other attachments. [Krd 3.35]

children.text: nabhasi ākāśe dhātṛ-sutaṃ brahma-putraṃ smaret | katham-bhūtam ? śaṅkhādivat śvetaṃ nirmalam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? sampūrṇāgama-vettāram | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? saudāmanī vidyut tasyās tatiḥ dīptis tadvat piśaṅgā kapilā yā jaṭā tasyāḥ kalāpaḥ samudāyo yatra tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? bhaktim icchantam | kim-bhūtām ? sthirām | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? atyanta-parityakta-parameśvara-bhinna-sakala-sambandham || KrdC_3.35 ||
children.translated_text: In the sky, one should visualize the son of the Creator (<s>Brahmā</s>), i.e., the son of <s>Brahmā</s>. Of what kind? White like a conch etc., pure. Again, of what kind? A knower of all scriptures completely. Again, of what kind? Lightning — its radiance, its brilliance; similarly tawny, coppery, is the matted hair; its mass, its collection — he who has such. Again, of what kind? Desiring devotion. Of what kind [is that devotion]? Firm, unwavering. Again, of what kind? Having completely abandoned all connections other than the Supreme Lord. [Commentary on Krd 3.35]
Again, of what kind?
With the enchanting <s>mūrchanā</s>s (musical modulations) belonging to the three <s>grāma</s>s (scales)
Of the seven <s>rāga</s>s (melodic modes) accompanied by the various <s>śruti</s> (microtonal) groups,
Pleasing Him with those [melodies] arising from great [devotion] —
One should meditate upon that foremost sage, the son of the Creator, in the sky. [Krd 3.36]

children.text: amuṃ nānā-prakāraḥ ṣaṭ-triṃśad-bhedātmako yaḥ śruti-gaṇaḥ nāda-samūhas tenānvitā ye sapta rāgāḥ niṣāda-rṣabha-gāndhāra-ṣaḍja-madhyama-dhaivata-pañcamākhyāḥ svarāḥ tatra trayāṇāṃ grāmāṇāṃ samāhāro grāma-trayī tatra grāma-trayyāṃ gatāḥ prāptāḥ yā mūrchanā manoharā ekatriṃśati-prakārās tābhiḥ saṃprīṇayantam |
children.translated_text: The group of <s>śruti</s>s (microtonal intervals), of thirty-six varieties, by that [group] are endowed the seven <s>rāga</s>s — the musical notes called <s>Niṣāda</s>, <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Gāndhāra</s>, <s>Ṣaḍja</s>, <s>Madhyama</s>, <s>Dhaivata</s>, and <s>Pañcama</s>; the combination of the three <s>grāma</s>s (tonal registers) is the <s>grāma-trayī</s>; therein, the <s>mūrchanā</s>s (melodic sequences) that are delightful, of thirty-one types, found in the three <s>grāma</s>s — by those [melodic sequences] he delights [his audience].

children.text: sapta-svarās trayo grāmā mūrchanās tv ekaviṃśatiḥ |
children.translated_text: There are seven <s>svara</s>s (musical notes), three <s>grāma</s>s (tonal registers), and twenty-one <s>mūrchanā</s>s (melodic sequences);
where a <s>svara</s> (note), being fully developed, attains the state of <s>rāga</s> (melodic mode),

children.text: mūrchanām iti tāṃ prāhuḥ kavayo grāma-sambhavām ||
children.translated_text: that [progression] the poets call a <s>mūrchanā</s>, arising from the <s>grāma</s>.

children.text: kimbhūtābhiḥ ? mahatyā sapta-tantrī-yuktayā nārada-vīṇayā uditābhir udgatābhiḥ || KrdC_3.36 ||
children.translated_text: Of what kind [are these <s>mūrchanā</s>s]? Produced from the great <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) of <s>Nārada</s>, which has seven strings. // KrdC 3.36 //
Now, concluding the main topic, he states the sequence of self-worship (<s>ātma-pūjā</s>):
Having thus meditated upon oneself as the son of <s>Nanda</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), with keen and clear intellect,
first, through the mind alone, with offerings such as <s>arghya</s> (water-offering) and other blameless presentations,

children.text: yajed bhūyo bhaktyā sva-vapuṣi bahiṣṭhaiś ca vibhavair
children.translated_text: one should worship further with devotion, on one's own body and with external materials;

children.text: vidhānaṃ tad brūmo vayam atula-sānnidhya-kṛd atha // Krd_3.37 //
children.translated_text: we shall now describe that procedure which creates incomparable divine presence. // Krd 3.37 //

children.text: iti pūrvokta-dhyāna-prakāreṇa paṭu-viśada-dhīḥ samarthā vicāra-kṣamā atha ca nirmalā evambhūtā buddhir yasya sa tathā ātmānaṃ nanda-tanayaṃ gopāla-kṛṣṇa-rūpaṃ dhyātvā ātma-nanda-tanayayor abhedaṃ cintayitvā puraḥ prathamato buddhyaiva manasaivārghya-prabhṛtibhir anindyopahṛtibhiḥ arghya-pādyādibhir upahṛtibhir aninditopacāraiḥ yathopadeśaṃ pūjayet | tripāṭhinas tu abhinandyeti pāṭhe dhṛtvā pūjayed ity artham āhuḥ | bhūyaḥ punar api sva-śarīre sākṣād bāhyopacārair arghyādibhiḥ pūjayet | athānantaraṃ tad-vidhānaṃ bahiṣṭha-vibhavārcana-prakāraṃ vayaṃ brumaḥ | kīdṛśam ? parameśvarātyanta-sānnidhya-dātāram || KrdC_3.37 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by the previously described method of meditation, one whose intellect is keen and clear — capable, fit for discernment, and also pure — having meditated upon oneself as the son of <s>Nanda</s>, i.e., in the form of <s>Gopāla Kṛṣṇa</s>, having contemplated the non-difference of oneself and <s>Nanda</s>'s son, first, through the mind alone, with offerings such as <s>arghya</s> (water-offering), <s>pādya</s> (foot-washing water), and other blameless services, one should worship as instructed. The <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s, however, in the reading '<s>abhinandya</s>,' state the meaning as 'having saluted, one should worship.' Again, one should worship on one's own body, directly, with external ritual articles such as <s>arghya</s> and the rest. Then, we shall describe that procedure — the method of worship with external materials. Of what kind? One that creates the utmost proximity of the Supreme Lord. // KrdC 3.37 //
He shows the procedure for filling the conch:
Having prepared on the ground with cow-dung and water
a ritual platform, and placed one's own seat there,
having taken one's place there, with water
one should purify the conch with the <s>astra-mantra</s> (weapon-mantra). // Krd 3.38 //

children.text: bhuvi pṛthivyāṃ sthaṇḍilaṃ pūjā-sthalaṃ gomaya-sahitena jalenāracayya upalipya amutra sthaṇḍile nijaṃ svīyaṃ viṣṭaram āsanaṃ vastra-kambalādikaṃ nyasya saṃsthāpya tatra viṣṭare vihitāspadaḥ kṛtāsano jalena śaṅkham astra-manunā mūlamantrāstra-mantreṇa astrāya phaḍ iti mantreṇa vā pralepayet || KrdC_3.38 ||
children.translated_text: On the ground, having prepared a ritual platform — the place of worship — by smearing it with water mixed with cow-dung; having placed there one's own seat — cloth, blanket, or the like — and being seated there, one should wash the conch with water [reciting] the <s>astra-mantra</s>, the weapon-mantra of the root-mantra, or the mantra '<s>astrāya phaṭ</s>.' // KrdC 3.38 //
Then, one should deposit therein sandalwood paste, flowers, and unbroken rice,
while reciting the <s>hṛdaya-mantra</s> (heart-mantra);
the wise one should fill [the conch] with pure water,
[reciting] the <s>mātṛkā</s> letters in reverse order, ending with the head [syllable]. // Krd 3.39 //

children.text: vāma-bhāga-kṛta-vahni-maṇḍalādhārake śaṅkhe sudhīḥ subuddhi-sādhakaḥ hṛdaya-mantraṃ mūla-mantram eva hṛdaya-mantram kevalaṃ hṛdayāya nama iti vā uccārya gandha-puṣpa-yava-taṇḍulān nikṣipet | tathā vimala-pāthasā nirmala-jalena pūrayet | mantram āha-pratigatair iti | pratiloma-gataiḥ pratiloma-paṭhitair mātṛkākṣaraiḥ kṣa-kārādyair akārāntaiḥ śiro 'ntakaiḥ sa-bindukaiḥ | bindv-antakair iti laghu-dīpikākāraḥ | svāhāntair iti vidyādharācāryaḥ vikrāya svāheyt antair iti tripāṭhinaḥ || KrdC_3.39 ||
children.translated_text: In the conch placed upon a fire-<s>maṇḍala</s> (circle) support on the left side, the wise practitioner, having uttered the <s>hṛdaya-mantra</s> — the root-mantra itself serving as the heart-mantra, or simply '<s>hṛdayāya namaḥ</s>' — should deposit sandalwood, flowers, and unbroken rice grains. Then, one should fill [it] with pure water. He states the mantra: 'in reverse order' — with the <s>mātṛkā</s> (alphabet) letters read in reverse, starting from <s>kṣa</s>-kāra and ending with <s>a</s>-kāra; 'ending with the head' means with <s>bindu</s> (dot). The author of the <s>Laghudīpikā</s> says 'ending with <s>bindu</s>.' <s>Vidyādharācārya</s> says 'ending with <s>svāhā</s>.' The <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s say 'ending with <s>vikrāya svāhā</s>.' // KrdC 3.39 //
With '<s>pīṭha</s>' etc.:
On the <s>pīṭha</s> (seat), conch, and water, the knower of <s>mantra</s>s
[should establish] the <s>maṇḍala</s>s (circles) of fire, sun, and moon in sequence;
with the letters '<s>viṣa</s>,' '<s>ka</s>,' '<s>śrava</s>' [i.e., <s>ma</s>, <s>a</s>, <s>u</s>],
one should worship, [each letter] preceded by the face [syllable, i.e., with <s>bindu</s>]. // Krd 3.40 //

children.text: pīṭhe śaṅkhe salile ca yathā-kramaṃ vahni-sūrya-candrāṇāṃ maṇḍalāni viṣaṃ ma-kāraḥ kaṃ śiras tatra nyasyamāno 'kāraḥ śravaḥ śrotraṃ tatra nyasyamāno-kāra ebhir akṣarair mantra-vid upāsakaḥ krameṇa pūjayet | kīdṛśaiḥ ? vadana-pūrva-dīpitaiḥ vadana-pūrve śirasi nyasyamānam aṃ bindur iti yāvat tena dīpitaiḥ sānusvārair ity arthaḥ | prayogas tu-maṃ vahni-maṇḍalāya daśa-kalātmane namaḥ | aṃ arka-maṇḍalāya dvādaśa-kalātmane namaḥ | uṃ soma-maṇḍalāya ṣoḍaśa-kalātmane namaḥ || KrdC_3.40 ||
children.translated_text: On the <s>pīṭha</s> (seat), conch, and water, in sequence, [one should establish] the <s>maṇḍala</s>s of fire, sun, and moon. '<s>Viṣa</s>' is <s>ma</s>-kāra; '<s>ka</s>' is the head — the <s>a</s>-kāra placed there; '<s>śrava</s>' is the ear — the <s>u</s>-kāra placed there — with these letters, the knower of mantras, the worshipper, should worship in sequence. Of what kind [are these letters]? 'Preceded by the face' — the <s>bindu</s> (dot) placed at the head, that is, with <s>anusvāra</s> — this is the meaning. The application is: '<s>maṃ vahni-maṇḍalāya daśa-kalātmane namaḥ</s>' (salutation to the fire-circle of ten digits); '<s>aṃ arka-maṇḍalāya dvādaśa-kalātmane namaḥ</s>' (salutation to the sun-circle of twelve digits); '<s>uṃ soma-maṇḍalāya ṣoḍaśa-kalātmane namaḥ</s>' (salutation to the moon-circle of sixteen digits). // KrdC 3.40 //
Therein, with the <s>tīrtha-mantra</s> (sacred waters invocation) one should invoke
the <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred water) from the orb of the radiant sun; then
from one's own heart-lotus, <s>Hari</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) likewise,
and one should display the <s>gālinī</s> [mudrā] with the <s>śikhā</s> (topknot mantra). // Krd 3.41 //

children.text: tatra śaṅkha-jale vakṣyamāṇa-tīrtha-mantreṇa sūrya-maṇḍala-tīrtham āvāhayet tathā tataḥ svīya-hṛt-padmāt kṛṣṇam āvāhayet | anantaraṃ śikhā-mantreṇa vakṣyamāṇāṃ gālinīṃ mudrāṃ pradarśayet ca-kārāt dhenu-mudrāṃ ca | vāma-hasta-tale dakṣiṇa-tarjanyā tāḍanaṃ prabodhanam || KrdC_3.41 ||
children.translated_text: Therein, in the conch-water, with the <s>tīrtha-mantra</s> to be described, one should invoke the sacred water from the sun-<s>maṇḍala</s>; then from one's own heart-lotus, one should invoke <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. Then, with the <s>śikhā-mantra</s> (topknot-mantra), one should display the <s>gālinī mudrā</s> to be described; and due to the word 'ca,' also the <s>dhenu-mudrā</s> (cow gesture). Tapping the left palm with the right index finger [constitutes] the awakening. // KrdC 3.41 //
That water, sanctified by the gaze of the <s>nayana-mantra</s> (eye-mantra),
enveloped by the <s>varma</s> (armor-mantra) with both arms,
made complete with the root-mantra, one should place [it];
and with the auxiliary [mantras], one should consecrate the directions with the <s>astra</s> (weapon-mantra). // Krd 3.42 //

children.text: taj-jalaṃ śaṅkha-jalaṃ vauṣaḍ iti nayana-mantreṇa vīkṣitaṃ yatra nayana-mantraḥ sambhavati tatraiva nayana-mantreṇa vīkṣaṇam iti tripāṭhinaḥ | varmaṇā hum iti kavaca-mantreṇāguṇṭhya mūla-mantra-sakalīkṛtaṃ mūla-mantrāṅga-sambandham | etasyaiva vivaraṇaṃ nyased iti | devatāṅge ṣaḍ-aṅgānāṃ nyāsaḥ syāt sakalī-kṛtir iti rudradharaḥ | yad vā, mūla-mantra-dhyānena sadaivatam iti tripāṭhinaḥ | aṅgakaiś ca nyased iti mūla-mantrasya ṣaḍ-aṅga-nyāsaṃ kuryād ity arthaḥ | anantaraṃ śaṅkhasya daśa diśaḥ astra-mantreṇa choṭikayā badhnīyāt || KrdC_3.42 ||
children.translated_text: That conch-water, sanctified by the gaze of the <s>nayana-mantra</s> (eye-mantra) '<s>vauṣaṭ</s>' — wherever the eye-mantra applies, there indeed should the gazing with the eye-mantra [be done], say the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s — enveloped by the <s>varma</s> (armor-mantra) '<s>huṃ</s>'; 'made complete with the root-mantra' means having the connection of root-mantra and auxiliaries. The explanation of this is 'one should place': the <s>nyāsa</s> (installation) of the six auxiliaries on the limbs of the deity constitutes the 'making complete' — so says <s>Rudradhara</s>. Or, by the meditation of the root-mantra, [it becomes] endowed with the deity — so say the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s. 'And with the auxiliaries one should place' means one should perform the six-auxiliary <s>nyāsa</s> of the root-mantra — this is the meaning. Then, one should seal the ten directions of the conch with the <s>astra-mantra</s> by snapping the fingers. // KrdC 3.42 //
[The water] made into <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), endowed with unbroken rice and the rest,
while touching [it], one should recite the mantra eight times;
moreover, one should deposit [some] in the <s>vardhanī</s> (sprinkling vessel) water,
and then sprinkle one's own body with that water. // Krd 3.43 //

children.text: taj-jalam abhagna-taṇḍula-candan-puṣpa-sahitaṃ viṣṇu-svarūpatāṃ nītaṃ spṛśan mūla-mantram aṣṭa-kṛtvo japet | anantaram ardha-jalasya kiñcit sva-dakṣiṇa-bhāga-sthāpita-vardhanī-jale prokṣaṇīya-pātra-jale nikṣipet | tad uktam-
children.translated_text: That water — endowed with unbroken rice, sandalwood, and flowers — brought to the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s own form, touching [it], one should recite the root-mantra eight times. Then, some of the half-water [should be deposited] in the <s>vardhanī</s> (sprinkling vessel) water — the water in the sprinkling vessel placed to one's right. As stated:

children.text:
dakṣiṇe prokṣaṇī-pātram ādāyādbhiḥ prapūjayet |
kiñcid arghyāmbu saṅgṛhya prokṣaṇy ambhasi yojayet || iti |
children.translated_text: 'Taking the sprinkling vessel on the right, one should worship with water; taking some <s>arghya</s> water, one should add it to the sprinkling vessel water.'

children.text: tad-anantaram argdha-pātra-jalena vāra-trayaṃ nija-śarīraṃ prokṣayet | vardhanī-ghaṭa-jaleneti vidyādharācāryāḥ || KrdC_3.43 ||
children.translated_text: Then, with the water from the <s>arghya</s> vessel, one should sprinkle one's own body three times. <s>Vidyādharācārya</s>s [say]: with the water from the <s>vardhanī</s> pot. // KrdC 3.43 //
Likewise, with the hand, three times, with the [root] mantra, all
the ritual implements — flowers, sandalwood, and the rest [should be purified];
thus the procedure for filling the conch has been declared —
this secret one, the foremost among worship [rites], here. // Krd 3.44 //

children.text: tathā mūla-mantreṇa dakṣa-hastena puṣpa-candanādikaṃ pūjopakaraṇa-dravyaṃ vāra-trayaṃ prokṣayet | upasaṃharati śaṅkheti | eṣa śaṅkha-pūraṇa-prakāraḥ samīritaḥ uktaḥ | kīdṛśaḥ ? iha āgama-śāstre yajanāgraṇīḥ prathama-vidhāne yaḥ śreṣṭhataraḥ || KrdC_3.44 ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, with the root-mantra, with the right hand, one should sprinkle the worship implements — flowers, sandalwood, and other ritual materials — three times. He concludes: 'the conch' etc. This procedure for filling the conch has been declared, stated. Of what kind? Here, in the <s>āgama-śāstra</s> (tantric scripture), the foremost among worship rites, the best among preliminary procedures. // KrdC 3.44 //
Now he shows the <s>tīrtha-mantra</s> (sacred waters invocation):

children.text: gaṅge ca yamune caiva godāvari sarasvati |
children.translated_text: O <s>Gaṅgā</s>, and <s>Yamunā</s> too, <s>Godāvarī</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>,

children.text: narmade sindhu-kāveri jale 'smin sannidhiṃ kuru // Krd_3.45 //
children.translated_text: <s>Narmadā</s>, <s>Sindhu</s>, <s>Kāverī</s> — in this water, establish your presence! // Krd 3.45 //
This <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred waters) [mantra] has been declared, which removes the flood of sins;
the little fingers and thumbs of both hands joined to each other, // Krd 3.46 //
the index, middle, and ring fingers pressed together and slightly curved —

children.text: mudraiṣā gālinī proktā śaṅkhasyopari cālitā // Krd_3.47 //
children.translated_text: this <s>mudrā</s> (hand gesture) is called '<s>gālinī</s>'; it is moved over the conch. // Krd 3.47 //

children.text: eṣa tīrthāvāhana-mantraḥ kathitaḥ duriteti pāpa-samūha-vināśakaḥ | adhunā gālinī mudrāyā lakṣaṇam āha-kaniṣṭhety ādinā | hastayor anyonya-kaniṣṭhāṅguṣṭhakau sambandhau tathā tarjanī-madhyamānāmikāḥ saṃhatāḥ kṛtvā bhugnāḥ kiñcid ākuñcitāḥ paraspara-saṃsaktāḥ kāryā ity arthaḥ | evaṃ ca sati eṣā gālinī mudrā proktā | śaṅkhasyopari cālitā satī devatā-prītiṃ sampādayatīty arthaḥ || KrdC_3.45-47 ||
children.translated_text: This <s>tīrtha</s>-invocation mantra has been declared, which destroys the mass of sins. Now he states the definition of the <s>gālinī mudrā</s> — with '<s>kaniṣṭhā</s>' etc.: the little fingers and thumbs of both hands [are] joined to each other; and the index, middle, and ring fingers, pressed together, should be made slightly curved, mutually interlocked — this is the meaning. Thus, this is the <s>gālinī mudrā</s> as declared. Moved over the conch, it produces the delight of the deity — this is the meaning. // KrdC 3.45-47 //
Then, at the crown of the head, in the center of the root <s>cakra</s> (energy center),
having duly worshipped one's own masters and <s>Gaṇanāyaka</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>),
in the sequence of installation, with the <s>pīṭha-mantra</s>s (seat-mantras),
[one should worship] with water, sandalwood, unbroken rice, flowers, incense, and lamps. // Krd 3.48 //
Now he states the sequence of <s>pīṭha-pūjā</s> (seat-worship) on one's own body:

children.text: athānantaraṃ mūrdhani svakīya-śirasi mūla-cakra-madhye mūlādhāra-cakre yathā-kramaṃ sva-nāthān sva-gurūn gaṇapatiṃ ca pūjayitvā pūrvokta-nyāsa-krameṇa pīṭha-mantrair ādhāra-śaktim ārabhya pīṭha-mantrāntaṃ tat-tan-mantrair jala-gandhākṣata-puṣpa-dhūpa-dīpaiḥ sva-śarīre pīṭha-pūjanaṃ kuryāt || KrdC_3.48 ||
children.translated_text: Then, at the crown — one's own head — in the center of the <s>mūlādhāra cakra</s> (root energy center), having worshipped in proper sequence one's own masters and <s>Gaṇapati</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>), by the previously described installation sequence, with the <s>pīṭha-mantra</s>s — from <s>ādhāra-śakti</s> (the supporting power) through the end of the seat-mantras — with their respective mantras, with water, sandalwood, unbroken rice, flowers, incense, and lamps, one should perform the seat-worship on one's own body. // KrdC 3.48 //
One should then worship the radiance of the root-mantra
at the base, at the heart, and between the eyebrows;
meditating upon the triad [of lights], one should contemplate it as unified,
a mass of bliss, like a flash of lightning. // Krd 3.49 //

children.text: athānantaraṃ tan-mūlādhāra-hṛdaya-bhrū-madhya-gata-tejas-tritayaṃ mūla-mantrātmakaṃ paraṃ jyotiḥ smarataḥ kāma-bījena klīm ity anenaikībhūtaṃ cintayet | kīdṛśaṃ ? ānanda-ghanaṃ cid-ānandam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? vidyut-prabham || KrdC_3.49 ||
children.translated_text: Then, the triad of radiances situated at the <s>mūlādhāra</s> (root center), heart, and between the eyebrows — that supreme light consisting of the root-mantra — meditating upon [it], one should contemplate it as unified by the <s>kāma-bīja</s> (desire seed-syllable) '<s>klīṃ</s>.' Of what kind? A mass of bliss — consciousness-bliss. Again of what kind? With the splendor of lightning. // KrdC 3.49 //
That radiance, having given it limbs with the auxiliaries, [performing] from <s>vibhūti</s> (divine manifestation)
through the limbs (<s>aṅga</s>s), having installed [them], one should worship with [offerings] beginning with the seat;
through [offerings] ending with ornaments, again with water, sandalwood, and the rest, one should perform worship
up to the completion of the <s>vibhūti</s> and limb procedures — [thus should] the <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner). // Krd 3.50 //

children.text: tad ekīkṛtaṃ tejaḥ pañcāṅgaiḥ sāvayavī-kṛtya śarīra-yuktaṃ sampādya tatra vibhūtyādy-aṅgāntaṃ vibhūti-pañjaram ārabhyāṅga-nyāsa-paryantaṃ sva-śarīre vinyasya āsanādi-bhūṣāntair upacārair devaṃ pūjayet | bhūyaḥ punar api jala-gandhādibhir vibhūti-pañjara-mūrti-pañjara-karastha-sṛṣṭi-sthiti-daśa-pañcāṅga-nyāsa-sthāneṣu nyāsa-krameṇaiva tan-mantrair eva pūjayet || KrdC_3.50 ||
children.translated_text: That unified radiance, having given it a body — made it embodied — with the five auxiliaries, then having installed on one's own body [the mantras] from <s>vibhūti-pañjara</s> (cage of divine manifestation) through the completion of the limb-<s>nyāsa</s>, one should worship the deity with offerings from the seat through ornaments. Again, with water, sandalwood, and the rest, at the stations of <s>vibhūti-pañjara</s>, <s>mūrti-pañjara</s> (cage of the form), hand-held creation and preservation, the ten [mantras], and the five-auxiliary <s>nyāsa</s> — in the sequence of installation, with those very mantras, one should worship. // KrdC 3.50 //
Again, the flute held at the mouth, and on the chest the <s>vanamālā</s> (forest-garland);

children.text: vakṣojo 'rdhaṃ prayajec ca śrīvatsaṃ kaustubha-ratnam // Krd_3.51 //
children.translated_text: on the upper half of the chest, one should worship the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark and the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem. // Krd 3.51 //

children.text: bhūyaḥ punar api mukha-sthaṃ veṇuṃ pūjayet hṛdaye ca vanamālāṃ kaṇṭham ārabhya pāda-dvayam avalambinīṃ patra-puṣpa-mayīṃ mālām | tad uktam-
children.translated_text: Again, one should worship the flute held at the mouth, and at the heart the <s>vanamālā</s> (forest-garland) — a garland of leaves and flowers hanging from the neck down to both feet. As stated:
'That which hangs from the neck down to both feet,
a garland made of leaves and flowers — that is called the <s>vanamālā</s> (forest-garland).'

children.text: stanasyopari śrīvatsaṃ kaustubhaṃ ca prapūjayet || KrdC_3.51 ||
children.translated_text: On the upper part of the chest, one should worship the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark and the <s>Kaustubha</s> [gem]. // KrdC 3.51 //
With the body anointed with flowing sandalwood paste,
with the root [mantra], on the forehead and other [places], decorative marks
should be drawn; then with the <s>pañjara-mūrti-mantra</s>s (cage-form mantras),
[marks] in the shape of lamp-flames, free from disease. // Krd 3.52 //

children.text: athānantaraṃ mūla-mantreṇa candana-paṅka-liptāṅgaḥ pūjaka eva lalāṭādiṣu mūrti-pañjara-nyāsa-sthāneṣu citrakāṇi tilakāni dīpa-śikhākārāṇi anāmikayā mūrti-pañjara-mantraiḥ aṃ oṃ keśava-dhātṛbhyāṃ nama ity ādinā dvādaśa-mūrtibhir likhyāt kuryād ity arthaḥ || KrdC_3.52 ||
children.translated_text: Then, with the root mantra, the worshipper, whose limbs are anointed with sandal-paste, should draw with the ring finger pictorial <s>tilaka</s> marks in the shape of lamp-flames at the forehead and other places of the <s>mūrti-pañjara-nyāsa</s> (image-cage installation), using the <s>mūrti-pañjara</s> mantras such as 'aṃ oṃ keśava-dhātṛbhyāṃ namaḥ' etc., with the twelve <s>mūrti</s>s — this is the meaning.
Now he shows the procedure for the flower-offering —
Then one should offer the flower-offering five times
With the root mantra, at the pair of feet with two <s>tulasī</s> (basil) [leaves];
In the middle, with a pair of oleander flowers; at the head, with a pair of lotuses;

children.text: dvandvena ṣaḍbhir api sarva-tanau ca sarvaiḥ // Krd_3.53 //
children.translated_text: And with all six on the entire body.

children.text: athānantaraṃ pañca-kṛtvaḥ pañca-vārān mūla-mantreṇa puṣpāñjaliṃ vitanuyāt | tulasī-dvayena śveta-kṛṣṇa-tulasī-dvayena pāda-yugale krameṇa dakṣiṇa-vāma-pādayor ity añjali-dvayaṃ madhye hṛdi hayāri-yugalena śveta-rakta-kara-vīrābhyām ity eko 'ñjaliḥ mūrdhni padma-dvayena śveta-rakta-padmābhyāṃ ity aparo 'ñjaliḥ sarvatanau sarvaiś ca ṣaḍbhir api tulasī-dvaya-karavīra-dvaya-padma-dvayaiś cāñjaliṃ tanuyād iti pañcamo 'ñjaliḥ || KrdC_3.53 ||
children.translated_text: Then, five times — on five occasions — one should offer the flower-offering with the root mantra. With two <s>tulasī</s> — white and dark <s>tulasī</s> — at the pair of feet, in order on the right and left feet — thus two offerings. In the middle, at the heart, with a pair of oleander flowers — white and red oleander — thus one offering. At the head, with a pair of lotuses — white and red lotuses — thus another offering. On the entire body, with all six — two <s>tulasī</s>, two oleander, and two lotuses — one should offer an additional offering — thus the fifth offering.
Now he shows the distribution of white and dark <s>tulasī</s> and other [flowers] —
White flowers, anointed with white sandal-paste, [should be offered] on the right side;
Red flowers, sprinkled with red sandal-paste, on the left side.

children.text: śvetāni tulasy-ādīni puṣpāṇi śveta-candana-paṅka-yuktāni dakṣiṇa-vibhāge deyāni raktāni tulasy-ādīni rakta-candana-paṅka-yuktāni vāma-vibhāge deyāni || KrdC_3.54 ||
children.translated_text: White <s>tulasī</s> and other flowers, combined with white sandal-paste, should be offered on the right side; red <s>tulasī</s> and other flowers, combined with red sandal-paste, should be offered on the left side.
He shows the offering of services —

children.text: tadvac ca dhūpa-dīpau samarpya dhinuyāt sudhā-rasaiḥ kṛṣṇam |
children.translated_text: Likewise, having offered incense and lamp, one should gratify <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with nectar-streams;
Having given mouth-freshener and the like, one should worship well with fragrance and other [articles].

children.text: dhūpa-dīpau samarpya sudhā-rasair brahma-randhra-sthita-śaśāṅka-bimba-galitāmṛta-dravair dhinuyāt prīṇayet | sudhā-rasair mantra-kṛta-jalair iti rudradharaḥ | śrī-kṛṣṇam prīṇayet | anantaraṃ mukha-vāsādyaṃ gandha-vaṭikāṃ dattvā gandha-puṣpaiḥ pūjayet || KrdC_3.55 ||
children.translated_text: Having offered incense and lamp, one should gratify — please — [the Lord] with nectar-streams, i.e., with the ambrosia-drops flowing from the moon-disc situated at the <s>brahma-randhra</s> (crown aperture). <s>Rudradhara</s> says: 'nectar-streams' means waters consecrated by mantras. One should gratify <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>. Then, having given mouth-freshener — a scented tablet — one should worship with fragrance and flowers.
Having pleased [the Lord] with betel, singing, dancing, and music,
Then with water from the cupped palm,
With the mantra called '<s>Brahmārpaṇa</s>' (offering to <s>Brahman</s>),
The <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) should perform the offering of one's own self.

children.text: tatas tad-anantaraṃ mantrī sādhakaḥ upāsakaḥ tāmbūla-gītādibhiḥ śrī-kṛṣṇaṃ paritoṣya culukodakena brahmārpaṇa-mantreṇa vakṣyamāṇa-svātma-samarpaṇaṃ kuryād ity arthaḥ || KrdC_3.56 ||
children.translated_text: Then, thereafter, the <s>mantrī</s> — the practitioner, the worshipper — having pleased <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> with betel, singing, and other [offerings], with water from the cupped palm, by means of the <s>Brahmārpaṇa</s> mantra, should perform the self-offering to be described — this is the meaning.
Note: The <s>Brahmārpaṇa</s> mantra is as follows —
<s>Brahman</s> is the offering; <s>Brahman</s> is the oblation; by <s>Brahman</s> it is offered in the fire of <s>Brahman</s>;

children.text: brahmaiva tena gantavyaṃ brahma-karma samādhinā || iti ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> indeed is to be reached by one who contemplates <s>Brahman</s> in action with deep absorption.
Now he addresses one who is unable [to perform the full rite] —
Alternatively, for those of limited intellect, this procedure beginning with the <s>mūrti-pañjara</s> (image-cage),

children.text: yady aṣṭādaśa-lipinā sārṇa-padāṅgaiś ca veṇu-pūrvaiḥ proktaḥ // Krd_3.57 //
children.translated_text: If with the eighteen-syllable [mantra], is stated with its syllables, words, and limbs, preceded by the flute [-mudrā].

children.text: athavā mandamatīnāṃ pūjakānāṃ pūjā-prakāro mūrti-pañjarādibhir ukta iyaṃ daśākṣareṇa pūjā aṣṭādaśākṣara-pūjām āha | yady aṣṭādaśākṣara-mantreṇa pūjā tadā kaca-bhuvi lalāṭādi-sthāneṣu mantrākṣara-nyāsa-pada-pañcāṅga-nyāsair veṇv-ādibhiś ca proktaḥ || KrdC_3.57 ||
children.translated_text: Alternatively, for worshippers of dull intellect, the worship procedure beginning with the <s>mūrti-pañjara</s> has been stated — this worship [thus far] is with the ten-syllable [mantra]; he now states the worship with the eighteen-syllable mantra. If worship is with the eighteen-syllable mantra, then it is stated with the installation of mantra-syllables, the five-word installation, and the five-limb installation at the head and other locations, and with the flute [-mudrā] and other [gestures].
He shows the procedure of recitation —
Then, meditating on the son of <s>Nanda</s> as very gracious,
One should recite the mantra with undivided [attention];
Upon completing the prescribed count with remembrance of the meaning,
One should perform <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control) effortlessly.

children.text: athānantaraṃ mantrārtha-smaraṇa-pūrvakaṃ mūla-mantraṃ japatu | kiṃ kurvan ? suprasannaṃ pūrvokta-rūpam ātma-bhinnaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ hṛdi bhāvayan | punaḥ kimbhūtaḥ ? ananyas tat-paraḥ yathokta-japa-saṅkhyā-pūraṇe sati asuyamanaṃ prāṇāyāmaṃ kuryāt japārambhe cātra vidyādharācāryaḥ bāhya-pūjā-śaktau ātma-pūjānantaraṃ japaṃ kuryāt śaktau tu pūjānantaram ity āha || KrdC_3.58 ||
children.translated_text: Then, thereafter, one should recite the root mantra preceded by remembrance of its meaning. Doing what? Meditating in the heart on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, in the form previously described, as very gracious, as non-different from oneself. Again of what kind? Undivided — devoted to that alone. Upon completing the prescribed count of recitations, one should perform <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control) without strain. <s>Vidyādharācārya</s> says: at the beginning of recitation and here too, when capable of external worship, one should perform recitation after self-worship; when capable, one should perform [recitation] after [external] worship.
He states the preliminary act of practice —
Having recited the <s>bīja</s> (seed-syllable) enclosed in <s>praṇava</s> one hundred and eight times,
The great-minded one should apply the <s>yoga</s>s received from the mouth of his own teacher;
Then, [meditating on the self as] of the nature of existence, immortality, consciousness, and bliss, one should conclude the recitation —

children.text: iti japa-vidhiḥ samyak prokto manu-dvitayāśritaḥ // Krd_3.59 //
children.translated_text: Thus the procedure of recitation, dependent on the two mantras, is well declared.

children.text: kāma-bījaṃ praṇava-puṭitaṃ sahitāṣṭakaṃ śatam aṣṭottara-śataṃ japtvā nija-guru-mukhāt prāptān yogān ātma-para-devatā-samāveśa-lakṣaṇān aṣṭama-paṭale vakṣyamāṇān mahāmatir yunaktu karotu | prakṛtam upasaṃharati-anantaraṃ sad-amṛta-cid-ānandātmāmuṃ japaṃ samāpayet ity anena prakāreṇa manu-dvitīyāśritaḥ daśākṣarāṣṭādaśākṣarāśritaḥ pūjā-prakāraḥ samyak prakāreṇoktaḥ || KrdC_3.59 ||
children.translated_text: Having recited the <s>Kāma-bīja</s> (desire seed-syllable [klīṃ]) enclosed in <s>praṇava</s> one hundred and eight times, the great-minded one should apply — perform — the <s>yoga</s>s characterized by the merging of self with the supreme deity, received from the mouth of one's own teacher, which will be described in the eighth chapter. He concludes the present [topic]: then, [meditating on the self] as having the nature of existence, immortality, consciousness, and bliss, one should conclude the recitation. Thus the worship procedure, dependent on the two mantras — the ten-syllable and the eighteen-syllable — is well declared in proper manner.
Whatever man follows this prescribed method,
He shall become dear to all living beings;
And he shall become the sole abode of the lotus of speech [<s>Sarasvatī</s>],
And attains that supreme radiance.

children.text: yo naro manuṣya imaṃ pūjā-prakāraṃ sevate 'sau śarīriṇām vallabho bhaviṣyati | tadā sarasvatī-lakṣmyor āvāso bhavitā ante deha-pātānantaraṃ tejaḥ samupaiti tad-rūpo bhavatīty arthaḥ || KrdC_3.60 ||
children.translated_text: Whatever man follows this worship procedure, he shall become dear to all living beings. Then he shall become the dwelling of <s>Sarasvatī</s> and <s>Lakṣmī</s>. At the end, after the fall of the body, he attains radiance — becomes one with that [divine] form — this is the meaning.

children.text: sanātanaḥ : vidhiṃ vidhānaṃ puraścaraṇa-lakṣaṇam | acirāt śīghraṃ kamalāyāḥ sarva-sampatter ekaṃ mukhyaṃ mandiraṃ ca bhājanaṃ bhavati | api vāk-kamalaika-mandiram iti pāṭhāntare vācaḥ sarasvatyāḥ kamalāyāś caika-mandiram api bhavati || KrdC_3.60 || (hbv 17.15)
children.translated_text: <s>Sanātana</s> [comments]: '<s>vidhi</s>' means prescribed procedure, characterized by <s>puraścaraṇa</s> (preparatory observance). Quickly — swiftly — he becomes the chief, foremost abode — vessel — of <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), all prosperity. In the alternative reading 'api vāk-kamalaika-mandiram,' [the meaning is:] he also becomes the sole abode of <s>Vāc</s> (<s>Sarasvatī</s>) and <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>).

Thus ends the fourth chapter in the <s>Kramadīpikā</s> composed by <s>Śrī Keśavācārya</s>.
||3||

(4)
Fourth Chapter
Now, the authority for mantra-recitation and other [practices] belongs only to one who is initiated; as stated in another <s>āgama</s> —
Just as for uninitiated <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s there is no authority in their own rites, study, and the like
Here [in this world]; but there would be [authority] after the investiture ceremony (<s>upanayana</s>) —

children.text:
tathātrādīkṣitānāṃ tu mantradevārcanādiṣu |
nādhikāro 'sty ataḥ kuryād ātmānaṃ śivasaṃstutam || iti |
children.translated_text: Similarly, for the uninitiated, there is no authority in mantra-deity worship and the like; therefore, one should make oneself consecrated by <s>Śiva</s>.
Therefore, 'I shall describe <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), which is the principal auxiliary of mantra-recitation' — thus he says —
Now is declared the means for the two excellent mantras,
The means for attaining all <s>siddhi</s>s (perfections);
Having performed which, the sages
<s>Nārada</s> and others attained the supreme perfection here [in this world].

children.text: sapadi sāmprataṃ manu-varyayoḥ daśākṣarāṣṭākṣarayoḥ sādhyate vāñchitam aneneti | sādhanaṃ dīkṣaṇaṃ kathyate | kīdṛśam ? sakala-phala-sādhanaṃ yat kṛtvā nāradādayo munayaḥ mahatīṃ siddhim iha jagati prāptavantaḥ || KrdC_4.1 ||
children.translated_text: Now — at this time — for the two excellent mantras, the ten-syllable and the eighteen-syllable, the means — <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), by which what is desired is accomplished — is declared. Of what kind? The means for all fruits; having performed which, the sages <s>Nārada</s> and others attained great <s>siddhi</s> (perfection) here in this world.
-o)O(o-
Since <s>dīkṣā</s> is to be accomplished through a teacher, he states the characteristics of the teacher —
A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who has completely destroyed the host of enemies beginning with desire; of pure body; bearing
The most excellent devotion, passionate for the dust of the pair of lotus feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;
A knower of the pure paths of the <s>Veda</s>s, <s>śāstra</s>s, and <s>āgama</s>s; respected among the virtuous; self-controlled —

children.text: vidyāṃ yaḥ saṃvivitsuḥ pravaṇa-tanu-manā deśikaṃ saṃśrayeta // Krd_4.2 //
children.translated_text: One who desires to learn the <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge/mantra) should take refuge in such a teacher, with body and mind bowed in humility.

children.text: yo vidyāṃ saṃvivitur mantraṃ samyak jñātum icchati sa etādṛśaṃ deśikaṃ guruṃ saṃśrayet seveta | kīdṛśam ? vipraṃ brāhmaṇa-jātam upadeśe kṣatriyāder anadhikārāt |
children.translated_text: One who desires to know properly the <s>vidyā</s> — the mantra — should resort to, serve, such a teacher (<s>deśika</s>). Of what kind? Born a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, since <s>Kṣatriya</s>s and others have no authority in giving instruction.

children.text: punaḥ kīdṛśam ? prakarṣeṇa dūrībhūtā kāmādy-ari-ṣaḍ-varga-ghaṭā tayā pūtaṃ śarīraṃ yasya tathā taṃ kāma-krodhau lobha-mohau mada-matsarau ete ripavaḥ kāmādayaḥ lobhādy-upahata-cittasya nirantaraṃ pratyavāyotpattyā sevyatvābhāvāt |
children.translated_text: Again of what kind? One in whom the host of six enemies — the group of six beginning with desire — namely desire, anger, greed, delusion, pride, and envy — have been thoroughly, completely removed; purified in body by that [conquest]. These are the enemies: desire and anger, greed and delusion, pride and envy. Because one whose mind is afflicted by greed etc. is not fit to be served, since faults constantly arise [from such a teacher].

children.text: punaḥ kīdṛśam ? śrī-kṛṣṇa-caraṇa-kamala-yugale yad-rajas- tatra rāga-yuktām atiśāyitāṃ bhaktiṃ dhārayantam abhyaktasya puruṣārthānavāpteḥ |
children.translated_text: Again of what kind? One who bears the most excellent devotion, full of passion, toward the dust of the pair of lotus feet of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>. Because one lacking [devotion] cannot attain the goals of human life.

children.text: punaḥ kīdṛśam ? veda-śāstrāgama-sambandhi-vimala-mārgāṇāṃ jñātāram anyathā āgama-śāstra-vicārānupapatteḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? satsu janeṣu madhye sammataṃ sajjanatvena prasiddham anyathā khalatvāt śuśrūṣānarhatvāt sac-chabdārtha eva na syāt |
children.translated_text: Again of what kind? A knower of the pure paths related to the <s>Veda</s>s, <s>śāstra</s>s, and <s>āgama</s>s — otherwise, the investigation of <s>āgama</s> and <s>śāstra</s> would not be possible. Again of what kind? Respected — well-regarded as a virtuous person — among good people; otherwise, due to being wicked, he would not be fit to be served, and the meaning of the word 'sat' (good) would not apply.

children.text: punaḥ kimbhūtam ? dāntaṃ vaśīkṛtendriyam avaśīkṛtendriyasya devatā-parāṅmukhatvāt | kīdṛśaḥ ? praṇatānamrā vinītātanuḥ kāyo mano hṛdayaṃ ca yasya sa tathā atrādhikaṃ mat-kṛta-śārada-tilake 'vagantavyam || KrdC_4.2 ||
children.translated_text: Again of what kind? Self-controlled — with senses subdued — because one with uncontrolled senses turns away from the deity. Of what kind? One whose body, mind, and heart are bowed, humble, and disciplined — thus constituted. More on this should be understood from my work, the <s>Śāradā-tilaka</s> [commentary].

children.text: sanātanaḥ (hbv 1.34) - nirmalāṅgaṃ vyādhi-rahitaṃ, veda-śāstrāgamānāṃ ye vimalāḥ panthāno mārgās teṣāṃ vettāram | satsu satāṃ mataṃ sammatam | vidyāṃ saṃsāra-duḥkha-taraṇādy-upāyaṃ mantram | pravaṇā namrā vinītā deśikaika-parā vā tanur manaś ca yasya tathābhūtaḥ san | deśikaṃ gurum | evaṃ pravaṇa-tanu-manas-tvādi śruty-ukta-samitpāṇitvādi ca gurūpasatter ādya-prakāro jñeyaḥ || KrdC_4.2 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sanātana</s> [comments] (HBV 1.34): '<s>nirmalāṅga</s>' means free from disease. A knower of the pure paths — the ways — of the <s>Veda</s>s, <s>śāstra</s>s, and <s>āgama</s>s. 'Respected among the good' means approved by virtuous people. '<s>Vidyā</s>' means the mantra, the means for crossing the ocean of worldly suffering. One whose body and mind are bowed, humble, devoted, or solely intent upon the teacher — being thus constituted. The teacher — the <s>guru</s>. Thus, the quality of having bowed body and mind etc., together with the Vedic [qualification of] holding firewood in hand etc. — this should be known as the first type of approaching a teacher.
-o)O(o-
He states the manner of serving the teacher —
With a guileless, exceedingly affectionate inner self, one should please

children.text: taṃ svair dhanaiś ca vapuṣāpy anukūlavāṇyā |
children.translated_text: Him with one's own wealth, with one's body, and with favorable speech;
For three years, with the understanding [that he is] <s>Padmanābha</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), with great steadfastness —

children.text: tuṣṭe vivakṣatu gurāv atha mantra-dīkṣām // Krd_4.3 //
children.translated_text: When the teacher is pleased, then one should request mantra-initiation.

children.text:
athānantaram ukta-lakṣaṇaṃ guruṃ vatsara-trayaṃ padmanābha-buddhyā santoṣayet | kaiḥ ? svīya-dravyaiḥ tathā śarīreṇa tathā priya-vacanena | kīdṛśaḥ ? sudhīraḥ paṇḍitaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? avakro 'tisnigdho antarātmā antaḥkaraṇaṃ yasya sa tathā athānantaraṃ tuṣṭe gurau mantra-dīkṣāṃ vivakṣatu vaktum icchatu śiṣya eva yat tv anyatroktam -
ekābdena bhaved vipro bhaved abda-dvayān nṛpaḥ |
bhaved abda-trayair vaiśyaḥ śūdro varṣa-catuṣṭayaiḥ || iti |
children.translated_text: Then, one should please the teacher possessing the stated characteristics for three years, with the understanding that he is <s>Padmanābha</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>). With what? With one's own wealth; likewise with one's body; likewise with pleasing speech. Of what kind? Very wise, learned. Again of what kind? One whose inner self — inner faculty — is guileless, exceedingly affectionate. Then, when the teacher is pleased, the disciple himself should desire to request — should wish to speak about — mantra-initiation. As stated elsewhere: 'A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [qualifies] in one year; a king in two years; a <s>Vaiśya</s> in three years; a <s>Śūdra</s> in four years.'

children.text:
anyathā tu -
triṣu varṣeṣu viprasya ṣaḍ-varṣeṣu nṛpasya ca |
viśo navasu varṣeṣu parīkṣeteti śasyate |
samāsv api dvādaśasu teṣāṃ ye vṛṣalādayaḥ || iti boddhavyam |
children.translated_text: Alternatively: 'One should test a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> for three years, a king for six years, a <s>Vaiśya</s> for nine years — this is recommended; and for twelve years those who are <s>Śūdra</s>s and others.' This should be understood.
The prescribed constellations and other [auspicious factors] should be understood from my work, the <s>Śāradā-tilakodyota</s> [commentary].
-o)O(o-

children.text: kalāvaty-ādi-bhedena dīkṣāyā bahu-vidhatvāt mayā punar atra prapañca-sāroktā kriyāvatī dīkṣaiva saṅkṣepeṇa pradarśyate ity āha-
children.translated_text: Since <s>dīkṣā</s> is of many kinds due to the distinction between <s>kalāvatī</s> and other [types], 'Here I shall briefly show only the <s>kriyāvatī dīkṣā</s> (initiation involving ritual action) as stated in the <s>Prapañcasāra</s>' — thus he says —
The <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) renowned in the <s>Prapañcasāra</s>
Is now recalled for the attainment of all <s>siddhi</s>s (perfections);
Without which, even constant reciters [of mantras]

children.text: siddhiṃ na vai dāsyati mantra-pūgaḥ // Krd_4.4 //
children.translated_text: Will not be granted perfection by the host of mantras.

children.text: samprati dīkṣā kriyāvatī saṃsmāryate tasyāḥ smaraṇa-mātraṃ kriyate na tu samyag abhidhīyate | atra hetuḥ yataḥ prapañca-sāre vivicyoktā | kim artham abhidhīyate ? sarveṣāṃ phalānāṃ prāptyai yayā dīkṣayā vinā sarvadā japa-kartuḥ puruṣasya mantra-samūhaḥ phalaṃ yasmān na dadāti | yad āhuḥ -
children.translated_text: Now the <s>kriyāvatī dīkṣā</s> (initiation involving ritual action) is recalled — only a brief remembrance of it is made, not a full exposition. The reason here is that it has been discussed in detail in the <s>Prapañcasāra</s>. For what purpose is it described? For the attainment of all fruits, since without this <s>dīkṣā</s>, the collection of mantras never grants fruit to the person who recites them. As they say —

children.text:
mantra-vargānusāreṇa sākṣāt-kṛtyeṣṭa-devatām |
guruś ced bodhayec chiṣyaṃ mantra-dīkṣeti socyate || iti |
children.translated_text: When the <s>guru</s> awakens the disciple by directly revealing the chosen deity in accordance with the group of mantras, that is called <s>mantra-dīkṣā</s> (mantra-initiation). Thus.
-o)O(o-
Now he describes the preliminary rite of the <s>maṇḍapa</s> (pavilion) — the <s>vāstu-bali</s> (site-offering) — to be performed at a place with a purified hall and the like —
Now, first, the wise one should offer the <s>vāstu-bali</s> (site-offering)
Upon the ground, according to the prescribed method;
Then he should construct a <s>maṇḍapa</s> (pavilion) measured by seven arm-lengths,
With a smooth platform. // <s>Krd</s> 4.5 //

children.text: athānantaraṃ prathamaṃ bhuvaḥ sthalīm adhi pṛthivyām upari yathāvidhi yathokta-prakāreṇa vāstu-baliṃ budho puro dadyāt | atra bali-dānādi-vidhiś ca mat-kṛta-śārada-tilakoddyote boddhavyaḥ | tatas tad-anantaram atra saṃskṛta-bhūmau maṇḍapaṃ kuryāt | kīdṛśam ? acala-dor-mitam sapta-hasta-parimitam | tu-śabdo anukta-samuccayārthaḥ | tena pañca-hasta-parimitaṃ nava-hasta-mitaṃ ceti boddhavyam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? masṛṇa-vedikaṃ cikkaṇa-vedikam uktṛṣṭa-vedikam ity arthaḥ || KrdC_4.5 ||
children.translated_text: Then, next, first upon the ground — on the earth — the wise one should offer the <s>vāstu-bali</s> (site-offering) according to the prescribed method. The procedure for offering the <s>bali</s> and other [rites] should be understood from my work, the <s>Śāradā-tilakodyota</s>. Then, after that, on this consecrated ground, one should construct the <s>maṇḍapa</s> (pavilion). Of what kind? Measured by seven arm-lengths (<s>acala-dor-mitam</s>). The word 'tu' serves to include what is unmentioned; thereby one should understand [that it may also be] five arm-lengths or nine arm-lengths. Again of what kind? With a smooth platform — a polished, elevated platform — this is the meaning. // <s>KrdC</s> 4.5 //
With a garland of <s>kuśa</s> grass joined with triple-stranded thread,
Encircled, adorned with eight banners;
With gateways made of milk-trees at the four entrances,
Resplendent with a white canopy, brilliant. // <s>Krd</s> 4.6 //

children.text: punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? kuśa-mālayā veṣṭitam | kimbhūtayā ? śveta-rakta-śyāma-varṇa-tantu-yuktayā yad vā triguṇī-kṛta-sūtra-yuktayā | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? aṣṭabhir dhvajair śobhitaṃ prakṛtir aṣṭa-saṅkhyayā | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? mukha-catuṣke dvāra-catuṣṭaye payas-tarubhir kṣīra-vṛkṣaiḥ toraṇaṃ bahir dvāraṃ yatra tādṛśam | kṣīra-vṛkṣās tu aśvatthodumbara-plakṣa-nyagrodhākhyāḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? śubhra-candrātapena śobhitam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? ujjvalaṃ nirmalam || KrdC_4.6 ||
children.translated_text: Again of what kind? Encircled with a garland of <s>kuśa</s> grass. Of what kind? Joined with threads of white, red, and dark colors — or joined with triple-wound cord. Again of what kind? Adorned with eight banners — '<s>prakṛti</s>' [here] denotes the number eight. Again of what kind? At the four entrances — the four doorways — having gateways made of milk-trees (<s>kṣīra-vṛkṣa</s>), that is, outer arches. The milk-trees are called <s>Aśvattha</s> (sacred fig), <s>Udumbara</s> (cluster fig), <s>Plakṣa</s> (white fig), and <s>Nyagrodha</s> (banyan). Again of what kind? Adorned with a bright white canopy. Again of what kind? Brilliant — spotless. // <s>KrdC</s> 4.6 //
He describes the procedure for the fire-pit (<s>kuṇḍa</s>) —
Having a pit excavated to the measure of twenty-four <s>aṅgula</s>s (finger-breadths), [with the depth of] a star,

children.text: vasor vasupater atho kakubhi-dhiṣṇyam asmin budhaḥ |
children.translated_text: The wise one should make the fire-altar (<s>dhiṣṇya</s>) in this [pavilion], in the direction of <s>Vasupati</s> (<s>Kubera</s>);
He should make it with the fire-girdle, four-cornered by [the measure of] half the eight <s>Vasu</s>s,
Marked with a <s>yoni</s> (source-channel) resembling the base of [an image of] an elephant, situated to the west. // <s>Krd</s> 4.7 //

children.text:
athānantaram asmin maṇḍape budhaḥ vasor vahner dhiṣṇyaṃ kuṇḍaṃ karotu | kīdṛśaṃ ? vasur aṣṭa-saṅkhyā aṣṭau vasavaḥ iti prasiddheḥ | teṣāṃ vasūnāṃ triguṇāni caturviṃśāṅgulāni, taiḥ pramitaṃ tat-pramāṇaṃ khātasya gartasya uccatvaṃ vistāraś ca yatra tādṛśam | kutra ? vasupateḥ kuberasya kakubhi diśi uttarasyām | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? vasu-mekhalam | atra vasu-śabdena agnir ucyate | sa ca gārhapatyāhavanīyety ādi trividhaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? vasu-gaṇārdha-koṇaṃ catuṣkoṇam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? paścima-diśy avasthitaṃ gajo 'ṣta-sadṛśa-dvādaśāṅgulāyāmā yā yonis tayā bhūṣitam | tad uktam-dvādaśāṅguli-rūpatvād yoniḥ syād dvādaśāṅguliḥ iti | aparo 'tra viśeṣaḥ śāradā-tilakato 'vagantavyaḥ
|| KrdC_4.7 ||
children.translated_text: Then, next, in this <s>maṇḍapa</s>, the wise one should make the <s>dhiṣṇya</s> — the fire-pit (<s>kuṇḍa</s>) — of <s>Vasu</s>, i.e., of fire. Of what kind? '<s>Vasu</s>' denotes the number eight, since the eight <s>Vasu</s>s are well known. Their triple is twenty-four <s>aṅgula</s>s (finger-breadths); measured by that [dimension] — such is the depth and width of the pit. Where? In the direction of <s>Vasupati</s> (<s>Kubera</s>), i.e., to the north. Again of what kind? With the fire-girdle (<s>vasu-mekhala</s>). Here the word '<s>vasu</s>' denotes fire. And that [fire] is of three kinds: <s>Gārhapatya</s>, <s>Āhavanīya</s>, and the like. Again of what kind? Four-cornered — '<s>vasu-gaṇārdha-koṇam</s>' means four-cornered. Again of what kind? Adorned with a <s>yoni</s> (source-channel) twelve <s>aṅgula</s>s in length, resembling the base of [an image of] an elephant (the number eight), situated in the western direction. As stated: 'Because of being twelve <s>aṅgula</s>s in form, the <s>yoni</s> should be twelve <s>aṅgula</s>s.' Further details here should be understood from the <s>Śāradā-tilaka</s>. // <s>KrdC</s> 4.7 //
Now [he describes] the procedure for the zodiac <s>maṇḍala</s> (diagram) —
Then, in the <s>maṇḍapa</s> sprinkled with cow-product-scented water,
One should properly draw the <s>maṇḍala</s> (diagram), an eight-petaled lotus;
With three circles, with the zodiac (<s>rāśi</s>) [signs], the pedestal, the base-row,
Endowed with four passages, ornamental panels, sub-panels, and corners. // <s>Krd</s> 4.8 //

children.text:
tato maṇḍapānantaram asmin maṇḍape samyak yathokta-prakāreṇa maṇḍalaṃ likhet | kīdṛśe ? gavyaiḥ pañca-gavyaiḥ śāradā-tilakokta-vaiṣṇava-gandhāṣṭaka-jalena prokṣite | kīdṛśaṃ ? aṣṭa-dala-padma-sahitam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? vṛtta-traya-sahitam | punaḥ rāśayo meṣādayaḥ pīṭhaṃ kalasa-sthāpana-sthānaṃ tasyāṅghri-pīṭha-pātra-catuṣṭayaṃ catasro vīthayaḥ catvāri-dvārāṇi śobhā upaśobhā asraṃ koṇam etair yuktam | ayam arthaḥ-sārdha-hasta-dvaya-pramāṇena samaṃ catur-asram bhū-bhāgaṃ pariṣkṛtya tatra pūrvāparāyatāni saptadaśa-sūtrāṇi pālayet | evaṃ sati ṣaṭ-pañcaāśad uttaraṃ dvi-śataṃ koṣṭhānāṃ bhavati | tatra koṣṭha-vibhāgo madhye ṣoḍaśabhiḥ koṣṭhair vṛtta-trayānvitaṃ padmaṃ
likhet | (tatra ca padmopari-śiṣṭe pīṭhaṃ tad-aṅgaṃ ca likhet | tad-bahir aṣṭādhika-catvāriṃśatā-dvādaśa-rāśīn likhet | tad-bahiḥ ṣaṭ-triṃśatā-pīṭhaṃ pīṭhāṅgaṃ ca likhet | (tad-bahir aśītibhiḥ padair likhet |) atredaṃ boddhavyaṃ padmasya dalāgra-sthaṃ vṛttaṃ pīṭha-śaktiś ca etayor madhye pūrva-dakṣiṇa-paścimottaraṃ sūtra-catuṣṭayaṃ dadyāt | anantaraṃ dvādaśādhikaiḥ śatapadair dvāra-śobhopaśobhā-koṇāni vilikhet | tatra sarvasyāṃ diśi dvāraṃ ṣaṭ-padam | tatra prakāraḥ bāhya-paṅkti-gata-madhya-koṣṭha-dvayaṃ tad-antargata-paṅkti-gatamadhya-koṣṭha-dvayam iti dvārasyaikasmin bhāge koṣṭha-catuṣṭayenaikā śobhā bhavati | tatra bāhya-paṅkti-gatam eka-koṣṭhaṃ tad-antargata-paṅkti-gataṃ koṣṭha-trayam iti | evaṃ
