koṣṭha-catuṣṭayenaikopaśobhā bhavati | atra bāhya-paṅkti-gata-koṣṭha-traya-tad-antargata-paṅkti-gatam ekaṃ koṣṭham iti tathā koṣṭha-ṣaṭkena koṇam iti | evam aparasmin bhāge 'pi śobhopaśobhā-koṇāni boddhavyāni | evaṃ dik-catuṣṭaye 'pi militvā dvādaśādhikaṃ śataṃ bhavatīti | atrānuktaṃ śāradā-tilake bodhyam || KrdC_4.8 ||
children.translated_text: Then, after [constructing] the <s>maṇḍapa</s>, in this <s>maṇḍapa</s> one should properly draw the <s>maṇḍala</s> (diagram) according to the prescribed method. On what kind [of surface]? One sprinkled with the five cow-products (<s>pañca-gavya</s>) and water infused with the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> eight-fragrance mixture as stated in the <s>Śāradā-tilaka</s>. Of what kind? Endowed with an eight-petaled lotus. Again of what kind? With three circles. Again: the zodiac signs beginning with <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries); the pedestal — the place for installing the water-pot; its base — the four support-vessels of the pedestal; the four passages — the four doorways; the ornamental panels (<s>śobhā</s>), sub-panels (<s>upaśobhā</s>), and corners (<s>asra</s>) — endowed with these. The meaning is: having prepared a square ground-area measuring two and a half arm-lengths evenly, one should draw seventeen lines running east-west therein. Thus there will be two hundred and fifty-six cells. The division of cells is as follows: in the center, with sixteen cells, one should draw the lotus with three circles. (There, on the remaining [space] above the lotus, one should draw the pedestal and its subsidiary. Beyond that, with forty-eight [cells], one should draw the twelve zodiac signs. Beyond that, with thirty-six [cells], one should draw the pedestal and its subsidiary. (Beyond that, with eighty pads, one should draw [the outer border].) Here it should be understood: between the circle at the tip of the lotus petals and the pedestal-<s>śakti</s>, one should place four lines in the east, south, west, and north directions. Then, with one hundred and twelve pads, one should draw the doorways, ornamental panels, sub-panels, and corners. There, in every direction, the doorway has six pads. The method is: two middle cells of the outer row and two middle cells of the next inner row — thus with four cells on one side of the doorway, one ornamental panel is formed. There, one cell of the outer row and three cells of the next inner row — thus with four cells, one sub-panel is formed. Here, three cells of the outer row and one cell of the next inner row — thus with six cells, a corner is formed. Similarly, the ornamental panels, sub-panels, and corners should be understood on the other side too. Thus in the four directions combined, there are one hundred and twelve. What is not stated here should be understood from the <s>Śāradā-tilaka</s>. // <s>KrdC</s> 4.8 //
Then the preceptor (<s>deśika</s>), having first bathed, performing the prescribed rites
Up to and including self-worship, being a knower of proper procedure;
To his own left, [should place] a conch-shell, and vessels filled
With <s>arghya</s> (guest-water), <s>pādya</s> (foot-water), <s>ācamana</s> (sipping-water), and the like. // <s>Krd</s> 4.9 //
Having placed elsewhere flowers, fragrances, unbroken rice, and the like,
And a vessel for hand-washing behind [him];
With rows of lamps illuminating everything, [he should place] all other
Ritual implements within his own field of vision. // <s>Krd</s> 4.10 //

children.text: tad-anantaraṃ vidhijñaḥ āgamokta-prakārajñaḥ deśiko guruḥ snāna-pūrvakaṃ vidhānaṃ sva-gṛhyoktādi-snāna-vidhim ātma-pūjā-paryantaṃ samāpya sva-vāmāgre śaṅkhārghya-pādyā-camānīya-pātrāṇi jalādi-svaccha-dravyaiḥ sampūritāni | kṛtvā yathottaraṃ sthāpayitvānyato dakṣiṇa-bhāge puṣpāṇi pūjā-dravyāṇi nidhāya kara-prakṣālaṇa-pātram ekaṃ pṛṣṭha-deśe nidhāya sarvam anyat sādhanam upakaraṇaṃ sva-dṛg-gocare cakṣur-gocare pradīpa-śreṇi-virājite sthāpayet | atrāparo viśeṣaḥ śrī-paramānanda-bhaṭṭācārya-kṛte prapañca-sāra-vivaraṇe draṣṭavyaḥ || KrdC_4.9-10 ||
children.translated_text: Then the preceptor (<s>deśika</s>) — the <s>guru</s> — being a knower of proper procedure as stated in the <s>āgama</s>s, having first performed the bathing rite as prescribed in his own <s>gṛhya</s> (household) manual and completing up to self-worship, [should place] to his left the conch-shell, <s>arghya</s> (guest-water), <s>pādya</s> (foot-water), and <s>ācamana</s> (sipping-water) vessels, and the offering vessel — all filled with water and other pure substances. Having done this and placed them in proper order, on the right side [he should place] flowers and worship materials; having placed one vessel for hand-washing behind him, he should place all other implements — all ritual equipment — within his field of vision, in a place illuminated by rows of lamps. Further details here should be seen in the <s>Prapañcasāra-vivaraṇa</s> composed by <s>Śrī Paramānanda Bhaṭṭācārya</s>. // <s>KrdC</s> 4.9-10 //
From the northwest (<s>Vāyavya</s>) to the northeast (<s>Īśāna</s>), the row [of seats]
To the north of the worship-pedestal, relating to the teacher [lineage], [should be worshipped] first;
Elsewhere too, the son of <s>Ambikā</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>) is to be worshipped, holding in his lotus-hands
A noose, a tusk, a goad, and [the gesture of] fearlessness. // <s>Krd</s> 4.11 //

children.text: pīṭhasya rāśi-pīṭhasya udak uttara-bhāge vāyavya-koṇād īśāna-koṇa-paryantaṃ guru-sambandhinī paṅktir ādau prathamataḥ pūjyā | prayogas tu oṃ gurubhyo namaḥ iti | anyatra dakṣiṇa-bhāge āmbikeyo gaṇapatiḥ pūjyaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ ? hasta-padmaiḥ sva-dantaṃ śṛṇim aṅkuśam abhayaṃ dadhānaḥ || KrdC_4.11 ||
children.translated_text: To the north of the pedestal — the zodiac pedestal — from the northwest (<s>Vāyavya</s>) corner to the northeast (<s>Īśāna</s>) corner, the row relating to the <s>guru</s> (teacher lineage) should be worshipped first. The procedure is: 'Oṃ, salutation to the <s>guru</s>s.' Elsewhere, on the southern side, <s>Āmbikeya</s> (<s>Gaṇapati</s>) should be worshipped. Of what kind? Holding in his lotus-hands his own tusk, a goad (<s>śṛṇi</s>/hook), and [the gesture of] fearlessness (<s>abhaya</s>). // <s>KrdC</s> 4.11 //

children.text: adhunā kalaśa-sthāpana-prakāraṃ darśayati yato deśika ity ādinā-
children.translated_text: Now he shows the manner of installing the water-pot (<s>kalaśa</s>), since [beginning with] 'the preceptor' and so forth —
Having worshipped, beginning with <s>Ādhāra-śakti</s> and the other divinities, then in the central portion,

children.text: dharmādīn vahnir akṣaḥ-pavana-śiva-gatān dikṣv adharmādikāṃś ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> and the others [placed] in the directions of fire, axis, wind, and <s>Śiva</s>, and <s>Adharma</s> and the others [in the intermediate directions];
In the center, <s>Śeṣa</s>, the lotus, the three discs, the <s>guṇa</s>-groups, the <s>ātman</s> and the rest; in the filaments,

children.text: vahner madhye ca śaktīr nava-samabhiyajet pīṭha-mantreṇa bhūyaḥ // Krd_4.12 //
children.translated_text: One should worship the nine <s>śakti</s>s of fire in the center, once again with the pedestal-mantra. // <s>Krd</s> 4.12 //

children.text: athānantaraṃ maṇḍala-madhya-bhāge ādhāra-śaktim ārabhya kalpa-vṛkṣa-paryantam ārādhya pūjayitvā pīṭha-nyāsa-krameṇa vahnīti agny-ādi-koṇa-gatān dharmādīn pūrvādi-caturdikṣu adharmādīn tathā madhye śeṣaṃ padmaṃ tathā sūrya-soma-vahnīnāṃ bimba-trayaṃ dvī̀adaśa-ṣoḍaśa-daśa-kalā-vyāptaṃ maṇḍala-trayaṃ tathātmādi-catuṣṭayaṃ pūjayet | atha keśarāṇāṃ madhye karṇikāyāṃ cca vimalādyā nava-śaktīḥ pūrvādi-krameṇa pūjayet | bhūyaḥ punar api pūrvoktena pīṭha-mantreṇa pīṭhaṃ pūjayed ity arthaḥ || KrdC_4.12 ||
children.translated_text: Then, next, in the central portion of the <s>maṇḍala</s>, having worshipped from <s>Ādhāra-śakti</s> up to the wish-fulfilling tree (<s>Kalpa-vṛkṣa</s>), in the order of pedestal-installation (<s>pīṭha-nyāsa</s>): <s>Dharma</s> and the others placed in the fire-corner and other intermediate directions; <s>Adharma</s> and the others in the four cardinal directions beginning with the east; likewise in the center, <s>Śeṣa</s>, the lotus, and the three discs of <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Soma</s>, and <s>Agni</s> — the three circles pervaded by twelve, sixteen, and ten <s>kalā</s>s respectively — and the <s>ātman</s> and the other four should be worshipped. Then, in the filaments — in the pericarp — one should worship the nine <s>śakti</s>s beginning with <s>Vimalā</s>, in order from the east. 'Once again' (<s>bhūyaḥ</s>) — again with the previously stated pedestal-mantra, one should worship the pedestal — this is the meaning. // <s>KrdC</s> 4.12 //
Then, placing rice grains, the best pure unhusked rice, in the center of the lotus,

children.text: api nyasyed darbhāṃs tad upari ca kūrcākṣata-yutān |
children.translated_text: And placing <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass) upon them, joined with a <s>kūrca</s> (grass-bundle) and unbroken rice;

children.text: nyaset prādakṣiṇyāt tad-upari kṛśānor daśa kalā-
children.translated_text: One should place clockwise upon that the ten <s>kalā</s>s of fire,

children.text: ya-kārādy-arṇādyā yajatu ca sugandhādibhir imāḥ // Krd_4.13 //
children.translated_text: Beginning with the letter 'ya' and other syllables, and should worship them with fragrances and the like. // <s>Krd</s> 4.13 //

children.text:
tad-anantaraṃ madhye-kamalaṃ kamala-madhye śālīn āḍhaka-parimitān tathā śubhrān śāly-aṣṭa-bhāga-parimitān taṇḍulān śreṣṭhān nyasyet sthāpayet | yad uktaṃ-
śālīn vai karṇikāyāṃ ca nikṣipyāḍhaka-saṃmitān |
taṇḍulāṃś ca tad-aṣṭāṃśān darbhaiḥ kūrcaiḥ pravinyaset || iti |
children.translated_text: Then, in the center of the lotus — in the lotus-center — one should place rice (<s>śāli</s>) measured by one <s>āḍhaka</s>, and likewise white husked rice (<s>taṇḍula</s>), the best, measured as one-eighth of the rice. As stated: 'One should place rice in the pericarp, measured by one <s>āḍhaka</s>; and husked rice of one-eighth that [quantity], arranging them with <s>darbha</s> grass and <s>kūrca</s> (grass-bundles).' Thus.

children.text: tad-upari taṇḍulopari kūrcākṣata-yuktān darbhān vinyaset | kuśa-traya-ghaṭito brahma-granthiḥ kūrca-śabdenocyate kūrcaḥ kuśa-muṣṭir iti tripāṭhinaḥ | tad-upari kūrcopari kṛśānor vahner daśa kalā ya-kārādayo daśa-varṇā ādyāḥ prathamā yāsāṃ tāḥ prādakṣiṇyena nyaset tad-anantaraṃ imā daśa kalā gandhādibhiḥ pūjayet |
children.translated_text: Upon that — upon the husked rice — one should place <s>darbha</s> grasses joined with a <s>kūrca</s> (grass-bundle) and unbroken rice. A <s>kūrca</s> is defined as a Brahmā-knot (<s>brahma-granthi</s>) made of three <s>kuśa</s> grasses; the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s say that <s>kūrca</s> means a handful of <s>kuśa</s> grass. Upon that — upon the <s>kūrca</s> — one should place the ten <s>kalā</s>s of fire, whose first [letters are] the letter 'ya' and the [subsequent] ten consonants, clockwise; then one should worship these ten <s>kalā</s>s with fragrances and the like.

children.text:
tāś ca-
dhūmrārcir-ūṣmā-jvalinī-jvālinī-visphuliṅginī |
suśrīḥ surūpā kapilā havya-vahā kavyavahā || iti |
children.translated_text:
And they are:
<s>Dhūmrā</s>, <s>Arci</s>, <s>Ūṣmā</s>, <s>Jvalinī</s>, <s>Jvālinī</s>, <s>Visphuliṅginī</s>,
<s>Suśrī</s>, <s>Surūpā</s>, <s>Kapilā</s>, <s>Havya-vahā</s>, and <s>Kavya-vahā</s>. Thus.

children.text: prayogas tu dhūmrārciṣe nama iti || KrdC_4.13 ||
children.translated_text: The procedure is: 'Salutation to <s>Dhūmrārci</s>' and so forth. // <s>KrdC</s> 4.13 //
One should place the water-pot (<s>kumbha</s>) there, bound with a shining triple-stranded thread,
While reciting <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ), perfumed with <s>joṅkaṭa</s>-incense smoke;
In this <s>kumbha</s> (water-pot), with pairs of syllables beginning with 'ka-bha' and ending with 'ṭha-ḍa',

children.text: tathānyasyābhyarcyās tad-anu kha-maṇer dvādaśa kalāḥ // Krd_4.14 //
children.translated_text: And likewise of the other [set]; then one should worship the twelve <s>kalā</s>s of the sun (<s>kha-maṇi</s>). // <s>Krd</s> 4.14 //

children.text:
tatra daśa-kalā-maye kūrce tī̀aram oṅkāram uccaran kumbhaṃ nyaset | kumbhas tu suvarṇādi-nirmitaḥ | tad uktam-
sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ vāpi mṛṇmayaṃ vā yathoditam |
kṣāṇayed astra-mantreṇa kumbhaṃ samyak sureśvari || iti |

kīdṛśam ? grīvāyāṃ triguṇitā lasantaḥ śobhamānā ye tantavaḥ kanyā-kartita-kārpāsa-sūtrāṇi taiḥ kalitam astra-mantreṇa veṣṭitam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? joṅkaṭa-mayaiḥ kṛṣṇāguru-pradhānair dhūpaiḥ sudhūpitaṃ tad-anantaraṃ khamaṇeḥ sūryasya dvādaśa-kalā asmin kumbhe nyasya anantaraṃ pūjyāḥ | kaiḥ ? varṇa-yugalaiḥ | kīdṛśaiḥ ? kabhādyaiḥ ka-kāra-bha-kārādyaiḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? ṭha-ḍa-vasitibhiḥ ṭha-kāra-ḍa-kārāvasānaiḥ | ayam arthaḥ-anuloma-paṭhita-ka-kārādy-ekaikam akṣaraṃ pratiloma-paṭhita-bha-kārādy-ekaikam akṣareṇa sahitaṃ tapiny-ādiṣu dvādaśa-kalāsu saṃyojya nyāsādikaṃ kāryam | tāś ca-
children.translated_text: Of what kind? At the neck, the triple-wound — beautifully shining — threads, cotton strings spun by a maiden, with those [threads] wound around, wrapped with the <s>astra-mantra</s>. Again, of what kind? Well-fumigated with incense made of <s>joṅkaṭa</s> (a fragrant substance), primarily of black <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood). After that, having placed in this <s>kumbha</s> the twelve <s>kalā</s>s (aspects) of <s>Khamaṇi</s> (<s>Sūrya</s>, the Sun), they should then be worshipped. With what? With pairs of syllables. Of what kind? Beginning with <s>ka</s> and <s>bha</s> — beginning with the letter <s>ka</s> and the letter <s>bha</s>. Again, of what kind? Ending with <s>ṭha</s> and <s>ḍa</s> — concluding with the letters <s>ṭha</s> and <s>ḍa</s>. The meaning is: each single syllable beginning with <s>ka</s> read in forward order, combined with each single syllable beginning with <s>bha</s> read in reverse order, should be joined with the twelve <s>kalā</s>s beginning with <s>Tapinī</s>, and <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement) and other [rites] should be performed. And those [kalā]s are —

children.text:
tapanī tāpanī dhūmrā bhrāmarī jvālinī ruciḥ |
suṣumṇā bhogadā viśvā bodhinī dhāriṇī kṣamā || iti |
children.translated_text:
<s>Tapanī</s>, <s>Tāpanī</s>, <s>Dhūmrā</s>, <s>Bhrāmarī</s>, <s>Jvālinī</s>, <s>Ruci</s>,
<s>Suṣumṇā</s>, <s>Bhogadā</s>, <s>Viśvā</s>, <s>Bodhinī</s>, <s>Dhāriṇī</s>, <s>Kṣamā</s>. Thus.

children.text: prayogas tu-kaṃ bhaṃ tapinyai namaḥ | khaṃ vaṃ tāinyai namaḥ ity ādi kāryam ||14||
children.translated_text: The application is: '<s>kaṃ bhaṃ</s> homage to <s>Tapinī</s>; <s>khaṃ vaṃ</s> homage to <s>Tāpinī</s>' — and so forth should be done. ||14||
Thus, having conceived of <s>Agni</s> (fire) in the form of the base (<s>ādhāra</s>),
And similarly <s>Bhānu</s> (the Sun) in the form of the <s>kumbha</s>, by those who know the prescribed procedure;
One should place upon it, together with unbroken rice and other [offerings],
The <s>kūrca</s> (bundle), resplendent with gold and the best of gems.

children.text:
evam anena prakāreṇādhāra-rūpam agniṃ saṅkalpya tadvat kumbha-rūpaṃ bhānuṃ vicintya tasmin kumbhe vidhijña āgamokta-prakārābhijñaḥ mūla-mantreṇākṣatādyaiḥ sahitaṃ kūrcaṃ pūrvokta-lakṣaṇaiḥ suvarṇa-ratna-varyair nava-ratnaiḥ śobhitaṃ nyaset | tad uktaṃ bhairaveṇa-
etān nayitvā tan-madhye śukla-puṣpaṃ sitākṣatam |
nava-ratnaṃ ca kūrcaṃ ca mūlenaiva vinikṣipet || iti || KrdC_4.15 ||
children.translated_text:
Thus, in this manner, having conceived of <s>Agni</s> in the form of the base, and similarly having meditated upon <s>Bhānu</s> (the Sun) in the form of the <s>kumbha</s>, one who knows the prescribed procedure — one well-versed in the methods stated in the <s>āgama</s>s — should place in that <s>kumbha</s>, with the <s>mūla-mantra</s> (root mantra), the <s>kūrca</s> together with unbroken rice and other [offerings], adorned with the previously described characteristics, embellished with gold and the best of gems — the nine gems. As stated by <s>Bhairava</s> —
'Having brought these into its center, one should deposit with the root [mantra] itself a white flower, white unbroken rice, the nine gems, and the <s>kūrca</s>.' Thus.
Now, with decoction-waters, with the syllables beginning with <s>kṣa</s>
And ending with <s>a</s>, one should fill it;
Concluding with three recitations of one's own mantra, with the milks

children.text: gavāṃ pañca-gavyair jalaiḥ kevalair vā // Krd_4.16 //
children.translated_text: Of cows, with <s>pañcagavya</s> (five cow-products), or with plain waters.

children.text: athānantaraṃ pīṭha-kumbhayor aikyaṃ vicintya pañcāśad-varṇair oṣadhi-toyaiḥ palāśa-tvag-jalaiḥ kṣīra-druma-tvak-kvātha-jalair vā sarvauṣadhi-jalair vā gavāṃ payobhir vā pañca-gavyair vā kevala-jalaiḥ karpūrādi-jalair vā tīrtha-jalair vā kṣa-kārādi-varṇair akārāvasānair viloma-mātṛkābhiḥ sva-mantra-trijapāvasānaṃ mūla-mantra-vāra-traya-japī̀antaṃ yathā syād evaṃ pūrayet || KrdC_4.16 ||
children.translated_text: Then, next, having contemplated the unity of the <s>pīṭha</s> (seat/pedestal) and the <s>kumbha</s>, with the fifty syllables, with herb-infused waters, with waters from the bark of <s>palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa), or with decoctions from the bark of milk-trees, or with waters of all herbs, or with cow's milk, or with <s>pañcagavya</s> (five cow-products), or with plain waters — camphor-infused waters — or with waters from sacred <s>tīrtha</s>s, with syllables beginning with <s>kṣa</s> and ending with <s>a</s> — with the reverse <s>mātṛkā</s> (alphabet) — concluding with three recitations of one's own mantra — such that the chanting of the <s>mūla-mantra</s> three times [occurs at the] end — one should thus fill [the vessel].
In this water of the <s>kalaśa</s> (ritual vessel), [the aspects] numbering twice eight (<s>vasu-yuga</s>, i.e., sixteen),
Preceded by the group of vowels, one should place likewise;
The <s>kalā</s>s (aspects) of <s>Uḍupa</s> (the Moon), [which are] fragrant with the water,
With unbroken rice and flowers, thereafter one should worship.

children.text: tasmin kalaśa-jale uḍupa-kalāś candra-kalāḥ vasu-yuga-saṅkhyāḥ ṣoḍaśa-saṅkhyāḥ svara-gaṇa-pūrvā a-kārādi-varṇa-pūrvā nyasatu | tad-anu tad-anantaraṃ tāś candra-kalās tathaiva tenaiva krameṇa puṣpāñjalibhiḥ pūjayet | tāś coktāḥ-
children.translated_text: In that water of the <s>kalaśa</s>, the <s>kalā</s>s (aspects) of <s>Uḍupa</s> (the Moon), the lunar aspects, numbering <s>vasu-yuga</s> (sixteen), preceded by the group of vowels — preceded by syllables beginning with <s>a</s> — one should place. Thereafter — subsequently — one should worship those lunar <s>kalā</s>s in that very manner, in the same order, with handfuls of flowers. And those are stated —

children.text:
amṛtā mānadā pūṣā tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭī ratir dhṛtiḥ |
śaśinī candrikā kāntir jyotsnā śrīḥ prītir aṅgadā |
children.translated_text:
<s>Amṛtā</s>, <s>Mānadā</s>, <s>Pūṣā</s>, <s>Tuṣṭi</s>, <s>Puṣṭi</s>, <s>Rati</s>, <s>Dhṛti</s>,
<s>Śaśinī</s>, <s>Candrikā</s>, <s>Kānti</s>, <s>Jyotsnā</s>, <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Prīti</s>, <s>Aṅgadā</s>,
<s>Pūrṇā</s> and <s>Pūrṇāmṛtā</s>. Thus.
Now he states the eightfold fragrance of <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> [worship] —
With northern [grass] (<s>udīcya</s>), <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron), water-<s>bālā</s>, iron [or black <s>aguru</s>], <s>jaṭā</s> (spikenard) together with <s>mura</s>,

children.text: saśītam ity udīritaṃ hareḥ priyāṣṭa-gandhakam // Krd_4.18 //
children.translated_text: Together with <s>śīta</s> (camphor/sandalwood) — thus is declared the eightfold fragrance dear to <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: udīcyam uśīraṃ kuṣṭaṃ kuṅkumam ambu-bālā netra-bālā lohaḥ kṛṣṇāgurur jaṭayā saha murā jaṭā māṃsī ca etaiḥ saha śītaṃ candanam iti hareḥ priya-kāri-gandhāṣṭakam uktam || KrdC_4.18 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Udīcya</s> is <s>uśīra</s> (vetiver); <s>kuṣṭha</s>; <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron); <s>ambu-bālā</s> is <s>netra-bālā</s>; <s>loha</s> is <s>kṛṣṇāguru</s> (black aloe-wood); <s>mura</s> together with <s>jaṭā</s> — <s>jaṭā</s> being <s>māṃsī</s> (spikenard) — with these, together with <s>śīta</s>, which is <s>candana</s> (sandalwood): thus is stated the eightfold fragrance pleasing to <s>Hari</s>.
He states the filling of the conch —
In the belly [of the conch] filled with decoction-water,
Having stirred in the eightfold fragrance according to the prescribed method;
The <s>kalā</s>s (aspects) of <s>Soma</s> (Moon), <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun), and <s>Śikhin</s> (Fire), separately,
One should employ the sprinkling rite in sequence.

children.text: udare śaṅkhe vidhināgamokta-prakāreṇa mūla-manteṇa pūrvokta-kvātha-jalena paripūrite gandhī̀aṣṭakaṃ namo-mantreṇa saviloḍya dattvā soma-sūrya-vahnīnāṃ kalāḥ pṛthak samāvāhya seca-karma prāṇa-pratiṣṭhā-karma krameṇa viniyojayet kuryāt || KrdC_4.19 ||
children.translated_text: In the belly — the conch — filled by the prescribed method, in the manner stated in the <s>āgama</s>s, with the <s>mūla-mantra</s>, filled with the previously described decoction-water, having stirred in and deposited the eightfold fragrance with the <s>namaḥ</s>-mantra, having separately invoked the <s>kalā</s>s (aspects) of <s>Soma</s> (Moon), <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun), and <s>Vahni</s> (Fire), one should employ — perform — the sprinkling rite, the <s>prāṇa-pratiṣṭhā</s> (life-installation) ritual, in sequence.
Likewise, the syllable-born [<s>kalā</s>s] with [consonants] beginning with <s>ka</s>,
With those beginning with <s>ṭa</s>; again, the <s>kalā</s>s born of <s>u</s>-vowel;
With those beginning with <s>pa</s>, the <s>malipi</s>-born; and the <s>bindu</s>-born
With those beginning with <s>ṣa</s>; with the group of vowels, the <s>nāda</s>-born.

children.text: pūrvokta-prakāreṇa ākṣara-bhavā a-kārākṣara-bhavā daśa kalāḥ kādibhiḥ ka-kārādibhir daśabhir akṣaraiḥ sahitāḥ punar u-kāra-jā u-kārākṣara-bhavā daśa kalāḥ ṭādibhir daśabhir akṣaraiḥ sahitās tathā malipi-jā ma-kārākṣara-bhavā daśa kalāḥ pādibhir daśabhir akṣaraiḥ sahitās tathā bindujā bindu-prabhavāḥ catasraḥ kalāḥ ṣādibhiś catur-akṣaraiḥ sahitāḥ tathā nādajā nāda-prabhavāḥ ṣoḍaśca kalāḥ svara-samūhena ṣoḍaśabhiḥ svaraiḥ sahitāḥ śaṅkha-salile nyasyāḥ | tāś ca-
children.translated_text: In the previously described manner, the <s>ākṣara-bhava</s> (syllable-born) — born from the syllable <s>a</s> — ten <s>kalā</s>s, together with the ten syllables beginning with <s>ka</s>; again, the <s>u-kāra-ja</s> (born from the syllable <s>u</s>) — born from the <s>u</s>-vowel syllable — ten <s>kalā</s>s, together with the ten syllables beginning with <s>ṭa</s>; likewise, the <s>malipi-ja</s> (born from the syllable <s>ma</s>) — born from the <s>ma</s>-vowel syllable — ten <s>kalā</s>s, together with the ten syllables beginning with <s>pa</s>; likewise, the <s>bindu-ja</s> (born from <s>bindu</s>) — arising from <s>bindu</s> (the dot) — four <s>kalā</s>s, together with the four syllables beginning with <s>ṣa</s>; likewise, the <s>nāda-ja</s> (born from <s>nāda</s>) — arising from <s>nāda</s> (resonance) — sixteen <s>kalā</s>s, together with the group of vowels — the sixteen vowels — should be placed in the conch-water. And those are —

children.text: sṛṣṭir ṛddhiḥ smṛtir medhā kāntir lakṣmīr dhṛitḥ sthirā |
children.translated_text: <s>Sṛṣṭi</s> (Creation), <s>Ṛddhi</s> (Prosperity), <s>Smṛti</s> (Memory), <s>Medhā</s> (Intelligence), <s>Kānti</s> (Radiance), <s>Lakṣmī</s> (Fortune), <s>Dhṛti</s> (Firmness), <s>Sthirā</s> (Stability);

children.text: sthitiḥ siddhir akārotthāḥ kalā daśa samīritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sthiti</s> (Steadiness), <s>Siddhi</s> (Perfection) — these ten <s>kalā</s>s are declared as arising from <s>a-kāra</s> (the syllable <s>a</s>).

children.text: jarā ca pālinī śāntir aiśvarī rati-kāmike |
children.translated_text: <s>Jarā</s> (Old Age), <s>Pālinī</s> (Protectress), <s>Śānti</s> (Peace), <s>Aiśvarī</s> (Sovereignty), <s>Rati</s> (Delight), <s>Kāmikā</s> (Desire),

children.text: varadā hlādinī prītir dīrghā cokāra-jāḥ kalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Varadā</s> (Boon-giver), <s>Hlādinī</s> (Joyful), <s>Prīti</s> (Love), <s>Dīrghā</s> (Long-lasting) — these are the <s>kalā</s>s born of <s>u-kāra</s> (the syllable <s>u</s>).

children.text: tīkṣṇā raudrā bhayā nidrā tantīr kṣut krodhanī kriyā |
children.translated_text: <s>Tīkṣṇā</s> (Sharp), <s>Raudrā</s> (Fierce), <s>Bhayā</s> (Fear), <s>Nidrā</s> (Sleep), <s>Tantrī</s> (Thread), <s>Kṣut</s> (Hunger), <s>Krodhanī</s> (Wrathful), <s>Kriyā</s> (Action),

children.text: utkārī caiva mṛtyuś ca makārākṣarajāḥ kalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Utkārī</s> (Uplifting) and <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death) — these are the <s>kalā</s>s born from <s>ma-kāra</s> (the syllable <s>ma</s>).

children.text: nivṛttiś ca pratiṣṭhā ca vidyā śāntis tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Nivṛtti</s> (Cessation), <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s> (Foundation), <s>Vidyā</s> (Knowledge), and <s>Śānti</s> (Peace) likewise,

children.text: indhikā dīpikā caiva recikā mocikā parā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indhikā</s> (Kindler), <s>Dīpikā</s> (Illuminator), <s>Recikā</s> (Releaser), <s>Mocikā</s> (Liberator), <s>Parā</s> (Supreme);

children.text:
sūkṣmā sūkṣmāmṛtā jñānājñānā cāpy āyanī tathā |
vyāpinī vyoma-rūpā ca anantā nāda-sambhavāḥ || iti |
children.translated_text:
<s>Sūkṣmā</s> (Subtle), <s>Sūkṣmāmṛtā</s> (Subtle-nectar), <s>Jñānā</s> (Knowledge), <s>Ajñānā</s> (Ignorance), and <s>Āyanī</s> (Pathway) likewise;
<s>Vyāpinī</s> (All-pervading), <s>Vyoma-rūpā</s> (Space-formed), <s>Anantā</s> (Infinite) — these are born from <s>nāda</s> (resonance). Thus.

children.text: prayogaś ca kaṃ sṛṣṭyai nama ity ādi || KrdC_4.20 ||
children.translated_text: And the application is: '<s>kaṃ</s> homage to <s>Sṛṣṭi</s>' — and so forth.
At the conclusion of the invocation, before the establishment of the life-breath (<s>prāṇa-pratiṣṭhā</s>),
The Vedic verses (<s>ṛc</s>s) should be recited at the respective [places] by the wise one;

children.text: samabhyarcya tās tāḥ pṛthak tac ca pātho
children.translated_text: Having duly worshipped those respective [<s>kalā</s>s] individually, that water
Should be offered into the <s>kumbha</s> with the <s>mūla-mantra</s> (root mantra) in proper manner.

children.text:
samāvāhanasyānte 'susaṃsthāpanāt prāk prāṇa-pratiṣṭhāyāḥ pūrvaṃ tatra tatra sthāne paṇḍitena dhāryāś cābhijapyāḥ paṭhanīyāḥ | ayam arthaḥ-śaṅkha-jale 'kāra-prabhava-ka-kārādi-kalāvāhanānantaraṃ prāṇa-pratiṣṭhāyāḥ pūrvaṃ haṃsaḥ śuciṣad iti ṛcaṃ paṭhet | u-kāra-prabhava-ṭadi-kalāvāhanānantaraṃ pratad viṣṇuḥ iti ṛcaṃ paṭhet | ma-kārādi-prabhava-pa-kārādi-kalāvāhanānantaraṃ tat savitur ity ādi ṛcaṃ paṭhet | nāda-prabhava-ta-kārādi-kalāvāhanānantaraṃ viṣṇor yonir ity ādi ṛcaṃ paṭhet | anantaraṃ mūla-mantraṃ śaṅkha-jale vilomena japet | tās tāḥ kalāḥ pṛthag ekaikaśaḥ yathāvat yathā-vidhi sampūjya tac ca pī̀athaḥ tac-chaṅkhodakaṃ mūla-mantraṃ paṭhitvā kumbhe vinikṣipet || KrdC_4.21
||
children.translated_text: At the conclusion of the invocation, before the establishment of the life-breath — before the <s>prāṇa-pratiṣṭhā</s> — at the respective places, the learned one should recite — chant — [the verses]. The meaning is: in the conch-water, after invoking the <s>kalā</s>s born of <s>a-kāra</s> beginning with <s>ka</s>, before the <s>prāṇa-pratiṣṭhā</s>, one should recite the <s>ṛc</s> (Vedic verse) '<s>haṃsaḥ śuciṣad</s>' (The swan dwelling in the pure). After invoking the <s>kalā</s>s born of <s>u-kāra</s> beginning with <s>ṭa</s>, one should recite the <s>ṛc</s> '<s>pratad viṣṇuḥ</s>' (Viṣṇu strode forth). After invoking the <s>kalā</s>s born of <s>ma-kāra</s> beginning with <s>pa</s>, one should recite the <s>ṛc</s> '<s>tat savitur</s>' etc. (the <s>Gāyatrī</s>). After invoking the <s>kalā</s>s born of <s>nāda</s> beginning with <s>ta</s>, one should recite the <s>ṛc</s> '<s>viṣṇor yoniḥ</s>' etc. Then one should recite the <s>mūla-mantra</s> in reverse order into the conch-water. Having duly worshipped those respective <s>kalā</s>s individually, one by one, as prescribed, that water — that conch-water — having recited the <s>mūla-mantra</s>, one should deposit it into the <s>kumbha</s>.
With sprigs of mango (<s>sahakāra</s>), <s>bodhi</s> (sacred fig), and jackfruit (<s>panasa</s>),
Bound with <s>śatamanyu</s>-creeper (indigo vine), the <s>kalaśa</s> (vessel);
One should cover [it] with flowers, fruits, and rice grains,
And also fill it with an auspicious circular plate (<s>cakrikā</s>).

children.text: sahakāra āmraḥ | bodhir aśvatthaḥ | panasaḥ kaṇṭaki-phala-vṛkṣaḥ | eteṣāṃ stavakaiḥ pallavaiḥ śatamanyu-valli-kalitair indavallī-baddhaiḥ kalaśaṃ kalaśa-mukhaṃ suradruma-dhiyā pidadhātu samācchādayatu tathā puṣpādibhiḥ paripūrṇayā śubha-cakrikayā śobhamāna-śarāveṇa tad-upari pidadhāt || KrdC_4.22 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sahakāra</s> is the mango tree; <s>bodhi</s> is the <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig, Ficus religiosa); <s>panasa</s> is the jackfruit tree. With sprigs — young shoots — of these, bound with <s>śatamanyu-vallī</s> (indigo creeper), the <s>kalaśa</s> — the mouth of the vessel — regarding it as the wish-fulfilling tree, one should cover it. Also, with an auspicious <s>cakrikā</s> — a beautiful saucer — filled with flowers and other [offerings], one should cover the top of it.
Thereafter, the wise one should wrap the mouth of the <s>kumbha</s>
With a pair of new, spotless cloths;
When it is thus adorned with flowers and the like,
One should invoke therein the supreme radiance (<s>mahas</s>).

children.text: tad anu tad-anantaraṃ nūtana-mala-rahita-vastra-dvayena paritḥ kumbha-mukham abhiveṣṭayet | anantaraṃ kumbhe puṣpādibhir alaṅkṛte paramotkṛṣṭaṃ mahas tejaḥ pūjya-devatā-svarūpam āvāhayet āvāhanādikaṃ kuryāt | yathā śrī-kṛṣṇehāgaccheha tiṣṭha iha saṃnidhehi || KrdC_4.23 ||
children.translated_text: Thereafter — subsequently — one should wrap the mouth of the <s>kumbha</s> all around with a pair of new, stain-free cloths. Then, when the <s>kumbha</s> is adorned with flowers and the like, one should invoke the supremely excellent radiance — the splendor — the essential form of the deity to be worshipped — one should perform the invocation and other [rites]. Thus: 'O <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, come here, stay here, be present here.'
Having made complete (<s>sakalīkṛtya</s>) this one dwelling in the <s>kalaśa</s>,
<s>Hari</s>, through placements of syllables, <s>tattva</s>s (principles), and mantras;
The <s>guru</s> should then worship with full attention,
Together with the retinue [deities], with the array of <s>upacāra</s>s (offerings).

children.text: amuṃ kalaśasthaṃ hariṃ sakalīkṛtya devatāṅge ṣaḍ-aṅgānāṃ nyāsaḥ syāt sakalīkṛtir iti | uttamāṅgaṃ vidhāya varṇa-tattvam anv iti akṣara-maya-tattva-mantra-nyāsaiḥ saheti rudradharaḥ | arṇa iti sṛṣṭi-saṃhāra-bhedena aṅgulyāropaṇa-bhedena ca mantra-varṇa-vinyāso 'rṇa-nyāso manu-nyāsaḥ manu-puṭita-mātṛkā-nyāsa ity arthaḥ | ity ādi-nyāsais tat-tejo-rūpa-dharaṃ sakalaṃ saguṇaṃ śarīraṃ kuryād iti bhairava-tripāṭhinaḥ | vidyādharo 'py evam āha-pīṭḥa-nyāsa-kara-nyāsau vināpi prathama-dvitīya-paṭala-prokta-nyāsādi-jātair iti | kecit aṣṭādaśākṣare pakṣe tattva-nyāsa-sthāne mantrākṣara-nyāso draṣṭavyaḥ | athānantaram avahitaḥ sāvadhāno guruḥ sa-parivāraṃ āvaraṇa-sametam upacāra-gaṇaiḥ ṣoḍaśa-pañcopacārānyatamopacāreṇa

children.translated_text: should worship.

This one — <s>Hari</s> — dwelling in the <s>kalaśa</s>, having made complete — <s>sakalīkaraṇa</s> being the placement of the six limbs (<s>ṣaḍaṅga</s>) upon the deity's body — having performed the <s>uttamāṅga</s> (supreme body), with syllable-composed <s>tattva</s>-mantra placements — thus [says] <s>Rudradhara</s>. '<s>Arṇa</s>' means the placement of mantra-syllables by distinction of creation and dissolution, and by distinction of finger-application; '<s>manu-nyāsa</s>' means the placement of the <s>mātṛkā</s> (alphabet) enclosed in the mantra — this is the meaning. Through these and other placements, one should make the body — infused with that [divine] radiance — complete (<s>sakala</s>), endowed with qualities — thus [say] the <s>Bhairava-tripāṭhin</s>s. <s>Vidyādhara</s> also says thus: 'Even without <s>pīṭha-nyāsa</s> (seat-placement) and <s>kara-nyāsa</s> (hand-placement), with the placements etc. stated in the first and second chapters.' Some [say that] in the case of the eighteen-syllable [mantra], at the place of <s>tattva-nyāsa</s>, the <s>mantrākṣara-nyāsa</s> (mantra-syllable placement) should be observed. Then, subsequently, the attentive <s>guru</s> should worship [<s>Hari</s>] together with the retinue — with the surrounding deities — with the array of <s>upacāra</s>s, by any one of the sixteen or five <s>upacāra</s>s (offerings),
He states the sequence of worship —
Having offered a seat, and having uttered 'welcome' (<s>svāgatam</s>),
Then the <s>arghya</s> (offering-water), <s>pādya</s> (foot-water), and <s>ācamanīya</s> (sipping-water);
These should be given first, together with <s>madhuparka</s> (honey-mixture),
To <s>Nandātmaja</s> (the son of <s>Nanda</s>, i.e., <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), ending with <s>ācamana</s> (ritual sipping).
A place [to stand], garments, and ornaments,
The <s>mantrī</s> (ritualist) should assign to him who is accompanied by his limbs [(<s>aṅga</s>-deities)];
Then, upon his body, with purified fragrant [substances] and flowers,
One should first worship according to the method of <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement).

children.text: tasmai sāṅgāya nandātmajāya kṛṣṇāya āsanaṃ padmādi-kusuma-rūpaṃ dattvā svāgatam ity udīrya svāgatam iti śabdam uccārya anantaraṃ pūrvaṃ prathamato 'rghya-pādyācamanīyakāni madhuparka-sahitāni deyāni ācamanāntakāni madhu-parkaṃ dattvā punar ācamanīyaṃ deyaṃ snānaṃ gandha-jalādibhiḥ kāryaṃ vāso vastra-yugalaṃ śarīre deyaṃ vibhūṣaṇāni kuṇḍalādīni yathā-sthānaṃ viniyojyāni | athānantaram asya parameśvarasya gātre śarīre pūrvaṃ prathamataḥ pavitraiḥ śuddhair gandha-puṣpair nyāsa-prakāreṇa yajet pūjayet || KrdC_4.25-26 ||
children.translated_text: To him — to <s>Nandātmaja</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the son of <s>Nanda</s>) who is accompanied by his limbs [(<s>aṅga</s>-deities)] — having offered a seat in the form of lotus and other flowers, and having uttered 'welcome,' thereafter, first the <s>arghya</s>, <s>pādya</s>, and <s>ācamanīya</s> together with <s>madhuparka</s> (honey-mixture) should be given, ending with <s>ācamana</s> — that is, after giving the <s>madhuparka</s>, <s>ācamanīya</s> should again be given; bathing should be done with fragrant waters and the like; a pair of garments should be placed upon the body; ornaments such as ear-rings should be assigned to their proper places. Then, thereafter, upon the body of this Supreme Lord, first — initially — one should worship with purified, pure fragrant [substances] and flowers, according to the method of <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement).
He states the method of worship itself —
The [aspects of] creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>) and maintenance (<s>sthiti</s>), the pair of his own limbs, the flute (<s>veṇu</s>),
The garland (<s>mālā</s>), the <s>abhijñāna</s> (recognition-mark), and the chief gem (<s>varāśma</s>);
Having duly worshipped [these] with the <s>mūla</s> [-mantra], as in the worship of the Self,
One should then worship the surrounding circles (<s>āvaraṇa</s>s) again.

children.text: varṇa-nyāsa-mantrair yathā-kramaṃ pūjayet | oṃ goṃ oṃ namaḥ ity ādi | sṛṣṭi-sthitī pūrvoktaṃ svāṅga-yugaṃ pañcāṅga-daśāṅga-nyāsau veṇuṃ mālāṃ vanamālām abhijñāna-varaṃ śrīvatsalāñchanam iti aśma-mukhyaḥ kaustubhaḥ | etāni sampūjya mūlena cātmārcanavat yathātmani parameśvara-pūjā mūla-mantreṇa pañca-kṛtvaḥ tulasyādi-puṣpāñjalibhiḥ pada-dvayādiṣu kṛtā tathā kumbhastham api sampūjya bhūyaḥ punar api āvaraṇāni vakṣyamāṇāni pūjayet | aṣṭādaśārṇa-pakṣe sṛṣṭy-ādi-sthāneṣu varṇa-nyāsa-pada-nyāsānāṃ pūjā kāryeti boddhavyam || KrdC_4.27 ||
children.translated_text: One should worship with the <s>varṇa-nyāsa</s> (syllable-placement) mantras in proper sequence. 'Oṃ goṃ oṃ namaḥ' and so forth. <s>Sṛṣṭi</s> (creation) and <s>sthiti</s> (maintenance) as previously described, the pair of his own limbs, the <s>pañcāṅga</s> (five-limb) and <s>daśāṅga</s> (ten-limb) placements, the flute (<s>veṇu</s>), the garland (<s>mālā</s>), the forest-garland (<s>vanamālā</s>), the recognition-mark and the boon (<s>abhijñāna-vara</s>), and the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark — the chief among gems is the <s>Kaustubha</s>. Having duly worshipped all these with the root mantra (<s>mūla</s>), as in the worship of the Self, the worship of the Supreme Lord with the root mantra should be performed five times with handfuls of <s>tulasī</s> and other flowers at the pairs of feet and other [places]; likewise, having worshipped that which is established in the <s>kumbha</s> (vessel), one should again worship the surrounding circles (<s>āvaraṇa</s>s) to be described hereafter. In the case of the eighteen-syllable [mantra], it should be understood that worship of the <s>varṇa-nyāsa</s> (syllable-placement) and <s>pada-nyāsa</s> (word-placement) should be performed at the places of creation and the like.
He states the sequence of the <s>āvaraṇa-pūjā</s> (enclosure-worship) —

children.text: dikṣv atha dāma-sudāmau vasudāmaḥ kiṅkiṇī ca sampūjyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then in the directions, <s>Dāma</s>, <s>Sudāma</s>, <s>Vasudāma</s>, and <s>Kiṅkiṇī</s> should be worshipped;

children.text: tejo-rūpās tad-bahiraṅgāni ca keśareṣu samabhiyajet // Krd_4.28 //
children.translated_text: They are luminous in form; and one should worship the outer limbs upon the filaments [of the lotus].

children.text: athānantaraṃ karṇikāyāṃ devasya pūrvādi-catur-dikṣu dāmādayaś catvāraḥ pūjyāḥ | kīdṛśāḥ ? tejo-rūpā dedīpyamānāḥ | prayogas tu-oṃ dāmāya nama ity ādi | dvitīyāvaraṇam āha tad-bahir iti | karṇikā-koṇeṣu aṅgāni samabhiyajet || KrdC_4.28 ||
children.translated_text: Then next, upon the pericarp [of the lotus], in the four directions beginning with the east, <s>Dāma</s> and the other four [attendants] should be worshipped. Of what kind? Luminous in form — brilliantly shining. The application is: 'Oṃ homage to <s>Dāma</s>' and so forth. He states the second enclosure with 'the outer [limbs]': upon the corners of the pericarp, one should worship the limb [deities].
He states the method of worship —
In the directions of <s>Hutavaha</s> (Fire, southeast), <s>Nirṛti</s> (southwest), <s>Samīra</s> (Wind, northwest), and <s>Śiva</s> (northeast), from <s>hṛd</s> (heart) to <s>varma</s> (armor);

children.text: pūrvādi-dikṣv athāstraṃ krameṇa gandhādibhiḥ suśuddha-manāḥ // Krd_4.29 //
children.translated_text: Then in the directions beginning with the east, the weapon (<s>astra</s>), in sequence, with sandal-paste and other [offerings], with a fully purified mind.

children.text: agny-ādi-koṇa-catuṣṭayeṣu hṛdayādi-kavacāntāni catvāry aṅgāni athānantaraṃ pūrvādi-catur-dikṣu astram aṅgaṃ pūjayet || KrdC_4.29 ||
children.translated_text: In the four corner-directions beginning with fire (southeast), the four limb [-deities] from heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>) to armor (<s>kavaca</s>); then next, in the four cardinal directions beginning with the east, one should worship the weapon (<s>astra</s>) limb [-deity].
He states the meditation on the limb-deities (<s>aṅga-devatā</s>s) —
Pearl, moonstone, blue lotus,
<s>Harinīla</s> (sapphire), and fire — these are their lustres; [they are] women;
With hands displaying the <s>abhaya</s> (fearlessness) and <s>vara</s> (boon) [gestures],
With serene faces — the limb-deities (<s>aṅga-devatā</s>s) should be thus meditated upon.

children.text: aṅga-devatā dhyeyāḥ | kimbhūtāḥ ? pramadāḥ strī-svabhāvāḥ | punaḥ kimbhūtāḥ ? muktāḥ indukāntaś candrakānta-maṇiḥ kuvalayaṃ nīla-padmaṃ harinīlaḥ indranīla-maṇiḥ hutāśo vahniś ca eteṣāṃ samānābhā prabhā varṇo yāsāntās tathā | kimbhūtāḥ ? abhayena vareṇa ca śobhitāḥ karā yāsāṃ tāḥ | kimbhūtāḥ ? prasanna-vadanāḥ || KrdC_4.30 ||
children.translated_text: The limb-deities should be meditated upon. Of what nature? <s>Pramadā</s>s — of feminine nature. Again, of what nature? <s>Mukta</s> is pearl; <s>indukānta</s> is the moonstone gem; <s>kuvalaya</s> is the blue lotus; <s>harinīla</s> is the sapphire gem; <s>hutāśa</s> is fire — having the same lustre, radiance, and color as these, respectively. Of what nature? Having hands adorned with the [gestures of] fearlessness and boon-giving. Of what nature? With serene countenances.
He states the third enclosure —
<s>Rukmiṇī</s> and the other chief queens,
Eight [in number], one should worship upon the petals; then,
Holding lotuses in their right hands,
Their other hands bearing vessels filled with wealth.

children.text: tatas tad-anantaraṃ daleṣu pūrvādi-patreṣu rukmiṇy-ādyāḥ aṣṭau mahiṣīr mukhyā mahā-devīḥ sampūjayet | kimbhūtāḥ ? dakṣiṇa-karair dhṛtāni kamalāni yābhis tās tathā | punaḥ kimbhūtāḥ ? vasu-pūrita-pātrair mudritāḥ pūritā anye vāma-karā yāsāṃ tās tathā || KrdC_4.31 ||
children.translated_text: Then, next, upon the petals beginning with the eastern petal, one should worship the eight chief queens (<s>mahiṣī</s>s), the great goddesses, beginning with <s>Rukmiṇī</s>. Of what nature? Those by whom lotuses are held in their right hands. Again, of what nature? Those whose other, left hands are filled — sealed — with vessels full of wealth.
<s>Rukmiṇī</s>, <s>Satyā</s>, together with <s>Nāgnajitī</s>, and <s>Sunandā</s>;

children.text: bhūyaś ca mitravindā sulakṣmaṇā ṛkṣajā suśīlā ca // Krd_4.32 //
children.translated_text: And also <s>Mitravindā</s>, <s>Sulakṣmaṇā</s>, <s>Ṛkṣajā</s>, and <s>Suśīlā</s>.
<s>Ṛkṣajā</s> is <s>Jāmbavatī</s>.
He shows their forms —
With the lustre of gold and emerald,
With bright and variegated garments, in pairs, these [queens];
With limbs languid from the weight of ample breasts,
Adorned with ornaments sparkling with clusters of various gems.

children.text: etā rukmiṇy-ādyā dviśaḥ yugmaśaḥ krameṇa kāñcana-marakatayor ivābhā dīptir yāsāṃ tās tathā | punaḥ kimbhūtāḥ ? śobhamānāni śuklāni nānā-prakārāṇi vastrāṇi yāsāṃ tās tathā | punaḥ kimbhūtāḥ ? acalā ye kucās teṣāṃ gauraveṇa alasāni niṣkriyāṇi aṅgāni yāsāṃ tās tathā | punaḥ kimbhūtāḥ ? nānā-prakāro maṇi-prakara indranīlādi-samūhas teṣu viśeṣeṇa śobhitāni ābharaṇāni yāsām || KrdC_4.33 ||
children.translated_text: These [queens] beginning with <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, in pairs, in order, have the lustre — radiance — resembling that of gold and emerald. Again, of what nature? Having bright, white, and variegated garments. Again, of what nature? Those whose limbs are languid — inactive — due to the weight of their firm breasts. Again, of what nature? Those whose ornaments are especially resplendent with clusters of various gems such as rubies and the like.
He states the fourth enclosure —

children.text: tato yajed dalāgreṣu vasudevaṃ ca devakīm |
children.translated_text: Then one should worship upon the petal-tips <s>Vasudeva</s> and <s>Devakī</s>,
<s>Nanda-gopa</s> (the cowherd <s>Nanda</s>) and <s>Yaśodā</s>, <s>Balabhadra</s> and <s>Subhadrā</s>,
And the cowherds (<s>gopā</s>s) and cowherd-women (<s>gopī</s>s), whose minds and eyes are absorbed in <s>Govinda</s>.

children.text: tatas tad-anantaraṃ dalāgreṣu pūrvādi-krameṇa vasudevādīn sampūjayet | kīdṛśāḥ ? govinde vilīnā sambaddhā matir locanaṃ yeṣāṃ te tathā || KrdC_4.34 ||
children.translated_text: Then, next, upon the petal-tips, in sequence beginning with the east, one should worship <s>Vasudeva</s> and the others. Of what nature? Those whose minds and eyes are absorbed — attached — in <s>Govinda</s>.
He shows the weapons of these [figures] —
The two fathers, with <s>jñāna-mudrā</s> (gesture of knowledge) and <s>abhaya</s> (fearlessness) hands, yellow and white;
And again the two mothers, adorned with divine garlands, garments, ointments, and ornaments.

children.text: jñāna-mudrā abhayaṃ ca kareṣu yayos tau pitarau vasudeva-nanda-gopau | kīdṛśau ? haridrābha-śvetau mātarau devakī-yaśode | kīdṛśyau ? divyāni devārhāṇi mālyāmbara-bhūṣaṇāni yayos tādṛśyau || KrdC_4.35 ||
children.translated_text: The two fathers are <s>Vasudeva</s> and <s>Nanda-gopa</s>, in whose hands are the gesture of knowledge and fearlessness. Of what nature? Turmeric-colored and white. The two mothers are <s>Devakī</s> and <s>Yaśodā</s>. Of what nature? Those who possess divine — god-worthy — garlands, garments, and ornaments.
Holding the <s>varada</s> (boon-giving) [gesture] and a vessel filled with <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-pudding),
Ruddy and dark-complexioned, adorned with necklaces, gems, and earrings.

children.text: varadaṃ vara-dānaṃ mudrā-viśeṣaṃ pāyasā-pūrṇa-pātraṃ ca dhārayantyau | punaḥ kimbhūte ? aruṇā-śyāmale | punaḥ kīdṛśyau ? hāra-kuṇḍalābhyāṃ śobhite || KrdC_4.36 ||
children.translated_text: [The two mothers are] holding the <s>varada</s> — the boon-giving — a specific gesture — and a vessel filled with <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-pudding). Again, of what nature? Ruddy and dark-complexioned. Again, of what nature? Adorned with necklaces and earrings.
<s>Bala</s> (<s>Balabhadra</s>), white as a conch and the moon, bearing a pestle (<s>musala</s>) and a plough (<s>lāṅgala</s>),
Fond of liquor (<s>hālā</s>), wearing blue garments, playful, with a single earring.

children.text: balo balabhadraḥ śaṅkhendu-dhavalaḥ śvetaḥ lāṅgalaṃ musalaṃ bibhrāṇaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? hālā mādhvī tasyāḥ pāne lolaḥ cañcalaḥ amṛṣya-kārī | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? nīla-vāsāḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? helāvān līlāvān | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? eka-kuṇḍala-dhārī || KrdC_4.37 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bala</s> is <s>Balabhadra</s>; conch-and-moon-white — white; bearing a plough and a pestle. Again, of what nature? Fond of <s>hālā</s> — <s>mādhvī</s> (honey-wine) — restless in its drinking, acting impetuously. Again, of what nature? Wearing blue garments. Again, of what nature? Playful — sporting. Again, of what nature? Wearing a single earring.
<s>Subhadrā</s>, dark as a gram-plant (<s>kalāya</s>), auspicious, with auspicious ornaments,
Endowed with <s>vara</s> (boon) and <s>abhaya</s> (fearlessness) [gestures], wearing yellow garments, in the fullness of youth.

children.text: subhadrā kalāya-śyāmalā bhadrā samīcīnā bhadra-bhūṣaṇā śobhamānābharaṇā | punaḥ kimbhūtā ? varābhaya-yutā | punaḥ kimbhūtā ? pīta-vasanā | punaḥ kimbhūtā ? prauḍha-yauvanā || KrdC_4.38 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Subhadrā</s>, dark as a gram-plant, auspicious — excellent — with auspicious ornaments — resplendent adornments. Again, of what nature? Endowed with the boon and fearlessness [gestures]. Again, of what nature? Wearing yellow garments. Again, of what nature? In the prime of mature youth.
With flutes (<s>veṇu</s>), <s>vīṇā</s>s, staffs (<s>vetra</s>), rods (<s>yaṣṭi</s>), conches (<s>śaṅkha</s>), horns (<s>śṛṅga</s>), and the like in their hands;
The cowherds (<s>gopā</s>s) and cowherd-women (<s>gopī</s>s), with lotus-hands bearing various offerings;

children.text: mandārādīṃś ca tad-bāhye pūjayet kalpa-pādapān // Krd_4.39 //
children.translated_text: And beyond that [circle], one should worship the wish-fulfilling trees (<s>kalpa-pādapa</s>s) such as <s>Mandāra</s> and others.

children.text: veṇur vaṃśī | vīnā tantrī | vetraṃ yaṣṭiḥ śaṅkhaḥ śṛṅgādi nānā-vastu pāṇau kare yeṣām evaṃ viśiṣṭā gopāḥ gopyaḥ punar nānā-prakāraṃ yat-prābhṛtam upaḍhaukanaṃ tenāttam āyattaṃ vaśīkṛtaṃ karābjaṃ yāsāṃ tāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Veṇu</s> is the bamboo flute; <s>vīṇā</s> is the stringed instrument; <s>vetra</s> is a staff; <s>śaṅkha</s> is a conch; <s>śṛṅga</s> and other various objects are in their hands — thus distinguished are the cowherds and cowherd-women; again, their lotus-hands are held — controlled — won over — by various kinds of offerings (<s>prābhṛta</s>).

children.text: pañcamāvaraṇam āha-mandārādīn iti | tad-bāhye tad-anantaraṃ mandārādīn agre vakṣyamāṇān kalpa-vṛkṣān pūjayet || KrdC_4.39 ||
children.translated_text: He states the fifth enclosure with '<s>Mandāra</s> and others': beyond that — next — one should worship the wish-fulfilling trees (<s>kalpa-vṛkṣa</s>s) such as <s>Mandāra</s> and others, to be described hereafter.
<s>Mandāra</s>, <s>Santānaka</s>, <s>Pārijāta</s>,
The one called <s>Kalpa-druma</s> (wish-fulfilling tree), and <s>Haricandana</s> (divine sandalwood);
In the center and in the four directions, skilled solely in granting desired objects,
With branches bending low with fruits.

children.text: tān evāha mandāreti | kutra kaḥ pūjanīyaḥ tatrāha madhye iti | madhye karṇikāyāṃ prathama-parityāge mānābhāvāt prathama-nirdiṣṭavat pūjā caturdikṣu pūrvādi-catur-dikṣu etādṛśān vāñchitā ākāṅkṣitā ye arthās teṣāṃ dāne ekaṃ advitīyā dakṣāḥ tān tathā phalaiḥ namrāḥ śākhā yeṣu tān | yad vā, ākāṅkṣita-dāne advitīya-samarthān tathā phalaiḥ namrāḥ śākhā yeṣu tān || KrdC_4.40 ||
children.translated_text: He describes those very [trees] with '<s>Mandāra</s>' etc. Where should each be worshipped? To that he says 'in the center': in the center — on the pericarp — in the first [position], since there is no reason for exclusion, the worship is as if first stated; in the four directions — in the four cardinal directions beginning with the east — such trees whose desired — longed-for — objects they alone are uniquely skilled in granting; with branches bending low with fruits. Alternatively: uniquely capable in granting desired things, with branches bending low with fruits.
He states the sixth enclosure —
<s>Hari</s> (<s>Indra</s>), <s>Havya-vāṭ</s> (<s>Agni</s>, Fire), <s>Taraṇija</s> (<s>Yama</s>, son of the Sun), <s>Kṣapācara</s> (<s>Nirṛti</s>),
<s>Ap</s> (<s>Varuṇa</s>), <s>Ativāyu</s> (<s>Vāyu</s>, Wind), <s>Soma</s>, <s>Śiva</s> (<s>Īśāna</s>), <s>Śeṣa</s>, and <s>Padmaja</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>);
One should worship [them] with purified mind in their respective directions,
Accompanied by their respective retinues of sovereign lords, weapons, mounts, and attendants.

children.text: harir indraḥ havya-vāḍ-agniḥ taraṇijo yamaḥ kṣapācaro niśācaro nirṛtiḥ appatir varuṇaḥ vāyuḥ somaḥ īśaḥ śeṣo 'nantaḥ padmajo brahmā etān sva-dikṣu pūrvādi-dikṣu nirmala-matiḥ pūjayet | atra nirṛti-varuṇayor madhye 'nantaṃ someśānayor madhye brahmāṇaṃ svādikṣv atikathanāt anyatra kalpita-pūrvādi-dikṣu pūjāvagamyate | tad uktam āgamāntare-
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> is <s>Indra</s>; <s>Havya-vāṭ</s> is <s>Agni</s> (Fire); <s>Taraṇija</s> is <s>Yama</s>; <s>Kṣapācara</s> — the night-wanderer — is <s>Nirṛti</s>; <s>Appati</s> is <s>Varuṇa</s>; <s>Vāyu</s>; <s>Soma</s>; <s>Īśa</s>; <s>Śeṣa</s> is <s>Ananta</s>; <s>Padmaja</s> is <s>Brahmā</s> — these [guardians] should be worshipped with purified mind in their respective directions beginning with the east. Here, <s>Ananta</s> is between <s>Nirṛti</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s> is between <s>Soma</s> and <s>Īśāna</s>; since it is stated 'in their own directions,' worship at specially assigned cardinal directions is understood for the others. Thus it is said in another <s>Āgama</s> —

children.text:
devāgre svasya vāpy agre prācī proktā ca deśikaiḥ |
prācī prācy eva vijñeyā muktaye devatārcanam || iti |
children.translated_text:
'The east is declared by the teachers as either in front of the deity or in front of oneself;
the east is to be known as the east itself — worship of the deity is for liberation.' Thus.

children.text: kīdṛśān ? sva-jātiḥ indratvādiḥ | adhīśvaro 'dhipatiḥ hetiḥ śastraṃ patraṃ vāhanaṃ parivāro gaṇaḥ etaiḥ saṃyuktān eteṣāṃ ca bījāni uccārayitavyāni | prayogas tu laṃ indrāya sarva-surādhipataye sāyudhāya savāhanāya saparivārāya nama evam anyatrāpy ūhanīyaḥ || KrdC_4.41 ||
children.translated_text: Of what nature? Their own rank (<s>jāti</s>) is <s>Indra</s>-ship and the like; the sovereign lord is the ruler; the weapon (<s>heti</s>) is the armament; the mount (<s>patra</s>) is the vehicle; the retinue (<s>parivāra</s>) is the assembly — accompanied by all these. And their seed-syllables should be uttered. The application is: '<s>laṃ</s> homage to <s>Indra</s>, the lord of all gods, together with his weapon, vehicle, and retinue' — thus in other cases too it should be analogously applied.
Now he states their colors —
Tawny, coppery, dark blue, dark, white, smoky,
Pure white, lustrous, and red — by color, <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>) and the others.
With their respective weapons shining in their lotus-hands, in divine attire,
Resplendent with ornaments sparkling with rays from clusters of various gems.

children.text: kapiśaḥ kanaka-varṇaḥ kapilas tāmra-varṇābhaḥ śyāmalaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ śvetaḥ śuklaḥ dhūmro 'sita-bhedaḥ amala-sitaḥ śvetaḥ śucir api śveta eva rakto lohita ete vāsavādyāḥ varṇato varṇena yathā-kramaṃ pūrvokta-kramataḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? hasta-padme śobhamānāni āyudhāni yeṣāṃ te | punaḥ utkṛṣṭa-veśā nānā-prakāra-maṇi-samūhānāṃ padma-rāgādīnām usreṇa kiraṇena prasphurad-dedīpyamānaṃ yad bhūṣaṇaṃ tenāḍhyā upacitāḥ śobhamānā ity arthaḥ || KrdC_4.42 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kapiśa</s> is golden-colored; <s>kapila</s> is coppery in hue; <s>śyāmala</s> is dark; <s>śveta</s> is white; <s>dhūmra</s> is a shade of dark; <s>amala-sita</s> is white; <s>śuci</s> is also white; <s>rakta</s> is red — these are the colors of <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>) and the others, in the order previously stated. Again, of what nature? Those in whose lotus-hands their weapons are resplendent. Again, of what nature? Of exalted attire — adorned with ornaments resplendent with the rays — beams — of clusters of various gems such as rubies and the like — abundantly endowed — this is the meaning.
He states the seventh enclosure —
<s>Dambholi</s> (thunderbolt), <s>Śakti</s> (spear), <s>Daṇḍa</s> (staff), <s>Kṛpāṇa</s> (sword), <s>Pāśa</s> (noose),
<s>Caṇḍāṅkuśa</s> (fierce goad), <s>Gadā</s> (mace), <s>Triśikha</s> (trident), <s>Ari</s> (discus), and <s>Padma</s> (lotus);
These should be worshipped outside, bearing their own well-marked crowns,
With lotus-hands raised [holding] their respective weapons and [showing] the <s>abhaya</s> (fearlessness) [gesture].

children.text: dambholir vajraṃ śakty-abhidhaṃ śakti-nāmakam astraṃ daṇḍaḥ kṛpāṇaḥ khaḍgaḥ caṇḍāṅkuśāhvayaḥ ugrāṅkuśākhyaḥ gadā triśikhaṃ triśūlam ari cakraṃ padmṃ ca etāni vahni-vāsavādito bahiḥ sampūjyāni | dambholi-prabhṛtayaḥ kīdṛśāḥ ? nija- sulakṣita-mauli-yuktāḥ vajrādi-lāñchita-mukuṭāḥ | punaḥ sva-svāyudhair astrair abhayena ca samudyataṃ sulakṣitaṃ hasta-padmaṃ yeṣāṃ te tathā || KrdC_4.43 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dambholi</s> is the thunderbolt; <s>śakty-abhidha</s> is the weapon named spear; <s>daṇḍa</s> is the staff; <s>kṛpāṇa</s> is the sword; <s>caṇḍāṅkuśāhvaya</s> is the one named the fierce goad; <s>gadā</s> is the mace; <s>triśikha</s> is the trident; <s>ari</s> is the discus; and <s>padma</s> is the lotus — these should be worshipped outside, beyond [the circle of] Fire and <s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>). Of what nature are these, beginning with <s>Dambholi</s>? Bearing their own well-marked crowns — diadems marked with the thunderbolt and the like. Again, those whose lotus-hands are raised — well-displayed — with their respective weapons and with [the gesture of] fearlessness.
He states the colors of the thunderbolt and the others —
With the lustres of gold, silver, rain-cloud, lightning,
Ruddy, snow[-white], dark blue, <s>javā</s> (hibiscus-red), and coral — in order.
In sequence, by color, the <s>vajra</s>-preceded ones —
with beautiful ointments, garments, garlands, and ornaments.

children.text: vajra-pūrvāḥ vajrādyāḥ rucā varṇena kramato 'nukrameṇaivaṃrūpā jñeyāḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśāḥ ? kāñcanaṃ raupyaṃ toyado meghaḥ abhraṃ campaka-puṣpam aruṇo raktaḥ himaṃ śvetaḥ nīlaḥ śyāmalaḥ javā auṇḍra-puṣpaṃ pravālo nava-pallavaḥ evambhūtā dīptir yeṣāṃ te tathā | punaḥ kīdṛśāḥ ? ruciraṃ manoharaṃ vilepanaṃ candanādi vastraṃ mālyaṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ ca yeṣāṃ te tathā || KrdC_4.44 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vajra-pūrvāḥ</s> means beginning with <s>Vajra</s> (Indra); by color (<s>rucā</s>) means by complexion; in sequence (<s>kramataḥ</s>) means in order — they should be known as having such forms. Again, what kind? <s>Kāñcana</s> (gold), <s>raupya</s> (silver), <s>toyada</s> means cloud (<s>megha</s>), <s>abhra</s> (cloud), <s>campaka</s>-flower, <s>aruṇa</s> means red, <s>hima</s> means white, <s>nīla</s> (blue), <s>śyāmala</s> (dark), <s>javā</s> is the <s>auṇḍra</s>-flower (hibiscus), <s>pravāla</s> is a new sprout — those whose radiance is of such nature are so described. Again, what kind? Those who have beautiful (<s>rucira</s>) ointment (<s>vilepana</s>) such as sandalwood, garments (<s>vastra</s>), garlands (<s>mālya</s>), and ornaments (<s>bhūṣaṇa</s>) are so described.
He concludes what was previously stated —
The sevenfold covering (<s>āvṛti-saptaka</s>) has been described in the method
of worshipping <s>Acyuta</s> (the Imperishable One), bestowing all happiness.
Or, with effort, through <s>Aṅga</s> (limb-deities), <s>Purandara</s> (Indra),
<s>Śani</s> (Saturn), and others as chief, this threefold covering [may be performed].

children.text: iti pūrvokta-prakāreṇa viṣṇu-pūjā-vidhau āvaraṇa-saptakaṃ kathitam | kīdṛśaṃ ? sakala-sukhārtha-dāyakam | aśaktaṃ pratyāha prayajatād iti | pūrvoktāśaktaḥ tritayāvaraṇam āvaraṇa-traya-sahitaṃ prayajet | kaiḥ ? aṅgam indra-vajram etan-mukhair etat pradhānair ity arthaḥ || KrdC_4.45 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the previously described manner, the sevenfold covering (<s>āvaraṇa-saptaka</s>) in the method of <s>Viṣṇu</s>-worship has been described. What kind? Bestowing all happiness and fulfillment. He addresses the incapable one by saying 'let him worship' (<s>prayajatāt</s>). The previously mentioned incapable person should worship with the threefold covering — accompanied by three coverings. By whom? <s>Aṅga</s> means <s>Indra's</s> thunderbolt — with these as chief, meaning with these as primary — this is the meaning.
Concluding the main topic, he states an alternative worship —
Having thus worshipped with water, fragrance, and flowers,
then with the <s>Kṛṣṇāṣṭaka</s> (eight names of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), the worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;
the wise one should perform — those names (<s>samāhvayāni</s>)
I shall declare, beginning with 'tāt' and ending with '<s>namaḥ</s>' (salutation).

children.text: iti pūrvokta-prakāreṇa jala-gandha-puṣpaiḥ pūjayitvā athānantaraṃ kṛṣṇāṣṭakena vakṣyamāṇena budhaḥ paṇḍitaḥ kṛṣṇa-pūjāṃ kuryāt tāni | samāhvayāni nāmāni praṇavādi-namo 'ntikāni vakṣyamāṇāni oṃ kṛṣṇāya nama ity ādīni || KrdC_4.46 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, having worshipped in the previously described manner with water, fragrance, and flowers, thereafter with the <s>Kṛṣṇāṣṭaka</s> — about to be stated — the wise one (<s>budha</s>), the learned, should perform the worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. Those names — beginning with <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ) and ending with <s>namaḥ</s> — about to be stated — such as 'Oṃ <s>Kṛṣṇāya namaḥ</s>' and so forth.
He displays those very [names] —
<s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and one called <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>;

children.text: devakī-nandano yadu-śreṣṭho vārṣṇeya ity api // Krd_4.47 //
children.translated_text: <s>Devakī-nandana</s> (Son of <s>Devakī</s>), <s>Yadu-śreṣṭha</s> (Best of the <s>Yadu</s>s), and also <s>Vārṣṇeya</s>.
The seventh ends with the word <s>Asurāntaka</s> (Destroyer of demons), <s>Bhārahārī</s> (Remover of burdens);

children.text: dharma-saṃsthāpakaś cāṣṭau caturthy-antāḥ kramād ime // Krd_4.48 //
children.translated_text: and the eighth is <s>Dharma-saṃsthāpaka</s> (Establisher of <s>dharma</s>) — these, in order, end in the fourth [case, i.e., dative].

children.text: asurāntaka-śabdānte bhāra-hārīty arthaḥ | ime kṛṣṇādayaḥ śabdāḥ kramād ekaikaśaḥ praṇavādyāś caturthy-antā namo 'ntakāś ca vijñeyāḥ || KrdC_4.47-48 ||
children.translated_text: The word <s>asurāntaka-śabdānte</s> means ending with <s>Bhārahārī</s> — this is the meaning. These words beginning with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, in sequence, one by one, beginning with <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ), ending in the dative case (fourth case) and ending with <s>namaḥ</s>, should be understood.
He addresses the extremely incapable one —
With these very [names], alternatively, worship should be performed for the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>;
by the wise, for crossing over the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), for the attainment of all desires.

children.text: athavā ebhir eva kṛṣṇādibhiḥ śabdaiḥ kaṃsavairiṇaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇasya pūjā budhaiḥ | paṇḍitaiḥ kartavyā | kim artham ? saṃsāra eva sāgaraḥ tasya uttīrtyai uttaraṇāya | punaḥ kim artham ? sakala-manoratha-prāpty-artham || KrdC_4.49 ||
children.translated_text: Alternatively, with these very words beginning with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, worship of the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> — <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> — should be performed by the wise, by the learned. For what purpose? For crossing over — for traversing — the ocean that is <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). And again, for what purpose? For the attainment of all desires.
He shows the method of offering incense (<s>dhūpa</s>) —
Upon good charcoal, with powdered [substances] mixed with ghee,
with <s>guggulu</s> (bdellium) and other richly fragrant [materials], having prepared the incense, the ritualist (<s>mantrī</s>)
should offer it low [at the navel] to the Destroyer of demons (<s>Danuja-mathana</s>), and then with the other hand
should ring a bell (<s>ghaṇṭā</s>) that has been worshipped with fragrance, unbroken rice, and flowers.

children.text: sārāṅgāre dṛḍha-kāṣṭhāṅgāre | khādirāṅgāre iti tripāṭhinaḥ | saṃvikīrṇaiḥ kṣiptaiḥ guggulv-ādyaiḥ guggulu-śarkarā-madhu-candanāguru-śīraiḥ ghṛta-vilulitair dhṛta-plutaiḥ jarjaraiḥ kuṭṭanena cūrṇitair ghana-parimalair niviḍa-saurabha-śālibhiḥ dhūpam āpādya kṛtvā mantrī upāsakaḥ nīcair nābhi-pradeśe danuja-mathanāya gopāla-kṛṣṇāya dadyāt | kiṃ kurvan ? athānantaram apareṇa vāmena doṣṇā hastena gaja-dhvani-mantra-mātaḥ svāheti ghaṇṭāṃ vādayan | kimbhūtām ? gandhākṣata-puṣpaiḥ pūjitām || KrdC_4.50 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sārāṅgāre</s> means upon firm wood-charcoal; 'upon <s>khādira</s> (acacia) charcoal' — thus [say] the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s. <s>Saṃvikīrṇaiḥ</s> means scattered, thrown; with <s>guggulu</s> and others — <s>guggulu</s>, sugar, honey, sandalwood, <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood), and <s>śīra</s> (vetiver); mixed with ghee (<s>ghṛta-vilulita</s>) means soaked in ghee; <s>jarjara</s> means pulverized by pounding; <s>ghana-parimala</s> means possessing dense fragrance. Having prepared the incense — having made it — the ritualist (<s>mantrī</s>), the worshipper, should offer it low, at the navel region, to <s>Danuja-mathana</s> — to <s>Gopāla Kṛṣṇa</s>. Doing what? Then, with the other — the left — hand, sounding the bell with the mantra '<s>gaja-dhvani</s>... <s>svāhā</s>.' Of what kind [is the bell]? Worshipped with fragrance, unbroken rice, and flowers.
He shows the method regarding the offering of a lamp (<s>dīpa</s>) —
Likewise, the lamp, with a wick soaked in fragrant ghee mixed with camphor,
blazing, the one of extremely clear intellect, [should show it] from the lotus [i.e., head] down, held high;

children.text: dattvā puṣpāñjalim api ca vidhāyārpayitvā ca pādyaṃ
children.translated_text: having offered a handful of flowers (<s>puṣpāñjali</s>) and also having offered foot-water (<s>pādya</s>),
together with <s>ācamana</s> (sipping water), one should arrange the food-offering (<s>nivedya</s>) in a large golden vessel.

children.text: tadvad āpādya dīpaṃ kuryāt | kayā ? surabhi sugandhi yad ghṛtaṃ tena siktā ukṣitā karpūra-sahitā vartis tayā | kīdṛśam ? dṛṣṭyā dīptam | dṛṣṭi-manoharam iti rudradharaḥ | padma-paryantaṃ mastaka-paryantam uccair upari dattvā dṛṣṭyādīti dakṣiṇāvartena padma-paryantam | caraṇa-kamala-paryantam iti tripāṭhinaḥ | pāda-paryantam iti kvacit pāṭhaḥ | anantaraṃ puṣpāñjalim api śirasi dattvā pādyācamanīye ca dattvā vipula-svarṇa-pātre bṛhat-kanaka-bhājane naivedyaṃ kalpayatu sampādayatu | sācāmam ācamana-sahitaṃ prathamaṃ vadanety ādibhir ācamanaṃ dattvā anantaraṃ naivedyaṃ dadātv ity arthaḥ || KrdC_4.51 ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, having prepared the lamp, one should perform [the offering]. With what? With a wick soaked (<s>siktā</s>) — moistened — in fragrant (<s>surabhi</s>) ghee, together with camphor. Of what kind? Blazing as seen by the eye — 'delightful to the eye' thus [says] <s>Rudradhara</s>. From the lotus [head] down to the top, showing it above — or, [moving it] clockwise from the viewing point to the lotus [feet] — 'down to the lotus-feet' thus [say] the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s. 'Down to the feet' is another reading. Then, having offered a handful of flowers upon the head, and having given foot-water and <s>ācamanīya</s>, in a large golden vessel — a big golden plate — one should arrange the food-offering (<s>naivedya</s>). Together with <s>ācamana</s> — first saying 'into the mouth' etc., having given <s>ācamana</s>, then one should give the <s>naivedya</s> — this is the meaning.
He shows the nature of the food-offering (<s>naivedya</s>) —
With very fragrant milk-rice (<s>dugdhānna</s>), well-cooked, with sugar
accompaniments, with delightful, pleasing, and varied flavors;
with curd (<s>dadhi</s>), fresh butter (<s>navanīta</s>), new rock-sugar (<s>sitopala</s>), cakes (<s>pūpa</s>), fried sweets (<s>puli</s>),
ghee, jaggery (<s>guḍa</s>), coconut (<s>nārikela</s>), banana (<s>kadalī</s>) fruits, and flower-juice [honey].

children.text: atisurabhiṇā dugdhānnena suśṛtena supakvena sitā-samupadeśakaiḥ śarkarā-vyañjanaiḥ saha | śarkarayā saha upadaṃśakair vyañjanair iti tripāṭhinaḥ | asmin pakṣe śucitena sitā-samupadaṃśakair iti pāṭhaḥ | rucira icchī̀akaraḥ hṛdyaḥ susvādaḥ vicitro madhurādi-raso yeṣu taiḥ nūtanaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ sitopalaṃ khaṇḍādi-prasiddhaṃ puṣpa-raso madhu etair dravyair naivedyaṃ kalpayatu || KrdC_4.52 ||
children.translated_text: With very fragrant milk-rice, well-cooked — well-prepared — with sugar accompaniments — with sugar side-dishes. 'With sugar, together with side-dishes (<s>upadaṃśaka</s>)' — thus [say] the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s. In this interpretation, the reading is '<s>śucitena sitā-samupadaṃśakair</s>.' Delightful (<s>rucira</s>) means desirable; <s>hṛdya</s> means of good taste; <s>vicitra</s> means varied flavors such as sweet etc. — with those. New (<s>nūtana</s>) means excellent; <s>sitopala</s> means the well-known sugar-candy (<s>khaṇḍa</s>) etc.; flower-juice (<s>puṣpa-rasa</s>) is honey. With these substances, one should arrange the food-offering.
What kind of special food-offering should one arrange? On that, he says —
Having sprinkled it with the weapon[-mantra], protecting it with the enemy's (<s>tad-ari</s>) <s>mudrā</s> (seal-gesture),
having dried away faults with the <s>Vāyavya</s> (wind-mantra), and with the fire-heat
having burnt [impurities], filling it with nectar-essence from the left hand,
having made it immortal nectar through mantras, one should then touch and recite.
The mantra eight times, with the <s>surabhi-mudrā</s> (fragrance-gesture),
[seeing it as] full, one should worship with fragrance and other [offerings].
One should worship <s>Hari</s>, then with joined palms filled with flowers,
from his mouth should radiance (<s>mahas</s>) proceed forth.

children.text:
mūla-mantrāstra-mantreṇāstrāya phaḍ-ity anena vā ukṣitaṃ siktaṃ cakra-mudrayābhirakṣya vāyavyeti vāyu-bīja-japtodaka-prokṣaṇa-pariśoṣita-doṣam agni-doṣṇā sandahyeti ram iti vahni-bījābhijapta-dakṣiṇa-kareṇa spṛṣṭvā doṣān dagdhvā vāma-kara-saudha-rasābhipūraṇam iti vāma-hastena pidhāya baṃ-bīja-japenāmṛta-rasābhipūrṇaṃ vicintya mūla-mantreṇāmṛta-rūpaṃ vicintyāthānantaraṃ tad etādṛśaṃ naivedyam abhimṛśan spṛṣṭvā manuṃ mantram aṣṭaśaḥ aṣṭa-vāraṃ prajapatu surabhi-mudrikayā dhenu-mudrikayā paripūrṇaṃ naivedyaṃ vicintya gandha-mukhaiḥ candanādyaiḥ pūjayatu | dāna-prakāraṃ darśayati-harim ity ādinā | kṛta-prasavāñjalir hariṃ pratyarcayet naivedya-grahaṇāyāsyatas tejo niḥsaratv iti prārthayet
| athānantaram asya harer āsyato mukhatas tejo niḥsaret prasaratv iti cintayet | naivedye saṃyojayed iti tripāṭhinaḥ || KrdC_4.53-54 ||
children.translated_text: Having sprinkled (<s>ukṣita</s>) with the root mantra (<s>mūla-mantra</s>) weapon-mantra — or with '<s>astrāya phaṭ</s>' — and having protected with the <s>cakra-mudrā</s> (discus-gesture); having dried away faults by sprinkling with water consecrated by reciting the <s>Vāyu-bīja</s> (wind-seed syllable) in the <s>Vāyavya</s> [manner]; with fire-heat — having touched with the right hand consecrated by reciting '<s>raṃ</s>' the <s>Vahni-bīja</s> (fire-seed syllable), having burnt the faults; filling with nectar-essence from the left hand — covering with the left hand, through recitation of the '<s>baṃ</s>'-seed syllable, visualizing it as filled with nectar-essence; having visualized it as nectar-form through the root mantra — then, touching such <s>naivedya</s>, one should recite the mantra (<s>manu</s>) eight times. With the <s>surabhi-mudrā</s> — the <s>dhenu-mudrā</s> (cow-gesture) — visualizing the <s>naivedya</s> as full, one should worship with fragrance — sandalwood and others. He shows the manner of offering — with '<s>Harim</s>' etc. With joined palms filled with flowers, one should worship <s>Hari</s> and pray that radiance may emerge from his mouth for accepting the <s>naivedya</s>. Then, from the mouth of this <s>Hari</s>, one should visualize radiance emerging and proceeding forth. 'One should unite [the radiance] with the <s>naivedya</s>' — thus [say] the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s.
Uttering the root mantra ending with <s>Vītihotra-dayitā</s> (beloved of the fire-god, i.e., <s>Svāhā</s>),
one should then drop water;
one should offer that oblation (<s>havis</s>) which has become immortal nectar,
lifting it with both hands together with beautiful flowers.

children.text: athānantaraṃ vīti-hotra-dayitāntaṃ svāhā-kārāntaṃ mūla-mantram uccaran kiṃcij jalaṃ tad-upari kṣipet prokṣayet | atra svāhānte 'pi mantre punaḥ svāhā-pada-prayogaḥ kāryaḥ etad-balād eva anantara-dor-yujā hasta-dvayena sa-kusumaṃ sa-puṣpaṃ samuddharan uttolayan tad-amṛtātmakaṃ haviḥ samarpayet || KrdC_4.55 ||
children.translated_text: Then, uttering the root mantra ending with <s>Vītihotra-dayitā</s> — ending with <s>Svāhā</s>-utterance — one should drop a little water upon it, sprinkle [it]. Here, even though the mantra already ends with <s>Svāhā</s>, the word <s>Svāhā</s> should be uttered again — by the force of this [rule], thereafter with both hands (<s>dor-yujā</s>), lifting — raising up — together with flowers (<s>sa-kusuma</s>), one should offer that oblation which has become immortal nectar.
He states the mantra for offering the <s>naivedya</s> —
'I offer to the Lord; may <s>Hari</s> accept this oblation;'
This is the <s>naivedya</s>-offering mantra, [used] in all worship with one's own name [of the deity].

children.text: ayaṃ mantraḥ sarvāsu devānāṃ pūjāsu nijākhyayeti hare ity asmin sthāne yasmai devāya dīyate tan-nāma-grahaṇaṃkartavyam iti nijākhyā-śabdārthaḥ | nivedyākhyayeti kecit || KrdC_4.56 ||
children.translated_text: This mantra [is used] in all worship of the gods, with one's own name — meaning at the place where '<s>Hare</s>' [appears], the name of whichever deity the offering is given to should be inserted — this is the meaning of the term '<s>nijākhyā</s>' (one's own name). 'With the name of the <s>nivedya</s> [deity]' — [say] some.
He shows the special <s>mudrā</s> (hand-gesture) associated with feeding —
The <s>grāsa-mudrā</s> (morsel-gesture), with the left hand, resembling a fully bloomed lotus;

children.text: pradarśayed dakṣiṇena prāṇādīnāṃ ca darśayet // Krd_4.57 //
children.translated_text: one should display [it], and with the right [hand] should show the [<s>mudrā</s>s] of <s>Prāṇa</s> and others.

children.text: vāma-doṣṇā grāsa-mudrāṃ darśayet | kimbhūtām ? praphullotpala-sadṛśīm | anantaraṃ dakṣiṇa-hastena prāṇādīnāṃ vakṣyamāṇāṃ mudrāṃ darśayed iti || KrdC_4.57 ||
children.translated_text: With the left hand, one should display the <s>grāsa-mudrā</s>. Of what kind? Resembling a fully bloomed lotus. Thereafter, with the right hand, one should display the <s>mudrā</s> of <s>Prāṇa</s> and others — about to be described.
One should touch the little finger and ring finger — these two —
with the tip of the thumb; this is the first <s>mudrā</s>.
Likewise, the second is with the index and middle fingers;
and the third is with the ring finger and middle finger.
The ring finger, index finger, and middle finger [together];
likewise, the fourth — with [the addition of] the little finger;
the fifth is likewise — thus are declared
the <s>Prāṇa</s> and other <s>mudrā</s>s, accompanied by their respective mantras.

children.text: kaniṣṭhopakaniṣṭhe kaniṣṭhānāmike dve svāṅguṣṭha-mūrdhnā spṛśet | iha mudrā prathamā tathā tarjanī-madhyame svāṅguṣṭha-mūrdhnā spṛśet anāmika-madhyamike ca tena spṛśed evaṃ vyāna-mudrā anāmā-tarjanī-madhyamās tena spṛśet | caturthī udānasya tās tisraḥ kaniṣṭhā-sahitāḥ | tadvat svāṅguṣṭha-mūrdhnā yadi spṛśet tadā samāna-mudrā ity anena prakāreṇa prāṇādi-mudrāḥ pradiṣṭāḥ kathitāḥ | kimbhūtāḥ ? yathāyogya-sva-mantra-sahitāḥ mantra-sāhityena tāsāṃ mudrātvaṃ bhavati bilva-mudrāvad ity arthaḥ || KrdC_4.58-59 ||
children.translated_text: The little finger and ring finger (<s>kaniṣṭhopakaniṣṭhe</s>) — the little finger and ring finger, these two — one should touch with the tip of one's thumb. This is the first <s>mudrā</s>. Likewise, the index and middle fingers — one should touch with the tip of one's thumb. And the ring finger and middle finger — one should touch with it [the thumb]. Thus is the <s>Vyāna-mudrā</s>. The ring finger, index finger, and middle finger — one should touch with it [the thumb]. The fourth is of <s>Udāna</s> — those three together with the little finger. Likewise, if one touches [all of them] with the tip of the thumb, then it is the <s>Samāna-mudrā</s>. In this manner, the <s>Prāṇa</s> and other <s>mudrā</s>s are declared — stated. Of what kind? Accompanied by their respective appropriate mantras — through the association with mantras, their nature as <s>mudrā</s>s is established, like the <s>bilva-mudrā</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: ke te mantrā ity ākāṅkṣāyāṃ prāṇādīnāṃ mantrān āha-
children.translated_text: In anticipation of 'what are those mantras?' — he states the mantras of <s>Prāṇa</s> and others —
<s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Apāna</s>, <s>Vyāna</s>, <s>Udāna</s>, and <s>Samāna</s> — in sequence, ending in the dative case (fourth case);

children.text: tārādhārā vadhvā ceddhāḥ kṛṣṇādhvanas tv ime manavaḥ // Krd_4.60 //
children.translated_text: based on <s>Tāra</s> (Oṃ), conjoined with the beloved (<s>vadhū</s>) of <s>Kṛṣṇādhvan</s> (fire, i.e., <s>Svāhā</s>) — these are the mantras.

children.text: prāṇādayaḥ pañca kramāc caturthī-vibhakti-sahitāḥ tathā tārā-dhārāḥ oṃkārādhārāḥ praṇavādyā ity arthaḥ | tathā kṛṣṇādhvano 'gner vadhvā priyayā iddhā uddīptāḥ sambaddhāḥ svāhā-kārāntā ity arthaḥ | evaṃ ca sati oṃ prāṇāya svāhā ity ādyāḥ pañca mantrā bhavatīty arthaḥ || KrdC_4.60 ||
children.translated_text: The five beginning with <s>Prāṇa</s>, in sequence, accompanied by the dative case (fourth inflection); likewise, based on <s>Tāra</s> — based on <s>Oṃkāra</s>, meaning beginning with <s>Praṇava</s>. And conjoined (<s>iddhā</s>) — connected with — the beloved (<s>vadhū</s>, wife) of <s>Kṛṣṇādhvan</s> (fire) — meaning ending with <s>Svāhā</s>. Thus, the five mantras are 'Oṃ <s>Prāṇāya Svāhā</s>' and so forth — this is the meaning.
Displaying the <s>nivedya-mudrā</s> (offering-gesture), he also shows the mantra —
Then, the <s>nivedya-mudrā</s> (offering-gesture), with the principal [fingers] on both hands;

children.text: spṛśann anāmikāṃ nijaṃ manuṃ japan pradarśayet // Krd_4.61 //
children.translated_text: touching the ring finger, reciting one's own mantra, one should display [it].

children.text: tatas tad-anantaraṃ nivedya-mudrāṃ pradarśayet | kiṃ kurvan ? kara-dvaye karayor anāmikāṃ pradhānayāṅguṣṭhena spṛśan | punaḥ kiṃ kurvan ? nijaṃ svīyaṃ manuṃ mantraṃ prajapan || KrdC_4.61 ||
children.translated_text: Then, immediately after that, one should display the <s>nivedya-mudrā</s> (offering gesture). How? Touching the ring finger — the principal one — with the thumb on both hands (<s>kara-dvaye</s>). Again, what else? While softly chanting (<s>prajapan</s>) one's own <s>manu</s> (mantra).
He extracts the mantra —

<s>Nandaja</s> (born of <s>Nanda</s>, i.e., the letter <s>ṭha</s>), water (<s>ambu</s>, i.e., the letter <s>va</s>), <s>manu</s> (i.e., the syllable <s>au</s>), joined with <s>bindu</s> (dot); <s>nati</s> (i.e., <s>namaḥ</s>);
<s>Pārśva</s> (i.e., the letter <s>pa</s>), <s>rā</s> as itself, <s>marut</s> (wind, i.e., the letter <s>ya</s>), <s>avātmane</s> with <s>ni</s> and <s>ca</s>;
<s>Ruddha</s> as itself, joined with <s>ṅe</s> (dative case); <s>nivedyam</s> (offering); <s>ātma-bhū</s> (self-born, i.e., the letter <s>ka</s>);
<s>Māsa</s> (i.e., the letter <s>la</s>), <s>pārśva</s> (i.e., the letter <s>pa</s>), <s>anila</s> (wind, i.e., the letter <s>ya</s>), likewise joined with <s>ami</s>.

children.text: nandajaḥ ṭha-kāraḥ ambuḥ va-kāraḥ manuḥ au-kāraḥ binduḥ etair yuktā natir namaḥ pārśvaḥ pa-kāraḥ rā iti svarūpaṃ marut ya-kāraḥ avātmane iti ani svarūpaṃ ruddhaṃ iti svarūpaṃ ṅe caturthī aniruddha-śabdaś caturthī-yukta ity arthaḥ | nivedyam iti trayaḥ ātma-bhūḥ ka-kāraḥ māṃso la-kāraḥ pārśvaḥ pa-kāraḥ la-kāra-ya-kārābhyāṃ yukto 'nilo ya-kāraḥ amīti svarūpaṃ tathā ṭhvauṃ namaḥ paryāvātmane aniruddhāya naivedyaṃ kalpayāmi iti mantraḥ || KrdC_4.62 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Nandaja</s> is the letter <s>ṭha</s>; <s>ambu</s> (water) is the letter <s>va</s>; <s>manu</s> is the syllable <s>au</s>; <s>bindu</s> — joined with these, <s>nati</s> means <s>namaḥ</s> (salutation). <s>Pārśva</s> is the letter <s>pa</s>; <s>rā</s> is itself; <s>marut</s> (wind) is the letter <s>ya</s>; <s>avātmane</s> — <s>ani</s> is itself; <s>ruddha</s> is itself; <s>ṅe</s> is the dative case — the word <s>aniruddha</s> in the dative case is the meaning. <s>Nivedyam</s> consists of three [syllables]; <s>ātma-bhū</s> (self-born) is the letter <s>ka</s>; <s>māṃsa</s> is the letter <s>la</s>; <s>pārśva</s> is the letter <s>pa</s>; joined with the letters <s>la</s> and <s>ya</s>, <s>anila</s> (wind) is the letter <s>ya</s>; <s>ami</s> is itself. Thus the mantra is: '<s>ṭhvauṃ namaḥ paryāvātmane Aniruddhāya naivedyaṃ kalpayāmi</s>' (I offer the <s>naivedya</s> to <s>Aniruddha</s>).
The <s>mantrī</s> (ritualist) all around the <s>maṇḍala</s>,
Having placed vessels of seed-sprouts;
Should also set up lamps made of flour,
Filled with ghee, with brightly blazing flames.

children.text: maṇḍala-parito bījāṅkura-pātrāṇi saṃsthāpya tathaiva piṣṭa-kṛtān ghṛta-paripūrṇān prajvalita-śikhān pradīpān sthāpayet || KrdC_4.63 ||
children.translated_text: Around the <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should set up vessels of seed-sprouts, and likewise lamps made of flour — filled with ghee, with kindled flames — one should place them.
He describes the procedure of the <s>homa</s> (fire-oblation) as part of <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) —
Then, in the duly consecrated fire, the one of pure intellect,
Having properly invoked and worshipped <s>Hari</s>,
Should offer oblations of milk prepared with
Sugar and ghee, through the moon-white [substance].
Having completed one thousand and eight [oblations],
After the <s>homa</s>, one should again offer <s>bali</s> (food-offerings);
To the presiding deities of the zodiacal signs (<s>rāśi</s>s),
To the <s>nakṣatra</s>s (lunar mansions), and then to the <s>karaṇa</s>s (half-lunar-days).

children.text:
