athānantaraṃ śāstrokta-saṃskāraiḥ saṃskṛte vahnau nirmala-buddhiḥ yathokta-rūpaṃ harim āvāhya gandhādibhiś ca yathāvidhi sampūjyāṣṭottara-sahasraṃ juhuyāt | kena sita-dīdhitinā bhaktena kīdṛśena payaḥ-parisādhitena dugdha-paripācitena paramānnenety arthaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśena ? sitā-ghṛta-yutena śarkarā-ghṛta-sahitena anantaraṃ yathokta-homaṃ samāpyāvaśiṣṭa-paramānnena rāśiṣu meṣādiṣu adhināthebhyo rāśi-devatābhyo maṅgalādibhyaḥ nakṣatrebhyo 'śvinyādibhyaḥ karaṇebhyo vavādibhyo baliṃ dadyāt | prayogas tu meṣa-vṛścikādhipataye maṅgalāya eṣa balir namaḥ evaṃ vṛṣa-tulādhipataye śukrāya mithuna-kanyādhipataye budhāya karkaṭādhipataye candrāya siṃhādhipataye sūryāya danur-mīnādhipataye gurave makara-kumbhādhipataye
śanaye eva balir namaḥ | evaṃ aśvanī-bharaṇī-kṛttikāpādīya-meṣa-rāśaye eṣa balir nama ity ādi | evaṃ vavavālakīlavataitila-gara-vaṇija-viṣṭibhyaḥ eṣa balir namaḥ || KrdC_4.64-65 ||
children.translated_text: Then, subsequently, in the fire consecrated with the rites prescribed in the <s>śāstra</s>s, the one of pure intellect, having invoked <s>Hari</s> in the prescribed form and having worshipped him duly with sandalwood and other [offerings], should offer one thousand and eight oblations. With what? With <s>sita-dīdhiti</s> (moon-white, i.e., rice-pudding) — of what kind? Prepared with milk (<s>payaḥ-parisādhita</s>), meaning cooked with milk — <s>paramānna</s> (the supreme food, i.e., rice-pudding) is the meaning. Again, of what kind? Mixed with sugar and ghee (<s>sitā-ghṛta-yuta</s>). Thereafter, having completed the prescribed <s>homa</s>, with the remaining <s>paramānna</s>, one should offer <s>bali</s> to the presiding deities of the zodiacal signs beginning with <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries) — to the <s>rāśi</s>-deities such as <s>Maṅgala</s> (Mars) and others — to the <s>nakṣatra</s>s beginning with <s>Aśvinī</s>, and to the <s>karaṇa</s>s beginning with <s>Vava</s>. The practical application is: 'To <s>Maṅgala</s>, the lord of <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries) and <s>Vṛścika</s> (Scorpio) — this <s>bali</s>, salutations.' Similarly, to <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), the lord of <s>Vṛṣa</s> (Taurus) and <s>Tulā</s> (Libra); to <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), the lord of <s>Mithuna</s> (Gemini) and <s>Kanyā</s> (Virgo); to <s>Candra</s> (Moon), the lord of <s>Karkaṭa</s> (Cancer); to <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun), the lord of <s>Siṃha</s> (Leo); to <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter), the lord of <s>Dhanus</s> (Sagittarius) and <s>Mīna</s> (Pisces); to <s>Śani</s> (Saturn), the lord of <s>Makara</s> (Capricorn) and <s>Kumbha</s> (Aquarius) — this <s>bali</s>, salutations. Similarly: 'To the <s>Meṣa-rāśi</s> of <s>Aśvinī</s>, <s>Bharaṇī</s>, and the first quarter of <s>Kṛttikā</s> — this <s>bali</s>, salutations' — and so forth. Similarly, to <s>Vava</s>, <s>Bālava</s>, <s>Kaulava</s>, <s>Taitila</s>, <s>Gara</s>, <s>Vaṇija</s>, and <s>Viṣṭi</s> — this <s>bali</s>, salutations.
He describes the procedure after worship —
Having given water and having removed the flame from the mouth [of the deity] into the mouth [of the vessel],
Having lifted the <s>naivedya</s> (food-offering) and offered it all around
To the army [of attendant deities], and having smeared the ground again,
Having prepared the drinking water as nectar and offered it,

children.text: pānīyam eva dhenu-mudrayā sudhāṃ kṛtvā pānārthaṃ kṛṣṇāya samarpyāmbho dattvā jalam ācamanārthaṃ dattvā mukhārcir-deva-mukhān naivedye 'vatāritaṃ teja āsye deva-mukhe udvāsya niveśya naivedyam uttolya viśvaksenāya deva-gaṇāya naivedyaṃ samarpya pṛthivīm upalipya || KrdC_4.66 ||
children.translated_text: Having transformed the water itself into nectar through the <s>dhenu-mudrā</s> (cow gesture) and offered it to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> for drinking, having given water — water for <s>ācamana</s> (ritual sipping) — having removed the <s>mukhārcis</s> (the radiance placed at the mouth of the deity) from the <s>naivedya</s> and placed it back in the mouth of the deity, having lifted the <s>naivedya</s>, having offered the <s>naivedya</s> to <s>Viśvaksena</s> and the host of deities all around, and having smeared the ground,
Mouthwash, tooth-cleaning, sipping-water, face-and-hand
Wiping, anointing, mouth-fragrance, garlands, ornaments;
Having also offered <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel), with excellent music, dance,

children.text: gītaiḥ sutṛptam abhipūjayatāt punar eva // Krd_4.67 //
children.translated_text: And songs, one should worship the fully satisfied [Lord] once again.

children.text: bhūyaḥ punar api gaṇḍūṣaṃ culūkodakaṃ danta-dhavanaṃ danta-kāṣṭham | danta-dhavanaṃ danta-dhāvanam iti tripāṭhinaḥ | ācamanaṃ śeṣācamane dvir-ācamanam āsya-hastayor mṛjyaṃ mukha-hastayoḥ proñchana-vastram anulepaś candanādiḥ mukhaṃ vāsyate surabhi kriyate aneneti mukha-vāsaṃ karpūrādi mālyaṃ puṣpaṃ bhūṣālaṅkaraṇaṃ tāmbūlam api samuccaye etāni samarpya punar eva yathā-pūrvaṃ pūjā kṛtā evaṃ suvādya-nṛtya-gītaiḥ sutṛptaṃ hariṃ natvā bhipūjayet || KrdC_4.67 ||
children.translated_text: Again — once more — <s>gaṇḍūṣa</s> is a mouthful of water; <s>danta-dhavana</s> is a tooth-stick; some read <s>danta-dhavana</s> as <s>danta-dhāvana</s> (tooth-washing) — thus the three readings. <s>Ācamana</s> is the residual sipping-water — sipping twice; <s>mṛjya</s> of the mouth and hands means a wiping cloth for the face and hands; <s>anulepa</s> is sandalwood and the like; <s>mukha-vāsa</s> — that by which the mouth is perfumed, made fragrant — is camphor and the like; <s>mālya</s> is flowers; <s>bhūṣā</s> is ornament; <s>tāmbūla</s> also — the word 'also' is for inclusion of all — having offered these, once again as before, just as worship was performed, so too with excellent music, dance, and songs, having bowed to the fully satisfied <s>Hari</s>, one should worship [Him].
With fragrant substances and the like, to him together with his retinue, then the <s>arghya</s> (offering-water),
Having given, and having offered a flower-<s>añjali</s> (cupped-hand offering) with devotion,
Having praised and bowed with the head, with a handful of water,
One should offer oneself at the base of those lotus-feet.

children.text: kaiḥ ? gandhādibhiḥ saparivāraṃ pūrvoktāvaraṇa-sahitam athānantaram asmai haraye arghyaṃ dattvā ādareṇa puṣpāñjaliṃ dattvā stutvā śirasā praṇamya sac-caraṇāravinda-mūle svātmānaṃ culukena argha-śeṣa-jalena samarpayatu || KrdC_4.68 ||
children.translated_text: With what? With fragrant substances and the like, together with the retinue — accompanied by the surrounding deities mentioned earlier. Then, subsequently, having given the <s>arghya</s> to <s>Hari</s>, having offered a flower-<s>añjali</s> with devotion, having praised [Him] and bowed with the head, at the base of those blessed lotus-feet, one should offer oneself with a <s>culuka</s> (cupped handful) of the remaining <s>arghya</s>-water.

children.text: ātmanaḥ samarpaṇa-mantram āha ita ity ādinā svātma-samarpaṇe ity antena granthena-
children.translated_text: He states the mantra for self-offering, beginning with '<s>ita</s>' and ending with '<s>svātma-samarpaṇe</s>' —

children.text: itaḥ pūrvaṃ prāṇa-buddhi-deha-dharmādhikārato jāgrat-svapna-suṣupty-avasthāsu manasā vācā karmaṇā hastābhyāṃ padbhyām udareṇa śiśnā yat smṛtaṃ yad uktaṃ yat kṛtaṃ tat sarvaṃ brahmārpaṇaṃ bhavatu svāhā māṃ madīyaṃ ca sakalaṃ haraye samyag arpaye oṃ tat sad iti ca prokta-mantraḥ svātma-samarpaṇe ||
children.translated_text: Before this, whatever has been remembered, spoken, or done — by virtue of life-breath, intellect, body, and dharma, in the states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep — by mind, speech, action, with hands, with feet, with the belly, with the organ — all that, may it become an offering to <s>Brahman</s>. <s>Svāhā</s>! I duly offer myself and all that is mine to <s>Hari</s>. <s>Oṃ tat sat</s> — thus is the declared mantra for the offering of one's own self.

children.text: etac ca mantra-trayaṃ spaṣṭatvān na likhyate-
children.translated_text: And this triad of mantras is not written here, being self-evident —
Meditating upon <s>Acyuta</s> (the Imperishable One) who dwells in the <s>kalaśa</s> (vessel), the wise one should chant
The <s>manu</s> (mantra) one thousand and eight times.
Then, upon the body of the Conqueror of the <s>Daitya</s>s (demons), the surrounding [deities],

children.text: vilāpya tās tad api nayet sudhātmatām // Krd_4.69 //
children.translated_text: Having dissolved them, one should lead that also to the state of nectar (<s>sudhātmatā</s>).

children.text: athānantaraṃ budhaḥ paṇḍitaḥ kalaśagaṃ kumbhādi-niṣṭhaṃ hariṃ cintayan sāṣṭakam aṣṭa-sahitaṃ sahasraṃ manuṃ mantraṃ japet | athānantaraṃ ditija-jitaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇasya vapuṣi śarīre tāḥ pūrvoktāḥ samāvṛtīḥ āvaraṇa-devatā vilāpy vilīnā iti vicintya tad api deva-vapuḥ sudhātmatām amṛtatāṃ nayet || KrdC_4.69 ||
children.translated_text: Then, subsequently, the wise one (<s>budha</s>), meditating upon <s>Hari</s> who resides in the <s>kumbha</s> (vessel) and other [receptacles], should chant the <s>manu</s> (mantra) one thousand and eight times. Then, subsequently, upon the body of the Conqueror of the <s>Daitya</s>s — of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> — those aforementioned <s>samāvṛti</s>s (surrounding deities of the <s>āvaraṇa</s>), having imagined them as dissolved — merged — that also — the divine body — one should lead to the state of nectar (<s>sudhātmatā</s>), to immortality.
The consciousness (<s>citi</s>) stationed in the flags, arches, directional vessels, and the like,
As well as that stationed in the pavilion, <s>maṇḍala</s>, and fire-pit —
Having concentrated [it all] into the <s>kalaśa</s>, with flowers,
Having worshipped, one should chant again one hundred and eight times.

children.text: kalaśe citiṃ mantra-devatāṃ caitanya-rūpam abhiyojya kusumaiḥ puṣpaiḥ sampūjya punar aṣṭa-sahitaṃ śataṃ japet | kimbhūtām ? citiṃ dhvaja-toraṇa-dik-kalaśādi-gatāṃ na kevalaṃ dhvajādi-gatām api tu maṇḍale maṇḍape kuṇḍa-gatām || KrdC_4.70 ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>kalaśa</s>, having concentrated the <s>citi</s> — the mantra-deity in the form of consciousness — and having worshipped with flowers, one should again chant one hundred and eight times. Of what kind is this <s>citi</s>? That which is stationed in the flags, arches, directional vessels, and the like — not only in the flags and such, but also in the <s>maṇḍala</s>, the pavilion, and the fire-pit.
Then, the disciple, having fasted, in the morning,
Having performed the daily rites, wearing white garments, well-adorned;
With gifts of land, wealth, grains, and cattle,
Should gratify the best of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, for the grace of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: athānantaram upoṣitaḥ kṛtopavāsaḥ śiṣyaḥ prabhāte prātaḥ-kāle kṛta-nitya-kṛtyaḥ śukla-vastra-dharaḥ suveśaḥ śobhana-bhūṣaṇaḥ dharaṇī pṛthivī dhanaṃ suvarṇādi dhānyaṃ vrīhy-ādi gaur dogdhrī dukūlaṃ paṭṭa-vastram etair yathā-yogyaṃ vipra-varān brāhmaṇa-śreṣṭhān dhinuyāt prīṇayet | kim-artham ? hareḥ śrī-kṛṣṇasya prasādārtham || KrdC_4.71 ||
children.translated_text: Then, subsequently, the disciple — who has observed a fast — in the morning, at dawn, having performed the daily rites, wearing white garments, well-adorned with beautiful ornaments — with land (<s>dharaṇī</s>), wealth (<s>dhana</s>) such as gold, grains (<s>dhānya</s>) such as rice, cows (<s>gau</s>) — milch-cows, and fine silk cloth (<s>dukūla</s>) — with these as appropriate, should gratify — please — the best of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s. For what purpose? For the grace of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>.
Again, having gratified and bowed to the preceptor (<s>deśika</s>),
To that Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s> (Person), the embodied one,
Abandoning stinginess of wealth, the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fee),

children.text: dattvā tanuṃ svāṃ ca samarpayet sudhīḥ // Krd_4.72 //
children.translated_text: Having given, the wise one should also offer his own body.

children.text: bhūyaḥ punar api pratarpya brāhmaṇān santoṣya punaḥ kathanam atyanta-tarpaṇārthaṃ parītyeti pāṭhe pradakṣiṇī-kṛtyety arthaḥ | deśikaṃ guruṃ praṇipatya namaskṛtya tasmai gurave dehine deha-dhāriṇe parasmai puruṣāya śrī-kṛṣṇāya dhana-śāṭhyaṃ parihṛtya vaibhavānusāreṇa tāṃ prasiddhāṃ vittārdhaṃ caturthāṃśaṃ vā dattvā na tu dakṣiṇām iva mantrādānānantaram eva tat-prasaṅgāt svāṃ svīyāṃ tanuṃ subuddhiḥ samarpayet || KrdC_4.72 ||
children.translated_text: Again — once more — having gratified the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, having pleased them; the repetition is for the sake of extreme gratification. In the reading '<s>parītya</s>,' the meaning is 'having circumambulated.' Having bowed — having made obeisance — to the preceptor (<s>deśika</s>), the <s>guru</s>; to that <s>guru</s>, the embodied one — the bearer of a body — to the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>; abandoning stinginess of wealth, according to one's means, having given that well-known [<s>dakṣiṇā</s>] — half or a quarter of one's wealth — not, however, the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> [only] at the time of mantra-initiation and immediately thereafter — on that occasion, the one of good intellect should offer his own body.
Then, in the consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) pavilion, comfortably seated on a seat,

children.text: gurur viśodhayed amuṃ pureva śoṣaṇādibhiḥ // Krd_4.73 //
children.translated_text: The <s>guru</s> should purify him as before, with the drying (<s>śoṣaṇa</s>) and other [rites].

children.text: athānantaraṃ gurur amuṃ śiṣyaṃ pureva pūrvavad eva śoṣaṇādibhir bhūta-śuddhy-ādibhir viśodhayet | kīdṛśam ? abhiṣeka-maṇḍape āsane sukhopaviṣṭam || KrdC_4.73 ||
children.translated_text: Then, subsequently, the <s>guru</s> should purify this disciple as before — just as previously — with the drying and other [rites], i.e., with the <s>bhūta-śuddhi</s> (elemental purification) and similar [procedures]. In what state? Comfortably seated on a seat in the consecration pavilion.
Upon the body, the one of pure intellect, having performed placements up to the <s>pīṭha-nyāsa</s> (seat-placement), of that sword-[like mantra],
Having worshipped with the mantra, having placed <s>rocanā</s> (yellow orpiment) adorned with <s>dūrvā</s> grass, unbroken rice, and flowers upon the head;
With blessings of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, with clear and resonant sounds, with singing, instrumental music, and ceremonial sounds,

children.text: māṅgalyair ānayattaṃ kalaśam abhivṛtas tat-samīpaṃ pratītaḥ // Krd_4.74 //
children.translated_text: With auspicious [rites], the chosen one, surrounded [by attendants], should bring that <s>kalaśa</s> (vessel) near him.

children.text: tasya śiṣyasya vapuṣi śarīre pīṭha-nyāsāvasānaṃ pīṭha-nyāsa-paryantaṃ sakalaṃ nyāsaṃ vinyasya āsikāyā āsanasya mantreṇāsanaṃ pūjayitvā rocanāṃ mastake nidhāya tilakaṃ kārayitvā | kīdṛśīṃ rocanām ? dūrvākṣata-puṣpa-sahitām | anantaraṃ dvijānām āśīrvādair gīti-maṅgalādi-śabdaiḥ | kīdṛśair etaiḥ ? viśada-paṭu-ravaiḥ spaṣṭottama-śabdaiḥ tathā anyair api māṅgalyair maṅgalasyopayuktaiḥ sahitaṃ taṃ kalaśam abhivṛta ācāryatvena vṛtaḥ tat-samīpaṃ śiṣya-samīpam ānayet | kīdṛśaḥ ? śiṣyātmīyatayā pratīto viśvāsānvito yaḥ kaścid ity arthaḥ || KrdC_4.74 ||
children.translated_text: Upon the body — the person — of that disciple, having performed all the placements up to and including the <s>pīṭha-nyāsa</s> (seat-placement), having worshipped the seat with the seat-mantra, having placed the <s>rocanā</s> (yellow orpiment) upon the head — having applied the <s>tilaka</s> mark — of what kind of <s>rocanā</s>? Accompanied by <s>dūrvā</s> grass, unbroken rice, and flowers. Thereafter, with the blessings of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>s, with songs, auspicious sounds, and the like — of what kind? Clear and resonant in sound — and also with other auspicious things conducive to auspiciousness, together with that <s>kalaśa</s>, the one chosen as <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor) should bring [it] near the disciple. Of what kind is he? One who is trusted, having confidence in the disciple as his own — whoever [such a person may be] — that is the meaning.
With that [vessel] in which are immersed gems, mantras, and great herbs,
With that radiance which partakes of the form of supreme nectar,
Filling the body of this [disciple], then extending
That unity (<s>sāmarasya</s>), one should perform the consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) duly.

children.text: kumbhasya palvalān śiṣya-śirasi nidhāya tena kalasenety arthād yathāvat yathā-yukta-prakāreṇābhiṣecayet abhiṣecanaṃ kuryāt | tad uktam-
children.translated_text: Having placed the base of the <s>kumbha</s> upon the disciple's head, with that <s>kalaśa</s> — this is the intended meaning — one should perform the consecration in the proper manner. As it has been stated: 'Having duly lifted the <s>kumbha</s>, having placed the wish-fulfilling trees situated at its mouth upon the head of the disciple, one should mentally chant the <s>Mātṛkā</s> (alphabet).'

children.text:
vidhivat kumbham uddhṛtya tan-mukhasthān sura-drumān |
śiśoḥ śirasi vinyasya mātṛkāṃ manasā japet || iti |
children.translated_text:
As prescribed, having lifted the <s>kumbha</s>, having placed upon the head of the disciple the divine trees at its mouth;
one should mentally chant the <s>Mātṛkā</s> — thus.

children.text: kimbhūtena ? abhilīnaḥ saṃlīnaḥ maṇir nava-ratnāni mantraḥ ṛk mahauṣadhaṃ divya-pippalī-prabhṛti yatra tena | kīdṛśena ? pareṇa dhāmnā para-tejaḥ-svarūpeṇa | punaḥ kīdṛśena ? paramāmṛta-rūpa-bhājā paramāmṛta-rūpa-mayena | kiṃ kurvan ? amuṣya śiśor vapuḥ śarīraṃ pūrayan | kiṃ kurvan ? tatas tad-anantaraṃ tat-sāmarasyaṃ tena tena tejo-rūpeṇa kalaśaikyaṃ vitanvan || KrdC_4.75 ||
children.translated_text: Of what kind? That in which are immersed (<s>abhilīna</s>) — merged — gems (<s>maṇi</s>), the nine precious stones; mantras — Vedic verses (<s>ṛk</s>); great herbs (<s>mahauṣadha</s>) such as divine long-pepper and the like. Of what kind? Possessing supreme radiance (<s>para-dhāman</s>), of the nature of supreme splendor. Again, of what kind? Partaking of the form of supreme nectar (<s>paramāmṛta-rūpa-bhāj</s>), consisting of the nature of supreme nectar. What doing? Filling the body — the person — of this disciple. What doing? Thereafter — subsequently — extending that <s>sāmarasya</s> (unity) — the oneness of the <s>kalaśa</s> with that radiant form.
He describes the consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) —

children.text: kṣādyair āntair varṇair abhipūrṇa-tanus trir ukta-mantrāntaiḥ |
children.translated_text: With the syllables beginning with <s>kṣa</s> and ending [with <s>a</s>], his body fully anointed, with mantras concluded by three recitations;
Wearing a pair of exceedingly white garments, the <s>vācaṃyama</s> (one observing silence) has performed <s>ācamana</s> (ritual sipping) twice. // Krd_4.76 //

children.text: kṣa-ādir yeṣāṃ taiḥ āntaiḥ a-kārānto yeṣāṃ tair varṇair mātṛkākṣarair mūla-mantra-tri-japāvasānair abhiṣikta-śarīraḥ śiṣyaḥ dhṛta-navīnātiśukla-vasana-yugalaḥ maunī kṛta-dvir-ācamanaḥ || KrdC_4.76 ||
children.translated_text: With those beginning with <s>kṣa</s> — by those [syllables]; ending [with <s>a</s>] — those whose final is the <s>a</s>-vowel; with those syllables — the <s>mātṛkā</s> letters — at the conclusion of the triple recitation of the <s>mūla-mantra</s>, the disciple whose body has been consecrated, wearing a pair of new, exceedingly white garments, observing silence, having performed <s>ācamana</s> twice. || KrdC_4.76 ||
Having prostrated many times before <s>Hari</s> bearing the name of the preceptor, then approaching [him];

children.text: tad-dakṣiṇata upāstām abhimukham ekāgra-mānasaḥ śiṣyaḥ // Krd_4.77 //
children.translated_text: The disciple should sit to his right, facing him, with single-pointed mind. // Krd_4.77 //

children.text: bahu-vāraṃ deśika-nāmānaṃ guru-rūpaṃ harim natvā athānantaram upasaṅgṛhya guru-caraṇau vyatyasta-hasta-dvayaṃ kṛtvā tad-dakṣiṇato guru-dakṣiṇe abhimukhaṃ guru-saṃmukham ekāgra-mānasaḥ eka-cittas tiṣṭhet upaviśet || KrdC_4.77 ||
children.translated_text: Having bowed many times before <s>Hari</s> in the form of the <s>guru</s> bearing the preceptor's name, then subsequently having clasped the <s>guru</s>'s feet with crossed hands, to his right — to the <s>guru</s>'s right — facing the <s>guru</s>, with single-pointed mind, with concentrated thought, he should stand or sit. || KrdC_4.77 ||
Having duly performed the <s>nyāsa</s>s (ritual placements) upon him in the manner of <s>Acyuta</s>,
Upon his body adorned with sandalwood paste, unbroken rice, and the like;
Then the excellent mantra, accompanied by its <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer) and other [elements], properly,

children.text: brūyāt triśo gurur anarghyam avāma-kareṇa // Krd_4.78 //
children.translated_text: The <s>guru</s> should recite thrice, [that] priceless [mantra], into the left ear. // Krd_4.78 //

children.text: athānantaraṃ yathā-vidhi yathokta-prakāreṇa nyāsaiḥ pañcāṅga-nyāsādibhiḥ te śiṣyam acyuta-sād-vidhāya śrī-kṛṣṇa-rūpaṃ kṛtvā gandhākṣata-puṣpaiḥ vibhūṣita-śarīrasyāsya avāma-karṇe dakṣiṇa-karṇe ṛṣi-cchando-devatā-sahitam anarghyam amūlyaṃ mantra-varaṃ mantra-śreṣṭhaṃ triśaḥ tri-vāraṃ brūyāt yathāvat yathokta-prakāreṇa sa ca prakāraḥ prathamaṃ dakṣiṇa-haste gurur jalaṃ dadāti amuka-mantraṃ dadāmīti anena śiṣyo 'pi dadasva iti brūyāt tato mantraṃ dadyād iti atrāvaśyaṃ vāra-trayaṃ guruṇā mantraḥ paṭhanīyaḥ datte yāvac chiṣyasya mantraḥ svāyatto bhavati tāvat paṭhanīya iti || KrdC_4.78 ||
children.translated_text: Then subsequently, in the prescribed manner — in the method stated — through <s>nyāsa</s>s such as the five-limbed placement (<s>pañcāṅga-nyāsa</s>), having transformed the disciple into the form of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> through the procedure of <s>Acyuta</s>, into the left ear — the right ear — of the one whose body has been adorned with sandalwood paste, unbroken rice, and flowers, the priceless — invaluable — excellent mantra — the best of mantras — accompanied by its <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer), <s>chandas</s> (metre), and <s>devatā</s> (deity), he should recite thrice — three times — properly, in the prescribed manner. And that method is: first the <s>guru</s> gives water in the right hand, [saying] 'I give such-and-such mantra,' and with this the disciple should say 'give [it to me]'; then he should give the mantra. Here it is essential that the mantra be recited by the <s>guru</s> three times; he should continue reciting until the mantra becomes the disciple's own possession. || KrdC_4.78 ||
He shows the duties of the disciple after receiving the mantra —
The mantra duly obtained from the <s>guru</s>,
Having recited one hundred and eight times, again;
Having then saluted, let him hear properly
The observances (<s>samaya</s>s), with body bowed in fullness of devotion. // Krd_4.79 //

children.text: yathā-vidhi guruṇā hetunā prāptaṃ mantraṃ prasādhitam anugraheṇa dattam iti tripāṭhinaḥ | aṣṭau ūrdhvaṃ yasya tasya tad aṣṭādhika-śataṃ prajapya bhūyaḥ punar api gurum abhivādyaṃ namaskṛtya daṇḍavat praṇamya tato gurutaḥ samayān ācārān samyak kṛtvā śṛṇotu yat tu vidyām aṣṭa-kṛtvo japed iti tat-tan-nyūna-saṅkhyā-kala-japa-niṣedha-param | kīdṛśaḥ ? bhaktyātiśayena namra-śarīraḥ || KrdC_4.79 ||
children.translated_text: The mantra obtained — perfected — given by the grace of the <s>guru</s> in the prescribed manner — thus [say] the <s>tripāṭhin</s>s. Eight above which is that — that is, one hundred and eight — having recited [that many times], again — once more — having saluted the <s>guru</s>, having bowed, having prostrated flat [on the ground], then from the <s>guru</s>, having properly performed the observances — the rules of conduct — let him hear. As for the [statement] 'one should recite the <s>vidyā</s> eight times,' that is meant to prohibit recitation of fewer than that number. Of what kind? With body bowed through an excess of devotion. || KrdC_4.79 ||
He states the duty of the <s>guru</s> after giving the mantra —

children.text: dattvā śiṣyāya manuṃ nyasyātha guruḥ kṛtātma-yajana-vidhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Having given the mantra to the disciple, having then performed the placements, the <s>guru</s>, having completed the rite of self-worship;
Should recite one thousand and eight [times], to prevent the loss of his own power. // Krd_4.80 //

children.text: athānantaraṃ guruḥ śiṣyāya mantraṃ dattvā nyasya nyāsādikaṃ kṛtvā kṛtātma-yajana-vidhiḥ kṛtābhyantara-yāgaḥ aṣṭādhikaṃ sahasraṃ sva-sāmarthya-hāny-anavāptaye sva-sāmarthya-rakṣārthaṃ datta-mantraṃ japet || KrdC_4.80 ||
children.translated_text: Then subsequently, the <s>guru</s>, having given the mantra to the disciple, having performed the placements and other [rites], having completed the rite of internal worship (<s>abhyantara-yāga</s>), should recite the given mantra one thousand and eight times, for the purpose of preventing the loss of his own power — for the protection of his own capacity. || KrdC_4.80 ||
He states the duty of the disciple —
Having offered all the <s>kumbha</s> (vessel) and other [items] to the <s>guru</s>,
He should also feed the best of <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s with various kinds of food;
Those who perform the consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) by this method here,

children.text: te sampadāṃ nilayanaṃ hi ta eva dhanyāḥ // Krd_4.81 //
children.translated_text: They are the abode of all prosperity — indeed, they alone are blessed. // Krd_4.81 //

children.text: kumbhādikaṃ sakalaṃ maṇḍala-sahitaṃ maṇḍapāvasthita-dravyaṃ gurave samarpya dattvā bhojya-samūhair dvija-śreṣṭhān santoṣayet etat-karaṇasya phalam āha-iha jagati anena vidhinā anayā paripāṭyā ye abhiṣekaṃ kurvanti te sampadāṃ sarva-samṛddhīnāṃ nilayanaṃ sthānaṃ ta eva dhanyāḥ puruṣārtha-bhāginaḥ || KrdC_4.81 ||
children.translated_text: Having offered — given — all the <s>kumbha</s> and other [items] together with the <s>maṇḍala</s> and the materials placed in the pavilion (<s>maṇḍapa</s>) to the <s>guru</s>, he should gratify the best of <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s with an array of food offerings. He states the fruit of performing this: in this world, those who perform the consecration by this method — by this procedure — they are the abode of all prosperity — of all wealth — they alone are blessed, partakers of the goals of human life (<s>puruṣārtha</s>). || KrdC_4.81 ||
He summarizes the stated matter —
The <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) has been stated somewhat in brief,
For the remembrance of those with clear intellects;
Having entered this [initiation], the <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) should recite all [mantras],

children.text: japej juhotu yajec ca manūn // Krd_4.82 //
children.translated_text: Offer oblations, and perform worship with the mantras. // Krd_4.82 //

children.text: kiṃcit saṅkṣipya dīkṣā uktā kathitā viśada-dhiyāṃ nirmala-buddhīnāṃ saṃsmaraṇāya etāṃ dīkṣāṃ praviśya prāpya mantrī sādhakaḥ sarvān mantrān japet yajej juhotu || KrdC_4.82 ||
children.translated_text: Somewhat in brief, the <s>dīkṣā</s> has been stated — described — for the remembrance of those with pure intellects. Having entered — obtained — this <s>dīkṣā</s>, the <s>mantrī</s> — the practitioner — should recite all mantras, worship, and offer oblations. || KrdC_4.82 ||
Thus ends the fourth chapter (<s>paṭala</s>) named '<s>Dīkṣā-pūjā</s>' (Initiation and Worship) in the <s>Kramadīpikā</s> composed by <s>Śrī Keśavācārya</s>. ||4||
(5) Fifth Chapter (<s>Paṭala</s>)
Now he shows the mantra-procedure for the initiated one —
Having performed this rite in the month of <s>Caitra</s>, in the bright fortnight (<s>accha-pakṣa</s>),
On an auspicious asterism (<s>nakṣatra</s>), having again received initiation from the preceptor;
Permitted by him, the preliminary practice (<s>pūrva-sevā</s>) in the second
Month, on the twelfth day (<s>dvādaśī</s>), the pure one should commence. // Krd_5.1 //

children.text: caitre māsi puṇya-rkṣe śubha-nakṣatre accha-pakṣe śukla-pakṣe etat karma mantra-dīkṣātmakaṃ karma kṛtvā bhūyaḥ punar api deśikāt guror dīkṣāṃ mantropadeśaṃ prāpyānantaraṃ tena guruṇānujñātaḥ dvitīye māsi vaiśākhe dvādaśyām tithau pūrva-sevāṃ puraścaraṇam ārabhet | caitre duḥkhāya dīkṣā syāt iti vacanaṃ gopāla-mantra-bhinna-dīkṣa-viṣayam || KrdC_5.1 ||
children.translated_text: In the month of <s>Caitra</s>, on an auspicious asterism — a favorable <s>nakṣatra</s> — in the bright fortnight — the <s>śukla-pakṣa</s> — having performed this rite — the rite consisting of mantra-initiation — again, subsequently, having obtained initiation — mantra instruction — from the preceptor, the <s>guru</s>, permitted by that <s>guru</s>, in the second month — <s>Vaiśākha</s> — on the twelfth <s>tithi</s> (lunar day), one should commence the preliminary practice — the <s>puraścaraṇa</s> (preparatory rites). The statement 'initiation in <s>Caitra</s> leads to suffering' pertains to initiations other than the <s>Gopāla-mantra</s> initiation. || KrdC_5.1 ||
Having performed the rites from bathing to body-worship,
Following the path previously stated, the foremost practitioner;
Pure, observing silence, celibate, eating only at night,
With tranquil mind, he should recite with a rosary of pure lotus seeds. // Krd_5.2 //

children.text: kṛtveti | mantri-mukhyaḥ sādhakaḥ snānam ārabhyātma-yogāntaṃ karma kṛtvā prāg īritaṃ vartmāśritya pūrvokta-pūjā-prakāram āśritya śuddho gāyatrī-japena niṣpāpo brāhmaṇādy-ukta-bāhyāntara-śauca-yukto maunī vāg-yato brahmacārī aṣṭa-vidha-maithuna-tyāgī niśāśī rātri-bhojī śāntātmā anuddhata-cittaḥ śukla-padma-bīja-mālayā japyāt |
children.translated_text: The foremost practitioner — the <s>sādhaka</s> — having performed the rites from bathing up to <s>ātma-yoga</s> (self-union), following the previously stated path — adopting the previously described method of worship — pure through <s>Gāyatrī</s> recitation, sinless, endowed with external and internal purity as prescribed for <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s and others, observing silence — restraining speech — celibate — renouncing the eight forms of sexual contact — eating at night — taking food only at night — with tranquil mind — with undisturbed consciousness — should recite with a rosary of white lotus seeds.

children.text: atraivam āgamāntaroktaṃ boddhavyam | śubhe dine krośaṃ krośa-dvayaṃ vā kṣetraṃ vihārārthaṃ parikalpya kṣīra-druma-bhava-vitasti-parimitāṣṭa-kīlakāḥ pratyekam ekadaiva vā daśa-kṛtvaḥ śata-kṛtvo vā japitvā aṣṭa-dig-devatāḥ sampūjya madhye kṣetre kṣetra-pāla-baliṃ dattvā pūjāṃ kṛtvā pūrvādy-aṣṭa-dikṣu tān nikhanyāt tatra tatra tat-tan-nāmnā dik-pati-baliṃ ca dattvā dīpakaṃ ca dattvā japa-pūrva-divase eka-bhojanam upavāso vā guruṃ brāhmaṇāṃś ca tarpayet |
children.translated_text: Here, the following should be understood as stated in other <s>Āgama</s>s: On an auspicious day, having designated a sacred field of one or two <s>krośa</s>s for circumambulation, eight pegs made of milky-tree [wood] measuring one <s>vitasti</s> (span) each — having recited [the mantra] ten or one hundred times over each one individually or all at once — having worshipped the deities of the eight directions, having offered <s>bali</s> (oblation) to the guardian of the field in the center of the sacred ground and performed worship, one should plant them in the eight directions beginning with east. Having offered <s>bali</s> to the directional guardian at each place by its respective name, and having offered a lamp, on the day before the recitation, one should observe a single meal or fasting, and should gratify the <s>guru</s> and <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s.

children.text:
tathā ca sanat-kumāra-kalpe-
viprāṃś ca bhojayed anna-bhojanācchādanādibhiḥ |
bahubhir vastra-bhūṣābhiḥ sampūjya gurum ātmanaḥ |
ārabheta japaṃ paścāt tad-anujñā-puraḥsaram || iti |
children.translated_text:
And thus in the <s>Sanat-kumāra-kalpa</s>:
'One should feed <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s with food, meals, clothing, and the like;
having duly worshipped one's own <s>guru</s> with many garments and ornaments,
one should then commence recitation, preceded by his permission.' Thus.

children.text: tato 'grima-dine snānādikaṃ kṛtvā saṅkalpaṃ kuryāt oṃ adyoṃ nama ity ādy uccāryāmuka-mantrasya siddhi-kāma iyat saṅkhyāka-japa-tad-daśāṃśāmuka-dravya-homa-tad-daśāṃśāmuka-dravya-tarpaṇa-tad-daśāṃśāmukābhiṣeka-tad-daśāṃśa-brāhmaṇa-sampradānaka-bhojya-dānātmaka-puraścaraṇa-karma kariṣye iti saṅkalpaṃ kuryāt | tato mantra-rṣi-chando-devatānāṃ kāma-sthāne puraścaraṇa-jape viniyoga iti | jape cāyaṃ niyamaḥ-
children.translated_text: Then on the following day, having performed bathing and the like, one should make the <s>saṅkalpa</s> (formal resolve): 'Oṃ, today, Oṃ namaḥ' — and so forth, having pronounced — 'desiring the accomplishment of such-and-such mantra, I shall perform the preparatory rite (<s>puraścaraṇa</s>) consisting of recitation of such number, oblation with such substance [being] one-tenth thereof, libation (<s>tarpaṇa</s>) with such substance [being] one-tenth thereof, consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) [being] one-tenth thereof, and feeding and gifting to <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s [being] one-tenth thereof.' Then: 'The <s>ṛṣi</s>, <s>chandas</s>, and <s>devatā</s> of the mantra — in the place of desire — the application is in the <s>puraścaraṇa</s> recitation.' And regarding recitation, this is the rule —
The rule of continuity is declared: one should not skip a day.
Sleeping on a bed of <s>darbha</s> grass, pure, with controlled mind;
If a day is missed, a fault arises — an obstruction to accomplishment (<s>siddhi</s>) is produced.
In the <s>Nāradīya</s> —

children.text: śanaiḥ śanair avispaṣṭaṃ na drutaṃ na vilambitam |
children.translated_text: Slowly, slowly, indistinctly, neither too fast nor too slow,

children.text: na nyūnaṃ nādhikaṃ vāpi japaṃ kuryād dine dine ||
children.translated_text: Neither less nor more — one should perform recitation day after day.

And elsewhere likewise:
With undivided mind, from the morning time until midday;
In the <s>Nāradīya</s> also thus —

children.text: na vadan na svapan gacchan nānyat kim api saṃsmaran |
children.translated_text: Not speaking, not sleeping, not walking, not recollecting anything else,
Not with mind disturbed by sneezing, yawning, hiccups, and the like;
One attains the accomplishment of the mantra (<s>mantra-siddhi</s>) — therefore one should be diligent.

children.text: uṣṇīṣo kañcukī nagno mukta-keśaḥ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: One wearing a turban, one wearing a jacket, one naked, one with loosened hair,
One with extended hands and feet — should not sit on a high seat.
And thus in the <s>Vaiśampāyana-saṃhitā</s> —

children.text: snānaṃ tri-savanaṃ proktam aśaktau dviḥ sakṛt tathā |
children.translated_text: Bathing three times a day (<s>tri-savana</s>) is prescribed; if unable, twice or once;

children.text: asnātasya phalaṃ nāsti na vā tarpayataḥ pitṝn ||
children.translated_text: For one who has not bathed there is no fruit, nor for one who does not offer libations to the ancestors (<s>pitṛ</s>s).
One should not speak falsehood, nor should one entice the senses;
Sleeping on a bed of <s>darbha</s> grass, pure, with controlled mind.

children.text: tad-vāsaḥ kṣālayen nityam anyathā vighnam āvahet |
children.translated_text: One should always wash that garment; otherwise it brings obstacles.
One should not recite the mantra wearing only one garment, nor ever wearing many garments.
The one performing <s>puraścaraṇa</s> should wear upper, lower, and outer garments.

children.text:
tathā nāradīye-
strī-śūdrābhyāṃ na sambhāṣed rātrau japa-paro na ca |
japen na sandhyā-kāleṣu pradoṣe nobhayeṣu ca |
brāhmaṇānīta-vastra-śuddha-jalena karmakṛd bhavet || iti || KrdC_5.2 ||

children.translated_text: Moreover, he states the duties —
Rendering service to cows, giving them food,
Extending compassion to [all] beings;
Saluting the presiding deity of the mantra,
<s>Durgā</s>, the <s>guru</s> who is the sun [dispelling] the darkness of difficult-to-comprehend [ignorance], and also, // Krd_5.3 //

children.text: goṣu śuśrūṣāṃ go-paricaryāṃ dhūma-kaṇḍūyanādi-rūpāṃ sevāṃ vistārayan | kiṃ kurvan ? tābhyo gobhyo grāsa ṃ prayacchan gopāla-mantra eva grāsādikam atropādānād anyatrānukteś ca | bhūteṣu prāṇiṣu karuṇāṃ dhārayan mantrādhiṣṭhātṛ-devatāṃ durgām ajñānāndhakāra-sūryaṃ guruṃ ca vandamānaḥ || KrdC_5.3 ||
children.translated_text: Rendering service to cows — cow-care in the form of fumigation, scratching, and such service — expanding [it]. Doing what? Giving food — fodder — to those cows. Since the <s>Gopāla-mantra</s> itself prescribes fodder and the like here, and [it is] not stated elsewhere. Bearing compassion toward beings — toward living creatures — saluting the presiding deity of the mantra, <s>Durgā</s>, and the <s>guru</s> who is the sun [dispelling] the darkness of ignorance. || KrdC_5.3 ||
Performing his own duties pertaining to <s>varṇa</s> (social order) and <s>āśrama</s> (life-stage),
Having recited the mantra, he should anoint [himself] thrice at bathing time;
Sipping water recited [with the mantra] the number of <s>tattva</s>s (principles),
And eating food [consecrated with] seven recitations, and collyrium and the like. // Krd_5.4 //

children.text: svīyaṃ varṇāśramoktaṃ karma kurvan ātmīyaṃ ātmano yo varṇo brāhmaṇādir yo vāśramo brahmacaryādis tatra tatrasthaṃ karma vihitaṃ tat tat kurvann ity arthaḥ | mantra-japta-jalena kāle vāra-trayaṃ svātmānam abhiṣiñcet tattva-saṅkhyā-prajaptaṃ dvātriṃśat-saṅkhyā-prajaptaṃ pañca-viṃśati-prajaptaṃ vā tathā jalam ācāman ittham evānnaṃ bhuñjānaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? sapta-japtam añjanādi-kajjalādi yasya sa tathā ādi-śabdena gandha-mālyādīnāṃ parigrahaḥ | añjanādya iti kvacit pāṭhaḥ || KrdC_5.4 ||
children.translated_text: Performing his own duties — one's own — prescribed for one's <s>varṇa</s> (whether <s>brāhmaṇa</s> or otherwise) and <s>āśrama</s> (whether <s>brahmacarya</s> or otherwise) — performing the duties enjoined for each respective station — this is the meaning. With water over which the mantra has been recited, at the [proper] time, thrice he should anoint himself. Having sipped water recited the number of <s>tattva</s>s — recited thirty-two times, or twenty-five times — likewise. Eating food in that very manner. Furthermore, of what kind? That over which collyrium and the like — eye-ointment — have been recited seven times — such is he. By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), sandalwood paste, garlands, and the like are included. '<s>Añjanādya</s>' is a variant reading in some [manuscripts]. || KrdC_5.4 ||
He states the place of recitation —
On a mountain peak, on a river bank, at the base of a <s>bilva</s> tree,
In chest-deep water, in a cow-settlement (<s>gokula</s>), in a <s>Viṣṇu</s> temple;
At the base of an <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig) tree, and also on the shore of the ocean,

children.text: sthāneṣv eteṣv āsīna ekaikaśas tu // Krd_5.5 //
children.translated_text: Seated in these places, one by one; // Krd_5.5 //

children.text: prajaped ayuta-catuṣkaṃ daśākṣaraṃ manu-varaṃ pṛthak kramaśaḥ |
children.translated_text: One should recite the excellent ten-syllable mantra forty thousand times, separately and in sequence;

children.text: aṣṭādaśākṣaraṃ ced ayuta-dvayam ity udīritā saṅkhyā // Krd_5.6 //
children.translated_text: If it is the eighteen-syllable [mantra], twenty thousand — thus the count is declared. // Krd_5.6 //

children.text: parvata-śṛṅge nadī-tīre bilva-vṛkṣa-samīpa-deśe hṛdaya-pramāṇa-jale goṣṭhe viṣṇu-pratimādhiṣṭhita-gehe pippala-vṛkṣa-samīpa-deśe samudrasya tīre aṣṭasu sthāneṣu āsīna upaviṣṭaḥ ekaikaśaḥ ekaikasmin sthāne sthāneṣu kramaśaḥ krameṇa pṛthak ayuta-catuṣkaṃ kṛtvā daśākṣara-mantraṃ japet yadāṣṭādaśākṣara-mantraḥ tadāyuta-dvayaṃ kṛtvā iti japa-saṅkhyodīritā atra na pratisthānam ayuta-catuṣkāyuta-dvaya-japaḥ kintu yathā japtavyaṃ yena sarvatra japena tāvaty eva saṅkhyā bhavati anyathāṣṭasu sthāneṣu japenāṣṭādaśāksare ṣoḍaśāyuta-japaḥ syāt | prapañca-sāre 'pi-ayuta-dvitayāvadhi-japaḥ syād iti | yadyapy aṣṭādaśākṣare iyaṃ saṅkhyā tathāpi tulya-nyāyād daśākṣare 'pi iyam eva vyavastheti

children.translated_text: thus [says] <s>Rudradhara</s>. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.5-6 ||

Seated at eight places — on a mountain peak, on a river bank, near a <s>bilva</s> tree, in water up to the heart's depth, in a cowpen, in a house presided over by a <s>Viṣṇu</s> image, near a <s>pippala</s> (sacred fig) tree, and on the seashore — at each place individually, in sequence, having performed four <s>ayuta</s>s (forty thousand) separately, one should recite the ten-syllable mantra. When using the eighteen-syllable mantra, then having performed two <s>ayuta</s>s (twenty thousand) — thus the count of recitation is stated. Here the four <s>ayuta</s>s or two <s>ayuta</s>s of recitation are not per each place, but rather the total amount to be recited, so that the same number applies everywhere through the recitation; otherwise, with recitation at eight places for the eighteen-syllable [mantra], there would be sixteen <s>ayuta</s>s of recitation. In the <s>Prapañcasāra</s> also — 'the recitation should be up to two <s>ayuta</s>s.' Although this number applies to the eighteen-syllable [mantra], by the principle of equal reasoning, the same arrangement applies to the ten-syllable [mantra] as well —
Regarding the aforementioned places, he states the dietary regulation in sequence —

children.text: śākaṃ mūlaṃ phalaṃ go-stana-bhava-dadhinī bhaikṣam annaṃ ca saktuṃ
children.translated_text: Vegetables, roots, fruits, milk born from a cow's udder, and curds, alms-food, and <s>saktu</s> (parched barley flour),

children.text: dugdhānnaṃ cety adānaḥ kṣiti-dhara-śikharādau kramāt sthāna-bhede |
children.translated_text: And milk-rice — thus, abstaining [from other food], at the different places beginning with the mountain peak, in sequence;

children.text: ekaṃ caiṣām aśaktau gaditam iha mayā pūrvāsevā-vidhānaṃ
children.translated_text: And one of these when unable — this preliminary practice (<s>pūrva-sevā</s>) method has been declared by me here;

children.text: nirvṛtte 'smin punaś ca prajapatu vidhivat siddhaye sādhakeśaḥ // Krd_5.7 //
children.translated_text: When this is completed, let the practitioner again recite properly according to rule, for the attainment of <s>siddhi</s>. // <s>Krd</s> 5.7 //

children.text: kṣiti-dhara-śikharādau pūrvokta-parvata-śṛṅgādau sthāna-viśeṣe kramād ekaikaṃ krameṇa vihitaṃ śākaṃ vāstukādi mūlaṃ śūraṇādi phalaṃ āmrādi go-stana-bhavaṃ dugdhaṃ dadhi ca dvandvaḥ bhaikṣaṃ bhikṣāta upalabdham annaṃ ca praśastaṃ haimatikaṃ sitāsvinnaṃ saktuṃ bhṛṣṭa-yava-cūrṇaṃ dugdhānnaṃ pāyasaṃ adāno bhakṣamāṇo japaṃ kuryāt mitodanam |
children.translated_text: At each particular place beginning with the mountain peak and the rest as mentioned before, in sequence — one by one, as prescribed: <s>śāka</s> (vegetables) such as <s>vāstuka</s> etc., <s>mūla</s> (roots) such as <s>śūraṇa</s> (yam) etc., <s>phala</s> (fruits) such as mango etc., <s>go-stana-bhava</s> (born from a cow's udder) meaning milk and curds — a <s>dvandva</s> compound — <s>bhaikṣa</s> (alms-food) obtained through begging, <s>anna</s> meaning excellent autumnal rice cooked with sugar, <s>saktu</s> meaning parched barley flour, <s>dugdhānna</s> meaning <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice pudding) — <s>adāna</s> meaning eating [only these], one should perform recitation; eating measured food —

children.text:
śastānnaṃ ca samaśnīyān mantra-siddhi-samīhayā |
tasmān nityaṃ prayatnena śastānnāśī bhaven naraḥ || iti |
children.translated_text:
'And one should eat recommended food, with the desire for mantra-<s>siddhi</s> (perfection);
therefore, a person should always endeavor to eat only recommended food.' Thus.

children.text: aśaktaṃ praty āha-ekam iti | aśaktau caiṣām adri-śṛṅgādy-aṣṭa-sthānānāṃ madhye ekaṃ sthānaṃ samāśritya śākādy-aṣṭa-vidheṣv ekaṃ bhojanam āśritya japaṃ kuryāt | tad uktaṃ nāradīye-
children.translated_text: Addressing the one who is unable, he says — '<s>ekam</s>' (one). When unable, among these eight places beginning with the mountain peak, taking shelter at one place, and resorting to one type of food among the eight kinds beginning with vegetables, one should perform recitation. That is stated in the <s>Nāradīya</s> —

children.text: mṛdu koṣṇaṃ supakvaṃ ca kuryād vai laghu-bhojanam |
children.translated_text: 'Soft, warm, and well-cooked — one should take light food;

children.text: nendriyāṇāṃ yathā vṛddhis tathā bhuñjīta sādhakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The practitioner should eat in such a way that the senses are not overstimulated.'

children.text: yad vā tad vā parityājyaṃ duṣṭānāṃ saṅgamaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: 'This or that should be abandoned, as well as the company of the wicked.'

children.text: iha granthe pūrva-sevāvidhānaṃ mayā gaditaṃ kathitam asminn nivṛtte sampūrṇe puraścaraṇa-jape punaś ca prajapatu siddhaye viśiṣṭa-phala-siddhaye vidhivat yathokta-prakāreṇa atra kecid asmin pūrva-sevārambhe karmaṇi nirvṛtte samāpte punaḥ puraścaraṇa-japaṃ karotv ity āhuḥ || KrdC_5.7 ||
children.translated_text: In this text, the method of preliminary practice (<s>pūrva-sevā</s>) has been declared by me; when this <s>puraścaraṇa</s> recitation is completed, let one again recite for the attainment of <s>siddhi</s> — for the attainment of special fruits — according to rule, in the prescribed manner. Here some [commentators] say: when this preliminary practice is completed, one should again perform the <s>puraścaraṇa</s> recitation. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.7 ||
At the end of bodily worship, daily, at the beginning of the day,
Any one of the methods taught in the <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation);
Having adopted [one], one should worship <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in a secluded
House, seated, eating the remnants of the fire-offering. // <s>Krd</s> 5.8 //

children.text: dehārcanānte deha-pūjāvasāne dinaśaḥ pratidinaṃ dinādau prātar dīkṣokta-mārgeṣu ṣoḍaśa-pañcopacārādiṣu anyataram ekaṃ vartmāśritya kṛṣṇaṃ prayajet pūjayatu āvaraṇa-bhedād vartma-bhedaḥ | kīdṛśaḥ ? vivikta ekānte gṛhe niṣaṇṇa upaviṣṭaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? huta-śiṣṭa-bhojī prātyahika-japa-daśāṃśa-homāvaśiṣṭa-bhojī || KrdC_5.8 ||
children.translated_text: At the end of bodily worship — at the conclusion of worship upon the body — daily, each day, at the beginning of the day, in the morning; among the methods taught in the <s>dīkṣā</s> — among the sixteen <s>upacāra</s>s, five <s>upacāra</s>s, etc. — having adopted any one path, one should worship <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. The difference of path is due to the difference of the surrounding circles (<s>āvaraṇa</s>s). What kind [of person]? Seated in a secluded house — sitting in a solitary dwelling. Again, what kind? <s>Huta-śiṣṭa-bhojī</s> — one who eats the remnants of the daily fire-offering, which constitutes one-tenth of the recitation. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.8 ||

children.text: prakārāntaram api mahate phalāya puraścaraṇam āha-daśa-lakṣam iti rudradharaḥ | vayaṃ tu paśyāmaḥ | prakṛta-yathokta-puraścaraṇam āha-
children.translated_text: <s>Rudradhara</s> says — he also states another form of <s>puraścaraṇa</s> for great fruit: 'ten <s>lakṣa</s>s.' But we hold as follows — he states the <s>puraścaraṇa</s> as described in the present context —
Having recited ten <s>lakṣa</s>s (one million) of the mantra, which bestows imperishable fruit, the ten-syllable one,
The one of trained intellect,
Should offer into the fire ten <s>ayuta</s>s (one hundred thousand) of fresh
Red lotuses, immersed in <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery), <s>ājya</s> (ghee), and honey. // <s>Krd</s> 5.9 //

children.text: śuddha-matiḥ sādhakaḥ akṣaya-phaladaṃ mokṣa-phalaṃ daśākṣaraṃ manuṃ daśa-lakṣaṃ pratijapya hutavahe saṃskṛtāgnau aruṇāmbujair aruṇa-kamalair daśā-yutaṃ lakṣam ekaṃ juhuyāt | kīdṛśaiḥ ? guḍājya-madhu-samplutaiḥ guḍa-ghṛta-madhu-saṃyuktaiḥ || KrdC_5.9 ||
children.translated_text: The practitioner of pure mind, having recited ten <s>lakṣa</s>s (one million) of the ten-syllable mantra that bestows imperishable fruit — the fruit of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) — should offer into the consecrated fire one <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand) of red lotuses. Of what kind? Immersed in <s>guḍa</s> (jaggery), <s>ghṛta</s> (ghee), and honey — combined with jaggery, ghee, and honey. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.9 ||
If the mantra has twice the number of aperture-letters (<s>śuṣira-yugala-varṇa</s>), five <s>lakṣa</s>s
One should recite, and should offer half a <s>lakṣa</s> according to the prescribed method;
The one of pure mind, in the absence of lotuses, with <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice),
Combined with ghee and sugar, should commence the <s>homa</s> (fire-offering). // <s>Krd</s> 5.10 //

children.text:
śuṣira-yugala-varṇaṃ śuṣiraṃ chidraṃ nava-saṅkhyātmakaṃ tasya yugalaṃ dvandvaṃ aṣṭādaśākṣaraṃ japet tadā pañca-lakṣaṃ prajapatu prokta-kptyā pūrvokta-paripāṭyā cārdha-lakṣam juhuyāt yathokta-homa-dravyālābhe dravyāntaram āha amala-matir iti śuddha-matiḥ ambujānāṃ padmānām alābhe 'prāptau pāyasaiḥ paramānnair homam ārabheta | kīdṛśaiḥ ? sahite ghṛta-site yeṣu taiḥ ghṛta-śarkarā-sahitair ity arthaḥ | svāhāntena homa-pūjeti sarvatra boddhavyaṃ homādeś cānuṣṭhāna-prakāro mat-kṛta-homānuṣṭhāna-paddhater avagantavyaḥ | nāradīye, yathā-
  japasya tu daśāṃśena homaḥ kāryo dine dine |
  athavā lakṣa-paryantaṃ homaḥ kāryo vipaścitā || iti || KrdC_5.10 ||
children.translated_text:
<s>Śuṣira-yugala-varṇa</s> — <s>śuṣira</s> means 'aperture,' whose numerical value is nine; its <s>yugala</s> (pair) makes eighteen syllables — one should recite; then five <s>lakṣa</s>s one should recite; according to the prescribed method — in the previously stated sequence — one should offer half a <s>lakṣa</s>. When the prescribed <s>homa</s> materials are unavailable, he states an alternative material — '<s>amala-mati</s>' — the one of pure mind; in the absence of — non-availability of — lotuses, with <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice pudding), one should commence the <s>homa</s>. Of what kind? <s>Sahita</s> meaning combined with ghee and sugar — that is, combined with ghee and crystallized sugar — this is the meaning. The <s>homa</s> and worship [should conclude] with <s>svāhā</s> — this should be understood everywhere. The practical procedure of <s>homa</s> etc. should be understood from the <s>homa</s> practice manual composed by me. In the <s>Nāradīya</s>, thus:
'One should perform <s>homa</s> daily with one-tenth of the recitation;
or the learned one should perform <s>homa</s> up to one <s>lakṣa</s>.' Thus. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.10 ||
For those unable to perform <s>homa</s>, the recitation multiplied by the numbers of the <s>Veda</s>s, <s>rasa</s>s (flavors), and <s>nāgendra</s>s (serpent-lords),

children.text: japaḥ kāryaś ceti divja-nṛpa-viśām āhur apare |
children.translated_text: Should be done — thus say others, for <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s, <s>kṣatriya</s>s, and <s>vaiśya</s>s;

children.text: sahomaś ced eṣāṃ sama iha japo homa-rahito
children.translated_text: If their recitation is with <s>homa</s>, it is equal [to the standard]; the <s>homa</s>-less [recitation]

children.text: ya ukto varṇānāṃ sa khalu vihitas tac-cala-dṛśām // Krd_5.11 //
children.translated_text: That is prescribed for the <s>varṇa</s>s, that indeed is ordained for their wives as well. // <s>Krd</s> 5.11 //
Addressing the one unable to perform <s>homa</s>, he says —

children.text: tāvad dravyādy-asampattyā homa-karmaṇi asamarthānāṃ brāhmaṇa-kṣatriya-vaiśyānāṃ yathā-sāṅkhyaṃ nigamā vedāś catvāraḥ rasāḥ ṣaṭ nāgendrā aṣṭau etair guṇitair japyo 'nuṣṭheya ity apare ācāryā āhuḥ | tatra kṛta eva japaḥ etair guṇita iti rudradharaḥ | vastutas tu-

children.translated_text: 'When unable to perform <s>homa</s>, one should perform recitation four times the <s>homa</s> count;
Six times and eight times, respectively, for the twice-born.'

When unable to perform the <s>homa</s> ritual due to lack of materials etc., for <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s, <s>kṣatriya</s>s, and <s>vaiśya</s>s, in their respective order: the <s>nigama</s>s (Vedas) are four, the <s>rasa</s>s (flavors) are six, the <s>nāgendra</s>s (serpent-lords) are eight — multiplied by these, the recitation should be performed — thus say other teachers. In that case, the recitation already performed is multiplied by these — thus [says] <s>Rudradhara</s>. But in truth —

children.text:
iti puraścaraṇa-candrikoktam eva yuktaṃ paśyāmaḥ |
homa-karmaṇy aśaktānāṃ viprāṇāṃ dviguṇo japaḥ |
itareṣāṃ tu varṇānāṃ triguṇo hi vidhīyate || iti |

eteṣāṃ matāpekṣayā apara ity uktam | eteṣāṃ ca mate tarpaṇādi-vyatirekeṇa mūla-bhūta-japa-dviguṇa-japenaiva puraścaraṇa-siddhir bhavati tathaiva granthāntare 'bhidhānāt | eṣāṃ brāhmaṇādīnāṃ homa-sahitaś cej japaḥ tadā trayāṇām api ayuta-catuṣṭayādi-samānam eva varṇānāṃ brāhmaṇādīnāṃ homa-rahito ya ukto japaḥ | atra homa-rahito yaś caturguṇo japa iti bhairava-tripāṭhinaḥ | sa eva tac-cala-dṛśāṃ tat-patnīnāṃ vihitaḥ || KrdC_5.11 ||
children.translated_text: With respect to their views, the term 'others' (<s>apara</s>) is used. And in their view, excluding <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) etc., the perfection of <s>puraścaraṇa</s> is achieved merely by doubling the fundamental recitation — since it is so stated in other texts. For these <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s etc., if the recitation is accompanied by <s>homa</s>, then for all three [<s>varṇa</s>s], it is the same — four <s>ayuta</s>s etc. The <s>homa</s>-less recitation that is prescribed for the <s>varṇa</s>s — the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s etc. — here, the <s>homa</s>-less four-fold recitation — thus [say] the <s>Bhairava-tripāṭhin</s>s — that same [amount] is ordained for <s>tac-cala-dṛśām</s> — their wives. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.11 ||

children.text: sanātanaḥ : home asamarthānāṃ vipra-kṣatriya-vaiśyānāṃ yathā-saṅkhyaṃ nigamādevāś catvāraḥ, rasāḥ ṣaṭ nāgendrā aṣṭau, etair guṇito japaḥ kāryaḥ | tv-arthe vā-śabdaḥ | apara iti-homa-karmaṇy asugamam eveti || (hbv 17.205 ṭīkā)
children.translated_text: <s>Sanātana</s> [comments]: For <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s, <s>kṣatriya</s>s, and <s>vaiśya</s>s who are unable to perform <s>homa</s>, in their respective order: the <s>nigama</s>s (Vedas) are four, the <s>rasa</s>s (flavors) are six, the <s>nāgendra</s>s (serpent-lords) are eight — multiplied by these, the recitation should be performed. The word '<s>vā</s>' is used in the sense of '<s>tu</s>' (but). '<s>Apara</s>' means — the <s>homa</s> ritual is indeed not easy to perform. (<s>HBV</s> 17.205 commentary)
Addressing the <s>śūdra</s>, he says —

children.text: yaṃ varṇam āśrito yaḥ śūdraḥ sa ca tan-nata-bhruvām |
children.translated_text: Whichever <s>varṇa</s> the <s>śūdra</s> has taken refuge in, he should perform the recitation [prescribed] for the wives of that [<s>varṇa</s>];

children.text: vidadhīta japaṃ vidhivac chraddhāvān bhakti-bharāvanamra-tanuḥ // Krd_5.12 //
children.translated_text: He should perform it duly, full of faith, with body bowed down by the weight of devotion. // <s>Krd</s> 5.12 //

children.text: brāhmaṇādīnāṃ madhye yaṃ varṇaṃ śūdraḥ samāśritaḥ sa tan-nata-bhruvāṃ teṣām eva dvijāty-ādīnāṃ strīṇāṃ vihitaṃ japaṃ vidhivat kathita-prakāreṇa vihitaṃ kuryāt | kīdṛśaḥ ? śraddhā-yutaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? bhakti-bhareṇa bhakty-atiśayena namro tanuḥ śarīraṃ yasya sa tathā | japaś cāyaṃ homa-rahita iti rudradharaḥ || KrdC_5.12 ||
children.translated_text: Among the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s and others, whichever <s>varṇa</s> the <s>śūdra</s> has taken refuge in, he should duly perform — in the manner prescribed — the recitation ordained for the wives of those same twice-born etc. What kind [of person]? One endowed with faith. Again, what kind? One whose body is bowed down by the weight of devotion — that is, one who is humble due to an abundance of <s>bhakti</s>. And this recitation is without <s>homa</s> — thus [says] <s>Rudradhara</s>. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.12 ||
He states the post-<s>puraścaraṇa</s> duties —

children.text: punar abhiṣikto guruṇā vidhivad viśrāṇya dakṣiṇāṃ tasmai |
children.translated_text: Again consecrated by the <s>guru</s> according to rule, having offered <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (honorarium) to him,

children.text: abhyavahārya ca viprān vibhavaiḥ samprīṇayec ca bhakti-yutaḥ // Krd_5.13 //
children.translated_text: And having fed <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s, one should gratify them with one's wealth, endowed with devotion. // <s>Krd</s> 5.13 //

children.text: guruṇā punar api vidhivat yathokta-vidhinā abhiṣiktaḥ kṛtābhiṣekaḥ tasmai gurave dakṣiṇāṃ viśrāṇya dattvā viprān abhyavahārya bhojayitvā bhakti-yutaḥ san samprīṇayet dhana-dhānyādibhiḥ prītiṃ kuryāt || KrdC_5.13 ||
children.translated_text: Consecrated again by the <s>guru</s> according to the prescribed procedure — having received re-consecration — having offered <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (honorarium) to that <s>guru</s>, having fed <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s, being endowed with devotion, one should gratify them with wealth, grains, and the like — one should bring them joy. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.13 ||
He states the duties of one whose mantra is perfected —
Thus, having perfected either of the two excellent mantras
Through recitation and other [practices], with mind fixed on <s>Acyuta</s> (the Imperishable);
One should recite at the three <s>savana</s>s (junctures of worship) daily,
Worshipping <s>Mukunda</s> according to rule, with pure mind. // <s>Krd</s> 5.14 //

children.text: ity anena prakāreṇa mantra-dvitayānyataraṃ mantra-dvitayayor madhye ekaṃ japādibhir japa-pūjā-homa-tarpaṇādibhiḥ parisādhya sādhayitvā acyuta-dhīr acyute śrī-kṛṣṇe dhīr buddhir yasya sa tathā | yad vā, acyutā na kṣaritā viṣṇau buddhir yasya sa tathā savana-tritaye sandhyādi-traye dinaśaḥ pratidinaṃ vidhinā ukta-prakāreṇa mukundaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ prayajet pūjayatu amanda-matiḥ śuddha-matiḥ || KrdC_5.14 ||
children.translated_text: Thus — in this manner — having perfected either of the two mantras — one among the two mantras — through recitation and other [practices] — recitation, worship, <s>homa</s>, <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation), etc. — <s>acyuta-dhī</s> meaning one whose mind is fixed on <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>); or alternatively, one whose intellect toward <s>Viṣṇu</s> has not fallen away — at the three <s>savana</s>s — at the three <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight) junctures etc. — daily, each day, according to rule — in the prescribed manner — one should worship <s>Mukunda</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>); <s>amanda-mati</s> meaning one of pure mind. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.14 ||
He states the morning meditation for worship —
Now, in a glorious garden-enclosed golden
Ground, within a gem-sparkling pavilion,
Beneath a shining wish-fulfilling tree, upon a radiant gem-studded
Platform, seated on a lotus throne — // <s>Krd</s> 5.15 //

children.text: sapta-ślokāntaṃ kulakam | athānantaraṃ bhakti-namraḥ bhakty-atiśayena namra-dehaḥ prage prātaḥ-kāle kathita-rūpaṃ kṛṣṇam anusmṛtya dhyātvā tad-aṅgendra-vajrādibhiḥ tasya kṛṣṇasyāṅgāni pūrvoktāni hṛdayādīni indrādayo daśa dik-pālāḥ vajrādayas tad-āyudhāni ca taiḥ saha pūjayitvā taṃ kṛṣṇaṃ sitā śarkarā mocā kadalī-viśeṣaḥ haiyaṅgavīnaṃ sadyo-jāta-ghṛtam | ebhis tathā dadhnā vimiśreṇa dadhi-saṃyuktena dogdhena pāyasena ca mantrī samprīṇayet | kīdṛśaṃ ? śrīmat śobhā-yuktaṃ yad udyānaṃ krīḍā-vanaṃ tena saṃvītaṃ veṣṭitaṃ yad-dhaima-sthalaṃ lasat-kāñcana-bhūmis tatrodbhāsīni udgata-kiraṇāni yāni yāni ratnāni taiḥ sphurat dedīpyamāno yo maṇḍapas tasyāntar-madhye dedīpyamāno yaḥ
kalpa-vṛkṣas tasyādhaś chāyāyām udgatā dīptir yasya tādṛśaṃ ratna-mayaṃ yat sthānaṃ tad-adhiṣṭhitaṃ tatrāvasthitaṃ yad ambhojaṃ padyaṃ tad eva pīṭhaṃ tatrādhirūḍham upaviṣṭam || KrdC_5.15 ||
children.translated_text: Wish-fulfilling tree; beneath it, in its shade, a gem-studded platform from which radiance arises — such a gem-made place; stationed there — situated there — is a lotus, which itself is the seat; thereupon seated — enthroned. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.15 ||

A <s>kulaka</s> (verse-cluster) extending for seven verses. Then — next — bowed with devotion — with body humbled by an abundance of <s>bhakti</s> — in the morning, at the early time, having contemplated — meditated upon — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in the described form, together with his limbs and [guardians] — his previously mentioned limbs such as the heart etc., the ten directional guardians beginning with <s>Indra</s>, and their weapons beginning with the thunderbolt — having worshipped [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] together with those, one should gratify that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with <s>sitā</s> (white sugar), <s>mocā</s> (a special type of banana), <s>haiyaṅgavīna</s> (freshly churned ghee), and also with <s>dadhi</s> (curds) mixed together, with milk, and with <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice pudding) — the ritualist should gratify [him]. Of what description? Glorious — that is, splendid — enclosed by a garden, a pleasure grove; a golden ground — a shining golden floor; therein, effulgent — with emanating rays — gems, by which sparkles — shines — a pavilion; within that, in the middle, a shining
Dark blue like a great sapphire, extremely young,
With hair loosely falling around a face smooth as jaggery;
With a face as enchanting as a fully blossomed lotus
Surrounded by swarms of bees, with beautiful lotus-eyes. // <s>Krd</s> 5.16 //

children.text: punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? mahā-nīla indra-nīlaḥ | tadvan nīlābhaṃ śyāmam | punar atyanta-bālaṃ pañca-vārṣikam | punaḥ, guḍāḥ kuṭilāḥ snigdhāḥ cikkaṇāḥ karṇānte kapole visrastāḥ paryākulāḥ | vaktrānteti pāṭhe visrastā mukhāvalambitāḥ keśā yasya tam | ali-vrātena bhramara-samūhena paryākulaṃ cañcalaṃ vyāptaṃ vā yat phullaṃ vikasitaṃ padmaṃ tadvat pramugdhaṃ manoharaṃ ānanaṃ mukhaṃ yasya tam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? śrīmat doṣa-rahitaṃ yad indīvaraṃ nīla-padmaṃ tat-sadṛśe akṣiṇī yasya tam || KrdC_5.16 ||
children.translated_text: Again, of what description? <s>Mahānīla</s> is the sapphire (<s>indranīla</s>); like that, dark blue — dark. Again, extremely young — five years old. Again, curly — tangled — smooth — glossy — loosely falling — disheveled at the edge of the ear, on the cheek. In the reading '<s>vaktrānta</s>,' loosely hanging upon the face — such are the locks of hair. With a face as enchanting as a fully blossomed lotus that is agitated — fluttering — pervaded by a swarm of bees (<s>ali-vrāta</s>). Again, of what description? Those whose eyes resemble the beautiful <s>indīvara</s> (blue lotus) — flawless and radiant.
Again, of what description?
With cheeks blooming and resplendent due to swinging earrings,
With a beautiful nose, with lips beautifully red, with a gently smiling face,
Radiant with a throat-ornament glistening with rays of many gems,
Wearing a tiger-claw [pendant] of <s>Pauṇḍarīka</s> (white lotus-like [beauty]).

children.text: cañcale ye kuṇḍale tābhyām unnatau ullasitau śobhamānau samphullau vikāśitau gaṇḍau yasya tam | punaḥ śobhamānā ghoṇā nāsā yasya tam | punaḥ suśoṇo lohito 'dharo yasya tam | punaḥ śobhanaṃ yat smitam īṣad-dhāsas tad-yuktam āsyaṃ yasya tam | punaḥ anekāni yāny aśmāni indranīla-prabhṛtīni ratnāni teṣāṃ ye raśmayaḥ kiraṇāḥ tair ullasantī yā kaṇṭha-bhūṣā tayā lasantaṃ śobhamānam | punaḥ pauṇḍarīkaṃ vyāghra-sambandhi-nakhaṃ vahantaṃ dhārayantam || KrdC_5.17 ||
children.translated_text: Those whose cheeks are elevated — resplendent — blooming — opened wide — due to the swinging earrings. Again, one whose nose (<s>ghoṇā</s>) is beautiful. Again, one whose lower lip is beautifully red. Again, one whose face has a beautiful smile — a gentle laugh. Again, radiant — resplendent — with a throat ornament glistening with the rays — beams — of many gems such as sapphire and the like. Again, wearing — bearing — a tiger-claw (<s>pauṇḍarīka</s>) [pendant].
Again, of what description?
With chest dusted by the dust of cows,
With well-nourished limbs, shining with ornaments of <s>aṣṭāpada</s> (gold);
At the region of the waist, upon the pair of beautiful shanks,
Bound with a string of tinkling little bells (<s>kiṅkiṇī</s>s).

children.text: dhenu-dhūlyā go-rajasā samuddhūsaraṃ dhūsaritam uraḥ-sthalaṃ yasya taṃ gavām anugamanāt suṣṭhu puṣṭam aṅgaṃ yasya tam | kīdṛśaṃ ? aṣṭāpadākalpa-dīptaṃ suvarṇa-ghaṭitālaṅkāreṇa śobhamānam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? kvaṇat-kiṅkiṇī-jāla-dāmnā śabdāyamāna-kṣudra-ghaṇṭikā-samūha-mālayā kaṭi-sthale śroṇi-taṭe cāru-jaṅghānta-yugme manohara-gulpha-dvayordhva-pradeśe pinaddhaṃ baddham || KrdC_5.18 ||
children.translated_text: One whose chest is made dusty — grayed — by the dust of cows; well-nourished limbs due to following the cows. Of what description? Shining with ornaments wrought of <s>aṣṭāpada</s> (gold). Again, of what description? Bound at the waist-region — at the hip — upon the pair of beautiful shanks — at the area above the pair of charming ankles — with a string of tinkling little bells — a garland of clusters of small bells that produce sound.
Again, of what description?
Laughing — [as if] laughing at the radiance of blooming <s>bandhujīva</s> (noon-flower) blossoms
With the magnificent lustre of his lotus-hands and lotus-feet;
In his right hand holding <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-pudding), in his left hand
Holding fresh, pure <s>haiyaṅgavīna</s> (freshly churned butter).

children.text: pāṇi-pādāmbujodāra-kāntyā hasta-caraṇa-padma-vipula-śobhayā hasad-bandhu-jīva-puṣpa-kāntiṃ hasantam upahasantam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? dakṣiṇe kare haste pāyasaṃ savya-haste vāma-kare navaṃ nūtanaṃ śuddhaṃ niṣkaluṣaṃ haiyaṅgavīnam navanītaṃ hyo go-dohanodbhavaṃ ghṛtaṃ dadhānaṃ dhārayantam || KrdC_5.19 ||
children.translated_text: With the extensive beauty of his lotus-hands and lotus-feet, [as if] laughing at — surpassing — the lustre of blooming <s>bandhujīva</s> flowers. Again, of what description? In his right hand, holding <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-pudding); in his left hand, holding fresh — newly prepared — pure — unblemished — <s>haiyaṅgavīna</s> (fresh butter) — butter produced from the previous day's milking.
Again, of what description?
The hosts of demons who had become a burden upon the earth,
<s>Anaḥ</s> (<s>Śakaṭāsura</s>), <s>Pūtanā</s>, and others — set upon destroying [them];
The Lord, surrounded by throngs of <s>gopikā</s>s (cowherd-women), <s>gopa</s>s (cowherds), and cows,
Worshipped by <s>Surendra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) and other hosts of gods.

children.text: mahī-bhāra-bhūtām arārāti-yūthān pṛthivī-bhāra-rūpa-daitya-samūhān anaḥ-pūtanādīn śakaṭāsura-prabhṛtīn nihantuṃ pravṛttam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? prabhuṃ samartham īśvaram | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? gopikā gopa-strī, gopaḥ gauḥ eteṣāṃ samūhena vītaṃ veṣṭitam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? indrādibhir deva-samūhair namaskṛtam || KrdC_5.20 ||
children.translated_text: The hosts of enemies who had become a burden upon the earth — the demon-hordes in the form of the earth's burden — <s>Anaḥ</s> (<s>Śakaṭāsura</s>, the cart-demon), <s>Pūtanā</s>, and others — set upon destroying them. Again, of what description? The Lord — capable, the Supreme Ruler. Again, of what description? Surrounded — encircled — by throngs of <s>gopikā</s>s (cowherd-women), <s>gopa</s>s (cowherds), and cows. Again, of what description? Worshipped — saluted — by <s>Indra</s> and other hosts of gods.
Having worshipped in the morning and then contemplated <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
With his limbs, <s>Indra</s>, the thunderbolt, and the other [enclosures], bowed down with devotion;
With white sugar, banana (<s>moca</s>), fresh butter (<s>haiyaṅgavīna</s>), and curds
Mixed with milk — one should gratify him.

children.text: pūrva-śloke vyākhyātam api kramānurodhena vyākhyāte prage prātaḥ-kāle ukta-prakāreṇa kṛṣṇam anusmṛtya dhyātvā upacāraiḥ sampūjya aṅgādy-āvaraṇaiḥ saha sampūjya naivedyaṃ dadyāt | naivedya-dravyam āha-siteti | sitā śarkarā mocā kadalī haiyaṅgavīnaṃ daugdhena pāyasena || KrdC_5.21 ||
children.translated_text: Although explained in the previous verse, in accordance with the sequence of the commentary: in the morning — at the early time — having contemplated <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in the described manner — having meditated [on him] — having worshipped with the <s>upacāra</s>s (offerings) — having worshipped together with the limbs and other encircling [deities] — one should give the <s>naivedya</s> (food-offering). He states the <s>naivedya</s> material with '<s>sitā</s>' etc.: <s>sitā</s> is white sugar; <s>mocā</s> is banana; <s>haiyaṅgavīna</s> is [fresh butter]; with <s>daugdha</s> meaning <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-pudding).
He states the fruit of the morning <s>savana</s> (juncture) worship —
Thus, whoever worships <s>Acyuta</s> (the Imperishable) every morning,
That person, daily, always, endowed with faith,
Will obtain before long complete prosperity (<s>Lakṣmī</s>);

children.text: iha pretya śuddhaṃ paraṃ dhāma bhūyāt // Krd_5.22 //
children.translated_text: And hereafter, having departed [this life], may he attain the supreme, pure abode.

children.text: ity anena prakāreṇa pratyahaṃ śaśvat sarvadā āstikya-yuktaḥ san yo naraḥ prātaḥ-kāle acyutam arcayet tam evāvaśyaṃ pūjayati sa iha loke acireṇaivālpa-kālenaiva samagrāṃ sampūrṇāṃ lakṣmīṃ sampadaṃ labhate prāpnoti pretya dehaṃ parityajya paraṃ śuddhaṃ brahmākhyaṃ mahaḥ bhūyāt prāpnoti tat-sarūpo bhavatīty arthaḥ || KrdC_5.22 ||
children.translated_text: In this manner, daily, always, endowed with faith, the person who worships <s>Acyuta</s> in the morning — who indeed necessarily worships him — in this world, before long — in a short time — obtains complete, full prosperity (<s>Lakṣmī</s>); having departed — having left the body — may he attain the supreme, pure abode called <s>Brahman</s> — he becomes of the same form as That — this is the meaning.

children.text: prātaḥ pūjāyām eva naivedyaṃ tarpaṇaṃ ca darśayati-
children.translated_text: Regarding the morning worship itself, he shows the <s>naivedya</s> (food-offering) and <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) —
At the break of day, daily, having thus worshipped <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),
Then having offered with curds, or [curds] combined with jaggery, with waters;
Having duly offered libation (<s>tarpaṇa</s>) at the auspicious mouth, with mind fixed on him,

children.text: japyāt sahasram atha sāṣṭakam ādareṇa // Krd_5.23 //
children.translated_text: One should recite with devotion one thousand and eight [times].

children.text: athavā śabdaḥ pāda-pūraṇe iti pūrvokta-prakāreṇa ahno-mukhe prātaḥ-kāle anudinaṃ pratyahaṃ śauriṃ kṛṣṇam abhipūjya guḍa-sahitena dadhnā naivedyaṃ dattvā jalais tad-dhiyā guḍa-sahita-buddhyā śrīmataḥ kṛṣṇasya mukhe samanutarpya athānantaraṃ taṃ mantram ādareṇa sāṣṭakaṃ sahasraṃ aṣṭottara-sahasraṃ japet || KrdC_5.23 ||
children.translated_text: The word '<s>athavā</s>' (or) is used as a metrical filler. In the previously described manner, at the break of day — in the morning — daily, each day, having worshipped <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), having offered the <s>naivedya</s> with curds combined with jaggery, with water — with the understanding of [it being combined with] jaggery — having performed <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) at the auspicious mouth of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, then next, one should recite that mantra with devotion one thousand and eight times.
He states the midday <s>savana</s> (juncture) meditation —
At midday, [one should meditate on Kṛṣṇa] whose form is distinguished by the method of <s>japa</s> (recitation),
Worthy of salutation by the foremost hosts of divine sages, ascetics, and celestial beings;
Surrounded by multitudes of cows, cowherds, and cowherd-women,
With limbs beautifully formed, captivating, with the complexion of a dense rain-cloud.

children.text: caturtha-śloka-stha-kriyayā yojanā evam anena prakāreṇa madhyandine madhyāhne nandajaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ dhyātvā indirā śrīs tasyā āpty-arthaṃ arcayatu | kīdṛśaṃ ? japa-vidhānena viśiṣṭaṃ rūpaṃ yasya taṃ japārthaṃ yat dhyānam | atha prakaṭa-saurabhety ādi tṛtīya-paṭalokta-dhyānaṃ tad evātrāpīti tripāṭhinaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? vandyaṃ śreṣṭham | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? surā indrādaya ṛṣayo nāradādayaḥ yatayaḥ sanakādayaḥ khecarāḥ svarga-vāsinaḥ eteṣāṃ mukhyāḥ śreṣṭhāḥ teṣāṃ vṛndaiḥ samūhaiḥ tathā gauḥ gopaḥ gopa-strī ca eteṣāṃ nikaraiḥ samūhaiḥ parītaṃ veṣṭitaṃ sāndro niviḍo yo ambudo meghas tadvac chavir yasya tat | atha ca sujātaṃ doṣa-rahitam | atha ca manoharaṃ netrotsava-kārakam

children.translated_text: whose limbs [are thus described].

The syntactical connection is made with the action stated in the fourth verse: in this manner, at midday — at noon — having meditated on <s>Nandaja</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, son of <s>Nanda</s>), one should worship for the attainment of <s>Indirā</s> (<s>Śrī</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>). Of what description? One whose form is distinguished by the method of <s>japa</s> — the meditation meant for the purpose of recitation. Now, the meditation described in the third chapter beginning with '<s>prakaṭa-saurabha</s>' etc. — that same [meditation] applies here too — thus [say] the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s. Again, of what description? Worthy of salutation — the most excellent. Again, of what description? The <s>sura</s>s are <s>Indra</s> and others; the <s>ṛṣi</s>s are <s>Nārada</s> and others; the <s>yati</s>s are <s>Sanaka</s> and others; the <s>khecara</s>s are the heaven-dwellers — surrounded by the hosts of the foremost among these; likewise by multitudes of cows, cowherds, and cowherd-women; <s>sāndra</s> means dense — having the complexion of a dense cloud; moreover, well-born — free from defects; moreover, captivating — a feast for the eyes —
Again, of what description?
With a beautiful topknot adorned with a peacock-feather crest-jewel,
With shining forehead-mark, with lotus-eyes,
With a face like the full moon's orb, with cheeks graced by gem-studded earrings,
With a beautiful nose, with an exceedingly beautiful gentle smile.

children.text: mayūrasyedaṃ māyūraṃ patraṃ pakṣaḥ māyūraṃ ca tat-patraṃ ceti māyūra-patraṃ tena parikpto yo vataṃsaḥ śiro-bhūṣaṇam | vaṣṭi-bhāgurirallopam avāpyorupasargayoḥ ity akāra-lopaḥ | tena ramyo dhammillaḥ keśa-pāśaḥ yasya tam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? ambujavat padmavat akṣiṇī yasya sa tathā tam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? sampūrṇo ya indu-bimbaś candra-maṇḍalaṃ tadvad vadanaṃ mukhaṃ yasya sa tathā tam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? maṇi-mayaṃ yat kuṇḍalaṃ tena śrī-yuktau śobhā-sahitau gaṇḍau yasya tam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? śobhanā nāsā yasya tam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? manohareṣad-hāsya-yuktam || KrdC_5.25 ||
children.translated_text: That which belongs to the peacock is <s>māyūra</s>; its feather is the plume; a peacock-feather — with that is adorned the <s>vataṃsa</s> (crest-ornament) — the head-ornament. By the rule '<s>vaṣṭi-bhāguri</s>...' the <s>a</s>-vowel is elided. By that is made beautiful the <s>dhammilla</s> — the mass of hair. Again, of what description? One whose eyes are like lotuses (<s>ambuja</s>). Again, of what description? One whose face is like the full moon's orb — the lunar disc. Again, of what description? One whose cheeks are graced — endowed with beauty — by gem-studded earrings. Again, of what description? One whose nose is beautiful. Again, of what description? Endowed with a captivating gentle smile.
Again, of what description?
Wearing yellow garments (<s>pītāmbara</s>), with limbs resplendent with beautiful anklets, necklaces, waist-bands,
Armlets, bracelets, and other [ornaments];
With a body anointed with divine unguents, bearing on [his] shoulder a splendid
Unfading, variegated forest-garland — radiant like the god of love.

children.text: pītāmbaraṃ vastraṃ yasya tam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? manohara-nūpurādibhiḥ śobhitam aṅgam yasya taṃ hāro muktāvalī kāñcī kṣudra-ghaṇṭikā keyūram aṅgadam ūrmir mudrikā kaṭakaḥ kaṅkaṇa ādi-padena kirīṭādīnāṃ parigrahaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? deva-sambandhinānulepanena kuṅkumādinā piśāṅgitaṃ piñjaritam aṃse skandhe rājantī śobhamānā amlānā akliṣṭā citrā nānā-prakārikā vanamālā patr-puṣpa-mayī āpāda-lambinī mālā yasya tam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? anaṅgavat kāmavat dīptam || KrdC_5.26 ||
children.translated_text: One whose garment is yellow (<s>pītāmbara</s>). Again, of what description? One whose limbs are resplendent with beautiful anklets and the like — necklace (<s>hāra</s>) is a pearl string; <s>kāñcī</s> is a girdle with small bells; <s>keyūra</s> is an armlet; <s>ūrmi</s> is a ring; <s>kaṭaka</s> is a bracelet — the word '<s>ādi</s>' includes the crown etc. Again, of what description? Tinged — made golden-yellow — with divine unguent of saffron and the like; on the shoulder, resplendent — beautiful — unfading — unwithered — variegated — of many kinds — the forest-garland, made of leaves and flowers, hanging down to the feet. Again, of what description? Radiant like <s>Anaṅga</s> (the god of love, <s>Kāma</s>).
Again, of what description?
Playing the flute (<s>veṇu</s>), or else holding it in one hand,
And in the other [hand] a cowherd's staff — of magnificent appearance;
In his right [hand], the best of gems, skilled in granting desired [wishes] —
Having thus meditated, one should worship <s>Nandaja</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) for the attainment of <s>Indirā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>).

children.text: veṇuṃ dhamantam vādayantam | athavā pakṣāntare sva-kare savyetare vāme go-rakṣaṇa-daṇḍaṃ dadhānaṃ tathā dakṣe dakṣiṇe īpsita-dāna-dakṣaṃ maṇiṃ dadhānam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? udāra-veṣam | udbhaṭa-veṣam iti rudra-dharaḥ | vastutas tu veṇuṃ vādayantaṃ tad eva darśayati atheti vāma-kare savyaṃ dakṣiṇa-vāmayor ity abhidhānāt dvayor evātra-tantreṇa saṅgrahaḥ tatra savye dvitīya-vāma-haste paśupa-yaṣṭiṃ paraśurakārthaṃ yaṣṭiṃ daṇḍaṃ tathā savye dakṣiṇe haste maṇi-pravaram maṇi-śreṣṭhaṃ cintāmaṇiṃ dadhānam | kīdṛśaṃ ? maṇi-pravaram īpsita-dāna-dakṣaṃ vāñchitārtha-dāna-kṣamam ity arthaḥ || KrdC_5.27 ||
children.translated_text: Playing — sounding — the flute. Or, in the alternative: in one hand, the left — holding a cowherd's staff for protecting cows; likewise, in the right [hand], holding the best of gems, skilled in granting desired [boons]. Again, of what description? Of magnificent appearance. <s>Rudradhara</s> [reads]: 'of extraordinary appearance.' In truth, [he is described as] playing the flute — that itself he shows with '<s>atha</s>': in the left hand — since '<s>savya</s>' refers to both right and left, here both are intended — in the left, the second left hand, a cowherd's staff — a rod for the purpose of guarding cattle; likewise, in the right (<s>savya</s> meaning right) hand, holding the best of gems — the <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem). Of what description? The best of gems, skilled in granting desired [wishes] — capable of granting desired objects — this is the meaning.
He states the manner of giving <s>naivedya</s> (food-offering) for the enclosure [deities] —
<s>Dāma</s> and others, the limb[-deities], the beloved queens, the friends, the wish-fulfilling trees,
The thunderbolt and other [weapons] — having worshipped according to the prescribed method;
The varieties of food-offerings described in the <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) procedure
One should duly offer in a golden vessel of the finest kind.

children.text: dāma ādir yasya | ādi-padena sudāmādīnāṃ parigrahaḥ | aṅgāni pūrvoktāni pañca dayitā rukmiṇy-ādyāḥ suhṛdo vasudevādyāḥ aṅghripā mandarādyāḥ pūrvoktā indrādayo daśa dikpālāḥ vajrādīni ca teṣāṃ āyudhāni pūrvoktāni | etair yathā-vidhānaṃ yathokta-prakāreṇa kṛṣṇaṃ sampūjya dīkṣā-vidhāne kathitaṃ naivedya-samūhaṃ haimaṃ suvarṇa-maye pātra-śreṣṭhe yathāvat nivedayatu || KrdC_5.28 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Dāma</s> is the beginning — the word '<s>ādi</s>' includes <s>Sudāma</s> and others. The limbs (<s>aṅga</s>s) are the five previously mentioned. The beloved are <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and others. The friends are <s>Vasudeva</s> and others. The trees (<s>aṅghripa</s>s) are <s>Mandāra</s> and the rest. The previously mentioned ten directional guardians beginning with <s>Indra</s>, and the thunderbolt and other weapons as previously described. Having worshipped <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> together with all these according to the prescribed method, the food-offering as described in the initiation procedure should be duly offered in a golden vessel of the finest quality.
He states the <s>homa</s> (fire-offering) and related [rites] —
Then one should offer one hundred and eight oblations with milk-rice,
Soaked in ghee, mixed with fine white sugar;
And one should give <s>bali</s> (offering) in the respective directions to the hosts of divine sages, yogis,
And subsidiary deities of the <s>varṇa</s>s (classes) — with exalted mind.
