children.text: anantaraṃ payo 'nnaiḥ pāyasaiḥ sarpiḥ-plutaiḥ susita-śarkarayā vimiśraiḥ atiśubhra-śarkarayā militaiḥ aṣṭādhikaṃ śatam juhuyāt homaṃ kuryāt | sāhacaryāt kalpanā-lāghavāc ca homokta-dravyeṇaiva nija-dikṣu sva-sva-dikṣu surarṣi-yogi- vargopadaivata-gaṇebhyo baliṃ dadyāt | tatra surā virañci-prabhṛtayaḥ pūrva-dik-sthāḥ ṛṣayo nāradādayo dakṣiṇa-dik-sthāḥ yogi-vargaḥ sanakādiḥ paścima-diksthāḥ upadeva-gaṇāḥ yakṣa-siddha-gandharva-vidyādharādyāḥ uttara-dik-sthā iti tripāṭhinaḥ | upadeva-gaṇāḥ daśa-dik-pālā iti rudradharaḥ | udagra-cetā udbhaṭa-cittaḥ sotsāha ity arthaḥ || KrdC_5.29 ||
children.translated_text: Subsequently, with <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice) offerings — foods of milk-rice saturated with ghee and mixed with exceedingly white sugar — one should offer one hundred and eight oblations into the fire. By association and for ease of arrangement, with the very substance prescribed for <s>homa</s>, one should give <s>bali</s> (offerings) in their respective directions to the groups of gods, sages, yogis, and subsidiary deities. Therein, the gods — <s>Virañci</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) and others — are situated in the eastern direction; the sages — <s>Nārada</s> and others — in the southern direction; the group of yogis — <s>Sanaka</s> and others — in the western direction; the subsidiary deities — <s>Yakṣa</s>s, <s>Siddha</s>s, <s>Gandharva</s>s, <s>Vidyādhara</s>s, and others — in the northern direction — thus [say] the <s>tripāṭhin</s>s. The subsidiary deities are the ten directional guardians — thus [says] <s>Rudradhara</s>. <s>Udagra-cetā</s> means one of exalted mind — that is, one who is enthusiastic. || KrdC_5.29 ||
With the intention of <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice) mixed with fresh butter, at the end of worship, with water, upon his face;

children.text: santarpya japatu mantrī sahasram aṣṭottara-śataṃ vāpi // Krd_5.30 //
children.translated_text: Having performed <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation), the <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) should recite one thousand and eight, or one hundred and eight. // Krd_5.30 //

children.text: arcanānte pūjāvasāne tasya devasya mukhe navanītena militaṃ sambaddhaṃ yat pāyasaṃ tad-buddhyā jalaiḥ santarpya tarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā mantrī sādhakaḥ aṣṭādhikaṃ sahasram śataṃ vā japatu || KrdC_5.30 ||
children.translated_text: At the end of worship — at the conclusion of <s>pūjā</s> — with the intention of <s>pāyasa</s> mixed — combined — with fresh butter, upon the face of the deity, having performed <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) with water, the <s>mantrī</s> — the <s>sādhaka</s> (practitioner) — should recite one thousand and eight, or one hundred [and eight]. || KrdC_5.30 ||
He states the fruit of this —
At midday, <s>Vallavī-vallabha</s> (the beloved of the cowherd women) — him,
The foremost among men who daily worships with devotion;
All the gods bow to him perpetually,
And all the worlds would indeed be under his control. // Krd_5.31 //

children.text: yo narāgryo nara-śreṣṭhaḥ ahno madhye madhyāhne taṃ vallavī-vallabhaṃ gopī-priyaṃ nityaṃ sarvadā bhaktyā sāttvikena bhāvenārcayet | taṃ nara-śreṣṭhaṃ sarve devāḥ namasyanti | tathā śaśvat sarvadā sarve janā eva tad-vaśe varteran tad-vaśyāḥ syur ity arthaḥ || KrdC_5.31 ||
children.translated_text: The foremost among men — the best of men — at midday — at noon — should worship him, <s>Vallavī-vallabha</s> — the beloved of the <s>gopī</s>s — always, with devotion — with a <s>sāttvika</s> disposition. All the gods bow to that best of men. Likewise, perpetually — always — all people indeed would be under his control — would be subject to him — this is the meaning. || KrdC_5.31 ||
Endowed with intelligence, long life, prosperity, beauty, and good fortune,
With sons, friends, cows, land, gems, and grains;
And with other abundant enjoyments, greatly enriched,

children.text: bhūyān bhūyo dhāma tac cācyutākhyam // Krd_5.32 //
children.translated_text: He shall again [attain] that supreme abode called <s>Acyuta</s>. // Krd_5.32 //

children.text: tathā iha loke medhā dhāraṇāvatī buddhiḥ āyuḥ jīvanaṃ, śrīḥ lakṣmīḥ | kāntiḥ śarīra-śobhā, saubhāgyaṃ sarvajana-priyatā | etaiḥ yuktaḥ sambaddhaḥ tathā putrair aurasaiḥ mitraiḥ suhṛdbhir gauḥ prthivī ratnaṃ dhānyaṃ vrīhyādiḥ | etaiś catathānyair bhūribhiḥ pracūraiḥ sukhair āḍhyaḥ upacitaḥ san punaḥ dehāvasāne acyutākhyaṃ kṛṣṇa-nāmakaṃ tejo maho bhūyān tad-rūpo bhavatīty arthaḥ || KrdC_5.32 ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, in this world: <s>medhā</s> is retentive intellect; <s>āyus</s> is life; <s>śrī</s> is <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune); <s>kānti</s> is bodily radiance; <s>saubhāgya</s> is being dear to all people. Endowed — connected — with these; likewise with sons — biological sons — with friends — well-wishers — cows, land, gems, grains such as rice etc. With these and other abundant — plentiful — enjoyments, enriched — filled — being so, again, at the end of the body [i.e., at death], he attains the radiance — the splendor — named <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) — he becomes of that form — this is the meaning. || KrdC_5.32 ||
He states the arrangement for the third-time worship —
Regarding the third-time worship, there is an alternative regarding the time;

children.text: sāyāhne niśi vety atra vadanty eke vipaścitaḥ // Krd_5.33 //
children.translated_text: 'In the evening' or 'at night' — here some learned ones say. // Krd_5.33 //

children.text: tṛtīya-kāla-pūjāyām kālasya velāyāṃ vikalpanā vikalpo 'sti tam evāha-sāyāhne sandhyāyāṃ niśi rātrau veti atra eke vipaścito vadanti || KrdC_5.33 ||
children.translated_text: Regarding the third-time worship, there is an alternative — an option — regarding the time — the occasion. He states it: 'in the evening' — at <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight) — 'at night' — these are the options. Here, some learned ones say thus. || KrdC_5.33 ||
What then? He says —
If with the ten-syllable [mantra], then at night; with the eighteen-syllable one, in the evening;

children.text: ubhayīm ubhayenaiva kuryād ity apare jaguḥ // Krd_5.34 //
children.translated_text: Both [worships] with both [mantras] — one should perform — thus say others. // Krd_5.34 //

children.text: ced yadi daśākṣareṇa mantreṇa pūjādikaṃ tadā rātrau yad aṣṭādaśārṇato aṣṭādaśākṣareṇa mantreṇa tadā sāyāhne ity ekeṣāṃ matam | apare ca punaḥ ubhayīm ubhaya-pūjām ubhayenaiva daśākṣareṇāṣṭādaśākṣareṇa ca tat kuryād iti jaguḥ kathayanti | tathā caicchiko vikalpa iti bhāvaḥ || KrdC_5.34 ||
children.translated_text: If — in case — with the ten-syllable mantra the worship etc. [is performed], then at night; if with the eighteen-syllable — the eighteen-lettered mantra — then in the evening — this is the view of some. And others again say — both worships with both — with the ten-syllable and the eighteen-syllable — one should perform — they declare. And thus it is an optional choice — this is the purport. || KrdC_5.34 ||

children.text: sāyāhna ity ādi | atra nava-ślokāntaṃ kulakam |
children.translated_text: 'In the evening' and so forth. Here, [the verses form] a <s>kulaka</s> (verse-cluster) ending with the ninth verse.
In the evening, in <s>Dvāravatī</s> (Dvārakā), adorned with wonderful gardens,
Surrounded by sixteen thousand mansions; // Krd_5.35 //
Surrounded by lakes filled with swans and cranes,
Abounding in lotuses and blue lotuses, with pure waters, in the finest mansion; // Krd_5.36 //
In a gem-pavilion whose brilliance rivals the radiance of the rising sun,
<s>Hari</s>, comfortably seated on a soft cushion, upon a golden lotus throne; // Krd_5.37 //
Surrounded by <s>Nārada</s> and others, [engaged] in the ascertainment of the nature of the Self,

children.text: tebhyo munibhyaḥ svaṃ dhāma diśantaṃ param akṣaram // Krd_5.38 //
children.translated_text: Revealing to those sages his own abode — the supreme, imperishable. // Krd_5.38 //

children.text: sāyāhne evam etādṛśa-veṣa-dhāriṇaṃ hariṃ dhyātvārcayet | kīdṛśaṃ ? mṛdvāstara-komalāsana-rūpe hemāmbhojāsane kanaka-padmāsane samāsīnam upaviṣṭaṃ kutrāvasthitaṃ maṇi-maṇḍape | kiṃ viśiṣṭe ? udgacchan yaḥ pradyotanaḥ sūryaḥ tasya dyotasya samānā dyutir yasya tasmin | kutra ? bhavanottame gṛha-śreṣṭhe | kiṃ viśiṣṭe ? citrodyānopaśobhite bahudhopavana-sevite | punaḥ kiṃ viśiṣṭe ? dvāravatyāṃ vidyamāne | punaḥ kiṃ viśiṣṭe ? bhavanair gṛhair abhisaṃvṛte | kīdṛśaiḥ ? dvyaṣṭa-sāhasra-saṅkhyātaiḥ |
children.translated_text: In the evening, having meditated upon <s>Hari</s> bearing such appearance, one should worship [him]. Of what description? Comfortably seated — enthroned — upon a golden lotus seat — a golden lotus throne — which is in the form of a soft cushion — a delicate seat. Where situated? In a gem-pavilion. Of what quality? Whose radiance is equal to the brilliance of the rising sun — <s>pradyotana</s> meaning the sun. Where? In the finest mansion — the best of dwellings. Of what quality? Adorned with wonderful gardens — endowed with various pleasure groves. Again of what quality? Located in <s>Dvāravatī</s> (Dvārakā). Again of what quality? Surrounded by mansions — dwellings. Of what number? Numbering sixteen thousand.

children.text: punaḥ kiṃ viśiṣṭe ? sarobhiḥ sarovaraiḥ parīte | kīdṛśaiḥ ? amalāmbhobhir nirmala-jalaiḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? haṃsa-sārasa-saṅkīrṇaiḥ haṃsādi-pakṣi-gaṇair vyāptaiḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? kamalotpala-śālibhiḥ padmotpala-sahitaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Again of what quality? Surrounded by lakes — ponds. Of what kind? With pure waters — limpid waters. Again of what kind? Filled with swans and cranes — pervaded by flocks of birds such as swans. Again of what kind? Abounding in lotuses and blue lotuses — endowed with lotus and water-lily [flowers].

children.text: hariṃ kīdṛśaṃ ? nāradādyair munibhiḥ parivṛtam veṣṭitam | kim-artham ? ātma-tattva-vinirṇaye ātma-tattva-niścaye nimitte | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? tebhyo nāradādibhyaḥ svaṃ dhāma jñāna-svarūpam ātmānaṃ kathayantam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? parama-vidyā-tat-kārya-rahitam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? akṣaram avināśi || KrdC_5.35-38 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> — of what description? Surrounded — encircled — by sages, <s>Nārada</s> and others. For what purpose? For the ascertainment of the nature of the Self — on the occasion of determining the Self-principle. Again of what description? Revealing to those <s>Nārada</s> and others his own abode — his own nature as knowledge itself. Again of what description? Free from supreme <s>vidyā</s> (ignorance) and its effects. Again of what description? Imperishable — indestructible. || KrdC_5.35-38 ||
Again of what description?
Resembling a blue lotus, gentle, with eyes reddish and elongated like lotus petals;
Resplendent with crown and diadem interspersed with glossy curls of hair. // Krd_5.39 //

children.text: indīvara-nibhaṃ nīlāmbhoja-sadṛśaṃ saumyaṃ ugratā-rahitam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? padma-patravad āyate dīrghe īkṣaṇe yasya tam | punaḥ snigdhāḥ cikkaṇā ye kuntalāḥ keśās taiḥ sambhinne milite kirīṭa-mukuṭe tābhyām ujjvalaṃ dedīpyamānam | tatra kirīṭa-śabdena lalāṭāśritaḥ tri-śṛṅgo 'laṅkāra-viśeṣaḥ kathyate | mukuṭa-śabdena ca mūrdhni madhya-bhāgāśritaṃ tac ca dīpa-śikhā-kāro 'laṅkāra-viśeṣaḥ kathyate || KrdC_5.39 ||
children.translated_text: Resembling a blue lotus — similar to a dark-blue water-lily — gentle — free from ferocity. Again of what description? One whose eyes are elongated — long — like lotus petals. Again, the glossy — smooth — curls of hair, by which the crown and diadem are interspersed — combined — resplendent — shining — through those two. Therein, by the word '<s>kirīṭa</s>' is meant a special ornament with three peaks resting on the forehead. And by the word '<s>mukuṭa</s>' is meant a special ornament in the shape of a lamp-flame resting on the central part of the head. || KrdC_5.39 ||
Again of what description?
With a beautiful, serene face, with sparkling <s>makara</s>-shaped (crocodile-shaped) earrings;
With <s>Śrīvatsa</s> on his chest, with the radiant <s>Kaustubha</s> [gem], wearing a forest garland (<s>vanamālā</s>). // Krd_5.40 //

children.text: cāru manoharaṃ prasannaṃ phala-dāyi vadanaṃ yasya tam | punaḥ sphuratī dedīpyamāne makarākṛtī kuṇḍale yasya tam | punaḥ śrīvatso vipra-pāda-prahāra-kṛta-cihna-viśeṣo vakṣasi yasya tam | punaḥ bhrājan dedīpyamānaḥ kaustubho maṇi-viśeṣo yasya tam | punaḥ vanamālā-dhāriṇam || KrdC_5.40 ||
children.translated_text: One whose face is charming — enchanting — and serene — bestowing grace. Again, one whose earrings, in the shape of <s>makara</s>s (mythical aquatic creatures), are sparkling — shining. Again, <s>Śrīvatsa</s> — a special mark made by the kick of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s foot — is on whose chest. Again, <s>Kaustubha</s> — a special gem — is radiant — gleaming — on whom. Again, one wearing a <s>vanamālā</s> (forest garland). || KrdC_5.40 ||
With chest tawny like <s>kāśmīra</s> (saffron), wearing yellow silken garments;
Adorned with necklace, armlet, bracelet, girdle, and other [ornaments]. // Krd_5.41 //

children.text: kāśmīreṇa kuṅkuma-varṇam uro yasya tam | punaḥ pīta-vastra-dhāriṇam | punaḥ hāraḥ muktāhāraḥ keyūram aṅgadaṃ bāhv-alaṅkāraḥ | kaṭakaḥ kaṅkaṇaḥ | rasanā kṣudra-ghaṇṭikā ādi-śabdenāṅgulīyakādeḥ parigrahaḥ etaiḥ pariṣkṛtaṃ śobhitam || KrdC_5.41 ||
children.translated_text: One whose chest is saffron-colored — tinted with <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron). Again, wearing yellow garments. Again, <s>hāra</s> is a pearl necklace; <s>keyūra</s> is an <s>aṅgada</s> — an arm ornament; <s>kaṭaka</s> is a bracelet; <s>rasanā</s> is a small tinkling bell; by the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), finger-rings and the like are included. Adorned — beautified — with these. || KrdC_5.41 ||
Again of what description?
Having removed the great burden of the earth, with delighted mind;
With four arms radiant with conch, discus, mace, and lotus. // Krd_5.42 //

children.text: hṛto 'panīto viśvambharāyāḥ pṛthvyā bhūri-bhāro bṛhad-bhāro 'surādi-lakṣaṇo yena tam | punaḥ muditaṃ hṛṣṭaṃ mānasaṃ yasya tam | punaḥ śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-padmaiḥ śobhitaṃ bāhu-catuṣṭayam yasya tam || KrdC_5.42 ||
children.translated_text: One by whom the great burden — the heavy burden characterized by <s>asura</s>s and the like — of <s>Viśvambharā</s> (the earth) has been removed — taken away. Again, one whose mind is delighted — joyful. Again, one whose four arms are made radiant by conch, discus, mace, and lotus. || KrdC_5.42 ||
Having thus meditated, the <s>mantrī</s> (ritualist) should worship the first encirclement (<s>āvṛti</s>) with his limb-[deities];

children.text: dvitīyāṃ mahiṣībhis tu tṛtīyāyāṃ samarcayet // Krd_5.43 //
children.translated_text: The second with the consorts (<s>mahiṣī</s>s), and in the third he should worship — // Krd_5.43 //
<s>Nārada</s>, <s>Parvata</s>, <s>Jiṣṇu</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), <s>Niśaṭha</s>, <s>Uddhava</s>, and <s>Dāruka</s>,

children.text: viśvaksenaṃ ca saineyaṃ dikṣv agre vinatā-sutam // Krd_5.44 //
children.translated_text: <s>Viśvaksena</s> and <s>Saineya</s> (<s>Sātyaki</s>) in the directions, and in front, the son of <s>Vinatā</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>). // Krd_5.44 //

children.text: atra pūjāyāṃ aṅgaiḥ pūrvoktaiḥ pañcāṅgaiḥ prathamāvaraṇaṃ bhavati | dvitīyāvaraṇaṃ mahiṣībhiḥ rukmiṇy-ādibhiḥ | tṛtīyāyām āvṛtau dikṣu pravādi-dikṣu vakṣyamāṇān nāradādīn agre ca vinatā-sutaṃ garuḍaṃ pūjayet | parvata-nāmā muni-viśeṣaḥ | jiṣṇur arjunaḥ | niśaṭho yādava-viśeṣaḥ | uddhavo 'pi tathā | dārukaḥ kṛṣṇa-sārathiḥ | viśvaksenaḥ bhāṇḍāgārikaḥ saineyaḥ sātyakiḥ || KrdC_5.43-44 ||
children.translated_text: In this worship, with the previously mentioned five limbs (<s>pañcāṅga</s>), the first encirclement is formed. The second encirclement is with the consorts — <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and others. In the third encirclement, in the directions — beginning with the eastern direction — one should worship the aforementioned <s>Nārada</s> and others, and in front, the son of <s>Vinatā</s> — <s>Garuḍa</s>. <s>Parvata</s> is a particular sage. <s>Jiṣṇu</s> is <s>Arjuna</s>. <s>Niśaṭha</s> is a particular <s>Yādava</s>. <s>Uddhava</s> likewise. <s>Dāruka</s> is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s charioteer. <s>Viśvaksena</s> is the keeper of the treasury. <s>Saineya</s> is <s>Sātyaki</s>. || KrdC_5.43-44 ||
With the world-guardians and their weapons, two more encirclements;

children.text: iti sampūjya vidhivat pāyasena nivedayet // Krd_5.45 //
children.translated_text: Thus having duly worshipped, one should make offering with <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice). // Krd_5.45 //

children.text: lokeśair indrādibhir ekam āvaraṇam | tat-praharaṇais tad-āyudhair vajrādibhir aparāvaraṇam | evaṃ krameṇāvaraṇa-dvayam ity anena prakāreṇa pañcāvaraṇakena sampūjya vidhivad dīkṣā-kathitaṃ pāyasaṃ dadyāt || KrdC_5.45 ||
children.translated_text: With the world-guardians — <s>Indra</s> and others — [constitutes] one encirclement. With their weapons — their arms such as the thunderbolt etc. — another encirclement. Thus, in this sequence, [forming] a pair of encirclements — by this method, having duly worshipped with five encirclements, one should offer the <s>pāyasa</s> prescribed in the initiation. || KrdC_5.45 ||
He shows the method of <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) and the count of recitation —
Having gratified <s>Hari</s> with water, with the thought of milk mixed with sugar;

children.text: japed aṣṭa-śataṃ mantrī bhāvayan puruṣottamam // Krd_5.46 //
children.translated_text: The <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) should recite one hundred and eight, meditating on <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person). // Krd_5.46 //

children.text: khaṇḍena śarkarayā vimiśraṃ militaṃ yad dugdhaṃ tad-buddhyā jalaiḥ kṛṣṇaṃ tarpayitvā puruṣottamaṃ bhāvayan dhyāyan mantrī sādhakaḥ aṣṭādhika-śataṃ japet | yadyapi tarpaṇasya ktvā-pratyayena pūrva-kālatā pratīyate tathāpi prathamaṃ japaḥ tad anu tarpaṇaṃ kāryaṃ tathaivānukramāt sampradāyāc ceti rudradharaḥ || KrdC_5.46 ||
children.translated_text: With water [regarded as] milk mixed — combined — with <s>khaṇḍa</s> (sugar), with that intention, having gratified <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, meditating upon — contemplating — <s>Puruṣottama</s>, the <s>mantrī</s> — the <s>sādhaka</s> — should recite one hundred and eight times. Although the precedence [of <s>tarpaṇa</s>] is understood from the <s>ktvā</s>-suffix [indicating prior action], nevertheless recitation is first, and <s>tarpaṇa</s> should be done thereafter — thus indeed from the sequence and tradition — [says] <s>Rudradhara</s>. || KrdC_5.46 ||
In all worships one should perform <s>homa</s> (fire-offering), or at midday;

children.text: āsanād arghya-paryantaṃ kṛtvā stutvā namet sudhīḥ // Krd_5.47 //
children.translated_text: Having performed [the rites] from the seat-[mantra] up to the <s>arghya</s> (offering), having praised, the wise one should bow. // Krd_5.47 //

children.text: sarvāsu tisṛṣv api pūjāsu homaṃ kuryāt | pakṣāntaram āha-athaveti | madhyandine madhyāhn-pūjāyāṃ vā homaṃ kuryād ity arthaḥ | āsanād iti | āsana-mantrād ārabhyārghya-paryantaṃ kṛtvā stutvā stavanaṃ kṛtvā namet daṇḍavat praṇamet | avasānārghyam avaśeṣayitvā madhye homaṃ kṛtvā tataḥ pūjāśeṣārghyam avasānārghya-saṃjñakaṃ parāṅmukhārghyāpara-paryāyaṃ dadyād ity arthaḥ || KrdC_5.47 ||
children.translated_text: In all — in all three — worships, one should perform <s>homa</s>. He states an alternative — 'or' — at midday — or one should perform <s>homa</s> in the midday worship — this is the meaning. 'From the seat' — beginning from the seat-mantra up to the <s>arghya</s>, having performed [the rites], having praised — having offered hymns of praise — one should bow — prostrate flat. Having reserved the concluding <s>arghya</s>, one should perform the <s>homa</s> in between, then one should give the remaining <s>arghya</s> of worship — called the concluding <s>arghya</s>, also known as the turning-away <s>arghya</s> — this is the meaning. || KrdC_5.47 ||
Having offered oneself, having dismissed that [deity] and placed [him] in one's own heart-lotus,

children.text: vinyasya tan-mayo bhūtvā punar ātmānam arcayet // Krd_5.48 //
children.translated_text: Having become one with him, one should again worship oneself. // Krd_5.48 //

children.text: ātma-samarpaṇa-mantreṇa svātmānaṃ parameśvare samarpya tat parameśvara-tejaḥ pūjā-sthānād udvāsya udvṛttya svakīya-hṛdaya-padme vinyasya tan-mayo bhūtvā punar ātmānam pūjayet || KrdC_5.48 ||
children.translated_text: With the mantra of self-offering, having offered oneself to the Supreme Lord, having dismissed — removed — that radiance of the Supreme Lord from the place of worship and placed [it] in one's own heart-lotus, having become one with him, one should again worship oneself. || KrdC_5.48 ||
He states the fruit of the evening worship —

children.text: sāyāhne vāsudevaṃ yo nityam eva yajen naraḥ |
children.translated_text: The man who daily worships <s>Vāsudeva</s> in the evening —

children.text: sarvān kāmān avāpyānte sa yāti paramāṃ gatim // Krd_5.49 //
children.translated_text: having attained all desires, at the end he goes to the supreme destination.

children.text: yo naraḥ sāyāhne vāsudevaṃ nityaṃ sarvadā evaṃ kathita-prakāreṇa yajet pūjā-tarpaṇa-homādibhiḥ paritoṣayet sarvān kāmān vāñchitān arthān avāpya dehāvasāne parāṃ gatiṃ viṣṇu-sāyujyaṃ prāpnoti || KrdC_5.49 ||
children.translated_text: The man who in the evening always, at all times, in the manner described, worships <s>Vāsudeva</s> — gratifies [him] through worship, <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation), <s>homa</s> (fire-offering), and the like — having attained all desires, all wished-for objects, at the end of the body [i.e., at death], he attains the supreme destination — <s>Viṣṇu-sāyujya</s> (union with <s>Viṣṇu</s>).
If at night, one should worship the son of <s>Devakī</s>, whose mind is overcome by love (<s>Manmatha</s>),
fatigued from the <s>rāsa</s> [-dance], situated in the midst of the circle of <s>gopī</s>s.

children.text: ced yadi rātrau pūjā kriyate tadā rāsaḥ krīḍā-viśeṣas tena pariśrāntaṃ devakī-nandanaṃ yajet manmathena ākrāntaṃ mānasaṃ hṛdayaṃ yasya tam | punaḥ gopīnāṃ maṇḍalaṃ goṣṭhī-viśeṣaḥ tasya madhye sthitam || KrdC_5.50 ||
children.translated_text: If — in the case that — worship is performed at night, then one should worship the son of <s>Devakī</s> — <s>Devakī-nandana</s> — fatigued from the <s>rāsa</s> — a special form of play — whose mind (<s>mānasa</s>), heart, is overcome (<s>ākrānta</s>) by <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love). Furthermore, situated in the midst of the <s>maṇḍala</s> — a special assembly — of <s>gopī</s>s.
He describes the <s>rāsa</s>-dance —
A thick, well-rounded, smooth [peg], raised a <s>vitasti</s> (span)
in height, having driven the stake (<s>śaṅku</s>) into the ground,
stepping upon [it] with both feet, with hands clasped one another's —
this whirling is indeed the <s>rāsa-goṣṭhī</s> (rāsa assembly).

children.text: itaretarātta-hastaiḥ paraspara-gṛhīta-hastaiḥ ayaṃ bhramo bhramaṇaṃ rāsa-goṣṭhī | kiṃ kṛtvā ? kau pṛthivyāṃ pṛthuṃ sthūlaṃ suvṛttaṃ vartulākāraṃ masṛṇaṃ snigdhaṃ vitasti-mātrotthitaṃ dvādaśāṅgula-pramāṇenordhvaṃ sthitaṃ śaṅku kāṣṭha-khaṇḍaṃ vinikhanya | punaḥ kiṃ kṛtvā ? padbhyāṃ śaṅkum ākramya niyantrya || KrdC_5.51 ||
children.translated_text: With hands clasped one another's (<s>itaretarātta-hasta</s>) — with hands mutually grasped — this whirling (<s>bhrama</s>), this revolving, is the <s>rāsa-goṣṭhī</s>. Having done what? On the ground (<s>kau</s>), a thick (<s>pṛthu</s>), well-rounded (<s>suvṛtta</s>) — circular in shape — smooth (<s>masṛṇa</s>) — sleek — stake (<s>śaṅku</s>), a piece of wood, raised a <s>vitasti</s> in height — standing upward to the measure of twelve finger-breadths — having driven [it] into [the ground]. And having done what else? Stepping upon the stake (<s>śaṅku</s>) with both feet — restraining [oneself upon it].
He states the meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) —
Bearing the pollen of land-lotuses (<s>sthala-nīraja</s>),
laden with a mass of wave-spray drops,
by a breeze that removes distress — on the vast,
pure bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, pervaded [by that breeze].

children.text:
dvādaśa-ślokāntaṃ kulakam | kalyāṇa-maya-svarūpam ajaṃ vicintya prathamodita-pīṭha-vare pūrvokta-dīkṣā-sambandhi-pūjā-pīṭha-śreṣṭhe vidhivat yathāvidhi prayatnena pūjayet | kīdṛśaṃ ? yamunā-puline yamunā-taṭe itaretara-baddha-kara-pramadā-gaṇa-kalpita-rāsa-vihāra-vidhau anyonya-baddha-hasta-strī-samūha-parikalpita-krīḍā-viśeṣa-vidhau maṇi-śaṅkugaṃ maṇimaya-śaṅku-madhya-gatam | kīdṛśe ? puline vāyunādhuyuṣite ākrānte | kīdṛśena ? sthala-nīrajaṃ sthala-kamalaṃ taṃ puṣpa-parāga-bhṛtā tat-keśara-saṃnikṛṣṭa-puṣpa-rajo-yuktena anena saugandhyaṃ varṇitaṃ punaḥ laharī-taraṅgas tasya kaṇa-jālaṃ bindu-samūhaḥ tasya bhareṇa prakarṣeṇa satām | utkṛṣṭena yukteneti tripāṭhinaḥ | anena śaityam uktam | punaḥ
paritāpa-hṛtā kheda-vināśakena anena māndyam uktam | punaḥ kīdṛśe puline ? vipule vistīrṇe punaḥ vimale śuddhe || KrdC_5.52 ||
children.translated_text: A <s>kulaka</s> (verse-cluster) extending for twelve verses. One should contemplate the auspicious, unborn (<s>aja</s>) form, and on the excellent seat — the previously mentioned worship-seat related to <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) — should worship duly, with effort, according to rule. Of what kind? On the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s> — on the shore of the <s>Yamunā</s> — in the ceremony of the <s>rāsa</s>-dance arranged by groups of women with hands clasped to one another — in the method of the special play arranged by the assemblage of women with mutually joined hands — stationed at the central gem-[studded] stake (<s>maṇi-śaṅku</s>). On what kind of bank? Pervaded by the wind — entered upon [by it]. By what kind [of wind]? <s>Sthala-nīraja</s> means land-lotus — bearing its flower-pollen, endowed with the pollen of adjacent flowers and their filaments — by this, its fragrance is described. Furthermore, <s>laharī</s> means wave; its <s>kaṇa-jāla</s> means a mass of droplets; laden (<s>bharena</s>) with abundance of those — 'endowed with excellence' — thus [say] the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s — by this, its coolness is described. Furthermore, that which removes distress (<s>paritāpa-hṛtā</s>) — by this, its gentleness is described. Again, what kind of bank? Vast (<s>vipula</s>) — expansive. And pure (<s>vimala</s>) — clean.
Crowded with hundreds of millions of women agitated
by the sharpened arrows of the bodiless one (<s>Aśarīra</s>, i.e., <s>Kāmadeva</s>);
with the directions illuminated by the rays
of the lord of stars (<s>Uḍunātha</s>, i.e., the Moon); swarming with roaming female bees.
Again, of what kind?

children.text:
aśarīraḥ kāmaḥ tasya yo niśāta-śaras tīkṣṇa-bāṇas tena unmathitā vyagrīkṛtā yāḥ
pramadās tāsāṃ śata-koṭibhir ākulitīkṛte itas tato 'vyāpteḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśe ? uḍunāthaś candras tasya karaiḥ kiraṇair viśadīkṛtaḥ prakāśito dik-
prasaro dig-avakāśo yatra tasmin | punaḥ kīdṛśe ? vicarantī bhramantī yā bhramarī tasyā nikaraḥ samūho yatra tasmin || KrdC_5.53 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aśarīra</s> is <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love); his sharpened arrow (<s>niśāta-śara</s>) — keen shaft — by that, the women (<s>pramadā</s>s) are agitated (<s>unmathita</s>) — made restless; crowded (<s>ākulita</s>) with hundreds of millions of them — pervaded everywhere by them. Again, of what kind? <s>Uḍunātha</s> is the Moon; by his rays (<s>kara</s>), the directional expanse (<s>dik-prasara</s>) is illuminated (<s>viśadīkṛta</s>) — made radiant — in such [a place]. Again, of what kind? Where there is an assemblage (<s>nikara</s>) of roaming (<s>vicarantī</s>), buzzing female bees (<s>bhramarī</s>) — in such [a place].
By <s>Vidyādhara</s>s, <s>Kinnara</s>s, <s>Siddha</s>s, and <s>Sura</s>s (gods),
<s>Gandharva</s>s, <s>Bhujaṅgama</s>s (serpents), and <s>Cāraṇa</s>s;
accompanied by their wives, travelling in splendid aerial chariots,
joyful, showering abundant flowers.
Again, of what kind?

children.text: vidyādhara-prabhṛtayo yathā prasiddhāḥ tathā bhujaṅgamaḥ hasta-pādādi-śarīrānvito nāga-loka-sthaḥ sarpaḥ etair dāropahitaiḥ sastrīkaiḥ śobhana-vimāna-gataiḥ ākāśa-niṣṭhaiḥ kṛta-puṣpa-vṛṣṭi-samūhaiḥ ākulite || KrdC_5.54 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vidyādhara</s>s and the rest are as is well known; <s>Bhujaṅgama</s> — a serpent, possessing a body with hands, feet, etc., dwelling in the <s>Nāga-loka</s> (serpent world). By these, accompanied by their wives (<s>dāropahita</s>), travelling in splendid aerial chariots (<s>vimāna</s>), stationed in the sky, with assemblages of flower-showers — [the place is] crowded.
Again, of what kind is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>?
In the ceremony of the <s>rāsa</s>-dance arranged by groups of women
with hands clasped one another's,
stationed at the gem-[studded] stake (<s>maṇi-śaṅku</s>), yet with that very body
having manifested his own divine form in manifold ways.

children.text: amunā vapuṣā anena maṇi-śaṅku-gaatena śarīreṇa nānā-prakāra-kṛta-svīya-divya-śarīram || KrdC_5.55 ||
children.translated_text: With that body — with this body stationed at the gem-stake — having created his own divine body in manifold ways.
Again, of what kind?
Stationed separately between each pair of beautiful-eyed women,
with both arms embraced by the group of beloved ones;
of those whose fire of <s>Anaṅga</s> (Love), blazing forth from his own touch,
has set their bodies aflame and produced rows of shining goosebumps.

children.text: sudṛśām kāminīnām ubhayor dvayoḥ pṛthak dvaya-dvaya-krameṇa antaragaṃ madhya-gatam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? dayitā-gaṇena nārī-samūhena baddhaṃ sva-hastenānyo 'nyaṃ grathitaṃ bhuja-dvitayaṃ yasya tam etenaitad uktaṃ bhavati kāminyor madhye kāminīnām eva hastena gṛhīta-hastaḥ parameśvara iti api samuccayena kevalaṃ śaṅkugaṃ kāminīnām api antareṇa yuktam iti bhāvaḥ | kīdṛśām ? nija-saṅgena gopāla-kṛṣṇa-saṅgena vijṛmbhamāṇaḥ prajvalito yo anaṅga-śikhī kāmāgnis tena jvalitaṃ pradīptaṃ yad āṅgaṃ tatra lasantī śobhamānā yā pulakālī romāñca-paṅktis tayā yujyante iti tad-yujas tāsām || KrdC_5.56 ||
children.translated_text: Between each pair (<s>ubhayoḥ</s>) of beautiful-eyed women (<s>sudṛśām</s>), stationed separately (<s>pṛthak</s>) — in the middle, one by one in pairs. Again, of what kind? Whose two arms (<s>bhuja-dvitaya</s>) are bound — grasped with their own hands, interlinked — by the group of beloved ones (<s>dayitā-gaṇa</s>), the assemblage of women. By this it is stated that the Supreme Lord is one whose hands are held by the hands of the women on either side of him. Moreover, by the word '<s>api</s>' (also) implying inclusion, he is not only stationed at the [central] stake, but is also present between the women — this is the import. Of what kind [are those women]? By his own contact (<s>nija-saṅga</s>) — by the touch of <s>Gopāla Kṛṣṇa</s> — the fire of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the god of Love), blazing forth (<s>vijṛmbhamāṇa</s>), has set their bodies (<s>aṅga</s>) ablaze; therein, the shining (<s>lasat</s>), resplendent rows of goosebumps (<s>pulakāli</s>) — of those [women] who are united with such [horripilation].
Again, of what kind?
With groups of diverse <s>śruti</s>s (musical intervals), the most enchanting
seven-tone scale (<s>svara-saptaka</s>), <s>mūrchanā</s>s (melodic progressions), and <s>tāla</s>-rhythms;
whirling with them [the <s>gopī</s>s], most beautiful with the tinkling
of resplendent, magnificent gem-ornaments.

children.text: amūbhir gopībhiḥ saha bhramamāṇam bhramīkurvāṇaṃ | kaiḥ ? vividho nānā-prakāraḥ śrutir nāma-svarārambhakāvayavaḥ śabda-viśeṣaḥ tena bhinnaṃ saṅgataṃ manojñataram ati-hṛdaya-grāhi yat svara-saptakaṃ niṣādety ādi tasya yā mūrcchanā ekaviṃśati-prakārikā bhāga-tālāśvatāla-paritālādayaḥ ūna-pañcāśat eteṣāṃ gaṇaiḥ samūhaiḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? udāra udūḍho yo maṇis tasya sphuṭaṃ pravyaktaṃ atitejasvitayā yan maṇḍanaṃ tasya śiñjitaṃ śabditaṃ tena cārutaraṃ hṛdayaṅgamam ||57||
children.translated_text: Whirling — revolving — with them (<s>amūbhiḥ</s>), the <s>gopī</s>s. With what? <s>Vividha</s> means of diverse kinds; <s>śruti</s> is the primary constituent of a musical note (<s>nāma-svarārambhaka-avayava</s>), a particular sound-element; <s>bhinna</s> means combined with that; <s>manojñatara</s> means most captivating to the heart; the seven-tone scale (<s>svara-saptaka</s>) — <s>Niṣāda</s> etc. — its <s>mūrchanā</s>s, of twenty-one varieties; <s>bhāga-tāla</s>, <s>aśva-tāla</s>, <s>paritāla</s>, and others — forty-nine [in total]; with groups of these. Again, of what kind? <s>Udāra</s> means excellent; the gems — whose brilliance (<s>sphuṭa</s>) is clearly manifest — their ornaments whose tinkling (<s>śiñjita</s>), their sound, makes him most beautiful (<s>cārutara</s>), captivating to the heart.
Again, of what kind?
Thus, with his body manifested [severally], united with the <s>gopī</s>s adorned with gems,
like an emerald strung with golden [beads];
situated in the center of a gem-made stake, shining
at the center of a vast red lotus.

children.text: iti bhinna-tanum | anena prakāreṇa gopībhir milita-dehaṃ gopāla-kṛṣṇaṃ kam iva tapanīya-mayaiḥ suvarṇa-mayaiḥ maṇibhir militaṃ grathitaṃ marakata-maṇim iva | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? maṇi-nirmito madhya-gato yaḥ śaṅkuḥ tal lagnaṃ lasad dedīpyamānaṃ yad vipulaṃ bṛhad-aruṇa-paṅkajaṃ tasya madhya-gatam || KrdC_5.58 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, with body manifested [severally] — in this manner, with body joined to the <s>gopī</s>s — <s>Gopāla Kṛṣṇa</s> — like what? Like an emerald (<s>marakata-maṇi</s>) strung (<s>milita</s>) with golden (<s>tapanīya-maya</s>) gems. Again, of what kind? The gem-made central stake (<s>maṇi-nirmita-madhyaga-śaṅku</s>) — attached to that, shining (<s>lasat</s>), resplendent — the vast, great red lotus — situated at its center.
Again, of what kind?
With a body resembling the hue of <s>atasī</s> (flax) flowers, youthful,
with eyes like the petals of a fresh, reddish lotus;
with a mass of hair adorned with peacock feathers in beautiful, variegated
clusters of new sprouts.

children.text: atasī-prasiddhā tasyāḥ kusumānīvābhā dīptir yasyās tanos tādṛśī tanur yasya tam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? taruṇeti nūtanāruṇa-padma-patra-sadṛśa-netram | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? naveti nūtana-pallava-nānā-vidha-stavaka-śobhamāna-mayūra-puccha-sambaddha-keśa-samūham || KrdC_5.59 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Atasī</s> is the well-known [flax plant]; the radiance (<s>ābhā</s>) [of him] is like its flowers — one whose body (<s>tanu</s>) has such [complexion]. Again, of what kind? With eyes like the petals of a fresh, reddish lotus. Again, of what kind? With a mass of hair bound with peacock tail-feathers adorning beautiful clusters of various new sprouts.
With playfully arching brows, with a face equal to the moon,
with both cheeks adorned by gem-[studded] ear-rings;
with lips the color of <s>śaśa-rakta</s> (hare's blood, i.e., bright red),
with manifold ornaments gleaming with gems.
Again, of what kind?

children.text: caṭula-bhruvaṃ calad-bhrū-latākam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? śukla-pakṣīya-pūrṇa-candra-sadṛśānanam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? maṇi-maya-kuṇḍala-śobhita-gaṇḍa-dvayam | puanḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? śaśa-śoṇita-tulyādharam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? maṇinā śobhamāna-nānā-prakārābharaṇam || KrdC_5.60 ||
children.translated_text: With playfully arching brows (<s>caṭula-bhru</s>) — with waving brow-creepers. Again, of what kind? With a face like the full moon of the bright fortnight. Again, of what kind? With both cheeks adorned by gem-studded ear-rings (<s>kuṇḍala</s>). Again, of what kind? With lips like hare's blood — red as <s>śaśa-śoṇita</s>. Again, of what kind? With manifold ornaments of various kinds, resplendent with gems.
With garments radiant like the flowers and leaves of the <s>asana</s>-tree,
a place of beautiful, sportive dwelling;
with palms of hands and soles of feet lovely like fresh coral,
with body adorned by garlands swarmed by bees.
Again, of what kind?

children.text: asano vṛkṣa-viśeṣaḥ tasya prasavaḥ puṣpaṃ tasya chedanaṃ patraṃ ca tadvad ujjvalaṃ śobhamānaṃ manoharaṃ vastraṃ yasya tam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? śobhana-krīḍā-vicitra-sthānam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? navo nūtano yo vidrumaḥ pravālas tadvat bhadraṃ manoharaṃ karāṅghri-talaṃ yasya tam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? bhramarair ākulaṃ vyāptaṃ yat puṣpa-dāma-mālā tena virājitaṃ bhuja-dvayaṃ yasya taṃ yad vā mālayā virājitā tanur yasya tam || KrdC_5.61 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Asana</s> is a particular tree; its blossom (<s>prasava</s>) is its flower; its cutting (<s>chedana</s>) is its leaf; with garments (<s>vasana</s>) radiant and beautiful like those — one who has such. Again, of what kind? A place of beautiful, variegated play. Again, of what kind? With palms of hands and soles of feet (<s>karāṅghri-tala</s>) lovely like fresh, new coral (<s>vidruma</s>) — one who has such. Again, of what kind? With body adorned (<s>virājita</s>) by a flower-garland (<s>puṣpa-dāma</s>) crowded with bees — or, one whose body is adorned by such a garland.
With a chest reddened by saffron from the embrace of young women's breasts,
with the gait of a bull;
absorbed in the music produced by the auspicious flute (<s>veṇu</s>),
agitated by love (<s>Smara</s>), the sole <s>guru</s> of the world.
Again, of what kind?

children.text: yuvatīnāṃ stana-dvayāliṅgana-sambaddha-kuṅkumāruṇitam uraḥ-sthalaṃ yasya tam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? ukṣa-gatiṃ vṛṣabha-gatim | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? śivaḥ kalyāṇa-prado yo veṇur vaṃśas tena samīritaṃ sampāditaṃ yad gānaṃ gītaṃ tat-paraṃ tad-āsaktam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? smareṇa kāmena vihvalitam anāyattam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? bhuvana-trayasya ekam advitīyaṃ gurum || KrdC_5.62 ||
children.translated_text: One whose chest (<s>uraḥ-sthala</s>) is reddened by saffron (<s>kuṅkuma</s>) from the embrace — the joining — of the breasts of young women. Again, of what kind? With the gait of a bull (<s>ukṣa-gati</s>) — with a bull's stride. Again, of what kind? <s>Śiva</s> means auspicious; the <s>veṇu</s> is the bamboo flute; by it, the music (<s>gāna</s>), the song, is produced — absorbed in that, devoted to that. Again, of what kind? Agitated (<s>vihvalita</s>) — overcome — by <s>Smara</s> (<s>Kāma</s>, the god of love). Again, of what kind? The sole, unrivalled <s>guru</s> (master) of the three worlds.
On the previously mentioned excellent seat, according to rule,
one should worship this form — the formless, unborn (<s>aja</s>);
first worshipping his limb-retinue (<s>aṅga-vṛtti</s>),
one should then worship the couples (<s>mithuna</s>s) participating in the <s>rāsa</s>.

children.text: iti rūpam ajaṃ prathamodite pīṭha-vare pūrva-kathita-devatā-kLpta-pīṭhe yajet arūpaṃ nirguṇam | āvaraṇāni darśayati-prathamam iti | tad-aṅga-vṛttiṃ pūrvoktāṅgāvaraṇaṃ prathamaṃ paripūjya tatas tad-anantaraṃ mithunāni keśava-kīrtyādīni rāsagāni rāsa-krīḍā-gatāni || KrdC_5.63 ||
children.translated_text: This form — the unborn (<s>aja</s>) — on the previously mentioned excellent seat — the seat prepared for the previously described deity — one should worship as formless (<s>arūpa</s>), without qualities. He shows the surrounding circles (<s>āvaraṇa</s>s) — with 'first' (<s>prathama</s>). Having first worshipped his limb-retinue (<s>aṅga-vṛtti</s>) — the previously described limb-covering (<s>aṅgāvaraṇa</s>) — then, after that, the couples (<s>mithuna</s>s) — <s>Keśava-Kīrti</s> etc. — participating in the <s>rāsa</s> — associated with the <s>rāsa</s>-dance.
On the sixteen petals, the group of <s>svara-mūrti</s>s (vowel-forms),
together with their <s>śakti</s>s (powers), belonging to the supreme <s>rāsa</s>;
<s>Saramā-Madana</s>, together with their own <s>kalā</s>s (aspects),
called couples (<s>mithuna</s>); and then <s>Indra</s>'s thunderbolt and the other principal [weapons].

children.text: dala-ṣoḍaśake ṣoḍaśa-patre pūjayet-mithunam eva kathayati svara-mūrti-gaṇam iti svara-bhavā akārādi-varṇa-bhavāḥ keśavādi-ṣoḍaśa-mūrtayaḥ | svara-mūrti-gaṇaṃ kīdṛśaṃ ? saha-śāktikaṃ kīrtyādi-śakti-sahitam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? uttamo yo rāsaḥ tatra gatam | kvacid uttara-rāsa-gatam iti pāṭhaḥ | tatra madhya-rāse parameśvara-pūjā uttarādi-rāse keśavādikaṃ pūjayet |
children.translated_text: On the sixteen petals — on the sixteen-petalled [lotus] — one should worship. He describes the couples themselves: the group of <s>svara-mūrti</s>s — the sixteen forms such as <s>Keśava</s> etc., born from the vowels, born from the syllables beginning with <s>a-kāra</s>. Of what kind is the <s>svara-mūrti</s> group? Together with their <s>śakti</s>s — accompanied by powers such as <s>Kīrti</s> etc. Again, of what kind? Belonging to the supreme <s>rāsa</s> (<s>uttama-rāsa</s>). In some readings: 'belonging to the northern <s>rāsa</s>' (<s>uttara-rāsa</s>). In that case, worship of the Supreme Lord is in the central <s>rāsa</s>, and <s>Keśava</s> and others should be worshipped in the northern and other <s>rāsa</s>s.

children.text: punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? ramā śrī-bījaṃ madanaḥ kāma-bījaṃ etābhyāṃ sahitam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? svakīyā yāḥ kalāḥ ṣoḍaśa-svarāḥ taiḥ sahitam | prayogaś ca-śrīṃ klīṃ aṃ keśava-kīrtibhyāṃ namaḥ ity ādi | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? mithunāhvam mithuna-saṃjñakam | athānantaram indra-pavi-pramukhān indrādīn vajrādīṃś ca pūjayed ity arthaḥ || KrdC_5.64 ||
children.translated_text: Again, of what description? <s>Ramā</s> is the <s>Śrī-bīja</s> (seed-syllable of Śrī), <s>Madana</s> is the <s>Kāma-bīja</s> (seed-syllable of desire) — accompanied by these two. Again, of what description? Its own <s>kalā</s>s — the sixteen vowels — accompanied by those. And the application is: '<s>śrīṃ klīṃ aṃ</s> homage to <s>Keśava</s> and <s>Kīrti</s>' — and so forth. Again, of what description? Called <s>mithuna</s> (pair) — bearing the designation of a couple. Then — next — one should worship the directional guardians beginning with <s>Indra</s> and their weapons beginning with the thunderbolt — this is the meaning. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.64 ||
He states the <s>naivedya</s> (food-offering) preceded by the previously mentioned count of repetitions —
Thus, having duly worshipped this <s>Hari</s>,
Enclosed by the four <s>āvaraṇa</s>s (surrounding circles), with tender mind,
In a silver-adorned cup, with sugar,
One should offer well-boiled milk to him. // <s>Krd</s> 5.65 //

children.text: anena prakāreṇa caturāvaraṇa-veṣṭitam amuṃ hariṃ samyak yathāvidhi sampūjya śraddhāvān rajatā-racite rūpya-nirmite caṣake pātre asya hareḥ sa-sitaṃ sa-śarkaraṃ sa-ghṛtaṃ ghṛta-sahitaṃ pāṭhāntaram | suśṛtam āvartitaṃ payo dugdhaṃ nivedayatu || KrdC_5.65 ||
children.translated_text: In this manner, having duly worshipped according to rule this <s>Hari</s> enclosed by the four surrounding circles (<s>āvaraṇa</s>s), the faithful one, in a silver-adorned — silver-made — cup, a vessel, should offer to this <s>Hari</s> milk that is <s>sa-sita</s> (with sugar), <s>sa-ghṛta</s> (with ghee) — ghee-accompanied being an alternate reading — <s>suśṛta</s> meaning well-boiled, milk (<s>payas</s>). || <s>KrdC</s> 5.65 ||
When there is wealth, in bronze
Cups, sixteen in number, in sequence,
Having offered milk with sugar to the pairs (<s>mithuna</s>s),
One should complete the rest as before. // <s>Krd</s> 5.66 //

children.text: vibhave sati yadi tādṛśam aiśvaryaṃ bhavati tadā kāṃsya-ghaṭiteṣu pṛthak ekaikaṃ ṣoḍaśasa-caṣakeṣu krameṇa mithuna-gaṇeṣu sa-sitaṃ payo nivedya athānantaraṃ purovat nivedayāmi bhagavate ity ādy-ukta-prakāreṇa sakalaṃ pūjā-viśeṣaṃ samāpayet || KrdC_5.66 ||
children.translated_text: When there is wealth — if such prosperity exists — then in bronze-made, separate, one by one, sixteen cups, in sequence, to the groups of pairs (<s>mithuna</s>s), having offered milk with sugar, then — subsequently — as before, in the manner stated as 'I offer to the Lord' etc., one should complete the entire special worship. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.66 ||
The rite that enchants all worlds — whoever
Regularly performs it night after night, with noble mind,
He indeed becomes worthy of worship by all people,

children.text: śriyam atulāṃ samavāpya yāty anantam // Krd_5.67 //
children.translated_text: And attaining incomparable prosperity, reaches the Infinite. // <s>Krd</s> 5.67 //
He states the fruit of the <s>rāsa-pūjā</s> (circular dance worship) —

children.text: amuṃ vidhiṃ rāsa-pūjā-prakāraṃ sakala-bhuvana-mohnaṃ sakala-bhuvana-vaśyakaraṃ niyatam abādhena yo niśi niśi prati-rajani udāra-cetāḥ prasanna-manāḥ san samyak bhajati kuryāt sa sarva-loka-pūjyaḥ san atulām atiśayitāṃ śriyaṃ samṛddhiṃ samavāpya anantaṃ viṣṇuṃ yāti prāpnoti || KrdC_5.67 ||
children.translated_text: This rite — the method of <s>rāsa-pūjā</s> — that enchants all worlds, that brings all worlds under one's power — whoever performs it regularly, without interruption, night after night, every night, with noble mind — with a pleased disposition — he, becoming worthy of worship by all people, attaining incomparable, surpassing prosperity and abundance, reaches the Infinite — <s>Viṣṇu</s> — that is, he attains [him]. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.67 ||
At night, or at the close of day,
One should worship <s>Acyuta</s> (the Imperishable) daily with devotion;
The fruit of both is equal; therefore
He who desires to cross the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) — // <s>Krd</s> 5.68 //

children.text: yaḥ pumān saṃsāra-sāgaraṃ taritum icchati so 'cyutaṃ bhaktyā niśi vā dinānta-samaye vā sandhyāyāṃ pūjayen nityaśaḥ pratyahaṃ hi yataḥ ubhaya-niśā-sandhyā-pūjana-dvayaṃ sama-phalam tatas tasmād dhetoḥ niśi vā dinānte vā pūjayed ity arthaḥ || KrdC_5.68 ||
children.translated_text: The person who desires to cross the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> should worship <s>Acyuta</s> with devotion at night, or at the close of day — at the <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight) — daily, each day. Since both — the worship at night and at the twilight — yield equal fruit, therefore one should worship either at night or at the close of day — this is the meaning. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.68 ||
He concludes what has been stated —

children.text: ity evaṃ manu-vigrahaṃ madhu-ripuṃ yo vā trikālaṃ yajet
children.translated_text: Thus, whoever worships the enemy of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Madhusūdana</s>), who has the mantra as his body, at the three times of day,
In the abode of the Ocean-born one (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), he who is dear to all classes of living beings —
In his hands are the trees of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>sukha</s> (happiness), <s>artha</s> (wealth), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), sought by the assembly of the virtuous,
Whose rows of fruits exude the flowing nectar of dense bliss. // <s>Krd</s> 5.69 //

children.text: ity amunā prakāreṇa yaḥ pumān mantra-śarīraṃ madhusūdanaṃ tri-kālaṃ vā pūjayet tasya nānā-vidha-prāṇi-samūha-vallabhasya ambhodhijā-veśmano lakṣmī-nivāsasya dharmādi-puruṣārtha-catuṣṭaya-vṛkṣā haste bhavantīti śeṣaḥ | kīdṛśāḥ ? satāṃ vargaḥ samūhaḥ tena prārthitāḥ | saṃsargīti pāṭhe sasargibhir nikaṭasthair yadyapi mokṣasya phalaṃ nāsti tathāpi mokṣa-padena tad-dhetu-bhūtaṃ tattva-jñānam uktaṃ yeṣāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ phala-paṅktayaḥ nityānanda-brahma svarūpa-mahā-rasa-dravadāḥ || KrdC_5.69 ||
children.translated_text: In this manner, the person who worships <s>Madhusūdana</s>, whose body is the mantra, at the three times of day — in the abode of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, the Ocean-born — for him who is dear to the multitudes of various living beings, the four trees of the <s>puruṣārtha</s>s (human goals) beginning with <s>dharma</s> are in his hands — this is to be supplied. Of what kind? Sought by the assembly — the group — of the virtuous. In the reading '<s>sasargī</s>,' by those nearby. Although <s>mokṣa</s> has no [further] fruit, nevertheless by the word '<s>mokṣa</s>' is meant the knowledge of reality (<s>tattva-jñāna</s>) that is its cause. The rows of fruits of those trees exude the flowing essence of the great bliss (<s>mahā-rasa</s>) that is the eternal bliss of <s>Brahman</s>. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.69 ||
Now is stated, at the conclusion of the worship of this Supreme Person,
The method of the previously mentioned <s>tarpaṇa</s>s (libation-offerings);
And the procedure for <s>kāmya</s> (desire-fulfilling) <s>tarpaṇa</s>s as well,

children.text: vināpi pūjāṃ khalu yaiḥ phalaṃ tat // Krd_5.70 //
children.translated_text: By which, even without worship, that very fruit [is obtained]. // <s>Krd</s> 5.70 //

children.text: athānantaraṃ paramasya puṃsaḥ śrī-gopāla-kṛṣṇasya pūjāvasāne pūjānantaraṃ pūrva-samīritānāṃ śīman-mukha-ity-ādi-kathitānāṃ nitya-tarpaṇānāṃ kalpaḥ prakāraḥ kāmyeṣv api tarpaṇeṣu prakāra ucyate yais tarpaṇaiḥ pūjāṃ vināpi tat-phalaṃ pūjā-phalaṃ prāpnoti yathā-pūjā tathaiva tarpaṇam || KrdC_5.70 ||
children.translated_text: Now — next — at the conclusion of the worship of the Supreme Person, <s>Śrī Gopāla Kṛṣṇa</s>, after the worship, the method of the previously mentioned regular <s>tarpaṇa</s>s — those stated beginning with '<s>śīman-mukha</s>' etc. — is declared. The method of desire-fulfilling (<s>kāmya</s>) <s>tarpaṇa</s>s is also stated — by which <s>tarpaṇa</s>s, even without worship, that fruit — the fruit of worship — is obtained; as is the worship, so indeed is the <s>tarpaṇa</s>. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.70 ||

children.text: santarpya pīṭha-mantraiḥ sakṛt prathamam acyutaṃ tatra |
children.translated_text: Having first offered <s>tarpaṇa</s> once with the <s>pīṭha-mantra</s>s (seat-mantras) to <s>Acyuta</s>,

children.text: āvāhya pūjayet taṃ toyair evākhilaiḥ samupahāraiḥ // Krd_5.71 //
children.translated_text: One should invoke and worship him there with water alone, as all the offerings. // <s>Krd</s> 5.71 //

children.text: prathamaṃ pīṭha-mantrair ādhāra-śaktyādi-mantraiḥ pīṭhāṅga-bhūta-devatāṃ sakṛt-sakṛd ekaika-vāraṃ santarpya anantaraṃ tatra toya-maye pīṭhe acyutam āvāhya jalair eva gandhādi-sakalopacārātmakaiḥ pūjayet || KrdC_5.71 ||
children.translated_text: First, with the <s>pīṭha-mantra</s>s — the mantras of <s>Ādhāra-śakti</s> (supporting power) etc. — the deities who form parts of the seat, once each — one time each — having offered <s>tarpaṇa</s>, then, there, on the seat made of water, having invoked <s>Acyuta</s>, one should worship with water alone, which serves as all the offerings including fragrance etc. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.71 ||
Then, having formed the <s>dhenu-mudrā</s> (cow gesture), preparing the <s>tarpaṇa</s> liquid with water,

children.text: tad buddhyāñjalinā taṃ suvarṇa-caṣakī-kṛtena tarpayatu // Krd_5.72 //
children.translated_text: One should offer <s>tarpaṇa</s> to him with a cupped hand visualized as a golden cup. // <s>Krd</s> 5.72 //

children.text: tato dhenu-mudrāṃ baddhvā toyais tarpaṇāḍhyaṃ sampādya tad-dravya-rūpatayā toyaṃ bhāvayitvā tad-buddhyā tat-kathita-dravya-tarpaṇa-dravya-buddhyā taṃ kṛṣṇaṃ tarpayatu kenāñjalinā kīdṛśena suvarṇa-caṣakatayā vicintitenety arthaḥ || KrdC_5.72 ||
children.translated_text: Then, having formed the <s>dhenu-mudrā</s> (cow gesture), having prepared the <s>tarpaṇa</s>-enriched [liquid] with water, having contemplated the water as having the form of that substance — with the understanding of it as the stated <s>tarpaṇa</s> substance — one should offer <s>tarpaṇa</s> to that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. With what? With a cupped hand. Of what kind? Visualized as a golden cup — this is the meaning. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.72 ||
Twenty plus eight — the count prescribed for the <s>tarpaṇa</s>s at the three times;

children.text: bhūyaḥ svakāla-vihitān sakaṛt tarpayec ca parivārān // Krd_5.73 //
children.translated_text: And again, one should offer <s>tarpaṇa</s> once to the retinue [deities] appointed for each respective time. // <s>Krd</s> 5.73 //

children.text: kāla-traya-tarpaṇeṣu trikāla-tarpaṇeṣu ekasmin kāle 'ṣtopetā aṣṭāviṃśatiḥ tarpaṇasya saṅkhyoktā punaḥ sva-kāla-vihitān svasmin prātar madhyāhnādau ye ye vihitāḥ parivārā āvaraṇa-devatās tān sakṛd ekaika-vāraṃ santarpayet || KrdC_5.73 ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>tarpaṇa</s>s at the three times — the three-time <s>tarpaṇa</s>s — at each time, twenty-eight is the prescribed count of <s>tarpaṇa</s>. Again, the retinue deities (<s>āvaraṇa-devatā</s>s) appointed for one's own time — those appointed for the morning, midday, etc. respectively — one should offer <s>tarpaṇa</s> to them once each, one time each. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.73 ||
He states the substances for the <s>tarpaṇa</s> at the three times —
In the morning, curds mixed with jaggery; at midday, <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice) with fresh butter;

children.text: kṣīraṃ tṛtīya-kāle sasitopalam ity udīritaṃ dravyam // Krd_5.74 //
children.translated_text: Milk at the third time, with rock sugar — thus the substances are declared. // <s>Krd</s> 5.74 //

children.text: guḍa-sahitaṃ dadhi prātaḥ-kāle navanīta-sahitaṃ pāyasaṃ madhyāhne sasitopalam śarkarā-vikāra-sahitaṃ kṣīraṃ tṛtīya-kāle ity amunā prakāreṇa dravyaṃ tarpaṇa-dravyaṃ kathitam || KrdC_5.74 ||
children.translated_text: Curds mixed with jaggery in the morning; <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice pudding) mixed with fresh butter at midday; milk with rock sugar — accompanied by a preparation of crystallized sugar — at the third time. Thus, in this manner, the <s>tarpaṇa</s> substance is declared. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.74 ||
He states the <s>tarpaṇa</s> mantra —
The phrase '<s>tarpayāmi</s>' (I offer libation) should be joined after the mantra, with one's own names [of deities],

children.text: dvitīyānteṣu tu tataḥ pūjāśeṣaṃ samāpayet // Krd_5.75 //
children.translated_text: In the accusative case; then one should complete the remainder of the worship. // <s>Krd</s> 5.75 //

children.text: mantrānte mūla-mantrāvasāne svakīyāni tarpaṇīya-devatānāṃ nāmāni teṣu tat-samīpeṣu dvitīyānteṣu amuka-devatām ity ādi-rūpeṣu tarpayāmīti-padaṃ yojyam anantaraṃ pūjāśeṣaṃ samāpayet || KrdC_5.75 ||
children.translated_text: After the mantra — at the end of the <s>mūla-mantra</s> (root mantra) — one's own names, the names of the deities to whom <s>tarpaṇa</s> is being offered, near those, in the accusative case — in the form 'to such-and-such deity' etc. — the phrase '<s>tarpayāmi</s>' should be joined. Thereafter, one should complete the remainder of the worship. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.75 ||
He states the concluding rites —
Having sprinkled oneself with the water of his grace, the knower of the <s>Veda</s>s,

children.text: taj japtvā tam athodvāsya tan-mayaḥ prajapen manum // Krd_5.76 //
children.translated_text: Having recited that [mantra], should drink the water; then, having dismissed him [the deity], absorbed in him, one should recite the mantra. // <s>Krd</s> 5.76 //

children.text: tat-prasādādbhiḥ parameśvara-prasāda-tat-tarpaṇa-jalaiḥ ātmānaṃ śarīraṃ siktvā taj japtvā mantraṃ japtvā apaḥ prapibet | athānantaraṃ taṃ devam udvāsya sva-hṛdaye saṃyojya tan-mayaḥ san-mantraṃ japet || KrdC_5.76 ||
children.translated_text: With the water of his grace — the <s>tarpaṇa</s> water that is the grace of the Supreme Lord — having sprinkled one's own body, having recited that mantra, one should drink the water. Then — next — having dismissed that deity, having united [him] with one's own heart, being absorbed in him (<s>tan-maya</s>), one should recite the mantra. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.76 ||
He states the desire-fulfilling (<s>kāmya</s>) <s>tarpaṇa</s> with its method and substances —

children.text: atha dravyāṇi kāmyeṣu vakṣyante tarpaṇeṣu tu |
children.translated_text: Now the substances for the desire-fulfilling <s>tarpaṇa</s>s shall be stated;
Having adopted any one of the prescribed procedures, one should worship. // <s>Krd</s> 5.77 //

children.text: athānantaraṃ kāmyeṣu tarpaṇeṣu yāni nāradādibhiḥ kathitāni dravyāṇi tāni vakṣyante prokta-vidhānānām trikālokta-vidhānānām anantaram ekaṃ vidhānam āśritya kāmya-tarpaṇa-karma bhajet || KrdC_5.77 ||
children.translated_text: Now — next — the substances for the desire-fulfilling <s>tarpaṇa</s>s, which have been stated by <s>Nārada</s> and others, shall be declared. Having adopted one procedure from among the prescribed three-time methods, one should perform the desire-fulfilling <s>tarpaṇa</s> rite. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.77 ||

children.text: dravyaiḥ ṣoḍaśabhir amuṃ pratarpayed ekaśaś catur-vāram |
children.translated_text: With sixteen substances, one should offer <s>tarpaṇa</s> to him, each one four times;

children.text: sa catuḥ-kṣīrādy-antaiḥ sakṛj-jalādy-antam acyutaṃ bhaktyā // Krd_5.78 //
children.translated_text: With the four milk-[offerings] at the beginning and end, once with water at the beginning and end, to <s>Acyuta</s>, with devotion. // <s>Krd</s> 5.78 //

children.text: ṣoḍaśabhir dravyair amuṃ śrī-kṛṣṇam ekaśaś catur-vāram tad-dravya-buddhyā jalair eva tarpayet | kīdṛśaiḥ ? catvāri kṣīrāṇi ādyaṃ yeṣāṃ taih | ṣoḍaśa-dravyāṇām ādau dugdhāñjali-catuṣṭayam ante ca catuṣṭayam ity arthaḥ | sakṛj-jalādy-antam iti kriyā-viśeṣaṇam | tathā ca prathamam eka-vāraṃ jalena tataś caturvāraṃ tataḥ caturvāraṃ kṣīraiḥ tataḥ sakṛj jalena iti paryavasannam || KrdC_5.78 ||
children.translated_text: With sixteen substances, to this <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, each one four times — with the understanding of those substances, one should offer <s>tarpaṇa</s> with water alone. Of what kind? Four milk-[offerings] are at the beginning — of those; at the beginning of the sixteen substances, four handfuls of milk, and at the end also four — this is the meaning. 'Once with water at the beginning and end' qualifies the action. Thus: first, once with water, then four times [with milk], then four times [with other substances], then with milk, then once with water — this is the conclusion. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.78 ||
He states the sixteen substances — '<s>pāyasa</s>' etc. —
<s>Pāyasa</s> (milk-rice), <s>dādhika</s> (curds-prepared food), <s>kṛsara</s> (rice-and-lentil dish), <s>gauḍānna</s> (jaggery-rice), milk, curds, fresh butter,

Ghee, <s>kadalī</s> (banana), <s>mocā</s> (a banana variety), <s>rajasvalā</s> (a banana variety), <s>coca</s> (a banana variety), <s>modaka</s> (sweetmeat), and <s>apūpa</s> (cake). // <s>Krd</s> 5.79 //

children.text: pṛthukaṃ lājopetaṃ dravyāṇāṃ kathitam iha ṣoḍaśakam |
children.translated_text: Flattened rice, together with parched grain — the sixteen substances are declared here;
After the parched grain and before the final milk-[offering], one should offer heaps of rock sugar. // <s>Krd</s> 5.80 //

children.text: pāyasaṃ paramānnam | dādhikaṃ dadhnā pariṣkṛtam annam | kṛsaraṃ mudgaudanaṃ gauḍānnaṃ guḍodaka-pakvam annam | payo dugdhaṃ dadhi prasiddhaṃ navanītam ājyaṃ ghṛtaṃ kadalī campā-kadalī mocā svarṇa-kadalī rajasvalā kadalī-viśeṣaḥ | coco 'pi kadalī-viśeṣaḥ | modako laḍḍukaḥ | apūpam pūlikā pṛthak cipiṭakaṃ lāja-sametaṃ lāja-sahitam iti dravyāṇāṃ ṣoḍaśakaṃ kathitam iha grantheti lājeti | lāja-tarpaṇānantaram antya-catuḥ-kṣīra-tarpaṇāt pūrvaṃ sitopalā-puñjaiḥ śveta-śarkarā-samūhaiḥ bhāvanayā toya-bhāvāpannaiḥ sakṛt santarpayet || KrdC_5.79-80 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pāyasa</s> is <s>paramānna</s> (supreme food, i.e., milk-rice pudding). <s>Dādhika</s> is food prepared with curds. <s>Kṛsara</s> is rice cooked with <s>mudga</s> (mung beans). <s>Gauḍānna</s> is food cooked with jaggery-water. <s>Payas</s> is milk. <s>Dadhi</s> is well-known curds. <s>Navanīta</s> is fresh butter. <s>Ājya</s> is ghee. <s>Kadalī</s> is the <s>Campā</s> banana. <s>Mocā</s> is the golden banana. <s>Rajasvalā</s> is a special variety of banana. <s>Coca</s> is also a variety of banana. <s>Modaka</s> is a <s>laḍḍuka</s> (round sweetmeat). <s>Apūpa</s> is a <s>pūlikā</s> (stuffed cake). <s>Pṛthuka</s> is flattened rice. Together with <s>lāja</s> (parched grain) — accompanied by parched grain — thus the sixteen substances are declared in this text — '<s>lāja</s>' etc. After the <s>lāja</s>-<s>tarpaṇa</s>, before the final four milk-<s>tarpaṇa</s>s, with heaps of rock sugar — groups of white crystallized sugar — visualized as having become water, one should offer <s>tarpaṇa</s> once. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.79-80 ||
He states the fruit of the aforementioned desire-fulfilling <s>tarpaṇa</s> —
In the morning, seventy-four times — whoever thus
Offers <s>tarpaṇa</s> to this <s>Hari</s> daily,
With undivided mind — all prosperities
Rest in his hand, from within a <s>maṇḍala</s> (cycle of days), as wished. // <s>Krd</s> 5.81 //

children.text: ity anena prakāreṇa prage prātaḥ-kāle catuḥ-saptati-vāram amuṃ hariṃ kṛṣṇaṃ yo naro 'nudinaṃ pratyaham ananya-dhīḥ ekāgra-cittaḥ san santarpayet tasya puṃsaḥ maṇḍalataḥ ekonapañcāśad-divasāt arvāg iti tripāṭhinaḥ aṣṭa-catvāriṃśad-divasābhyantara iti laghu-dīpikā-kāraḥ | pañcatriṃśad-divasābhyantara iti rudradharaḥ | abhivāñchitā ākāṅkṣitāḥ sakala-siddhi-samṛddhayaḥ hasta-sthitā bhavanti atra sitopalā-puñjasya gaṇanā na kāryā || KrdC_5.81 ||
children.translated_text: In this manner, in the morning, seventy-four times — whoever offers <s>tarpaṇa</s> to this <s>Hari</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, daily, each day, with undivided mind — with single-pointed concentration — for that person, within a <s>maṇḍala</s> — within forty-nine days according to the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s; within forty-eight days according to the author of the <s>Laghu-dīpikā</s>; within thirty-five days according to <s>Rudradhara</s> — the desired, longed-for, complete <s>siddhi</s>s (perfections) and prosperities come to rest in the hand. Here the heap of rock sugar is not to be counted [in the seventy-four]. || <s>KrdC</s> 5.81 ||
After the desire-fulfilling <s>tarpaṇa</s>, he states —
Fresh warm milk, cooked milk, curds, fresh butter, ghee, and milk-rice;

children.text: matsyaṇḍī-madhv-amṛtaṃ dvādaśaśaḥ tarpayen navabhir ebhiḥ // Krd_5.82 //
children.translated_text: <s>Matsyaṇḍī</s> (a type of sugar), honey, and <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) — with these nine, one should offer <s>tarpaṇa</s> twelve times each. // <s>Krd</s> 5.82 //

children.text: dhāroṣṇaṃ payaḥ tadānīntanam eva niṣpāditaṃ dugdhaṃ tathā pakvam payaḥ sādhitaṃ dugdhaṃ dhāroṣṇa-pakve ca payasī ca amū dhāroṣṇa-pakva-payasī | dadhi prasiddhaṃ navanītaṃ ghṛtaṃ daugdhānnaṃ pāyasaṃ matsyaṇḍī śarkarā-viśeṣaḥ sa-śarkaraṃ vinaṣṭa-dugdham iti tripāṭhinaḥ | madhu prasiddham amṛtam etair navabhir dravyair dvādaśaśa-vāraṃ tarpayet || KrdC_5.82 ||
children.translated_text: Freshly-drawn milk (<s>dhāroṣṇa</s>) — milk just produced at that very time; likewise, cooked milk (<s>pakva payaḥ</s>) — milk that has been prepared; these are the freshly-drawn and cooked milks. Curds (<s>dadhi</s>) — well known; butter (<s>navanīta</s>); ghee (<s>ghṛta</s>); milk-rice (<s>daugdhānna</s>) — <s>pāyasa</s>; <s>matsyaṇḍī</s> — a special kind of sugar; some read it as sugar-mixed spoiled milk (<s>sa-śarkaraṃ vinaṣṭa-dugdham</s>). Honey (<s>madhu</s>) — well known; nectar (<s>amṛta</s>). With these nine substances, one should perform <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) twelve times each.
He states the fruit of this —
This is another method of <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation), yielding the same fruit as the one previously described, numbering one hundred and eight;

children.text: kārmaṇa-karmaṇi kīrtau jana-saṃvanane viśeṣato vihitaḥ // Krd_5.83 //
children.translated_text: It is especially prescribed for enchantment rituals (<s>kārmaṇa-karman</s>), for fame, and for winning over people.

children.text: ayaṃ tarpaṇa-prakāraḥ pūrvokta-tarpaṇa-prakārād bhinnaḥ | kīdṛśaḥ ? pūrva-kathita-tarpaṇa-phala-sama-phalaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? aṣṭottara-śata-pramāṇakaḥ tato navabhir dravyair dvādaśa-kṛtvā tarpaṇenāṣṭottara-saṅkhyā bhavati | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? kārmaṇa-karmaṇi vaśya-karaṇa-karmaṇi tathā kīrtau sat-kathāyāṃ jana-saṃvanane loka-vaśī-karaṇe loka-priyatvena vā viśeṣeṇa vihitaḥ || KrdC_5.83 ||
children.translated_text: This method of <s>tarpaṇa</s> is different from the previously described method of <s>tarpaṇa</s>. Of what kind? Yielding the same fruit as the fruit of the previously described <s>tarpaṇa</s>. Again, of what kind? Having the measure of one hundred and eight — thus, by performing <s>tarpaṇa</s> twelve times with the nine substances, the count of one hundred and eight is reached. Again, of what kind? Especially prescribed for <s>kārmaṇa-karman</s> — the rite of subjugation — as well as for fame — glorious narration — and for winning over people (<s>jana-saṃvanana</s>) — subjugation of the populace, or becoming dear to all people.
He states what follows after <s>tarpaṇa</s> —
With unbroken [sugar] and freshly-drawn [milk], meditating on <s>Mukunda</s>,
Going to towns and villages, and having gratified [people],
The <s>mantrī</s> (ritualist), together with servants, would obtain savory food,
Garments, grains, and wealth.

children.text: sakhaṇḍa-dhāroṣṇa-dhiyāmukundaṃ vrajan pura-grāmam api pratarpya labheta bhojyaṃ sarasaṃ sa-bhṛtyair vāsāṃsi dhānyāni dhanāni mantrī || KrdC_5.84 ||
children.translated_text: With unbroken [sugar] and freshly-drawn [milk], meditating on <s>Mukunda</s>, going to towns and villages, and having gratified [people], the <s>mantrī</s> (ritualist), together with servants, would obtain savory food, garments, grains, and wealth.
He demonstrates that <s>tarpaṇa</s> is the bestower of all fruits, and describes the post-<s>tarpaṇa</s> duties —

children.text: yāvat santarpayen mantrī tāvat-saṅkhyaṃ japen manum |
children.translated_text: As many times as the <s>mantrī</s> (ritualist) performs <s>tarpaṇa</s>, that many times should he recite the <s>manu</s> (mantra);

children.text: tarpaṇenaiva kāryāṇi sādhayed akhilāny api // Krd_5.85 //
children.translated_text: By <s>tarpaṇa</s> alone, one may accomplish all purposes whatsoever.

children.text: akhilāni samastāni kāryāṇi vāñchitāni tarpaṇenaiva vināpi pūjā-homaṃ sādhayet | atra yāvat-saṅkhyaṃ tarpaṇaṃ karoti tāvat-saṅkhyaṃ mantraṃ japet || KrdC_5.85 ||
children.translated_text: All — every — desired purpose may be accomplished by <s>tarpaṇa</s> alone, even without worship and <s>homa</s>. Here, as many times as one performs <s>tarpaṇa</s>, that many times one should recite the mantra.
He states another practical application —
A twice-born (<s>dvija</s>) whose livelihood is begging, who here daily, becoming

children.text: svayaṃ bhūtvā bhikṣām aṭati viharan gopa-sudṛśām |
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda-tanaya</s> (the son of <s>Nanda</s>, i.e., <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) himself, wanders begging, playing with the beautiful cowherd women (<s>gopa-sudṛś</s>);
Together with their hearts, through his own most enchanting playful acts,
He obtains abundant alms rich in curds, milk, and ghee.

children.text: bhikṣā-vṛttir jīvanopāyo yasya sa dvijo traivarṇiko dinaśaḥ pratidinaṃ svayaṃ nanda-tanayo bhūtvā tad-rūpeṇātmānaṃ vicintya iha bhikṣām aṭati yācate | kiṃ kurvan ? svakīyair lalita-lalitaiḥ atimanoharaiḥ narma-vidhibhiḥ krīḍā-karmabhir gopa-sudṛśāṃ gopa-strīṇāṃ cetobhiḥ sārdhaṃ viharan amā-śabdaḥ sahārthe sa-dadhi-dugdha-ghṛta-pracurāṃ bahu-bhikṣāṃ prāpnoti || KrdC_5.86 ||
children.translated_text: A <s>dvija</s> (twice-born) — one of the three <s>varṇa</s>s — whose livelihood is begging; daily, having become <s>Nanda-tanaya</s> (the son of <s>Nanda</s>) himself — visualizing himself in that form — wanders begging here. What doing? With his own most enchanting — extremely captivating — playful acts — sportive deeds — playing together with the hearts of the beautiful cowherd women (<s>gopa-strī</s>s); the word <s>amā</s> means 'together with' — he obtains abundant alms rich in curds, milk, and ghee.

children.text: madhye koṇeṣu ṣaṭsv apy anala-puṭasyālikhet karṇikāyāṃ

children.translated_text: <s>Kandarpa</s> (the love-god's seed-syllable), joined with the name of the person to be accomplished, and the six syllables placed in the interstices, twice on the filaments;
Preceded by <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Śrī</s> [seed-syllables], the syllables of the eighteen-letter mantra, in the middle of the petals,

children.text: madhye varṇān daśānāṃ daśa-lipi-manu-varyasya caikekaśo 'bjam // Krd_5.87 //
children.translated_text: The letters of the ten-letter supreme mantra, one by one in each of the ten [petals] — [thus draw] the lotus.
In the center, in the six angles of the fire-triangle, one should draw on the <s>karṇikā</s> (pericarp)

children.text: daśa-dala-padmaṃ vilikhya karṇikāyāṃ ṣaṭ-koṇaṃ vahni-gṛhaṃ vilikhya vahni-gṛha-yugmasya madhye ṣaṭ-koṇeṣu vilikhet | lekhana-prakāram āha-karṇikāyāṃ madhye sādhya-nāma-sahitam amukasyāmukaṃ sidhyatv ity anena sahitaṃ kandarpaṃ kāma-bījaṃ vilikhet | tathā vivara-gataṃ ṣaḍ-arṇaṃ ṣaṭ-koṇa-gata-vakṣyamāṇa-ṣaḍ-akṣaraṃ vilikhet tathā keśareṣu daśa-dala-mūleṣu dviśaḥ dvau dvau kṛtvā dvi-nava-lipi-manor aṣṭādaśākṣara-mantrasya śakti-śrī-pūrvakāni bhuvaneśvarī-bīja-śrī-bījādyāny akṣarāṇi vilikhet | tathā daśānāṃ pātrāṇāṃ madhye daśa-lipi-manu-varyasya daśākṣara-mantra-śreṣṭhasya varṇān ekaikaśo vilikhet tato 'bjaṃ padmam || KrdC_5.87 ||
children.translated_text: Having drawn a ten-petalled lotus, having drawn a hexagram (<s>ṣaṭ-koṇa</s>) — a fire-house (<s>vahni-gṛha</s>) — on the pericarp (<s>karṇikā</s>), one should draw in the center of the pair of fire-houses, in the six angles. He states the method of drawing: in the center of the pericarp, one should draw the <s>Kandarpa</s> (love-god's seed-syllable, <s>kāma-bīja</s>) together with the name of the person to be accomplished — i.e., accompanied by 'may such-and-such be accomplished for so-and-so.' Likewise, one should draw the six syllables — the six letters to be described — placed in the angles of the hexagram. Likewise, on the filaments — at the bases of the ten petals — in pairs of two, the syllables of the eighteen-syllable mantra, preceded by the <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Śrī</s> [seed-syllables] — preceded by the <s>Bhuvaneśvarī</s> seed-syllable, the <s>Śrī</s> seed-syllable, etc. — one should write them. Likewise, in the middle of the ten petals, the letters of the ten-letter supreme mantra — the best of ten-syllable mantras — one by one, one should write. Then the lotus.
Enclosed by the earth-house (<s>bhū-sadma</s>, a square), with the love-god's [syllable] without garland at the corners,
Written with yellow orpiment (<s>gorocanā</s>) using a golden needle;
On a gold-fashioned plate, rolled up —
This <s>Gopāla-yantra</s> (talisman of <s>Gopāla</s>) is said to bestow all desires.

children.text: bhū-bimbena catur-asreṇa veṣṭitaṃ kuryāt | kīdṛśena ? bhū-sadmanā asraga-manmathena koṇa-gata-kāma-bījena etad akhilārthadaṃ gopāla-yantram uktaṃ kīdṛśam ? suvarṇa-śalākayā gorocanādinā suvarṇa-racite paṭṭe likhitam | anantaraṃ vartulīkṛtam || KrdC_5.88 ||
children.translated_text: One should make it enclosed by the earth-figure (<s>bhū-bimba</s>) — a square. Of what kind? With the earth-house (<s>bhū-sadma</s>) having the love-god's seed-syllable at the corners, without garland (<s>asraga</s>). This <s>Gopāla-yantra</s> bestows all desires. Of what kind? Written with a golden stylus using yellow orpiment (<s>gorocanā</s>) and the like, on a gold-fashioned plate. Thereafter, rolled into a cylindrical form.
Sprinkled with the remnant oblation-ghee and consecrated with mantras, this [<s>yantra</s>]
Should be worn by the great ones — it is uniquely capable of subjugating the three worlds;
By those desiring protection, fame, sons, land, wealth, grains, prosperity,
And good fortune — it is of priceless power, to be worn constantly.

children.text: idaṃ mantraṃ sampāta-siktam āhūti-dāna-śeṣa-puraḥ-sthita-ghṛta-siktaṃ tathā mantreṇābhimantritam rakṣā-bhaya-nivāraṇaṃ yaśaḥ sat-kathā-prakāśaḥ sutaḥ putraḥ mahī pṛthivī dhanaṃ suvarṇādi lakṣmīḥ sarva-sampattiḥ saubhāgyaṃ sarva-jana-priyatvam etat prāptum icchadbhir mahadbhiḥ śauca-yuktaiḥ satataṃ dhāraṇīyam | ayam arthaḥ-yathoktaṃ yantraṃ sampādya prāṇa-pratiṣṭhāṃ kṛtvā pañcāmṛtādibhiḥ abhiṣicya aṣṭottara-śataṃ sahasraṃ vā sampāta-ghṛta-siktaṃ kṛtvā yathokta-saṅkhyaṃ japtvā dhārayed iti kīdṛśaṃ ? jagat-traya-vaśīkaraṇaika-kuśalam | punaḥ anarghya-vīryaṃ mahā-prabhāvam || KrdC_5.89 ||
children.translated_text: This <s>yantra</s>, sprinkled with the remnant-ghee (<s>sampāta-sikta</s>) — sprinkled with the ghee remaining after the oblation offerings — and likewise consecrated with the mantra. Protection — removal of fear; fame — the spread of good reputation; sons — progeny; land — territory; wealth — gold and the like; prosperity (<s>lakṣmī</s>) — all riches; good fortune (<s>saubhāgya</s>) — being dear to all people — by those desiring to obtain these, the great ones — those endowed with purity — should wear it constantly. The meaning is: having prepared the <s>yantra</s> as described, having performed <s>prāṇa-pratiṣṭhā</s> (establishment of life-breath), having bathed it with the five nectars (<s>pañcāmṛta</s>) and the like, having sprinkled it with the remnant-oblation ghee, having recited the mantra the prescribed number of times — one hundred and eight or one thousand — one should wear it. Of what kind? Uniquely skilled in subjugating the three worlds. Again, of priceless power — of great potency.
He shows the use of the <s>yantra</s> in other applications besides wearing —
For those afflicted by ghosts, madness, epilepsy, poison, fainting, delirium, and fever,

children.text: dhyāyan śirasi prajapen mantram imaṃ jhaṭiti śamayituṃ vikṛtim // Krd_5.90 //
children.translated_text: Meditating [the <s>yantra</s>] upon their head, one should recite this mantra to swiftly pacify the affliction.

children.text: bhūtaḥ śamśāna-deśa-vartī adṛśya-rūpo 'niṣṭa-kārī unmādaś citta-vibhramaḥ apasmṛtir apasmāraṇa-yogaḥ viṣaṃ mūrchākāri-sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca mūrcchā aceṣṭā vibhramaḥ prasādaḥ jvaro roga-viśeṣaḥ etair ārtānāṃ pīḍitānāṃ śirasi mastakopari idaṃ yantra-rūpaṃ dhyāyan imaṃ gopāla-mantraṃ japet kiṃ kartum ? vikṛtiṃ jhaṭiti śīghraṃ śamayituṃ nāśayitum || KrdC_5.90 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūta</s> — an invisible malevolent being dwelling in cremation grounds; <s>unmāda</s> — mental derangement; <s>apasmṛti</s> — epileptic condition; <s>viṣa</s> — poison causing fainting, both plant-derived and animal-derived; <s>mūrcchā</s> — unconsciousness; <s>vibhrama</s> — confusion; <s>jvara</s> — a particular disease (fever). For those afflicted — tormented — by these, upon the head — on top of the crown — visualizing this <s>yantra</s>-form, one should recite this <s>Gopāla</s>-mantra. For what purpose? To swiftly — quickly — pacify — destroy — the affliction.
He extracts the six-syllable mantra for the <s>yantra</s> —
<s>Smara</s> (love-god), <s>Trivikrama</s>, joined; <s>Cakrī</s> (the disc-bearer); <s>Kṛṣṇāya</s>; <s>hṛd</s> (heart, i.e., <s>namaḥ</s>) — this is it;
This six-syllable [mantra] is declared to be the bestower of all <s>siddhi</s>s (accomplishments).

children.text: smaraḥ kāma-bījaṃ trivikramaḥ ṛ-kāraḥ tena krāntaḥ sambaddhaḥ cakrī ka-kāraḥ tathā kṛ iti ṣṇāyeti svarūpaṃ hṛn namaḥ ity anena prakāreṇāsau ṣaḍ-akṣaro 'yaṃ mantraḥ samproktaḥ sarva-siddhi-karaḥ akhila-kāmadaḥ || KrdC_5.91 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Smara</s> is the <s>kāma-bīja</s> (love-seed syllable); <s>Trivikrama</s> is the letter <s>ṛ</s>; joined (<s>krānta</s>) — connected — with that; <s>Cakrī</s> is the letter <s>ka</s>; likewise <s>kṛ</s>; <s>ṣṇāya</s> is itself; <s>hṛt</s> is <s>namaḥ</s> — in this manner, this six-syllable mantra is declared as the bestower of all <s>siddhi</s>s — the fulfiller of all desires.
He extracts the <s>Śakti-bīja</s> (power seed-syllable) —
<s>Kroḍa</s> (the letter <s>ha</s>), blazing with fire; <s>Māyāvī</s> (the long <s>ī</s>-vowel), with the head marked by a drop (<s>lava</s>, i.e., <s>bindu</s>);

children.text: saiṣā śaktiḥ parā sūkṣmā nityā saṃvit-svarūpiṇī // Krd_5.92 //
children.translated_text: This is the supreme <s>Śakti</s> (power) — subtle, eternal, of the nature of consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>).

children.text: kroḍo ha-kāraḥ | kīdṛśaḥ ? agninā repheṇa dīptaḥ | punaḥ māyāvī dīrgha-ī-kāraḥ tad-yuktaḥ | punaḥ lavena bindunā lāñchitaṃ mastakaṃ yasya saḥ | tathā sānusvāra ity arthaḥ | eṣā śaktiḥ parā utkṛṣṭā sūkṣmā mṛṇāla-tantu-sadṛśī nityā janma-nāśa-rahitā saṃvit-svarūpiṇī sva-prakāśa-svarūpiṇī || KrdC_5.92 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kroḍa</s> is the letter <s>ha</s>. Of what kind? Blazing (<s>dīpta</s>) with fire — the letter <s>ra</s> (repha). Again, <s>Māyāvī</s> is the long <s>ī</s>-vowel; joined with that. Again, one whose head is marked by <s>lava</s> — <s>bindu</s> (the nasal dot) — meaning with <s>anusvāra</s>. This <s>Śakti</s> is supreme (<s>parā</s>) — most excellent; subtle (<s>sūkṣmā</s>) — like the fiber of a lotus stalk; eternal (<s>nityā</s>) — free from birth and destruction; of the nature of consciousness (<s>saṃvit-svarūpiṇī</s>) — of the nature of self-luminous awareness.
He extracts the <s>Śrī-bīja</s> (prosperity seed-syllable) —

With the elements bone (<s>asthi</s>, i.e., <s>śa</s>), fire (<s>agni</s>, i.e., <s>ra</s>), <s>Govinda</s> (i.e., long <s>ī</s>), and drop (<s>lava</s>, i.e., <s>bindu</s>), the <s>Lakṣmī-bīja</s> (seed-syllable of <s>Lakṣmī</s>) is proclaimed;

children.text: ābhyām aṣṭādaśa-lipiḥ syād viṃśaty akṣaro manuḥ // Krd_5.93 //
children.translated_text: With these two [seed-syllables], the eighteen-letter [mantra] becomes a twenty-syllable mantra.

children.text: asthi śa-kāraḥ agniḥ rephaḥ govindo dīrgha-ī-kāraḥ lavo binduḥ etaiḥ saṃyuktaiḥ śrī-bījaṃ samīritaṃ kathitam | ābhyām śakti-śrī-bījābhyāṃ sahitaḥ pūrvoktāṣṭādaśākṣara-mantraḥ viṃśaty akṣaro bhavati || KrdC_5.93 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Asthi</s> (bone) is the letter <s>śa</s>; <s>agni</s> (fire) is <s>ra</s> (repha); <s>Govinda</s> is the long <s>ī</s>-vowel; <s>lava</s> (drop) is <s>bindu</s>. Combined with these, the <s>Śrī-bīja</s> is proclaimed — declared. With these two — the <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Śrī</s> seed-syllables — the previously mentioned eighteen-syllable mantra becomes twenty syllables.
He shows the prescribed places of worship for the Supreme Lord —

children.text: śālagrāme maṇau yantre maṇḍale pratimāsu ca |
children.translated_text: In a <s>Śālagrāma</s> (sacred stone), in a gem, in a <s>yantra</s> (diagram), in a <s>maṇḍala</s> (ritual circle), and in images;

children.text: nityaṃ pūjā hareḥ kāryā na tu kevala-bhūtale // Krd_5.94 //
children.translated_text: The daily worship of <s>Hari</s> should be performed — not on the bare ground alone.

children.text: śālagrāme prasiddhe maṇau gomeda-padmarāgādau yantre 'sminn eva gopāla-yantre maṇḍale sarvato-bhadrādau soma-sūryāgni-maṇḍale veti rudradharaḥ | pratimāsu suvarṇādi-gopāla-pratimāyām | atra harer nityaṃ sarvadā pūjā kāryā na tu kevalāyāṃ bhūmau || KrdC_5.94 ||
children.translated_text: In a <s>Śālagrāma</s> — well known; in a gem — such as cat's-eye (<s>gomeda</s>) or ruby (<s>padmarāga</s>); in a <s>yantra</s> — specifically in this <s>Gopāla-yantra</s>; in a <s>maṇḍala</s> — such as the <s>Sarvatobhadra</s> or the circles of <s>Soma</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, and <s>Agni</s> — thus [says] <s>Rudradhara</s>. In images — in golden or other images of <s>Gopāla</s>. Here, the daily worship of <s>Hari</s> should always be performed — not on the bare ground alone.
He shows the fruit of the methods described —
Thus, whoever here worships <s>Mukunda</s> through recitation, fire-offering, worship, <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation), and other [practices],

children.text: ya iha bhajati mavor ekam āśritya nityam |
children.translated_text: Daily, having taken refuge in one of the two [mantras] of <s>Mādhava</s>,

children.text: sa tu suciram ayatnāt prāpya bhogān viśeṣān
children.translated_text: He indeed, effortlessly, having long enjoyed special pleasures,
Again goes to the supremely pure abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Thus ends the fifth chapter (<s>paṭala</s>) of the <s>Krama-dīpikā</s> composed by <s>Śrī Keśava Bhaṭṭācārya</s>.

children.text: iti kathita-prakārair japa-homa-pūjā-tarpaṇaiḥ ādi-padād abhiṣekādinā yo mukundaṃ nityaṃ sevate | kiṃ kṛtvā ? manvor daśāṣṭādaśākṣarayor ekaṃ gṛhītvā iha loke ayatnāt suciraṃ sarva-kālaṃ sarvān bhogān prāpya punar ante prasiddhaṃ nirmalaṃ tejaḥ prāpnoti tad-dhāmābhavatīty arthaḥ || KrdC_5.95 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the described manner — through recitation, <s>homa</s>, worship, <s>tarpaṇa</s>, and the like — the word '<s>ādi</s>' includes consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) etc. — whoever serves <s>Mukunda</s> daily. Having done what? Having adopted one — among the two mantras of ten and eighteen syllables — here, in this world, effortlessly, for a very long time — at all times — having obtained all enjoyments, and again, at the end, he attains the well-known, pure radiance — the meaning is that he becomes [one with] that abode.
