Thus ends the fifth chapter (<s>paṭala</s>) of the commentary (<s>vivaraṇa</s>) on the <s>Krama-dīpikā</s> composed by <s>Śrī Vidyāvinoda Govinda Bhaṭṭācārya</s>.
||5||

(6)
Sixth Chapter (<s>Ṣaṣṭha Paṭala</s>)
Now, for the mantras that have been thus perfected, he describes the applications and other [matters] —

children.text: viniyogān atho vakṣye mantrayor ubhayoḥ samān |
children.translated_text: I shall now describe the applications (<s>viniyoga</s>s) common to both mantras,
And certain mantras that accomplish their purposes, of infinite power.

children.text: atho 'nantaraṃ mantrayor daśāṣṭādaśākṣarayoḥ samān dhyāna-viśeṣeṇa viniyogān tathā tad-artha-kāriṇo 'nanta-vīryān bahu-phala-dātṝn kāṃścin mantrān vakṣye || KrdC_6.1 ||
children.translated_text: Next — subsequently — for the two mantras, the ten-syllable and eighteen-syllable, I shall describe the common applications — distinguished by specific meditations; likewise, I shall describe certain mantras that accomplish those purposes, of infinite power — bestowers of abundant fruits.
He states the meditation for the ten- and eighteen-syllable [mantras] for the purpose of application —
I salute that son of <s>Devakī</s>, just born, radiant as the sky,
Wearing yellow garments, with conch, discus, mace, and lotus shining in his hands.

children.text: ukta-rūpaṃ prasiddhaṃ devakī-putraṃ sadyo-jātaṃ bālakaṃ dyu-saprabham ākāśa-samāna-kāntiṃ śyāmaṃ pīta-vastraṃ kare lasanti śobhamānāni śaṅkha-cakra-gadā-padmāni yasya taṃ vande namaskaromi || KrdC_6.2 ||
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Devakī</s> of the described form — well known — just born — an infant; radiant as the sky — having a luster equal to the sky — dark-complexioned; wearing yellow garments; in whose hands shine — gleam — the conch, discus, mace, and lotus — him I salute — I bow to.

children.text: evaṃ dhyātvā japel lakṣaṃ mantraṃ brāhme muhūrtake |
children.translated_text: Having thus meditated, one should recite one <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand) of the mantra at the <s>brāhma-muhūrta</s> (pre-dawn hour);

children.text: svādu-plutaiś ca kusumaiḥ palāśair ayutaṃ hunet // Krd_6.3 //
children.translated_text: And with sweet-soaked flowers of <s>palāśa</s> (Butea monosperma), one should offer ten thousand oblations.

children.text: evam amunā prakāreṇa brāhme muhūrtake udayāt prāk daṇḍa-dvaye daṇḍa-catuṣṭaya iti kaścit mantram ubhayor eka-lakṣaṃ japet | anantaraṃ palāśa-puṣpaiḥ svādu-plutair ghṛta-madhu-śarkarā-sahitair daśa-sahasraṃ juhuyāt || KrdC_6.3 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in this manner, at the <s>Brāhma muhūrta</s> (auspicious pre-dawn hour) — two <s>daṇḍa</s>s (time-units) or four <s>daṇḍa</s>s before sunrise, according to some — one should recite one <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand) of either of the two mantras. Thereafter, with <s>palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa) flowers soaked in sweet [water], combined with ghee, honey, and sugar, one should offer ten thousand [oblations].
He states the fruit —
Whoever performs [this] thus with either of the two mantras, fully concentrated,

children.text: smṛtiṃ medhāṃ mati-balaṃ labdhvā sa kavirāḍ bhavet |
children.translated_text: Having obtained memory, intelligence, and mental strength, he becomes a king among poets;
The other mantra yields the same fruit of recitation, meditation, and <s>homa</s> (fire-offering).

children.text: manvor daśāṣṭā-daśākarayor anyatareṇa ekena susamāhitaḥ susaṃyataḥ san ya evaṃ kuryāt sa smṛtiṃ smaraṇaṃ medhāṃ dhāraṇāvatīṃ buddhiṃ matiṃ samyak jñānaṃ balaṃ mahā-prāṇatvam etat sarvaṃ prāpya kavirāṭ kavi-śreṣṭho bhavati syād iti aparo 'gre vakṣyamāṇa-mantraḥ kathita-mantra-dvaya-samāna-japa-dhyāna-homa-phalo bhavati || KrdC_6.4 ||
children.translated_text: With either one of the two mantras — the ten-syllable and the eighteen-syllable — being fully concentrated — well-restrained — whoever performs [this] thus, he obtains memory — the power of recollection — intelligence (<s>medhā</s>) — a retentive faculty of understanding — right knowledge (<s>mati</s>) — and strength — great vitality — having obtained all these, he becomes a king among poets — the foremost of poets. The other — the mantra to be stated next — yields the same fruit of recitation, meditation, and <s>homa</s> as the two mantras already described.
He states the mantra —
'<s>Śrīman-Mukunda</s>-<s>caraṇau</s> <s>sadā</s>' — thus; then '<s>śaraṇam</s>';

children.text: ahaṃ prapadya ity ukto maukundo 'ṣṭādaśākṣaraḥ // Krd_6.5 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Ahaṃ prapadye</s>' — thus is declared the eighteen-syllable <s>Maukunda</s> (pertaining to <s>Mukunda</s>) [mantra].

children.text: śrīman-mukunda-caraṇau sadeti svarūpaṃ tatas tad-anantaraṃ śaraṇam iti svarūpam ahaṃ prapadya iti svarūpam ity anena prakāreṇa maukundo mukunda-sambandhī aṣṭādśākṣaro mantraḥ kathitaḥ || KrdC_6.5 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Śrīman-Mukunda-caraṇau sadā</s>' — this is the form; then, next, '<s>śaraṇam</s>' — this is the form; '<s>ahaṃ prapadye</s>' — this is the form. In this manner, the <s>Maukunda</s> — pertaining to <s>Mukunda</s> — eighteen-syllable mantra is declared.

children.text: mantroddhāraḥ: śrī-mukunda-caraṇau sadā śaraṇam ahaṃ prapadye |
children.translated_text: Mantra extraction: '<s>Śrī-Mukunda-caraṇau sadā śaraṇam ahaṃ prapadye</s>' (I eternally take refuge at the feet of the glorious <s>Mukunda</s>).
He states the <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer) and the rest —
Its [seer is] <s>Nārada</s>, [the meter is] <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and <s>Mukunda</s> [is the deity] — preceded by the <s>ṛṣi</s>;

children.text: prātaḥ prātaḥ pibet toyaṃ japtaṃ yo 'ṣtottaraṃ śatam |
children.translated_text: Whoever drinks water in the morning, over which [this mantra] has been recited one hundred and eight times,

children.text: anena ṣaḍbhir māsaiḥ sa bhavec chrutadharo naraḥ // Krd_6.6 //
children.translated_text: By this [practice], within six months, that person becomes one who retains all that is heard.

children.text: asya mantrasya nārado munir gāyatrī-chando mukundo devatā ṛṣi-pūrvakāḥ ṛṣy-ādyāḥ ṛṣi-cchando devatā ity arthaḥ | te ca nāradādayaḥ | prayogam āha-prātaḥ pratyaham aṣṭottaraṃ śataṃ japtaṃ mantra-japtaṃ jalaṃ pibet | sa naro anena vidhānena ṣaḍbhir māsaiḥ śruta-dharo bhavet || KrdC_6.6 ||
children.translated_text: Of this mantra, <s>Nārada</s> is the sage; <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the meter; <s>Mukunda</s> is the deity — 'preceded by the <s>ṛṣi</s>' means the <s>ṛṣi</s> and the rest — namely the seer, meter, and deity — and these are <s>Nārada</s> and the others. He states the application: in the morning, daily, one should drink water over which one hundred and eight [recitations] have been recited — water charged with the mantra. That person, by this method, within six months, becomes one who retains all that is heard (<s>śruta-dhara</s>).
He states another application —
Having withdrawn the divine limbs, as before, [meditating on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] seated on his mother's lap,

children.text: calad-doś caraṇaṃ bālaṃ nīlābhaṃ saṃsmaran japet // Krd_6.7 //
children.translated_text: With moving arms and feet, a child, dark blue — contemplating [him] thus, one should recite.

children.text: upasaṃhṛta-divyāṅgaṃ tyakta-caturbāhu-rūpaṃ dhṛta-bāhu-dvayaṃ purovat yathā-vasudeva-sadmani bhītena divyāṅgam upasaṃhṛtaṃ mātur aṅkagaṃ devakī-kroḍe sthitaṃ calad-doś-caraṇaṃ cañcala-hasta-pādaṃ bālaṃ śiśuṃ nīlābhaṃ kaṃ saṃsmaret || KrdC_6.7 ||
children.translated_text: Having withdrawn the divine limbs — having abandoned the four-armed form and assumed the two-armed form — as before — as in <s>Vasudeva</s>'s house, when out of fear the divine form was withdrawn — seated on his mother's lap — situated in <s>Devakī</s>'s embrace — with moving arms and feet — with restless hands and feet — a child — an infant — dark blue. One should contemplate [him thus].

children.text: ayutaṃ tāvad evājyair juhuyāc ca hutāśane |
children.translated_text: One should recite ten thousand [times], and with the same amount of ghee should offer [oblations] into the fire;

children.text: sa labhed acalāṃ bhaktiṃ śraddhāṃ śāntiṃ ca śāśvatīm // Krd_6.8 //
children.translated_text: He shall obtain unwavering devotion (<s>bhakti</s>), faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), and eternal peace (<s>śānti</s>).

children.text: ayutaṃ japet tāvad evāgnāv ājyair ghṛtair juhuyāt yaḥ sa sthirāṃ parameśvara-viṣayiṇīm ārādhyatva-buddhiṃ śuddhāṃ śāstra-bodhite 'rghe 'vaśyambhāvi-niścayātmikā śāntiṃ mokṣa-rūpāṃ śāśvatīṃ nityāṃ prāpnoti daśāṣṭādaśākṣarayor viśeṣa-dhyānam idaṃ prayogārtham iti bhairava-tripāṭhinaḥ || KrdC_6.8 ||
children.translated_text: One should recite ten thousand [times]; with the same amount, in the fire, with ghee, one should offer [oblations]. He who does so obtains firm devotion directed toward the Supreme Lord — the conviction of [the Lord's] worthiness of worship — pure faith — the certain conviction regarding the value taught in scripture — and eternal, everlasting peace in the form of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>). This is the special meditation for the ten-syllable and eighteen-syllable [mantras] for the purpose of application — thus [say] the <s>Bhairava-tripāṭhin</s>s.
He states another mantra —
With this [mantra], at the end of the complete [root-mantra], the word '<s>marun-namita</s>';

children.text: bāla-līlātmane huṃ phaṭ nama ity amunāthavā // Krd_6.9 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Bāla-līlātmane huṃ phaṭ namaḥ</s>' — or with this [one].

children.text: athavāmunā vakṣyamāṇa-mantreṇaitat-prayoga-jātaṃ sādhayet | mantram āha-samasteti | svarūpam asyānte marun-namita iti svarūpam | etasmāc chabdāt bāla-līlātmane huṃ phaḍ iti svarūpaṃ nama iti svarūpam | ayam apy aṣṭādaśākṣaraḥ daśāṣṭādaśākṣara-samānaḥ || KrdC_6.9 ||
children.translated_text: Or, with this — the mantra to be described — one should accomplish the previously stated applications. He states the mantra with '<s>samasta</s>' etc.: the form — at the end of this [root-mantra], '<s>marun-namita</s>' is the form; from this word, '<s>bāla-līlātmane huṃ phaṭ</s>' is the form; '<s>namaḥ</s>' is the form. This too is an eighteen-syllable [mantra], equal to the ten- and eighteen-syllable [mantras].

children.text: mantroddhāraḥ: samasta-manrun-namitaḥ bāla-līlātmane huṃ phaṭ svāhā |
children.translated_text: Mantra extraction: '<s>Samasta-marun-namitaḥ bāla-līlātmane huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>' (Homage to him who is bowed to by all the winds, whose nature is child's play, <s>huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>).
He states the <s>ṛṣi</s> and the rest —
<s>Nalakūvara</s>, <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and <s>Bāla-Kṛṣṇa</s> are declared

children.text: ṛsyādyāḥ siddhayaḥ sarvāḥ syur japādyair ihāmunā // Krd_6.10 //
children.translated_text: As the <s>ṛṣi</s> and the rest; all <s>siddhi</s>s (perfections) arise here from recitation and the like with this [mantra].

children.text: asya mantrasya ṛṣy-ādyāḥ ṛṣiḥ chando devatā nalakūvara-prabhṛtayaḥ | tatra nalakūvaro munir gāyatrī chandaḥ bāla-kṛṣṇo devatā iti | iha bhuvane japādyaiḥ sarvāḥ siddhayo bhavanti || KrdC_6.10 ||
children.translated_text: Of this mantra, the <s>ṛṣi</s> and the rest — the seer, meter, and deity — are <s>Nalakūvara</s> and the others. Therein, <s>Nalakūvara</s> is the sage; <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the meter; <s>Bāla-Kṛṣṇa</s> (child <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) is the deity. In this world, from recitation and the like, all <s>siddhi</s>s (perfections) arise.
Suspended in a child's cradle, crying, being watched
By the cowherd-women — one should satisfy [him] with [the thought of] milk; he shall obtain food.

children.text: bāla-śayane āndolikāyāṃ lambitaṃ sthitaṃ rudantaṃ krandamānaṃ vallavī-janair gopībhiḥ prekṣyamāṇaṃ dṛśyamānaṃ preryamāṇam iti pāṭhe cālyamānam ity arthaḥ | dugdha-buddhyā jalena tarpayet | aśanaṃ bhakṣya-vastu aśnute prāpnoti || KrdC_6.11 ||
children.translated_text: Suspended — situated — in a child's cradle — in a swing — crying — wailing — being watched — being observed — by the cowherd-women (<s>vallavī</s>s, <s>gopī</s>s); in the reading '<s>preryamāṇam</s>,' the meaning is 'being rocked.' With the thought of milk — [imagining the water to be] milk — one should satisfy [him by offering]. <s>Aśana</s> — food — he obtains.
He states another mantra —
With this [mantra], or at the end of '<s>anna-rūpa</s>' (food-form), one should utter the word '<s>rasa-rūpa</s>' (essence-form);
'<s>Tuṣṭa-rūpa</s> (satisfied-form), <s>namaḥ</s>' — the pair; '<s>annādhipataye mama</s>';

children.text: annaṃ prayaccha svāheti triṃśad-arṇo 'nnado manuḥ // Krd_6.12 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Annaṃ prayaccha svāhā</s>' — the thirty-syllable food-granting (<s>annada</s>) mantra.

children.text: amunā mantreṇa pūrvoktaṃ kuryāt | mantram āha-anna-rūpa iti śabdānte rasa-rūpa iti svarūpaṃ tuṣṭa-rūpeti svarūpaṃ namo dvandvam iti namo nama svarūpam ānnādhipataye mamānnaṃ prayaccha svāheti triṃśad-akṣaro annada-mantraḥ daśāṣṭāḍaśākṣara-samānaḥ || KrdC_6.12 ||
children.translated_text: With this mantra one should perform the previously stated [rites]. He states the mantra: '<s>anna-rūpa</s>' — at the end of this word, '<s>rasa-rūpa</s>' is the form; '<s>tuṣṭa-rūpa</s>' is the form; '<s>namo dvandvam</s>' means '<s>namo namaḥ</s>' is the form; '<s>annādhipataye mama annaṃ prayaccha svāhā</s>' — the thirty-syllable food-granting mantra, equal to the ten- and eighteen-syllable [mantras].

children.text: mantroddhāraḥ: anna-rūpa rasa-rūpa tuṣṭa-rūpa namo namaḥ annādhipataye manānnaṃ prayaccha svāhā |
children.translated_text: Mantra extraction: '<s>Anna-rūpa rasa-rūpa tuṣṭa-rūpa namo namaḥ annādhipataye mama annaṃ prayaccha svāhā</s>' (O form of food, form of essence, form of satisfaction — homage, homage! O lord of food, grant me food, <s>svāhā</s>!).
He states the <s>ṛṣi</s> and the rest —
<s>Nārada</s>, <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, and <s>Annādhipati</s> (Lord of Food) — these are its <s>ṛṣi</s> and the rest.
For afflictions caused by ghosts, child-seizing demons (<s>bāla-graha</s>), madness, loss of memory, and other calamities,
One should recite while contemplating [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] drinking from <s>Pūtanā</s>'s breast, on the head of the afflicted one.

children.text: asya mantrasya nārado muniḥ, anuṣṭup-chandaḥ, annādhipatir devatā | prayogam āha-bhūteti | bhūta-piśācādir bāla-graho roga-viśeṣaḥ | unmādaś citta-bhramaḥ smṛti-bhraṃśaḥ sammohaḥ | etair upadravair upatāpair grasta-mūrdhni upatapta-mastake pūtanā-stana-pāyinaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ smaran mantraṃ japet || KrdC_6.13 ||
children.translated_text: Of this mantra, <s>Nārada</s> is the sage; <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> is the meter; <s>Annādhipati</s> (Lord of Food) is the deity. He states the application with '<s>bhūta</s>' etc.: <s>bhūta</s> means ghosts, <s>piśāca</s>s, etc.; <s>bāla-graha</s> is a specific disease [seizing children]; <s>unmāda</s> is mental derangement; <s>smṛti-bhraṃśa</s> is bewilderment. For these afflictions — these torments — on the head of the afflicted one, while contemplating <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> drinking from <s>Pūtanā</s>'s breast, one should recite the mantra.
One should visualize that <s>Pūtanā</s>, crying — wailing —
Her entire body shattered by the sucking out [of her life-breath] along with her <s>āsu</s> (life-force), crying;

children.text: āviśya sarve muktvā taṃ vidravanti drutaṃ grahāḥ // Krd_6.14 //
children.translated_text: Having entered [her form], all the afflicting spirits, abandoning that [person], flee swiftly.

children.text: punaḥ kīdṛśīm ? sāsu-cūṣanaṃ saha prāṇena yat cūṣaṇaṃ samākarṣaṇaṃ tena nirbhinnam anāyataṃ sarvāṅgaṃ yasyāḥ sā | tathā tāṃ kiṃ bhūtvā japet ? āviśya aham eva harir iti bhāvayitvā | anantaraṃ taṃ grastaṃ sarve grahā upadravā muktvā parityajya drutaṃ śīghraṃ vidravanti palāyante | atra daśāṣṭādaśākṣarayor viśeṣa-dhyānam idaṃ prayogārtham iti tripāṭhinaḥ || KrdC_6.14 ||
children.translated_text: Again, of what description? Her whose entire body is shattered — destroyed — by the sucking (<s>cūṣaṇa</s>) — the drawing out — together with her life-breath (<s>āsu</s>). And in what state should one recite? Having entered — having visualized 'I myself am <s>Hari</s>.' Thereafter, all the afflicting spirits — the calamities — abandoning — leaving — that afflicted [person], swiftly — quickly — flee — run away. Here, this is the special meditation for the ten- and eighteen-syllable [mantras] for the purpose of application — thus [say] the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s.
He states another application —
One should offer into the fire with <s>khara-mañjarī</s> (<s>apāmārga</s>, rough chaff-flower) sprigs,
Bathed well with <s>pañca-gavya</s> (five cow-products) waters, into the face of the slayer of <s>Pūtanā</s>.

children.text: khara-mañjaryā apāmārgasya mañjarībhir agra-bhāgaiḥ pañca-gavya-jalaiḥ siktair vibhāvasau vahnau pūjanā-hantuḥ kṛṣṇasyānana-rūpe juhuyāt || KrdC_6.15 ||
children.translated_text: With <s>khara-mañjarī</s> — the sprigs — the top portions — of <s>apāmārga</s> (Achyranthes aspera), sprinkled with <s>pañca-gavya</s> (five cow-products) water, one should offer into the fire — into the fire representing the face of the slayer of <s>Pūtanā</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
One should feed [the afflicted one] with the remaining <s>gavya</s> (cow-products) and sprinkle with that <s>kalaśa</s> (vessel) [water];
This is to be accomplished with one thousand recitations, for the pacification of all afflictions.

children.text: homāvaśiṣṭaṃ pañca-gavya-sādhyaṃ prāśayet sahasra-japtena pūrvokta-vidhinā sādhitena kalaśena vābhiṣecayet sarvopadra-nivṛtty-artham || KrdC_6.16 ||
children.translated_text: The remaining <s>pañca-gavya</s> from the <s>homa</s> — one should feed [the afflicted person]; or sprinkle with the <s>kalaśa</s> (vessel) consecrated with one thousand recitations by the previously stated method — for the purpose of removing all afflictions.
He states another mantra —

children.text: amunaitad dvādaśārṇaṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhāntakena vā |
children.translated_text: With this [mantra], or with the twelve-syllable [<s>Vāsudeva</s> mantra] ending with '<s>huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>';
Its <s>ṛṣi</s> and the rest are <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and <s>Graha-ghna</s> (affliction-destroying) <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: etat-pūrvokta-prayoga-dvayaṃ vakṣyamāṇa-mantreṇa vā kuryāt | mantram āha-dvādaśeti-pūrvokta-vāsudeva-dvādaśākṣarānte huṃ phaṭ svāheti ṣoḍaśākṣaro mantraḥ daśāṣṭādaśākṣara-samānaḥ | ṛṣy-ādikam āha-ṛṣyādyā iti | ṛṣi-prabhṛtayo brahmādayaḥ | tatra brahmā ṛṣiḥ | gāyatrī cchandaḥ | grahaghna-rūpo harir devatā || KrdC_6.17 ||
children.translated_text: The two previously stated applications may be performed with this mantra to be described. He states the mantra with '<s>dvādaśa</s>' etc.: at the end of the previously stated twelve-syllable <s>Vāsudeva</s> [mantra], '<s>huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>' — [this makes] a sixteen-syllable mantra, equal to the ten- and eighteen-syllable [mantras]. He states the <s>ṛṣi</s> and the rest with '<s>ṛṣyādyā</s>': the <s>ṛṣi</s> and others are <s>Brahmā</s> and the rest. Therein, <s>Brahmā</s> is the seer; <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the meter; <s>Hari</s> in the form of the destroyer of afflictions (<s>graha-ghna</s>) is the deity.

children.text: mantroddhāraḥ: oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya huṃ phaṭ svāhā |
children.translated_text: Mantra extraction: '<s>Oṃ namo bhagavate Vāsudevāya huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.'
Contemplating [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] who has overturned the cart-[demon] with his own lotus-feet, one should recite
Ten thousand [times] of either of the two mantras, for the pacification of all obstacles.

children.text: nija-caraṇa-kamala-nikṣipta-śakaṭaṃ hariṃ cintayet | mantrayoḥ pūrva-mantrāpara-mantrayor ekam ayutaṃ japet | kim-artham ? sakala-vighnopaśamanārthaṃ daśāṣṭādaśākṣarayor eva sarva-vighna-śānty-arthaṃ viśeṣa-dhyānam iti tripāṭhinaḥ || KrdC_6.18 ||
children.translated_text: One should contemplate <s>Hari</s> who cast down the cart-[demon <s>Śakaṭāsura</s>] with his own lotus-feet. Of the two mantras — the former and the latter — one should recite ten thousand of either one. For what purpose? For the pacification of all obstacles. This is the special meditation for the ten- and eighteen-syllable [mantras] for the purpose of pacifying all obstacles — thus [say] the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s.
The limbs of these mantras [are formed] with [the syllables] beginning with '<s>ā-cakra</s>'; worship

children.text: aṅgair indrādi-vajrādyair uditā sampade sadā // Krd_6.19 //
children.translated_text: With the limbs [consisting of] <s>Indra</s> and others and the thunderbolt and other [weapons] — is always declared for [attaining] prosperity.

children.text: amīṣāṃ kathita-mantrāṇām ācakrādibhir daśākṣara-kathitair aṅgāni kāryāṇi arcanā pūjās tu aṅgais tathendrādyais tad-āyudhaiś ceti sampatty-arthaṃ sadā kathitā || KrdC_6.19 ||
children.translated_text: The limbs of these described mantras should be formed with [the syllables] beginning with '<s>ā-cakra</s>' as stated for the ten-syllable [mantra]. The worship, however, with the limbs — with <s>Indra</s> and others and their weapons — is always declared for the purpose of attaining prosperity.
He shows the <s>mṛtyuñjaya</s> (death-conquering) procedure —

children.text: bālo nīla-tanur dorbhyāṃ dadhy-utthaṃ pāyasaṃ dadhat |
children.translated_text: A child, with dark-blue body, holding in his two arms curd-born [butter] and <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-pudding),
May <s>Hari</s> protect you — adorned with tiger-claw [pendants] and strings of little bells (<s>kiṅkiṇī</s>s).

children.text: daśāṣṭādaśākṣarayor vārogyārthaṃ viśeṣa-dhyānam āha-bāla ity ādineti tripāṭhinaḥ | harir vo yuṣmān rakṣatu | kīdṛśo bālaḥ ? pañca-varṣīyaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? nīla-tanuḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? hastābhyāṃ dadhy-utthaṃ navanītaṃ pāyasaṃ paramānnaṃ ca dhārayet | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? vyāghra-nakha-kṣudra-ghaṇṭikā-samūhābhyām alaṅkṛtaḥ || KrdC_6.20 ||
children.translated_text: He states the special meditation for the ten- and eighteen-syllable [mantras] for the purpose of health — with '<s>bāla</s>' etc. — thus [say] the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s. May <s>Hari</s> protect you all. Of what description? A child — five years old. Again, of what description? With a dark-blue body. Again, of what description? Holding in his two hands butter born from curds (<s>navanīta</s>) and <s>pāyasa</s> — the finest milk-pudding. Again, of what description? Adorned with tiger-claw [pendants] and clusters of small bells.
Having meditated thus, one should offer into the fire with triplets of <s>śatavīrya</s> (<s>dūrvā</s>, sacred grass) sprouts,

children.text: payaḥ-sarpiḥ-plutair lakṣam ekaṃ tāvaj japen manum // Krd_6.21 //
children.translated_text: Soaked in milk and ghee, one <s>lakṣa</s> [oblations]; and recite the mantra the same [number of times].

children.text: evambhūtaṃ hariṃ dhyātvā vahnau śatavīryāṅkurair durvāṅkurais tribhiḥ | kīdṛśaiḥ ? payo dugdhaṃ sarpi-ghṛtaṃ tābhyāṃ plutaiḥ siktaiḥ ekaṃ lakṣaṃ juhuyāt lakṣam ekaṃ japet || KrdC_6.21 ||
children.translated_text: Having meditated on <s>Hari</s> of such description, [one should offer] into the fire with <s>śatavīrya</s> sprouts — <s>dūrvā</s> (sacred grass) sprouts — in triplets. Of what kind? Soaked — sprinkled — with milk and ghee. One should offer one <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand) [oblations]; and one should recite one <s>lakṣa</s>.
Having given <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (honorarium) to the <s>guru</s>, one should feed the foremost <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s;

children.text: sa hy abdānāṃ śataṃ jīven na rogo nātra saṃśayaḥ // Krd_6.22 //
children.translated_text: He shall indeed live a hundred years — no disease — of this there is no doubt.

children.text: anantaraṃ gurave dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā brāhmaṇān bhojayec ca sa varṣāṇāṃ śataṃ roga-rahitaḥ san jīvet-atra saṃśayo nāsti || KrdC_6.22 ||
children.translated_text: Thereafter, having given <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (honorarium) to the <s>guru</s>, one should feed the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s; and he shall live a hundred years, free from disease — of this there is no doubt.
He states another mantra —
Here, another mantra: at the end of the twelve-syllable [mantra], '<s>Puruṣottama</s>,

children.text: āyur me dehi sambhāṣya viṣṇave prabhaviṣṇave // Krd_6.23 //
children.translated_text: Grant me life' — addressing <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the all-powerful.
Ending with '<s>namaḥ</s>' — a thirty-two-syllable [mantra]; its seer is <s>Nārada</s>;

children.text: chando 'nuṣṭup-devatā ca śrī-kṛṣṇo 'ṅgāny ato bruve // Krd_6.24 //
children.translated_text: The meter is <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, and the deity is <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> — I shall now state the limbs.

children.text: etādṛśe kārye 'paro mantro 'sti | mantram āha-dvādaśākṣara-vāsudeva-mantrānte puruṣottama iti svarūpam āyur me dehīti svarūpaṃ viṣṇave prabhaviṣṇave iti svarūpam | nama ity anto dvy-adhika-triṃśad-arṇo dvātriṃśad-akṣaro mantraḥ kathitas tu | punar asya mantrasya nārada ṛṣir anuṣṭup-chando devatā śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ iti ato 'nantaram aṅgāni bruve vadāmi || KrdC_6.23-24 ||
children.translated_text: For such a purpose, there is another mantra. He states the mantra: at the end of the twelve-syllable <s>Vāsudeva</s> mantra, '<s>puruṣottama</s>' — this is the form; '<s>āyur me dehi</s>' (grant me long life) — this is the form; '<s>viṣṇave prabhaviṣṇave</s>' — this is the form. Ending with '<s>namaḥ</s>' — a mantra of thirty-two syllables has been described. Furthermore, for this mantra, <s>Nārada</s> is the <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer), <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> is the <s>chandas</s> (metre), <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> is the <s>devatā</s> (deity). After this, I shall state — declare — the limbs (<s>aṅga</s>s). || KrdC_6.23-24 ||

children.text: mantroddhāraḥ: oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya puruṣottam āyur me dehi viṣṇave prabhaviṣṇave namaḥ |
children.translated_text: Extraction of the mantra: <s>Oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya puruṣottama āyur me dehi viṣṇave prabhaviṣṇave namaḥ</s>.
With syllables numbering as the sun (12), elements (5), senses (5), <s>Vasu</s>s (8), and eyes (2), ending in <s>ātmane</s>;
With the words <s>Mahānanda</s>, <s>pada</s>, <s>jyotis</s>, <s>Māyā</s>, and <s>Vidyā</s>, in sequence. // Krd_6.25 //

children.text: dvādaśa-pañca-pañcāṣṭa-dvi-saṅkhyātair mantrākṣarair ātmanepadāntair mahānandādi-padaiḥ saha krameṇa pañcāṅgāni | sahānandety api kvacit pāṭhaḥ || KrdC_6.25 ||
children.translated_text: With mantra-syllables numbering twelve, five, five, eight, and two, ending in <s>ātmane-pada</s>, together with the words <s>Mahānanda</s> and the rest — the five limbs (<s>pañcāṅga</s>) are [assigned] in sequence. '<s>Sahānanda</s>' is also a variant reading in some [manuscripts]. || KrdC_6.25 ||
He states the <s>puraścaraṇa</s> (preparatory rites) and other [details] for this [mantra] —

children.text: japtvā lakṣam imaṃ mantram ayutaṃ pāyasair hunet |
children.translated_text: Having recited this mantra one <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand) times, one should offer ten thousand oblations with <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice);

children.text: pūrvavad dūrvayā juhvad āyur dīrghataraṃ labhet // Krd_6.26 //
children.translated_text: As before, offering oblations with <s>dūrvā</s> grass, one obtains exceedingly long life. // Krd_6.26 //

children.text: imaṃ mantraṃ lakṣaṃ japtvā pāyasair ayutaṃ hunet juhuyāt | evaṃ mantraṃ saṃsādhya pūrvavad dūrvayāṅkurakaiḥ dugdha-ghṛta-militair lakṣam ekaṃ juhuyāt | japaiś ca dīrghataram atiśayam āyuḥ prāpnoti || KrdC_6.26 ||
children.translated_text: Having recited this mantra one <s>lakṣa</s> times, one should offer — perform <s>homa</s> — ten thousand [oblations] with <s>pāyasa</s>. Thus, having perfected the mantra, as before, with <s>dūrvā</s> sprouts mixed with milk and ghee, one should offer one <s>lakṣa</s> [oblations]. And through recitation, one obtains exceedingly — abundantly — long life. || KrdC_6.26 ||

children.text: dārayantaṃ bakaṃ dorbhyāṃ kṛṣṇaṃ saṃgṛhya tuṇḍayoḥ |
children.translated_text: Meditating on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> tearing apart <s>Baka</s> with both arms, grasping [him] by the beaks;
When children are in danger, having touched [them], one should practice one [of the mantras],

children.text: taj-japta-tilajābhyaṅgād bhaveyuḥ sukhinaś ca te // Krd_6.27 //
children.translated_text: And from anointing with sesame oil recited with that [mantra], they shall become happy. // Krd_6.27 //

children.text: śiśūnāṃ bālānām ātaṅke bhaye samupasthite tān bālān spṛṣṭvā kṛṣṇaṃ smaran anyataram ukteṣv ekaṃ mantram abhyasej japyāt | kīdṛśaṃ kṛṣṇam ? karābhyāṃ tuṇḍayoḥ saṃgṛhya baka-nāmānam asuraṃ vidārayantam | tan-mantra-japta-tailābhyaṅgāt te bālāḥ sukhino bhavanti | smarann iti śuśu-nāmānaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ smaran, ke śirasi spṛṣṭvā japyād iti boddhavya-mantra-daśāṣṭādaśākṣarayor viśeṣa-dhyānam iti tripāṭhinaḥ || KrdC_6.27 ||
children.translated_text: When danger — fear — has befallen children — infants — having touched those children, recollecting <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, one should practice — recite — one among the stated [mantras]. What kind of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>? One who, grasping by the beaks with both hands, is tearing apart the <s>asura</s> named <s>Baka</s>. From anointing with oil recited with that mantra, those children become happy. 'Recollecting' means recollecting <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> named <s>Śiśu</s> (child); having touched [them] on the head, one should recite — this is how the specific meditations for the ten- and eighteen-syllable [mantras] should be understood — [say] the <s>tripāṭhin</s>s. || KrdC_6.27 ||
For this very purpose of child-protection, there is also another mantra — he says —
Here too is another mantra: '<s>bāla-vapuṣe</s>' (to the child-formed one), '<s>vahni-vallabhā</s>' (<s>svāhā</s>);

children.text: gorakṣāyāṃ kvaṇad-veṇuṃ cārayantaṃ paśūṃs tathā // Krd_6.28 //
children.translated_text: For the protection of cows, [one should meditate on him] playing the sounding flute and herding cattle. // Krd_6.28 //

children.text: bāla-vapuṣe iti svarūpaṃ vahni-vallabheti svāhā asminn arthe gorakṣāyāṃ ca viśeṣa-dhyānam āha-kvaṇad iti | veṇu-vādana-paraṃ paśūṃś cārayantaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ smaran japyāt || KrdC_6.28 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Bāla-vapuṣe</s>' — this is the form; '<s>vahni-vallabhā</s>' is <s>svāhā</s>. For this purpose and for cow-protection, he states the specific meditation: '<s>kvaṇat</s>' (sounding) — meditating on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> absorbed in playing the flute and herding cattle, one should recite. || KrdC_6.28 ||

children.text: asminn eva bāla-rakṣārthe go-rakṣāyāṃ ca mantrāntaram āha-
children.translated_text: For this very purpose of child-protection and cow-protection, he states another mantra —
Having uttered the word '<s>gopālaka</s>' (cowherd), and again '<s>veśadharāya</s>' (to the one bearing that guise);
'<s>Vāsudevāya</s>'; the armor, weapon, and head [syllables] — [making it] eighteen syllables. // Krd_6.29 //

children.text: gopālaka ity uktvā punar veśadharāya ity uktvā vāsudevāyeti vadet varma hum astraṃ phaḍ iti śiraḥ svāhā etāni vadet | evaṃ sati aṣṭādaśākṣaro bhavati || KrdC_6.29 ||
children.translated_text: Having uttered '<s>gopālaka</s>' and again '<s>veśadharāya</s>' and then saying '<s>vāsudevāya</s>'; the armor is '<s>huṃ</s>,' the weapon is '<s>phaṭ</s>,' and the head is '<s>svāhā</s>' — one should utter these. Thus, it becomes eighteen syllables. || KrdC_6.29 ||

children.text: mantroddhāraḥ: gopālaka-veśa-dharāya vāsudevāya huṃ phaṭ svāhā |
children.translated_text: Extraction of the mantra: <s>gopālaka-veśa-dharāya vāsudevāya huṃ phaṭ svāhā</s>.
Of the mantra, <s>Nārada</s> is the seer, <s>Gāyatrī</s> the metre, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> the deity; with this, or
With the one having the discus etc. as limbs, the wise one should perform the protection of cows (<s>gopāla-saṃrakṣā</s>). // Krd_6.30 //

children.text: asya pūrvoktasya ca manor nārado munir gāyatrī-cchandaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇo devatā anena vā mantreṇa ukta-dravyādinā vā gopāla-rakṣāṃ kuryāt | kīdṛśena ? ācakrādy-aṅga-yuktena || KrdC_6.30 ||
children.translated_text: Of this previously stated mantra: <s>Nārada</s> is the sage, <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the metre, <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> is the deity. With this mantra, or with the previously stated substances, one should perform the protection of cows. Of what kind? With [the mantra] accompanied by the limbs of disc etc. || KrdC_6.30 ||
He states the application for removing poison —
When afflicted by cobra-poison and the like, meditating on <s>Hari</s> upon the head of the bitten one,
Dancing upon the stage of <s>Kāliya</s>'s hoods, one should practice one [of the mantras]. // Krd_6.31 //

children.text: dṛśā pīyūṣa-varṣiṇyā siñcantaṃ tat tanuṃ budhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Sprinkling that body with a gaze showering nectar, the wise one,

children.text: tarjayan vāma-tarjanyā taṃ drāṅ mocayate viṣāt // Krd_6.32 //
children.translated_text: Threatening with the left index finger, quickly frees him from poison. // Krd_6.32 //

children.text: kumbhī-nasādi-kṣveḍārtau sarpa-viṣa-pīḍāyām | kumbhīnasās tu te sarpā ye syur dṛṣṭi-viṣolbaṇāḥ iti dharaṇiḥ | ādi-padād vṛścikādi-saṅgraho daṣṭa-mūrdhni ārta-mastake spṛṣṭvā kāliyo nāga-viśeṣas tasya phaṇā saivaa raṅga-bhūmis tatra nṛtyantaṃ smaran anyatama-mantram abhyaset japet | kīdṛśaṃ ? hariṃ tat tanuṃ śarīram amṛta-varṣiṇyā dṛṣṭyā siñcantam | kiṃ kurvan ? smaret vāma-tarjanyātarjayan | evaṃ sati taṃ daṣṭaṃ mantrī drāk śīghraṃ viṣān mocayet | atra daśāṣṭādaśākṣarayor viśeṣa-dhyānam iti tripāṭhinaḥ || KrdC_6.31-32 ||
children.translated_text: When afflicted by cobra-poison and the like — by the pain of serpent-venom; '<s>kumbhīnasa</s>s are those serpents whose poison is fearsome through their gaze' — thus <s>Dharaṇi</s>. By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), scorpions and the like are included. Upon the head of the bitten one — having touched the crown of the afflicted one — <s>Kāliya</s> is a particular <s>nāga</s> (serpent-king); his hoods are themselves the stage — upon which [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is] dancing — meditating thus, one should practice — recite — one of the mantras. Of what description? <s>Hari</s> sprinkling that body — the body [of the afflicted] — with a gaze showering nectar. Doing what? One should meditate [on him] threatening with the left index finger. Thus, the <s>mantrī</s> quickly frees the bitten one from poison. Here, the specific meditations for the ten- and eighteen-syllable [mantras] are [to be understood] — [say] the <s>tripāṭhin</s>s. || KrdC_6.31-32 ||
He states another application —
Having filled a <s>kalaśa</s> (vessel) with water, meditating on the subduer of <s>Kāliya</s>,

children.text: japtvāṣṭa-śatam āsiñced viṣiṇaṃ sa sukhī bhavet // Krd_6.33 //
children.translated_text: Having recited one hundred and eight times, one should sprinkle the poisoned one — he shall become well. // Krd_6.33 //

children.text: kalaśaṃ toyair āpūryānantaraṃ kāliya-mardanaṃ devaṃ smṛtvāṣṭādhikaṃ śataṃ japtvā tena kalaśena viṣa-yuktam āsiñcet | anantaraṃ viṣāt sukhī bhavati || KrdC_6.33 ||
children.translated_text: Having filled a <s>kalaśa</s> with water, then meditating on the deity who subdues <s>Kāliya</s>, having recited one hundred and eight times, one should sprinkle the poison-afflicted one with that <s>kalaśa</s>-[water]. Thereafter, he becomes free from poison — happy. || KrdC_6.33 ||
He states the <s>Kāliya-mardana</s> (subduer of <s>Kāliya</s>) mantra —
In the middle of '<s>kāvya</s>' (the syllables <s>kā</s>), at the end of '<s>liya</s>,' the syllables '<s>phaṇā-madhye</s>' (in the midst of the hoods);

children.text: uktvā punar vaden nṛtyaṃ karoti tam anantaram // Krd_6.34 //
children.translated_text: Having uttered [these], one should again say '<s>nṛtyaṃ karoti tam</s>' (he dances upon him); then — // Krd_6.34 //
Having said '<s>namāmi Devakī-putra</s>' (I salute the son of <s>Devakī</s>), after the word '<s>nṛtya</s>' (dance),

children.text: rājānam acyutaṃ brūyād iti danta-lipir manuḥ // Krd_6.35 //
children.translated_text: One should say '<s>rājānam Acyutam</s>' (the king, <s>Acyuta</s>) — thus this '<s>danta-lipi</s>' (thirty-two-lettered) mantra. // Krd_6.35 //

children.text: kāvya ity akṣara-dvayor madhye liyasyeti svarūpam etasyānte phaṇā-madhyādi iti svarūpam ity antān vaded anantaraṃ nṛtyaṃ karoti tam iti | anantaraṃ namāmi devakī-putram iti vadet | anantaraṃ nṛtya-śabdataḥ nṛtya-śabdānte rājanam acyutam iti brūyād ity anena prakāreṇa danta-lipir dvātriṃśad-akṣaro mantraḥ kathitaḥ || KrdC_6.34-35 ||
children.translated_text: Between the two syllables of '<s>kāvya</s>' — '<s>liyasya</s>' is the form — at the end of this, '<s>phaṇā-madhyādi</s>' is the form — one should utter [syllables] ending thus; then '<s>nṛtyaṃ karoti tam</s>.' Then one should say '<s>namāmi Devakī-putram</s>.' Then, after the word '<s>nṛtya</s>' — at the end of the word '<s>nṛtya</s>' — '<s>rājānam Acyutam</s>' — one should say thus. By this method, a thirty-two-syllabled '<s>danta-lipi</s>' mantra has been described. || KrdC_6.34-35 ||
Extraction of the mantra:
'<s>Kāliya-vyaphaṇā-madhye</s>' — thus — '<s>nṛtyaṃ karoti taṃ</s>';
'<s>Devakī-putraṃ namāmi nṛtya rājānam ucyatam</s>.'
He shows the limbs (<s>aṅga</s>s) and other [details] of this mantra —
Its limbs are assigned by its individual feet (<s>pāda</s>s) and collectively; <s>Nārada</s> is the sage;

children.text: chando 'nuṣṭub devatā ca kṛṣṇaḥ kāliya-mardanaḥ // Krd_6.36 //
children.translated_text: <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> is the metre, and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the subduer of <s>Kāliya</s>, is the deity. // Krd_6.36 //

children.text: asya mantrasya vyastair ekaikam aṅghribhiś caturbhiḥ pādaiḥ samastair mantrātmakaiś cāṅgāni pañcāṅgāni kathitāni muniḥ nāradaḥ chando 'nuṣṭup kālīya-mardanaḥ kṛṣṇo devatā || KrdC_6.36 ||
children.translated_text: Of this mantra, with the individual — one by one — four feet (<s>pāda</s>s) and with the collective — consisting of the complete mantra — the five limbs (<s>pañcāṅga</s>) are declared. The sage is <s>Nārada</s>; the metre is <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>; <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the subduer of <s>Kāliya</s>, is the deity. || KrdC_6.36 ||
He states the <s>puraścaraṇa</s> (preparatory rites) —

children.text: japyo lakṣaṃ manur ayaṃ hotavyaṃ sarpiṣāyutam |
children.translated_text: This mantra should be recited one <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand) times; ten thousand [oblations] should be offered with ghee;
Its worship is proclaimed with the limb-deities, directional guardians, and thunderbolt etc. [as encirclements]. // Krd_6.37 //

children.text: ayaṃ mantraḥ lakṣaṃ japyaḥ sarpiṣā ghṛtena punar ayutaṃ hotavyam | aṅga-dik-pāla-vajrādyais tribhir āvaraṇair arcanā pūjā kathitā ||
children.translated_text: This mantra should be recited one <s>lakṣa</s> times; with ghee, ten thousand [oblations] should be offered. The worship is declared with three encirclements: the limb-[deities], the directional guardians, and the thunderbolt etc.
He states the application —

children.text: kriyā sarvā ca kartavyā visaghnī pūrvam īritā |
children.translated_text: All the poison-destroying procedures previously stated should be done [with this mantra];

children.text: sadṛśo 'nena jagati nahi kṣveḍa-haro manuḥ // Krd_6.38 //
children.translated_text: Indeed, there is no mantra equal to this in the world for removing venom. // Krd_6.38 //

children.text: pūrva-mantra-kathitā viṣaghnī sarvā kriyā amunaiva mantreṇa kartavyā hi yataḥ jagati saṃsāre anena mantreṇa sadṛśaḥ samānaḥ kṣveḍa-haraḥ viṣaharo nāsti || KrdC_6.38 ||
children.translated_text: All the poison-destroying procedures described for the previous mantra should be performed with this very mantra, because in the world — in existence — there is no mantra equal — comparable — to this one for removing poison. || KrdC_6.38 ||
He states another poison-destroying application —
With the parts of a <s>śuka</s>-tree (parrot-tree), ground into pills with cow-urine;
Through anointment, collyrium, and application, [the pill] becomes poison-destroying when consecrated with this [mantra]. // Krd_6.39 //

children.text: śukataroḥ karañja-vṛkṣasyeti bhairava-tripāṭhinaḥ | kiṃśuka-vṛkṣasyeti laghu-dīpikā-kāraḥ | aṅgais tvagbhir iti rudradharaḥ | pañcāṅgair iti tripāṭhinaḥ | dhenu-vāriṇā sa-vatsā go-mūtreṇa piṣṭaiḥ sampāditā gulikā amunā mantreṇa sādhitā satī viṣaghnī bhavati kair ānanasyāñjanālepa-prakāraiḥ || KrdC_6.39 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>śuka</s>-tree is the <s>karañja</s> (Pongamia) tree — thus [say] the <s>Bhairava-tripāṭhin</s>s. The <s>kiṃśuka</s> (Butea) tree — thus [says] the author of the <s>Laghu-dīpikā</s>. 'Parts' means bark — thus <s>Rudradhara</s>. 'The five parts' — thus the <s>tripāṭhin</s>s. Ground — prepared — with cow-urine from a cow with calf, the pill, consecrated with this mantra, becomes poison-destroying. By what means? Through application, collyrium, and anointing methods. || KrdC_6.39 ||
Now he shows another application —
With the raised staff of the left arm holding <s>Govardhana</s> mountain,
With the face placed upon the flute whose notes are made clear by the fingers of the other hand; // Krd_6.40 //

children.text: dhyāyan hariṃ japan manvor ekaṃ chatraṃ vinā vrajet |
children.translated_text: Meditating on <s>Hari</s> thus, reciting one of the two mantras, one should go without an umbrella;

children.text: varṣa-vātāśanibhyaḥ syād bhayaṃ tasya nahi kvacit // Krd_6.41 //
children.translated_text: There shall be no fear for him anywhere from rain, wind, or lightning. // Krd_6.41 //

children.text: uttālito yo vāma-bāhu-daṇḍas tena dhṛto govardhanācalo yena tam anya-hastāṅgkulibhiḥ vyakta-svaro yasya vaṃśasya tatrārpitam ānanaṃ yena tam evambhūtaṃ hariṃ cintayan manvor daśāṣṭādaśākṣarayor ekaṃ japan chatraṃ vinā vrajet yas tasya vṛṣṭi-vāyu-vajrādibhyo bhayaṃ kvāpi na vidyate || KrdC_6.40-41 ||
children.translated_text: The left arm-staff that is raised — by which <s>Govardhana</s> mountain is held — him; by the fingers of the other hand, the flute whose notes are made clear — whose face is placed upon it — him, of such description. Meditating — contemplating — on <s>Hari</s>, reciting one of the two mantras — the ten- or eighteen-syllable — one should go without an umbrella. For such a person, there is no fear anywhere from rain, wind, thunderbolt, and the like. || KrdC_6.40-41 ||
He states another application —
Meditating on him before whom <s>Indra</s> retreated when the effort of the mass of clouds was rendered futile, one should offer oblations

children.text: lavaṇair ayuta-saṅkhyātair anāvṛṣṭir na saṃśayaḥ // Krd_6.42 //
children.translated_text: With salt, numbering ten thousand — [and] drought [will occur], without doubt. // Krd_6.42 //

children.text: mogho niṣphalo yo megha-samūhas tasya yatnaḥ tenāpagataḥ indor yasmāt tam etādṛśaṃ hariṃ cintayan ayuta-saṅkhyātair lavaṇair juhuyāt anantaram anāvṛṣṭir bhavati nātra saṃśayaḥ || KrdC_6.42 ||
children.translated_text: Futile — fruitless — the effort of the mass of clouds; by which <s>Indra</s> departed — meditating on <s>Hari</s> of such description, one should offer ten thousand [oblations] with salt. Thereafter, drought occurs — there is no doubt about this. || KrdC_6.42 ||
He states another application —
Playing in the waters of the <s>Yamunā</s>, diving, floating, and the like;
Being sprinkled by beloved persons with showers of spray-water from that [river]; // Krd_6.43 //
Having meditated [thus], one should offer ten thousand oblations with <s>vānīra</s> (willow) branches sprinkled with milk;

children.text: vṛṣṭir bhavat kāle 'pi mahatī nātra saṃśayaḥ // Krd_6.44 //
children.translated_text: Rain will come, even at an unseasonable time, abundantly — there is no doubt. // Krd_6.44 //

children.text: yamunā-jale majjanonmajjanaiḥ krīḍantaṃ krīḍāṃ kurvantam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? priyā-janai rukmiṇī-prabhṛtibhis tac-chīkara-jalāsāraiḥ yaumnā-jala-dhārā-rūpaiḥ sicyamānam evambhūtaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ dhyātvā vānīra-tarpaṇaiḥ vetasa-samidbhiḥ payaḥ-siktair dugdhokṣitair ayutaṃ juhuyāt | evaṃ sati akālo 'pi mahatī-vṛṣṭir bhavati nātra saṃśayaḥ || KrdC_6.43-44 ||
children.translated_text: Playing — sporting — in the water of the <s>Yamunā</s> by diving and surfacing. Again, of what description? Being sprinkled by beloved persons — <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and others — with showers of spray-water from the <s>Yamunā</s>, in the form of streams of water. Having meditated on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> of such description, with <s>vānīra</s> (willow) branches — <s>vetasa</s> (cane) fuel-sticks — sprinkled with milk — moistened with milk — one should offer ten thousand oblations. Thus, even out of season, abundant rain occurs — there is no doubt about this. || KrdC_6.43-44 ||
With this very meditation, he states another application —
Meditating on this very [form] upon the head of one afflicted by poison-boils, fever, and the like,

children.text: sa-dāha-mohair ārtasya japec chāntir bhavet kṣaṇāt // Krd_6.45 //
children.translated_text: With burning and delirium — one should recite, and peace shall come instantly. // Krd_6.45 //

children.text: dāha-moha-sahitair vuṣa-sphoṭa-jvarādibhir ārtasya mūrdhni mastake amum eva pūrvokta-rūpaṃ dhyātvā japet anantaraṃ tasya pīḍitasya kṣaṇād śāntiḥ svāsthyaṃ bhavati || KrdC_6.45 ||
children.translated_text: For one afflicted by poison-boils, fever, and the like, accompanied by burning and delirium — upon the head, upon the crown — having meditated on this very previously described form, one should recite. Thereafter, for that tormented one, peace — health — comes instantly. || KrdC_6.45 ||
For this very affliction, he states another method —
Or, [meditating on] <s>Acyuta</s> mounted on <s>Garuḍa</s>, accompanied by <s>Bala</s> and <s>Pradyumna</s>,
Praised by the [defeated] fever crushed by his own fever; // Krd_6.46 //
Having meditated [thus], one should practice one of the [mantras] upon the head of the fever-stricken one for overcoming the fever;

children.text: śāntiṃ vrajed asādhyo 'pi jvaraḥ sopadravaḥ kṣaṇāt // Krd_6.47 //
children.translated_text: Even an incurable fever with complications shall be pacified instantly. // Krd_6.47 //

children.text: athavā jvarābhibhūtyasya mastake 'cyutam dhyātvā anyataram dvayor madhye ekaṃ mantram abhyaset japet | kīdṛśaṃ ? acyutaṃ garuḍārūḍhaṃ | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? bala-pradyumnābhyāṃ saṃyutam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? nija-jvareṇa vaiṣṇava-jvareṇa śītākhyenāyudha-rūpeṇa viniṣpiṣṭaś cūrnito yo raudra-jvara uṣṇākhyāyudha-rūpas tena sṭutam | anantaraṃ asyāsādhyo 'pi jvaraḥ śīghram eva nāśaṃ gacchati | kīdṛśo jvaraḥ ? upadravo gātra-pīḍādi tat-sahitaḥ || KrdC_6.47 ||
children.translated_text: Alternatively, for one overcome by fever, having meditated on <s>Acyuta</s> upon his head, one should practice — recite — either one of the two mantras. Of what description? <s>Acyuta</s> mounted on <s>Garuḍa</s>. Again, of what description? Accompanied by <s>Bala</s> and <s>Pradyumna</s>. Again, of what description? The <s>Raudra</s> fever — of the nature of a hot weapon — has been crushed, pulverized by his own fever — the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> fever, called 'the cold one,' in the form of a weapon. Thereafter, even the incurable fever of this [patient] swiftly reaches destruction. Of what kind of fever? Accompanied by complications (<s>upadrava</s>) such as bodily pain and the like. || <s>KrdC</s> 6.47 ||
He states another application with this same meditation —
Having thus meditated, having worshipped in the fire, with four-finger-sized pieces
Soaked in milk, one should offer an <s>ayuta</s> (ten thousand) of <s>amṛtā</s> pieces (<s>guḍūcī</s>) for the pacification of fever. // <s>Krd</s> 6.48 //

children.text: evaṃ pūrvokta-rūpaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ dhyātvā vahnau sampūjya jvara-śānty-arthaṃ catur-aṅgula-parimitair dugdhāsiktair amṛtākhaṇḍair guḍcī-khaṇḍair ayutaṃ juhuyāt || KrdC_6.48 ||
children.translated_text: Having thus meditated on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in the previously described form, having duly worshipped in the fire, for the purpose of pacifying fever, with four-finger-sized pieces of <s>amṛtā</s> — <s>guḍūcī</s> (Tinospora cordifolia) — soaked in milk, one should offer an <s>ayuta</s> (ten thousand oblations). || <s>KrdC</s> 6.48 ||
He states another application —
Meditating on <s>Hari</s> who removes the agony of <s>Bhīṣma</s> pierced by sharp arrows,

children.text: smṛtvā spṛśan japed ārtaṃ pāṇibhyāṃ roga-śāntaye // Krd_6.49 //
children.translated_text: Touching the afflicted person with both hands, one should recite [the mantra] for the pacification of disease. // <s>Krd</s> 6.49 //

children.text: niśātas tīkṣṇo yaḥ śaras tena nirbhinno biddho yo bhīṣmas tasya yas tāpas taṃ harati | evambhūtaṃ harim dhyātvā ārtaṃ jvarādi-pīḍitaṃ pāṇibhyāṃ spṛṣṭvā jvara-nāśārthaṃ manvor ekataraṃ japet || KrdC_6.49 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Niśāta</s> means sharp; <s>śara</s> means arrow; by that pierced — wounded — is <s>Bhīṣma</s>; his agony — that he removes. Having meditated on <s>Hari</s> of such a nature, having touched the afflicted one — the one tormented by fever and the like — with both hands, one should recite either of the two mantras for the purpose of destroying the fever. || <s>KrdC</s> 6.49 ||
He states another application —
For the destruction of untimely death, meditating on [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] who restored the son of <s>Sāndīpani</s>,
One should offer an <s>ayuta</s> (ten thousand) of <s>amṛta-latā</s> (<s>guḍūcī</s>) pieces soaked in milk. // <s>Krd</s> 6.50 //

children.text: sāndīpaniḥ kṛṣṇa-guruḥ | tasya suta-pradaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ dhyātvā amṛta-latā-khaṇḍaiḥ guḍcī-khaṇḍaiḥ kṣīrāktair dugdha-siktair ayutaṃ hunet juhuyāt | kasmai ? apamṛtyur akāla-maraṇaṃ tasya vināśāya nivṛttaye || KrdC_6.50 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sāndīpani</s> is the <s>guru</s> of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. Having meditated on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> who restored his son, with pieces of <s>amṛta-latā</s> — <s>guḍūcī</s> — soaked in milk, one should offer an <s>ayuta</s> (ten thousand oblations). For what purpose? For the destruction — the removal — of <s>apamṛtyu</s> (untimely death). || <s>KrdC</s> 6.50 ||
He states another application —
Meditating on [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] who gave sons to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> whose sons had died, together with <s>Arjuna</s>,

children.text: dhyātvā lakṣaṃ japed ekaṃ manvoḥ suta-vivṛddhaye // Krd_6.51 //
children.translated_text: One should recite one <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand) of either mantra for the increase of progeny. // <s>Krd</s> 6.51 //

children.text: mṛta-putrāya viprāya putrān dadataṃ sārjunam arjuna-sahitaṃ dhyātvā manvor ekaṃ lakṣaṃ japet | kim-artham ? suta-vṛddhi-nimittam || KrdC_6.51 ||
children.translated_text: Having meditated on [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] who gave sons to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> whose sons had died, together with <s>Arjuna</s>, one should recite one <s>lakṣa</s> of either mantra. For what purpose? For the purpose of the increase of sons. || <s>KrdC</s> 6.51 ||
He states another application —
One should offer an <s>ayuta</s> (ten thousand) in a fire kindled with the wood of the <s>putra-jīva</s> tree (Putranjiva roxburghii),

children.text: tat-phalair madhurāktaiḥ syuḥ putrā dīrghāyuṣo 'sya tu // Krd_6.52 //
children.translated_text: With its fruits soaked in sweets — then his sons shall be long-lived. // <s>Krd</s> 6.52 //

children.text: jīvāputreti yasya prasiddhiḥ tasya indhanena yute sampādite vahnau tat-phalaiḥ putra-jīvāphalair madhurāktais tri-madhv-aktair manvor ekenāyutaṃ juhuyāt | anantaram asya homa-kartuḥ puttāḥ dīrghāyuṣo bhavanti || KrdC_6.52 ||
children.translated_text: The tree popularly known as <s>jīvāputra</s> — in a fire prepared with its wood, with its fruits — the fruits of the <s>putra-jīva</s> tree — soaked in the three sweets (<s>tri-madhu</s>), one should offer an <s>ayuta</s> with either mantra. Thereafter, the sons of this performer of the <s>homa</s> become long-lived. || <s>KrdC</s> 6.52 ||
He states another application —
Having duly worshipped at night a <s>kalaśa</s> (vessel) filled with decoction of milk-tree bark,

children.text: japtvāyutaṃ prage nārīm abhiṣiñced dviṣaṭ-dinam // Krd_6.53 //
children.translated_text: Having recited an <s>ayuta</s> (ten thousand), in the morning one should sprinkle the woman for twelve days. // <s>Krd</s> 6.53 //
She, even if barren, obtains long-lived, disease-free sons —

children.text: labhate nātra sandehas taj-japtājyāśinī satī // Krd_6.54 //
children.translated_text: There is no doubt about this, provided she eats ghee consecrated with the mantra. // <s>Krd</s> 6.54 //

children.text: kalaśa-pūraṇa-vidhānena kṣīra-vṛkṣa-kvāthena sampūrṇam kalaśaṃ niśi rātrau sampūjyāyutaṃ japtvā prage prātaḥ-kāle putrārthinīṃ striyaṃ dviṣaṭ-dinam dvādaśa-dināni vyāpyābhiṣiñcet | anantaraṃ sābhiṣiktā bandhyāpi apatya-janana-samaya-yogyā ajanitāpatyo 'pi putrān dīrghāyuṣo roga-rahitān prāpnoti | kimbhūtā satī ? mantra-japtājya-bhojinī satī | atrārthe sandeho nāsti || KrdC_6.53-54 ||
children.translated_text: According to the method of filling the <s>kalaśa</s>, having filled the vessel with the decoction of milk-trees (<s>kṣīra-vṛkṣa</s>), at night — in the evening — having duly worshipped and recited an <s>ayuta</s>, in the morning, one should sprinkle the woman who desires a son for twelve days. Thereafter, she who is thus sprinkled, even if barren — even if she has not given birth at the suitable time for bearing children — obtains sons who are long-lived and free from disease. Being of what kind? Being one who eats ghee consecrated with the mantra. There is no doubt in this matter. || <s>KrdC</s> 6.53-54 ||
He states another application —
In the morning, observing silence, a woman desiring a son, [should take] water in a <s>bodhi</s> (sacred fig) leaf-cup,
And having consecrated it one hundred and eight times [with the mantra], should drink it — she will surely [obtain a son]. // <s>Krd</s> 6.55 //

children.text: prātaḥ-kāle vācaṃ-yamā mauninī putrīyatī ātmanaḥ putram icchantī bodhi-cchada-puṭe pippala-patra-puṭe jalaṃ manvor anyatareṇāṣṭottara-śataṃ japtaṃ māsaṃ vyāpya pibet | anantaraṃ putraṃ prāpnotīti śeṣaḥ | jala-pāna-mantram āha-devakī-putreti | atra prasaṅgāt asmin granthe anukto 'pi santāna-gopāla-mantraḥ kathyate | tad yathā-

children.translated_text: 'O son of <s>Devakī</s>, O <s>Govinda</s>, O <s>Vāsudeva</s>, O teacher of the world,

children.text: dehi me tanayaṃ kṛṣṇa tvām ahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Give me a son, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — I have taken refuge in you.'

In the morning, observing silence — being a silent one — the woman desiring a son — wishing for her own child — in a <s>bodhi-cchada-puṭa</s> — a cup made of <s>pippala</s> (sacred fig) leaves — water consecrated with either of the two mantras one hundred and eight times, for a month continuously, she should drink. Thereafter, she obtains a son — this is to be supplied. He states the mantra for drinking the water — '<s>Devakī-putra</s>' etc. Here, incidentally, though not stated in this text, the <s>Santāna-gopāla</s> mantra is described. It is as follows —

children.text: asya mantrasya nārado munir anuṣṭup-chandaḥ santāna-prado gopāla-kṛṣṇo devatā padair vyastair vā pañcāṅgāni | dhyānaṃ yathā-

children.translated_text: '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, bearing the conch and discus, standing in a chariot, four-armed,
Resplendent with all ornaments, wearing yellow garments, <s>Acyuta</s>,

Of this mantra, the sage is <s>Nārada</s>; the meter is <s>anuṣṭubh</s>; the deity is <s>Santāna-prada Gopāla-Kṛṣṇa</s> (the progeny-bestowing <s>Gopāla Kṛṣṇa</s>); the five limbs are [formed] from the individual words. The meditation is as follows —

children.text:
mayūra-piccha-saṃyuktaṃ viṣṇu-tejopabṛṃhitam |
samarpayantaṃ viprāya naṣṭān ānīya bālakān |
karuṇāmṛta-sampūrṇa-dṛṣṭyekṣantaṃ ca taṃ dvijām || iti || KrdC_6.55 ||
children.translated_text:
Adorned with peacock feathers, radiant with the splendor of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
presenting to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> the lost children who have been brought back,
and gazing upon that twice-born with eyes brimming with the nectar of compassion.' Thus. || <s>KrdC</s> 6.55 ||
He states another application —
Meditating on <s>Hari</s> who cut down with his own discus the <s>Kṛtyā</s> (destructive spell) sent by the king of <s>Kāśī</s>,

children.text: tat-tejasā tan-nagarīṃ dahantaṃ bhāvayan harim // Krd_6.56 //
children.translated_text: And with its power burned that city, // <s>Krd</s> 6.56 //
One should offer [oblations] at night for seven days with mustard seeds anointed with their own oil;

children.text: kṛtyā kartāram evāsau kupitā nāśayed dhruvam // Krd_6.57 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Kṛtyā</s>, enraged, will surely destroy its own creator. // <s>Krd</s> 6.57 //

children.text: prahitāṃ preṣitāṃ kāśīśvareṇa kṛtyāṃ ghātakartīṃ nijāriṇā nija-cakreṇa chitvā anantaraṃ tat-tejasā tasya kāśīśvara-rājasya nagarīṃ dahantaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ bhāvayan sva-snehāktair sarṣapa-taila-yuktaiḥ sarṣapaiḥ sapta-dināni vyāpya rātrau manvor ekatareṇa juhuyāt | athānantaraṃ asau kṛtyā kruddhā satī dhruvaṃ niścitaṃ kartāram eva nāśayet || KrdC_6.57 ||
children.translated_text: Having meditated on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> who cut down with his own discus (<s>cakra</s>) the <s>Kṛtyā</s> — the destructive spell — sent by the lord of <s>Kāśī</s>, and thereafter with its power burned the city of that king of <s>Kāśī</s>, with mustard seeds anointed with their own oil — mixed with mustard oil — for seven days, at night, with either mantra, one should offer oblations. Then thereafter, this <s>Kṛtyā</s>, being enraged, will surely — certainly — destroy the creator himself [who sent it]. || <s>KrdC</s> 6.57 ||
He states another application —
Seated in a divine hermitage adorned with a grove of <s>badarī</s> (jujube) trees,
Touching with his lotus-hands the body of <s>Ghaṇṭākarṇa</s>, // <s>Krd</s> 6.58 //
Having thus meditated on <s>Acyuta</s>, one should offer a <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand) of sesame seeds soaked in the three sweets (<s>tri-madhura</s>),

children.text: muktaye sarva-pāpānāṃ śāntaye kāntaye tanoḥ // Krd_6.59 //
children.translated_text: For liberation from all sins, for peace, and for the radiance of the body. // <s>Krd</s> 6.59 //

children.text: badarī-ṣaṇḍo badarī-samūhas tena maṇḍite śobhite divye utkṛṣṭe āśrama āsīnam upaviṣṭaṃ tathā hasta-paṅkajābhyāṃ ghaṇṭākarṇasya mahādeva-mūrteḥ kasyacit mahādeva-bhaktasya vā kalevaram śarīraṃ spṛśantam acyutaṃ dhyātvā tilais tri-madhurāplutair ghṛta-madhu-śarkarā-miśritair manvor ekena lakṣaṃ juhuyāt | kim-artham ? mokṣāya tathā sakala-pāpānāṃ vināśārthaṃ tathā tanor dehasya kāntaye dīpty-artham || KrdC_6.58-59 ||
children.translated_text: A grove of <s>badarī</s> (jujube) — a cluster of jujube trees — adorned, made beautiful by that; in a divine — excellent — hermitage, seated — sitting; and touching with his lotus-hands the body — the form — of <s>Ghaṇṭākarṇa</s>, a certain form of <s>Mahādeva</s> (or a certain great devotee of <s>Mahādeva</s>); having meditated on <s>Acyuta</s> thus, with sesame seeds soaked in the three sweets — mixed with ghee, honey, and sugar — with either mantra, one should offer a <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand). For what purpose? For <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), and for the destruction of all sins, and for the radiance — the brilliance — of the body. || <s>KrdC</s> 6.58-59 ||
He states another application —
Recalling <s>Hari</s> who caused enmity between <s>Rukmī</s> and <s>Bala</s> (i.e., <s>Balarāma</s>) who were engaged in gambling,

children.text: juhuyād iṣṭayor dviṣṭyai gulikā gomayodbhavāḥ // Krd_6.60 //
children.translated_text: One should offer cow-dung pellets, for creating discord between two desired [targets]. // <s>Krd</s> 6.60 //

children.text: dyūtāsaktau dyūta-karma kurvantau rukmi-balabhadrau dveṣayantaṃ parasparaṃ dveṣam utpādayantaṃ hariṃ smaran gomayotpannā gulikā manvor ekena juhuyāt | atra sahasra-homo boddhavyaḥ | anuktāyāṃ tu saṅkhyāyāṃ sahasraṃ tatra nirdiśet iti vacanāt | kim-artham ? iṣṭayor mitrayor dviṣṭyai vidveṣaṇārtham || KrdC_6.60 ||
children.translated_text: Recalling <s>Hari</s> who caused mutual hatred — generated enmity — between <s>Rukmī</s> and <s>Balabhadra</s> who were engaged in gambling, one should offer cow-dung-made pellets with either mantra. Here a thousand oblations should be understood, since the rule states: 'When no count is specified, one thousand should be prescribed.' For what purpose? For creating discord (<s>vidveṣaṇa</s>) between two friends. || <s>KrdC</s> 6.60 ||
He states another application —
The banner-bearer of <s>Garuḍa</s>, raining arrows with blazing fire at their tips,
Pursuing the fleeing host of enemies — <s>Acyuta</s>, // <s>Krd</s> 6.61 //
Having thus meditated, one should recite seven thousand of either mantra;

children.text: uccāṭanaṃ bhaved etad-ripūṇāṃ saptabhir dinaiḥ // Krd_6.62 //
children.translated_text: This becomes the <s>uccāṭana</s> (eradication) of enemies within seven days. // <s>Krd</s> 6.62 //

children.text: jvalan dedīpyamāno yo vahnis tadvan mukhaṃ yeṣāṃ tair bāṇair varṣantaṃ tāḍayantaṃ tathā garuḍārūḍhaṃ tathā dhāvamānaṃ śatru-samūham anupaścād dhāvantaṃ hariṃ dhyātvā manvor daśāṣṭādaśākṣarayor ekaṃ sapta-sahasrakam abhyaset japet | evaṃ kṛte sati etasya śatrūṇāṃ saptabhir dinair uccāṭanaṃ bhavati sva-deśād apayānaṃ bhavati || KrdC_6.62 ||
children.translated_text: Blazing — shining — fire, whose faces are like that — with such arrows — raining — striking; mounted on <s>Garuḍa</s>; pursuing — chasing after — the fleeing host of enemies; having meditated on <s>Hari</s> thus, of the two mantras of ten and eighteen syllables, one should practice — recite — seven thousand of either. When this is done, within seven days the <s>uccāṭana</s> (eradication) of this person's enemies occurs — they depart from their own country. || <s>KrdC</s> 6.62 ||
He states another application —
Meditating on [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] who tossed up the calf-[demon] and who stole the <s>kapittha</s> (wood-apple) fruit,

children.text: ayutaṃ prajapet sādhyam uccāṭayati tat-kṣaṇāt // Krd_6.63 //
children.translated_text: One should recite an <s>ayuta</s> (ten thousand) — the target is eradicated instantly. // <s>Krd</s> 6.63 //

children.text: utkṣipta ūrdhvaṃ kṣipto vatso vatsa-rūpo vatsakāsuro yena tathā kapitthasya phalaṃ haratīti kṛṣṇaṃ dhyātvā manvor madhye ekaṃ ayutaṃ japet | anantaraṃ tat-kṣaṇāt śīghram eva sādhyam uccāṭanīyam uccāṭayati || KrdC_6.63 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Utkṣipta</s> means thrown upward; <s>vatsa</s> — the calf-formed demon <s>Vatsaka</s> — by whom, thus; the one who steals the fruit of the <s>kapittha</s> (wood-apple tree) — having meditated on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> thus, one should recite an <s>ayuta</s> of either of the two mantras. Thereafter, instantly — very quickly — the target to be eradicated is eradicated. || <s>KrdC</s> 6.63 ||
He states another application —
Having meditated on oneself as <s>Kaṃsa-mathana</s> (the destroyer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>), and the enemy as <s>Kaṃsa</s> himself, cast down from the platform,

children.text: kaṃsātmānam ariṃ karṣan gatāsuṃ prajapen manum // Krd_6.64 //
children.translated_text: Dragging [him], bereft of life, one should recite the mantra. // <s>Krd</s> 6.64 //
One should offer an <s>ayuta</s> (ten thousand) with oblations of the wood of the [enemy's] birth-star tree;

children.text: api sevita-pīyūṣo miryate 'rir na saṃśayaḥ // Krd_6.65 //
children.translated_text: Even one who has consumed the nectar of immortality — the enemy shall die, there is no doubt. // <s>Krd</s> 6.65 //

children.text: ātmānaṃ kaṃsa-mathanaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ dhyātvā kaṃsa-mathanāt manor aikyaṃ vicintya tathā ripuṃ kaṃsa-svarūpaṃ apagata-prāṇaṃ dhyātvā ripu-kaṃsayor abhedaṃ vicintyeti bhāvaḥ | mañcād adhaḥ-kṛtaṃ ākarṣayan ākarṣaṇaṃ bhāvayan manvor ekam ayutaṃ japet | asya ripoḥ janmoḍutarutarpaṇaiḥ samidbhir juhuyāc ca |
children.translated_text: Having meditated on oneself as <s>Kaṃsa-mathana</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the destroyer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>) — contemplating one's identity with the mantra of <s>Kaṃsa</s>'s destruction — and having meditated on the enemy in the form of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, bereft of life — contemplating the non-difference of the enemy and <s>Kaṃsa</s> — this is the purport. Having cast him down from the platform, dragging him — visualizing the act of dragging — one should recite an <s>ayuta</s> of either mantra. One should also offer oblations with the firewood of this enemy's birth-star tree —
<s>Kāraskara</s> (Strychnos nux-vomica), then <s>dhātrī</s> (Indian gooseberry), then the <s>udumbara</s> (fig) tree,
<s>Jambū</s> (rose-apple), <s>khadira</s> (acacia), <s>kṛṣṇa</s> (dark plum), <s>vaṃśa</s> (bamboo), and <s>pippala</s> (sacred fig),
<s>Nāga</s> (Mesua ferrea) and <s>rohita</s> (a tree), <s>palāśa</s> (Butea monosperma) and <s>plakṣa</s> (wavy-leaf fig),
<s>Ambaṣṭha</s> (a medicinal tree), <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple), <s>arjuna</s> (Terminalia arjuna), <s>vikaṅkata</s> (thorny tree),
<s>Bahala</s>, <s>savala</s>, <s>kharjūra</s> (date-palm), <s>bhaṇḍila</s>, <s>panasa</s> (jackfruit), and <s>arka</s> (milkweed),
<s>Śamī</s> (Prosopis), <s>damba</s>, <s>āmra</s> (mango), <s>nimba</s> (neem), <s>madhuka</s> (mahua), and <s>ṛkṣa</s> trees.

children.text: iti saptaviṃśati-nakṣatrāṇāṃ vṛkṣāḥ | janma-nakṣatra-vṛkṣa evaṃ kṛte seivta-pīyūṣo 'pi mriyate nātra saṃśayaḥ || KrdC_6.64-65 ||
children.translated_text: These are the trees of the twenty-seven <s>nakṣatra</s>s (lunar asterisms). The birth-star tree [is to be used]. When this is done, even one who has consumed the nectar of immortality shall die — there is no doubt in this matter. || <s>KrdC</s> 6.64-65 ||
He shows that this same purpose can be achieved by another method as well —
Alternatively, with <s>vibhītaka</s> (Terminalia bellirica) [wood-pieces] anointed with neem oil,

children.text: ayutaṃ prayato rātrau maraṇāya ripoḥ kṣaṇāt // Krd_6.66 //
children.translated_text: One should offer an <s>ayuta</s> (ten thousand), purified, at night, for the swift death of the enemy. // <s>Krd</s> 6.66 //

children.text: nimba-taila-siktair akṣajaiḥ vibhītaka-samidbhiḥ prayataḥ pavitraḥ san rātrau manvor ekena ayutaṃ hunet | kim-artham ? śatroḥ śīghra-vināśāya || KrdC_6.66 ||
children.translated_text: With <s>vibhītaka</s> firewood anointed — sprinkled — with neem oil, being purified — being in a state of purity — at night, with either mantra, one should offer an <s>ayuta</s>. For what purpose? For the swift destruction of the enemy. || <s>KrdC</s> 6.66 ||
He states yet another application for this same purpose —
With pellets of turmeric, <s>ariṣṭa</s> (soap-nut or <s>vibhītaka</s>) leaves, <s>vyoṣa</s> (the three pungents), and cotton seeds, anointed with castor oil, at night,
One should offer oblations, stationed in a cremation ground, for the destruction of the enemy. // <s>Krd</s> 6.67 //

children.text: doṣā haridrā ariṣṭa-dalaṃ vibhītaka-patram iti rudradharaḥ | bhallātaka-patram iti rudradhaaḥ | nimba-patram iti bhairava-tripāṭhinaḥ | vyoṣaṃ trikaṭukaṃ kārpāsāsthi kārpāsā-bījaṃ kaṇaṃ pipplaī etair militair eraṇḍa-taila-siktaiḥ smaśānasthaḥ mṛta-saṃskāra-sthānasthaḥ san niśi rātrau manvor ekena juhuyāt | kim-arthaṃ ? śatru-nāśārtham || KrdC_6.67 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Doṣā</s> is turmeric. <s>Ariṣṭa-dala</s> is <s>vibhītaka</s> leaf — thus [says] <s>Rudradhara</s>; <s>bhallātaka</s> (marking-nut) leaf — thus [also says] <s>Rudradhara</s>; neem leaf — thus [say] the <s>Bhairava-tripāṭhin</s>s. <s>Vyoṣa</s> is the three pungents (<s>trikaṭuka</s>: ginger, pepper, long pepper). <s>Kārpāsāsthi</s> is cotton seed. <s>Kaṇa</s> is long pepper (<s>pippalī</s>). With these combined, anointed with castor oil, being stationed in a cremation ground — a place where funerary rites are performed — at night, with either mantra, one should offer oblations. For what purpose? For the destruction of the enemy. || <s>KrdC</s> 6.67 ||
Due to passion, he states the expiation for the application of killing rites —

children.text: na śastaṃ māraṇaṃ karma kuryāc ced ayutaṃ japet |
children.translated_text: The rite of killing (<s>māraṇa</s>) is not commended; if one performs it, one should recite ten thousand [mantras],

children.text: huned vā pāyasais tāvat śāntaye śāntamāsaḥ // Krd_6.68 //
children.translated_text: Or offer that many oblations of <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice), for pacification, with a peaceful mind.

children.text: māraṇaṃ karma śiṣṭa-janasya na praśastaṃ tathāpi yadi vā rāgāt kuryāt tadā manvor madhye ekaṃ mantraṃ ayutaṃ japet paramānnena vā ayutaṃ juhuyāt | śāntaye pāpa-nāśāya śānta-mānaso nirmatsaraḥ || KrdC_6.68 ||
children.translated_text: The rite of killing (<s>māraṇa-karman</s>) is not commended for a person of good conduct; nevertheless, if one performs it out of passion, then one should recite one of the two mantras ten thousand times, or offer ten thousand oblations with <s>paramānna</s> (milk-rice pudding). For pacification — for the destruction of sin — with a peaceful mind, free from envy.
He states another application —
One desiring victory should recite one <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand), meditating on <s>Hari</s> as the one who stole the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree;

children.text: smaran parājayas tasya na kutaścid bhaviṣyati // Krd_6.69 //
children.translated_text: Defeat for him will never come from any quarter.

children.text: jaya-kāmaḥ pumān balād indra-sakāśāt svargastha-pārijātāpahāriṇaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ bhāvayan manvor ekaṃ lakṣaṃ japet | evaṃ kṛte tasya bhaṅgaḥ kasmād api na bhaviṣyatīti || KrdC_6.69 ||
children.translated_text: A person desiring victory, meditating on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as the one who forcibly took the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree from <s>Indra</s>'s presence in heaven, should recite one of the two mantras one hundred thousand times. When this is done, his defeat will never come from any source whatsoever.
He states another application —
Meditating on <s>Hari</s> as the one imparting the meaning of the <s>Gītā</s> to <s>Pārtha</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), with the <s>vyākhyā-mudrā</s> (gesture of exposition) in his hand,

children.text: rathasthaṃ bhāvayan japyād dharma-vṛddhyai śamāya ca // Krd_6.70 //
children.translated_text: Seated on the chariot, one should recite for the increase of <s>dharma</s> and for peace.

children.text: pārthe 'rjune gītārthaṃ diśantaṃ kathayantaṃ tathā vyākhyā-mudrāṃ kare yasya tam uttāna-tarjany-aṅguṣṭha-yutā vyākhyā-mudrā tathā rathārūḍhaṃ hariṃ bhāvayan manvor ekaṃ lakṣaṃ japet | kim-artham ? dharmotpatty-arthaṃ mokṣārthaṃ ca || KrdC_6.70 ||
children.translated_text: Meditating on [<s>Hari</s>] as the one imparting — narrating — the meaning of the <s>Gītā</s> to <s>Pārtha</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), and in whose hand is the <s>vyākhyā-mudrā</s> (gesture of exposition) — the <s>vyākhyā-mudrā</s> being formed with the index finger and thumb extended upward — likewise, mounted on the chariot; meditating on <s>Hari</s> thus, one should recite one of the two mantras one hundred thousand times. For what purpose? For the arising of <s>dharma</s> and for <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).
He states another application —
Whoever offers one <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand) oblations with <s>palāśa</s> (Butea) flowers soaked in sweet [substances],

children.text: vyākhyātā sarva-śāstrāṇāṃ sa kavir vādirāḍ bhavet // Krd_6.71 //
children.translated_text: He would become an expounder of all <s>śāstra</s>s, a great poet, and a king among debaters.

children.text: yaḥ palāśa-puṣpair ghṛta-madhu-śarkarā-miśrair manvor ekena lakṣaṃ juhuyāt sa sakala-śāstrāṇāṃ vyākhyātā kavirāṭ kavi-śreṣṭhaś ca bhavet || KrdC_6.71 ||
children.translated_text: Whoever offers one hundred thousand oblations with <s>palāśa</s> flowers mixed with ghee, honey, and sugar, using one of the two mantras, he would become an expounder of all <s>śāstra</s>s, a king of poets (<s>kavirāṭ</s>) — the best among poets.
He states another application —
Meditating on <s>Hari</s> as bearing the cosmic form (<s>Viśvarūpa</s>), with radiance equal to ten million rising suns,
Resembling molten gold, of the nature of <s>Agni</s> (fire) and <s>Soma</s> (moon),
Whose lotus-feet outshine the brilliance of the sun and fire, wearing divine ornaments,
Bearing various weapons, pervading all the space of the universe,
For the protection of the kingdom, city, village, dwelling, and body,

children.text: prajapen mantrayor ekataraṃ dhyātvaivam ādarāt // Krd_6.74 //
children.translated_text: One should recite one of the two mantras, having meditated thus, with devotion.

children.text: viśvarūpa-dharam etad vyācaṣṭe udyad-āditya-koṭi-samāna-kāntiṃ tathā dravībhūta-suvarṇa-tulyaṃ tathā agni-soma-svarūpaṃ | sūrya-somātmakam iti tripāṭhinaḥ | tathā sūryāgnivad ujjvalaṃ mukhaṃ pāda-padmaṃ yasya | tathā cāru-bhūṣaṇaṃ tathā vividha-śastra-dharaṃ tathā vyāpta-saṃsārākāśābhyantaram, etādṛśaṃ hariṃ dhyātvā ādarāt mantrayor ekaṃ japet | kim-artham ? rāṣṭrau deśe pūr nagaraṃ grāmo 'lpa-jana-vāsa-sthānaṃ vāstu eka-gṛha-svāmi-vāsaḥ | kṣetram iti govinda-miśrāḥ | vastv iti pāṭhe hiraṇyādi | eteṣāṃ śarīrasya ca rakṣaṇe rakṣā-nimittam || KrdC_6.72-74 ||
children.translated_text: He explains the cosmic form (<s>Viśvarūpa</s>): having radiance equal to ten million rising suns; likewise, resembling molten gold; likewise, of the nature of <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>; some read 'of the nature of <s>Sūrya</s> and <s>Soma</s>.' Likewise, whose face and lotus-feet are blazing like the sun and fire; likewise, wearing beautiful ornaments; likewise, bearing various weapons; likewise, pervading the interior of the entire cosmic space. Having meditated on <s>Hari</s> of such description, one should recite one of the two mantras with devotion. For what purpose? <s>Rāṣṭra</s> is the country; <s>pūr</s> is the city; <s>grāma</s> is a small settlement; <s>vāstu</s> is a single householder's dwelling; <s>Govinda Miśra</s>s [read it as] '<s>kṣetra</s>' (field); in the reading '<s>vastu</s>,' [it means] gold and the like. For the protection of these and of the body.
He states another application —
Alternatively, [the mantra] whose <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer) is <s>Arjuna</s>, whose limbs are composed of all the feet taken separately,
<s>Triṣṭubh</s> as its meter, <s>Viśvarūpa Viṣṇu</s> as its presiding deity —
One should recite the <s>Gītā-manu</s> (the mantra of the <s>Gītā</s>) at the [appropriate] place, beginning with '<s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>'; or offer oblations with ghee,
For all-round protection and for the pacification of all sorrows.

children.text: athavā sthāne hṛṣīkeśādyaṃ gītā-manuṃ japet | kimbhūtaṃ manum ? vyastam ekaikaṃ sarve samastā ye aṅghrayaḥ pāda-catuṣṭayaṃ taiḥ racitam aṅgaṃ pañcāṅgam | arjunaḥ ṛṣir yatra taṃ vyasta-sarvāṅghri-racitāṅgaś cārjuna ṛṣikaś ceti dvandvaḥ taṃ triṣṭup-chando yatra taṃ viśvarūpo viṣṇur adhidevatā yasya tam | ājyakair ghṛtair huned vā vāśabdaḥ samuccaye hunet | ṭīkāntare ukta-prayogeṣu yatra japa-homayoḥ saṅkhyā na uktā tatra saṃnidhānoktā gṛhyate tad-abhāve 'ṣtottaraṃ sahasraṃ śataṃ vā aṣṭau sahasrāṇīty eke | jagan-mohanākhya-tantre-
children.translated_text: Alternatively, at the [appropriate] place, one should recite the <s>Gītā-manu</s> (mantra of the <s>Gītā</s>) beginning with '<s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>.' Of what kind is this mantra? That whose limbs (<s>aṅga</s>, the five ancillaries) are composed of all the feet (<s>pāda</s>s, the four quarter-verses) taken separately, one by one; and whose seer (<s>ṛṣi</s>) is <s>Arjuna</s> — this is a <s>dvandva</s> compound: 'that which has limbs composed of all separately-taken feet, and whose seer is <s>Arjuna</s>'; whose meter is <s>Triṣṭubh</s>; whose presiding deity is <s>Viśvarūpa Viṣṇu</s>. One should also offer oblations with ghee — the word '<s>vā</s>' is used in the sense of inclusion — one should offer oblations. In another commentary: in the applications described, where the count of recitation and <s>homa</s> is not stated, the count mentioned in the vicinity should be adopted; in the absence of that, one thousand and eight, or one hundred, or eight thousand — thus say some. In the <s>Jaganmohana-tantra</s>:

children.text: lakṣaṃ vāpy ayutaṃ vāpi sahasraṃ śatam eva ca |
children.translated_text: Whether one <s>lakṣa</s>, or ten thousand, or one thousand, or even one hundred,

children.text: kāryāṇāṃ gaurvān mantrī tat-tad-dhomaṃ samācaret || KrdC_6.75-76 ||
children.translated_text: The ritualist should perform the respective <s>homa</s> according to the gravity of the purposes.

Thus ends the sixth chapter (<s>paṭala</s>) of the <s>Krama-dīpikā</s> composed by <s>Śrī Keśava Bhaṭṭācārya</s>.
||6||

(7)
Seventh Chapter (<s>Saptama Paṭala</s>)
For the purpose of describing numerous mantras, he commences the seventh chapter, beginning with '<s>vakṣya</s>' ('I shall describe') —
I shall describe the practice (<s>pratipatti</s>) of the Lord of <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>),

children.text: suguptāṃ dhana-nāthādyair dhanyair yā kriyate sadā // Krd_7.1 //
children.translated_text: Well-concealed, which is always performed by the lords of wealth and other blessed ones, for the attainment of inexhaustible wealth.

children.text: śriyaḥ pater gopālasya pratipattiṃ dhyānaṃ mantra-pūjā-dhyānādi-prakāraṃ vā vakṣye | yā pratipattir dhana-nāthādyaiḥ kubera-prabhṛtibhir mahādhanaiḥ kriyate | kasyai ? akṣayam avināśi yad dhanaṃ tat-prāptyai | suguptā nātyanta-prakaṭitāṃ dvijair ity arthaḥ || KrdC_7.1 ||
children.translated_text: I shall describe the practice (<s>pratipatti</s>) — the meditation, mantra-worship-meditation procedure, etc. — of <s>Gopāla</s>, the Lord of <s>Śrī</s>. Which practice is performed by the lords of wealth (<s>dhana-nātha</s>) and others — by <s>Kubera</s> and other great wealthy ones. For what purpose? For the attainment of inexhaustible — imperishable — wealth. Well-concealed (<s>suguptā</s>) — not widely revealed — by the twice-born — this is the meaning.
A <s>kulaka</s> (verse-cluster) of seven verses beginning with 'In <s>Dvāravatī</s>' —
In <s>Dvāravatī</s>, with the finest mansions blazing like a thousand suns,

children.text: analpaiḥ kalpa-vṛkṣaiś ca parīte maṇḍapottame // Krd_7.2 //
children.translated_text: In the supreme pavilion, surrounded by abundant wish-fulfilling trees,

children.text: acyuto dhyeyaḥ kutra ? dvāravatyāṃ maṇi-maṇḍape maṇi-siṃhāsanāmbuje āsīno dvārakā-nagarī-gata-maṇi-maṇḍapāvasthita-maṇi-maya-siṃhāsanopaviṣṭaḥ maṇi-maṇḍape | kīdṛśe ? bhavanottamaiḥ gṛhottamaiḥ kalpa-vṛkṣaiś ca parīte veṣṭite | kimbhūtaiḥ ? sahasra-sūryāḥ tadvad bhāsvarair dīptair analpair vistaraiḥ || KrdC_7.2 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Acyuta</s> (the Imperishable One) is to be meditated upon — where? In <s>Dvāravatī</s>, on a gem-pavilion, seated on a lotus upon a gem-throne — seated upon a gem-made throne in a gem-pavilion situated in the city of <s>Dvārakā</s>. In what kind [of pavilion]? Surrounded — enclosed — by the finest mansions and wish-fulfilling trees. Of what kind? Blazing — radiant — like a thousand suns, and extensive — vast.
With pillars, doorways, arches, and walls made of blazing gems,
With pearls hanging from colorful canopies adorned with garlands of full-blown flowers.

children.text: punaḥ kīdṛśe ? jvalanti dīptāni yāni ratnāni tan-mayaṃ tat-pradhānaṃ stambhaḥ gṛhādhāra-bhūtaṃ dvāra-toraṇaṃ kuḍyaṃ bhittir yatra tasmin praphullā vikāsanīyā srak puṣpa-mālā ullasac-chobamānaṃ pavitraṃ nānā-prakāraṃ vitānaṃ tatrālambi mauktikaṃ yatra tatra || KrdC_7.3 ||
children.translated_text: Again, of what kind? In which there are pillars — supports of the mansion — doorways, arches, and walls (<s>kuḍya</s>) — all made of blazing, radiant gems; where there are full-blown — blossoming — garlands (<s>srak</s>) of flowers, shining — beautiful — variegated canopies, from which hang pearls.
Again, of what kind is this gem-pavilion?
In the middle of a ground of <s>padma-rāga</s> (rubies) and a resplendent river of gems,
Beneath the celestial tree (<s>svas-taru</s>, i.e., <s>Pārijāta</s>) from which gem-nectar flows incessantly.

children.text: padma-rāga-mayī yā sthalī rājad dedīpyamāna-ratna-mayī ca yā nadī tayor madhye svas-taroḥ pārijātasyādhaḥ | svas-taror kimbhūtasya ? anārataṃ sarvadā galantī ratnamayī sudhā amṛtaṃ yasya tasya || KrdC_7.4 ||
children.translated_text: The ground made of rubies (<s>padma-rāga</s>), and the river made of resplendent — shining — gems; in the middle of these two, beneath the celestial tree — the <s>Pārijāta</s>. Of what kind is this celestial tree? That from which gem-nectar (<s>ratna-sudhā</s>) — gem-like ambrosia — flows incessantly — at all times.
