Again, of what kind is this gem-pavilion?
With the quarters illuminated by rows of gem-lamps,
Resembling the rising sun — on a lotus upon a gem-throne.

children.text: ratna-pradīpāvalibhir jvalad-ratnaiḥ pradīpitam udbhāsitaṃ diśām antarālam avakāśo yatra maṇi-siṃhāsane | kimbhūte ? udyat prādurbhavan ya ādityas tasya saṅkāśe sadṛśe || KrdC_7.5 ||
children.translated_text: Illuminated — made radiant — in the interstices of the directions by rows of gem-lamps — blazing gems. On a gem-throne — of what kind? Resembling — similar to — the rising sun that appears.
Of what kind is <s>Acyuta</s>?
<s>Acyuta</s> (the Imperishable One) is to be meditated upon as seated, resembling molten gold,
With radiance equal to ten million simultaneously rising moons, suns, and lightnings.

children.text: druta-hāṭaka-saṃnibhaḥ dravī-bhūta-svarṇa-tulyaḥ samānoditā ekadodgatā yā candrārkānāṃ koṭiḥ taḍitām api koṭiḥ tat-sama-dyutir yasya saḥ || KrdC_7.6 ||
children.translated_text: Resembling molten gold (<s>druta-hāṭaka</s>) — like liquefied gold. Whose radiance equals that of ten million simultaneously rising moons, suns, and lightnings all at once.
Again, of what kind?
Beautiful in all limbs, gentle, adorned with all ornaments,
Wearing yellow garments, with arms resplendent with discus, conch, mace, and lotus.

children.text: sarvāṅgena mukhādinā sundaro ramyaḥ saumyo 'nuddhataḥ sarvābharaṇenaa kuṇḍalādy-alaṅkāreṇa bhūṣitaḥ | pīta-vāsāḥ pīta-vāsasī yasya saḥ | cakra-śaṅkha-gadā-padmar ujjvalā dīptā bhujā yasya saḥ || KrdC_7.7 ||
children.translated_text: Beautiful — lovely — in all limbs such as the face etc.; gentle (<s>saumya</s>) — not aggressive; adorned with all ornaments such as ear-rings and the like. Wearing yellow garments — one whose garment is yellow. With arms resplendent — shining — with discus, conch, mace, and lotus.
Again, of what kind?
Touching with the tip of his left lotus-foot a vessel from which flows an incessant flood of gem-streams,
Which [foot-tip] steals the beauty of tender sprouts.

children.text: vāma-pādāmbujāgreṇa anārataṃ sarvadā ucchalantī yā ratna-dhārā tasyā oghaḥ pravāho yatra sa cāsau kalasaś ceti karmadhārayaḥ | taṃ spṛśan vāma-pādāmbujāgreṇa | kimbhūtena ? pallava-cchavim muṣṇatā kiśalaya-kāntiṃ corayatā || KrdC_7.8 ||
children.translated_text: With the tip of his left lotus-foot — the stream of gems flowing incessantly — always — that flood — current — which is also a vessel (<s>kalaśa</s>) — a <s>karmadhāraya</s> compound — touching that [vessel] with the tip of his left lotus-foot. Of what kind [is that foot-tip]? One that steals — surpasses — the beauty of tender sprouts.
He states the meditation on the eight chief queens (<s>aṣṭa-mahiṣī</s>) —
<s>Rukmiṇī</s> and <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, on his head, with a stream of heaped gems,
Pouring [from vessels] — stationed at his right and left, from vessels held in their own arms.

children.text: rukmiṇī-satyabhāme dhyeye | kimbhūte ? asya harer mūrdhni śirasi ratna-pravāha-dhārayā siñcantyau | kīdṛśe ? dakṣa-vāma-sthe | atra rukmiṇī dakṣiṇe satyā vāme | kimbhūtayā dhārayā ? sva-hasta-stha-ghaṭodbhavayā || KrdC_7.9 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and <s>Satyabhāmā</s> are to be meditated upon. Of what kind? Pouring upon the head — the crown — of this <s>Hari</s>, with a stream of gem-flood. Of what kind? Stationed at the right and left. Here, <s>Rukmiṇī</s> is on the right, <s>Satyā</s> (<s>Satyabhāmā</s>) on the left. With what kind of stream? Arising from vessels held in their own hands.
<s>Nāgnajitī</s> and <s>Sunandā</s> are also to be meditated upon. Of what kind are they?

children.text: nāgnajitī sunandā ca diśantyā kalaśau tayoḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Nāgnajitī</s> and <s>Sunandā</s>, offering vessels to those two [<s>Rukmiṇī</s> and <s>Satyabhāmā</s>],
Stationed at the right and left of those two are <s>Mitravindā</s> and <s>Sulakṣmaṇā</s>.

children.text: tayo rukmiṇī-satyabhāmayoḥ sthāne ratna-ghaṭau diśantyau dadatyau | kīdṛśe ? dakṣa-vāma-sthe | tathā mitravindā-sulakṣaṇe dakṣiṇa-vāma-sthe dhyeye | kimbhūte ? tābhyāṃ nāgnajitī-sunandābhyāṃ kalaśaṃ diśantībhyāṃ kalaśaṃ dadatyau || KrdC_7.10 ||
children.translated_text: Offering — giving — gem-vessels to those two, <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, in their place. Of what kind? Stationed at the right and left. Likewise, <s>Mitravindā</s> and <s>Sulakṣaṇā</s>, stationed at the right and left, are to be meditated upon. Of what kind? Offering vessels to those two — <s>Nāgnajitī</s> and <s>Sunandā</s> — giving vessels to them.
<s>Jāmbavatī</s> and <s>Suśīlā</s>, drawing up from the gem-river two gem-filled vessels,

children.text: jāmbavatī suśīlā ca diśantyau dakṣa-vāma-ge // Krd_7.11 //
children.translated_text: Offering [them] — stationed at the right and left.

children.text: tathā dakṣa-vāme jāmbavatī-suśīle ca dhyeye | kimbhūte ? ratna-nadyā ratna-pūrṇau ghaṭau samuddhṛtya tayor sulakṣmaṇā-mitravindayor diśantyau || KrdC_7.11 ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, <s>Jāmbavatī</s> and <s>Suśīlā</s>, stationed at the right and left, are to be meditated upon. Of what kind? Drawing up gem-filled vessels from the gem-river and offering them to those two — <s>Sulakṣmaṇā</s> and <s>Mitravindā</s>.
Outside [them], sixteen thousand women all around
Are to be meditated upon, resplendent with vessels [streaming] floods of all kinds of gems.

children.text: tad-bahiḥ ṣoḍaśa-sāhasra-saṅkhyātāḥ priyā dhyeyāḥ | kimbhūtāḥ ? kanakaṃ suvarṇaṃ ratnāni padmādīni teṣām oghaḥ samūhaḥ | tasya dhārāṃ yunaktīti tad-yuk yaḥ kalaśaḥ tena dīptāḥ || KrdC_7.12 ||
children.translated_text: Outside them, sixteen thousand wives are to be meditated upon. Of what kind? Gold — precious gold; gems — rubies and the like; their flood — multitude; the stream thereof; vessels endowed with that — resplendent by those.
And outside them, the eight <s>nidhi</s>s (treasures) are to be meditated upon. Of what kind?

children.text: tad bahiś cāṣṭa-nidhayaḥ pūrayanto dhanair dharām |
children.translated_text: Outside them, the eight <s>nidhi</s>s (treasures), filling the earth with wealth;

children.text: tad-bahir vṛṣṇayaḥ sarve purovac ca surādayaḥ // Krd_7.13 //
children.translated_text: Outside them, all the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>s (the Yādava clan), and the gods and others as before.

children.text: dharāṃ pṛthvīṃ dhanaiḥ pūrayantaḥ tad-bahir vṛṣṇayo yādavā dhyeyāḥ | anantaraṃ purovat dikṣu sthitāḥ surādayo devarṣi-siddha-vidyādhara-gandharva-prabhṛtayo ratnābhiṣekaṃ kurvanto dhyeyāḥ || KrdC_7.13 ||
children.translated_text: Filling the earth — the ground — with wealth; outside them, the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>s — the <s>Yādava</s>s — are to be meditated upon. Thereafter, as before — stationed in the directions — the gods and others — celestials, divine sages, <s>Siddha</s>s, <s>Vidyādhara</s>s, <s>Gandharva</s>s, and so forth — performing the gem-consecration (<s>ratnābhiṣeka</s>) — are to be meditated upon.
Having thus meditated upon the Supreme Self, one should recite the twenty-syllable mantra,
Four <s>lakṣa</s>s (four hundred thousand) [times]; and should offer forty thousand oblations with ghee.

children.text: evaṃ paramātma-rūpaṃ aśarīriṇaṃ dhyātvā viṃsaty-akṣaraṃ mantraṃ catur-lakṣaṃ japet | ājyair ghṛtaiś catvāriṃśat-sahasrakam hunet juhūyāt || KrdC_7.14 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, having meditated upon the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) form — the bodiless one — one should recite the twenty-syllable mantra four <s>lakṣa</s>s (four hundred thousand times). With <s>ājya</s> — ghee — one should offer forty thousand oblations into the fire.
He extracts the twenty-syllable mantra —
The eighteen-syllable [mantra], preceded by <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Śrī</s> [seed-syllables], becomes of twenty syllables;

children.text: matreṇānena sadṛśo manur nahi jagat traye // Krd_7.15 //
children.translated_text: No mantra in the three worlds is equal to this mantra.

children.text: śaktir bhuvaneśvarī-bījaṃ śrīḥ śrī-bījaṃ etad-bīja-dvaya-pūrvakaḥ pūrvoktāṣṭādaśākṣara-mantra eva viṃśaty-akṣaro bhavatīty arthaḥ | anena mantreṇa sadṛśo mantra jagat-traye nāsti || KrdC_7.15 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śakti</s> is the <s>Bhuvaneśvarī-bīja</s> (seed-syllable of <s>Bhuvaneśvarī</s>); <s>Śrī</s> is the <s>Śrī-bīja</s> (seed-syllable of <s>Śrī</s>). The previously mentioned eighteen-syllable mantra, preceded by these two seed-syllables, becomes a twenty-syllable mantra — this is the meaning. There is no mantra in the three worlds equal to this mantra.
He shows the <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer) and other [attributes] —

children.text: ṛṣir brahmā ca gāyatrī-cchandaḥ kṛṣṇas tu devatā |
children.translated_text: The <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer) is <s>Brahmā</s>, the meter (<s>chandas</s>) is <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and the deity is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;
The designation of seed-syllable (<s>bīja</s>), power (<s>śakti</s>), and so forth for this [mantra] is as previously stated.

children.text: asya mantrasya bīja-śakty-ādi-kalpanā pūrvoktavat daśākṣaravat tathā ca daśākṣarasya yad bījādikaṃ tad asyāpīty arthaḥ || KrdC_7.16 ||
children.translated_text: The designation of seed-syllable, power, and so forth for this mantra is as previously stated — as for the ten-syllable [mantra]. Thus, whatever seed-syllable etc. belongs to the ten-syllable [mantra], that also belongs to this one — this is the meaning.
He states the method of worship —
The ritual procedure (<s>kalpa</s>) as taught by <s>Sanatkumāra</s> for this mantra is now described;
having performed <s>pīṭha-nyāsa</s> (seat-placement) and the like, in the previously stated sequence, the wise one —

children.text: asya mantrasya sanat-kumāra-kathitaḥ pūjā-prakāraḥ samprati mayā kathyate | pūrvokta-kramataḥ daśākṣarokta-prakāreṇa pīṭha-nyāsa-prāṇāyāmādikaṃ kṛtvā || KrdC_7.17 ||
children.translated_text: The method of worship for this mantra, as taught by <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, is now described by me. In the previously stated sequence — in the manner described for the ten-syllable [mantra] — having performed <s>pīṭha-nyāsa</s>, <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, and the like —
On the finger-tips and palms of both hands, one should place the six limbs (<s>aṅga-ṣaṭka</s>);

children.text: mantreṇa vyāpakaṃ kṛtvā mātṛkāṃ manu-sampuṭām // Krd_7.18 //
children.translated_text: having performed the pervading [placement] (<s>vyāpaka</s>) with the mantra, the <s>mātṛkā</s> (alphabet), enclosed in the mantra —
By the path of dissolution and creation, one should place the ten <s>tattva</s>s (principles);

children.text: punaś ca vyāpakaṃ kṛtvā mantra-varṇās tanau nyaset // Krd_7.19 //
children.translated_text: and again, having performed the pervading [placement], one should place the mantra-syllables upon the body.

children.text: ubhaya-karāṅguliṣu ubhaya-kara-taleṣu ca ṣaḍ-aṅgāni kramān nyaset | mantreṇeti viṃśaty akṣara-mantreṇa vyāpakaṃ sarvatanau nyāsaṃ kṛtvā mātṛkāṃ mātṛkā-nyāsaṃ manu-sampuṭāṃ viṃśaty-akṣara-puṭita-pratyakṣarāṃ pūrvokta-mātṛkā-sthāneṣu vinyaset | prayogaś ca-hrīṃ aṃ hrīṃ nama ity ādiḥ | evaṃ bha-paryantaṃ dvir-āvṛttiḥ | tato hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ | klīṃ krīṃ paṃ klīṃ krīṃ nama ity ādiḥ | saṃhāra-sṛṣṭi-mārgeṇa daśa-tattvāni mahī-salila-prabhṛtīni vinyaset | punar api viṃśaty-akṣara-mantreṇa vyāpaka-nyāsaṃ kṛtvā viṃśati-mantrākṣarāṇi tanau sva-śarīre nyaset || KrdC_7.19 ||
children.translated_text: On the fingers of both hands and on the palms of both hands, one should place the six limbs (<s>ṣaḍ-aṅga</s>) in sequence. 'With the mantra' — with the twenty-syllable mantra, having performed the pervading placement (<s>vyāpaka-nyāsa</s>) upon the entire body; the <s>mātṛkā</s> — the <s>mātṛkā-nyāsa</s> (alphabet placement), enclosed in the mantra — with each letter enclosed in the twenty-syllable [mantra] — one should place at the previously described <s>mātṛkā</s>-stations. The practical application is: '<s>hrīṃ aṃ hrīṃ namaḥ</s>' and so forth. Thus, up to <s>bha</s>, [it is performed] twice. Then: '<s>hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ namaḥ</s>; <s>klīṃ krīṃ paṃ klīṃ krīṃ namaḥ</s>' and so forth. By the path of dissolution and creation, one should place the ten <s>tattva</s>s — earth (<s>mahī</s>), water (<s>salila</s>), and so forth. Again, having performed the pervading placement with the twenty-syllable mantra, one should place the twenty mantra-syllables upon the body — upon one's own body.
He states the stations for syllable-placement —

children.text: mūrdhni bhāle bhruvor madhye netrayoḥ karṇayor nasoḥ |
children.translated_text: On the crown (<s>mūrdhan</s>), on the forehead (<s>bhāla</s>), between the brows, on the eyes, on the ears, on the nose,

children.text: ānane cibuke kaṇṭhe dor-mūle hṛdi tanduke // Krd_7.20 //
children.translated_text: on the face, on the chin, on the throat, at the base of the arms, on the heart, on the stomach (<s>tanduka</s>),

children.text: nābhau liṅge tathādhāre kaṭyor jānvoś ca jaṅghayoḥ |
children.translated_text: on the navel, on the genitals (<s>liṅga</s>), likewise on the base (<s>ādhāra</s>), on the hips, on the knees, on the calves,

children.text: gulphayoḥ pādayor nyaset sṛṣṭir eṣā samīritā // Krd_7.21 //
children.translated_text: on the ankles, on the feet — one should place [them]. This is called the creation [order] (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>).

children.text: mastake bhāle lalāṭe bhrū-madhye ity ādāv ekaikam akṣaraṃ nyaset | ādhāre liṅgādhas trikoṇa-sthāne eṣa sṛṣṭi-nyāsa-prakāra uktaḥ || KrdC_7.21 ||
children.translated_text: On the crown (<s>mastaka</s>), on the forehead (<s>bhāla</s>), on the brow-center, and so forth — one should place one syllable at each [station]. The <s>ādhāra</s> is the triangular region below the genitals. This method of creation-placement (<s>sṛṣṭi-nyāsa</s>) has been stated.
The maintenance [order] (<s>sthiti</s>) begins from the heart and onwards; the withdrawal [order] (<s>saṃhṛti</s>) begins from the feet and onwards.
Having performed thus five times, ending with the maintenance [order], the body-cage (<s>mūrti-pañjara</s>);

children.text: sṛṣṭi-sthitī ca vinyasya ṣaḍ-aṅga-nyāsam ācaret // Krd_7.22 //
children.translated_text: having placed [in] creation and maintenance [orders], one should perform the six-limb placement (<s>ṣaḍ-aṅga-nyāsa</s>).

children.text: hṛd-ādikāṃsāṃ tā sthitiḥ hṛdayam ārabhyāṃsa-paryanta-nyāsaḥ sthitiḥ saṃhṛtiś caraṇādikāpādāvārabhyamūrdhānta-nyāsaḥ vidhāyeti | evaṃ pañca-vārān sthity-antaṃ nyāsaṃ kṛtvā iti gṛhasthābhiprāyeṇa tathā pūrvokta-murti-pañjara-nyāsaṃ kṛtvā punaḥ sṛṣṭi-sthitī vinyasya sṛṣṭi-sthiti-prakāreṇa mantra-varṇān vinyasya ṣaḍ-aṅga-nyāsam ācaret || KrdC_7.22 ||
children.translated_text: Beginning from the heart up to the shoulders — that is the maintenance (<s>sthiti</s>) [placement]; the withdrawal (<s>saṃhṛti</s>) is the placement beginning from the feet up to the crown. 'Having performed' — thus, having done the placement five times ending with the maintenance [order] — this is from the perspective of a householder (<s>gṛhastha</s>). Likewise, having performed the previously described body-cage placement (<s>mūrti-pañjara-nyāsa</s>), again, having placed in the creation and maintenance orders — having placed the mantra-syllables in the creation and maintenance manner — one should perform the six-limb placement.
He shows the six limbs —
With the syllables [corresponding to the numbers] of <s>guṇa</s>s (3), fires (3), <s>Veda</s>s (4), senses (<s>karaṇa</s>, 4), senses (4 again), and eyes (2) of the mantra,

children.text: mudrāṃ baddhvā kirīṭākhyāṃ dig-bandhaṃ pūrvavac caret |
children.translated_text: having formed the <s>mudrā</s> called <s>kirīṭa</s> (crown), one should perform the binding of directions (<s>dig-bandha</s>) as before;
having meditated and recited, one should worship upon the body, preceded by the body-cage [placement].

children.text: manor mantrasya guṇās trayaḥ agnayas trayaḥ vedāś catvāraḥ karaṇam antaḥ-karaṇa-catuṣṭayaṃ | punaḥ karaṇa-catuṣṭayam akṣi-dvayam etair akṣarair mantra-sambhavaiḥ ṣaḍ-aṅgāni kāryāṇīty arthaḥ | mudrām iti kirīṭākhyāṃ kirīṭābhidhāṃ baddhvā kṛtvā kirīṭādyām iti pāṭhe kaustubha-śrīvatsa-mudrayoḥ parigrahaḥ pūrvavad astra-mantreṇa dig-bandhanaṃ kuryāt |
children.translated_text: Of the mantra: the <s>guṇa</s>s are three; the fires are three; the <s>Veda</s>s are four; <s>karaṇa</s> is the fourfold inner organ (<s>antaḥ-karaṇa-catuṣṭaya</s>); again, [another] set of four senses; and two eyes — with these syllables, produced from the mantra, the six limbs should be constructed — this is the meaning. The <s>mudrā</s> — called <s>kirīṭa</s> (crown) — having formed, having made it. In the reading '<s>kirīṭādyām</s>' (beginning with the crown), the <s>Kaustubha</s> and <s>Śrīvatsa</s> <s>mudrā</s>s are also included. As before — with the weapon-mantra (<s>astra-mantra</s>) — one should perform the binding of the directions.

children.text: ātma-pūjām āha-dhyātveti | pūrvoditaṃ dhyānaṃ kṛtvā aṣṭottara-śataṃ ca japtvā mūrti-pañjara-pūrvakam dehe pūjayet tathācābhyantare prathamaṃ parameśvarā-rādhanaṃ tad anu mūrti-pañjarasya tad anu sṛṣṭi-sthiti-nyāsaṃ tad anu ṣaḍ-aṅgasyeti ||23||
children.translated_text: He states the self-worship (<s>ātma-pūjā</s>) — with 'having meditated.' Having performed the previously described meditation, and having recited one hundred and eight [times], one should worship upon the body, preceded by the body-cage [placement]. And the [order of] internal [worship] is: first, the worship of the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>); after that, [the placement of] the body-cage; after that, the creation-maintenance placement; after that, the six-limb [placement].
He states the method of external worship —

children.text: athavā hye 'rcayed viṣṇuṃ tad-arthaṃ yantram ucyate |
children.translated_text: Or alternatively, one should worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> externally; for that purpose, the <s>yantra</s> (diagram) is described;
having smeared the ground with cow-dung, one should place a seat (<s>pīṭha</s>) there.

children.text: athātma-pūjānantaraṃ bāhye viṣṇuṃ pūjayet | tat-pūjārthaṃ pūjā-sthānam ucyate | gomaya-jalena pṛthivīm upalipya tatra lipta-sthāne pīṭhaṃ pūjādhāra-priyaṃ pātraṃ sthāpayet || KrdC_7.24 ||
children.translated_text: Then, after self-worship, one should worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> externally. The place of worship for that purpose is described. Having smeared the earth with cow-dung water, there — at the smeared place — one should place a seat (<s>pīṭha</s>) — a suitable vessel for worship.
Having anointed [it] with sandalwood paste, one should draw an eight-petalled lotus;

children.text: karṇikāyāṃ tu ṣaṭ-koṇaṃ sa-sādhyaṃ tatra manmatham // Krd_7.25 //
children.translated_text: on the pericarp, a hexagram (<s>ṣaṭ-koṇa</s>), with the love-seed (<s>Manmatha</s> [seed-syllable]), together with the object to be accomplished.

children.text: anantaraṃ tat-pīṭhaṃ candana-paṅkena vilipya tatrāṣṭa-dala-padmaṃ vilikhya karṇikāyāṃ padmaṃ vilikhya madhya-sthāne ṣaṭ-koṇa-puṭitaṃ vahni-pura-dvayaṃ likhet | tatra ṣaṭ-koṇa-madhye sa-sādhyaṃ karma-sahitaṃ sādhya-nāma-sahitaṃ manmathaṃ kāma-bījaṃ likhet | sādhya-grahaṇāt dhāraṇārtham apy etad boddhavyam iti tripāṭhinaḥ || KrdC_7.25 ||
children.translated_text: Then, having anointed that seat with sandalwood paste, having drawn an eight-petalled lotus thereon, having drawn a [smaller] lotus on the pericarp, one should draw at the center a pair of fire-houses (<s>vahni-pura</s>) forming a hexagram. There, in the middle of the hexagram, together with the object to be accomplished — accompanied by the desired ritual objective, together with the name of the person to be accomplished — one should write the <s>Manmatha</s> [syllable], the love-seed (<s>kāma-bīja</s>). 'Since the mention of <s>sādhya</s> (object of accomplishment) implies that this is also to be understood for the purpose of wearing [as an amulet]' — thus [say] the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s.

children.text: śiṣṭais taṃ saptadaśabhir akṣarair veṣṭayet smaram |
children.translated_text: With the remaining seventeen syllables, one should surround the love-[seed] (<s>Smara</s>);
in the east, south-west, and north-west corners, [place] <s>Śrī</s> [seed-syllable]; in the remaining [corners], <s>Saṃvid</s> [seed-syllable].

children.text: śiṣṭaiḥ sapta saptadaśabhir akṣarais taṃ kāma-bījaṃ veṣṭayet | ṣaṭ-koṇasya pūrva-nairṛti-vāyavya-koṇeṣu śriyaṃ śrī-bīja-trayaṃ likhet | śiṣṭeṣu triṣu koṇeṣu paścimeśānāgni-koṇeṣu saṃvidam bhuvaneśvarī-bījaṃ vilikhet || KrdC_7.26 ||
children.translated_text: With the remaining seven — seventeen — syllables, one should surround that love-seed (<s>kāma-bīja</s>). In the east, south-west (<s>Nairṛti</s>), and north-west (<s>Vāyavya</s>) corners of the hexagram, one should write <s>Śrī</s> — a trio of <s>Śrī-bīja</s>s. In the remaining three corners — the west, north-east (<s>Īśāna</s>), and south-east (<s>Āgneya</s>) — one should write <s>Saṃvid</s> — the <s>Bhuvaneśvarī-bīja</s>.

children.text: ṣaḍ-akṣaraṃ sandhiṣu ca keśareṣu triśas triśaḥ |
children.translated_text: The six syllables at the junctions, and on the filaments, in groups of three;
one should write the <s>Kāma-Gāyatrī</s>; on the eight petals, the garland-mantra (<s>mālā-mantra</s>).
Having written [them] in groups of six, one should surround the exterior with the <s>mātṛkā</s>-letters (alphabet);

children.text: bhū-bimbaṃ ca likhed bāhye śrī-māye dig-vidikṣv api // Krd_7.28 //
children.translated_text: and one should draw the earth-figure (<s>bhū-bimba</s>) on the outside, and <s>Śrī</s> and <s>Māyā</s> [seed-syllables] in the cardinal and intermediate directions.

children.text: sandhiṣu ṣaṭ-koṇa-sandhiṣu ṣaḍ-akṣaraṃ kāma-bīja-pūrvaka-kṛṣṇāya nama iti ṣaḍ-akṣaraṃ likhet | keśara-sthāne kāma-gāyatrīṃ vakṣyamāṇāṃ triśo 'kṣara-trayaṃ kṛtvā vilikhet | patrāṣṭake vakṣyamāṇāṃ mālā-mantraṃ ṣaḍśaḥ ṣaḍ-akṣarāṇi kṛtvā vilikhya padma-bāhye mātṛkākṣarair veṣṭayet | mātṛkāveṣṭana-bāhya eva vakṣyamāṇa-svarūpaṃ bhū-bimbaṃ ca likhet | bhū-bimba-dig-vidikṣu śrī-māye dikṣu śrī-bījaṃ koṇeṣu bhuvaneśvarī-bījaṃ likhed ity arthaḥ || KrdC_7.28 ||
children.translated_text: At the junctions — at the junctions of the hexagram — the six syllables: '<s>kāma-bīja</s>-preceded <s>Kṛṣṇāya namaḥ</s>' — these six syllables should be written. At the filament-stations, the <s>Kāma-Gāyatrī</s> — about to be described — should be written in groups of three syllables. On the eight petals, the garland-mantra — about to be described — in groups of six syllables, having written [them], on the outside of the lotus, one should surround with the <s>mātṛkā</s>-letters (alphabet). On the outside of the <s>mātṛkā</s>-enclosure itself, one should draw the earth-figure (<s>bhū-bimba</s>) — about to be described in form. In the cardinal directions of the earth-figure, one should write the <s>Śrī</s>-[seed syllable]; in the intermediate directions, the <s>Bhuvaneśvarī-bīja</s> (<s>Māyā</s>) — this is the meaning.
Having inscribed this <s>yantra</s> on plates of gold and the like, as before,

children.text: sādhitaṃ dhārayed yo vai so 'rcyeta tradaśair api // Krd_7.29 //
children.translated_text: whoever wears it duly consecrated — he is worshipped even by the gods.

children.text: etad yantraṃ pūjāyām apy upayuktaṃ yo dhārayet sa devair api pūjyate | kiṃ kṛtvā ? suvarṇa-rajata-tāmrādi-paṭṭeṣu yathā-kathita-dravyeṇālikhya pūrvavad yaḥ pūjāsu | yad vā, pūrva-mantravat kṛta-prāṇa-pratiṣṭhādi-kriyam | kīdṛśam ? sādhitaṃ yathā-kathita-prakāreṇa sampādita-prajaptaṃ ca || KrdC_7.29 ||
children.translated_text: This <s>yantra</s>, useful also in worship — whoever wears it is worshipped even by the gods. Having done what? Having inscribed it with the prescribed materials on plates of gold, silver, copper, and the like, as before — in all worship [rites]. Or alternatively, [as before means] having performed <s>prāṇa-pratiṣṭhā</s> (establishment of life-breath) and other rites as for the previous mantra. Of what kind? Consecrated (<s>sādhita</s>) — properly prepared and recited in the prescribed manner.
He extracts the <s>Kāma-Gāyatrī</s> —
The <s>Gāyatrī</s> would be: '<s>Kāmadeva</s>' and '<s>Puṣpabāṇa</s>' (Flower-arrowed), ending in the dative case;
joined with '<s>vidmahe</s>' and '<s>dhīmahi</s>'; then 'may <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless One) inspire us (<s>pracodayāt</s>).'
One should recite this, which enchants all people, at the beginning of the recitation of the <s>Gopāla</s> mantras.

children.text: kāma-deva-puṣpa-bāṇa-śabdau krameṇa caturthy-antau | kimbhūtau ? vidmahe-dhīmahi-śabda-sahitau | tad-anu tan no 'naṅgaḥ pracodayād iti svarūpam | evaṃ sati kāma-gāyatrī syād bhavati | japyād iti gopāla-mantrāṇāṃ japādau japopakrame etāṃ kāma-gāyatrīṃ japyāt | yata iyaṃ jana-rañjanīṃ vaśyakarīm ity arthaḥ || KrdC_7.30 ||
children.translated_text: The words '<s>Kāmadeva</s>' and '<s>Puṣpabāṇa</s>' are in sequence in the dative case. Of what kind? Accompanied by the words '<s>vidmahe</s>' and '<s>dhīmahi</s>.' After that, the form is 'may <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless One) inspire us (<s>tan no 'naṅgaḥ pracodayāt</s>).' This being so, it constitutes the <s>Kāma-Gāyatrī</s>. 'One should recite' — at the commencement of the recitation of the <s>Gopāla</s>-mantras, one should recite this <s>Kāma-Gāyatrī</s>. Because this is <s>jana-rañjanī</s> — capable of enchanting and subjugating all people — this is the meaning.
He extracts the garland-mantra (<s>mālā-mantra</s>) — beginning with '<s>naty-anta</s>' etc.
Ending with salutation (<s>naty-ante</s>), '<s>Kāmadevāya</s>' (to the Love-god), ending in the dative, '<s>sarva-jana-priya</s>' (dear to all people);

children.text: uktvā sarva-janānte tu saṃmohana-padaṃ tathā // Krd_7.31 //
children.translated_text: having uttered [this], after '<s>sarva-jana</s>' (of all people), the word '<s>saṃmohana</s>' (enchantment) likewise;

children.text: jvala jvala prajvaleti prokto sarva-janasya ca |
children.translated_text: '<s>jvala jvala prajvala</s>' (blaze, blaze, blaze forth) — thus proclaimed; and of all people,

children.text: hṛdayaṃ ca mama brūyāt vaśaṃ kuru-yugaṃ śiraḥ |
children.translated_text: 'the heart' (<s>hṛdaya</s>), and 'mine' (<s>mama</s>), one should say; 'bring under control' (<s>vaśaṃ kuru</s>), paired; '<s>śiraḥ</s>' (head, i.e., <s>svāhā</s>);
this <s>Madana</s>-mantra (Love-god's mantra) is proclaimed with forty-eight syllables.

children.text: namaḥ-śabdānte kāma-devāyeti svarūpaṃ tad-anu caturthy-ante sarva-jana-priya-śabdam uccārya tad-anu sarva-jana-śabdam uktvā saṃmohana-padaṃ vadet | tad-anu jvala jvala prajvaleti svarūpam uktvā sarva-janasya hṛdayaṃ mameti svarūpam uktvā vaśam iti svarūpam uktvā kuru kuru iti svarūpam uktvā śiraḥ svāhā iti vadet | evaṃ ca sati aṣṭa-catvāriṃśad akṣarakair madana-mantraḥ || KrdC_7.31-32 ||
children.translated_text: After the word '<s>namaḥ</s>' (salutation), '<s>Kāmadevāya</s>' is the form; after that, in the dative case, having uttered the word '<s>sarva-jana-priya</s>' (dear to all people); after that, having spoken the word '<s>sarva-jana</s>' (all people), one should say the word '<s>saṃmohana</s>' (enchantment). After that, having uttered the form '<s>jvala jvala prajvala</s>' (blaze, blaze, blaze forth); having uttered the form '<s>sarva-janasya hṛdayaṃ mama</s>' (the heart of all people [bring to] me); having uttered the form '<s>vaśam</s>' (under control); having uttered the form '<s>kuru kuru</s>' (do, do); one should say '<s>śiraḥ svāhā</s>' (head, <s>svāhā</s>). Thus, the <s>Madana</s>-mantra consists of forty-eight syllables.
He shows the application (<s>viniyoga</s>) —
At the beginning of recitation, preceded by the love-seed (<s>māra-bīja</s>), it has the power to subjugate the three worlds;
the earth-house (<s>bhū-gṛha</s>) should be square, adorned with thunderbolts (<s>vajra</s>) at the corners.

children.text: yatra yathodbhūta eva japa-pūjā-homādau tu yadi kāma-bījādyo bhavati tadā jagat-traya-vaśīkaraṇa-kṣamaḥ yadāya mantraḥ svatantreṇa japyate tadeti tripāṭhinaḥ | bhū-gṛham uddharati-bhū-gṛham iti | koṇa-saṃlagnāṣṭa-vajrālaṅkṛta-caturasraṃ koṇa-catuṣṭaya-sahitaṃ bhū-vilambam iti pāṭho vā || KrdC_7.33 ||
children.translated_text: Wherever and whenever in recitation, worship, fire-offering, and the like, if [the mantra] is preceded by the love-seed (<s>kāma-bīja</s>), then it becomes capable of subjugating the three worlds. 'When this mantra is recited independently' — thus [say] the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s. He extracts the earth-house (<s>bhū-gṛha</s>) — with '<s>bhū-gṛha</s>.' A square adorned with eight thunderbolts attached to the corners — endowed with four corners. Or the reading is '<s>bhū-vilamba</s>' (earth-pendant).
He states the method of worship on the <s>yantra</s> —
Having worshipped the seat (<s>pīṭha</s>) as before, having visualized the human form (<s>pauruṣī mūrti</s>);
having invoked <s>Acyuta</s> (the Imperishable) there, having made [him] complete (<s>sakalīkṛtya</s>), one should worship with devotion.

children.text: pūrvavad daśākṣaravat gurvāpīṭha-pūjāntam abhyarcya tatra pauruṣīṃ puruṣākṛtiṃ mūrtiṃ pārameśvarīṃ vicintya tatra mūrtāv acyutam āvāhya sakalīkṛtya bhaktyā pūjayet | suṣumṇā pravāha-nāḍyā puṣpa-yuktam uttāna-pāṇī-hṛdaya-stha-mūrtes tejaḥ saṃyojya tejo devatā brahma-randhreṇa deva-śarīra-gataṃ vicintya sva-sva-mudrayā bāhye saṃsthāpya sannidhāpya saṇniruddhyāvaguṇṭhya devatāṅge ṣaḍ-aṅga-nyāsaṃ kṛtvā ṣoḍaśopacāraiḥ sampūjayed ity arthaḥ || KrdC_7.34 ||
children.translated_text: As before — as for the ten-syllable [mantra] — having worshipped up to and including the <s>guru</s>-seat worship; there, having visualized the human form (<s>pauruṣī</s>) — the figure of the Supreme Lord in human shape; having invoked <s>Acyuta</s> into that form, having made [him] complete, one should worship with devotion. [The procedure is:] Through the <s>suṣumṇā</s> channel — the flow-channel — with palms facing upward holding flowers, uniting the radiance of the deity dwelling in the heart with the radiance [in the image]; visualizing the deity's radiance as having entered the divine body through the <s>brahma-randhra</s> (crown aperture); establishing and making [the deity] present externally with the respective <s>mudrā</s>s; confining and veiling [the deity]; having performed the six-limb placement (<s>ṣaḍ-aṅga-nyāsa</s>) upon the deity's body — one should worship with the sixteen <s>upacāra</s>s (offerings) — this is the meaning.
Beginning with the seat (<s>āsana</s>) and ending with ornaments (<s>bhūṣaṇa</s>), one should again worship in the sequence of <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement).

children.text: sṛṣṭi-sthitī ṣaḍ-aṅgaṃ ca kirīṭaṃ kuṇḍala-dvayam // Krd_7.35 //
children.translated_text: <s>Sṛṣṭi</s> (creation) and <s>sthiti</s> (maintenance), the six limbs (<s>ṣaḍ-aṅga</s>), the crown (<s>kirīṭa</s>), and the pair of earrings;
The discus (<s>cakra</s>), conch (<s>śaṅkha</s>), mace (<s>gadā</s>), lotus (<s>padma</s>), garland (<s>mālā</s>), <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, and <s>Kaustubha</s>;
Having worshipped these with sandal-paste, unbroken rice-grains, and flowers, with the <s>mūla</s> (root mantra), as before.

children.text: āsanādi vibhūṣāntaṃ yathā syād evaṃ pūjayet āsanam ārabhya bhūṣāntair upacāraiḥ pūjayed ity arthaḥ | punar nyāsa-kramāt sṛṣṭy-ādīn yajet | prathamaṃ sṛṣṭy-ādīnāṃ nyāsaṃ vidhāya tatas tān pūjayet | athavā nyāsa-kramād yathā teṣāṃ nyāsaḥ kṛtas tena krameṇety arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: From the seat (<s>āsana</s>) to the ornaments — one should worship in this manner: beginning from the seat, one should worship with the <s>upacāra</s>s (offerings) ending with ornaments — this is the meaning. Again, following the sequence of <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement), one should worship the <s>sṛṣṭi</s> and the like. First, having performed the <s>nyāsa</s> of <s>sṛṣṭi</s> and the others, then one should worship them. Alternatively, 'following the sequence of <s>nyāsa</s>' means in the same order in which their <s>nyāsa</s> was performed — this is the meaning.

children.text: gandhākṣateti | akṣatā yavā gandhākṣata-puṣpaiś ca pūrvavat mūla-mantreṇa kṛṣṇaṃ pūjayitvā saptāvṛtīḥ sampūjayed ity arthaḥ || KrdC_7.36 ||
children.translated_text: With '<s>gandhākṣata</s>' etc.: <s>akṣata</s> means barley grains — with sandal-paste, unbroken grains, and flowers, as before, having worshipped <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with the root mantra, one should then worship the seven enclosures (<s>āvṛti</s>s) — this is the meaning.
He states the enclosures —
First, one should worship the limbs (<s>aṅga</s>s) at the corners of the pair of fire-city [triangles];

children.text: sahṛc-chiraḥ śikhā-varma-netram astram iti kramāt // Krd_7.37 //
children.translated_text: Heart (<s>hṛd</s>), head (<s>śiras</s>), topknot (<s>śikhā</s>), armor (<s>varma</s>), eye (<s>netra</s>), and weapon (<s>astra</s>), in sequence.

children.text: prathamaṃ vahni-pura-yugala-sambandhi-ṣaṭ-koṇeṣu āgneya-koṇam ārabhya ṣaḍ-aṅgāni pūjayed ity arthaḥ | aṅgāny āha-sahṛd iti | saha-hṛd āvartata iti sahṛt hṛdayaṃ śiraḥ śikhā-varma-kavacaṃ netram astraṃ ceti prathamāvaraṇam || KrdC_7.37 ||
children.translated_text: First, at the six corners associated with the pair of fire-city triangles, beginning from the southeast corner, one should worship the six limbs — this is the meaning. He states the limbs with '<s>sahṛd</s>' etc.: <s>sahṛt</s> — '<s>saha-hṛd āvartate</s>' — means the heart; head; topknot; armor (<s>kavaca</s>); eye; and weapon — this constitutes the first enclosure.
He states the second enclosure with '<s>Vāsudeva</s>' —
<s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, <s>Pradyumna</s>, and <s>Aniruddha</s>;

children.text: agny-ādi-dala-mūleṣu śāntiḥ śrīś ca sarasvatī // Krd_7.38 //
children.translated_text: At the bases of the petals beginning with the fire[-direction], <s>Śānti</s> (Peace), <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), and <s>Sarasvatī</s>;

children.text: ratiś ca dig-daleṣv arcyās tato 'ṣtau mahiṣīr yajet |
children.translated_text: <s>Rati</s> (Love) — these should be worshipped at the directional petals; then one should worship the eight chief queens;

children.text: rukmiṇy-ādyā dakṣa-savye kramāt patrāgrakeṣu ca // Krd_7.39 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and the others, at the right and left in sequence, and at the tips of the petals.

children.text: agny-ādi-koṇa-dala-mūleṣu keśara-sthāneṣu vāsudevādayaḥ pūjyās tathaiva pūrvādi-catur-dikṣu dala-mūleṣu śānty-ādayaḥ pūjyā ity arthaḥ | tṛtīyāvaraṇam āha-tato 'ṣṭāv iti | tad-anantaram aṣṭau mahiṣyaḥ pūjyā ity arthaḥ | tā hi rukmiṇy-ādyā iti | pūjā-sthānam āha-dakṣa-savye iti | parameśvarasya dakṣiṇa-bhāge catasraḥ vāma-bhāge catasraḥ krameṇa pūjyā ity arthaḥ || KrdC_7.38-39 ||
children.translated_text: At the bases of the corner-petals beginning with fire (southeast) — at the filament positions — <s>Vāsudeva</s> and the others should be worshipped; likewise, at the petal-bases of the four cardinal directions beginning with the east, <s>Śānti</s> and the others should be worshipped — this is the meaning. He states the third enclosure with 'then the eight': thereafter, the eight chief queens should be worshipped — this is the meaning. And they are <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and the others. He states the place of worship with '<s>dakṣa-savye</s>': on the right side of the Supreme Lord, four [queens], and on the left side, four — to be worshipped in sequence — this is the meaning.
He states the fourth enclosure with '<s>tataḥ</s>' —
Then, the sixteen thousand [wives] — one should worship [them] all at once as beloved ones;
The <s>Indranīla</s>, <s>Mukunda</s>, and other [treasures], <s>Makara</s>, <s>Anaṅga</s>, <s>Kacchapa</s>,

children.text: padma-śaṅkhādikāṃś cāpi nidhīn aṣṭau kramād yajet |
children.translated_text: <s>Padma</s>, <s>Śaṅkha</s>, and the other <s>nidhi</s>s (treasures) — eight, in sequence, one should worship;

children.text: tad bahiś cendra-vajrād ye āvṛtī samprapūjayet // Krd_7.41 //
children.translated_text: And beyond that, [the enclosures of] <s>Indra</s>, the thunderbolt, and the rest — one should duly worship the [remaining] enclosures.

children.text: pūrvādi-dalāgreṣu ṣoḍaśa-sahasraṃ priyāḥ deva-patnīḥ sakṛd eva eka-krameṇaivārcayet | pañcamam āvaraṇam āha-indranīlādyān aṣṭau nidhīn pūrvādi-krameṇa pūjayet | atrendrādi-śabdānantaraṃ pratyekaṃ caturthy-antaṃ nidhi-padaṃ deyam | prayogaś ca-oṃ indra-nidhaye namaḥ ity ādiḥ | ṣaṣṭha-saptamāvaraṇa-dvayam āha-tad bahir iti | tad-bāhye indrādikaṃ vajrādikaṃ ca pūjayet || KrdC_7.40-41 ||
children.translated_text: At the petal-tips beginning with the east, the sixteen thousand beloved wives — the consorts of the Lord — should all be worshipped at once, in a single sequence. He states the fifth enclosure with '<s>Indranīla</s> and others': the eight <s>nidhi</s>s (treasures) should be worshipped in the sequence beginning with the east. Here, after each word such as '<s>Indra</s>' etc., the word '<s>nidhi</s>' in the dative case should be supplied. The application is: 'Oṃ homage to the <s>Indra-nidhi</s>' and so forth. He states the sixth and seventh enclosure-pair with 'beyond that': beyond that, one should worship <s>Indra</s> and others, and the thunderbolt and the others.
Having shown the enclosures, he shows the <s>naivedya</s> (food-offering) —
Thus, having worshipped <s>Acyuta</s> (the Imperishable One), surrounded by seven enclosures, with devotion,
One should gratify [him] with <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice) mixed with curds, sugar, and ghee.

children.text: ity anena prakāreṇa saptāvaraṇa-veṣṭitaṃ kṛṣṇam ādara-pūrvakaṃ sampūjya dadhi-śarkarā-ghṛta-sahitena pāyasena prīṇayed ity arthaḥ || KrdC_7.42 ||
children.translated_text: In this manner, having worshipped <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — encircled by seven enclosures — with devotion, one should gratify [him] with <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice) combined with curds, sugar, and ghee — this is the meaning.

children.text: rājopacāraṃ dattvātha stutvā natvā ca keśavam |
children.translated_text: Having offered royal honors (<s>rājopacāra</s>), then, having praised and bowed to <s>Keśava</s>,
One should dismiss [him] into one's own heart, together with the retinue of attendants.

children.text: chatra-cāmarādīni dattvā athānantaraṃ stavaṃ kṛtvā aṣṭāṅga-pañcāṅgānyatareṇa praṇamya parivāra-gaṇaiḥ saha keśavaṃ hṛdaye udvāsayet uttolya sthāpayet || KrdC_7.43 ||
children.translated_text: Having offered the royal honors — parasol, fly-whisk, and the like — thereafter, having offered praise, having prostrated with either the eightfold or fivefold [prostration], together with the retinue of attendants, one should dismiss <s>Keśava</s> — lift [him] up and establish [him] — in the heart.
Having offered oneself and worshipped [oneself], becoming one with him, one should recite the mantra;
The gem-consecration (<s>ratnābhiṣeka</s>) meditation-worship is said to be associated with the twenty-syllable [mantra].
Whoever devotes himself to this mantra through recitation, <s>homa</s> (fire-offering), worship, and meditation —

children.text: tad veśma pūryate ratnaiḥ svarṇa-dhānyair anāratam // Krd_7.45 //
children.translated_text: His house is constantly filled with gems, gold, and grains.

children.text: nyastvā pūjā pūrvoktaṃ sṛṣṭy-ādi-nyāsaṃ kṛtvā ātma-pūjāṃ vidhāya tan-mayaḥ pūjya-deva-svarūpo bhūtvā pūjāṅga-mantraṃ japet | parkṛtam upasaṃharati-ratneti | dhyānaṃ ca ijyā ca pūjā ca ity arthaḥ | tathā ca yasyāṃ pūjāyāṃ kṛṣṇasya ratnābhiṣeka-dhyānaṃ tatra kṛṣṇasya viṃśaty-akṣaroktā pūjeyam uktā | phalaṃ darśayati-japeti | japādibhir yo amuṃ mantraṃ sevate tasya gṛhaṃ padma-rāgādibhiḥ ratnaiḥ kāñcanair dhānyaiś cānāratam anavarataṃ pūryate || KrdC_7.44-45 ||
children.translated_text: Having offered — having performed the previously described placement of <s>sṛṣṭi</s> and the like — having performed self-worship, becoming one with the deity to be worshipped — taking on the form of the deity — one should recite the mantra associated with worship. He summarizes what was discussed with '<s>ratna</s>' etc.: meditation and worship — this is the meaning. And in that worship where the gem-consecration meditation of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [is performed], there the worship of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is said to be associated with the twenty-syllable [mantra]. He shows the fruit with '<s>japa</s>' etc.: whoever serves this mantra through recitation and the like, his house is constantly — incessantly — filled with gems such as rubies, gold, and grains.

children.text: pṛthvī pṛthvī kare tasya savasasy akulākulā |
children.translated_text: The entire earth upon his hand, [overflowing] with abundantly heaped crops;

children.text: putrair mitraiḥ susampannaḥ prayāty ante parāṃ gatim // Krd_7.46 //
children.translated_text: Well-endowed with sons and friends, he attains at the end the supreme destination.
He shows the application —
Having worshipped <s>Govinda</s> in the fire, with white flowers mixed with rice grains,

children.text: ājyāktair ayutaṃ hutvā bhasma tan-mūrdhni dhārayet |
children.translated_text: Anointed with ghee, having offered ten thousand [oblations], one should wear the ash on one's head;
He shall have abundance of food and other [blessings]; all women shall be under his control.

children.text: yathokta-prakāreṇāgnim ādhāya tatra yathokta-prakāreṇa govindaṃ sampūjya ghṛtāktais taṇḍula-sahitaiḥ śukla-puṣpair daśa-sahasrāṇi hutvā homāgni-bhasma yaḥ pumān mūrdhani dhārayet tasya nānā-samṛddhiḥ sampattir bhavati sarvāś ca striyas tad-āyattā bhavanti || KrdC_7.47 ||
children.translated_text: Having kindled the fire in the prescribed manner, having worshipped <s>Govinda</s> therein in the prescribed manner, with white flowers combined with rice grains, anointed with ghee, having offered ten thousand [oblations], the man who wears the ash of the <s>homa</s>-fire on his head — he shall have various kinds of abundance and prosperity; and all women shall be subject to him.
He states another application —

children.text: ājyair lakṣaṃ huned rakta-padmair vā madhurāplutaiḥ |
children.translated_text: One should offer one <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand) [oblations] with ghee, or with red lotuses soaked in sweet [substances];

children.text: śriyā tasyaindram aiśvaryaṃ tṛṇaleśāyate dhruvam // Krd_7.48 //
children.translated_text: His wealth shall make even the sovereignty of <s>Indra</s> seem [no more than] a blade of grass — certainly.

children.text: ghṛtaiḥ kevalaiḥ ghṛta-madhu-śarkarāyutaiḥ rakta-padmair vā yo lakṣaṃ juhoti tasya sādhakasya śriyā lakṣmyā kṛtvā indra-sambandhi aiśvaryaṃ tṛṇa-samānaṃ bhavati dhruvam utprekṣāyām || KrdC_7.48 ||
children.translated_text: With ghee alone, or ghee combined with honey and sugar, or with red lotuses — whoever offers one <s>lakṣa</s>, for that practitioner, through <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), the sovereignty of <s>Indra</s> becomes equal to a blade of grass — certainly. [The word '<s>dhruvam</s>' is used] in the sense of emphatic assertion.
He states another application —

children.text: śuklādi-vastra-lābhāya śuklādi-kusumair hunet | trimadhvaktair daśa-śatam ājyāktair vāṣṭa-saṃyutam // Krd_7.49 //
children.translated_text: For obtaining white and other garments, one should offer with white and other flowers, anointed with the three sweets, one thousand and eight, or anointed with ghee.

children.text: śuklādi-vastra-prāpty-arthaṃ ghṛta-madhu-śarkarā-sahitaiḥ śukla-puṣpaiḥ ghṛāktair vā aṣṭadhika-daśa-śataṃ juhuyāt || KrdC_7.49 ||
children.translated_text: For the purpose of obtaining white and other garments, with white flowers combined with ghee, honey, and sugar, or anointed with ghee, one should offer one thousand and eight [oblations].
He states another application —
With white flowers sprinkled with honey, one thousand and eight [oblations],

children.text: hunen nityaṃ sa ṣaḍ-māsān purodhā nṛpater bhavet // Krd_7.50 //
children.translated_text: Should be offered daily; within six months he shall become the <s>purohita</s> (royal priest) of a king.

children.text: madhu-miśritaiḥ śukla-puṣpair aṣṭādhika-sahasraṃ pratyahaṃ yo juhuyāt sa ṣaṭke atīte rājñaḥ purohito bhavati || KrdC_7.50 ||
children.translated_text: With white flowers mixed with honey, whoever offers one thousand and eight daily, after six [months] have passed, he becomes the king's <s>purohita</s> (chief priest).
The recitation, meditation, <s>homa</s>, and other [practices] stated for the ten- and eighteen-syllable [mantras]

children.text: vidadhyāt karma cānena tābhyām apy atra kīrtitam // Krd_7.51 //
children.translated_text: Should be performed with this [mantra] as well; and what is stated here [for this mantra] should also [be performed] with those two.

children.text: daśāṣṭādaśākṣarayor uktaṃ japa-dhyāna-homādikam anena mantreṇa kuryāt | atra mantre kathitaṃ prayogādikaṃ tābhyāṃ ca kuryāt || KrdC_7.51 ||
children.translated_text: The recitation, meditation, <s>homa</s>, and other [practices] stated for the ten- and eighteen-syllable [mantras] should be performed with this mantra. And the applications etc. stated for this mantra should also be performed with those two.
He states another mantra —
'<s>Śrī</s>-seed, <s>śakti</s>-seed, <s>smara</s> (love)-seed, <s>Kṛṣṇāya</s>, <s>Govindāya</s>' — the head-mantra;
A twelve-syllable [mantra]; <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> are its <s>ṛṣi</s> and the rest.

children.text: śrī-bījaṃ śakti-bījaṃ smaraḥ kāma-bījaṃ kṛṣṇāya govindāyeti svarūpaṃ śiraḥ svāheti svarūpaṃ ravyārṇo mantraḥ ṛṣir ādau yeṣāṃ te ṛṣy-ādayo brahma-gāyatrī-kṛṣṇā ṛṣy-ādaya ity arthaḥ | asya brahmā ṛṣiḥ gāyatrī-cchandaḥ kṛṣṇo devatā ity arthaḥ | bīja-śaktyādi-pūrvavat || KrdC_7.52 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>śrī</s>-seed, the <s>śakti</s>-seed, <s>smara</s> is the <s>kāma</s>-seed (love-seed); '<s>Kṛṣṇāya Govindāya</s>' is the form; '<s>śiras</s>' meaning '<s>svāhā</s>' is the form. A twelve-syllable mantra. Those whose <s>ṛṣi</s> comes first — these are the <s>ṛṣi</s> and the rest, namely <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. That is: <s>Brahmā</s> is the seer; <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the meter; <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is the deity — this is the meaning. The seed-syllable, <s>śakti</s>, and the rest are as before.
With [the three] seeds, the limb-sextet is here stated, with [syllables of] three, paired-Vedic, number;
The recitation, meditation, <s>homa</s>, and worship procedures stated for the twenty-syllable [mantra] —
This mantra should be practised by the wise who desire complete sovereignty.

children.text: iha mantre aṅga-ṣaṭkaṃ ṣaḍ-aṅgaṃ kathitaṃ kais tribhir bījair aṅga-trayaṃ tathā triveda-yugmārṇaiḥ tribhiś caturbhir dvābhyāṃ cāparāṅga-trayam iti | viṃśeti | ayaṃ mantraḥ viṃśaty-akṣara-mantrokta-japa-dhyāna-homa-pūjā-sahitaḥ sakalaiśvarya-kāmaiḥ paṇḍitair upāsyatām || KrdC_7.53 ||
children.translated_text: In this mantra, the limb-sextet — the six limbs — is stated. With which? With three seeds, three limbs; and with [syllables of] three-Vedic (3), paired (4), and two numbers, the other three limbs — thus. With '<s>viṃśa</s>' etc.: this mantra, together with the recitation, meditation, <s>homa</s>, and worship stated for the twenty-syllable mantra, should be practised — worshipped — by scholars who desire complete sovereignty.
He states another mantra —
'<s>Śrī</s>-seed, <s>śakti</s>-seed, <s>kāma</s>-seed' prefixed, with '<s>aṅga-janma</s>-seed, <s>śakti</s>-seed, <s>ramā</s>-seed' at the end;
A ten-syllable [mantra becomes such]; if at the beginning with <s>śakti</s>-seed and <s>ramā</s>-seed [added to] <s>sarāva</s> [= the basic ten-syllable mantra],
These two mantras are variants, non-vowel-bearing, with limbs [formed] from '<s>ā-cakra</s>' and the rest.

children.text: śrī-bījaṃ bhuvaneśvarī-bījaṃ kāma-bījaṃ ca | ete pūrve yasya daśākṣarasya tathāṅga-janma kāma-bījaṃ śaktir bhuvaneśvarī-bījaṃ ramā-śrī-bījam-ete ante yasya daśākṣarasya | evaṃ bhūtādy-anta-viśiṣṭo daśākṣaro ṣoḍaśākṣara-mantor bhavati tathā sa eva daśākṣaro mantraḥ ādau śakti-ramā-yutaḥ bhuvaneśvarī-śrī-bīja-sahitaś cet tadā dvādaśākṣara-mantro bhavati | evaṃ ca sati imau vikṛtir avyārṇau ṣoḍaśākṣara-dvādaśākṣarau mantrau ācakrādy-aṅginau daśākṣaroktāni ācakrādy-aṅgāni yayos tādṛśau jñeyau || KrdC_7.54 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>śrī</s>-seed, the <s>bhuvaneśvarī</s>-seed, and the <s>kāma</s>-seed — these are prefixed to the ten-syllable [mantra]; and <s>aṅga-janma</s> is the <s>kāma</s>-seed, <s>śakti</s> is the <s>bhuvaneśvarī</s>-seed, <s>ramā</s> is the <s>śrī</s>-seed — these are at the end of the ten-syllable [mantra]. The ten-syllable [mantra] thus distinguished at the beginning and end becomes a sixteen-syllable mantra. Likewise, that same ten-syllable mantra, at the beginning with <s>śakti</s> and <s>ramā</s> — the <s>bhuvaneśvarī</s>-seed and the <s>śrī</s>-seed — becomes a twelve-syllable mantra. And in this case, these two variants — the sixteen-syllable and the twelve-syllable — are non-vowel-bearing mantras, with limbs [formed] from '<s>ā-cakra</s>' and the rest as stated for the ten-syllable [mantra] — thus they should be understood.
In the worship-method stated for the twenty-syllable [mantra], one should then meditate upon <s>Acyuta</s>,
Embracing with his <s>varada</s> (boon-giving) and <s>abhaya</s> (fearlessness) hands the beloved ones seated on his lap,
Who are embraced by him, holding lotus and blue-lotus in their hands — resplendent with discus and other [weapons].

children.text: viṃśaty-akṣara-kathita-pūjā-prakārāv etau athānantaram acyutaṃ cintayet | kīdṛśaṃ ? svāṅkage sva-kroḍa-sthite priye lakṣmī-sarasvatyau | yad vā, rukmiṇī-satyabhāme śliṣyantam āliṅgantam | kābhyām ? varadābhaya-hastābhyāṃ varaṃ dadātīti varadaḥ | na vidyate bhayaṃ yasmāt sa varadābhayau ca tau hastau ceti varadābhaya-hastau tābhyām ity arthaḥ | priye kīdṛśe ? padmaṃ sāmānya-paṅkajam utpalaṃ nīla-padmaṃ te karayor yayos te tādṛg-vidhe | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? tābhyāṃ priyābhyāṃ śliṣṭam āliṅgitam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? śaṅkha-cakrābhyām ujjvalam || KrdC_7.55 ||
children.translated_text: These two [mantras] follow the worship-method stated for the twenty-syllable [mantra]. Then, next, one should meditate upon <s>Acyuta</s> (the Imperishable One). Of what description? Embracing the beloved ones seated on his own lap — <s>Lakṣmī</s> and <s>Sarasvatī</s>; or alternatively, <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and <s>Satyabhāmā</s>. With which [hands]? With the <s>varada</s> and <s>abhaya</s> hands — '<s>varada</s>' is the boon-giver; that from which there is no fear — these two are '<s>varada</s>' and '<s>abhaya</s>' as hands — with those two — this is the meaning. The beloved ones — of what description? Those in whose hands are the lotus — the common lotus — and the blue lotus — those of such description. Again, of what description? Embraced — held in embrace — by those two beloved ones. Again, of what description? Resplendent with the conch and discus.
He states the <s>puraścaraṇa</s> recitation and the like —
One should recite ten <s>lakṣa</s>s (one million) [times]; with an equivalent number of thousands of ghee-oblations in <s>homa</s>;

children.text: siddhāv imau manū sarva-sampat-saubhāgyadau nṛṇām // Krd_7.56 //
children.translated_text: When perfected, these two mantras bestow upon men all wealth and good fortune.

children.text: daśa-lakṣa-saṅkhyaṃ japed ājyair ghṛtais tāvat-sahasra-homato daśa-sahasra-homataḥ siddhau imau mantrau manuṣyāṇāṃ sarvaiśvarya-sarva-jana-priya-pradau bhavataḥ || KrdC_7.56 ||
children.translated_text: One should recite ten <s>lakṣa</s>s in number; with ghee, with an equivalent number of thousands — ten thousand — oblations in <s>homa</s>; when perfected, these two mantras bestow upon human beings all sovereignty and all-people-attracting [power].
Now he extracts the mantras in sequence —
'<s>Māra</s> (love-seed), <s>śakti</s>-seed, <s>ramā</s>-seed' prefixed; '<s>śakti</s>-seed, <s>śrī</s>-seed, <s>māra</s>-seed' prefixed;

children.text: śrī-śakti-māra-pūrvaś ca daśārṇo manavas trayaḥ // Krd_7.57 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Śrī</s>-seed, <s>śakti</s>-seed, <s>māra</s>-seed' prefixed — thus three ten-syllable mantras.

children.text: annādyaḥ kāma-bhuvaneśvarī-śrī-bīja-pūrvā daśākṣaraḥ bhuvaneśvarī śrīr māraḥ pūrvo yasyeti dvitīyaḥ śrī- bhuvaneśvarī-kāma-bīja-pūrvo daśākṣara iti tṛtīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The first: with <s>kāma</s>-seed, <s>bhuvaneśvarī</s>-seed, and <s>śrī</s>-seed prefixed to the ten-syllable [mantra]. The second: with <s>bhuvaneśvarī</s>, <s>śrī</s>, and <s>māra</s> (love-seed) prefixed. The third: with <s>śrī</s>-seed, <s>bhuvaneśvarī</s>-seed, and <s>kāma</s>-seed prefixed to the ten-syllable [mantra].
The limbs, <s>ṛṣi</s>s (seers), and other [ancillaries] of these excellent mantras are as for the ten-syllable [mantra];
Bearing conch, discus, bow, arrows, noose, and goad, of reddish hue,

children.text: veṇuṃ dhaman dhṛtaṃ dorbhyāṃ kṛṣṇo dhyeyo divākare // Krd_7.58 //
children.translated_text: Playing the flute, held in both arms — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is to be meditated upon in the solar disc.

children.text: ādye manau dhyānam evaṃ dvitīye viṃśad-arṇavat |
children.translated_text: For the first mantra, the meditation is thus; for the second, as for the twenty-syllable [mantra];
For the third, as for the ten-syllable; worship with the limbs, directional guardians, and other [deities].

children.text: pañca-lakṣaṃ japet tāvad ayutaṃ pāyasair hunet |
children.translated_text: One should recite five <s>lakṣa</s>s (five hundred thousand); and offer that many — ten thousand — oblations with <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice);

children.text: tataḥ sidhyanti manavo nṛṇāṃ sampatti-kānti-dāḥ // Krd_7.60 //
children.translated_text: Then the mantras become perfected — bestowers of wealth and beauty upon men.

children.text: eteṣām ity ādi sugamam | divākare sūrya-maṇḍale || KrdC_7.58-60 ||
children.translated_text: 'Of these' and so forth is self-evident. '<s>Divākara</s>' means in the solar disc.
He clearly extracts another mantra —
The eighteen-syllable [mantra] ending with '<s>bhāra</s>' is a bestower of sons and wealth;
Its <s>ṛṣi</s> and other [ancillaries] are as stated for the eighteen-syllable [mantra]; with the long vowels accompanied by <s>Māra</s> (the love-god's syllable), in order,

children.text: aṅgāny asya manor aṅga dikpālādyaiḥ samarcanā // Krd_7.61 //
children.translated_text: Are the limbs of this mantra; worship with the limbs, directional guardians, and other [deities].

children.text: kāma-bījāntaḥ pūrvoktāṣṭādaśākṣara-mantraḥ suta-dhana-pradaḥ mārārūḍhair napuṃsaka-rahita-kāma-bīja-sahitaiḥ dīrgha-svara-ṣaṭkaiḥ krāṃ krīm ity ādi ṣaṭkaiḥ kramād asya manoḥ ṣaḍ-aṅgāni || KrdC_7.61 ||
children.translated_text: The previously stated eighteen-syllable mantra with the <s>kāma-bīja</s> (love-god's seed-syllable) within — this is the bestower of sons and wealth. With the <s>Māra</s>-accompanied [syllables] — the six long vowels combined with the <s>kāma-bīja</s> minus the neuter — <s>krāṃ</s>, <s>krīm</s>, and so forth — these six, in order, constitute the six limbs of this mantra.
He states the meditation —

children.text: pāṇau pāyasa-pakvam āhita-rasaṃ bibhran mudā dakṣiṇe
children.translated_text: In his right hand, holding cooked <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice pudding) imbued with flavor, with delight,
In his left, bearing fresh butter (<s>haiyaṅgavīna</s>) resembling the disc of the autumnal moon,
Wearing a <s>puṇḍarīka</s> (white lotus) fashioned as a necklace on his throat, bearing exceedingly brilliant radiance,

children.text: devo divya-digambaro diśatu vaḥ saukhyaṃ yaśodā-śiśuḥ // Krd_7.62 //
children.translated_text: May the god, the child of <s>Yaśodā</s>, divinely unclad (<s>digambara</s>), bestow happiness upon you.

children.text: pāṇau pāyasa-pakvaṃ supakvaṃ pāyasaṃ susvādv ity arthaḥ | atyuddāma-dīptim atyudbhaṭa-kānti | divya iti divyaś cāsau digambaraś ceti samāsaḥ | divya-deva-svarūpa iti || KrdC_7.62 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Pāyasa-pakva</s>' means well-cooked <s>pāyasa</s> — meaning very delicious. '<s>Atyuddāma-dīpti</s>' means exceedingly brilliant radiance. '<s>Divya</s>' — the compound is: 'divine and unclad' (<s>divya</s> and <s>digambara</s>). Meaning: of a divine, godly form.
Daily, having worshipped <s>Govinda</s>, one should recite thirty-two <s>lakṣa</s>s (3,200,000) in measure;

children.text: japtvā daśāṃśaṃ juhuyāt sitājyena payo 'ndhasā // Krd_7.63 //
children.translated_text: And offer one-tenth as oblations with <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice) [mixed] with sugar and ghee.
With sugar and ghee — with <s>paramānna</s> (milk-rice pudding) combined with crystallized sugar and ghee.
Having worshipped the deity seated on a lotus, one should perform <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) at his lotus-face,

children.text: kṣīreṇa kadalī-pakvair dadhnā haiyaṅgavena ca // Krd_7.64 //
children.translated_text: With milk, ripe bananas, curds, and fresh butter (<s>haiyaṅgavīna</s>).

children.text: sutārthī tarpayed evaṃ vatsarāl labhate sutam |
children.translated_text: One desiring a son, performing <s>tarpaṇa</s> thus, obtains a son within a year;

children.text: yad yad icchati tat sarvaṃ tarpaṇād eva siddhyati // Krd_7.65 //
children.translated_text: Whatever one desires, all of that is accomplished by <s>tarpaṇa</s> alone.

children.text: kṣīreṇety ādinā tarpaṇaṃ yad uktaṃ taj-jalenaiva kṣīrādi-dravya-buddhyā kāryam || KrdC_7.64-65 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>tarpaṇa</s> described beginning with 'with milk' etc. should be performed with water alone, with the mental conception of the substances such as milk and the like.
He extracts another mantra —
<s>Vāg-bhava</s> (the speech seed-syllable), <s>Māra-bīja</s> (the love-god's seed-syllable), '<s>Kṛṣṇāya</s>,' <s>Bhuvaneśvarī</s> (the world-sovereign goddess's syllable),
'<s>Govindāya</s>,' <s>Ramā</s> (the <s>Śrī</s>-syllable), '<s>Gopījanavallabha</s>' in the dative with <s>śiras</s> (head, i.e., <s>svāhā</s>).

children.text: vāg-bhavam aim iti bījaṃ māra-bījaṃ klīṃ kṛṣṇāyeti svarūpaṃ bhuvaneśvarī-bījaṃ hrīṃ govindāyeti svarūpaṃ ramā-śrī-bījaṃ gopī-jana-vallabha iti svarūpaṃ ṅe caturthy-eka-vacanaṃ śiraḥ svāhā śuklaḥ śa-kāraś caturdaśa-svarūpeṇopeta au-kāra-sahitaḥ śukra iti pāṭhe dantya-sa-kāraḥ saṃ śukrātmane nama iti | nyāsa-vidhānāt sargī visarga-sahitaḥ | tad-ūrdhvata iti tasya ūrdhvaṃ tasya ekaviṃśaty-akṣarasya ūrdhvataḥ prathama-bījam etad iti rudradharaḥ || KrdC_7.66 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāg-bhava</s> is the seed-syllable '<s>aim</s>'; <s>Māra-bīja</s> is '<s>klīm</s>'; '<s>Kṛṣṇāya</s>' is itself; the <s>Bhuvaneśvarī</s> seed-syllable is '<s>hrīm</s>'; '<s>Govindāya</s>' is itself; the <s>Ramā</s>-<s>Śrī</s> seed-syllable [is '<s>śrīm</s>']; '<s>Gopī-jana-vallabha</s>' is itself; <s>ṅe</s> is the dative singular; <s>śiras</s> (head) is '<s>svāhā</s>.' <s>Śukla</s> — the letter <s>śa</s> endowed with the fourteenth vowel-form — combined with <s>au</s>-vowel; in the reading '<s>śukra</s>,' the dental <s>sa</s>: '<s>saṃ śukrātmane namaḥ</s>.' From the <s>nyāsa</s> prescriptions, '<s>sargī</s>' means accompanied by <s>visarga</s>. '<s>Tad-ūrdhvataḥ</s>' — above that, above the twenty-one-syllable [mantra], this is the first seed-syllable — thus [says] <s>Rudradhara</s>.
The [letter <s>śa</s>] endowed with the fourteenth [vowel], <s>śukla</s>, with <s>visarga</s>, placed above that;
This twenty-two-syllable mantra is the accomplisher of mastery over speech.

children.text: vāg-bhavam aim iti bījaṃ māra-bījaṃ klīṃ kṛṣṇāyeti svarūpaṃ bhuvaneśvarī-bījaṃ hrīṃ govindāyeti svarūpaṃ ramā-bījaṃ gopī-jana-vallabha iti svarūpaṃ ṅe caturthy-eka-vacanaṃ śiraḥ svāhā śuklaḥ śa-kāraś caturdaśa-svareṇopeta au-kāra-sahitaḥ śukra iti pāṭhe dantya-sa-kāraḥ saṃ śukrātmane nama iti | nyāsa-vidhānāt sargī visarga-sahitaḥ tad ūrdhvata iti tasya ūrdhvaṃ tasya ekaviṃśaty-akṣarasya ūrdhvataḥ prathama-bījam etad iti rudradharaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Vāg-bhava</s> is the seed-syllable '<s>aim</s>'; <s>Māra-bīja</s> is '<s>klīm</s>'; '<s>Kṛṣṇāya</s>' is itself; the <s>Bhuvaneśvarī</s> seed-syllable is '<s>hrīm</s>'; '<s>Govindāya</s>' is itself; the <s>Ramā</s> seed-syllable [is '<s>śrīm</s>']; '<s>Gopī-jana-vallabha</s>' is itself; <s>ṅe</s> is the dative singular; <s>śiras</s> (head) is '<s>svāhā</s>.' <s>Śukla</s> — the letter <s>śa</s> endowed with the fourteenth vowel — combined with <s>au</s>-vowel; in the reading '<s>śukra</s>,' the dental <s>sa</s>: '<s>saṃ śukrātmane namaḥ</s>.' From the <s>nyāsa</s> prescriptions, '<s>sargī</s>' means accompanied by <s>visarga</s>. '<s>Tad-ūrdhvataḥ</s>' — above that twenty-one-syllable [mantra], this is the first seed-syllable — thus [says] <s>Rudradhara</s>.

children.text: tad-ūrdhvataḥ-svāhā-kārordhvataḥ iti laghu-dīpikākāraḥ | anena bījena saha dvāviṃśaty-akṣaro mantro bhavati | kīdṛśo 'yam ? vacaneśvaratva-dātā || KrdC_7.66-67 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Tad-ūrdhvataḥ</s>' — above the <s>svāhā</s>-syllable — thus [says] the author of the <s>Laghu-dīpikā</s>. With this seed-syllable together, the mantra becomes twenty-two syllables. Of what kind is this? The bestower of mastery over speech (<s>vacaneśvaratva</s>).
All the limbs, <s>ṛṣi</s>, and other [ancillaries] of this [mantra] are as for the eighteen-syllable [mantra];

children.text: pūjā ca viṃśaty-arṇoktā pratipattis tu kathyate // Krd_7.68 //
children.translated_text: But the worship is as stated for the twenty-syllable [mantra]; the meditation (<s>pratipatti</s>) is now described.

children.text: asya ṛṣi-cchandodhiṣṭātṛ-devatā-bīja-śakty-aṅgāni sarvāṇi aṣṭādaśārṇavat yathāṣṭādaśākṣara-mantre tathātrāpīty arthaḥ | pūjā punaḥ viṃśaty-akṣara-kathitā boddhavyā pratipattir dhyānaṃ kathyate punaḥ || KrdC_7.68 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>ṛṣi</s>, <s>chandas</s> (meter), presiding deity, <s>bīja</s> (seed-syllable), <s>śakti</s> (power), and limbs of this [mantra] — all are as for the eighteen-syllable [mantra], meaning: as in the eighteen-syllable mantra, so here also — this is the meaning. The worship, however, should be understood as stated for the twenty-syllable [mantra]. The meditation (<s>pratipatti</s>) is now described again.
In his upper left hand, holding a book — the repository of all knowledge,

children.text: akṣamālāṃ ca dakṣordhve sphāṭikīṃ mātṛkā-mayīm // Krd_7.69 //
children.translated_text: And in his upper right, a crystal <s>akṣamālā</s> (rosary) composed of the <s>Mātṛkā</s> (alphabet);
A flute of the nature of the <s>Śabda-Brahman</s> (the Absolute as Sound), sounded by the two lower hands,
Singing, wearing yellow garments, dark-complexioned, of tender beauty;
With a crest-ornament made of peacock feathers, omniscient, worshipped by all-knowing ones,

children.text: upāsitaṃ muni-gaṇair upatiṣṭhed dhariṃ sadā // Krd_7.71 //
children.translated_text: And by hosts of sages — one should always attend upon <s>Hari</s>.

children.text:
śloka-trayeṇātrādi-kulakam | harim upatiṣṭhet dhyāyet | vāmordhva-haste vidyā-sarvasva-pustakaṃ vedānta-pustakaṃ dhārayantaṃ dakṣordhve pañcāśat-saṅkhya-mātṛkākṣara-samitāṃ pañāśat-sphaṭika-baddhām akṣa-mālāṃ dhārayantam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? adhaḥ sthita-kara-dvayena īritaṃ vāditaṃ śabda-brahma-mayaṃ śabda-brahma-svarūpaṃ veṇu-randhraṃ dadhānam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? veṇunaiva gāyantam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? pīta-vastre yasya taṃ śyāma-varṇaṃ ca | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? komalā manoharā chavir yasya sa tathā tam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? barhī mayūras tasya barhaṃ picchaṃ tena kṛta uttaṃsaḥ śirobhūṣaṇaṃ yena tam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? sarva-sākṣiṇaṃ | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? sarvadā upāsitaṃ
sevitam | kaiḥ ? sarva-vedibhiḥ atītānāgatajñaiḥ muni-gaṇaiḥ sanakādibhiḥ || KrdC_7.69-71 ||
children.translated_text:
A <s>kulaka</s> (verse-cluster) beginning here, of three verses. One should attend upon — meditate upon — <s>Hari</s>. Holding in the upper left hand a book of all knowledge — a <s>Vedānta</s> text; in the upper right, holding a rosary (<s>akṣa-mālā</s>) of fifty crystals bound together, containing the fifty <s>Mātṛkā</s> (alphabet) letters. Again, of what kind? Holding — bearing — in the two lower hands, a flute that is sounded — played — which is of the nature of <s>Śabda-Brahman</s> (the Absolute as Sound) — of the very form of <s>Śabda-Brahman</s> — its apertures. Again, of what kind? Singing with the flute itself. Again, of what kind? One whose garment is yellow — wearing yellow clothes; of dark complexion. Again, of what kind? One whose beauty (<s>chavi</s>) is tender — enchanting. Again, of what kind? One whose crest-ornament (<s>uttaṃsa</s>) is made of the feather (<s>barha</s>) of a peacock (<s>barhī</s>). Again, of what kind? The witness of all. Again, of what kind? Always worshipped —
served. By whom? By all-knowers — those who know past and future — hosts of sages such as <s>Sanaka</s> and others.
He states the <s>puraścaraṇa</s> (preliminary practice) —
Having thus meditated upon the Lord of the universe in the attire and grace of a beautiful woman,

children.text: caturlakṣaṃ japen mantram imaṃ mantrī susaṃyataḥ // Krd_7.72 //
children.translated_text: The well-controlled <s>mantrī</s> (ritualist) should recite this mantra four <s>lakṣa</s>s (four hundred thousand) times.

children.text: evaṃ pūrvoktaṃ bhuvaneśvaraṃ śrī-kṛṣṇaṃ pramadā strī tasyā veśaḥ saṃsthāna-viśeṣaḥ | tasya vilāsa āhlādo yasya taṃ pramadā-rūpa-dhāriṇam ity arthaḥ | yad vā, strī-rūpa-dharaṃ strī-vilāsaṃ ca dhyātvā imaṃ mantraṃ lakṣa-catuṣṭayaṃ japet susaṃyataḥ san pūrvokta-puraścaraṇavān || KrdC_7.72 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, the previously described Lord of the universe, <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>; <s>pramadā</s> means woman; her <s>veśa</s> is a particular form of attire; the delight (<s>vilāsa</s>) of that — meaning one who bears the form of a woman — this is the meaning. Alternatively, meditating on [Him as] bearing a female form and female graces, one should recite this mantra four hundred thousand times, being well-controlled — possessing the previously described <s>puraścaraṇa</s> [discipline].
He states the <s>homa</s> (fire-oblation) —
With <s>palāśa</s> (Butea) flowers soaked in sweet [substances], forty thousand [oblations]

children.text: juhyāt karmaṇānena manuḥ siddho bhaved dhruvam // Krd_7.73 //
children.translated_text: One should offer; by this procedure, the mantra will certainly become perfected.

children.text: ghṛta-madhu-śarkarānvitaiḥ palāśa-puṣpaiś catvāriṃśat-sahasrakaṃ juhuyāt | anena vidhinā avaśyaṃ mantraḥ sidhyati || KrdC_7.73 ||
children.translated_text: With <s>palāśa</s> flowers combined with ghee, honey, and sugar, one should offer forty thousand oblations. By this method, the mantra will certainly become perfected.
He shows the fruit —
Whoever, the <s>mantrī</s> (ritualist), with intellect absorbed in this mantra, abides — from the cavern of his mouth
Speech in prose and verse flows for him like the current of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.

children.text: yo mantrī asmin mantre niṣṇāta-dhīr datta-matir vartate tasya sādhakasya vaktra-gahvarāt mukha-madhyato gadya-padya-mayī vāṇī pravartate gaṅgā-pravāhavat viśuddhānavara-tattvena gaṅgā-pravāheṇopamā || KrdC_7.74 ||
children.translated_text: Whichever ritualist has his intellect absorbed — his mind devoted — in this mantra and abides [in it], for that practitioner, from the cavern of the mouth — from within the mouth — speech composed of prose and verse flows forth like the current of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — the comparison is with the <s>Gaṅgā</s> stream in its pure, unsurpassed quality.
Becoming a scholar in all <s>Veda</s>s, <s>śāstra</s>s, and [arts of] music,

children.text: saṃvittiṃ paramāṃ labdhvā cānte bhūyāt paraṃ padam // Krd_7.75 //
children.translated_text: Having attained supreme knowledge (<s>saṃvitti</s>), at the end he attains the supreme abode.

children.text: sarveṣu ṛg-vedādiṣu śāstreṣu vedānteṣu paṇḍito viveka-buddhi-yuktaḥ san saṃvittim utkṛṣṭa-jñānaṃ prāpya ante dehāvasāne viṣṇu-lokaṃ prāpnoti || KrdC_7.75 ||
children.translated_text: Becoming a scholar — endowed with discriminating intellect — in all the <s>Ṛg-Veda</s> and other [<s>Veda</s>s], in the <s>śāstra</s>s — the <s>Vedānta</s>s — having obtained supreme knowledge — the highest <s>jñāna</s> — at the end — at the dissolution of the body — he attains the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
He states another mantra —

children.text: tāraṃ hṛd bhagavān ṅe 'nto nanda-putra-padaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: <s>Tāra</s> (i.e., <s>Oṃ</s>), <s>hṛd</s> (i.e., <s>namaḥ</s>), '<s>Bhagavān</s>' in the dative, the word '<s>Nanda-putra</s>' likewise,
Ending with '<s>Ānanda</s>,' '<s>vapuṣe</s>' (for the body); bone-fire (<s>asthi-agni</s>, i.e., <s>Śrī</s>-bīja); ending with '<s>āyā</s>' — this is the ten-syllable [addition].
This is a twenty-eight-syllable [mantra]; I now state the thirty-two-syllable one:
The word '<s>Nanda-putra</s>' in the dative, the word '<s>Śyāmalāṅga</s>' (dark-limbed) likewise,
In the dative; '<s>Bāla-vapuḥ</s>' (of infant form), '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,' '<s>Govinda</s>' — this is the ten-syllable [addition].

children.text:
tāraṃ praṇavaḥ hṛt namaḥ ṅe 'ntaś caturthy-anto bhagavān bhagavata iti svarūpaṃ nanda-putraṃ tathā ṅe 'ntaṃ caturthy-antaṃ nanda-putrāyeti padānte ānanda iti śabda-śeṣe vapuṣe iti svarūpam | asthi śa-kāraḥ agnī rephaḥ māyā dīrgha-ī-kāraḥ tathā ca śrī-bījam asyānte daśārṇakaḥ daśākṣara-mantraḥ etenāyaṃ mantraḥ aṣṭāviṃśaty-akṣaro bhavati |
adhunā dvātriṃśa-mantram uddharati-nandeti | nanda-putra-padaṃ caturthy-antaṃ śyāmalāṅgaṃ padam api caturthy-antaṃ bāla-vapuḥ kṛṣṇa-govinda-śabdāś ca pratyekaṃ caturthy-antāḥ | anantaraṃ pūrvokta-daśākṣara-mantraḥ | etena dvātriṃśad-akṣaro mantro bhavati || KrdC_7.76-77 ||
children.translated_text:
<s>Tāra</s> is <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>); <s>hṛt</s> is <s>namaḥ</s>; '<s>ṅe</s>-ending' means ending in the dative; '<s>Bhagavān</s>' — '<s>Bhagavate</s>' is its form; '<s>Nanda-putra</s>' likewise, '<s>ṅe</s>-ending' means ending in the dative — '<s>Nanda-putrāya</s>'; at the end of the word, '<s>Ānanda</s>' is the remainder of the word; '<s>vapuṣe</s>' is its form. <s>Asthi</s> (bone) is the letter <s>śa</s>; <s>agni</s> (fire) is <s>ra</s> (repha); <s>māyā</s> is the long <s>ī</s>-vowel — and thus the <s>Śrī</s>-bīja; at the end of this, the ten-syllable mantra. Thus this mantra has twenty-eight syllables.
Now he extracts the thirty-two[-syllable mantra], beginning with '<s>Nanda</s>': the word '<s>Nanda-putra</s>' in the dative; the word '<s>Śyāmalāṅga</s>' also in the dative; '<s>Bāla-vapuḥ</s>,' '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,' '<s>Govinda</s>' — each in the dative ending. Then the aforementioned ten-syllable mantra. Thus the thirty-two-syllable mantra is formed.

children.text: vimarśaḥ-oṃ namo bhagavate nanda-putrāya ānanda-vapuṣe śrīṃ gopī-jana-vallabhāya svāhā || KrdC_7.76 ||
children.translated_text: Examination: '<s>Oṃ namo bhagavate Nanda-putrāya ānanda-vapuṣe śrīṃ gopī-jana-vallabhāya svāhā</s>.'

children.text: nanda-putrāya śyāmalāṅgāya bāla-vapuṣe kṛṣṇāya govindāya gopījanavallabhāya svāhā || KrdC_7.77 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Nanda-putrāya śyāmalāṅgāya bāla-vapuṣe Kṛṣṇāya Govindāya gopījanavallabhāya svāhā</s>.'
He shows the <s>ṛṣi</s> and other [ancillaries] —
For both of these, <s>Nārada</s> is the <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer); the meters are <s>Triṣṭubh</s> and <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> respectively;

children.text: ācakrādyair aṅgam aṅga-dik-pālādyaiś ca pūjanam // Krd_7.78 //
children.translated_text: The limbs are formed with '<s>ācakra</s>' and so forth; worship is with the limbs, directional guardians, and others.

children.text: anayor nārada ṛṣiḥ | yathā-kramaṃ triṣṭub-anuṣṭup-chandasī ācakrādyaiḥ pūrvoktair aṅga-pañcakam aṅga-dik-pāla-vajrādyair āvaraṇa-pūjanaṃ pīṭha-pūjā tu pūrvavat || KrdC_7.78 ||
children.translated_text: For both of these, <s>Nārada</s> is the <s>ṛṣi</s>. In respective order, <s>Triṣṭubh</s> and <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> are the meters. The five limbs are formed with the previously stated '<s>ācakra</s>' and so forth. The surrounding worship is with the limbs, directional guardians, thunderbolt-weapons, and the like; but the seat-worship (<s>pīṭha-pūjā</s>) is as before.
He shows the meditation —
In his right [hand], a gem-cup (<s>ratna-caṣaka</s>); in his left, a golden staff (<s>vetraka</s>);

children.text: kare dadhānaṃ devībhyām āśliṣṭaṃ cintayed dharim // Krd_7.79 //
children.translated_text: Holding [these] in his hands, embraced by two goddesses — thus one should meditate on <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: hariṃ cintayet | kīdṛśaṃ ? dakṣiṇa-haste ratna-pātraṃ vāma-haste suvarṇa-ghaṭita-vetraṃ dadhānam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? devībhyāṃ lakṣmī-sarasvatībhyāṃ rukmiṇī-satyabhāmābhyāṃ vā āliṅgitam || KrdC_7.79 ||
children.translated_text: One should meditate on <s>Hari</s>. Of what kind? Holding in his right hand a gem-cup, and in his left hand a golden staff. Again, of what kind? Embraced by two goddesses — <s>Lakṣmī</s> and <s>Sarasvatī</s>, or <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and <s>Satyabhāmā</s>.

children.text: japel lakṣaṃ manu-varau pāyasair ayutaṃ hunet |
children.translated_text: One should recite each of the two excellent mantras one <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand) times; and offer ten thousand oblations with <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice);

children.text: evaṃ siddha-manur mantrī trailokyaiśvarya-bhāg bhavet // Krd_7.80 //
children.translated_text: Thus, the <s>mantrī</s> (ritualist) whose mantra is perfected would become the possessor of sovereignty over the three worlds.

children.text: mantra-śreṣṭhau pratyekaṃ lakṣaṃ japet | anantaraṃ paramānnena daśa-sahasraṃ juhuyāt anena siddhau mantro yasya mantrī loka-trayiśvarya-bhājanaṃ bhavati || KrdC_7.80 ||
children.translated_text: One should recite each of the two supreme mantras one hundred thousand times. Thereafter, one should offer ten thousand oblations with <s>paramānna</s> (milk-rice pudding). The ritualist whose mantra is thus perfected becomes the recipient of sovereignty over the three worlds.
He states another mantra —
Enriched with <s>Tāra</s> (Oṃ), <s>Śrī</s>-bīja, and <s>Śakti</s>-bīja; the word '<s>namo bhagavate</s>';
The word '<s>Nanda-putra</s>' in the dative; '<s>Bhūdhara</s>' (earth-bearer) joined with face-circle (<s>mukha-vṛtta</s>);
'<s>Māsa</s>-ending, <s>vapuṣe</s>' — the mantra has nineteen syllables.

children.text: tāraṃ praṇavaḥ śrī-bījaṃ bhuvaneśvarī-bījam etad-bīja-trayāḍhya namo bhagavate iti svarūpaṃ tataś caturthy-anta-nanda-putra-padaṃ bhūdharo ba-kāraḥ mukha-vṛttam ā-kāraḥ tad-yuktaḥ māṃso la-kāras tad-ante vapuṣe iti svarūpam etena ūnaviṃśati-varṇako mantra uddhṛto bhavati || KrdC_7.81 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>tāra</s> is <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ); <s>Śrī-bīja</s> (the seed-syllable of <s>Śrī</s>); <s>Bhuvaneśvarī-bīja</s>; enriched with these three seed-syllables; '<s>namo bhagavate</s>' — this is the form; then the word '<s>Nanda-putra</s>' (son of <s>Nanda</s>) in the dative case; '<s>bhūdhara</s>' is the letter <s>ba</s>; '<s>mukha-vṛtta</s>' (face-circle) is the letter <s>ā</s>; joined with that; '<s>māṃsa</s>' (flesh) is the letter <s>la</s>; at the end of that, '<s>vapuṣe</s>' — this is the form. By this, a mantra of nineteen syllables is extracted. || KrdC_7.81 ||

children.text: mantroddhāraḥ: oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ namo bhagavate nanda-putrāya bāla-vapuṣe ||
children.translated_text: Extraction of the mantra: <s>Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ namo bhagavate Nanda-putrāya bāla-vapuṣe</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s> is the <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer), <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> the metre, and the rest as previously stated is the same;
This [mantra] should be served by the wise for the attainment of all prosperity. // Krd_7.82 //

children.text: asya mantrasya brahmā ṛṣiś chando 'nuṣṭub anyad uditam | anyat sarvaṃ samānaṃ pūrvoktavad veditavyam ity arthaḥ || KrdC_7.82 ||
children.translated_text: Of this mantra, <s>Brahmā</s> is the <s>ṛṣi</s>, <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> is the metre, the rest has been stated. Everything else is the same — should be understood as previously described — this is the meaning. || KrdC_7.82 ||
He extracts [another] mantra —

children.text: tāraṃ hṛt bhagavān ṅe 'nto rukmiṇī-vallabhas tathā |
children.translated_text: The <s>tāra</s> (Oṃ), <s>hṛt</s> (<s>namaḥ</s>), '<s>bhagavān</s>' ending in dative, '<s>Rukmiṇī-vallabha</s>' likewise,
Ending with '<s>śiras</s>' (<s>svāhā</s>) — this is a sixteen-syllable [mantra] named after <s>Rukmiṇī-vallabha</s> (the beloved of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>). // Krd_7.83 //

children.text: tāraḥ praṇavaḥ hṛn namaḥ caturthy-anto bhagavān tathā caturthy-anto rukmiṇī-vallabha-śabdaḥ śiro 'ntaḥ svāhā-śabdāntaḥ etena rukmiṇī-vallabhākhyaḥ ṣoḍaśākṣaro mantraḥ kathitaḥ || KrdC_7.83 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>tāra</s> is <s>praṇava</s>; <s>hṛt</s> is <s>namaḥ</s>; '<s>bhagavān</s>' in the dative case; likewise the word '<s>Rukmiṇī-vallabha</s>' in the dative case; ending with '<s>śiras</s>' — ending with <s>svāhā</s>. By this, a sixteen-syllable mantra called <s>Rukmiṇī-vallabha</s> has been described. || KrdC_7.83 ||

children.text: vimarśaḥ : oṃ namo bhagavate rukmiṇī-vallabhāya svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Analysis: <s>Oṃ namo bhagavate Rukmiṇī-vallabhāya svāhā</s>.
This mantra bestows all prosperity; <s>Nārada</s> is remembered as its sage;
<s>Anuṣṭubh</s> is the metre, and <s>Rukmiṇī-vallabha</s> <s>Hari</s> is the deity;
With syllables [numbering] one, two, four, seven, and two — its five limbs (<s>pañcāṅga</s>). // Krd_7.84 //

children.text: asya ṛṣir nāradaḥ anuṣṭup-chandaḥ rukmiṇī-vallabho harir devateti | eketi | asya mantrasya pañcāṅgāni bhavanti | kaiḥ ? mantrasya eka-dvi-catuḥ-sapta-dvi-varṇaiḥ || KrdC_7.84 ||
children.translated_text: Its <s>ṛṣi</s> is <s>Nārada</s>; <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> is the metre; <s>Rukmiṇī-vallabha</s> <s>Hari</s> is the deity. The five limbs of this mantra are [assigned] with how many [syllables]? With one, two, four, seven, and two syllables of the mantra. || KrdC_7.84 ||
He states the meditation —
The complexion of a <s>tāpiccha</s> (tamāla) tree, his beloved upon his lap, radiant like gold, with a lotus
Rising in the left hand — embracing [her] with his own left arm, with the <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem);
She herself embracing [him] — with a golden staff shining in the other hand — may he long
Protect you — <s>Hari</s>, wearing garments yellow as <s>asana</s>-blossoms, adorned with various ornaments! // Krd_7.85 //

children.text: tāpiccha-cchavis tamāla-kāntir harir vo yuṣmān pāyāt rakṣatu | kiṃ kurvan ? aṅkasthāṃ gaurāṅgīṃ priyatamāṃ cintāmaṇi-ratna-sahitena hastena āliṅgan | ātmānaṃ devaṃ vā dakṣiṇa-kareṇa āśliṣyantīm ālliṅgantīm | kīdṛśo hariḥ ? āliṅganānya-haste kāñcana-daṇḍo yasya | tathā punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? asana-vṛkṣa-puṣpavat pīte vastre yasya saḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? nānā-prakāro 'laṅkāro yasya || KrdC_7.85 ||
children.translated_text: Of <s>tāpiccha</s> (tamāla) complexion — with the luster of the tamāla tree — may <s>Hari</s> protect you all. Doing what? Embracing his dearest one — the fair-limbed beloved — seated on his lap, with a hand bearing the <s>cintāmaṇi</s> gem. She embracing — clasping — the Lord himself with her right hand. Of what kind is <s>Hari</s>? In whose other hand — the hand not embracing — is a golden staff. Again, of what kind? Whose garment is yellow like the flowers of the <s>asana</s> tree. Again, of what kind? One adorned with various kinds of ornaments. || KrdC_7.85 ||
He states the <s>puraścaraṇa</s> (preparatory rites) —

children.text: dhyātvaivaṃ rukmiṇī-nāthaṃ japyāl lakṣam imaṃ manum |
children.translated_text: Having thus meditated on the lord of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, one should recite this mantra one <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand) times;

children.text: ayutaṃ juhuyāt padmair aruṇair madhurāplutaiḥ // Krd_7.86 //
children.translated_text: And should offer ten thousand oblations with red lotuses immersed in sweetness. // Krd_7.86 //

children.text: evaṃ pūrvoktaṃ rukmiṇī-vallabhaṃ rukmiṇī-nāthaṃ dhyātvā imaṃ mantraṃ lakṣam ekaṃ japatu | ghṛta-madhu-śarkarāsiktaiḥ lohita-padmair api daśa-sahasraṃ juhuyāt || KrdC_7.86 ||
children.translated_text: Having thus meditated on the previously described <s>Rukmiṇī-vallabha</s> — the lord of <s>Rukmiṇī</s> — one should recite this mantra one <s>lakṣa</s> times.
