With red lotuses sprinkled with ghee, honey, and sugar, one should also offer ten thousand oblations. || KrdC_7.86 ||
He shows the worship —

children.text: arcayen nityam aṅgais taṃ nāradādyair diśādhipaiḥ |
children.translated_text: One should daily worship him with the limb-[deities], <s>Nārada</s> and others, the directional lords,
And the thunderbolt etc. — a man [does this] for the attainment of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). // Krd_7.87 //

children.text: pīṭha-pūjā pūrvavat | āvaraṇa-pūjā tu kathyate-pratyahaṃ taṃ hariṃ pūjayet | kair aṅgair ācakrādyaiḥ sāyāhna-pūjoktaiḥ nārada-prabhṛtibhiś ca diśādhipair indrādyaiḥ teṣām āyudhair vajrādyaiḥ | kīdṛśaṃ ? puruṣārtha-catuṣṭaya-pradam || KrdC_7.87 ||
children.translated_text: The seat-worship (<s>pīṭha-pūjā</s>) is as before. The encirclement worship is described: daily one should worship that <s>Hari</s>. With which [deities]? With the limbs — discus etc. — as stated in the evening worship, and <s>Nārada</s> and others, with directional lords — <s>Indra</s> etc. — and their weapons — thunderbolt etc. Of what kind? Bestowing the four goals of human life (<s>puruṣārtha</s>). || KrdC_7.87 ||
He extracts another mantra —
At the end of '<s>līlā-daṇḍa</s>' (playful staff), the word '<s>gopī-jana-saṃsakta-doḥ</s>' (with arm attached to the cowherd-women);
At the end of '<s>daṇḍa</s>,' '<s>bāla-rūpa</s>' (of child-form); then the word '<s>megha-śyāma</s>' (cloud-dark). // Krd_7.88 //

children.text: bhagavān viṣṇur ity uktvā vahni-jāyāntako manuḥ |
children.translated_text: Having said '<s>bhagavān Viṣṇuḥ</s>,' ending with '<s>vahni-jāyā</s>' (<s>svāhā</s>) — the mantra;
It is of twenty-nine syllables; <s>Nārada</s> is declared as its sage. // Krd_7.89 //
<s>Anuṣṭubh</s> is the metre, and the deity is <s>Hari</s> bearing the playful staff (<s>līlā-daṇḍa</s>);
With syllables [numbering as] Manu (14), ocean (4), sense-organ (5), fire (3), and ocean (4), the limb-assignment is established. // Krd_7.90 //

children.text: līlā-daṇḍāvadhau līlā-daṇḍa-śabdānte gopī-jana-saṃsakta-doḥ padam anantaraṃ daṇḍa-śabdānte bāla-rūpeti padaṃ tad anu megha-śyāmeti padaṃ tataḥ śabdo 'pi kākākṣivat sambadhyate | tad anu bhagavān viṣṇuḥ sambodhanāntam uktvā svāhā-śabdānte ekonatriṃśad-akṣaro mantra uddhriyatām ity arthaḥ | asya mantrasya nārada ṛṣir anuṣṭup chando līlā-daṇḍo harir devateti | manv-abdhīti | asya mantrasyāṅga-kriyā manuś caturdaśaḥ abdhiś catuṣṭayaṃ karaṇaṃ pañca agnis trayaś catvāro 'bdhir etat-saṅkhyākair mantra-varṇair matā saṃmatā pañcāṅgānīty arthaḥ || KrdC_7.90 ||
children.translated_text: At the end of the word '<s>līlā-daṇḍa</s>,' the word '<s>gopī-jana-saṃsakta-doḥ</s>'; then at the end of the word '<s>daṇḍa</s>,' the word '<s>bāla-rūpa</s>'; then the word '<s>megha-śyāma</s>'; the word '<s>tataḥ</s>' also connects [like] the crow-and-eye [principle]. Then, having said '<s>bhagavān Viṣṇuḥ</s>' in the vocative, ending with <s>svāhā</s> — a mantra of twenty-nine syllables should be extracted — this is the meaning. Of this mantra, <s>Nārada</s> is the <s>ṛṣi</s>, <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> the metre, <s>Hari</s> bearing the <s>līlā-daṇḍa</s> is the deity. The limb-assignment of this mantra: <s>Manu</s> is fourteen; <s>abdhi</s> (ocean) is four; <s>karaṇa</s> (sense-organ) is five; <s>agni</s> (fire) is three; <s>abdhi</s> (ocean) is four — the five limbs (<s>pañcāṅga</s>) are established with mantra-syllables of these numbers — this is the meaning. || KrdC_7.90 ||
Extraction of the mantra: <s>Līlā-daṇḍa-gopī-jana-saṃsakta-dor-daṇḍa-bāla-rūpa-megha-śyāma bhagavan Viṣṇo svāhā</s>.
He states the meditation —
Enchanting with the playful staff held in his own left hand,
The cowherd maidens and the celestial beauties;
May the deity, slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, of mighty strides, with the right hand upon his beloved on his lap,

children.text: devaḥ śriyaṃ nihata-kaṃsa urukramo vaḥ // Krd_7.91 //
children.translated_text: Grant you all prosperity! // Krd_7.91 //

children.text: saṃmohayan nija-kavāmakarastha-līlā-daṇḍena gopa-yuvatīḥ sura-sundarīś ca diśyān nija-priyatamāṃsaga-dakṣa-hasto devaḥ śriyaṃ nihata-kaṃsa urukramo vaḥ || KrdC_7.91 ||
children.translated_text: Enchanting with the playful staff held in his own left hand, the cowherd maidens and the celestial beauties; may the deity, slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, of mighty strides (<s>Urukrama</s>), with the right hand upon his beloved on his lap, grant you all prosperity! || KrdC_7.91 ||
He states the <s>puraścaraṇa</s> —
Having thus meditated, one should recite one <s>lakṣa</s>; with sesame and rice-grains
Anointed with the three sweets, one should offer oblations; and should worship with the limbs, directional guardians, etc. // Krd_7.92 //

children.text: evaṃ pūrvoktaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ dhyātvā lakṣam ekaṃ japet | tad anu ghṛta-madhu-śarkarā-sahitais tila-taṇḍulair daśa-sahasraṃ juhuyāt | aṅgeti | pīṭha-pūjā pūrvavad āvaraṇa-pūjā-pañcāṅgair indrādyaiś ceti || KrdC_7.92 ||
children.translated_text: Having thus meditated on the previously described <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, one should recite one <s>lakṣa</s>. Then, with sesame and rice-grains combined with ghee, honey, and sugar, one should offer ten thousand oblations. The seat-worship is as before; the encirclement worship [is done] with the five limbs, <s>Indra</s> and others, etc. || KrdC_7.92 ||
He states the fruit of daily worship —

children.text: līlā-daṇḍaṃ hariṃ yo vai bhajate nityam ādarāt |
children.translated_text: Whoever indeed worships <s>Hari</s> bearing the playful staff daily with reverence,

children.text: sa pūjyate sarva-lokais taṃ bhajed indirā sadā // Krd_7.93 //
children.translated_text: He is honored by all people, and <s>Indirā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) always serves him. // Krd_7.93 //

children.text: yo manuṣyaḥ pratyahaṃ līlā-daṇḍa-dharaṃ hariṃ sevate sa sarva-janaiḥ pūjyate | tam indirā lakṣmīḥ sarvadā bhajate || KrdC_7.93 ||
children.translated_text: Whatever man daily serves <s>Hari</s> bearing the playful staff, he is honored by all people. <s>Indirā</s> — <s>Lakṣmī</s> — always serves him. || KrdC_7.93 ||
He extracts another mantra —
The thirteenth vowel (<s>Oṃ</s>) joined with '<s>śārṅgī</s>' (the archer, i.e., letter <s>ga</s>), the distinction being '<s>sa-keśava</s>' (with <s>a</s>);

children.text: tathā māṃsa-yugaṃ bhāya śiraḥ saptākṣaro manuḥ // Krd_7.94 //
children.translated_text: Likewise a pair of '<s>māṃsa</s>' (flesh, i.e., <s>la</s>-letters), '<s>bhāya</s>,' and '<s>śiras</s>' (<s>svāhā</s>) — a seven-syllable mantra. // Krd_7.94 //

children.text: trayodaśa-svara oṃkāras tena yutaḥ śārṅgī ga-kāraḥ medo va-kāraḥ | kīdṛśaḥ ? sa keśavaḥ a-kāra-sahitaḥ | tathā māṃsa-yugaṃ la-kāra-dvayam iti bhāya śiraḥ svāhā | anena saptākṣaro mantra uktaḥ || KrdC_7.94 ||
children.translated_text: The thirteenth vowel is <s>Oṃkāra</s>; joined with that, '<s>śārṅgī</s>' is the letter <s>ga</s>; '<s>meda</s>' (fat) is the letter <s>va</s>. Of what kind? '<s>Sa-keśava</s>' — accompanied by the letter <s>a</s>. Likewise, '<s>māṃsa-yuga</s>' (pair of flesh-letters) is two <s>la</s>-letters. '<s>Bhāya</s>' — '<s>śiras</s>' is <s>svāhā</s>. By this, a seven-syllable mantra is stated. || KrdC_7.94 ||
Form of the mantra: <s>Go-vallabhāya svāhā</s>.
He states the <s>ṛṣi</s> etc. —
The limb-assignment is with discus etc.; <s>Nārada</s> is remembered as its sage;

children.text: chanda uṣṇig-devatā ca go-vallabha udāhṛtaḥ // Krd_7.95 //
children.translated_text: The metre is <s>Uṣṇik</s>, and the deity is declared as <s>Go-vallabha</s> (the beloved of cows). // Krd_7.95 //

children.text: ācakrādyaiḥ pañcāṅga-karaṇam | asya mantrasya nārada ṛṣiḥ | uṣṇik chandaḥ | go-vallabhaḥ kṛṣṇo devateti || KrdC_7.95 ||
children.translated_text: The five-limb assignment is with discus etc. Of this mantra, <s>Nārada</s> is the <s>ṛṣi</s>; <s>Uṣṇik</s> is the metre; <s>Go-vallabha</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) is the deity. || KrdC_7.95 ||
He states the meditation —
<s>Acyuta</s> is to be meditated upon, standing in the midst of a herd of tawny (<s>kapilā</s>) cows,
Calling them, holding a flute in his left arm;
A lasso and a staff in the other [hand], cloud-dark in complexion,
Wearing yellow garments, with a crest-ornament made of peacock feathers. // Krd_7.96 //

children.text: acyutaḥ kṛṣṇo dhyeyaḥ | kīdṛśaḥ ? kapilā-gaṇo go-viśeṣa-samūhas tasyābhyantara-vartī | kiṃ kurvan ? tāḥ kapilā āhvayan abhimukhīkurvan | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? adakṣiṇa-doṣṇi vāma-hastena sa-randhraṃ vaṃśaṃ vahan | aparatra dakṣiṇa-haste daṇḍa-sahita-go-bandhana-rajjuṃ dadhat | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? payoda-nīlau megha-śyāmaḥ pīta-vasanaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? ahi-ripur mayūraḥ | tasya picchaṃ śikhaṇḍaḥ | tena kṛto 'vataṃsaḥ karṇālaṅkāraḥ śiro-bhūṣaṇaṃ vā yena sa tathā || KrdC_7.96 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Acyuta</s> — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — is to be meditated upon. Of what kind? Situated within a herd of <s>kapilā</s> cows — a particular breed of cow. Doing what? Calling — attracting — those <s>kapilā</s> cows. Again, of what kind? Holding in the left arm a perforated bamboo flute. In the other — the right hand — bearing a cow-tethering rope with a staff. Again, of what kind? Cloud-dark — dark like a raincloud — wearing yellow garments. Again, of what kind? '<s>Ahi-ripu</s>' (enemy of serpents) is the peacock; its feather is the <s>picccha</s> (plume); with that is made the <s>avataṃsa</s> — ear-ornament or head-ornament — such is he. || KrdC_7.96 ||
He states the <s>puraścaraṇa</s> —
One should recite this seven <s>lakṣa</s>s (seven hundred thousand) times; and offer seven thousand oblations
With cow's milk; [in worship,] between the limbs and directional guardians, one should worship eight groups of cows. // Krd_7.97 //

children.text: imaṃ mantraṃ muni-lakṣaṃ sapta-lakṣaṃ japet | go-dugdhaiḥ sapta-sahasraṃ juhuyāt | aṅga-pūjānantraṃ dikpāla-pūjāyāḥ prāk go-gaṇāṣṭakaṃ pūjanīyaṃ go-gaṇāṣṭakaṃ ca prathamādi yathā syāt |
children.translated_text: One should recite this mantra seven <s>lakṣa</s>s times. One should offer seven thousand oblations with cow's milk. After the limb-worship and before the directional-guardian worship, the eight groups of cows should be worshipped. And the eight groups of cows, in order, are as follows:
The first is golden-colored, the <s>kapilā</s>; the second is tawny-reddish;
The third is tawny-eyed; the fourth is jaggery-tawny.

children.text:
pañcamī abhra-varṇā syād etāḥ syur uttamā gavām |
caturthī piṅgalā ṣaṣṭhī saptamī khura-piṅgalā |
aṣṭamī kapilā goṣu vijñeyaḥ kapilā-gaṇaḥ || ity anenoktam || KrdC_7.97 ||

children.translated_text: He states another application —
Whoever daily offers one thousand and eight [oblations] with milk,

children.text: pakṣāt sa go-gaṇair āḍhyo daśārṇenaiṣa vā vidhiḥ // Krd_7.98 //
children.translated_text: Within a fortnight he becomes rich in herds of cows; with the ten-syllable [mantra], this is also the procedure. // Krd_7.98 //

children.text: go-dugdhaiḥ pratidinaṃ yo 'ṣtādhikaṃ sahasraṃ juhuyāt sa pañcadaśa-dinābhyantare go-samūhena sampanno bhavati | eṣa vidhi-prayogo daśākṣara-mantreṇa vā kārya ity arthaḥ || KrdC_7.98 ||
children.translated_text: Whoever daily offers one thousand and eight oblations with cow's milk, within fifteen days he becomes endowed with a herd of cows. This application-procedure should be performed with the ten-syllable mantra as well — this is the meaning. || KrdC_7.98 ||
He states another mantra —

children.text: sa-lavo vāsudevo hṛt ṅe 'ntaṃ ca bhagavat-padam |
children.translated_text: '<s>Sa-lava</s>' (with <s>bindu</s>) <s>Vāsudeva</s> [= Oṃ]; <s>hṛt</s> (<s>namaḥ</s>); the word '<s>bhagavat</s>' ending in dative;
The word '<s>Śrī-Govinda</s>' likewise [in dative] — this is declared as twelve syllables. // Krd_7.99 //

children.text: lavo binduḥ | tat-sahito vāsudevaḥ oṃkāraḥ arthāt praṇavaḥ | oṃ namaḥ caturthy-antaṃ bhagavat-padaṃ tathā śrī-govinda-padaṃ caturthy-antam | etena dvādaśākṣaro mantra uddhṛtaḥ || KrdC_7.99 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Lava</s>' is <s>bindu</s> (the nasal dot); accompanied by that, '<s>Vāsudeva</s>' is <s>Oṃkāra</s> — that is, <s>praṇava</s>. '<s>Oṃ namaḥ</s>' — the word '<s>bhagavat</s>' in the dative; likewise the word '<s>Śrī-Govinda</s>' in the dative. By this, a twelve-syllable mantra is extracted. || KrdC_7.99 ||
Form of the mantra: <s>Oṃ namo bhagavate Śrī-Govindāya</s>.
He states the <s>ṛṣi</s> etc. —
The mantra has <s>Nārada</s> as sage, <s>Gāyatrī</s> as metre, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as deity; then the limbs
Should be assigned with syllables [numbering as] eye (1-2), <s>Veda</s> (4), and elements (5), both individually and collectively. // Krd_7.100 //

children.text: kvacin munir iti pāṭho na yuktaḥ | asamanvayāt paunarukutyāc ca kintu manur ity eva pāṭhaḥ | ayam iti pāṭho yuktyālabhyata iti rudradharaḥ || KrdC_7.100 ||
children.translated_text: The reading '<s>muni</s>' (sage) in some [manuscripts] is not appropriate — due to lack of syntactic connection and redundancy. Rather, the reading '<s>manu</s>' (mantra) is correct. The reading '<s>ayam</s>' (this) is obtained by reasoning — [says] <s>Rudradhara</s>. || KrdC_7.100 ||
He states the meditation —
I salute <s>Murāri</s> (the slayer of <s>Mura</s>), seated on a gem-throne at the foot of a wish-fulfilling tree,
Dark-hued, wearing yellow garments, with conch and staff shining in his lotus-hands;
Surrounded by cows with flowing milk, bathed by streams of nectar pouring from a vessel
Held in the mighty hand of <s>Indra</s> (the lord of the immortals), with eyes [beautiful] like fresh lotus petals. // Krd_7.101 //

children.text: murāriṃ vande | kīdṛśaṃ ? kalpa-vṛkṣa-mūlāvasthite padma-rāga-maṇi-ghaṭite siṃhāsane upaviṣṭam | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ ? nīlābhaṃ śyāmaṃ tathā pīta-vastraṃ tathā hasta-padme śobhamānau śaṅkha-vetrau yasya | taṃ tathā sa-praśravābhiḥ kṣīra-stanābhiḥ gobhir vṛtaṃ veṣṭitam | tathā amara-pater indrasya prauḍho baliṣṭho yo hastas tad-avasthito yaḥ kumbhaḥ ghaṭas tasmāt prasravad amṛta-dhārābhiḥ snapitaṃ tathābhinavaṃ nūtanaṃ yad ambhojaṃ padmaṃ tasya patravad ābhā kāntir nayanayor yasya tam || KrdC_7.101 ||
children.translated_text: I salute <s>Murāri</s> (the enemy of <s>Mura</s>). Of what description? Seated upon a throne made of <s>padma-rāga</s> (ruby) gems, situated at the base of a wish-fulfilling tree. Again, of what description? Dark-complexioned (<s>nīlābha</s>), wearing yellow garments, with conch and staff adorning his lotus-hands. Surrounded — encircled — by cows with flowing milk-udders (<s>sa-praśrava</s>). And bathed by streams of nectar flowing from a vessel held in the powerful hand of <s>Indra</s>, the lord of the gods. With eyes having the luster of the petals of a fresh, newly-bloomed lotus. || <s>KrdC</s> 7.101 ||
He states the <s>puraścaraṇa</s> (preparatory practice) —

children.text: dhyātvaivam acyutaṃ japtvā ravi-lakṣaṃ hunet tataḥ |
children.translated_text: Having thus meditated on <s>Acyuta</s>, having recited [the mantra], one should then offer twelve <s>lakṣa</s>s;
With milk, twelve thousand [oblations]; and one should worship him daily. // <s>Krd</s> 7.102 //

children.text: evaṃ pūrvoktam acyutaṃ dhyātvā dvādaśa-lakṣaṃ japtvā dugdhair dvādaśa-sahasraṃ juhuyāt | pratyahaṃ vā amuṃ pūjayet || KrdC_7.102 ||
children.translated_text: Having thus meditated on <s>Acyuta</s> in the previously described form, having recited twelve <s>lakṣa</s>s (1.2 million), one should offer twelve thousand oblations with milk. Or, one should worship him daily. || <s>KrdC</s> 7.102 ||
He shows the special worship at temples and other places —
Established in a cowpen, or at one's own home, in images and the like;
The worship of the entire retinue — those are <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s attendants (<s>pārṣada</s>s). // <s>Krd</s> 7.103 //
At the front of the doorway, on the offering-altar (<s>bali-pīṭha</s>), they should be worshipped; and the king of birds (<s>Garuḍa</s>), in front of it;

children.text: caṇḍa-pracaṇḍau prāg dhātṛ-vidhātārau ca dakṣiṇe // Krd_7.104 //
children.translated_text: <s>Caṇḍa</s> and <s>Pracaṇḍa</s> in the east; <s>Dhātṛ</s> and <s>Vidhātṛ</s> in the south; // <s>Krd</s> 7.104 //

children.text: jayaḥ sa-vijayaḥ paścād balaḥ prabala uttare |
children.translated_text: <s>Jaya</s> and <s>Vijaya</s> in the west; <s>Bala</s> and <s>Prabala</s> in the north;

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ dvāra-śriyaṃ ceṣṭvā dvāstheśān yugmaśo 'rcayet // Krd_7.105 //
children.translated_text: Above, having worshipped <s>Dvāra-śrī</s> (the Fortune of the Door), one should worship the door-guardians in pairs. // <s>Krd</s> 7.105 //
The <s>Vāstu-puruṣa</s> (spirit of the dwelling) is to be worshipped there, stationed in the middle of the door-altar;

children.text: dvārāntaḥ-pārśvayor arcyā gaṅgā ca yamunā nidhī // Krd_7.106 //
children.translated_text: On the inner sides of the doorway, <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>, and the [two] treasuries (<s>nidhi</s>s), should be worshipped. // <s>Krd</s> 7.106 //

children.text: koṇeṣu vighnaṃ durgāṃ ca vāṇīṃ kṣetreśam arcayet |
children.translated_text: In the corners, one should worship <s>Vighna</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>), <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Vāṇī</s> (<s>Sarasvatī</s>), and the Lord of the field (<s>Kṣetreśa</s>);
One should worship the <s>Vāstu-puruṣa</s> in the center of the dwelling, with concentrated mind,
Or in the south-west direction, following the arrangement of the deities — the wise one [should do so]. // <s>Krd</s> 7.107 //

children.text: goṣṭhe go-sthāne pratiṣṭhitaṃ sthāpitaṃ | tathā ātma-gehe suvarṇādi-ghaṭita- pratimādiṣu pratiṣṭhitaṃ viṣṇuṃ pūjayed iti pūrveṇānvayaḥ | tāḥ pūrvoktā eva samasta-parivāra-pūjāḥ kāryāḥ | tathā vakṣyamāṇāś ca viṣṇu-pārṣadāḥ pūrvādi-caturdvārāgra-bhāge bali-dāna-pīṭhe dviśaḥ pūjyā atra tripāṭhinaḥ |
children.translated_text: Established — installed — in a cowpen, a place for cows. And in one's own home, in images fashioned of gold etc. — thus installed, one should worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> — this connects with the preceding [verse]. Those same previously mentioned complete retinue-worships should be performed. And the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-attendants about to be described — at the offering-altar at the front portion of the four doorways in the east and other directions — should be worshipped in pairs — thus the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s.

children.text: dvādaśākṣara-govinda-mantrasya pūjā-prasaṅgena pūrvokta-dīkṣā-pūjāyāṃ tathāikāla-pūjāysv api pūrvādi-catur-dvāra-pūjā viśeṣataḥ kartavyatvena jñātavyā samasta-parivārāyācyutāya namo namaḥ | viṣṇu-pārṣadebhyo namo namaḥ | anena mantra-dvayena pūrvādi-caturdvārāgra-bhāge bali-dāna-pīṭhe pūjayed ity arthaḥ | pakṣīndro garuḍaḥ | tad-agrataḥ bali-dāna-pīṭhāgrataḥ pūjyaḥ |
children.translated_text: In connection with the worship of the twelve-syllable <s>Govinda</s>-mantra, the previously described <s>dīkṣā</s>-worship as well as the single-time worship should be understood as requiring the worship at the four doors in the east etc. in particular: '<s>samasta-parivārāya acyutāya namo namaḥ</s>' (Homage to <s>Acyuta</s> with the entire retinue); '<s>viṣṇu-pārṣadebhyo namo namaḥ</s>' (Homage to <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s attendants) — with these two mantras, one should worship at the offering-altar at the front of the four doors in the east etc. — this is the meaning. The king of birds (<s>pakṣīndra</s>) is <s>Garuḍa</s>; he should be worshipped in front of the offering-altar.

children.text: viṣṇu-pārṣadān darśayati-prāg iti | catur-asra-catur-dvārordhva-bhāge dvāra-śriyaṃ pūjayitvā caṇḍādīn dvau dvau kṛtvā pūjayet | anukrameṇa pūrva-dvāram ārabhya dvāra-bali-pīṭhayor madhye vāstu-puruṣāya nama iti pūjayet | dvārānta iti catur-dvāra-madhyobhaya-phalake gaṅgā-yamune pūjye, tathā śaṅkha-nidhi-padma-nidhī ca pūjyau | tad anu maṇḍape praviśyāgneyādi-koṇeṣu punar vāstu-puruṣaṃ saṃyataḥ san pūjayet || KrdC_7.103-107 ||
children.translated_text: He shows the <s>Viṣṇu</s>-attendants — beginning with '<s>prāk</s>' (in the east). At the upper portion of the four doors of the quadrangular [structure], having worshipped <s>Dvāra-śrī</s> (the Fortune of the Door), one should worship <s>Caṇḍa</s> and the others in pairs of two. In sequence, beginning from the eastern door, in the middle of the doorway and the offering-altar, one should worship with '<s>vāstu-puruṣāya namaḥ</s>.' At the inner sides — on both panels of the middle of the four doors — <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s> should be worshipped; likewise the <s>Śaṅkha-nidhi</s> (conch-treasure) and <s>Padma-nidhi</s> (lotus-treasure) should be worshipped. After that, entering the hall (<s>maṇḍapa</s>), in the south-east and other corners, one should again worship the <s>Vāstu-puruṣa</s> with controlled mind. || <s>KrdC</s> 7.103-107 ||
He extracts the weapon-mantra (<s>astra</s>) —

children.text: tāraṃ śārṅga-padaṃ ṅe 'ntaṃ sa-pūrvaṃ ca śarāsanam |
children.translated_text: <s>Tāra</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>); the word '<s>Śārṅga</s>' (the bow) in the dative; combined with the preceding [syllable]; and '<s>Śarāsana</s>' (bow);

children.text: huṃ phaṭ natir ity uktvāstra-mudrayāgre sthito hareḥ // Krd_7.108 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Huṃ phaṭ namaḥ</s>' — having uttered this, with the weapon-<s>mudrā</s> (gesture), standing before <s>Hari</s>, // <s>Krd</s> 7.108 //
One should cast flowers and rice-grains in the directions; then, being seated on one's seat,

children.text: vidheyam etat sarvatra sthāpiteṣu viśeṣataḥ // Krd_7.109 //
children.translated_text: This should be performed everywhere, especially for installed [images]. // <s>Krd</s> 7.109 //

children.text: tāraṃ praṇavaḥ | śārṅga-padaṃ ṅe 'ntaṃ caturthy-antaṃ sa-pūrvaṃ sa-śarāsana-śabdaṃ caturthy-antaṃ huṃ phaṭ namaḥ ity uktvā puṣpākṣataṃ catur-dikṣu astra-mudrayā choṭikayā nikṣipet | kīdṛśaḥ ? harer agre sthitaḥ | tataḥ āsane svocite upaviśet | etat sarvaṃ sarva-pūjādau kartavyaṃ sthāpiteṣu pratimādiṣu punar viśeṣataḥ kartavyam eva || KrdC_7.108-109 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tāra</s> is <s>praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>). The word '<s>Śārṅga</s>' in the dative (<s>ṅe</s>-ending, fourth case). Combined with the preceding — with the word '<s>śarāsana</s>' (bow) in the dative case. '<s>Huṃ phaṭ namaḥ</s>' — having uttered this, with the weapon-<s>mudrā</s> — a finger-snap (<s>choṭikā</s>) — one should cast flowers and rice-grains in the four directions. Of what kind? Standing before <s>Hari</s>. Then, one should be seated on one's appropriate seat. All this should be done at the beginning of every worship; for installed images and the like, it must especially be performed. || <s>KrdC</s> 7.108-109 ||
He states the seat-worship (<s>pīṭha-pūjā</s>) —
Having performed up to and including the self-worship (<s>ātmārcana</s>), then the <s>guru</s>-lineage as previously stated;
The illustrious <s>guru</s>s, beginning with the supreme [<s>guru</s>], preceded by 'great' (<s>mahā</s>), 'our' (<s>asmat</s>), and 'all' (<s>sarva</s>). // <s>Krd</s> 7.110 //

children.text: sva-dehe pūrvokta-svarūpeṇa pīṭham ārabhya sampūjya hṛdi bhagavantam abhyarcya anantaraṃ bāhya-pīṭhe pūrvavat pūrvokta-dīkṣā-prakaraṇa-kathitottara-dig-vibhāge itivad guru-paṅktiṃ pūjayet | guru-paṅktim evāha-śrī-gurūn iti | śrī-śabda-pūrvān gurūn parama-gurūn | prayogaś ca-śrī-gurubhyo namaḥ | śrīa-parama-gurubhyo namaḥ | śrī-mahā-gurubhyo namaḥ | śrī-asmad-gurubhyo namaḥ | sarva-gurubhyo namaḥ || KrdC_7.110 ||
children.translated_text: Having worshipped the seat beginning with <s>Ādhāra-śakti</s> etc. in the previously described form upon one's own body, and having worshipped the Lord in the heart, thereafter, on the external seat, as before — in the northern section as stated in the previously described <s>dīkṣā</s> chapter — one should worship the <s>guru</s>-lineage. He specifies the <s>guru</s>-lineage — '<s>Śrī-gurūn</s>' etc. The <s>guru</s>s preceded by the word '<s>Śrī</s>'; the supreme <s>guru</s>s (<s>parama-guru</s>). The application is: '<s>Śrī-gurubhyo namaḥ</s>' (Homage to the illustrious <s>guru</s>s); '<s>Śrī-parama-gurubhyo namaḥ</s>' (Homage to the illustrious supreme <s>guru</s>s); '<s>Śrī-mahā-gurubhyo namaḥ</s>' (Homage to the illustrious great <s>guru</s>s); '<s>Śrī-asmad-gurubhyo namaḥ</s>' (Homage to our illustrious <s>guru</s>s); '<s>Sarva-gurubhyo namaḥ</s>' (Homage to all <s>guru</s>s). || <s>KrdC</s> 7.110 ||
Their sandals (<s>pādukā</s>s); <s>Nārada</s> and others of the earlier <s>siddha</s>s (perfected ones); thereafter,

children.text: tato bhāgavatāṃś ceṣṭvā vighnaṃ dakṣiṇato 'rcayet // Krd_7.111 //
children.translated_text: Having worshipped the <s>Bhāgavata</s>s (devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s>), one should worship <s>Vighna</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>) to the south. // <s>Krd</s> 7.111 //

children.text: tat pādukābhyaḥ nāradādibhyaḥ pūrva-siddhebhyaḥ bhāgavatebhya iti laghu-dīpikā-kāraḥ | śrī-guru-pādukābhyo namaḥ | śrī-parama-guru-pādukā-ādi-guru-pādukā-mahā-guru-pādukā-asmad-guru-pādukā-sarva-guru-pādukābhyo nama iti tripāṭhinaḥ | evaṃ guru-paṅkti-pīṭhasyottare samabhyarcya dakṣiṇe gaṇeśaṃ pūjayet || KrdC_7.111 ||
children.translated_text: To those sandals (<s>pādukā</s>s); to <s>Nārada</s> and others; to the earlier <s>siddha</s>s; to the <s>Bhāgavata</s>s — thus [says] the author of the <s>Laghu-dīpikā</s>. '<s>Śrī-guru-pādukābhyo namaḥ</s>' (Homage to the sandals of the illustrious <s>guru</s>); '<s>Śrī-parama-guru-pādukā</s>, <s>ādi-guru-pādukā</s>, <s>mahā-guru-pādukā</s>, <s>asmad-guru-pādukā</s>, <s>sarva-guru-pādukābhyo namaḥ</s>' — thus [say] the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s. Thus, having worshipped to the north of the <s>guru</s>-lineage seat, one should worship <s>Gaṇeśa</s> to the south. || <s>KrdC</s> 7.111 ||
Having worshipped the seat as before, one should then worship <s>Śrī Govinda</s>;

children.text: rukmiṇīṃ satyabhāmāṃ ca pārśvayor indram agrataḥ // Krd_7.112 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and <s>Satyabhāmā</s> on the sides; <s>Indra</s> in front; // <s>Krd</s> 7.112 //
Behind, having worshipped <s>Surabhi</s> (the wish-fulfilling cow), on the filaments [of the lotus], the limb-deities (<s>aṅga-devatā</s>s);

children.text: arcyā hṛdādi-varmāntā dikṣv astraṃ koṇakeṣu ca // Krd_7.113 //
children.translated_text: Should be worshipped, from the heart [limb] to the armor [limb]; the weapon [mantra] in the directions and corners. // <s>Krd</s> 7.113 //

children.text: pūrvokta-prakāreṇādhāra-śaktyādi-pīṭha-mantrāntaṃ sampūjya devam āvāhya aghyādibhir upacāraiḥ pūjayet | āvaraṇa-pūjām āha-rukmiṇīm iti | govinda-dakṣiṇa-vāmayoḥ pārśvayoḥ karṇikāyāṃ rukmiṇī satyabhāmā ca sampūjyā devāgre ca indraṃ sampūjya deva-pṛṣṭhe tu surabhiṃ pūrvādi-caturdik-koṇeṣu keśareṣu hṛd-ādi-varmāntā aṅga-devatāḥ pūjyāḥ | keśareṣu koṇeṣu punar-astram aṅgaṃ pūjayet || KrdC_7.112-113 ||
children.translated_text: Having worshipped the seat in the previously described manner from <s>Ādhāra-śakti</s> up to the <s>pīṭha-mantra</s>s, having invoked the deity, one should worship with <s>arghya</s> and other <s>upacāra</s>s (offerings). He states the <s>āvaraṇa</s>-worship (worship of surrounding circles) — '<s>Rukmiṇī</s>' etc. On the right and left sides of <s>Govinda</s>, on the pericarp, <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and <s>Satyabhāmā</s> should be worshipped. In front of the deity, <s>Indra</s> should be worshipped. Behind the deity, <s>Surabhi</s> (the celestial cow) [should be worshipped]. On the four directional filaments and corners, the limb-deities from the heart to the armor should be worshipped. On the corner-filaments, one should again worship the weapon limb (<s>astra-aṅga</s>). || <s>KrdC</s> 7.112-113 ||
<s>Kālindī</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Nāgnajitī</s>, and the other six consorts (<s>śakti</s>s),

children.text: daleṣu pīṭha-koṇeṣu vahny-ādy-arcyāś ca kiṅkiṇīḥ // Krd_7.114 //
children.translated_text: On the petals; on the corners of the seat, fire [-god] and others should be worshipped; and the bells (<s>kiṅkiṇī</s>), // <s>Krd</s> 7.114 //
The ropes (<s>dāman</s>), the staff (<s>yaṣṭi</s>), and the flute (<s>veṇu</s>), in front; the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> and <s>Kaustubha</s> [marks],

children.text: agrato vanamālāṃ ca dikṣv aṣṭāsu tato 'rcayet // Krd_7.115 //
children.translated_text: And in front the <s>Vanamālā</s> (forest-garland); then in the eight directions one should worship: // <s>Krd</s> 7.115 //

children.text: pāñcajanyaṃ gadāṃ cakraṃ vasudevaṃ ca devakīm |
children.translated_text: The <s>Pāñcajanya</s> (conch), the mace (<s>gadā</s>), the discus (<s>cakra</s>), <s>Vasudeva</s> and <s>Devakī</s>,
<s>Nanda-gopa</s> and <s>Yaśodā</s>, together with cows, cowherds, and cowherd-girls (<s>gopikā</s>s). // <s>Krd</s> 7.116 //

children.text: kālindy-ādyāḥ śaktayo deva-patnyaḥ patreṣu pūjyāḥ | ādi-padena sunandā-mitravindā-sulakṣmaṇā-parigrahaḥ āgneyādi-pīṭha-koṇeṣu kiṅkiṇi-dāmādīn pūjayet | tatra śrī-kṛṣṇa-kṣudra-ghaṇṭikām agni-koṇe | go-rakṣaṇārthaṃ dāmāni nairṛte go-preraṇārthaṃ lakuṭaṃ vāyau vaṃśam īśāna-koṇe devasyāgre śrīvatsa-kaustubhau | śrīvatsa-kaustubhāgrataḥ vanamālāṃ tad-upari aṣṭa- dikṣu pāñcajanyādaya iti | pāñcajanyāya namaḥ sa-go-gopāla-gopikābhyo nama ity antāḥ pūjyāḥ ādi-padena gadā-cakra-vasudeva-devakīnanda-yaśodā-parigrahaḥ || KrdC_7.114-116 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kālindī</s> and the other consorts — the wives of the deity — should be worshipped on the petals. By the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), <s>Sunandā</s>, <s>Mitravindā</s>, and <s>Sulakṣmaṇā</s> are included. On the corners of the seat in the south-east etc., one should worship the bells and ropes etc. Specifically: the small bell (<s>kṣudra-ghaṇṭikā</s>) of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> in the south-east corner; the ropes (<s>dāman</s>) for cow-protection in the south-west; the staff (<s>lakuṭa</s>) for driving cows in the north-west; the bamboo flute (<s>vaṃśa</s>) in the north-east corner. In front of the deity, the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> and <s>Kaustubha</s> [marks]; in front of the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> and <s>Kaustubha</s>, the <s>Vanamālā</s> (forest-garland); above that, in the eight directions, the <s>Pāñcajanya</s> etc. — '<s>Pāñcajanyāya namaḥ</s>' up to '<s>sa-go-gopāla-gopikābhyo namaḥ</s>' should be worshipped. By the word '<s>ādi</s>,' the mace, discus, <s>Vasudeva</s>, <s>Devakī</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, and <s>Yaśodā</s> are included. || <s>KrdC</s> 7.114-116 ||
<s>Indra</s> and the other [directional guardians]; <s>Kumuda</s> and the other [elephants]; and <s>Viśvaksena</s> to the north. // <s>Krd</s> 7.117 //
<s>Kumuda</s>, <s>Kumudākṣa</s>, <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>, and <s>Vāmana</s>;
<s>Śaṅku-karṇa</s>, <s>Sarva-netra</s>, <s>Sumukha</s>, and <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s>.

children.text: indrādyāḥ sva-sva-dikṣu pūjyāḥ tad-astrāṇi vajrādīny ādi-śabda-grāhyāṇi tathā kumudādyāś cāṣṭa-gajāḥ tat-upari sva-sva-dikṣu pūjyāḥ tad-bahir-devatottare viṣvaksenaṃ pūjayet || KrdC_7.117 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> and the others should be worshipped in their respective directions. Their weapons — the thunderbolt etc. — are to be understood from the word '<s>ādi</s>.' Likewise, <s>Kumuda</s> and the other eight elephants should be worshipped in their respective directions above [the directional guardians]. Beyond those deities, to the north, one should worship <s>Viśvaksena</s>. || <s>KrdC</s> 7.117 ||
He states the fruit of the worship —

children.text: eka-kālaṃ dvikālaṃ vā tri-kālaṃ ceti goṣṭhagam |
children.translated_text: Once daily, twice daily, or thrice daily — <s>Śrī Govinda</s> who dwells in the cowpen,

children.text: śrī-govindaṃ yajen nityaṃ gobhyaś ca yavasa-pradaḥ // Krd_7.118 //
children.translated_text: One should worship always, and offer fodder to the cows. // <s>Krd</s> 7.118 //
Long-lived, free from affliction, with milch-cows, grains, wealth, and the like,

children.text: putrair mitrair ihāḍho 'nte prayāti paraṃ padam // Krd_7.119 //
children.translated_text: With sons and friends — prosperous here, at the end one goes to the supreme abode. // <s>Krd</s> 7.119 //

children.text: goṣṭhagaṃ vraja-gaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ pratyahaṃ eka-kālaṃ dvikālaṃ tri-kālaṃ pūjayet | gobhyaś ca grāsa-pradaḥ sannihita-loke cirāyur nirbhayo dhenu-dhānya-suvarṇādibhiḥ putra-mitrādibhiś ca sampanno bhavati deha-pātānte ca viṣṇu-lokaṃ ca gacchati || KrdC_7.118-119 ||
children.translated_text: One should worship <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> who dwells in the cowpen — who goes to <s>Vraja</s> — every day, once, twice, or three times. And one who provides fodder to the cows — in this world, he becomes long-lived, fearless, endowed with milch-cows, grains, gold, and the like, and prosperous with sons and friends; and at the time of death, he goes to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. || <s>KrdC</s> 7.118-119 ||
He states another mantra —
The upper dental [letter] (<s>Oṃ</s>); <s>Śārṅgī</s> (the letter <s>ga</s>); <s>Cakrī</s> (the letter <s>ka</s>); combined with the right ear [vowel] (<s>u</s>);
<s>Māṃsa</s> (the letter <s>la</s>); '<s>nāthāya</s>' (to the Lord) in its own form; ending with salutation (<s>namaḥ</s>) — the root mantra of eight syllables. // <s>Krd</s> 7.120 //

children.text: ūrdhvad-antaḥ oṃkāraḥ tena sahitaḥ śārṅgī ga-kāraḥ cakrī ka-kāraḥ dakṣiṇa-karṇa-yuk u-kāra-sahitaḥ māṃsī la-kāraḥ nāthāyeti svarūpaṃ naty-anto namaḥ padāntaḥ ayam aṣṭākṣaro mūla-mantra-saṃjñakaḥ || KrdC_7.120 ||
children.translated_text: The upper dental [letter] is <s>Oṃkāra</s>; combined with that; <s>Śārṅgī</s> is the letter <s>ga</s>; <s>Cakrī</s> is the letter <s>ka</s>; combined with the right-ear [vowel] (<s>u</s>-vowel); <s>māṃsī</s> is the letter <s>la</s>; '<s>nāthāya</s>' is in its own form; ending with '<s>namaḥ</s>.' This eight-syllable [mantra] bears the designation of root mantra (<s>mūla-mantra</s>). || <s>KrdC</s> 7.120 ||
He states the sage (<s>ṛṣi</s>) and other [details] —

children.text: ṛṣir brahmā ca gāyatrī-cchandaḥ kṛṣṇas tu devatā |
children.translated_text: The sage (<s>ṛṣi</s>) is <s>Brahmā</s>; the meter is <s>Gāyatrī</s>; the deity is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;

children.text: yuga-varṇaiḥ samastena proktaṃ syād aṅga-pañcakam // Krd_7.121 //
children.translated_text: With the paired syllables [taken] together, the fivefold limbs (<s>aṅga-pañcaka</s>) are declared. // <s>Krd</s> 7.121 //

children.text: asya mantrasya brahmā ṛṣiḥ gāyatrī-cchandaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇo devatā ca śabdo 'nukta-samuccaye tena bīja-śakty-adhiṣṭhātṛ-devatā daśākṣaravat tathā asya mantrasya mantrottha-varṇānāṃ caturbhir yugma-varṇaiś caturaṅga-samagreṇa ca mantreṇāṅga-pañcakaṃ jñeyam || KrdC_7.121 ||
children.translated_text: Of this mantra, <s>Brahmā</s> is the sage; <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the meter; <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> is the deity. The word '<s>ca</s>' indicates unstated inclusion — thereby the seed (<s>bīja</s>), power (<s>śakti</s>), and presiding deity are as for the ten-syllable [mantra]. Likewise, for this mantra, with four paired syllables derived from the mantra, and with the complete mantra, the fivefold limbs should be understood. || <s>KrdC</s> 7.121 ||
He states the meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) —
Five years old, exceedingly spirited, in the courtyard,
Running about, with curly locks tumbling over his eyes,
Adorned with bells, bracelets, necklaces, and anklets —
Meditate upon this cowherd boy (<s>gopa-bālaka</s>). // <s>Krd</s> 7.122 //

children.text: gopa-śiśuṃ namata | kīdṛśaṃ ? pañca-varṣa-vayaḥsthaṃ tathā atibaliṣṭhaṃ tathā prāṅgaṇe dhāvamānaṃ tathā cāticañcalekṣaṇaṃ tathā kiṅkiṇī kṣudra-ghaṇṭikā valayaḥ kaṅkaṇaḥ hāro muktāhāraḥ nūpuras tulākoṭir etair añjitaṃ bhūṣitam || KrdC_7.122 ||
children.translated_text: Salute the cowherd child. Of what description? Five years of age; and exceedingly powerful; and running in the courtyard; and with very restless eyes; adorned — decorated — with bells (<s>kiṅkiṇī</s>, small bells), bracelets (<s>valaya</s>), necklace (<s>hāra</s>, pearl necklace), and anklets (<s>nūpura</s>). || <s>KrdC</s> 7.122 ||
He states the <s>puraścaraṇa</s> —
Having thus meditated, one should recite eight <s>lakṣa</s>s (800,000); then the same number in thousands,
One should offer with firewood from the <s>Brahma</s>-tree (<s>palāśa</s>), or with <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice). // <s>Krd</s> 7.123 //

children.text: evaṃ pūrvoktaṃ dhyātvā aṣṭa-lakṣaṃ mantraṃ japet | tad anu palāśa-vṛkṣa-samidbhiḥ paramānnena vāṣṭa-sahasraṃ juhuyāt || KrdC_7.123 ||
children.translated_text: Having thus meditated in the previously described form, one should recite the mantra eight <s>lakṣa</s>s (800,000 times). Thereafter, with firewood from the <s>palāśa</s> (Butea monosperma) tree, or with <s>paramānna</s> (milk-rice pudding), one should offer eight thousand oblations. || <s>KrdC</s> 7.123 ||
He states the method of worship —
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> installed in a temple should be worshipped daily with this [mantra];
Having performed the door-worship etc. up to and including the seat-worship, according to the stated path. // <s>Krd</s> 7.124 //

children.text: dhavala-gṛhe sthāpitaṃ kṛṣṇam amunā vakṣyamāṇa-prakāreṇa pratyahaṃ pūjayet | dvāra-pūjām ārabhya pīṭha-pūjā-paryantaṃ pūrvokta-mantra-vartmanā kuryāt || KrdC_7.124 ||
children.translated_text: Having installed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in a white house, one should worship [him] daily in the manner about to be described. From the door-worship up to the seat-worship, one should perform [everything] along the path of the previously stated mantra.

children.text: madhye 'rca-pad dhariṃ dikṣu vidikṣv aṅgāni ca kramāt |
children.translated_text: In the center, one should worship <s>Hari</s> upon the lotus; in the cardinal directions and intermediate directions, the limbs (<s>aṅga</s>s) in sequence.
<s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, <s>Pradyumna</s>, and <s>Aniruddha</s>;

children.text: rukmiṇī satyabhāmā ca lakṣmaṇā jāmbavaty api |
children.translated_text: <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇā</s>, and <s>Jāmbavatī</s> as well;

children.text: dig-vidikṣv arcayed etān indra-vajrādikān bahiḥ // Krd_7.126 //
children.translated_text: one should worship these in the cardinal and intermediate directions; outside, <s>Indra</s>, the thunderbolt (<s>vajra</s>), and the others.

children.text: padma-madhye hariṃ pūjayet | pūrvādi-dik-keśareṣu hṛd-ādy-aṅga-catuṣṭayam | āgneyādi-vidik-keśareṣu astram aṅgam pūjayet | vāsudeva iti | pūrvādi-dik-patreṣu vāsudevādīn pūjayet | āgneyādi-vidik-patreṣu rukmiṇy-ādyāḥ pūjayet | tad-bāhye sva-sva-dikṣu indādīn, tad anu vajrādīn pūjayed ity arthaḥ || KrdC_7.126 ||
children.translated_text: In the center of the lotus, one should worship <s>Hari</s>. On the filaments in the cardinal directions beginning with the east, [one should worship] the four limbs beginning with <s>hṛd</s> (heart). On the filaments in the intermediate directions beginning with the south-east, one should worship the weapon (<s>astra</s>) limb. '<s>Vāsudeva</s>' etc. — on the petals in the cardinal directions beginning with the east, one should worship <s>Vāsudeva</s> and the others. On the petals in the intermediate directions beginning with the south-east, one should worship <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and the others. Outside of that, in their respective directions, [one should worship] <s>Indra</s> and the others; thereafter, the thunderbolt (<s>vajra</s>) and the others — this is the meaning.
He states the fruit —

children.text: yo 'muṃ mantraṃ japen nityaṃ vidhinety arcayed dharim |
children.translated_text: Whoever recites this mantra daily and worships <s>Hari</s> according to rule,

children.text: sa sarva-sampat-sampūrṇo nityaṃ śuddhaṃ padaṃ vrajet // Krd_7.127 //
children.translated_text: he, filled with all prosperity, goes eternally to the pure abode.

children.text: yaḥ pumān ukta-vidhinā harim arcayet | amuṃ mantraṃ japet sa sarvaiśvaryaṃ sampannaḥ san nityam avināśi śuddham avidyā tat-kārya-rahitaṃ padaṃ brahmākhyaṃ prāpnoti || KrdC_7.127 ||
children.translated_text: The man who worships <s>Hari</s> according to the stated rule and recites this mantra — he, having become endowed with all sovereignty, attains the eternal, imperishable, pure — free from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and its effects — abode called <s>Brahman</s>.
He states another mantra —
After <s>Tāra</s> (Oṃ), <s>Śrī</s> [seed-syllable], <s>Śakti</s> [seed-syllable], and <s>Māra</s> (love-seed), one should utter the word '<s>Śrī Kṛṣṇāya</s>';
above that, '<s>Śrī Govindāya</s>'; then '<s>Śrī Gopī-jana</s>';

children.text: vallabhāya tatas triḥ śrī-siddhi-gopālako manuḥ // Krd_7.128 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Vallabhāya</s>'; then <s>Śrī</s> three times — [this] is the <s>Siddhi-Gopālaka</s> mantra.

children.text: tāraḥ praṇavaḥ śrīḥ śrī-bījaṃ śakti-bījaṃ kāma-bījānte śrī-kṛṣṇāyeti svarūpaṃ tad anu śrī-govindāyeti svarūpaṃ tad anu śrī-gopī-jana-vallabhāyeti svarūpaṃ śrī-bīja-trayam iti siddhi-gopālako mantra uddhṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Tāra</s> is <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ); <s>Śrī</s> is the <s>Śrī-bīja</s> (seed-syllable of <s>Śrī</s>); <s>Śakti-bīja</s> [and] <s>Kāma-bīja</s> at the end; '<s>Śrī Kṛṣṇāya</s>' is the form; after that, '<s>Śrī Govindāya</s>' is the form; after that, '<s>Śrī Gopī-jana-vallabhāya</s>' is the form; with the trio of <s>Śrī-bīja</s>s — thus the <s>Siddhi-Gopālaka</s> mantra is extracted.
He states the meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) —
Seated in a bower of <s>mādhavī</s>-creepers, guarded by <s>Garuḍa</s>;
absorbed in divine play — meditating on <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, one should recite.

children.text: cakrī vasu-svara-yutaḥ sargy ekārṇo manur mataḥ // Krd_7.130 //
children.translated_text: <s>Cakrī</s> (the disc, i.e., <s>ka</s>); with <s>vasu-svara</s> (the eighth vowel); <s>sargī</s> (with <s>visarga</s>) — this one-syllable mantra is considered.

children.text: rāma-kṛṣṇau smaran japet | kīdṛśau ? mādhavī-latā-maṇḍapa-samupasthitau tathā garuḍena sevitau | ekākṣarādi-gopāla-mantrān darśayati-cakrīti | ka-kāro vasu-svaraḥ aṣṭama-svaraḥ ṛ-kāras tena sahita iti laghu-dīpikā-kāraḥ | munisvaraḥ sapta-svaras tena sahita iti rudra-dharaḥ | sargī visarga-sahitaḥ ity ekākṣaro mantraḥ || KrdC_7.129-130 ||
children.translated_text: Meditating on <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, one should recite. Of what kind? Seated in a bower of <s>mādhavī</s>-creeper, and attended by <s>Garuḍa</s>. He shows the one-syllable and other <s>Gopāla</s>-mantras — with '<s>Cakrī</s>' etc. <s>Ka</s>-letter; <s>vasu-svara</s> is the eighth vowel, the <s>ṛ</s>-letter, combined with that — thus [says] the author of the <s>Laghu-dīpikā</s>. '<s>Muni-svara</s> is the seventh vowel,' combined with that — thus [says] <s>Rudradhara</s>. '<s>Sargī</s>' means accompanied by <s>visarga</s> — thus the one-syllable mantra.

children.text: kṛṣṇeti dvy-akṣaraḥ kāma-pūrvas try-arṇaḥ sa eva tu |
children.translated_text: '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' — [this] is the two-syllable [mantra]; preceded by the love-seed (<s>kāma</s>), [it becomes] three-syllable; that same [mantra]

children.text: sa eva catur-arṇaḥ syāt ṅe 'nto 'nyaś catur-akṣaraḥ // Krd_7.131 //
children.translated_text: becomes four-syllable [with dative ending]; another four-syllable [mantra] ends in the dative (<s>ṅe</s>).

children.text: vakṣyate pañca-varṇaḥ syāt kṛṣṇāya nama ity api |
children.translated_text: The five-syllable [mantra] will be stated; '<s>Kṛṣṇāya namaḥ</s>' is also [one];
'<s>Kṛṣṇāya</s>' placed between a pair of love-seeds (<s>smara-dvandva</s>) — another five-syllable [mantra].

children.text: kṛṣṇeti svarūpaṃ dvy-akṣaro mantraḥ | sa eva dvy-akṣaraḥ kāma-bīja-pūrvaś cet tadā try-akṣaro mantro bhavati-sa eva try-akṣaraḥ caturthī-vibhakty-antaś cet tadā catur-akṣaro mantraḥ anyaḥ kṛṣṇāyeti svarūpaṃ smara-dvandva-kāma-bīja-dvayasya madhye yadā bhavati tadā aparaḥ pañcākṣaro mantro bhavati || KrdC_7.131-132 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' is the form — a two-syllable mantra. That same two-syllable [mantra], if preceded by the love-seed (<s>kāma-bīja</s>), then it becomes a three-syllable mantra. That same three-syllable [mantra], if ending in the dative case (fourth inflection), then it becomes a four-syllable mantra. Another — '<s>Kṛṣṇāya</s>' is the form — placed between a pair of love-seeds (<s>kāma-bīja-dvaya</s>), when [it is so arranged], it becomes another five-syllable mantra.
'<s>Gopālāya</s>' ending with the fire-god's wife (<s>Svāhā</s>) — the six-syllable [mantra] is declared;
'<s>Kṛṣṇāya</s>' enriched with the love-seed, ending with the fire-god's wife — another [six-syllable mantra].
The [first] six-syllable [mantra] was previously stated; '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' and '<s>Govinda</s>' again,
in the dative case, [form] the seven-syllable [mantra]; another seven-syllable [mantra] was previously stated.

children.text: gopālāyeti svarūpaṃ vahnijāyā svāheti pada-dvayena ṣaḍ-akṣaraḥ kathitaḥ | kāma-bīja-sahita-kṛṣṇāyeti svāheti pada-dvayena ca ṣaḍ-akṣaro mantra uddhṛtas tayāparaḥ ṣaḍ-akṣaraḥ prāg eva kathitaḥ sa ca klīṃ kṛṣṇāya namaḥ iti | kṛṣṇa-govindakau śabdau yadi caturthy-antau bhavatas tadā saptākṣaro mantro 'paraḥ saptākṣaraḥ prāg uditaḥ sa ca go-vallabhāya svāheti || KrdC_7.133-4 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Gopālāya</s>' is the form; <s>Vahni-jāyā</s> (fire-god's wife) is <s>Svāhā</s> — with these two words, the six-syllable [mantra] is described. '<s>Kṛṣṇāya</s>' combined with the love-seed, and with the word <s>Svāhā</s> — another six-syllable mantra is extracted. Yet another six-syllable [mantra] was previously stated — that is '<s>klīṃ Kṛṣṇāya namaḥ</s>.' If the words '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' and '<s>Govinda</s>' end in the dative case, then [they form] a seven-syllable mantra. Another seven-syllable [mantra] was previously stated — that is '<s>Go-vallabhāya svāhā</s>.'
<s>Śrī</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, and <s>Māra</s> [seed-syllables]; '<s>Kṛṣṇāya</s>'; <s>Māra</s> — another seven-syllable [mantra];
'<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' and '<s>Govinda</s>' in the dative, enriched with <s>Smara</s> (love-seed) — the eight-syllable [mantra].

children.text: śrī-śakti-mārāḥ śrī-bhuvaneśvarī-māra-bījāni kṛṣṇāyeti mārānto 'paraḥ saptākṣaro mantraḥ kṛṣṇa-govinda-śabdau ṅe 'ntau caturthy-antau | kīdṛśau ? kāma-bījāḍhyau iti vasu-varṇaḥ aṣṭākṣaro mantraḥ || KrdC_7.135 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī-Śakti-Māra</s> — the <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Bhuvaneśvarī</s>, and <s>Māra</s> seed-syllables; '<s>Kṛṣṇāya</s>'; ending with <s>Māra</s> — another seven-syllable mantra. The words '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' and '<s>Govinda</s>' in the dative (<s>ṅe-anta</s>). Of what kind? Enriched with the love-seed (<s>kāma-bīja</s>) — thus the eight-syllable (<s>vasu-varṇa</s>) mantra.
'<s>Dadhi-bhakṣaṇa</s>' (curd-eater) in the dative, with the fire-god's wife (<s>Svāhā</s>) — another eight[-syllable mantra];

children.text: suprasannātmane proktvā mama ity aparo 'ṣtakaḥ // Krd_7.136 //
children.translated_text: having uttered '<s>Suprasannātmane</s>' (to the one of supremely serene self), [with] '<s>mama</s>' (mine) — another eight[-syllable mantra].

children.text: caturthy-anto dadhi-bhakṣaṇa-śabdaḥ vahnijāyā svāhā etair varṇair aparo 'ṣtākṣaro mantraḥ suprasannātmane svarūpam uktvā nama iti vadet ity aparo 'ṣtākṣaro mantraḥ || KrdC_7.136 ||
children.translated_text: The word '<s>Dadhi-bhakṣaṇa</s>' in the dative case; <s>Vahni-jāyā</s> is <s>Svāhā</s> — with these syllables, another eight-syllable mantra. '<s>Suprasannātmane</s>' is the form; having uttered [this], one should say '<s>namaḥ</s>' — thus another eight-syllable mantra.

children.text: prāk prokto mūla-mantraś ca navārṇaḥ smara-saṃyutaḥ |
children.translated_text: The previously proclaimed root mantra (<s>mūla-mantra</s>) — the nine-syllable [mantra] — is conjoined with <s>Smara</s> (love-seed);
'<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' and '<s>Govinda</s>' in the dative, ending with '<s>namaḥ</s>' — another nine-syllable [mantra].

children.text: prāg-uktaś cāṣṭākṣaro mūla-mantraḥ smara-saṃyutaḥ kāma-bīja-yuktaḥ san navākṣaro bhavati | sa ca klīṃ gokula-nāthāya nama iti | kṛṣṇa-govindakau ṅe 'ntau caturthy-antau smara-saṃyutau yadi bhavatas tadā navākṣaro mantro bhavati | yady etāv eva namo 'ntakau namaḥ śabdāntau bhavatas tadā paro navākṣaro mantraḥ || KrdC_7.137 ||
children.translated_text: The previously stated eight-syllable root mantra, conjoined with <s>Smara</s> — combined with the love-seed — becomes nine-syllable. That is: '<s>klīṃ Gokula-nāthāya namaḥ</s>.' If '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' and '<s>Govinda</s>' in the dative case are conjoined with <s>Smara</s>, then [they form] a nine-syllable mantra. If these same two end with '<s>namaḥ</s>' — end with the word <s>namaḥ</s> — then [that is] another nine-syllable mantra.

children.text: klīṃ glauṃ klīṃ śyāmalāṅgāya namas tu syād daśārṇakaḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Klīṃ glauṃ klīṃ Śyāmalāṅgāya namaḥ</s>' — this would be the ten-syllable [mantra];

children.text: śiro 'nto bāla-vapuṣe klīṃ kṛṣṇāya smṛto budhaiḥ // Krd_7.138 //
children.translated_text: ending with <s>śiras</s> (<s>svāhā</s>), '<s>Bāla-vapuṣe klīṃ Kṛṣṇāya</s>' — [this] is recognized by the wise.

children.text: uktaṃ chandas tu gāyatrī devatā kṛṣṇa īḍitaḥ |
children.translated_text: The meter (<s>chandas</s>) stated [for these] is <s>Gāyatrī</s>; the deity worshipped is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;

children.text: ka-lā-ṣaḍga-dīrghakair aṅgam athāmuṃ cintayed dharim // Krd_7.139 //
children.translated_text: with <s>ka</s>, <s>la</s>, and long vowels in groups of six, [one forms] the limbs; then one should meditate on this <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: klīṃ glauṃ klīṃ śyāmalāṅgāya nama iti daśa-varṇako mantraḥ śiro 'ntaḥ svāhāntaḥ bāla-vapuṣe iti padaṃ klīṃ kṛṣṇāyeti ekādaśākṣaro mantraḥ budhaiḥ smṛtaḥ | uktānām ṛṣy-ādikam āha-eteṣām ekākṣaram ārabhyaikādaśākṣara-paryantānāṃ dvāviṃśati mantrāṇām ṛṣir nāradaḥ gāyatrī-chandaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇo devatā | aṅgāny āha-kaleti | ka-kāra-la-kārābhyāṃ ṣaḍ-dīrghakair napuṃsaka-rahita-ṣaḍ-dīrgha-svaraiḥ klāṃ klīṃ klūṃ klauṃ kalaḥ ebhir ity arthaḥ || KrdC_7.139 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Klīṃ glauṃ klīṃ Śyāmalāṅgāya namaḥ</s>' — this is the ten-syllable mantra. Ending with <s>śiras</s> (<s>svāhā</s>), '<s>Bāla-vapuṣe</s>' is the word; '<s>klīṃ Kṛṣṇāya</s>' — this is the eleven-syllable mantra, recognized by the wise. He states the <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer) and other attributes of the stated [mantras]: for these twenty-two mantras, from the one-syllable up to the eleven-syllable, the <s>ṛṣi</s> is <s>Nārada</s>; the meter is <s>Gāyatrī</s>; the deity is <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>. He states the limbs — with '<s>kala</s>' etc. With <s>ka</s>-letter and <s>la</s>-letter, [combined with] the six long vowels excluding the neuter [vowels] — <s>klāṃ</s>, <s>klīṃ</s>, <s>klūṃ</s>, <s>klauṃ</s>, <s>kalaḥ</s> — with these — this is the meaning.
He states the meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) —
May <s>Mukunda</s> protect [you] — radiant as a deeply dark blue lotus, with eyes like red lotuses, seated upon a lotus;
a child, with tinkling bells placed upon the calves, waist, and chest;

children.text: dorbhyāṃ haiyaṅgavīṇaṃ dadhad ativimalaṃ pāyasaṃ viśva-vandyo
children.translated_text: holding in both hands fresh butter (<s>haiyaṅgavīna</s>) and extremely pure milk-rice (<s>pāyasa</s>), worshipped by the entire universe,
surrounded by cows, <s>gopī</s>s, and cowherds, with a necklace gleaming with tiger-claw [gems] — may he [protect] you forever.

children.text: avyād vyākopa-nīlāmbuja-rucir aruṇāmbhoja-netrāmbujastho bālo jaṅghā-kaṭīra-sthala-kalita-raṇat-kiṅkiṇīko mukundaḥ dorbhyāṃ haiyaṅgavīṇaṃ dadhad ativimalaṃ pāyasaṃ viśva-vandyo go-gopī-gopa-vīto rurunakha-vilasat-kaṇṭha-bhūṣaś ciraṃ vaḥ || KrdC_7.140 ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Mukunda</s> protect [you] — radiant as a deeply dark blue lotus, with eyes like red lotuses, seated upon a lotus; a child, with tinkling bells placed upon the calves, waist, and chest; holding in both hands fresh butter (<s>haiyaṅgavīna</s>) and extremely pure milk-rice, worshipped by the entire universe, surrounded by cows, <s>gopī</s>s, and cowherds, with a necklace gleaming with tiger-claw [gems] — may he [protect] you forever.
He states the <s>puraścaraṇa</s> (preliminary practice) for these [mantras] —

children.text: dhyātvaivam ekam eteṣāṃ lakṣaṃ japyān manuṃ tataḥ |
children.translated_text: Having meditated thus, one should recite one <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand) of any one of these mantras; then
with <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice) combined with ghee and rock-sugar, one should offer ten thousand (<s>ayuta</s>) oblations.

children.text: yathoktaṃ dhyānaṃ kṛtvā eteṣāṃ madhye ekaṃ mantraṃ lakṣaṃ japet | tad anu ghṛta-khaṇḍa-sāra-yuktaiḥ paramānnair daśa-sahasraṃ juhuyāt || KrdC_7.141 ||
children.translated_text: Having performed the meditation as described, one should recite one <s>lakṣa</s> of any one among these mantras. After that, with <s>paramānna</s> (fine milk-rice) combined with ghee and sugar-candy essence, one should offer ten thousand oblations into the fire.
One should perform <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) for the same count as the <s>homa</s> (fire-offering) count of the other mantras;

children.text: tarpaṇaṃ vihitaṃ nityaṃ yo 'rcayet susamāhitaḥ // Krd_7.142 //
children.translated_text: <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) is prescribed; whoever worships daily with full concentration —
the limbs (<s>aṅga</s>s) [beginning from] fire (<s>Agni</s>) and ending with peace (<s>Śānti</s>), from heart (<s>hṛd</s>) to armor (<s>kavaca</s>);

children.text: arcayet purato netram astraṃ dikṣu vahniḥ punaḥ // Krd_7.143 //
children.translated_text: one should worship; in front, the eye (<s>netra</s>) and the weapon (<s>astra</s>); in the directions, fire again;
<s>Indra</s>, the thunderbolt (<s>vajra</s>), and others should be worshipped — this worship has been declared.

children.text: ity ekam eṣāṃ mantrāṇāṃ bhajed yo manu-vittamaḥ // Krd_7.144 //
children.translated_text: Thus, whoever — the best knower of mantras — among these mantras, worships even one,
all objects are within his grasp; he is worshipped by the immortals.

children.text: sadyaḥ phala-pradaṃ mantraṃ vakṣye 'nyaṃ catur-akṣaram // Krd_7.145 //
children.translated_text: I shall declare another four-syllable mantra that bestows immediate fruit;
that [mantra] is proclaimed as having the word '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' placed between a pair of <s>Māra</s> (love-seeds);

children.text: ṛṣy-ādyam aṅga-ṣaṭkaṃ ca prāg-uktaṃ proktam asya tu // Krd_7.146 //
children.translated_text: the <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer) and other [attributes], and the six limbs, are as previously stated for this [mantra].

children.text: tad anu tāvad daśa-sahasraṃ tarpayet | evaṃ prakāreṇaikasmin mantre siddhe jāte tad anyeṣāṃ sakṛt puraścaraṇānām ekaviṃśati mantrāṇāṃ japa-homa-saṅkhyayā vinaiva hutāyutena tarpaṇam eva puraścaraṇaṃ vihitaṃ karaṇīyam | eteṣāṃ mantrāṇāṃ homa-saṅkhyayā ayutenaiva tarpaṇaṃ vihitam |
children.translated_text: Thereafter, one should perform <s>tarpaṇa</s> of ten thousand. In this manner, when one mantra has been perfected, then for the remaining twenty-one mantras — without the counts of recitation and fire-offering of each individual <s>puraścaraṇa</s> — merely <s>tarpaṇa</s> with ten thousand [oblations] constitutes the <s>puraścaraṇa</s>. For these mantras, <s>tarpaṇa</s> with ten thousand — equal to the <s>homa</s> count — is prescribed.

children.text: pūjām āha-nityam iti | nityaṃ sarvadā susamāhitaḥ saṃyataḥ san pūjayet | vahny-ādī-śāntam āgneya-koṇam ārabhya īśāna-koṇa-paryanta-hṛd-ādi-kavaca-paryantam aṅga-catuṣṭayaṃ pūjayet purato 'gre netram astraṃ pūjayet |
children.translated_text: He states the worship — with 'daily.' Daily — at all times — being well-concentrated (<s>susamāhita</s>), one should worship. From the south-east corner beginning with <s>Agni</s> up to the north-east corner of <s>Īśāna</s>, ending with peace — one should worship the four limbs from heart (<s>hṛd</s>) up to armor (<s>kavaca</s>). In front — before [the deity] — one should worship the eye (<s>netra</s>) and the weapon (<s>astra</s>).

children.text: pūrvādi-caturdikṣu indrādīn pūjayet | tad anu-vajrādīn iti upasaṃharati | eṣāṃ mantrāṇāṃ saparyā pūjā kathitā |
children.translated_text: In the four cardinal directions beginning with the east, one should worship <s>Indra</s> and the others. Thereafter, the thunderbolt and the others — he concludes. The worship (<s>saparyā</s>) of these mantras has been described.

children.text: phalam āha-ity ekam iti | amunā prakāreṇa yaḥ sādhakottama eṣāṃ mantrāṇāṃ madhye ekaṃ mantraṃ bhajet upāsīta tasya sarve puruṣārthā hasta-prāpyāḥ devaiś cāsau pūjyate |
children.translated_text: He states the fruit — with 'thus one' etc. In the described manner, whoever — the best among practitioners — among these mantras, worships even one mantra — serves and practices [it] — for him, all <s>puruṣārtha</s>s (goals of human life) are within hand's reach, and he is worshipped by the gods as well.

children.text: mantrāntaram āha-sadya iti | tātkālika-phala-dāyakam aparaṃ caturakṣara-mantraṃ vakṣye sa-catur-akṣaraḥ kāma-bīja-dvaya-madhyasthena kṛṣṇa-padena kathitaḥ |
children.translated_text: He states another mantra — with 'immediate' etc. I shall declare another four-syllable mantra that bestows immediate (<s>tātkālika</s>) fruit. That four-syllable [mantra] is described with the word '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' placed between a pair of love-seeds.

children.text: ṛṣy-ādikam asya ṛṣiś chando daivatam aṅga-ṣaṭkaṃ ca prāg uktaṃ pūrva-mantra-samuhe kathitaṃ boddhavyam || KrdC_7.142-146 ||
children.translated_text: Its <s>ṛṣi</s> and other [attributes] — the seer, meter, deity, and six limbs — are as previously stated, as declared in the preceding group of mantras — this should be understood.
He states the meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) —
<s>Vāsudeva</s>, seated on the shining pericarp of a lotus arisen from the root of the glorious wish-fulfilling tree,
bathed by innumerable gems cascading from the interior of a lotus hanging from the branch of that [tree];

children.text: hemābhaḥ sva-prabhābhis tri-bhuvanam akhilaṃ bhāsayan vāsudevaḥ
children.translated_text: golden in hue, illuminating the entire three worlds with his own radiance,

children.text: pāyād vaḥ pāyasādo 'navarata-navanītāmṛtāśī vaśī saḥ // Krd_7.147 //
children.translated_text: may he protect you — the eater of milk-rice, the one who ceaselessly partakes of ever-fresh butter-nectar, the self-controlled one.

children.text: vāsudevo vo yuṣmān pāyāt | kīdṛśaḥ ? yaḥ śrī-yukta-kalpa-vṛkṣa-mūlodgata-padme śobhamānā yā karṇikā tatropaviṣṭaḥ | tathā kalpa-druma-śākhālambi yat padmaṃ tasyodaraṃ tato vigalanti prasaranti yāni asaṅkhyātāni ratnāni tair abhiṣiktaḥ | tathā suvarṇa-gauraḥ tathāva-kāntibhiḥ samastaṃ trailokyaṃ bhāsayan kṣīrānnāśī tathā sva-kāntibhiḥ samastaṃ trailokyaṃ bhāsayan kṣīrānnāśī tathā anavaratam anuvelaṃ nūtanaṃ navanītam evāmṛtaṃ tad aśnātīti || KrdC_7.147 ||
children.translated_text: May <s>Vāsudeva</s> protect you all. Of what kind? Seated on the shining pericarp of a lotus arisen from the root of the glorious wish-fulfilling tree (<s>kalpa-vṛkṣa</s>). Likewise, from the interior of a lotus hanging from the branch of the wish-fulfilling tree, innumerable gems cascade and flow forth — bathed (<s>abhiṣikta</s>) by those. Likewise, of golden complexion (<s>suvarṇa-gaura</s>); likewise, illuminating the entire three worlds with his own radiance; an eater of milk-rice (<s>kṣīrānna</s>); likewise, ceaselessly — at all times — partaking of ever-fresh butter that is itself nectar.
He states the <s>puraścaraṇa</s> (preliminary practice) —

children.text: dhyatvaivaṃ prajapel lakṣaṃ catuṣkaṃ juhuyāt tataḥ |
children.translated_text: Having thus meditated, one should recite four <s>lakṣa</s>s (four hundred thousand); then one should offer
With <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) fruits anointed with the three sweets, forty thousand [oblations].

children.text: yathoktaṃ dhyānaṃ kṛtvā lakṣa-catuṣṭayaṃ japet | tad anu ghṛta-madhu-śarkarāyutair bilva-phalaiś catvāriṃśat-sahasraṃ juhuyāt || KrdC_7.148 ||
children.translated_text: Having performed the described meditation, one should recite four <s>lakṣa</s>s. Thereafter, with <s>bilva</s> fruits combined with ghee, honey, and sugar, one should offer forty thousand [oblations].
He states the worship —
The worship is described with the limbs (<s>aṅga</s>s), treasures (<s>nidhi</s>s), <s>Indra</s> and other [directional guardians], and the thunderbolt and other [weapons];

children.text: tarpayed dinaśaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ svādu-traya-dhiyā jalaiḥ // Krd_7.149 //
children.translated_text: One should satisfy <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> daily with waters, [imagined as] the three sweets.

children.text: ṣaḍ-aṅgair nidhibhir indrādy-aṣṭa-nidhibhir indrādyair vajrādyaiś cānīlārcanā pūjā kathitā | tarpaṇam āha--tarpayed iti | pratidinaṃ svādu-traya-dhiyā ghṛta-madhu-śarkarā-buddhyā jalaiḥ kṛṣṇaṃ pūjayet || KrdC_7.149 ||
children.translated_text: The worship is described as [performed] with the six limbs, the eight treasures, <s>Indra</s> and the others, and the thunderbolt and other [weapons]. He states the <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) with 'one should satisfy': daily, with the thought of the three sweets — ghee, honey, and sugar — one should satisfy <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with water.
He states another mantra —

children.text: mārayor asya māṃsādhor raktaṃ ced aparo manuḥ |
children.translated_text: If in the <s>māra</s>-pair (the two love-seeds) of this [mantra], beneath the '<s>māṃsādha</s>' (<s>la</s>-letter), '<s>rakta</s>' (the letter <s>ra</s>) [is placed], it becomes another mantra;
The six limbs of this gem of a mantra-crown are [formed] with the six <s>kalā</s>s (vowel-extensions) lengthened.

children.text: asya pūrvokta-caturakṣara-mantrasya mārayor ādy-anta-kāma-bījayor māṃsādho la-kārasyādhastāt ced yadi raktaṃ repho bhavati tadāparaś caturakṣaraḥ klīṃ kṛṣṇa klīm iti mantraḥ | asya mantra-śikhāmaṇe mantra-śiro ratnasya kala-ṣaṭ-dīrgha kalā ṣaḍ-aṅgāni kuryād iti śeṣaḥ || KrdC_7.150 ||
children.translated_text: Of this previously described four-syllable mantra, if between the two <s>māra</s> (love-seed) positions — the beginning and end <s>kāma</s>-seeds — beneath '<s>māṃsādha</s>' (the <s>la</s>-letter), '<s>rakta</s>' (the letter <s>ra</s>) is [placed], then another four-syllable [mantra arises]: '<s>klīṃ kṛṣṇa klīm</s>.' The six limbs of this gem of a mantra-crown should be formed with the six <s>kalā</s>s (vowel-extensions) lengthened — this is to be supplied.

children.text: mantra-svarūpam: klīṃ klūṃ kleṃ kloṃ klauṃ klaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Form of the mantra: <s>klīṃ klūṃ kleṃ kloṃ klauṃ klaḥ</s>.
He states the meditation —
Seated upon a shining golden swing on the treetop of a wish-fulfilling tree in a crimson garden,
Being swung by two cowherd-women, with the radiance of blooming fresh <s>bandhūka</s> (noon-flower) and vermilion,
A child, dark-haired and beautiful, with clusters of little bells adorning his swaying waist,
I salute <s>Mukunda</s>, resplendent with a throat-ornament beautifully set with tiger-claw and love-god's-goad [pendants].

children.text: mukundam vande | kīdṛśaṃ ? āraktam aruṇaṃ yad udyānaṃ tatra yaḥ kalpa-vṛkṣas tasya śikharam agraṃ tatra lasantī yā śobhamānā suvarṇa-mayī dolā tatropaviṣṭaṃ tathā gopāṅganābhyāṃ preṅkhyamānaṃ dolāyamānaṃ vikasitaṃ praphullaṃ navīnaṃ yad bandhu-jīva-puṣpaṃ sindūraṃ tayor iva bhāvaṃ yasya taṃ tathā bālaṃ śiśuṃ tathā kṛṣṇa-keśaṃ tathā kaṭi-taṭe itas tato gacchantī yā kṣudra-ghaṇṭikā ghaṇṭā-kṣudra-ghaṇṭikā samūhas tena sambaddhaṃ tathā śārdūlasya vyāghrasya kāmāṅkuśena śobhamānaṃ yat kaṇṭhābharaṇaṃ tena śobhamānam || KrdC_7.151 ||
children.translated_text: I salute <s>Mukunda</s>. Of what description? In a crimson — reddish — garden, upon the treetop of a wish-fulfilling tree, there is a shining — beautiful — golden swing; seated upon it. Likewise, being swung — rocked — by two cowherd-women. Having the radiance of blooming — blossoming — fresh <s>bandhujīva</s> flowers and vermilion. Likewise, a child — an infant. Likewise, with dark hair. Likewise, at his waist, jingling little bells — clusters of small bells — moving here and there, adorned with those. Likewise, resplendent with a throat-ornament beautifully set with tiger-claw and love-god's-goad [pendants].
Thus —
Having thus meditated, and having recited this [mantra] in the previously stated number, with fresh red lotuses,

children.text: madhuttraya-plutair hutvāpy arcayet pūrvavad dharim // Krd_7.152 //
children.translated_text: Soaked in the three sweets, having offered [oblations] — one should worship <s>Hari</s> as before.

children.text: pūrvoktaṃ mukundaṃ dhyātvā enaṃ mantraṃ pūrvokta-saṅkhyam eva japtvā rakta-padmair nūtanair ghṛta-madhu-śarkarāyutaiḥ pūrvokta-saṅkhyam eva hutvā pūrvokta-prakāreṇa hariṃ pūjayet || KrdC_7.152 ||
children.translated_text: Having meditated upon the previously described <s>Mukunda</s>, having recited this mantra in the previously stated number, with fresh red lotuses combined with ghee, honey, and sugar, having offered the previously stated number [of oblations], one should worship <s>Hari</s> in the previously described manner.
He shows the application of the two mantras stated nearby —
With rice-sprigs (<s>śāli-mañjarī</s>), reddish, combined with the three sweets,

children.text: juhuyān nityaśo 'ṣṭārdhaṃ śatam ekena mantrayoḥ // Krd_7.153 //
children.translated_text: One should offer daily one hundred and eight, with either one of the two mantras.
Within one <s>maṇḍala</s> (cycle of days), his land shall be overflowing with abundant crops;

children.text: syāc chāli-puñja-pūrṇaṃ ca tad-veśmāśu prajāyate // Krd_7.154 //
children.translated_text: And his house shall quickly become filled with heaps of rice.

children.text: ghṛta-madhu-śarkarāmiśritāṃ lohitāṃ haimantika-dhānya-mañjarīm aṣṭottara-śatamatayor mantrayor madhye ekena mantreṇa pratyekaṃ pratyahaṃ yo juhuyāt tasya puṃsaḥ maṇḍalataḥ ekona-pañcāśad-dinād arvāk ṣaḍ-viṃśati-dinād iti laghu-dīpikā-kāraḥ | pañca-catvāriṃśad-dinānantaram iti rudradharaḥ | mahatī pṛthivī dhānyādi-samūha-vyāptā bhavati tathā tad-gṛhaṃ śāli-dhānya-samūha-vyāptaṃ śīghraṃ bhavati || KrdC_7.153-154 ||
children.translated_text: With reddish winter rice-sprigs mixed with ghee, honey, and sugar, one hundred and eight [oblations], with either one of the two mantras individually, whoever offers daily — within a <s>maṇḍala</s> — within forty-nine days, according to the <s>Laghu-dīpikā</s>-author it is within twenty-six days; according to <s>Rudradhara</s>, after forty-five days — his vast earth becomes pervaded with grain-heaps and the like; likewise his house quickly becomes filled with heaps of rice and grain.
He states the fruit —

children.text: yas tv etayor niyatam anyataraṃ bhajeta
children.translated_text: Whoever constantly devotes himself to either of these two [mantras],
Through recitation, worship, <s>homa</s>, and other [practices], having attained devotion;

children.text: śrīmān sa manmatha iva pramadāsu vāgmī
children.translated_text: Prosperous, he shall become like <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love) among women, and eloquent;

children.text: bhūyāt tanor vipadi tac ca mahocyutākhyam // Krd_7.155 //
children.translated_text: And after the [fall of the] body, in calamity, [he attains] that [abode] called the great <s>Acyuta</s>.

children.text: yaḥ pumān etayor ekaṃ niyataṃ niyato bhajeta sādhayet | kaiḥ ? japa-pūjā-homādibhiḥ | kīdṛśaḥ ? prāpta-bhaktiḥ sa lakṣmī-yuktaḥ strīṣu kāmadevavat utkṛṣṭa-vacana-bhāg bhavati | tanor vipadi śarīra-pātānantaraṃ viṣṇu-lokaṃ ca gacchati || KrdC_7.155 ||
children.translated_text: The man who constantly — with restraint — devotes himself to either one of these two [mantras] — accomplishes [the practice]. By what means? Through recitation, worship, <s>homa</s>, and other [practices]. Of what kind? Having attained devotion — he becomes endowed with <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity); among women, like the god of love; and endowed with excellent speech. After the fall of the body — after death — he goes to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

Thus ends the seventh chapter of the <s>Krama-dīpikā</s> composed by <s>Śrī Keśava Bhaṭṭācārya</s>.
||7||

(8)
Eighth Chapter
Now the <s>vaśyakara</s> (attraction-producing) application is stated —
Now is stated the <s>vaśya-vidhi</s> (attraction procedure), from the previously stated
Ten-syllable and eighteen-syllable [mantras];
The two mantras which, merely by remembrance, always bestow upon the practitioner
The quality of being dear to all the world.

children.text: pūrvokta-daśākṣarasyāṣṭadaśākṣarasya ca yau mantrau smaraṇa-mātreṇa sādhakasya sarva-jana-vallabhatvaṃ sarvadā kurutaḥ || KrdC_8.1 ||
children.translated_text: The two mantras — the previously stated ten-syllable and eighteen-syllable [mantras] — which, merely by being remembered, always make the practitioner dear to all people.

children.text: phullair vanya-pasūnair amum aruṇatarair arcayitvā dinādau
children.translated_text: Having worshipped [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], deep red, with blooming wild flowers of the most crimson hue, at the start of the day,
Daily, during the daily rites, with the worship-method stated for midday, <s>Mukunda</s>;

children.text: aṣṭopetaṃ sahasraṃ daśa-lipim anuvarya japed yaḥ sa mantrī
children.translated_text: Whoever recites the ten-syllable [mantra], the best of mantras, one thousand and eight times — that <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner)

children.text: kuryād vaśyāny avaśyaṃ mukhara-mukha-bhuvāṃ maṇḍalān maṇḍalāni // Krd_8.2 //
children.translated_text: Shall certainly bring under control circles upon circles of those on whose lips eloquence resides (i.e., learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s).

children.text: puṣpitaiḥ vanodbhava-puṣpair atilohitam amuṃ mukundaṃ nityaṃ sarvadā nitya-karmānuṣṭhāna-niṣṭhaṃ dinādau prati pratyahaḥ madhyāhnokta-pūjā-prakāreṇa pūjayitvā yo mantrī daśākṣaraṃ mantra-śreṣṭham aṣṭādhikaṃ sahasraṃ japet | maṇḍalād eva pañcāśad-dinād arvāk mukhara-mukha-bhuvāṃ vidvad-brāhmaṇānāṃ maṇḍalāni samūhān avaśyaṃ vaśyāni kuryād vaśayatīty arthaḥ || KrdC_8.2 ||
children.translated_text: With blooming wild flowers, of the deepest red, [worshipping] <s>Mukunda</s> — always, devoted to the observance of daily rites — at the beginning of the day, daily, in the manner of worship prescribed for midday, having worshipped [him], the <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) who recites the ten-syllable mantra, the best of mantras, one thousand and eight times — within a <s>maṇḍala</s>, within fifty days — shall certainly bring under control groups upon groups of learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s with eloquent speech — this is the meaning.
He shows three applications for the <s>kṣatriya</s>, <s>vaiśya</s>, and <s>śūdra</s> as well —
With jasmine (<s>jātī</s>) flowers, [meditating on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] in the attire of the best cowherd;
Absorbed in play, [or] with red <s>karavīra</s> (oleander) flowers;
With blue lotuses (<s>nīlotpala</s>), [meditating on him] absorbed in singing — having worshipped as before,
One should bring under control kings and others, in sequence.

children.text: vara-gopa-veṣaṃ śreṣṭha-gopa-rūpa-dharaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇaṃ vicintya jātī-puṣpaiḥ pūrvokta-prakāreṇa pūjayitvā daśākṣara-mantram aṣṭottara-sahasraṃ japtvā kṣatriyaṃ vaśayet krīḍāsaktaṃ dhyātvā rakta-karavīra-puṣpaiḥ pūrvokta-prakāreṇa pūjayitvā daśākṣara-mantram aṣṭottaraṃ sahasraṃ japtvā vaiśyaṃ vaśayet gīti-rataṃ gītāsaktaṃ dhyātvā nīlotpalaiḥ pūrvokta-prakāreṇa pūjayitvā daśākṣara-mantram aṣṭottara-sahasraṃ japtvā śūdraṃ vaśayet ity anena prakāreṇa nṛpādīn vaśayed ity arthaḥ || KrdC_8.3 ||
children.translated_text: Having meditated on <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> wearing the attire of the best cowherd, having worshipped in the previously described manner with jasmine flowers, having recited the ten-syllable mantra one thousand and eight times, one brings a <s>kṣatriya</s> under control. Having meditated on [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] absorbed in play, having worshipped in the previously described manner with red <s>karavīra</s> (oleander) flowers, having recited the ten-syllable mantra one thousand and eight times, one brings a <s>vaiśya</s> under control. Having meditated on [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] absorbed in singing, having worshipped in the previously described manner with blue lotuses, having recited the ten-syllable mantra one thousand and eight times, one brings a <s>śūdra</s> under control — in this manner one brings kings and others under control — this is the meaning.
He states another application —
With rice grains mixed with white flowers, sprinkled with ghee,
Having offered one thousand daily for seven nights;

children.text: kaca-bhuvi ca lalāṭe bhasma tad dhārayannā
children.translated_text: Wearing the <s>homa</s>-ash on the head and on the forehead,

children.text: vaśayati manujas trīṃ sāpi nṝṃs tadvad eva // Krd_8.4 //
children.translated_text: A man brings a woman under his control; and she too [can bring] men [under control] in the same way.

children.text: śveta-puṣpa-sahitaiḥ śveta-taṇḍulair ghṛta-miśrita-daśākṣara-mantreṇa daśa-śataṃ hutvā nityaśaḥ sapta-dina-paryantaṃ tad anu tad dhoma bhasma kaca bhuvi śirasi lalāṭe ca dhārayan nā puruṣaḥ manuja-strīṃ manuṣya-nārīm iti rudra-dharaḥ | taruṇīṃ striyaṃ vaśayatīti tripāṭhitaḥ | sāpi strī anena prayogeṇa nṝn vaśayed ity arthaḥ || KrdC_8.4 ||
children.translated_text: With white rice grains combined with white flowers, with the ten-syllable mantra, having offered one thousand [oblations], daily for seven days, thereafter wearing that <s>homa</s>-ash on the head and on the forehead — a man brings a human woman under his control — thus [says] <s>Rudradhara</s>; [he brings] a young woman under control — thus [say] the <s>Tripāṭhin</s>s. She too — a woman — by this application can bring men under control — this is the meaning.
He states another application —
Betel (<s>tāmbūla</s>), garments, flowers, collyrium (<s>añjana</s>), sandalwood paste, and other [items],
Charged with three thousand [recitations] of either one of the two mantras;
To whomever the mantra-knower gives [these], that person quickly

children.text: syāt kiṅkarā na khalu tatra vicāraṇīyam // Krd_8.5 //
children.translated_text: Becomes his servant — of this there is surely no question.

children.text: tāmbūlaṃ vastraṃ puṣpaṃ kajjalaṃ candanaṃ ca etad yad anyad vastu manvor daśāṣṭādaśākṣarayor anyatareṇaikena sahasra-trayaṃ saṃjaptaṃ yasmai janāya dadāti sādhakaḥ sa naro 'sya sādhakasya maṅkṣu śīghraṃ vaśyo bhavati | nātra saṃśaya ity arthaḥ || KrdC_8.5 ||
children.translated_text: Betel, garments, flowers, collyrium, sandalwood paste, and whatever other object — charged with three thousand recitations of either one of the two mantras — the ten-syllable or the eighteen-syllable — the practitioner gives to whichever person, that person quickly becomes subservient to the practitioner — of this there is no doubt — this is the meaning.
At the king's gate, in legal proceedings, in an assembly,
In gambling, in debate — having recited one hundred and eight [times],
Whoever utters the first word [after recitation],
He shall prevail over those seated there in that [forum].
He states another application —

children.text: rāja-samīpe kraya-vikraye sadasi akṣa-krīḍādau vāde ca yo manvor ekam aṣṭottara-śataṃ japtvā prathamata eva yāṃ vācaṃ vadati tayaiva vācā tatra vādādau upaviṣṭān asau varteta taj-jayī bhavatīty arthaḥ || KrdC_8.6 ||
children.translated_text: In the king's presence, in buying and selling, in an assembly, in dice-play and the like, and in debate — whoever, having recited one hundred and eight [times] of either mantra, then speaks whatever word first — by that very word, in that debate and the like, he prevails over those seated [opponents] — that is, he becomes victorious over them — this is the meaning.
Seated at the foot of a <s>kadamba</s> tree, the slayer of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),
Singing most sweetly with the women of <s>Vraja</s> —
Having contemplated [him thus], offering into the fire with peacock-feather [kindling-sticks] (<s>mayūra-kedhmair</s>) soaked in honey,
The mantra-knower brings the three worlds under his control.
He states another application —

children.text: kadamba-mūle upaviṣṭaṃ muramathanaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ gopībhir madhurataraṃ gāyantaṃ dhyātvā vahnau madhu-snutair mayūra-kedhmair apāmārga-samidbhir hutvā asau sādhako loka-trayaṃ vaśayati || KrdC_8.7 ||
children.translated_text: Having meditated on the slayer of <s>Mura</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, seated at the foot of a <s>kadamba</s> tree, singing most sweetly with the <s>gopī</s>s — having offered into the fire with <s>apāmārga</s> fuel-sticks (<s>mayūra-kedhmair</s>) soaked in honey — that practitioner brings the three worlds under his control.
Contemplating <s>Acyuta</s> (the Imperishable One) situated in the midst of the <s>rāsa</s> (-dance),
Whoever recites the ten-syllable [mantra] one thousand [times]
Daily — within one month, that man
Shall quickly obtain the desired maiden.
He states another application —

children.text: yo naraḥ pūrvokta-rāsa-madhya-gataṃ kṛṣṇaṃ dhyāyan daśākṣaraṃ mantraṃ pratyahaṃ daśa-śataṃ japet sa māsaikena śīghram eva vāñchitāṃ kanyāṃ prāpnoti ||8||
children.translated_text: The man who, meditating on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> situated in the midst of the previously described <s>rāsa</s> (-dance), recites the ten-syllable mantra one thousand times daily — within a single month, he quickly obtains the desired maiden.
He states another application —
Or, meditating on <s>Acyuta</s> seated upon a tall <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) [bush],
Daily, one thousand
And eight — the maiden who recites [thus], within one <s>maṇḍala</s> (cycle),
Shall obtain the desired bridegroom.

children.text: ucca-kadamba-vṛkṣa-sthaṃ vicintya pratyaham aṣṭottara-sahasraṃ daśākṣaraṃ yā kanyakā japati sā hi niścayena maṇḍalād ekona-pañcāśad dinād arvāk vāñchita-varaṃ prāpnoti || KrdC_8.9 ||
children.translated_text: Meditating on [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] situated upon a tall <s>kadamba</s> tree, daily, whichever maiden recites the ten-syllable [mantra] one thousand and eight times, she indeed certainly — within one <s>maṇḍala</s>, within forty-nine days — obtains the desired bridegroom.
He states another application with equal fruit —
Meditating on him dancing, grasping the lotus-hands of the beautiful women of <s>Vraja</s>,
The mantra-knower, reciting one <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand) of the eighteen-syllable supreme mantra,
Or else offering ten thousand [oblations] with parched rice (<s>lāja</s>) or powders soaked in honey into the fire,

children.text: uddhoḍhuṃ prajapec ca tāvad acirād ākāṅkṣitāṃ kanyakām // Krd_8.10 //
children.translated_text: Should further recite the same [number] to obtain the desired maiden before long.

children.text: acirāt śīghraṃ vāñchitāṃ kanyāṃ pariṇetuṃ mantravit sādhakaḥ gopa-yuvatī-hasta-padmāni saṃgṛhya dhṛtvā nṛtyantaṃ taṃ prasiddhaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇaṃ dhyātvā lakṣa-mātra-parimitam aṣṭādaśākṣaraṃ mantra-śreṣṭhaṃ japet | athavā lājānāṃ cūrṇair madhu-drutatarair ghṛta-madhu-śarkarā-pracurānvitaiḥ madhunā dravībhūtair iti rudradharaḥ | daśa-sahasraṃ hutvā tāvad eva saṃkhyaṃ japed ity arthaḥ || KrdC_8.10 ||
children.translated_text: Quickly — swiftly — the mantra-knower, the <s>sādhaka</s> (practitioner), grasping — holding — the lotus-hands of the cowherd maidens, meditating on that well-known <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> dancing, should recite the excellent eighteen-syllable mantra exactly one <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand) times. Or, with the powder of parched grains (<s>lājā</s>), very soft with honey — <s>Rudradhara</s> [interprets as] 'made liquid with honey' — abundantly combined with ghee, honey, and sugar, having offered ten thousand [oblations], one should recite the same count — this is the meaning. || KrdC_8.10 ||
He states another application —
With the eighteen-syllable [mantra], with [fuel-sticks] born of the <s>dvija</s>-tree (<s>palāśa</s>), anointed with the three sweets, ten thousand;

children.text: kuśais tilair vā sa-taṇḍulair vaśayituṃ dvijān juhuyāt // Krd_8.11 //
children.translated_text: Or with <s>kuśa</s> grass, sesame, or rice-grains — to subjugate <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s, one should offer oblations. // Krd_8.11 //

children.text: dvijān brāhmaṇān vaśayitum aṣṭādaśākṣara-mantreṇa dvija-tarujaiḥ palāśa-vṛkṣa-samudbhavaiḥ samidbhis tri-madhurāktaiḥ ghṛta-madhu-śarkarā-miśritair ayutaṃ daśa-sahasraṃ juhuyāt athavā tri-madhv-aktaiḥ kuśais tilaiḥ taṇḍulair vā juhuyāt || KrdC_8.11 ||
