children.translated_text: To subjugate <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s — to bring <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s under control — with the eighteen-syllable mantra, with [fuel-sticks] born of the <s>dvija</s>-tree — the <s>palāśa</s> (Butea) tree — as fuel-sticks, anointed with the three sweets — mixed with ghee, honey, and sugar — one should offer ten thousand oblations. Or, with <s>kuśa</s> grass, sesame, and rice-grains anointed with the three sweets, one should offer oblations. || KrdC_8.11 ||
He states another application —
With buds born of the <s>kṛtamāla</s> (cassia) tree, one should subjugate kings;
And with those born of the <s>kuruṇṭaka</s> (jhiṇṭī) plant, likewise;
For the merchant class (<s>viśa</s>), with sugarcane; and with those born of the <s>pāṭala</s> tree,

children.text: itarān api tadvad atho vaśayet // Krd_8.12 //
children.translated_text: One should likewise subjugate the others as well. // Krd_8.12 //

children.text: kṛta-māla-bhavaiḥ rāja-vṛkṣa-samudbhavaiḥ mukulaiḥ kalikābhiḥ hutvā nṛpatīn kṣatriyān vaśayen | kuruṇṭakajaiś ca jhiṇṭī-samudbhavaiḥ mukulair hutvā veśyāṇ vaśayet | ikṣu-rasaiḥ ikṣurakair iti pāṭhe kokilākṣomathīn atha ity arthaḥ | pāṭala-samudbhavaiḥ mukulair vā hutvā itarān śūdrān vaśayet | anukta-saṅkhyā homasya boddhavyā tasyā eva prakaraṇatvād iti || KrdC_8.12 ||
children.translated_text: With those born of the <s>kṛtamāla</s> — the rāja-vṛkṣa (royal tree) — with buds — flower-buds — having offered oblations, one should subjugate kings — <s>kṣatriya</s>s. With those born of the <s>kuruṇṭaka</s> — the <s>jhiṇṭī</s> plant — with buds, having offered oblations, one should subjugate <s>vaiśya</s>s. With sugarcane-juice — in the reading '<s>ikṣuraka</s>,' [it means] <s>kokilākṣa</s> (a herb) — '<s>atha</s>' means thus. With buds born of the <s>pāṭala</s> tree, or having offered oblations, one should subjugate the others — <s>śūdra</s>s. The unstated count of oblations should be understood [as ten thousand], since that is the count pertaining to this context. || KrdC_8.12 ||
He states another application —
With fresh lotuses, red water-lilies,
And with <s>campaka</s> and <s>pāṭala</s> flowers combined with sweetness;
One should offer ten thousand oblations in sequence, to quickly
Subjugate the finest women of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and other classes. // Krd_8.13 //

children.text: śīghraṃ mukhajādi-varāṅganā brāhmaṇādi-striyo vaśayituṃ caturbhir dravyaiḥ samadhurair madhura-traya-militaiḥ kramaśaḥ pratyekaṃ sārdha-sahasra-dvayaṃ kṛtvā daśa-sahasraṃ pratihunet juhuyāt | dravyāṇy āha-nūtanaiḥ śveta-padmaiḥ raktotpalaiś campaka-puṣpaiḥ pāṭala-puṣpaiḥ || KrdC_8.13 ||
children.translated_text: To quickly subjugate the finest women of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and other classes, with four kinds of substances mixed with the three sweets, in sequence — each numbering two thousand five hundred — making ten thousand, one should offer oblations. He states the substances: with fresh white lotuses, red water-lilies, <s>campaka</s> flowers, and <s>pāṭala</s> flowers. || KrdC_8.13 ||
He states another application —
With fresh <s>hayāri</s> (oleander) flowers, drenched in the three sweets, daily,
One thousand [oblations] for seven days — the wise one should offer at midnight;
He forcefully, instantly, renders the haughty-minded courtesan,
Tormented by the arrows of love, his own maidservant. // Krd_8.14 //

children.text: hayāri-kusumaiḥ karavīra-kusumaiḥ nūtanaiḥ tri-madhura-miśritaiḥ pratyahaṃ sahasraṃ ṛṣi-vāsaraṃ sapta-vāsaraṃ budhaḥ sādhako niśīthe rātrau pratyahaṃ pratidinaṃ juhuyāt asau ahaṅkāravatīṃ vārayoṣāṃ veśyākāma-vāṇaiḥ pīḍitāṃ haṭhāt balāt jhaṭiti śīghraṃ nija-dāsīṃ karoti || KrdC_8.14 ||
children.translated_text: With <s>hayāri</s> (oleander) flowers — flowers of the <s>karavīra</s> plant — fresh ones, mixed with the three sweets, daily — each day — one thousand [oblations], for seven days — the wise <s>sādhaka</s> (practitioner) should offer at midnight — at night — daily. He renders the proud courtesan — the prostitute tormented by the arrows of <s>Kāma</s> (the love-god) — forcefully, instantly, quickly, his own maidservant. || KrdC_8.14 ||

______________________________
He states another application —
With mustard seeds combined with salt and very soft with the three sweets,
Three thousand;
For one who offers [oblations] at night, even the beloved of <s>Śacī</s> (<s>Indra</s>)

children.text: avaśo vaśī bhavati kiṃ nv apare // Krd_8.15 //
children.translated_text: Becomes helplessly subject — what then of others? // Krd_8.15 //

children.text: lavaṇa-saṃyutaiḥ kaṭu-saṃyutair iti pāṭhe kaṭuka-saṃyutair ity arthaḥ | madhurārdratarair ghṛta-madhu-śarkarā-snigdhaiḥ | apiḥ samuccaye sarṣapair daśa-śataṃ tritayaṃ tri-sahasraṃ niśi rātrau juhvataḥ puruṣasya śacī-dayitaḥ indro 'pi avaśo vaśī bhavati kiṃ punar anye || KrdC_8.15 ||
children.translated_text: Combined with salt — in the reading '<s>kaṭu-saṃyuta</s>' (combined with pungent [spice]), it means combined with pungent [substances]. Made very soft with sweetness — moistened with ghee, honey, and sugar. '<s>Api</s>' is cumulative. With mustard seeds, three thousand at night — for a man who offers [oblations], even the beloved of <s>Śacī</s> — <s>Indra</s> — becomes helplessly subject. How much more so others? || KrdC_8.15 ||
He states another application —
Then, with products of the <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) tree — fruit, fuel-sticks, flowers,
And leaves, very soft with honey, by offering oblations;
And with lotuses accompanied by white unbroken-rice, separately —
One subjugates <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) permanently, in a short time. // Krd_8.16 //

children.text: bilva-vṛkṣodbhavaiḥ phala-samit-puṣpa-patraiḥ śveta-padmair atyanta-madhurāplutaiḥ sitākṣata-yutaiḥ śarkarā-taṇḍula-miśritaiḥ sitājya-sahitair iti pāṭhe sitāśarkarā ājyaṃ ghṛtaṃ tat-sahitaiḥ pṛthak ekaikaṃ vastu-tri-sahasra-homāt cira-kālam acirāt śīghraṃ kamalāṃ lakṣmīṃ vaśayet | atra saṅkhyā-samanantaroktā || KrdC_8.16 ||
children.translated_text: With products of the <s>bilva</s> tree — fruit, fuel-sticks, flowers, and leaves — and with white lotuses extremely drenched in sweetness, combined with white unbroken rice — in the reading '<s>sitājya-sahita</s>,' white sugar and ghee are combined — separately, each item [offered as] three thousand oblations — from such <s>homa</s>, one subjugates <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) for a long time, quickly. Here the count is as just previously stated. || KrdC_8.16 ||
He states another application —
Having stolen the garments of the cowherd women, <s>Acyuta</s>
Climbed a <s>kadamba</s> tree, with their hearts [captivated];
Recollecting [him], one should recite at night one thousand — he brings

children.text: drutam urvaśīm api haṭhād daśāhataḥ // Krd_8.17 //
children.translated_text: Even <s>Urvaśī</s> quickly, forcefully, within ten days. // Krd_8.17 //

children.text: hṛdayaiḥ amā saha haṭhāt gopa-yuvatī-vastrāṇy apahṛtya gṛhītvā kadamba-vṛkṣam adhirūḍhaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ smaran niśi rātrau sahasraṃ japet sa daśāhato daśa-divasa-madhye haṭhān mantrasya balāt urvaśīm api deva-veśyām api vaśam ānayet nija-nikaṭam iti śeṣaḥ || KrdC_8.17 ||
children.translated_text: With their hearts — along with [their captivated] hearts — having forcefully stolen — taken — the garments of the cowherd maidens, meditating on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> who has climbed the <s>kadamba</s> tree, one should recite one thousand at night. He, within ten days, by the force of the mantra, brings even <s>Urvaśī</s> — even the celestial courtesan — under control, to his own vicinity — this is the remainder [of the meaning]. || KrdC_8.17 ||
He states the greatness of the two mantras —
What need of much discourse here? Of the two mantras,

children.text: anayoḥ sadṛk na hi paro vaśī kṛtau |
children.translated_text: There is no other equal in the act of subjugation;
In the work of attracting sophisticated women,
Of these two whose bodies are made of the love-god's weapon. // Krd_8.18 //

children.text: atra granthe bahunā kathitena kiṃ prayojanam ? anayor daśāṣṭādaśākṣarayoḥ sadṛk samaḥ vaśīkaraṇe iha jagati aparo nāsti | kimbhūtayor nagara-strīṇām ākarṣaṇa-karmaṇi kāmāstra-śarīrayoḥ || KrdC_8.18 ||
children.translated_text: In this treatise, what purpose is served by much discourse? Equal — comparable — to these two, the ten- and eighteen-syllable [mantras], in subjugation there is no other in this world. Of what kind? In the work of attracting city-women, of those whose bodies consist of <s>Kāma</s>'s (love-god's) weapon. || KrdC_8.18 ||
He states another application for the attainment of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) —
I salute <s>Mukunda</s> — white as jasmine and the moon, youthful, with eyes resembling red lotus petals,

children.text: cakraṃ śaṅkhaṃ gadābje nija-bhuja-parighair āyatair ādadhānam |
children.translated_text: Holding discus, conch, mace, and lotus in his long, club-like arms;
Blazing with divine ornaments, body-paints, and a garland of fresh shining lotuses,

children.text: prodyat-pītāmbarāḍhyaṃ munibhir abhivṛtaṃ padma-saṃsthaṃ mukundam // Krd_8.19 //
children.translated_text: Resplendent in rising yellow garments, surrounded by sages, seated upon a lotus. // Krd_8.19 //

children.text: mukundaṃ vande | kunda-puṣpaṃ candraś ca tadvat śuklaṃ tathā yuvānaṃ tathā rakta-padma-sadṛśa-locanaṃ tathā dīrghair nija-bāhu-parighair mud-garākāra-sva-bāhubhiḥ śaṅkhaṃ cakraṃ gadāṃ padmaṃ ca dhārayantaṃ tathā deva-yogyālaṅkārāṅga-rāgaiḥ navāni yāni padmāni teṣāṃ lasantī dedīpyamānā yā mālā tayā ca pradīptaṃ tathā dedīpyamāna-haridrābha-vastra-yuktaṃ tathā nāradādibhir veṣṭitaṃ tathā paṅkajāsīnam || KrdC_8.19 ||
children.translated_text: I salute <s>Mukunda</s>. As white as jasmine flowers and the moon; likewise youthful; likewise with eyes resembling red lotuses; likewise holding conch, discus, mace, and lotus with his own long club-like arms; likewise with ornaments fit for gods and body-ointments; with a garland that is of fresh lotuses — shining, resplendent — blazing by that; likewise endowed with resplendent saffron-colored garments; likewise surrounded by <s>Nārada</s> and others; likewise seated on a lotus. || KrdC_8.19 ||
Having thus meditated on the Supreme Person with fully blossomed heart-lotus, the primordial one, seated,

children.text: sāndrābhoja-cchaviṃ vā druta-kanaka-nibhaṃ vā japed arka-lakṣam |
children.translated_text: Of deep lotus-complexion, or of molten gold hue, one should recite twelve <s>lakṣa</s>s;
One of the two mantras, enclosed between two <s>praṇava</s>s; then should offer twelve thousand oblations with fuel-sticks
Of milk-trees, accompanied by milk, or with <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice) combined with honey, ghee, and sugar. // Krd_8.20 //

children.text: evaṃ-vidhaṃ pūrvoktaṃ mukundaṃ dhyātvā praphulla-hṛdaya-padmāsanopaviṣṭaṃ tathā ādyaṃ prathamaṃ sa-jala-jalada-śyāmaṃ sāndrābhoja-cchavim iti pāṭhe masṛṇa-padma-kāntiṃ vā dhyātvā divtārāntaragaṃ praṇava-dvaya-madhya-gataṃ manvor daśāṣṭādaśākṣarayor ekam arka-lakṣaṃ dvādaśa-lakṣaṃ japet | atha japānantaram arka-sahasraṃ idhmaiḥ samidbhiḥ kṣīra-drutyair aśvatthodumbara-plakṣa-nyagrodhānyatama-samudbhavaiḥ payoktaiḥ dugdha-plutaiḥ athavā ghṛta-madhu-śarkarā-sahitena paramānnena juhuyāt || KrdC_8.20 ||
children.translated_text: Having thus meditated on the previously described <s>Mukunda</s> — seated on the fully blossomed heart-lotus — likewise the primordial one, dark as a rain-cloud full of water — in the reading '<s>sāndrābhoja-cchavim</s>,' of smooth lotus-luster — or having meditated [thus], one of the two mantras — the ten- or eighteen-syllable — placed between two <s>praṇava</s>s, one should recite twelve <s>lakṣa</s>s (1,200,000 times). Then, after recitation, twelve thousand [oblations] with fuel-sticks of milk-trees — born of <s>aśvattha</s> (sacred fig), <s>udumbara</s> (cluster fig), <s>plakṣa</s> (white fig), or <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) — any one of them — drenched in milk; or with <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice pudding) combined with ghee, honey, and sugar, one should offer oblations. || KrdC_8.20 ||
Then, the overlord of the worlds, of imperishable, supreme bliss-form,
In one's own heart-lotus, the sun that dispels the darkness of worldly existence;
Meditating with identity with him, the mantra, with pure mind, daily,
One should recite three thousand, and should worship according to the evening method. // Krd_8.21 //

children.text: tatas tad-anantaraṃ lokādhyakṣaṃ loka-svāminam | avināśi-jñānaṃ tat-sukha-svarūpa-śarīraṃ saṃsārāndhakāra-viccheda-sūryam amuṃ kṛṣṇaṃ nija-hṛdaya-padme nijaikyena svābhedena bhāvayan amala-cetāḥ nirmalāntaḥkaraṇaḥ pratidinaṃ tri-sahasraṃ sahasra-trayaṃ juhuyāt tathā pūrvokta-sāyāhna-pūjā-prakāreṇa pūjayatu homam api karotu || KrdC_8.21 ||
children.translated_text: Then — thereafter — the overlord of the worlds — the lord of the universe; of imperishable knowledge, of bliss-form body, the sun that dispels the darkness of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) — this <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — in one's own heart-lotus, meditating with identity with oneself — contemplating non-difference — with pure mind — with purified inner instrument — daily, one should recite — offer — three thousand. Likewise, one should worship according to the previously described evening-worship method, and should also perform <s>homa</s>. || KrdC_8.21 ||

children.text: vidhiṃ yo 'muṃ bhaktyā bhajati niyataṃ susthira-matir
children.translated_text: He who serves this procedure with devotion, always, with firmly steadfast mind,
The fearsome ocean of worldly existence, [filled] with hosts of crocodiles in the form of dangerous sense-objects,
Vast with towering waves called birth and death —

children.text: samuttīryānantaṃ vrajati paramaṃ dhāma sa hareḥ // Krd_8.22 //
children.translated_text: Having crossed [that ocean], he attains the supreme, infinite abode of <s>Hari</s>. // Krd_8.22 //

children.text: sa sthira-matiḥ pumān amuṃ vidhiṃ prakāraṃ niyataṃ satataṃ bhaktyā bhajati sevate sa bhavāmbhodhiṃ saṃsāra-sāgaraṃ samuttīrya hareḥ ananyaṃ na vidyate anyo yasmāt sarva-mayam utkṛṣṭaṃ dhāma prāpnoti | kīdṛśaṃ ? ambhodhir iva bhayaṅkaraṃ kair viṣamā durnivārā ye viṣayāḥ śabdādayaṃ athavā srak-candana-vanitādyāḥ ta eva grāha-rūpā makara-kacchapādyās teṣāṃ nikaraiḥ samūhaiḥ | tathā janma-maraṇa-nāma-dheyais taraṅgair uttuṅgair mahadbhir vistīrṇam || KrdC_8.22 ||
children.translated_text: That man of steady mind who always — constantly — serves — follows — this procedure with devotion, having crossed the ocean of worldly existence — the sea of <s>saṃsāra</s> — attains the supreme abode of <s>Hari</s>, which is infinite — beyond which there is no other — all-pervading, supreme. Of what kind? Fearsome like an ocean; with what? With hosts of <s>grāha</s>s (crocodiles) in the form of dangerous — unavoidable — sense-objects such as sound etc., or garlands, sandalwood, women, etc.; likewise, vast with towering — great — waves named birth and death. || KrdC_8.22 ||
Chanting his names, hearing his
Stories, constantly remembering his forms;
Bowing to his lotus-feet, humbly bent with devotion —

children.text: sa pūjyo budhair nitya-yuktaḥ sa eva // Krd_8.23 //
children.translated_text: He is worthy of honor by the wise; he alone is ever-united [with the Lord]. // Krd_8.23 //

children.text: sa puruṣaḥ budhaiḥ prājñaiḥ pūjyaḥ sa eva ca nitya-yukto nitya-yoga-bhāk | kiṃ kurvan ? asya śrī-kṛṣṇasya nāmāni gṛṇan vadan, tadīyāḥ kathā ākalpayan | tasya śrī-kṛṣṇasya rūpāṇi mūrtīḥ sarvadā dhyāyan | tat-padāmbhoruhaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇa-pāda-padmaṃ bhakti-namraḥ sevā'vanataḥ adhika-namratva-khyāpanārthaṃ paunaruktyam || KrdC_8.23 ||
children.translated_text: That person is worthy of honor by the wise — the learned; he alone is ever-united — always connected in <s>yoga</s>. Doing what? Chanting — uttering — the names of this <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>; hearing his stories. Always meditating on — contemplating — the forms — images — of that <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>. Humbly bent with devotion — bowed down in service — to his lotus-feet — to the lotus-feet of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>. The repetition [of 'humility'] is for emphasizing the degree of humility. || KrdC_8.23 ||
Now he describes the pair of supreme mantras —
I shall now describe another pair of exceedingly secret mantras,
In brief, named '<s>bhuvana-mohana</s>' (world-enchanting);
With <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, the left-eye (<s>Vāmanāyanā</s>), and the moon honored as first,
Preceded by that, with <s>vidyā</s> (space), <s>ṛṣi</s> (one), <s>ka</s>-letter, <s>yuteśa</s> (lord combined), and <s>hṛt</s> (<s>namaḥ</s>). // Krd_8.24 //

children.text: athānantaram anyat mantra-dvayam atigopyaṃ jagan-mohana-saṃjñakaṃ svalpoktyā vakṣye | brahma ka-kāraḥ | indro la-kāraḥ | vāma-nayanaṃ dīrgha-ī-kāraḥ | indur anusvāraḥ | etaiḥ saṃyuktaḥ kāma-bīja-rūpaḥ prathamo mantra uddhṛtaḥ | tat-pūrvakaḥ viyat ha-kāraḥ ṛṣīka iti svarūpaṃ tābhyāṃ yukta īśa-śabdaḥ hṛṣīkeśa iti svarūpaṃ ṅe caturthy-eka-vacanaṃ hṛn namaḥ | klīṃ hṛṣīkeśāya namaḥ iti dvitīyo mantraḥ | atrāyaṃ puruṣottama-mantra iti bhairava-tripāṭhinaḥ || KrdC_8.24 ||
children.translated_text: Then, subsequently, another pair of mantras — extremely secret, called <s>Jaganmohana</s> (World-enchanting) — I shall describe briefly. <s>Brahman</s> is the letter <s>ka</s>; <s>Indra</s> is the letter <s>la</s>; 'left eye' is the long <s>ī</s>-vowel; 'moon' (<s>indu</s>) is <s>anusvāra</s>. Combined with these, the first mantra — in the form of the <s>kāma-bīja</s> (love-god's seed-syllable) — is extracted. Preceded by that, '<s>viyat</s>' (sky) is the letter <s>ha</s>; '<s>ṛṣīka</s>' is itself; combined with these two, the word '<s>Īśa</s>' — '<s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>' is the form; <s>ṅe</s> is the dative singular; <s>hṛt</s> is <s>namaḥ</s>. '<s>Klīṃ Hṛṣīkeśāya namaḥ</s>' — this is the second mantra. Here, this is the <s>Puruṣottama</s>-mantra — thus [say] the <s>Bhairava-tripāṭhin</s>s.
He states the <s>ṛṣi</s> and other [ancillaries] —
For both mantras, the sage <s>Saṃmohana-Nārada</s> is the <s>muni</s> (seer);
The meter is declared by the wise as <s>Gāyatrī</s>;
For both of these, the deity is

children.text: syād devatā vacmy adhunā ṣaḍ-aṅgakam // Krd_8.25 //
children.translated_text: <s>Trailokya-saṃmohana-Viṣṇu</s> (the world-enchanting <s>Viṣṇu</s>); now I state the six limbs.

children.text: anayor mantrayoḥ saṃmohana-nārado muniḥ | chandaḥ punar gāyatram | mantrajñaiḥ kathitaṃ trailokya-saṃmohana-viṣṇur devateti || KrdC_8.25 ||
children.translated_text: For these two mantras, <s>Saṃmohana-Nārada</s> is the seer. The meter is <s>Gāyatrī</s>. It is stated by the knowers of mantras that <s>Trailokya-saṃmohana-Viṣṇu</s> is the deity.
Now I state the six limbs —

children.text: aklīb-adīrghaiḥ sa-lavais tad api ca kalāsanārūḍhaiḥ |
children.translated_text: With the non-neuter long [vowels], accompanied by <s>bindu</s> (<s>lava</s>), and also mounted upon '<s>kalā</s>' and '<s>sa</s>';

children.text: uktaṃ pūrvavad āsana-vinyāsāntaṃ samācared atha tu // Krd_8.26 //
children.translated_text: As stated before, one should perform [the rites] up to the conclusion of seat-placement (<s>āsana-vinyāsa</s>).

children.text: ṛ-ṝ---varjita-ṣaṭ-dīrgha-svaraiḥ bindu-sahitaiḥ kalety akṣara-dvaya-sambaddhaiḥ klāṃ klīṃ klūṃ klaiṃ klauṃ klaḥ ebhis tat ṣaḍ-aṅgam uktam | athānantaraṃ pūrvavad daśākṣara-kathita-pūjā-paryantaṃ kāryam || KrdC_8.26 ||
children.translated_text: With the six long vowels excluding <s>ṛ</s> and <s>ṝ</s>, accompanied by <s>bindu</s>, connected with the two syllables '<s>kla</s>' — <s>klāṃ</s>, <s>klīṃ</s>, <s>klūṃ</s>, <s>klaiṃ</s>, <s>klauṃ</s>, <s>klaḥ</s> — by these, the six limbs are stated. Then, subsequently, as before, one should perform everything up to the worship described for the ten-syllable [mantra].

children.text: karayoḥ śākhāsu tale nyasya ṣaḍ-aṅgāni cāṅgulīṣu śarān |
children.translated_text: On the branches [fingers] and palms of both hands, one should place the six limbs; and upon the fingers, the arrows;

children.text: manu-puṭita-mātṛkārṇair nyasyāṅge 'ṅgāni vinyasec ca śarān // Krd_8.27 //
children.translated_text: With the <s>Mātṛkā</s> (alphabet) letters enclosed in the mantra, placing [them] on the body; and one should also place the limbs and arrows.

children.text: karayoḥ śākhāsu aṅgulīṣu ubhaya-kara-tale ca ṣaḍ-aṅgāni vinyasya punar aṅgulīṣu ca kāma-bāṇān vinyasya ādy-anta-sthita-mantra-mātṛkākṣair mātṛkā-sthāneṣu vinyasya dīrgha-yukta-kāma-bījaiḥ ṣaḍ-aṅgāni sva-śarīre vinyasya bāṇa-nyāsaṃ ca kuryāt || KrdC_8.27 ||
children.translated_text: On the branches — fingers — of both hands and on both palms, one should place the six limbs; again on the fingers, one should place the <s>kāma-bāṇa</s>s (arrows of the love-god); with the <s>Mātṛkā</s> letters of the mantra placed at the beginning and end, one should place [them] at the <s>Mātṛkā</s> positions; with the <s>kāma-bīja</s>s accompanied by long [vowels], one should place the six limbs on one's own body and also perform the arrow-placement (<s>bāṇa-nyāsa</s>).
He states the locations for arrow-placement (<s>bāṇa-nyāsa</s>) —
On the head, heart, <s>liṅga</s> (generative organ), and feet, with the finger-branches, ending with <s>namaḥ</s>, in the dative,
The [arrows of] desiccation (<s>śoṣaṇa</s>), enchantment (<s>mohana</s>), inflaming (<s>sandīpana</s>), scorching (<s>tāpana</s>), and maddening (<s>mādana</s>), in order.

children.text: śiro-vadana-hṛdaya-liṅga-pādeṣu aṅgulībhiḥ aṅguṣṭhādika-niṣṭha-kāntābhiḥ ekaikayā aṅgulyā caturthī namaḥ-pada-sahitān vakṣyamāṇān pañca-bāṇān krameṇa vinyaset || KrdC_8.28 ||
children.translated_text: On the head, face, heart, <s>liṅga</s> (generative organ), and feet — with the fingers, one by one from the thumb to the little finger — with each single finger, one should place in order the five arrows to be described, accompanied by the dative case and the word <s>namaḥ</s>.
He states the names of the arrows —

children.text: pañcaite samproktā hrāṃ-hrīṃ-klīṃ-klūṃ sa ādikā bāṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: These five arrows are declared, having <s>hrāṃ</s>, <s>hrīṃ</s>, <s>klīṃ</s>, <s>klūṃ</s>, and <s>sa</s> as their initial [syllables];

children.text: saṃmohanam atha jagataṃ dhyāyet puruṣottamaṃ samāhita-dhīḥ // Krd_8.29 //
children.translated_text: Then, the one of concentrated mind should meditate on <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person) as the enchanter of the worlds.

children.text: hrāṃ-hrīṃ-klīṃ-klūṃ sa etāni pañca-bījāni ekaikāni ādau yeṣāṃ evaṃ ete pañca-bāṇāḥ śoṣaṇādayaḥ proktāḥ | prayogas tu-hrāṃ śoṣaṇāya namaḥ ity aṅguṣṭhena śirasi hrīṃ mohanāya namaḥ iti tarjanyā mukhe ity ādi athānantaram | saṃyata-cittaḥ tribhuvana-vaśya-karaṃ puruṣottamaṃ cintayet || KrdC_8.29 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hrāṃ</s>, <s>hrīṃ</s>, <s>klīṃ</s>, <s>klūṃ</s>, <s>sa</s> — these five seed-syllables, each one as the initial of the respective [arrow] — thus these five arrows beginning with <s>Śoṣaṇa</s> (Desiccation) are declared. The practical application is: '<s>hrāṃ Śoṣaṇāya namaḥ</s>' — with the thumb on the head; '<s>hrīṃ Mohanāya namaḥ</s>' — with the index finger on the face — and so forth. Then, subsequently, with concentrated mind, one should meditate on <s>Puruṣottama</s>, the subjugator of the three worlds.
He states the meditation —
Beneath a great wish-fulfilling tree of brilliant radiance, rising in a garden of divine trees,
Situated on a lotus-throne of auspicious origin, resplendent on a ground of gems,
Seated upon <s>Suparṇa</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>), the life-breath of the universe, whose radiance equals the rising sun,
With raised shoulders, with limbs beautiful as coral, agitated by the god of love (<s>Aṅgaja</s>);
Holding in his own arms discus, conch, goad, noose, flower-arrows, sugarcane-bow, lotus, and mace,
With reddish, elongated, large, rolling pair of lotus-eyes;
With gem-studded crown, earrings, necklace, armlets, bracelets, rings, and other [ornaments],
Blazing with reddish garlands and unguents, wearing yellow garments;
Seated on his own left thigh, embracing [him], holding a lotus in her left hand,
<s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), with moist <s>yoni</s> (womanhood), her limb-creeper resplendent, distracted by the intoxication of passion;
Adorned with lovely ornaments, garlands, unguents, and clad in fine white garments,
A young woman whose dark, restless bee-like eyes are engaged upon [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s] lotus-face;
[<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] embracing [her] firmly with his left arm, which holds the sugarcane-bow,
His heart overflowing with supreme bliss born from that [embrace], the sole preceptor of all moving and non-moving beings;
Surrounded by thousands of women — celestial, <s>Daitya</s> (demon), <s>Nāga</s> (serpent), <s>Guhyaka</s> (treasure-guardian), <s>Gandharva</s> (celestial musician), and other [divine] ladies,
Whose limbs are languid with the intoxication of love, resplendent with divine ornaments;
Having thus meditated with the sense of non-difference from the Self, one should recite the one-syllable [<s>kāma-bīja</s>] or the eight-syllable [mantra],

children.text: prajaped dina-kara-lakṣaṃ trimadhura-siktais tu kiṃśuka-prasavaiḥ // Krd_8.38 //
children.translated_text: Twelve <s>lakṣa</s>s (1,200,000) times; and [offer oblations] with <s>kiṃśuka</s> (<s>palāśa</s>) blossoms sprinkled with the three sweets.

children.text:
nava-ślokānāṃ kulakam | ittham evaṃ vāsudevaṃ dhyātvā ekākṣara-kāma-bījam athavāṣṭākṣara-mantraṃ dinakara-lakṣaṃ dvādaśa-lakṣaṃ japet | kīdṛśam ? dhyātvā deva-sambandhi-vṛkṣodyāne kalpa-vṛkṣodyāne udyan vṛddhiṃ gacchan manoharo yaḥ pārijāta-vṛkṣas tasya tale garuḍasyonnatāṃse upaviṣṭam | kīdṛśasya garuḍasya ? padmarāgādi-ghaṭita-bhū-bhāga-śobhamāna-śreṣṭha-padma-pīṭhopaviṣṭasya tathā sakala-jīva-bhūtasya parameśvarasyāṃśatvāt tathā udita-sūrya-sama-kānteḥ | kīdṛśaṃ vāsudevam ? pravāla-sundarāṅgaṃ, kāma-vyākulitaṃ sva-dorbhiḥ sva-bāhubhir dakṣiṇa-vāma-krameṇa cakra-śaṅkhāṅkuśa-pāśa-puṣpa-śarekṣu-cāpa-padma-gadāḥ bibhrāṇaṃ tathā raktaṃ dīrghaṃ bṛhad-vighūrṇitaṃ
netra-dvaya-rūpaṃ padmaṃ yasya sa tathā tam, padma-rāgādi-maṇi-ghaṭita-śiro 'laṅkāra-karṇa-bhūṣaṇam uktāhāra-bāhu-bhūṣaṇa-kara-mūla-bhūṣaṇa-mudrikā-kṣudra-ghaṇṭikā-prabhṛtibhiḥ rakta-mālya-gandhaiś ca dedīpyamānaṃ tathā pīte vāsasī paridhānam ācchādanaṃ yasya sa tathā taṃ tathā dhṛtekṣu-cāpena vāma-bāhu-daṇḍena dṛḍhaṃ yathā syād evaṃ śriyam āliṅganam |
children.translated_text:
A <s>kulaka</s> (verse-cluster) of nine verses. Thus — in this manner — having meditated on <s>Vāsudeva</s>, one should recite the one-syllable <s>kāma-bīja</s>, or alternatively the eight-syllable mantra, twelve <s>lakṣa</s>s (1,200,000) times. Of what kind [is this meditation]? Having meditated [upon <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] beneath a wish-fulfilling tree in a divine garden — a garden of <s>kalpa-vṛkṣa</s>s — the rising, growing, enchanting <s>Pārijāta</s> tree; beneath that, seated on <s>Garuḍa</s> with raised shoulders. Of what kind of <s>Garuḍa</s>? Seated on a supreme lotus-throne made of ruby and other gems, situated on a gem-encrusted ground; likewise, being the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) of all living beings, as a portion of the Supreme Lord; likewise, with radiance equal to the rising sun. Of what kind is <s>Vāsudeva</s>? With limbs beautiful as coral; agitated by desire (<s>Kāma</s>); bearing in his own arms — right and left in order — discus, conch, goad, noose, flower-arrows, sugarcane-bow, lotus, and mace; likewise, with reddish, elongated, large, rolling
eye-pair like lotuses; with crown, ear-ornaments, necklace, arm-ornaments, wrist-ornaments, rings, small bells, and other [ornaments] set with rubies and other gems; blazing with reddish garlands and fragrances; likewise, wearing yellow garments as his covering; likewise, embracing <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) firmly with the left arm holding the sugarcane-bow;

children.text: kīdṛśīm ? svīya-vāmoru-deśe upaviṣṭāṃ, tathā āliṅgantīṃ, tathā vāma-hasta-gṛhīta-padmāṃ, tathā sarasī-bhūta-guhyāṃ tathā kāmena vyākulīkṛtā anāyattī-kṛtā aṅga-latā yasyās tāṃ manoharāṇi alaṅkāra-māla-candanāni yasyās tāṃ tathā śveta-vastra-paridhānāṃ tathā kṛṣṇa-mukha-padme vyāpṛtaṃ samyag vyāpāra-yuktaṃ caṭulaṃ manoharaṃ cañcalaṃ vā asitaṃ śyāmaṃ yan netraṃ sa eva madhukaro bhramaraḥ yasyās tāṃ tathā taruī̀eīṃ yuvatīm | punaḥ kīdṛśīm ? priyāliṅgana-janita-parama-sukha-pūrṇa-hṛdayaṃ tathā jagad-guruṃ tathā deva-daitya-sarpa-deva-yoni-deva-gāyana-vidyādhara-strī-sahasrair madatayā kāmena ca stambha-yuktam aṅgaṃ yeṣāṃ tair devārhaṇa-bhūṣaṇa-dīptair veṣṭitaṃ kayā

children.translated_text: method? Having meditated with the sense of oneness with the Self.

Of what kind [is <s>Lakṣmī</s>]? Seated on his own left thigh; likewise, embracing [him]; likewise, holding a lotus in her left hand; likewise, with moist womanhood; likewise, her limb-creeper rendered unsteady — made helpless — by desire; possessing lovely ornaments, garlands, and sandalwood; likewise, clad in white garments; likewise, [with] a dark, enchanting, restless eye — which is like a bee (<s>madhukara</s>) — engaged upon — fully occupied with — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s lotus-face; likewise, a young woman. Again, of what kind? Whose heart is filled with supreme bliss born from the embrace of the beloved; likewise, the preceptor of the universe; likewise, surrounded by thousands of women of the gods, demons, serpents, divine spirits, celestial musicians, <s>Vidyādhara</s>s — whose limbs are stiffened by intoxication and by desire — resplendent with divine ornaments. By what

children.text: juhuāt taraṇi-sahasraṃ vimalaiḥ salilaiś ca tarpayet tāvat |
children.translated_text: One should offer twelve thousand oblations; and with pure water, perform <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) that many times;

children.text: viṃśaty-arṇe prokte yantre dinaśo 'mum arcayet bhaktyā // Krd_8.39 //
children.translated_text: In the <s>yantra</s> described for the twenty-syllable [mantra], one should worship him daily with devotion.

children.text: dhyāna-japānantaraṃ ghṛta-madhu-śarkarā-sahitaiḥ palāśa-puṣpair dvādaśa-sahasraṃ juhuyāt | homānantaraṃ nirmalair jalair dvādaśa-sahasraṃ tarpaṇaṃ kuryāt | viṃśaty-arṇeti | pūrvokta-viṃśaty-akṣarodita-pīṭha-vidhānena tan-mantroddhṛta-yantre amuṃ kṛṣṇaṃ bhaktyā pratidinaṃ pūjayet || KrdC_8.39 ||
children.translated_text: After meditation and recitation, one should offer twelve thousand oblations with <s>palāśa</s> flowers combined with ghee, honey, and sugar. After the <s>homa</s>, one should perform twelve thousand <s>tarpaṇa</s> libations with pure water. Regarding 'the twenty-syllable' — in the <s>yantra</s> constructed according to the seat-procedure described for the previously stated twenty-syllable [mantra], one should worship <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> daily with devotion.

children.text: pūjā-prakāram āha sārdhaṃ catuḥślokena | garuḍa-mantram āha-
children.translated_text: He states the method of worship in four-and-a-half verses. He states the <s>Garuḍa</s>-mantra —

In the seat-procedure, at the end of '<s>Pakṣī</s>' (the bird, i.e., <s>Garuḍa</s>), '<s>Rājāya</s>' with '<s>śiras</s>' (<s>svāhā</s>) — with this, having worshipped the enemy of serpents (<s>Garuḍa</s>),

children.text: harim āvāhya skandhe tasyārghādyaiḥ samarcya bhūṣāntai // Krd_8.40 //
children.translated_text: Having invoked <s>Hari</s> upon his (<s>Garuḍa</s>'s) back, one should worship with <s>arghya</s> and other [offerings] up to ornaments.

children.text: aṅgāni ca bāṇāṃś ca nyāsa-kramataḥ kirīṭam api śirasi |
children.translated_text: And the limbs and arrows, according to the order of <s>nyāsa</s> (placement); also the crown upon the head,

children.text: śravasoś ca kuṇḍale 'ri-pramukhāni praharaṇāni pāṇiṣu ca // Krd_8.41 //
children.translated_text: And earrings at the ears; the foremost weapons such as discus in the hands.

children.text: śrīvatsa-kaustubhau ca stanayor ūrdhve gale ca vanamālām |
children.translated_text: And <s>Śrīvatsa</s> and <s>Kaustubha</s> upon the chest, above; and the forest-garland (<s>vanamālā</s>) at the throat,

children.text: pīta-vasanaṃ nitambe vāmāṅke śriyam api sva-bījena // Krd_8.42 //
children.translated_text: Yellow garments on the hips, <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) on the left side — [worshipped] with her own seed-syllable.

children.text: iṣṭvātha karṇikāyām aṅgāni vidigdaśāsu dikṣu śarān |
children.translated_text: Having thus worshipped on the pericarp (<s>karṇikā</s>), the limbs in the ten intermediate directions; the arrows in the [four] corners;

children.text: koṇeṣu pañcamaṃ punar agny-ādi-daleṣu śaktayaḥ pūjyāḥ // Krd_8.43 //
children.translated_text: The fifth [arrow] again; in the petals beginning with the fire-direction, the <s>Śakti</s>s (powers) should be worshipped.

children.text: pūjā-vidhau pakṣi-śabdānte rājāyeti svarūpaṃ śiraḥ svāhā anena prakāreṇa pīṭha-madhye ahi-ripuṃ garuḍaṃ sampūjya tasya garuḍasya pṛṣṭhe śrī-kṛṣṇam āvāhyāvāhanādi yathāvat kṛtvārghādyair bhūṣāntair upacāraiś ca sampūjya aṅgāni ca sampūjya pañca-bāṇāṃś ca sampūjya bhūṣaṇāni ca sampūjya dig-daleṣu śaktayaḥ pūjyā iti anenānvayaḥ |
children.translated_text:
In the worship procedure, at the end of the word '<s>Pakṣī</s>' (bird), '<s>Rājāya</s>' is the form, '<s>śiras</s>' is <s>svāhā</s> — in this manner, having duly worshipped <s>Garuḍa</s>, the enemy of serpents, in the center of the seat (<s>pīṭha</s>); upon the back of that <s>Garuḍa</s>, having invoked <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> and having performed invocation and other [rites] properly; having worshipped with <s>arghya</s> and other <s>upacāra</s>s (offerings) up to ornaments; having worshipped the limbs; having worshipped the five arrows; having worshipped the ornaments; in the directional petals, the <s>Śakti</s>s should be worshipped — this is the syntactic connection.
He clarifies this with 'according to the order of <s>nyāsa</s>' and so forth: wherever on the Supreme Lord's body the <s>nyāsa</s> (placement) of each [item] was done, there should be understood its worship — thus: the crown on the head; the word '<s>api</s>' is a metrical filler; earrings at the ears; the chief weapons — discus and the like — the armaments — in the hands; above the chest — on the heart — the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> and <s>Kaustubha</s>; at the throat, the <s>vanamālā</s> (forest-garland) hanging down to the feet — a lotus-garland; on the hips — at the waist — the golden-hued garment; on the left side — the left portion — <s>Lakṣmī</s> also, with her own seed-syllable, the <s>Śrī</s>-bīja. Having thus worshipped, on the pericarp, in the intermediate directions and corners, the limbs as before should be worshipped; in the [four] directions, the arrows; in the corners, the fifth arrow should be worshipped. Again, in the petals beginning with the fire-direction, the eight <s>Śakti</s>s should be worshipped.

children.text: etad eva spaṣṭayati-nyāsa-kramata ity ādinā | yatra parameśvarāṅge yasya nyāsaḥ | tasya pūjā boddhavyā tatra śirasi kirīṭaṃ api-pāda-pūraṇe śrotrayoḥ kuṇḍale ari-mukhāni cakrādīni praharaṇāni āyudhāni hasteṣu stanayo ūrdhvaṃ hṛdi śrīvatsa-kaustubhau gale vana-mālām āpāda-lambinīṃ padma-mālāṃ nitambe kaṭyāṃ haridrābha-vastraṃ vāmāṅge vāma-bhāge lakṣmīṃ ca sva-bījena śrī-bījena iṣṭvā sampūjya karṇikāyāṃ dig-vidiśāsu koṇeṣu dikṣu ca aṅgāni pūrvavat sampūjya dikṣu śarān agny-ādi-koṇeṣu ca pañcamaṃ bāṇaṃ pūjayet punar agny-ādi-daleṣu aṣṭau śaktayaḥ pūjyāḥ || KrdC_8.40-43 ||
children.translated_text: He clarifies this very [point] with 'according to the order of <s>nyāsa</s>' and so forth: wherever on the Supreme Lord's body the <s>nyāsa</s> (placement) of each [item] was performed, there should be understood its worship — thus: the crown on the head; the word '<s>api</s>' is a metrical filler; earrings at the two ears; the chief weapons — discus and the like — the armaments — in the hands; above the breasts — on the heart — the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> and <s>Kaustubha</s>; at the throat, the <s>vanamālā</s> (forest-garland) — a lotus-garland hanging down to the feet; on the hips — at the waist — the turmeric-hued garment; on the left side — the left portion — <s>Lakṣmī</s> too, with her own seed-syllable, the <s>Śrī</s>-bīja — having [thus] worshipped [her]; on the pericarp (<s>karṇikā</s>), in the directions and intermediate directions — in the corners and the cardinal directions — having worshipped the limbs as before; in the [cardinal] directions the arrows, and in the corners beginning with the fire-direction the fifth arrow, one should worship; again, in the petals beginning with the fire-direction, the eight <s>Śakti</s>s should be worshipped.
He states the colors of the <s>Śakti</s>s —
<s>Lakṣmī</s> and <s>Sarasvatī</s> are golden-hued; <s>Rati</s> and <s>Prīti</s> are deeply reddish;

children.text: kīrtiḥ kāntiś ca site tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭiś ca marakata-pratime // Krd_8.44 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kīrti</s> and <s>Kānti</s> are white; <s>Tuṣṭi</s> and <s>Puṣṭi</s> are emerald-colored.

children.text: svarṇābhe pīta-varṇe aruṇatare atirakte site śukle marakata-pratime haridrā-varṇe || KrdC_8.44 ||
children.translated_text: 'Golden-hued' means yellow-colored; 'deeply reddish' means extremely red; 'white' means bright white; 'emerald-colored' means of turmeric hue.
Of what kind are these <s>Śakti</s>s?
With limb-creepers adorned with divine unguents, ornaments, garlands, and fine silk garments,
With smiling faces, afflicted by the arrows of <s>Smāra</s> (the love-god), with beautiful hands holding <s>cāmara</s>s (fly-whisks).

children.text: deva-yogyānulepanālaṅkāra-granthita-puṣpa-sūkṣma-vastrair bhūṣita-dehā aṅga-latā-śabdaḥ svarūpa-vācī tathā īsad-dhāsya-vadanā tathā kāma-bāṇa-pīḍitāḥ tathā gṛhīta-cāmara-manoharās tāḥ || KrdC_8.45 ||
children.translated_text: With bodies adorned by ointments worthy of the gods, ornaments, woven flower-garlands, and fine delicate garments — the word 'limb-creeper' (<s>aṅga-latā</s>) denotes their essential nature; likewise, with slightly smiling faces; likewise, afflicted by the arrows of <s>Kāma</s> (the love-god); likewise, holding <s>cāmara</s>s (fly-whisks) — beautiful are they.

children.text: lokeśā bahir arcyāḥ kathitety arcā manu-dvayodbhūtā |
children.translated_text: The directional guardians should be worshipped outside; the worship described is produced from the pair of mantras;

children.text: prāyaḥ puruṣottama-vidhir evaṃ hi sa nocyate 'tra bahulatvāt // Krd_8.46 //
children.translated_text: The procedure is mostly that of <s>Puruṣottama</s>; thus it is not described here in full, due to its extensiveness.

children.text: tad bahir indrādayaḥ vajrādayaś ca pūjyāḥ ity evaṃ pūjā mantra-dvaya-sambhavā kathitā prāyo bāhulyena puruṣottama-mantra-kathita-prakāro 'py evaṃ paraṃ sa iha spaṣṭīkṛtya nocyate bahu-vaktavyatvāt prāyaḥ puruṣottama-vidher evam ihānyato 'vagantavyam iti ṭīkāntara-sammataṃ pāṭhāntaram || KrdC_8.46 ||
children.translated_text: Outside of that, <s>Indra</s> and the others, and the thunderbolt (<s>vajra</s>) and the others should be worshipped. Thus, the worship arising from the pair of mantras has been described. For the most part, the method described for the <s>Puruṣottama</s>-mantra is also similar, but it has not been explicitly clarified here due to the excessive length of exposition. The method of the <s>Puruṣottama</s> ritual should mostly be understood from elsewhere here — this is the reading approved in other commentaries.
He states the <s>Sammohana-Gāyatrī</s> (enchantment-<s>Gāyatrī</s>) —
Having uttered '<s>Trailokya-mohanāya</s>' (to the enchanter of the three worlds), '<s>vidmahe</s>'; '<s>Smarāya</s>' (to the god of love);

children.text: tat dhīmahīti tan no 'nte viṣṇus tad anu pracodayāt // Krd_8.47 //
children.translated_text: then '<s>dhīmahi</s>'; at the end, '<s>tan naḥ</s>' (may for us); then '<s>Viṣṇuḥ pracodayāt</s>' (may <s>Viṣṇu</s> inspire).

children.text: trailokya-mohanāyeti svarūpam uktvā tad-anantaraṃ vidmaha iti smarāyeti tad-anu dhīmahīti tan no viṣṇuḥ pracodayād iti svarūpaṃ vadet || KrdC_8.47 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Trailokya-mohanāya</s>' is the form; having uttered that, then '<s>vidmahe</s>'; '<s>Smarāya</s>'; after that, '<s>dhīmahi</s>'; [then] '<s>tan no Viṣṇuḥ pracodayāt</s>' (may <s>Viṣṇu</s> inspire us) is the form — one should recite.
He states the power [of this <s>Gāyatrī</s>] —

children.text: japyaiṣā hi japādau durita-harī śrī-karī japārcana-havanaiḥ |
children.translated_text: This should be recited at the beginning of recitation; it destroys sins and bestows <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity); through recitation, worship, and fire-offering,
one should sprinkle for the purpose of purification — with this [<s>Gāyatrī</s>], the self, the place of worship, and the ritual materials in worship.

children.text: eṣā gāyatrī japāt pūrvaṃ japanīyā sva-mantra-japa-pūjā-homaiḥ punaḥ pāpa-nāśinī lakṣmī-pradā ca bhavati | anayā gāyatryā ca pūjāyāṃ śuddhy-artham ātma-yāga-bhū-dravyāṇi ātmānaṃ yāga-bhuvaṃ dravyāṇi ca prokṣayatu || KrdC_8.48 ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Gāyatrī</s> should be recited before the recitation [of the main mantra]. Through the recitation, worship, and <s>homa</s> of one's own mantra, it becomes a destroyer of sins and a bestower of <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity). And with this <s>Gāyatrī</s>, in worship, for the purpose of purification, one should sprinkle the self (<s>ātman</s>), the place of worship (<s>yāga-bhū</s>), and the ritual materials (<s>dravya</s>).
He states the <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) common to both mantras —

children.text: manvor ekena śataṃ tarpayen mohanī-prasūna-yutair yaḥ |
children.translated_text: Whoever with one of the two mantras performs <s>tarpaṇa</s> a hundred [times] with waters mixed with <s>mohanī</s>-flowers,

children.text: toyair dinaśaḥ prātaḥ sa tu labhate vāñchitān ayatnataḥ kāmān // Krd_8.49 //
children.translated_text: daily in the morning — he obtains his desired wishes effortlessly.

children.text: yaḥ pūrvokta-mantrayor ekena mohanī-puṣpa-miśritaiḥ śakrāsana-padmāsana-puṣpa-sahitair jalaiḥ prati pratyahaṃ śataṃ tarpayet | sa vāñchitān kāmān anāyāsena prāpnoti || KrdC_8.49 ||
children.translated_text: Whoever with one of the two previously mentioned mantras, with waters mixed with <s>mohanī</s>-flowers — accompanied by <s>śakrāsana</s> and <s>padmāsana</s> flowers — performs a hundred <s>tarpaṇa</s>s daily, each day — he attains his desired wishes without effort.
He states another application related to the pair of mantras —
Having offered ten thousand (<s>ayuta</s>) [oblations] into the fire, with the remnant oblation-ghee (<s>huta-śeṣa-sampāta-ājya</s>), duly consecrated [by recitation],

children.text: bhojayatu svāmīkaṃ ramaṇī-ramaṇo 'pi tāṃ sva-vaśatāṃ netum // Krd_8.50 //
children.translated_text: one should feed the master (lover) of [a] woman — or alternatively, the lover [should feed] her — to bring her under his control.

children.text: ghṛtena vahnāv ayutaṃ āhuti-śeṣa-ghṛtena mantra-japtena ramaṇī sva-vaśatāṃ netuṃ prāpayituṃ ātmīyaṃ kāmukaṃ bhojayatu kāmukaḥ striyaṃ bhojayatu || KrdC_8.50 ||
children.translated_text: With ghee [offered] into the fire ten thousand times, with the ghee remaining from the oblation, consecrated by mantra-recitation — to bring a woman under control (<s>sva-vaśatā</s>), to make [her] attainable — one should feed one's own desired person. [Or] the man desiring love should feed the woman.
The procedures prescribed for the eighteen-syllable [mantra] should be performed for subjugation with these two [mantras];

children.text: manvor anayoḥ sadṛgbhyo vaina manus trailokya-vaśya-karmaṇi jagati // Krd_8.51 //
children.translated_text: among these two mantras, there is no [other] mantra in the world equal to them for the act of subjugating the three worlds.

children.text: aṣṭādaśākṣara-mantra-kathitā vaśya-kāriṇaḥ prayogā ābhyāṃ mantrābhyāṃ kāryā hi niścayena jagati sakala-jagad-āyattatā-kārye anayoḥ samāno 'nyomantro nāsti || KrdC_8.51 ||
children.translated_text: The subjugation-procedures described for the eighteen-syllable mantra should be performed with these two mantras. Indeed, with certainty, in the world, for the purpose of bringing the entire world under one's control, there is no other mantra equal to these two.
Here, in the recitation of the one-syllable [mantra] and the like, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with flute and [characteristic] gait should be meditated upon;
with red, beautiful body and attire; or alternatively, <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of Love), holding noose, goad, and bow.

children.text: atra samanantarokta-dvaya-madhye ekākṣara-mantrasya japa-pūjā-homādau kṛṣṇo bhāvanīyaḥ | kīdṛk ? sa-veṇu-gatir iti vaṃśottha-gāna-paraḥ | tathā lohita-manohara-śarīrābharaṇaḥ | athavā, atraiva mantra-japādau pāśāṅkuśa-dhanur-bāṇa-dharaḥ kāmadevo dhyeyaḥ | mantrasyādi-devātmakatvād iti bhāvaḥ || KrdC_8.52 ||
children.translated_text: Here, among the two [mantras] mentioned immediately before, in the recitation, worship, <s>homa</s>, etc. of the one-syllable mantra, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> should be contemplated. Of what kind? With flute and [characteristic] gait — absorbed in the music produced from the bamboo [flute]. Likewise, with red, beautiful body and ornaments. Or alternatively, here in this very mantra-recitation etc., <s>Kāmadeva</s> (the god of Love), holding noose (<s>pāśa</s>), goad (<s>aṅkuśa</s>), bow (<s>dhanus</s>), and arrow (<s>bāṇa</s>), should be meditated upon — because the mantra has the nature of the presiding deity at its beginning, this is the import.
He concludes the main topic —

children.text: yas tv ekataraṃ manum etayor vimala-dhīḥ sadā bhajati mantrī |
children.translated_text: Whoever — the ritualist (<s>mantrī</s>) of pure intellect — always worships one of these two mantras,

children.text: so 'mutrāpi ca siddhiṃ vipulām ihātitarām eti // Krd_8.53 //
children.translated_text: he attains exceedingly abundant <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) both in this world and in the next.

children.text: yo mantrī anayor mantrayor ekaṃ mantra-śreṣṭhaṃ sadā japādibhiḥ sevate, sa iha loke 'mutra ca atyarthaṃ vipulāṃ siddhiṃ prāpnoti || KrdC_8.53 ||
children.translated_text: The ritualist who always serves — through recitation and other [practices] — one mantra-supreme among these two mantras, he attains exceedingly abundant <s>siddhi</s> in this world and in the next.
Now he extracts the <s>Rukmiṇī-vallabha</s> (beloved of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>) mantra —
Now, <s>Satya</s> (<s>da</s>) and <s>Śauri</s> (<s>dha</s>), and the third and fourth [consonants of the <s>ja</s>-group],
adorned with fire (<s>śikhi</s>, i.e., <s>repha</s>), left eye (<s>vāma-netra</s>, i.e., long <s>ī</s>), and moon-crescent (<s>śaśi-khaṇḍa</s>, i.e., <s>bindu</s>);
the pair '<s>Jaya Kṛṣṇa</s>', followed without break by self-born (<s>ātma-bhū</s>, i.e., <s>ka</s>),
fire (<s>śikhi</s>, i.e., <s>ra</s>), <s>Śakti</s> (i.e., <s>ī</s>), <s>ḍā</s>, surrounded, attached syllables;
'<s>pra-ni</s>' — in between, '<s>mudita-cetase</s>' (to the joyful-minded); then
'<s>tya</s>,' '<s>pa</s>,' '<s>rakta</s>' (red), '<s>dṛg</s>' (eye, i.e., <s>i</s>), '<s>yā</s>,' '<s>guru</s>' (heavy, i.e., <s>ā</s>), wind (<s>māruta</s>, i.e., <s>ya</s>) — these syllables;
the word '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' with the fourth case [ending]; <s>ikṣu-kārmuka</s> (sugarcane-bowed, i.e., <s>kāma-bīja</s>) —

children.text: daśa-varṇakaś ca manuvaryakas tv asau // Krd_8.55 //
children.translated_text: this is the ten-syllable [mantra], and that is the excellent supreme mantra.

With the syllables <s>la</s>, <s>va</s>, <s>ādha</s> (half, i.e., <s>bindu</s>), <s>rra</s> (mountain, i.e., <s>ai</s>), <s>acala-sutā</s> (daughter of the mountain, i.e., <s>Bhuvaneśvarī-bīja</s>), <s>ramā</s> (i.e., <s>Śrī-bīja</s>),
enclosed (<s>puṭita</s>) by the syllables in sequence, like a box (<s>samudga</s>);
thus, with <s>danta</s> (32) + <s>sūrya</s> (12) + <s>vasu</s> (8) syllables, [this mantra] is extracted —
the producer of poetic delight and <s>Lakṣmī</s> (beauty), the destroyer of sins.

children.text:
satyo da-kāraḥ | śaurir dha-kāraś ca | tṛtīya-turyeti ja-kāraḥ jha-kāraś ca | ete catvāro varṇāḥ pratyekaṃ śikhī rephaḥ vāma-netram ī-kāraḥ śaśi-khaṇḍo binduḥ | etaiḥ śobhanāḥ sambaddhā ity arthaḥ | tathā ca, drīṃ dhrīṃ jrīṃ jhrīṃ iti | tad anu jaya-kṛṣṇeti tripāṭhi-govinda-miśra-prabhṛtayaḥ | vastutaḥ jaya-kṛṣṇeti padasya yugmaṃ tad-anu nirantareti svarūpam ātma-bhūḥ ka-kāraḥ śikhī rephaḥ śaktir ī-kāraḥ | tathā krī-svarūpam | tad anu ḍa-svarūpaṃ āsya-vṛtam ā-kāraḥ ḍā-svarūpam | sakta iti svarūpaṃ pranimadhyato pranīti akṣarayor madhye mudita-cetase iti tato ni-śabdānte tyeti svarūpaṃ tad anu pa-svarūpam | rakto rephaḥ | dṛg i-kāraḥ prathamātikrame kāraṇābhāvāt hrasva-i-kāro labhyate | tathā ca,
pri iti svarūpaṃ tato ya iti svarūpaṃ gurur ā-kāraḥ | yā iti svarūpam | tad anu māruto ya-kāraḥ | tad-anu sa-caturthi-kṛṣṇa-padam kṛṣṇāyeti svarūpam | tad-anu ikṣu-kārmukaḥ kāma-bījaṃ | tad-anu pūrvokta-daśākṣara-mantraḥ | tad anu lavo binduḥ tat-sahitā dharā ai-kāraḥ aiṃ iti svarūpam | acalaḥ parvataḥ tat-sutā pārvatī bhuvaneśvarī-bījam ity arthaḥ | ramā śrī-bījam | ebhis tribhir bījair mantrānte pratiloma-paṭhitaiḥ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ante śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ iti samudgavat sampuṭavat puṭito 'yaṃ dvipañcāśad-varṇo mantraḥ siddho bhavati |
mantra-varṇa-saṅkhyām āha-itīti | danta = 32, sūrya = 12, vasu = 8 | ebhir militaiḥ saṅkhyā dvipañcāśad-varṇātmako (52) mantro bhavatīty arthaḥ | kīdṛśaḥ ? kavitālokānurāga-lakṣmī sampādakaḥ tathāgha-hṛt pāpa-hartā || KrdC_8.54-56 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Satya</s> is the letter <s>da</s>; <s>Śauri</s> is the letter <s>dha</s>. Third and fourth — <s>ja</s> and <s>jha</s>. These four letters are each [adorned with]: <s>śikhi</s> (fire) is <s>repha</s> (<s>ra</s>); <s>vāma-netra</s> (left eye) is the <s>ī</s>-vowel; <s>śaśi-khaṇḍa</s> (moon-crescent) is <s>bindu</s> (the nasal dot). Adorned — connected — with these, the meaning is: thus, <s>drīṃ dhrīṃ jrīṃ jhrīṃ</s>. After that, '<s>Jaya Kṛṣṇa</s>' — thus [say] the <s>Tripāṭhi-Govinda-Miśra</s> and others. In reality, the pair of the word '<s>Jaya Kṛṣṇa</s>'; after that, '<s>nirantara</s>' is the form; <s>ātma-bhū</s> is the letter <s>ka</s>; <s>śikhi</s> (fire) is <s>repha</s>; <s>Śakti</s> is the <s>ī</s>-vowel — thus '<s>krī</s>' is the form. After that, '<s>ḍa</s>' is the form; '<s>āsya-vṛta</s>' (mouth-surrounded) is the <s>ā</s>-vowel — '<s>ḍā</s>' is the form. '<s>Sakta</s>' is the form; '<s>pra-ni</s>' — between these two syllables, '<s>mudita-cetase</s>'; then after '<s>ni</s>', '<s>tya</s>' is the form; then '<s>pa</s>' is the form; '<s>rakta</s>' (red) is <s>repha</s>; '<s>dṛg</s>' (eye) is the <s>i</s>-vowel — since there is no reason for exceeding the basic form, the short <s>i</s>-vowel is obtained; thus '<s>pri</s>' is the form; then '<s>ya</s>' is the form; '<s>guru</s>' (heavy) is the <s>ā</s>-vowel — '<s>yā</s>' is the form. Then <s>māruta</s> (wind) is the <s>ya</s>-letter. Then the word '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' with the fourth case (dative) — '<s>Kṛṣṇāya</s>' is the form. Then <s>ikṣu-kārmuka</s> (sugarcane-bowed one) is the <s>kāma-bīja</s> (love-seed syllable). Then the previously stated ten-syllable mantra. Then <s>lava</s> (drop) is <s>bindu</s>; <s>dharā</s> (earth) combined with it is the <s>ai</s>-vowel — '<s>aiṃ</s>' is the form. <s>Acala</s> (mountain); its daughter (<s>sutā</s>) is <s>Pārvatī</s> — the <s>Bhuvaneśvarī-bīja</s>, this is the meaning. <s>Ramā</s> is the <s>Śrī-bīja</s>. With these three seed-syllables, read in reverse order at the end of the mantra — <s>aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ</s> at the end, <s>śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ</s> — enclosed like a box (<s>samudga</s>), this fifty-two-syllable mantra becomes perfected. He states the syllable-count of the mantra — with 'thus': <s>danta</s> = 32, <s>sūrya</s> = 12, <s>vasu</s> = 8 — combined, the count is fifty-two syllables — this is the meaning. Of what kind? The producer of poetic delight and the beauty of <s>Lakṣmī</s>; likewise, the destroyer of sins (<s>agha-hṛt</s>).

children.text: mantra-svarūpam-aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ drīṃ jrīṃ jhrīṃ jaya kṛṣṇa jaya kṛṣṇa nirantara-krīḍāsakta-pramudita-cetase nitya-priyāya kṛṣṇāya krīṃ gopī-jana-vallabhāya svāhā śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ ||
children.translated_text: The form of the mantra: <s>aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ drīṃ jrīṃ jhrīṃ jaya kṛṣṇa jaya kṛṣṇa nirantara-krīḍāsakta-pramudita-cetase nitya-priyāya kṛṣṇāya krīṃ gopī-jana-vallabhāya svāhā śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ</s>.
He states the <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer) and other [attributes] of this mantra —
<s>Mukha-vṛtta</s> (face-round, i.e., <s>ā</s>) joined with <s>Nanda</s> — <s>Nārada</s> is the seer (<s>muni</s>);
the meter is said to be <s>Amṛtādi-Virāṭ</s>;
<s>Hari</s>, known as <s>Trijagad-vimohana</s> (Enchanter of the Three Worlds),
is indeed the deity of this [mantra], as declared by the sages.

children.text: mukha-vṛttam ā-kāraḥ nandeti svarūpam ābhyāṃ yuto nāradaḥ | tathā ca ānanda-nārada-ṛsiḥ amṛtādikaṃ virāṭ chandas trailokya-mohano harir devatā nāradādibhir munibhiḥ kathitā || KrdC_8.57 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mukha-vṛtta</s> (face-round) is the <s>ā</s>-letter; '<s>Nanda</s>' is the form — joined with these two [gives] <s>Nārada</s>. Thus, <s>Ānanda-Nārada</s> is the seer (<s>ṛṣi</s>). <s>Amṛtādi-Virāṭ</s> is the meter (<s>chandas</s>). <s>Trailokya-mohana Hari</s> (Enchanter of the Three Worlds) is the deity — as declared by <s>Nārada</s> and other sages.
He shows the method of the limbs (<s>aṅga</s>s) —
With the syllables of the mantra [numbered] <s>vasu</s> (8), <s>mitra</s> (12), <s>bhūdhara</s> (7), <s>gaja</s> (8), <s>ātmā</s> (1), <s>dik</s> (10),
arranged in triplets (<s>tripuṭa</s>), separately,
joined with their own kind — the six limbs (<s>ṣaḍ-aṅga</s>) are thus declared;
by their very performance, they produce the enchantment of all people.

children.text: vasuḥ = 8, mitraḥ = 12, bhūdharaḥ = 7, gajaḥ = 8, ātmā = 1, dik = 10 | etat saṅkhyākair mantrākṣarais tripuṭa-saṃsthitaiḥ | tathā ca aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ drīṃ vrīṃ jrīṃ jhrīṃ jaya-kṛṣṇa aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ | aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ jaya-kṛṣṇa-nirantara-krīḍāsakta aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ śirase svāhā - ity ādi kriyayaiva ṣaḍ-aṅga-kriyayaiva sarva-janānurāgaṃ janayati || KrdC_8.58 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vasu</s> = 8, <s>Mitra</s> = 12, <s>Bhūdhara</s> = 7, <s>Gaja</s> = 8, <s>Ātmā</s> = 1, <s>Dik</s> = 10 — with mantra-syllables of these counts, arranged in triplets. Thus: '<s>aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ drīṃ vrīṃ jrīṃ jhrīṃ jaya-kṛṣṇa aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ</s>'; '<s>aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ jaya-kṛṣṇa-nirantara-krīḍāsakta aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ śirase svāhā</s>' — and so forth. By the very performance of the six-limb ritual, it produces the affection of all people.
He states the <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement) —
Then, having purified the body through the previously taught method,
having arranged the seat (<s>pīṭha</s>) also with one's own body;
on the two hands, in the sequence of the ten-syllable method, one should place
the six limbs, the arrows (<s>sāyaka</s>), and the fivefold [forms of] <s>Anaṅga</s> (the god of Love).

children.text: athānantaraṃ tanuṃ śarīram ukta-mārgataḥ pūrvokta-bhūta-śuddhyāḥ prakāreṇa saṃśodhyānantaraṃ sva-varṣmaṇā sva-śarīreṇa pīṭham āracayya karayoḥ kara-yugale daśākṣarokta-prakāreṇa ṣaḍ-aṅga-ṣaṭkaṃ sāyakān ca śoṣaṇādīn bāṇān anaṅga-pañcakaṃ kāma-bīja-manmatha-kandarpa-makara-dhvaja-manobhūta-saṃjñakaṃ kāma-pañcakaṃ nyaset || KrdC_8.59 ||
children.translated_text: Then, having purified the body — through the previously described method of <s>bhūta-śuddhi</s> (purification of elements); thereafter, having arranged the seat with one's own body; on both hands, in the manner described for the ten-syllable [mantra], one should place the six limbs, the arrows — the drying and other arrows (<s>śoṣaṇa</s> etc.) — and the fivefold <s>Anaṅga</s> — the five [aspects of] <s>Kāma</s> named <s>Kāma-bīja</s>, <s>Manmatha</s>, <s>Kandarpa</s>, <s>Makara-dhvaja</s>, and <s>Manobhūta</s>.
He shows this very meaning in detail —
With the mantra, one should place three times upon the entire body,
enclosed in <s>Smara</s> (love-seed); thereafter, with the <s>mātṛkā</s>-letters (alphabet);
the ten <s>tattva</s>s and the rest, described with ten syllables —
then one should perform [the placements] up to and ending with the body-cage (<s>mūrti-pañjara</s>).

children.text: manunā mūla-mantreṇa pūrvaṃ śarīre tri-vyāpakaṃ kuryāt | tad-anantaraṃ prativarṇaṃ kāma-bīja-puṭitair mātṛkākṣaraiḥ triśo nyasatu | daśa-varṇa-kīrtitaṃ daśākṣarokta-daśa-tattvakān nyaset | tattva-nyāsādi-mūrti-pañjarāntaṃ vinyasya || KrdC_8.60 ||
children.translated_text: With the mantra — the root mantra — one should first perform the pervading [placement] (<s>vyāpaka</s>) three times upon the body. Thereafter, with <s>mātṛkā</s>-letters enclosed in the love-seed for each letter, one should place three times. The ten <s>tattva</s>s described with ten syllables — one should place them as described for the ten-syllable [mantra]. Having placed from the <s>tattva-nyāsa</s> up to and ending with the body-cage (<s>mūrti-pañjara</s>) —
one should perform the creation and maintenance [placements], the ten [<s>tattva</s>s], six limbs, and arrows;
then one should place [them]; everything else, as previously stated.
Having duly performed [all this], meditating upon <s>Mukunda</s>, the sole witness of all worlds —
the one of faultless, steady intellect should remember [him].

children.text: sṛṣṭi-sthitī samācaret daśāṅgāni ṣaḍ-aṅgāni bāṇāṃś ca dehe vinyaset | tad-anantaram ātmārcanādy-akhilaṃ pūrvavat kṛtvā sakala-loka-draṣṭāraṃ śrī-kṛṣṇaṃ smaratāt cintayatu, nirmalāsthirā buddhir yasya sa tathā tādṛśaḥ sādhakaḥ || KrdC_8.61 ||
children.translated_text: One should perform the creation and maintenance [placements]; one should place the ten [<s>tattva</s>s], six limbs, and arrows upon the body. Thereafter, having performed all the rest — self-worship (<s>ātmārcana</s>) etc. — as before, one should remember — contemplate — <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, the seer of all worlds. [The practitioner should be] one whose intellect is pure and steady — such a practitioner.
He states the meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>) —
Then, in [a city] adorned by mountains and oceans, with lofty, great
halls, gateways, and broad avenues;
crowded with towering mansions touching the dense [clouds],
with gem-[studded] palaces, expansive doors, and platforms —

children.text: athānantaraṃ svake pure maṇi-maṇḍape sura-pādapasya kalpa-vṛkṣasyādho maṇi-maya-bhūtale parisphurat pṛthu-siṃha-vaktra-caraṇāmbujāsane sthūla-siṃha-mukhākāra-pādānvita-pīṭha-padmāsane samupaviṣṭam acyutam abhicintayet | kīdṛśe pure ? bhūdharāḥ parvatāḥ udadhiḥ samudraḥ etaiḥ pariṣkṛte veṣṭite tathā mahonnataḥ atyuccaḥ śālaḥ prakāro gopuraṃ bahir-dvāraṃ ca yatra tasmin tathā viśālā mahatī vīthikā panthāḥ yatra tatra karmadhārayaḥ tathā megha-sparśi atiśuddha-dhavala-gṛha-vyāpte tathā maṇi-maya-gṛhe vistīrṇāḥ kapāṭāḥ tathā vedikā pariṣkṛta-bhūmir yatra tatra || KrdC_8.62 ||
children.translated_text: Then, in his own city, in a gem-pavilion, beneath a divine tree — a wish-fulfilling tree (<s>kalpa-vṛkṣa</s>) — on a gem-paved ground, upon a lotus-throne with feet in the form of thick, shining lion-faces — upon a seat-lotus with legs shaped as stout lion-heads — one should contemplate <s>Acyuta</s> (the Imperishable) seated [thus]. In what kind of city? Adorned (<s>pariṣkṛta</s>) — surrounded — by mountains (<s>bhūdhara</s>) and ocean (<s>udadhi</s>); with lofty (<s>mahonnata</s>) — very tall — enclosure walls (<s>śāla</s>) and outer gateways (<s>gopura</s>); with broad (<s>viśāla</s>) — great — avenues (<s>vīthikā</s>), paths — a compound [of these terms]; likewise, pervaded by cloud-touching, extremely pure, white mansions; with expansive doors in gem-studded palaces; and with platforms (<s>vedikā</s>) — decorated ground-levels — in such [a city].
Again, in what kind of city?
With houses of <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s, kings (<s>bhūpa</s>), merchants (<s>viṭ</s>), and those of <s>śūdra</s> (<s>caraṇa</s>) birth,
and with various dwellings of artisan-folk (<s>śilpi-jana</s>); likewise,
with elephants, horses, camels, donkeys, cows, bulls —
And with goat-pens, gleaming, by the thousands. // <s>Krd</s> 8.63 //

children.text: sahasraśo lokair brāhmaṇa-kṣatriya-vaiśya-śūdrāṇāṃ nānā-prakāra-gṛhaiḥ tathā śilpi-janānāṃ gṛhas tathā hasty aśvameṣa-gardabha-dhenu-mahiṣa-cchagalānāṃ gṛhaiḥ śobhite || KrdC_8.63 ||
children.translated_text: By thousands of people, adorned with the various houses of <s>brāhmaṇa</s>s, <s>kṣatriya</s>s, <s>vaiśya</s>s, and <s>śūdra</s>s; likewise with the houses of artisans; and with the stables and pens of elephants, horses, rams, donkeys, milch-cows, buffaloes, and goats. || <s>KrdC</s> 8.63 ||
Again, of what description [is the city]?
Filled with the accumulated wealth of buying and selling, brought by great merchants frequenting various market-streets,
And adorned
With the splendid houses of beautiful women skilled in captivating the minds of people,
Most charming. // <s>Krd</s> 8.64 //

children.text: nānā-prakāra-vipaṇi-samāśrite mahā-janāhṛta-kraya-vikraya-draviṇa-saṃcaya-vyāpte | punaḥ kīdṛśe ? janānāṃ cittāpaharaṇe caturāḥ ye veśyā-janās teṣāṃ gṛhaiḥ śobhamānair alaṅkṛte || KrdC_8.64 ||
children.translated_text: Frequented by various market-streets — filled with the accumulated wealth of buying and selling brought by great merchants. Again, of what description? Adorned with the splendid houses of courtesans — those who are clever at stealing the minds of people. || <s>KrdC</s> 8.64 ||
With broad, limpid pools of clear water, where glitter
Fully blossomed lotuses, [attended by] birds greedy for their nectar —
Noble swans, cranes, and <s>cakravāka</s>s (ruddy geese) by name —
Whose calls fill all the directions, in his own city. // <s>Krd</s> 8.65 //
Again, of what description is the city?

children.text: sthūla-sarovara-nirmalodake dedīpyamāna-vikasita-kamala-makarandākhya-rasa-lolupaiḥ śreṣṭha-haṃsa-sārasa-cakravāka-saṃjñakaiḥ pakṣibhir dhvanitā diśo yasmin || KrdC_8.65 ||
children.translated_text: With the clear water of broad lakes, birds greedy for the nectar of shining, fully blossomed lotuses — noble swans, <s>sārasa</s> cranes, and <s>cakravāka</s>s (ruddy geese) by name — by whom the directions resound. || <s>KrdC</s> 8.65 ||
Again, of what description is the gem-pavilion?
With divine wish-fulfilling trees, swarming with bees greedy for fragrant blossoms,
Bestowing various desires upon people,
With tips swaying in the auspicious, gentle breeze, enclosed [by them] —
In the gem-pavilion, radiant as a thousand suns. // <s>Krd</s> 8.66 //

children.text: kalpa-vṛkṣaiḥ sugandhi-puṣpa-lubdha-bhramara-vyāptair manuṣyāṇāṃ vividha-kāmadaiḥ śubha-manda-māruta-calad-agra-bhāgais tair veṣṭite | sūrya-sahasra-māna-prabhe || KrdC_8.66 ||
children.translated_text: With wish-fulfilling trees, pervaded by bees attracted to fragrant flowers, bestowing various desires upon humans, with their upper parts swaying in the auspicious, gentle breeze — enclosed by them. Having the radiance equal to a thousand suns. || <s>KrdC</s> 8.66 ||
Again, of what description?
With its interior illuminated by clusters of gem-lamps,
Furnished with fine, variegated, expansive canopies,
Graceful, with garlands of various [flowers accompanied by the calls of] cuckoos,
With its floor sprinkled with richly fragrant scented water. // <s>Krd</s> 8.67 //

children.text: maṇir eva dīpikā tasyāḥ samūhe prakāśita-madhya-bhāge | punaḥ kīdṛśe ? sūkṣma-vicitra-vistīrṇa-candrātapa-yukte | punaḥ kīdṛśe ? vikasita-nānā-prakāra-puṣpa-mālābhiḥ śobhite atisurabhi-salila-sikta-sthāne || KrdC_8.67 ||
children.translated_text: Gems themselves serve as lamps — with clusters of those illuminating the interior. Again, of what description? Furnished with fine, variegated, spacious awnings. Again, of what description? Adorned with garlands of fully blossomed flowers of various kinds; with its floor sprinkled with exceedingly fragrant water. || <s>KrdC</s> 8.67 ||
Again, of what description?
Attended by hundreds of women with eyes rolling in intoxication,
Languid with rapture, with <s>cāmara</s> fly-whisks trembling in their hands,
With sweetly faltering speech,
With slender waists bending under the weight of their breasts. // <s>Krd</s> 8.68 //

children.text: strī-śatair mada-vighūrṇita-netrair mada-janitālasya-sahitaiḥ hasta-sthita-cañcala-cāmarair īṣat-skhalita-manohara-vacanaiḥ stana-bhāra-namra-sūkṣma-madhya-pradeśaiḥ paritaḥ sevite || KrdC_8.68 ||
children.translated_text: Attended all around by hundreds of women with eyes rolling in intoxication, with languor born of rapture, with trembling <s>cāmara</s> fly-whisks held in their hands, with slightly faltering, charming speech, with slender midsections bending under the weight of their breasts. || <s>KrdC</s> 8.68 ||
Of what description is the wish-fulfilling tree?
Ceaselessly showering streams of the finest gems,
Dripping nectar-essence that removes fatigue — beneath [it],
Of the divine tree, on a gem-studded ground, a resplendent
Broad lion-faced throne with lotus-seat. // <s>Krd</s> 8.69 //
Ceaselessly showering streams of the finest gems. Again, of what description? Dripping nectar-essence that removes fatigue. || <s>KrdC</s> 8.69 ||
Of what description is <s>Acyuta</s>?
One should meditate on <s>Acyuta</s>, comfortably seated,
With a complexion soft as a fresh, dark-blue water-lily,
With a crown glittering upon curly-tipped locks,
With ear-ornaments fashioned of smile-like flowers and gems. // <s>Krd</s> 8.70 //

children.text: nūtana-nīlotpala-ramya-kāntim | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? kuṭilāgra-keśeṣu sphurat kirīṭaṃ yasya tam | punaḥ kīdṛśam ? smitam īṣad vikasitaṃ puṣpaṃ ratnāni ca te racito 'vataṃso yena tam || KrdC_8.70 ||
children.translated_text: With the beautiful luster of a fresh dark-blue lotus. Again, of what description? With a crown glittering upon curly-tipped locks. Again, of what description? With ear-ornaments fashioned of slightly blossoming flowers and gems. || <s>KrdC</s> 8.70 ||
With a beautiful forehead, a prominent nose, and uplifted brows,
With large, reddish, long, restless eyes,
With cheeks illuminated by the rays of gem-studded earrings,
With lips as red as fresh <s>bandhujīva</s> (noon-flower) blossoms. // <s>Krd</s> 8.71 //
Again, of what description?

children.text: tathā śobhamāna-lalāṭaṃ tathā ucca-nāsikam udgacchad-bhrū-latākam, tathā sthūlāruṇa-varṇa-dīrgha-cañcala-nayanaṃ, tathā maṇi-maya-kuṇḍala-kiraṇa-pariśobhita-gaṇḍa-sthalaṃ yathā nūtana-bandhu-jīva-puṣpa-sadṛśāruṇādharam || KrdC_8.71 ||
children.translated_text: Likewise with a beautiful forehead; with a high nose and rising brow-creepers; with large, reddish, long, restless eyes; with cheek-surfaces beautified by the rays of gem-studded earrings; with lips as red as fresh <s>bandhujīva</s> flowers. || <s>KrdC</s> 8.71 ||
Again, of what description is the Supreme Lord?
With the directions illuminated by the moonlight of his smile, with a face
Adorned with tiny beads of perspiration from the thrills of joy,
With shoulders adorned by finest necklaces and garlands,
Brilliant with ornaments blazing with clusters of radiant gems. // <s>Krd</s> 8.72 //

With the directions whitened by the rays of the moon of his laughter; with a face beautified by drops of perspiration born from manifest goosebumps. Again, of what description? With shoulders adorned by garlands of the finest necklaces, ornaments blazing with clusters of radiant, glittering gems. || <s>KrdC</s> 8.72 ||
With a body anointed with camphor and <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron),
Resplendent with twelve broad, long arms,
With auspicious lotus-feet beautiful as fresh lotuses,
With limbs tormented [by love], and two lotus-hands resting on his lap. // <s>Krd</s> 8.73 //
Again, of what description?

children.text: punaś candana-kuṅkumābhyāṃ parilipta-śarīraṃ punaḥ sthūla-dīrgha-dvādaśa-hastair virājitaṃ tathā nūtanāruṇa-varṇa-padma-sadṛśa-caraṇa-padmaṃ punaḥ kāma-pīḍita-dehaṃ punaḥ svāṅke āropita-hasta-dvayam || KrdC_8.73 ||
children.translated_text: Again, with a body smeared with sandalwood and saffron; again, resplendent with twelve broad, long arms; likewise, with lotus-feet resembling fresh, reddish-hued lotuses; again, with a body afflicted by love; again, with two hands placed upon his own lap. || <s>KrdC</s> 8.73 ||
Seated on his lap, the daughter of <s>Bhīṣmaka</s>, between her broad thighs,
Her — of the luster of molten gold — with his own lotus-arms,
Embracing; and she, with moistened loins, embracing
Him with her long, shining, sprout-like hands. // <s>Krd</s> 8.74 //

children.text: punaḥ svāṅke sthitāyā rukmiṇyā ūru-dvayābhyantare vidyamānaṃ | punas tāṃ rukmiṇīṃ tapta-suvarṇa-kāntiṃ svīya-hasta-padmābhyām āliṅgantam | kīdṛśīṃ tām ? ārdra-jaghanām punar ātmānam śrī-kṛṣṇaṃ dīrgha-manohara-pāṇi-pallavābhyāṃ āliṅgantīm || KrdC_8.74 ||
children.translated_text: Again, situated between the two thighs of <s>Rukmiṇī</s> seated on his lap. Again, embracing that <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, who has the luster of molten gold, with his own lotus-hands. Of what kind is she? With moistened loins. Again, she embracing <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> himself with her long, charming, sprout-like hands. || <s>KrdC</s> 8.74 ||
Overcome by the excess of bliss, with half-closed lotus-eyes, with limbs gone limp,
With body adorned by pearl-like dewdrops of dense perspiration arising from manifest goosebumps,
With all outer and inner faculties absorbed in him, with motionless limbs,
Submerged, with stilled and various thoughts, in the ocean of incomparable, great bliss. // <s>Krd</s> 8.75 //

children.text: punaḥ svātmānandodreka-vyāptāṃ | punaḥ mudrita-nayana-nīlotpalāṃ | punaḥ prodyat-tanu-pulaka-janya-niviḍa-prasveda-bindu-rūpa-mauktika-śobhita-dehāṃ | punaḥ ātmani śrī-kṛṣṇe samyag-vilīna-bāhyābhyantarendriya-samūhāṃ | punar vyāpāra-rahitaiḥ śarīraāvayavair atiśayita-mahānanda-samūha-sāgare nimagnāṃ | punaḥ vigata-cañcala-matim || KrdC_8.75 ||
children.translated_text: Again, overcome by the surge of her own bliss. Again, with half-closed lotus-like dark eyes. Again, with a body beautified by pearl-like dense drops of perspiration born from manifest bodily horripilation. Again, with all outer and inner sense-faculties fully absorbed in <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>. Again, submerged in the ocean of surpassing great bliss with inactive bodily limbs. Again, with stilled, unflickering mind. || <s>KrdC</s> 8.75 ||
Again, of what description is the Supreme Lord?
[Embraced] by <s>Satyā</s> (<s>Satyabhāmā</s>) and <s>Jāmbavatī</s>,
[Who are adorned] with divine silken garments, unguents, and ornaments,
Tormented by the arrows of the Love-god (<s>Manmatha</s>),
With bee-like restless eyes [fixed] upon the lotus of his face. // <s>Krd</s> 8.76 //

children.text: satyabhhāmā-jāmbavatībhyām āliṅganam | kathambhūtābhyām ? utkṛṣṭāni paṭṭa-vastrānulepanābharaṇāni yayos tābhyāṃ | punaḥ kāma-śara-pīḍitābhyāṃ | punaḥ kṛṣṇa-mukha-viṣayaka-cañcala-netra-bhramarābhyām || KrdC_8.76 ||
children.translated_text: The embrace by <s>Satyabhāmā</s> and <s>Jāmbavatī</s>. Of what description are they? With exquisite silk garments, unguents, and ornaments. Again, tormented by the arrows of the Love-god. Again, with bee-like restless eyes [fixed] upon the lotus of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s face. || <s>KrdC</s> 8.76 ||
Embraced by a pair of serpents [i.e., his arms],
With dark and reddish, graceful, tender body-creepers,
Embracing him, stationed at his right
And left, with lotuses gleaming in their hands. // <s>Krd</s> 8.77 //

children.text: punaḥ parameśvarasya bhuja-yugalenāliṅgitābhyām | yathā-krama-nīlāruṇa-varṇe manohare komale cāṅga-late yayos tābhyāṃ | punaḥ parameśvarasya dakṣiṇa-vāma-gatābhyāṃ | punaḥ pāṇi-sphurita-padmābhyām || KrdC_8.77 ||
children.translated_text: Again, embraced by the pair of the Supreme Lord's arms. With body-creepers that are, respectively, dark and reddish, charming, and tender. Again, stationed at the Supreme Lord's right and left. Again, with lotuses gleaming in their hands. || <s>KrdC</s> 8.77 ||
Embraced from behind by <s>Kālindī</s> (the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s>, i.e., <s>Yamunā</s>), with lotus-hand joined [to him],
Of collyrium-dark complexion, tormented by love,
With two pairs of arms bearing the lotus, mace, discus, and conch,
And two arms holding a flute, with a lotus-face radiant. // <s>Krd</s> 8.78 //
Again, of what description?

children.text: parameśvara-pṛṣṭha-deśa-vartinyā yamunayā hasta-dhṛta-kamalayā samāliṅgitam | kimbhūtayā śyāmayā ? punaḥ kāma-pīḍitayā | punaḥ kīdṛśaṃ parameśvaram ? padma-gadā-śaṅkha-cakra-yukta-hasta-catuṣṭayaṃ hasta-dvaya-dhṛta-vaṃśa-vilasan-mukha-kamalam || KrdC_8.78 ||
children.translated_text: Embraced by <s>Yamunā</s> (<s>Kālindī</s>), stationed behind the Supreme Lord, with a lotus held in her hand — of dark complexion. Again, tormented by love. Again, of what description is the Supreme Lord? With four hands bearing lotus, mace, conch, and discus; with a lotus-face radiant [while] two hands hold a flute. || <s>KrdC</s> 8.78 ||
In the directions outside, by divine sages and ascetics, by the foremost of sky-travelers (<s>khecara</s>s),
With bodies bowed by the weight of devotion, with mouths murmuring praises,
Constantly served — beyond the reach of mind and speech,
The bestower of the four goals of life, the father of the three worlds — him [one should meditate upon]. // <s>Krd</s> 8.79 //

children.text: tṛtīya-paṭalokta-krameṇety arthaḥ | punaḥ bahir dikṣu devarṣi-yatibhiḥ khecara-mukhyair bhakty-atiśaya-namra-dehaiḥ | parivṛḍhaiḥ pradhānaiḥ stutibhiḥ vācāla-vadanair nirantaraṃ sevitaṃ punaḥ manaso vācām agocaraṃ punar dharmārtha-kāma-mokṣa-phala-catuṣṭaya-pradaṃ punas trailokya-janakam || KrdC_8.79 ||
children.translated_text: In the sequence stated in the third chapter — this is the meaning. Again, in the outer directions, by divine sages and ascetics, by the foremost of sky-travelers, with bodies bowed by an excess of devotion; by the principal ones; with mouths loquacious with praises — constantly served. Again, beyond the reach of the mind and speech. Again, the bestower of the four fruits — <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s>. Again, the father of the three worlds. || <s>KrdC</s> 8.79 ||
Immersed in the ocean of dense bliss, established in his own pure radiance —

children.text: dhyātvaivaṃ paramaṃ pumāṃsam anaghāt samprāpya dīkṣāṃ guroḥ |
children.translated_text: Having thus meditated on the Supreme Person, having obtained initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) from a sinless <s>guru</s>,

children.text: labdhvāmuṃ manum ādareṇa sita-dhīr lakṣaṃ japed yoṣitāṃ
children.translated_text: Having received this mantra, the one of pure mind should recite one <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand) with devotion, avoiding
The hearing of talk, seeing, etc. of women — the ritualist [should avoid] even [women who are] teachers. // <s>Krd</s> 8.80 //

children.text: punar niviḍānanda-mahā-samudra-magnam | svīye nirmale tejasi-tad-rūpeṇāvasthitam evam ukta-rūpaṃ parameśvaraṃ vicintya niṣpāpāt guror dīkṣā-mantropadeśa-vidhiṃ prāpyāmuṃ mantraṃ labdhvā tīkṣṇa-buddhiḥ ādarāt lakṣam ekaṃ japet | kīdṛśaḥ sādhakaḥ ? strīṇāṃ vṛddhānām api kathā-śravaṇa-nirīkṣaṇa-parāṅmukhaḥ || KrdC_8.80 ||
children.translated_text: Again, immersed in the great ocean of dense bliss. Established in his own pure radiance — existing in that form. Having contemplated the Supreme Lord in the described form, having obtained from a sinless <s>guru</s> the procedure of <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) and mantra-instruction, having received this mantra, the one of keen intellect should recite one <s>lakṣa</s> with devotion. Of what kind is the practitioner? One who turns away from hearing the conversation, seeing, etc. of women — even elderly ones. || <s>KrdC</s> 8.80 ||
He states the <s>homa</s> (fire-offering) and the practice —
One should offer one-tenth [of the recitation count] into the fire,
With <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice) mixed with sugar, honey, and ghee;
On the excellent seat previously described,
One should worship him daily, for liberation from impermanence. // <s>Krd</s> 8.81 //

children.text: hutāśe vahnau daśāṃśakaṃ | ayutam ekaṃ śarkarā-madhu-ghṛta-yuktena paramānnena juhuyāt | kiṃ ca pūrvokta-daśāṣṭādaśākṣara-kathite pīṭha-śreṣṭhe nityam amuṃ yajet | kim artham ? anityaḥ saṃsāras tasya pariharaṇāya || KrdC_8.81 ||
children.translated_text: Into the fire, one-tenth — one <s>ayuta</s> (ten thousand) — with <s>paramānna</s> (fine milk-rice) mixed with sugar, honey, and ghee, one should offer. Furthermore, on the excellent seat described in the ten- and eighteen-syllable [mantra sections] previously, one should worship him daily. For what purpose? For the removal of <s>saṃsāra</s> (impermanent worldly existence). || <s>KrdC</s> 8.81 ||
Having begun and performed in the sequence of <s>vibhūti-nyāsa</s> (glory-placement), up to the weapon (<s>astra</s>), worship;
From <s>mūrti</s> (form) up to the limbs — and [worship of] the Self, on the excellent <s>yantra</s> proclaimed with twenty syllables; // <s>Krd</s> 8.82 //
Having written the central seed-syllable, all around in the directions of <s>Varuṇa</s> (west), <s>Indu</s> (north-east), <s>Yama</s> (south), and <s>Indra</s> (east),

children.text: bīja-catuṣkaṃ tad api catvāriṃśadbhir akṣarair dvy-adhikaiḥ // Krd_8.83 //
children.translated_text: A group of four seed-syllables; and that [surrounded] by forty-two syllables; // <s>Krd</s> 8.83 //

children.text: śiṣṭaiḥ praveṣṭya śiva-hari-vasv-ādy-aśriṣv atha kramād vilikhet |
children.translated_text: With the remaining [syllables], having entered [them] into the corners of <s>Śiva</s> (north-east), <s>Hari</s> (south-west), <s>Vasu</s> (north-west), etc., one should then write in sequence;
The <s>Vāk</s> (speech), <s>Māyā</s>, and <s>Śrī</s> mantras, similarly in the corners of <s>Rakṣas</s> (south-west), water (west), and wind (north-west). // <s>Krd</s> 8.84 //

children.text: śeṣaṃ pūrvoditavad vidhāya pīṭhaṃ yathāvad abhyarcya |
children.translated_text: Having performed the remainder as previously stated, having duly worshipped the seat (<s>pīṭha</s>);

children.text: saṅkalayya mūrtim atrāvāhyābhyarcayatu madhya-bīje tam // Krd_8.85 //
children.translated_text: Having mentally formed the image (<s>mūrti</s>), invoked [it] here, one should worship him at the central seed-syllable.

children.text:
ārabhyety ādi vibhūti-pañjaram ārabhya nyāsa-krameṇa bāṇa-paryantaṃ pūjayitvā mūrti-nyāsam ārabhyāṅga-nyāsa-paryantaṃ cātma-rūpaṃ sampūjya pūrvokta-viṃśaty-akṣara-mantroktaṃ yantra-śreṣṭha-karṇikā-madhya-sthita-vahni-pura-yuga-madhye madhyama-bīja-madhye bījam iti pāṭha-svarasāt hal-lekhā-bījam iti rudradhara-govinda-miśra-prabhṛtayaḥ | parastah-madhyama-bījam iti pāṭhe kāma-bījaṃ vilikhya tat-paritaś ca paścimottara-pūrva-dakṣiṇa-dikṣu bīja-catuṣkaṃ drīṃ trīṃ jīṃ jhrīṃ iti bīja-catuṣṭayaṃ vilikhya tad api bīja-catuṣṭayaṃ dvi-catvāriṃśat japādi-svāhāntaiḥ śiṣṭair mantrākṣarair upari veṣṭayet | anantaraṃ śiva īśānaḥ harir indraḥ pūrvādi dig ity arthaḥ | vasur agniḥ āgneyādika evaṃ nairṛtī-vāruṇī-vāyavī-dig
eteṣu koṇeṣu krameṇa vāg-bhava-bhuvaneśvarī-śrī-bījāni trir āvṛtya vilikhet |
children.translated_text:
Beginning from '<s>ārabhya</s>' etc. — beginning from the <s>vibhūti-pañjara</s> (glory-cage), having worshipped in the order of <s>nyāsa</s> (placement) up to the arrows, and from the image-placement up to the limb-placement, having worshipped the Self-form; at the center of the pair of fire-city [triangles] situated in the middle of the pericarp of the supreme <s>yantra</s> as described for the twenty-syllable mantra, at the central seed-syllable — by the natural reading '<s>bīja</s>' means the <s>hal-lekhā</s> seed-syllable according to <s>Rudradhara</s>, <s>Govinda Miśra</s>, and others; in the reading '<s>madhyama-bīja</s>' the <s>kāma-bīja</s> (love-seed) should be inscribed; and around it, in the western, northern, eastern, and southern directions, the four seed-syllables <s>drīṃ trīṃ jīṃ jhrīṃ</s> should be inscribed; those four seed-syllables too should be encircled above with the remaining mantra-syllables — forty-two — ending with '<s>japādi-svāhā</s>.'
