Then, '<s>Śiva</s>' means <s>Īśāna</s> (northeast); '<s>Hari</s>' means <s>Indra</s> (east); meaning the directions beginning with the east. '<s>Vasu</s>' means <s>Agni</s> (fire, southeast); and so likewise southwest, west, and northwest —
at these corners, in sequence, the <s>vāg-bhava</s>, <s>bhuvaneśvarī</s>, and <s>śrī</s> seed-syllables should be inscribed, repeated three times.

children.text: avaśiṣṭaṃ pīṭha-vidhānaṃ pūrvavat samāpya pīṭhaṃ yathāvat pūjayitvā tatra pīṭhe karṇikā-madhya-sthita-kāma-bīje rukmiṇī-vallabha-mūrtiṃ saṅkalpya dhyātvā tam āvāhya pūjayet || KrdC_8.82-85 ||
children.translated_text: Having completed the remaining seat-procedure as before, having duly worshipped the seat, upon that seat — at the <s>kāma-bīja</s> in the middle of the pericarp — one should mentally form the image of the beloved of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, meditate [upon him], invoke [him], and worship [him].
At the seed-syllables in front, to the right, to the left, and behind [the deity], the <s>Śakti</s>s (powers) should be worshipped in sequence;

children.text: rukmiṇy-ādyāḥ ṣaṭsv atha koṇeṣv aṅgāni keśareṣu śarān // Krd_8.86 //
children.translated_text: <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and the others; then at the six corners, the limbs (<s>aṅga</s>s); at the filaments, the arrows (<s>śara</s>s).

children.text: anantaraṃ devasya san-mukha-dakṣiṇa-vāma-pṛṣṭha-pradeśa-gateṣu bīja-catuṣṭayeṣu rukmiṇy-ādyāḥ śaktayaḥ pūjyāḥ ṣaṭ-koṇeṣu aṅgāni keśareṣu śarān pūjayet || KrdC_8.86 ||
children.translated_text: Next, at the four seed-syllables situated in the positions in front, to the right, to the left, and behind the deity, <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and the other <s>Śakti</s>s should be worshipped. At the six corners, the limbs [should be worshipped]; at the filaments, one should worship the arrows.

children.text: lakṣmy-ādyā dala-madhyeṣv agny-ādiṣu tad bahir dhvaja-pramukhān |
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s> and the others at the middle of the petals beginning with fire (southeast); beyond that, <s>Dhvaja</s> and the other foremost [attendants];

children.text: agre ketuṃ śyāma pṛṣṭhe vipam aruṇam amala-rakta-rucī // Krd_8.87 //
children.translated_text: In front, <s>Ketu</s>, dark-colored; behind, <s>Vipa</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>), ruddy, of pure, red lustre;
On the two flanks, the lords of treasures (<s>Nidhīśa</s>s), constantly showering floods of wealth;
<s>Heramba</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>), <s>Śāstṛ</s> (<s>Skanda</s>), <s>Durgā</s>, and <s>Viṣvaksena</s> in the intermediate directions beginning with fire (southeast);
With the lustres of coral, emerald, <s>dūrvā</s>-grass, and gold; beyond that, <s>Indra</s>, the thunderbolt, and the other [directional guardians and weapons];
Thus is declared the worship-procedure of <s>Mukunda</s>, endowed with seven enclosures.

children.text: agny-ādi-patra-madhyeṣu lakṣmy-ādyā pūjyāḥ | tatra bahir-bhāge dhvaja-prabhṛtīn pūjayet | anantaraṃ devasya san-mukhe śyāma-varṇa-ketu-nāmānaṃ gaṇaṃ pūjayet | deva-pṛṣṭha-bhāge aruṇa-varṇaṃ garuḍaṃ pūjayet | deva-pārśva-dvaye nirmala-rakta-rucīr nidhīśvarau pūjyau kīdrśau ? nirantara-dhārābhir vṛṣṭa-dhana-samūhau |
children.translated_text: At the middle of the petals beginning with fire (southeast), <s>Lakṣmī</s> and the others should be worshipped. In the outer area, <s>Dhvaja</s> (Banner) and the other [attendants] should be worshipped. Then, in front of the deity, one should worship the attendant named <s>Ketu</s>, dark in color. At the back of the deity, one should worship <s>Garuḍa</s>, ruddy in color. On the two flanks of the deity, the two lords of treasures should be worshipped — of what kind? Those who shower unceasing streams of heaped wealth.

children.text: vahny-ādi-vidikṣu herambādīn pravālādi-varṇān pūjayet | anantaraṃ bahir-dikṣu indrādi-loka-pālān tathā varjārdy-āyudhāni pūjayet | iti pūrvokta-prakāreṇa mukundasya śrī-kṛṣṇasyāvaraṇa-saptakaṃ pūjā-vidhānaṃ kathitam iti || KrdC_8.87-89 ||
children.translated_text: At the intermediate directions beginning with fire (southeast), one should worship <s>Heramba</s> (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>) and the others, with colors of coral and the like. Then, in the outer cardinal directions, one should worship <s>Indra</s> and the other world-guardians, and likewise the weapons such as the thunderbolt. Thus, in the previously described manner, the worship-procedure of <s>Mukunda</s> (<s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>) with seven enclosures has been described.
Thus worshipping <s>Acyuta</s> (the Imperishable One) with devotion,
Whoever serves this supreme mantra, with mind subdued,
He, worshipped even by divine beings, becomes for all people
A blazing sun [illuminating] the lotus-hearts and lotus-eyes [of all].

children.text: iti amunā prakāreṇa yo jitendriyo acyutaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ bhaktyā pūjayan amuṃ mantra-śreṣṭhaṃ sevate sa puruṣaḥ surair api pūjyate | kīdṛśaḥ ? lokānāṃ hṛdaya-padma-locana-padmayoḥ sūryaḥ sarva-jana-vaśīkaraṇa-mantraḥ samartha ity api pāṭhaḥ || KrdC_8.90 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in this manner, the self-controlled person who, worshipping <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) with devotion, serves this supreme mantra — that person is worshipped even by the gods. Of what kind? He becomes a sun to the lotus-hearts and lotus-eyes of all people — that is, a mantra capable of subjugating all people — thus also another reading.
With the intention of offering milk mixed with refined white sugar,
One should satisfy [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] at the start of each day, daily, one hundred [times]
With waters; he reduces the splendor of <s>Śatamakha</s> (<s>Indra</s>)
To a mere water-drop in the ocean of his own glory.

children.text: sita-śarkarā-pradhāna-pratipattyā dugdha-buddhyāḥ jalair eva dina-mukhe prātaḥ-kāle pratidinaṃ śata-kṛtvas taṃ tarpayet | anantaraṃ sādhakaḥ svādhipatya-samudre indrasya lakṣmīṃ jala-binduvat || KrdC_8.91 ||
children.translated_text: With the intention of [offering] milk dominated by refined white sugar — with water [imagined as] milk — at the beginning of the day, in the morning, daily, one should satisfy [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] one hundred times. Then the practitioner [renders] the splendor of <s>Indra</s> like a water-drop in the ocean of his own sovereignty.
With jasmine (<s>jātī</s>) and <s>mālatī</s> flowers, which are the best of fragrant blossoms,
Immersed in abundant liquid of camphor and sandalwood;
By offering ten thousand oblations with this mantra —

children.text: trijagat priyaḥ sa manuvit kavirāṭ syāt // Krd_8.92 //
children.translated_text: That mantra-knower becomes dear to the three worlds and a king among poets.

children.text: anena mantreṇa sumanaso jātī-mālatīnām adheyasya sumanobhiḥ puṣpaiḥ vikasi | taiḥ karpūra-yukta-candanasya bahu-drava-vyāptair ayuta-saṅkhyaṃ havanato 'yuta-home na sa mantrī trailokyasya priyaḥ kavi-śreṣṭhaś ca bhavati || KrdC_8.92 ||
children.translated_text: With this mantra, with jasmine and <s>mālatī</s> flowers — the best of fragrant blossoms — blooming. With those, immersed in abundant liquid of camphor-infused sandalwood, offering ten thousand oblations — by that <s>homa</s> — that <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner) becomes dear to the three worlds and the foremost of poets.

children.text: dhyānād evāsya sadyas tridaśa-mṛga-dṛśor vaśyatāṃ yānty avaśyaṃ
children.translated_text: Merely from meditating upon him, the doe-eyed women of the thirty [gods] certainly come under [his] sway;

children.text: kandarpārtājapādyaiḥ kim atha na sulabhaṃ mantrato 'smān narasya |
children.translated_text: Then what through recitation and the like is not easily obtainable from this mantra for a man?

children.text: spardhām uddhūya citraṃ mahad idam api naisargikīṃ śaśvad enaṃ
children.translated_text: Casting away their perennial rivalry — this is a wonder — constantly

children.text: sevete mantri-mukhyaṃ sarasija-nilayā cāpi vācām adhīśā // Krd_8.93 //
children.translated_text: Both <s>Sarasija-nilayā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>, she who dwells on the lotus) and the Mistress of Speech (<s>Sarasvatī</s>) attend upon this chief among <s>mantrī</s>s (practitioners).

children.text: asya rukmiṇī-vallabhasya dhyānāt śīghraṃ tridaśa-mṛga-dṛśaḥ devāṅganā avaśyaṃ vaśyatām āyāttatāṃ prāpnuvanti | kathambhūtāḥ ? kāma-pīḍitā | athānantaraṃ japa-homādināsmāt mantrāt sādhakasya kiṃ na sulabham | api tu sarvam eva sulabham ity arthaḥ | kiṃ ca, idam api mahac citraṃ yat sarasija-nilayā lakṣmīḥ vācām adhīśā sarasvatī ca svābhāvikīm asūyāṃ tyaktvā nityam enaṃ sādhaka-śreṣṭhaṃ sevete || KrdC_8.93 ||
children.translated_text: From meditating upon this beloved of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, quickly the doe-eyed divine women — the celestial maidens — certainly come under [his] sway. Of what kind? Those afflicted by love. Then, next, through recitation, <s>homa</s>, and the like, from this mantra, what is not easily obtainable for the practitioner? Rather, everything indeed becomes easily obtainable — this is the meaning. Moreover, this is a great wonder: <s>Sarasija-nilayā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) and the Mistress of Speech (<s>Sarasvatī</s>), casting aside their natural rivalry, constantly attend upon this chief among practitioners.
From mental anguish (<s>ādhi</s>), bodily disease (<s>vyādhi</s>), old age, untimely death, sins, ghosts, all poisons,

children.text: daubhāgyena daridratādibhir asau dūraṃ vimuktaś ciram |
children.translated_text: Ill fortune, poverty, and such — he is released far and for long;
Blessed with good sons, good daughters, friends, and retinues; always endowed with every kind of

children.text: sampadbhiḥ parijuṣṭa īḍita-yaśā jīved anekāḥ samāḥ // Krd_8.94 //
children.translated_text: Prosperity, with celebrated fame — he shall live many years.

children.text: kiṃ ca mano-duḥkha-roga-jarāpamṛtyu-śoka-śūnyaḥ sakala-prāṇibhir viṣaiḥ tathā duradṛṣṭena tathā daridratādibhir atiśayena parityakto bahu-kālaṃ vyāpya-viśiṣṭa-putra-sametaḥ sat-putrī-mitra-samūhena sevitaḥ sadā samṛddhaḥ īdita-yaśāḥ stuta-yaśāḥ asau sādhakaḥ anekāḥ samā hāyanāni jīvet || KrdC_8.94 ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, free from mental suffering, disease, old age, untimely death, and grief — from all living beings, from poisons, from ill fortune, from poverty and the like — exceedingly liberated for a long time; endowed with excellent sons, attended by good daughters and friends; always prosperous; with celebrated fame — that practitioner shall live many years.
He declares the superiority of [this mantra] over other mantras —
Among all mantras, the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> mantras are the most powerful;
Among those, the <s>Gopāla</s> mantras are endowed with the most exalted fruits;
Among those, this one called <s>Saṃmohana</s> (Enchantment) is the most potent —
A wish-fulfilling tree whose branches are the bestowal of incomparable wealth.

children.text: sarveṣu mantreṣu vaiṣṇava-mantrā atiśayena savīryāḥ teṣv api vaiṣṇava-mantreṣu gopāla-mantrā atipūjita-phala-yuktāḥ teṣv api gopāla-mantreṣu eṣa saṃmohanākhya-mantraḥ prabalataraḥ prakṛṣṭa-bala-yuktaḥ | punaḥ nirupamaiśvarya-dānaika-kalpa-vṛkṣaḥ || KrdC_8.95 ||
children.translated_text: Among all mantras, the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> mantras are exceedingly powerful; among those <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> mantras, the <s>Gopāla</s> mantras are endowed with the most honored fruits; among those <s>Gopāla</s> mantras, this mantra called <s>Saṃmohana</s> (Enchantment) is the most potent — supremely powerful. Moreover, it is the sole wish-fulfilling tree for the bestowal of incomparable sovereignty.

children.text: manum imam atihṛdyaṃ yo bhajed bhakti-namro
children.translated_text: Whoever serves this most delightful mantra, bowed with devotion,
Through recitation, <s>homa</s>, worship, and other [practices], endowed with meditation — the chief among <s>mantrī</s>s (practitioners),
With all the knots of <s>karma</s> shattered, with awakened consciousness,

children.text: vrajati sa tu padaṃ tan nitya-śuddhaṃ murāreḥ // Krd_8.96 //
children.translated_text: He truly goes to that eternally pure abode of <s>Murāri</s> (the slayer of <s>Mura</s>).

children.text: yo mantri-mukhyaḥ sādhaka-śreṣṭhaḥ dhyāna-yuktaḥ bhaktyā ārādhyatva-jñānena imaṃ mantraṃ manoharaṃ japa-dhyāna-homādibhir bhajet sa murāres tat-prasiddhaṃ padaṃ vrajati prāpnoti murā avidyā tasyā nāśakasya padam | kīdṛśaṃ padam ? avināśi sarva-kāluṣya-rahitam | sa kīdṛśaḥ ? vināśita-sakala-karma-bandhanaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? udbuddha-cetā vastu-grahaṇonmukha-cittaḥ || KrdC_8.96 ||
children.translated_text: The chief among practitioners — the best of <s>sādhaka</s>s — endowed with meditation, through the knowledge of [the Lord's] worthiness of worship, with devotion, serves this captivating mantra through recitation, meditation, <s>homa</s>, and other [practices] — he goes to — attains — that well-known abode of <s>Murāri</s> (the slayer of <s>Mura</s>, i.e., ignorance). Of what kind is that abode? Imperishable, free from all impurity. Of what kind is he? One whose bonds of all <s>karma</s>s have been destroyed. Again, of what kind? One whose consciousness is awakened — whose mind is directed toward the apprehension of Reality.
Now he states the yoga —

children.text: aṅgīkṛtyaikam eṣāṃ manum atha japa-homārcanādyair manūnām
children.translated_text: Having accepted one of these mantras and [perfected it] through recitation, <s>homa</s>, worship, and other [practices],
Having expelled enemies through the eightfold [yoga], with inner Self purified, delighted, and serene,

children.text: yogī yuñjīta yogān samucita-vihṛti-svapna-bodhā hṛtiḥ syāt
children.translated_text: The <s>yogī</s> should practice the yogas; eating, sleeping, and waking should be appropriate; with composed [mind],

children.text: prāgāsyaś cāsane sve sumṛduni samukhaṃ mīlitākṣo niviṣṭaḥ // Krd_8.97 //
children.translated_text: Facing east, seated on his own soft seat, eyes closed, [one should sit] facing [the deity].

children.text: eṣāṃ manūnāṃ mantrāṇāṃ madhye ekaṃ manum mantra-japa-homādibhiḥ svīkṛtya vaśīkṛtya aṣṭāṅgena yama-niyama-prāṇāyāma-pratyāhāra-dhyāna-dhāraṇā-samādhi-lakṣaṇena utsāritās tyaktāḥ kāma-krodhādayo 'rayo yena sa tathā harṣita-nirmala-prasanna-citto yogī prāg-vadanaḥ san yogān citta-vṛtti-nirodhādīn karotu | kīdṛśo yogī ? yathocita-vihāra-nidrā-prabodhāhāraḥ | punaḥ svakīye sukomale āsane samupaviṣṭaḥ | punaḥ kīdṛśaḥ ? sukhenānāyasena saṃmīlite mudrite akṣiṇī yena saḥ ||97||
children.translated_text: From among these mantras, having accepted — mastered — one mantra through recitation, <s>homa</s>, and other [practices]; having expelled — abandoned — enemies such as desire, anger, and the like through the eightfold [yoga] characterized by <s>yama</s>, <s>niyama</s>, <s>prāṇāyāma</s>, <s>pratyāhāra</s>, <s>dhyāna</s>, <s>dhāraṇā</s>, and <s>samādhi</s>; the <s>yogī</s> whose mind is joyful, pure, and serene, facing east, should practice the yogas — the restraints of mental activity and the like. Of what kind is this <s>yogī</s>? One whose recreation, sleep, and awakening are appropriate. Moreover, seated upon his own soft seat. Again, of what kind? One whose eyes are comfortably — effortlessly — closed.
The entire universe, consisting of elements, senses, and inner faculties — all of it, in the form of moon, fire,
And sun, composed of syllables — into the <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) in the form of the seed-syllable endowed with <s>kalā</s> and <s>nayana</s> (parts), with steadfastness;

children.text: nītvā tat-puṃsi bindv-ātmani tam api parātmany atho kāla-tattve
children.translated_text: Having led [it], and that into <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Person), who is of the nature of <s>bindu</s> (the dot); him too into the Supreme Self; then into the <s>kāla-tattva</s> (time-principle);

children.text: taṃ vai śaktau cid-ātmany api nayatu ca tāṃ kevale dhāmni śānte // Krd_8.98 //
children.translated_text: Him indeed into <s>Śakti</s> (Power), who is of the nature of consciousness; and one should lead her too into the solitary (<s>kevala</s>), peaceful abode.

children.text: etad-varṇātmakaṃ samastaṃ viśvaṃ bhūtendriyāntaḥ-karaṇa-rūpaṃ sūryendv-agni-rūpaṃ pradhāne prakṛti-rūpe kāma-bīje praṇavena nītvā tatra vilīnaṃ vicintya tat kāma-bījaṃ bindv-ātmani prasiddhe 'nusvārākhye tam api bindv-ātmānaṃ nādākhye kāla-tattve paramātmani saṃharet tam api kāla-tattvaṃ cid-rūpāyāṃ śaktau saṃharet tām api śaktiṃ kevale tejo-maye sva-prakāśe dhāmni tejasi śānte sarvopadrava-rahite nayatu || KrdC_8.98 ||
children.translated_text: The entire universe, consisting of elements, senses, and inner faculties, in the form of sun, moon, and fire, composed of these syllables — into the <s>Pradhāna</s> (<s>Prakṛti</s>, primordial nature) in the form of the <s>kāma-bīja</s> (love-seed), with the <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ), having led [it there] and having visualized its dissolution therein; that <s>kāma-bīja</s> into the well-known <s>bindu</s> (the <s>anusvāra</s>, nasal dot); that <s>bindu</s>-nature too into the <s>nāda</s>-named <s>kāla-tattva</s> (time-principle), the Supreme Self — one should absorb [it]; that <s>kāla-tattva</s> too into <s>Śakti</s>, which is of the nature of consciousness — one should absorb [it]; that <s>Śakti</s> too into the solitary, luminous, self-radiant abode (<s>dhāman</s>), peaceful — free from all disturbance — one should lead [it there].
Of what kind [is that abode]?
Free from dualities, without distinctions, dense with supreme and unsurpassable bliss, without
End, eternal — denoted by the stainless words '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' and others — in one's own Self, thus;
Having absorbed [all] and practiced the supreme seed-syllable, then gradually, with breath and mind dissolved,
With both merit and demerit exhausted — he shall become of the nature of the incomparable supreme consciousness.

children.text: nirdvandve śītoṣṇādi-dvandva-viśeṣa-rahite viśeṣo vaidharmyaṃ tad-rahite atyantānanda-ghane anante kṛṣṇa-govindādi-nirmala-śabdānāṃ pratipādye ātma-svarūpe ittham amunā prakāreṇa saṃhṛtya saṃhāraṃ kṛtvā kāma-bījaṃ japan | athānantaraṃ svayam eva niścala-śvāsa-citto bhūtvā prakṣīṇa-pāpa-puṇyaś ca bhūtvā sa yogī nirupamaḥ parama-saṃvin-mayo bhavati || KrdC_8.99 ||
children.translated_text: Free from dualities — free from the distinctions of heat and cold and the like; without distinction — without difference; dense with supreme bliss — without limit; denoted by the stainless words '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,' '<s>Govinda</s>,' and the like — in one's own Self-nature; thus, in this manner, having absorbed — having performed the absorption — while reciting the <s>kāma-bīja</s>; then, next, having himself become one of still breath and still mind; and having become one whose sins and merits are exhausted — that <s>yogī</s> becomes incomparable — becomes of the nature of supreme consciousness.
In the <s>Mūlādhāra</s> (root center), in the triangle, flashing with the brilliance of the young sun,
<s>Kāma</s> (Desire), with the radiance of billions of rising suns, blazing fires, and deer-marked [moons];
Enchantingly resplendent, like a thousand garlands of lightning, [radiant as] laughing <s>bandhujīva</s> (noon-flower) blossoms
Pervaded by the three <s>guṇa</s>s (qualities), whose <s>bindu</s> (dot) is [thus characterized] — the sole cause of the world's creation and dissolution — one should contemplate. // Krd_8.100 //

children.text: trikoṇātmake mūlādhāre udyad-ādityavat prakāśamāne bhramamāṇaṃ kāma-bījaṃ nūtanāditya-pralaya-kālīna-vahni-candra-koṭi-tulya-kāntiṃ punas taḍin-mālā-sahasra-kāntiṃ punaḥ nūtana-puṣpita-bandhukavan manoharaṃ sattvādi-guṇa-trayeṇa vyāpto 'nusvāra-saṃjñako bindur yena taṃ punaḥ viśvotpatti-nāśaika-kāraṇam || KrdC_8.100 ||
children.translated_text: In the triangular <s>mūlādhāra</s> (root center), shining like the rising sun, the revolving <s>kāma-bīja</s> (seed-syllable of desire) — having a radiance equal to ten million rising suns, dissolution-fires, and moons; again, having the radiance of a thousand garlands of lightning; again, enchanting like a newly blossoming <s>bandhūka</s> flower — the <s>bindu</s> called <s>anusvāra</s>, which is pervaded by the three qualities — <s>sattva</s> and the rest; again, the sole cause of the universe's creation and destruction. || KrdC_8.100 ||
Above it, [the <s>kuṇḍalinī</s>] shining forth, of brilliance like a mass of vivid, beautiful lightning,
Rising through the <s>suṣumnā</s> channel, like a flame, up to the moon-disc at the forehead;
Pure consciousness alone, of subtle form, containing the entire universe, a <s>kalā</s> (phase) knowable through <s>nāda</s> (resonance),

children.text: mūlaṃ yā sarva-dhāmnāṃ smaratu nirupamāṃ huṅkṛtodañciteraḥ // Krd_8.101 //
children.translated_text: The root of all radiances — one should contemplate her, the incomparable one, with the <s>apāna</s> breath raised upward by the <s>huṃ</s>-syllable. // Krd_8.101 //

children.text: tasya kāma-bījasya upari bidnu-gata-kuṇḍalinīṃ śaktiṃ dīpyamānāṃ cintayatu | kimbhūtām ? pravyakta-manohara-vidyut-sahasravat prakāśamāna-kāntiṃ, punaḥ lalāṭa-candra-bimbāntaṃ suṣumṇā-randhraṃ yāntīṃ, punaḥ anu anugatā bīja-gata-biimbātmake vahni-śikhā jvālā yasyāṃ sā tathā tām | punaḥ kimbhūtām ? cit-svarūpām | punaḥ durlakṣāṃ | punar āpta-sakala-viśvāṃ | punaḥ kalā-rūpām | punaḥ nādānumeyāṃ | punaḥ sarva-tejasāṃ mūla-bhūtām | kīdṛśo 'dhikārī ? huṅkāreṇa udañcita ūrdhvam utpāṭita iro vāyur apānākhyo yena sa tathā || KrdC_8.101 ||
children.translated_text: Above that <s>kāma-bīja</s>, one should contemplate the <s>kuṇḍalinī</s> <s>śakti</s> (power) residing in the <s>bindu</s>, blazing. Of what kind? Shining with a radiance like a thousand clearly visible, enchanting lightning flashes; again, going through the <s>suṣumnā</s> channel up to the moon-disc at the forehead; again, following — accompanying — the flame, the blaze, that is in the seed-syllable and <s>bindu</s>. Again, of what kind? Of the nature of pure consciousness. Again, difficult to perceive. Again, containing the entire universe. Again, in the form of <s>kalā</s> (phase). Again, inferable through <s>nāda</s> (subtle sound). Again, the root — the source — of all radiances. Of what kind is the practitioner? He whose <s>apāna</s> breath has been raised upward — lifted up — by the <s>huṃ</s>-syllable. || KrdC_8.101 ||
Having led her slowly upward to the downward-facing thousand-petalled red lotus, in whose interior
Shines the full moon-disc, from which flows a stream of nectar;

children.text: raktāṃ mantramayīṃ nipīya ca sudhā-nisyanda-rūpāṃ viśed
children.translated_text: Having drunk that red, mantra-formed, nectar-flowing [stream], one should re-enter

children.text: bhūyo 'py ātma-niketanaṃ punar api protthāya pītvā viśet // Krd_8.102 //
children.translated_text: One's own abode again; and rising again, drinking again, one should re-enter. // Krd_8.102 //

children.text: tāṃ kuṇḍalinīṃ śaktiṃ śanakair yathā syād evam adhomukha-sahasra-dalāruṇa-kamala-madhya-dyotamāna-pūrṇa-candra-maṇḍalaṃ nītvā asmāc candra-bimbād amṛta-dhārā-vṛṣṭiṃ rakta-varṇāṃ varṇātmikām amṛta-srava-rūpāṃ pāyayitvā ātma-niketanaṃ mūlādhāre praveśayet | bhūyo 'nantaram api tathaiva tām utthāpya tathā kṛtvā punas tathā nija-sthānaṃ prāpayed iti || KrdC_8.102 ||
children.translated_text: Having led that <s>kuṇḍalinī</s> <s>śakti</s> slowly to the full moon-disc shining in the center of the downward-facing thousand-petalled red lotus; from this moon-disc, having caused [her] to drink the shower of nectar-stream — red in color, consisting of mantra-syllables, in the form of nectar-flow — one should cause her to enter one's own abode — the <s>mūlādhāra</s>. Again thereafter, having likewise raised her, having done the same, one should again bring her to her own place. || KrdC_8.102 ||
He states the fruit of such practice —
He who practices daily in this manner the seed-lord (<s>kāma-bīja</s>) within the self,
Having conquered sin, old age, untimely death, and disease;
He himself, like an embodied <s>Anaṅga</s> (bodiless Kāma, the love-god),
Shall live long, with hair-locks dark as bees. // Krd_8.103 //

children.text: yaḥ pratyaham anena prakāreṇa śarīra-madhye kāma-bījam abhyasyaty ātmano 'ntaṃ mano-layāntam idam abhyasyatīti kriyā-viśeṣaṇam asau sādhakaḥ durita-jarāpamṛtyu-rogān parābhūya svayam eva deha-dhāri-kandarpo bhūtvā cira-kālaṃ jīvati | kīdṛśaḥ ? bhramara-varṇavat śyāma-keśa-samūhaḥ || KrdC_8.103 ||
children.translated_text: He who daily practices the <s>kāma-bīja</s> within the body in this manner, up to the dissolution of the mind — this modifies the practice — that <s>sādhaka</s>, having overcome sin, old age, untimely death, and disease, becoming himself an embodied god of love, lives for a very long time. Of what kind? With a mass of hair dark as the hue of bees. || KrdC_8.103 ||
Clear, sweet, with beautiful strings of syllable-words, of wondrous meaning —
Speech flows forth instantly from his lotus-face;

children.text: api ca sakala-mantrās tasya sidhyanti maṅkṣu
children.translated_text: Moreover, all mantras are swiftly accomplished for him,
And he abides as the sole seat of unceasing, dense bliss. // Krd_8.104 //

children.text: asya sādhakasya mukha-kamalān śīghraṃ sarasvatī prabhavatī | kimbhūtā ? pravyakta-manohara-pada-varṇa-samūhātmikā atyāścarya-viṣayā kintu asya sādhakasya maṅkṣu anye 'pi mantrāḥ sidhyanti kiṃ ca sa sādhakaḥ aviśrānta-niviḍa-sukha-mātra-sthānṃ bhūtvā tiṣṭhati || KrdC_8.104 ||
children.translated_text: From the lotus-face of this <s>sādhaka</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s> (eloquence) swiftly manifests. Of what kind? Consisting of clearly visible, enchanting strings of syllables and words, of wondrous subject-matter. Moreover, for this <s>sādhaka</s>, other mantras too are swiftly accomplished. And furthermore, that <s>sādhaka</s> abides as the sole locus of uninterrupted, dense bliss. || KrdC_8.104 ||
The revolving form of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the love-god's seed-syllable) from the <s>mūla-cakra</s> (root center),
With its own radiances, together with red nectar-streams;
Contemplating [it as] filling the entire space of the universe,
Those [beings] should be mentally projected there, for the purpose of subjugation. // Krd_8.105 //

children.text: nāryo naro vā nagarī sabhāpi vā
children.translated_text: Whether women, or a man, or a city, or an assembly —
Those projected therein by the one with sharpened mind
Become his servants instantly, perpetually,

children.text: cirāya tan nighna-dhiyo na saṃśayaḥ // Krd_8.106 //
children.translated_text: For a long time — their minds absorbed in him — without doubt. // Krd_8.106 //

children.text: mūla-cakrān mūlādhāre atra saptamy-arthe pañcamī bhramaṇa-mūrtiṃ kāma-bījaṃ svakīyābhir dīptibhir lohitāmṛta-yuktābhir brahmāṇḍa-madhya-pradeśe pūryamāṇaṃ dhyātvā niśāta-cetasā tīkṣṇa-matinā tatra nārī-prabhṛtayaḥ sādhyāvaśyārthaṃ pratyāveśyāḥ prakṣeptavyā | anantaraṃ tatra praveśitāḥ praveśa-prāpitāḥ strī-prabhṛtayas tan-nimagna-dhiyas tena hṛta-cittāḥ | tasya sādhakasya śīghraṃ cira-kālam ājñā-kāriṇo bhavanti nātra sandehaḥ || KrdC_8.105-106 ||
children.translated_text: From the <s>mūla-cakra</s> — in the <s>mūlādhāra</s>, here the fifth [case ending] is used in the sense of the seventh — the revolving form of the <s>kāma-bīja</s>, with its own radiances combined with red nectar, filling — pervading — the middle region of the universe — having meditated [thus], with sharpened — keen — mind, women and the rest should be mentally projected — cast — therein, for the purpose of subjugation. Thereafter, those women and others who have been projected — who have been caused to enter — therein, with their minds absorbed in him — their consciousness captured by him — become the servants of that <s>sādhaka</s>, instantly and for a long time, perpetually obeying his commands — there is no doubt about this. || KrdC_8.105-106 ||
In the heart-lotus endowed with sun-[like] petals, red like the <s>indra-gopa</s> insect,
With the shining, beautiful center [illuminated] by the discs of sun, moon, and fire;
In the heart-lotus, him — dark-complexioned, of tender limbs,

children.text: susukham upaniviṣṭaṃ taṃ smared vāsudevam // Krd_8.107 //
children.translated_text: Comfortably seated — one should meditate on that <s>Vāsudeva</s>. // Krd_8.107 //

children.text: tad-dvādaśa-dala-yukte hṛdaya-kamale indra-gopākhyo rakta-kīṭa-viśeṣaḥ tadvad aruṇe sūrya-vahni-candra-maṇḍala-śobhita-cāru-madhya-pradeśe amuṃ śyāma-varṇaṃ komalāṅgaṃ sukumārāṅgaṃ sukha-prakāreṇopaviṣṭaṃ vāsudevaṃ cintayet || KrdC_8.107 ||
children.translated_text: In the heart-lotus endowed with twelve petals — red like the insect known as <s>indra-gopa</s> — in the beautiful central region adorned by the discs of sun, fire, and moon — him, dark in complexion, of tender limbs — delicate-bodied — comfortably seated — one should contemplate <s>Vāsudeva</s>. || KrdC_8.107 ||
On the pair of lotus-feet, on the toes [beautiful] like pure sprouts, on the rows of beautiful nails,
On the lovely, prominent tortoise-like instep, on the pair of joined forefeet, on the shining pair of shin-staffs,

children.text: jānvor ūrvoḥ piśaṅge nava-vasana-vare mekhalā-dāmni nābhau
children.translated_text: On the knees, on the tawny thighs, on the finest new garment, on the girdle-cord, on the navel,

children.text: romāvalyām udārodara-bhuvi vipule vakṣasi prauḍha-hāre // Krd_8.108 //
children.translated_text: On the line of hair, on the noble belly, on the broad chest with its magnificent necklace. // Krd_8.108 //

children.text: ādi-puṃsaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇasya pādāmbhojam ārabhya hasitānteṣu sthāneṣu vakṣyamāṇeṣu śanair yathā syāt tathā iti kramataḥ sthāna-kramataḥ sthāna-krameṇa svīyaṃ manaḥ sthāpayatu | tathā pāda-padma-dvaye prathamaṃ manaḥ sthāpayet | tad-anantaraṃ pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ apohyāpara-sthāneṣu mano nidadhyād aṅgulya evāmala-kiśalayā nirmala-pallavās teṣu | tad anu nakhānāṃ śobhamāna-paṅktau tad-anu prapada-yuji pāda-dvaye | kīdṛśe ? kūrma-pṛṣṭhavad upari-bhāge unnate | tad-anu dedīpyamāna-jaṅghā-dvaye | tad-anu jānu-dvaye ūru-dvaye pīta-varṇe nūtana-vastrayoḥ śreṣṭhe kṣudra-ghaṇṭikā-mālāyāṃ nābhi-pradeśe tan-niṣṭha-roma-paṅktau ca vipulodara-sthāne mahāhāra-yukte vistīrṇe vakṣasi || KrdC_8.108 ||
children.translated_text: Of the primordial person, <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, beginning from the lotus-feet up to the smile — at the places to be described — slowly, in sequence, place by place, one should establish one's mind. Thus, first on the pair of lotus-feet, one should place the mind. Then, setting aside each previous [location], one should fix the mind on the subsequent places: on the toes themselves — the pure sprouts — the spotless leaf-buds — thereon. Then on the beautiful rows of nails; then on the pair of forefeet — of what kind? With the upper part arched like a tortoise's back. Then on the shining pair of shins; then on the pair of knees, on the pair of thighs — yellow-colored; on the pair of finest new garments; on the girdle of small bells; on the navel region; on the line of hair connected thereto; on the broad belly-region; on the expansive chest endowed with a great necklace. || KrdC_8.108 ||
On the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, on the <s>Kaustubha</s>, on the clearly lotus-shining chest-garland, on the arms
At the base [adorned with] resplendent armlets, on the world-protecting pair of arms adorned with bracelets,
On the fingers of the pair of hands, on the flute in which the entire universe is dissolved in exceedingly sweet sound,
On the throat, on the pair of cheeks illuminated by the beautiful rays of the fine earrings. // Krd_8.109 //

children.text: śrīvatse vipra-pādāvaghāta-tarjanyordhva-romātmake kaustubhe hṛdaya-niviṣṭa-maṇi-viśeṣe vikasita-padma-mālāyāṃ keyūra-śobhita-bāhvor mūle saṃsāra-rakṣaṇa-dakṣe kaṅkaṇa-yukte bāhu-dvaye hasta-dvayāṅguli-niṣṭhe atimadhura-śabdena magnaṃ jagat-trayaṃ yena evambhūte veṇau | tad-anu kaṇṭhe ramya-kuṇḍala-kiraṇa-prakāśita-manohara-kapola-stha-yugale || KrdC_8.109 ||
children.translated_text: On the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> — the distinctive mark with upward hair made by the kick of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s foot; on the <s>Kaustubha</s> — the special gem situated on the heart; on the garland of blossoming lotuses; on the bases of the arms adorned with resplendent armlets; on the pair of arms skilled in protecting the world — adorned with bracelets; on the fingers of the pair of hands; on the flute by whose exceedingly sweet sound the three worlds are absorbed — of such description. Then on the throat; on the pair [of cheeks] at the cheeks, enchanting, illuminated by the rays of beautiful earrings. || KrdC_8.109 ||

children.text: karṇa-dvandve ca ghoṇe nayana-nalinayor bhrū-vilāse lalāṭe
children.translated_text: On the pair of ears, on the nose, on the lotus-eyes, on the play of the eyebrows, on the forehead,
On the hair — with waving peacock feathers, resplendent with exceedingly fragrant, enchanting flowers;
On the reddish [lip] upon which the flute is placed, on the sprout-like lower lip, on the row of teeth, on the smile

children.text: jyotsnāyām ādi-puṃsaḥ krama iti ca śanaiḥ svaṃ manaḥ saṃnidhattām // Krd_8.110 //
children.translated_text: Called moonlight — of the primordial Person — in this order, one should slowly fix one's own mind. // Krd_8.110 //

children.text: karṇa-dvaye nāsā-yugale netra-padma-dvaye bhrū-vikṣepe lalāṭe cañcala-mayūra-puccha-yukteṣu atisugandhita-manohara-puṣpojjvaleṣu keśeṣu śoṇa-varṇe āropita-veṇau adhara-pallave danta-paṅktyāṃ smitam ākhyā nāma yasyā tasyāṃ jyotsnāyām candra-kāntau jyotsnā-tulye smite || KrdC_8.110 ||
children.translated_text: On the pair of ears, on the pair of nostrils, on the pair of lotus-eyes, on the play of the eyebrows, on the forehead, on the hair — endowed with waving peacock plumes, resplendent with exceedingly fragrant enchanting flowers — on the reddish [lip] upon which the flute is placed, on the sprout-like lower lip, on the row of teeth; the smile is called (<s>ākhyā</s>) — named — that which is like moonlight — moonlight-like — that smile, like the luster of the moon. || KrdC_8.110 ||
Until the mind dissolves in <s>Hari</s>'s noble
Gentle smile, one should practice the <s>Anaṅga-bīja</s> (love-seed syllable);
Or the eighteen-syllable [mantra], or indeed the ten-syllable one,
The <s>mantrī</s> (practitioner), slowly, with controlled breath. // Krd_8.111 //

children.text: harer udāre śobhamāne manda-smite mano yāvad vilayam viśeṣato layam eti tāvad anaṅga-bījam aṣṭādaśārṇam daśārṇaṃ vā prajapatu | kimbhūtaḥ ? samāhita-mātariśvā pratyāharīkṛtaḥ prāṇa-vāyuḥ || KrdC_8.111 ||
children.translated_text: Until the mind achieves complete dissolution in <s>Hari</s>'s noble — resplendent — gentle smile, one should recite the <s>Anaṅga-bīja</s>, or the eighteen-syllable, or the ten-syllable [mantra]. Of what kind? With controlled breath — with the <s>prāṇa</s> breath restrained and withdrawn. || KrdC_8.111 ||
Repeatedly placing and replacing the mind from the lotus-feet to the gentle smile,

children.text: tatra vilāpya kṣīṇe cetasi sukha-cit-sad-ātmako bhavati // Krd_8.112 //
children.translated_text: Dissolving [it] there — when the mind is diminished, one becomes of the nature of bliss, consciousness, and being. // Krd_8.112 //

children.text: manaḥ padāravindam ārabhya īsad-hāsya-paryantaṃ samāropyānantaram | tatra vilāpya līnaṃ kṛtvā kṣīṇe śuddhe citte sati sukha-jñāna-sad-ātmako bhavati sādhakaḥ || KrdC_8.112 ||
children.translated_text: Placing the mind beginning from the lotus-feet up to the gentle smile, then dissolving it there — making it absorbed — when the mind becomes diminished — purified — the <s>sādhaka</s> becomes of the nature of bliss (<s>sukha</s>), knowledge (<s>cit</s>), and being (<s>sat</s>). || KrdC_8.112 ||

Of <s>nyāsa</s> (placement), <s>japa</s> (recitation), <s>homa</s> (fire-offering), <s>pūjā</s> (worship), <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation), <s>mantrābhiṣeka</s> (mantra-consecration), and <s>viniyoga</s> (application) —
The sequence, as described for all the mantras, has been illuminated by me through this <s>Dīpikā</s> (Illumination) alone. // Krd_8.113 //

children.text: kṛṣṇa-mantra-samūha-kathitānāṃ nyāsa-japādīnāṃ krama-dīpikayaiva kramaḥ prakāśitaḥ || KrdC_8.113 ||
children.translated_text: The sequence of <s>nyāsa</s>, <s>japa</s>, and the rest, as described for the entire collection of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-mantras, has been illuminated by this <s>Krama-dīpikā</s> alone. || KrdC_8.113 ||
This <s>Krama-dīpikā</s>, which cuts through the darkness of doubt, by the good

children.text: kara-dīpikeva dhāryā sasneham aharniśaṃ samasta-sukhāptyai // Krd_8.114 //
children.translated_text: Should be held like a lamp in the hand, with loving care, day and night, for the attainment of all happiness. // Krd_8.114 //

children.text: saiṣā krama-dīpikā sādhu-janaiḥ sa-snehaṃ yathā syāt tathā kara-dīpikeva dhāryā | kimbhūtā ? saṃśaya-rūpāndhakāra-cchedayitrī anyāpi tailādi-sneha-sahitaṃ yathā syāt tathā dhāryate andhakāra-nāśinī bhavati | kim arthaṃ dhāryā ? samasta-sukha-prāpty-artham || KrdC_8.114 ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Krama-dīpikā</s> should be held by the good people — the virtuous — with loving care, like a lamp in the hand. Of what kind? One that dispels the darkness in the form of doubt. Just as [a lamp is held] with oil and the like — with affection — so it should be held; it destroys darkness. For what purpose should it be held? For the attainment of all happiness. || KrdC_8.114 ||

children.text: jagad idam anubiddhaṃ yena yasmāt prasūte
children.translated_text: By whom this world is pervaded, from whom it is born,

children.text: yad anu tatam ajasraṃ pāti cādhiṣṭhitā yam |
children.translated_text: By whom it is continuously sustained, supported, and protected;

children.text: yad uru maha udarcir yaṃ vidhatte ca gopī
children.translated_text: Whose great, rising radiance — whom the cowherd-maiden (<s>Gopī</s>) [i.e., <s>Śrī</s>] manifests —
To him, the light of immortal bliss and knowledge — to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, I bow. // Krd_8.115 //

children.text: jagad idam anuviddham anusyūtaṃ yena jyotiṣā yasmāt parameśvarāt imaṃ jana-lokaṃ saṃsārākhyaṃ prasūte prasūtiṃ prānotīty arthaḥ | yasminn ity api pāṭhaḥ | tathā parameśvaram adhiṣṭhātāram āśritā satī anutataṃ vistṛtaṃ jagat ajasraṃ sarvadā pāti rakṣati yasya parameśvarasya ūru vipulaṃ mahaḥ tejaḥ tat udarcis tat-tejasā udita-dīptiḥ satī yaṃ pratibimba-rūpeṇa dhatte tam uktānandaṃ sva-prakāśaṃ naumi staumi || KrdC_8.115 ||
children.translated_text: By whose light this world is pervaded — threaded through — from the Supreme Lord this world — this realm of beings — called <s>saṃsāra</s> — is born — receives birth — this is the meaning. There is also the reading '<s>yasminn</s>' (in whom). Likewise, having taken refuge in the Supreme Lord — the controller — continuously, the expanded universe is always protected. Whose great — vast — radiance — that radiance — whose splendor arises from that — being so, she manifests him as a reflected image. To him — of the described bliss, self-luminous — I bow, I praise. || KrdC_8.115 ||
He who, though established in his own abode, [uses] the discus as an instrument of his play —
Given by the enemy of <s>Manmatha</s> (i.e., <s>Śiva</s>) for the purpose of protection, dispelling the afflictions of the world;
He bears [the discus] — resplendent with blazing newness, eternally free from sin, having assumed <s>Māyā</s> (divine illusion);

children.text: vande kāya-vimardanaṃ vadha-kṛtāṃ bhuñjad-dyukaṃ yādavam // Krd_8.116 //
children.translated_text: I salute the <s>Yādava</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) whose body crushes [the enemies], the destroyer of the slain, who enjoys the heavenly [realm].

children.text:
yaḥ parameśvaraḥ śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ vakṣyamāṇa-lakṣaṇaṃ cakraṃ dhatte taṃ vande ity anvayaḥ | kathambhūtaṃ cakram ? nija-keli-sādhanaṃ nija-yuddha-krīḍā-karaṇam | kīdṛśaḥ parameśvaraḥ ? adhiṣṭhāna-sthito 'pi samādhi-sthito 'pi | yad vā, bāhya-sthito 'pi prabhuḥ svāmī | punaḥ kīdṛśaiḥ ? manmatha-śatruṇā mahā-devena avane avana-kṛte sarva-loka-rakṣārthaṃ dattam | punar dūrīkṛtātivṛṣṭy-anāvṛṣṭy-ādy-apadravaṃ, punaḥ dīpta-navena iva śobhanaṃ dedīpyamānam | kiṃ bhūtaṃ kṛṣṇam ? pāpa-rahitaṃ svīkṛta-māyaṃ punar dhruvam avināśinaṃ punar vadha-kṛtām upadrava-kāriṇāṃ kāya-vimardanaṃ śarīra-nāśakaṃ punaḥ bhuñjad-dyukaṃ bhuñjat-svarga-lokaṃ punar jātyāyād avam ity arthaḥ
| atra padye cakra-bandhe grantha-kartā sva-nāma prakṣiptavān iti bodhyam || KrdC_8.116 ||
children.translated_text:
The Supreme Lord <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> who bears the discus of the description to be stated — him I salute — this is the syntactic connection. Of what kind is the discus? An instrument for his own sport — a means for his war-play. Of what kind is the Supreme Lord? Even while abiding in his seat — even while established in <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption); alternatively, even while outwardly present, he is the master, the Lord. Again, of what kind? Given by the enemy of <s>Manmatha</s> — by <s>Mahādeva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) — for protection, for the sake of protecting all the worlds. Again, having removed the calamities of excessive rain, drought, and other disasters. Again, resplendent — blazing — as if with new radiance. Of what kind is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>? Free from sin, having assumed <s>Māyā</s> (divine power); again, imperishable — indestructible; again, the crusher of the bodies of those who cause harm — the destroyer of [hostile] bodies; again, enjoying the heavenly world; again, of the <s>Yādava</s> lineage — this is the meaning.
Here, in this verse composed in the <s>cakra-bandha</s> (wheel-pattern), the author has inserted his own name — this should be understood.

Thus ends the eighth chapter (<s>paṭala</s>) of the <s>Krama-dīpikā</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Mahāmahopādhyāya</s> (Great Great Preceptor) <s>Śrī Keśava Kāśmīri Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī</s>.
||8||
This treatise is complete.
